## Appeal ≠ constitutional judicial review
- Act provides a statutory appeal route to the **Supreme Court subject to statutory conditions**.
- **High Court judicial review under Articles 226/227 remains**; **Balkrishna Ram (9 January 2020)** expressly affirms this. PDF's blanket 'only Supreme Court' excludes this distinction incorrectly. [Supreme Court judgment](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2017/4913/4913_2017_15_1501_19348_Judgement_09-Jan-2020.pdf).
- Source January 2025 discussion: additional benches for J&K/Himachal to reduce pendency; treat proposed expansion separately from actual constitution of a bench.
## Embedded tribunal recall
- **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, **Part XIV-A**: **Article 323A**, public-service administrative tribunals, Parliament; **323B**, tribunals for specified other matters, Parliament or state legislatures within competence.
- **Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985**: CAT/SAT framework; do not assume every specialised tribunal, including AFT, is automatically created under 323A.
- Examples in graphic: CAT, NGT, ITAT, CESTAT, SAT (securities), water-disputes tribunals; old **COMPAT** label is historical because competition appeals moved to NCLAT.
- Expertise and access must accompany institutional independence, vacancies filled and constitutional review.

topics.title: Alaknanda and Panch Prayag
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## River route
- Garhwal Himalayas, **Uttarakhand**; meltwaters of **Satopanth and Bhagirath Kharak glaciers**; approximately **190 km** to Devprayag.
- Main Ganga headstreams: **Alaknanda and Bhagirathi**; join at **Devprayag → Ganga**. Alaknanda contributes the larger flow, while Bhagirathi is traditionally treated as the source stream.
| Confluence, upstream → downstream | Alaknanda joins |
| --- | --- |
| Vishnuprayag | Dhauliganga |
| Nandprayag | Nandakini |
| Karnaprayag | Pindar |
| Rudraprayag | Mandakini |
| Devprayag | Bhagirathi |
- Valley links **Badrinath, Joshimath** and routes towards **Hemkund Sahib**; Hemkund is reached via a tributary-valley route, not situated on the main Alaknanda channel.
- Uttarakhand Char Dham: **Badrinath, Kedarnath, Gangotri, Yamunotri**; not all four lie along the Alaknanda itself.
## Landslide-dam risk
- January 2025 source cites **IIT Roorkee** study: landslides can block the river, create temporary reservoirs, then breach and release flood pulses.
- Combine slope monitoring, drainage/land-use safeguards, upstream blockage detection and downstream warning/evacuation. See [landslides](landslides.html) through the main topic index if browsing across subjects.

topics.title: Common noctule bat and migration
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Species recall
- **Nyctalus noctula**; insectivorous mammal; narrow pointed wings, strong direct flight/steep insect-chasing dives; golden to dark-brown upper body, paler underside.
- Forest/tree hollows and some buildings/crevices; open-country/settlement foraging. Hibernates in winter; urban roosts important in parts of eastern Europe.
- Source distribution spans **Europe and temperate Asia**, with peripheral localities; **IUCN Least Concern** is the source status, not absence of local threats.
- Echolocation around **25 kHz**; this is **ultrasound**, above the usual ~20-kHz human limit. Some lower-frequency components may be audible; source's blanket '25 kHz heard by children' is unreliable.
## January 2025 migration study
- Common noctules exploit **warm tailwinds ahead of storm fronts**: temperature rises/pressure falls → departures → longer travel with lower energy use.
- Study tracked **71 females**, moving generally northeast from Swiss wintering areas; **no single fixed corridor**, feeding stops and almost **400 km in one night** recorded. Study tracked portions, not every individual's entire annual migration. [Max Planck study](https://www.mpg.de/23893833/bats-surf-storm-fronts-during-continental-migration).
- Ecological role: insect control; conservation use: predict migration windows and reduce wind-turbine collision mortality.

topics.title: BHARATPOL and INTERPOL cooperation
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Platform
- **CBI-developed**, launched **7 January 2025** by Union Home Minister; **CBI is NCB-New Delhi**, India's National Central Bureau for INTERPOL.
- Single digital channel connects Indian law-enforcement agencies with CBI/INTERPOL cooperation: standard requests, faster intelligence sharing, notices, documents and training.
- Crimes: cybercrime, trafficking in persons/drugs/arms, financial fraud, terrorism/online radicalisation; cross-border data requests need lawful safeguards.
| Module | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| Connect | CBI/NCB and Indian agencies on one platform |
| INTERPOL Notices | Notice requests |
| Broadcast | Disseminate foreign assistance/intelligence requests |
| References | International investigative assistance |
| Resources | Documents and capacity building |
- The PDF misassigns Notice functionality to **Connect**; keep the modules distinct. [MHA/PIB](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2099539&lang=2&reg=48).
## INTERPOL and notices
- **International Criminal Police Organization; 1923; Lyon, France**. Source states **196 members**; '195 other countries' is consistent with India being one of 196, but '195 total members' is outdated.
| Notice | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Red | Locate and provisionally arrest a wanted person for extradition/surrender or similar lawful action |
| Blue | Obtain identity/location/activity information |
| Green | Warning about persons posing a criminal threat |
| Yellow | Missing persons, often minors; identify persons unable to identify themselves |
| Black | Identify bodies |
| Orange | Warn of dangerous events/objects/materials/methods |
| Purple | Criminal methods, devices or concealment techniques |
| INTERPOL–UNSC special | Individuals/entities subject to UNSC sanctions |
- **Red Notice is not an international arrest warrant**; national law controls legal effect. [INTERPOL notices](https://www.interpol.int/How-we-work/Notices/), [official safeguards FAQ](https://www.interpol.int/content/download/15314/file/INTERPOL%20FAQ%20on%20Personal%20Data%20Safeguards.pdf).
- Institutional priorities in graphic: counter-terrorism, organised/emerging crime and cybercrime.
## INTERPOL Silver Notice: January 2025
- **First published 10 January**, requested by **Italy** to trace assets of a senior mafia member. Assets: property, vehicles, financial accounts/business interests linked to crime.
- Pilot **52 countries/territories including India**, planned at least to **November 2025**, collective ceiling **500 Silver Notices/diffusions**, not 500 for each country. Based on **2023 Vienna General Assembly** resolution. [INTERPOL announcement](https://www.interpol.int/News-and-Events/News/2025/INTERPOL-publishes-first-Silver-Notice-targeting-criminal-assets).
- Asset tracing can support fraud/corruption/drug/environmental-crime investigations; **does not automatically freeze, confiscate or repatriate assets**. National legal process/evidence, international cooperation and judicial safeguards remain necessary.
- **Silver = assets; Red = locate/request provisional arrest of persons under applicable law**. Source CBI Director's claim “more effective than MLAT” is an assessment; notices do not replace every mutual legal assistance requirement.

topics.title: Net-zero banking and financed emissions
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 framework
- **Net-Zero Banking Alliance (NZBA)**: bank-led, **UNEP Finance Initiative-convened**, launched **2021**; voluntary alignment of lending/investment/capital-market portfolios with **net-zero by 2050 or sooner**, Paris goals.
- Targets for **2030**, intermediate milestones; priority to emissions-intensive energy, transport, agriculture and other sectors; annual **absolute emissions and intensity** reporting.
- CEO-signed commitment, member-bank Steering Group and UNEP FI secretariat support; source describes intermediary sector targets within **36 months**. Historical framework requirements changed later.
- Source January 2025 context: major US banks withdrawing; **no Indian bank member** reported at that time. Do not present this as current membership.
- **Financed emissions ≠ only office/branch emissions**; portfolio reductions should support real-economy transition. Offsets require credible quality and disclosure, not substitution for every reduction.
## Mains evaluation and later status
- Benefits: comparable targets, accountability and transition finance; limitations: voluntary enforcement, exits, inconsistent scope, greenwashing and undue offset reliance.
- **August 2025**: activities paused while members voted on transition to a framework. Today's official page presents **Net-Zero Banking Resources**, not a current member roster; the January alliance description is historical. [UNEP FI August update](https://www.unepfi.org/net-zero-banking/media/nzba-update-august-2025/), [resources](https://www.unepfi.org/net-zero-banking/).

topics.title: Crowd crush and stampede prevention
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## How crowd disasters develop
- Dense crowds + bottleneck/opposing flows/sudden stopping/barrier failure → pressure waves, falls or pile-ups → injury and **compressive/traumatic asphyxia**.
- Source types: **unidirectional** (same flow suddenly obstructed) and **turbulent/multidirectional** (flows converge/disordered pressure). A crush need not require irrational panic or running.
- Chest/upper-abdominal compression impairs breathing; head/neck/internal-organ injury and cardiac events also possible. Source **3–4 persons/m²** warning is not one universal safe/unsafe threshold; venue geometry and flow matter.
- Hazards: inadequate lighting/exits, stalls/parking narrowing paths, counterflows, weak structures, fire/electrical/LPG risks, poor communication and rumours.
- Impacts: deaths/disability, PTSD, income loss, medical/legal/compensation costs, infrastructure damage and loss of public trust.
## Prevention: capacity → flow → monitoring → response
- Assess venue carrying capacity, arrival/departure peaks and vulnerable groups; timed/ticketed entry where appropriate, separate ingress/egress and keep emergency access clear.
- Coordinated police/organiser command; route maps, multilingual public-address/signage, suitable barricades, CCTV and staff trained to relieve pressure early.
- Ambulances, medical teams, hospital links, evacuation drills; safe electrical wiring, LPG and fireworks controls. [NDMA safety guidance via PIB](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/printrelease.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=151549).
- **NDMA**, chaired by **Prime Minister**, statutory under **Disaster Management Act 2005**: policy/plans/guidelines; connect preparedness to **Sendai Framework**.
- Density sensors/LiDAR, RFID and drones may aid monitoring where lawful and reliable; privacy, accessibility, power/network backup and actionable thresholds matter. PDF's bioluminescent pavement/automatic colour-changing schemes are suggestions, not established NDMA mandates.
- Source's 'upcoming Asian Ministerial Conference with UNISDR' is recycled older material, not a January 2025 event announcement.
## Indian examples in the embedded graphic
| Date | Event / place |
| --- | --- |
| 27 August 2003 | Nashik Kumbh, Maharashtra |
| 25 January 2005 | Mandhardevi, Satara, Maharashtra |
| 3 August 2008 | Naina Devi, Bilaspur, Himachal Pradesh |
| 30 September 2008 | Chamunda Devi, Jodhpur, Rajasthan |
| 4 March 2010 | Ram Janki temple, Pratapgarh, Uttar Pradesh |
| 8 November 2011 | Haridwar, Uttarakhand |
| 19 November 2012 | Adalat Ghat, Patna; makeshift bridge failure |
| 13 October 2013 | Ratangarh temple, Datia, Madhya Pradesh |
| 3 October 2014 | Gandhi Maidan, Patna |
| 14 July 2015 | Godavari Pushkaram, Rajahmundry, Andhra Pradesh |
| 1 January 2022 | Vaishno Devi, Jammu and Kashmir |
| March 2023 | Indore temple stepwell-cover collapse; structural disaster, not simply crowd panic |
| July 2024 | Hathras, Uttar Pradesh |
- Graphic tolls range from **12 to 340**, including an early **116** for Hathras; provisional and sometimes inconsistent counts are not settled final totals. Useful for comparing crowd/structure failures without memorising disputed precision.
- Supplied 'Daily Mains Question' is coaching practice, not a year-identified UPSC PYQ.
## Railway crowd management
- February 15, 2025 New Delhi station tragedy: anticipate pilgrimage demand; coordinate entry holding areas, platforms, train information and emergency routes with RPF/local services.
- CCTV must feed timely decisions; reliable announcements, trained staff and usable exits matter more than equipment alone.
- The 2017 Elphinstone Road event was a **crowd crush**, not a bridge collapse. Source passenger-per-coach arithmetic lacks a consistent train/coach/time denominator.

## 4 May 2025: Goa temple tragedy
- Embedded clipping reports a crowd disaster during **Lairai Devi Jatra, Shirgao, Goa, 3 May 2025**. Its early headline says seven killed/80 injured; treat these as provisional source counts rather than settled totals. The Goa Governor’s official condolence confirms the incident. [Goa Government](https://dip.goa.gov.in/governor-expresses-grief-over-shirgao-jatra-stampede/).
- The accompanying material repeats the prevention framework above: capacity/flow planning, clear exits, police-organiser coordination, medical response and monitoring. Sensor/RFID/drone/lighting proposals are aids requiring reliable operation, not proof they were deployed or would automatically prevent a crush.
- Historical comparison graphic also recalls **1954 Allahabad Kumbh, 1989 Hillsborough stadium, 1993 Lan Kwai Fong and 2010 Cambodia bridge festival**. These illustrate bottlenecks, crowd compression and failed crowd management; quoted tolls are not harmonised final totals. Avoid attributing every incident simply to panic.

## 5 June 2025: Bengaluru celebration tragedy
- **4 June, M. Chinnaswamy Stadium, Bengaluru:** crowd crush during **RCB’s IPL victory celebration** killed **11**, with reported injuries; official enquiry announced. These are dated incident reports, not a completed finding assigning every organiser’s liability. [Official broadcaster report](https://newsonair.gov.in/bengaluru-at-least-6-killed-in-stampede-during-rcb-victory-celebrations/).
- Sudden popular celebrations require capacity limits, reliable entry information, separate ingress/egress, police–organiser command, crowd-pressure monitoring and immediate medical access. Dense compression can kill without a crowd irrationally running.
- Goa clipping and historical disaster graphics repeat earlier examples; source’s new lighting/AI/RFID proposals are not NDMA mandates. A monitoring device must trigger timely action; it cannot replace usable exits or safe capacity planning.

topics.title: Saudi floods and arid-region urban risk
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 case
- Source reports heavy rain, thunderstorms and flooding in **Mecca/Makkah, Madinah and Jeddah**, Saudi Arabia; roads/buildings inundated, vehicles displaced, travel disrupted.
- Source rainfall snapshot: **Al-Shafiyah, Madinah 49.2 mm; Al-Basateen, Jeddah 38 mm**; accumulation period unspecified, so do not compare with annual rainfall.
- **National Center of Meteorology (NCM)** alerts; **Saudi Red Crescent Authority** preparedness. 'Unprecedented' is the article's description, not a verified historical record.
## Mechanism and mains application
- Arid climate does **not exclude flash flooding**: concentrated rainfall + rapid runoff/impervious surfaces + insufficient drainage → short-warning floods.
- **Mecca**: Kaaba/Hajj pilgrimage; **Jeddah**, Red Sea gateway/transport hub; pilgrimage demand raises exposure and evacuation complexity.
- Impacts: disrupted roads/tourism/business, damaged infrastructure, contaminated water/waterborne-disease risk and rescue demands.
- Actions: rainfall nowcasting, drainage/wadi-flow protection, resilient roads, public warnings, rescue/health coordination and safe drinking water.
- Climate change can increase intense-rain risk, but attributing this specific event requires evidence; the PDF alone does not establish causation or a region-wide trend.

topics.title: India–Afghanistan engagement
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 diplomatic step
- **8 January 2025, Dubai**: Foreign Secretary **Vikram Misri** met Taliban administration's acting Foreign Minister **Amir Khan Muttaqi**; an upgrade to Foreign Secretary-level contact after the **2021 Taliban takeover**, not the first India–Afghanistan meeting ever.
- Humanitarian assistance, Afghan needs, trade via **Chabahar, Iran**, connectivity and regional security. **Engagement did not constitute formal Indian recognition of the Taliban government** in this January context.
- **1950 Treaty of Friendship**; development links include **Salma/Afghan–India Friendship Dam, Herat; 218-km Zaranj–Delaram road; Afghan Parliament; Indira Gandhi Institute of Child Health and Habibia School, Kabul**.
- Source graphic also cites **Pul-e-Khumri–Kabul 220-kV transmission line and Chimtala substation**, plus historical aid commitment **~$3.1 billion since November 2001**; not an annual aid figure.
## Interests → constraints → response
- Central Asian access and trade; Chabahar bypasses Pakistan-dependent overland access. Afghanistan is **landlocked**, not an Arabian Sea port state.
- Prevent terrorist safe havens; humanitarian goodwill and people-to-people links; avoid abandoning Afghan citizens amid political change.
- Constraints: Taliban governance/rights and security concerns, Pakistan transit/security factor and growing Chinese engagement.
- Practical response: conditional project delivery, aid with accountability, diplomatic channels and connectivity, without conflating contact with endorsement of domestic practices.
## Map PYQ revision
- **2022 Afghanistan borders: (c), Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan** among the five listed countries. Afghanistan also borders **Pakistan, Iran and China**; **Azerbaijan and Kyrgyzstan do not border Afghanistan**. River segments include the Amu Darya system; do not assume every boundary segment is one river.

topics.title: Dam safety: institutions, engineering and risks
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Dam Safety Act, 2021
- Surveillance, inspection, operation and maintenance of **specified dams**; prevent failure disasters and strengthen institutional responsibility.
| Level | Institution / role |
| --- | --- |
| National | **NCDS**, policy/protocol/standard-setting; chaired by CWC Chairperson |
| National | **NDSA**, implement/enforce framework and specified dispute-resolution functions |
| State | **State Committee on Dam Safety**, policy oversight |
| State | **State Dam Safety Organisation**, surveillance, monitoring and safety work |
- **Section 5**: NCDS constitution. **Both NCDS and NDSA notified 17 February 2022**; the PDF's January 2025 blanket 'NCDS not constituted' claim conflicts with official records. Distinguish initial constitution, periodic reconstitution and operational gaps. [Jal Shakti release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1807799&lang=2&reg=48).
## Risks and safeguards
- Ageing/structural deterioration; seismic exposure (**Tehri**); inadequate staff/maintenance; extreme inflows; sedimentation/storage loss; interstate operation disputes (**Mullaperiyar, Kerala–Tamil Nadu**); **2019 Tiware breach, Maharashtra**.
- Dams support irrigation, hydropower, water supply and flood moderation, but cannot eliminate every flood.
- Source ranks India **third in large-dam ownership**, gives **over 5,000/~5,700 dams**, **75–80% over 25 years**, **~200/227/234 over 100 years** across text/graphics. Snapshots differ; don't combine into one current inventory. **75% irrigation dependent on dams** is an unverified scope claim.
- **NRLD**, CWC inventory; **DRIP**, rehabilitation with World Bank/AIIB support for relevant phases; **DHARMA**, Dam Health and Rehabilitation Monitoring Application. Digital records are not automatically continuous sensor measurements.
- Source earthquake-safety centre example: seismic assessment/research; do not infer a separate universal enforcement authority from its name.
- Inspect before/after monsoon and distress events; funded rehabilitation, trained staff, instrumentation, emergency action plans, downstream warning/drills, sediment management and climate-sensitive operating rules. Drones/IoT/satellite/AI complement engineering inspections.
## Structure recall from the graphic
| Type | How it resists load |
| --- | --- |
| Embankment | Compacted earth/rockfill, controlled permeability/core and drainage |
| Gravity | Concrete/masonry mass resists water pressure; sound foundation |
| Arch | Curved concrete transfers load to strong canyon abutments |
| Buttress | Sloping slab/face supported by buttresses; transfers force to foundation |
- **Crest** top; **heel** upstream base; **toe** downstream base; **spillway** controlled overflow; **outlet/sluice** release; **gallery** internal inspection/drainage passage; **freeboard** vertical gap above water level to crest. Permeable material allows flow, impervious material restricts it.
## Historical NRLD-2019 graphic: completion-year recall
| Dam / tank | Year | State |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Thonnur Tank | 1000 | Karnataka |
| Cumbhum | 1500 | Andhra Pradesh |
| Swarup Sagar | 1560 | Rajasthan |
| Udai Sagar | 1585 | Rajasthan |
| Dhamapur | 1600 | Maharashtra |
| Rajsamand | 1676 | Rajasthan |
| Barwa Sagar, Magar Pur, Pachwara Lake | 1694 | Uttar Pradesh |
| Jai Samand | 1730 | Rajasthan |
| Jagannathasagar | 1781 | Odisha |
| Kalapvihir, Mudana, Rushi | 1800 | Maharashtra |
| Vihar | 1860 | Maharashtra |
- Names/years reproduced as **dated inventory recall** from the source, not proof all reservoirs have identical original/completion histories; older structures may be reconstructed.
## May 2025: specified dams and responsibilities
- **Dam Safety Act 2021** covers dams **over 15 m**, and **10–15 m with specified qualifying features**; owner obligations include inspection, maintenance, records and emergency preparedness. NCDS/NDSA/State committees/organisations are already mapped in this topic; NDSA's specified regulatory/dispute functions do not settle every water-allocation dispute. [Act](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/17002/1/A202141.pdf).
## Question revision and source-label audit
- **2022 reservoir pairs:** Ghataprabha—**Karnataka**; Gandhi Sagar—**Madhya Pradesh**; Indira Sagar—**Madhya Pradesh**; Maithon—**Jharkhand**. **Three wrongly matched**, (c).
- Dam–river recall: **Tehri—Bhagirathi; Sardar Sarovar—Narmada; Bhakra/Nangal—Sutlej; Nagarjuna Sagar—Krishna; Mettur—Cauvery**. Their printed 2019/2014 question labels are not authenticated by this issue.
- Extreme catchment inflows/flash floods, seismic events, inadequate spillways, design/construction deficiencies, deterioration and operational mistakes can cause failure. The printed **2017 dam-threat question** is unverified; urbanisation can affect exposure, runoff and encroachment, so avoid its absolute assertion that urbanisation never affects safety.
- **2023 Mains dam-failure, 150 words/10 marks**, is authentic: causes plus two examples. **Machchhu II, Gujarat (1979)** and **Banqiao, China (1975)** illustrate extreme-rainfall/overtopping and systemic engineering/preparedness risks; source Banqiao **171,000 deaths** is an aggregate disaster estimate including indirect effects, not a precise confirmed immediate dam-death count.
- Source **2018 mountain-valley question** belongs to **GS IV Ethics**, not GS III; official **Q5(a), 150 words/10 marks**, authenticated from the cached original. 2015 environmental/social impacts, 2012 interlinking and 2009 Tehri prompts remain **unverified labelled questions**, not reliable PYQ entries. **GS III format began in 2013**, making earlier GS III labels anachronistic.
## Useful answer content
- Large dams alter flows, sediment supply and aquatic ecosystems; reservoirs can submerge forests, settlements and cultural assets. Benefits—water supply, irrigation, hydropower/flood moderation—must be weighed against ecological and social costs.
- Impact assessment, genuine community consultation, rehabilitation/compensation/livelihood restoration, safety studies, early warning and contingency plans; suitable ecological flows/fish passage and catchment management. Afforestation cannot instantly replace lost mature habitats.
- Interlinking may improve supply in particular cases but “surplus” varies seasonally; high finance/energy needs, ecological changes and displacement require basin-level assessment. Tehri illustrates Himalayan seismic/rehabilitation debate; neither every dam is unsafe nor every project automatically sustainable.

topics.title: Flamingo Festival and wetland ecotourism
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 event and locations
- Source scheduled **18–20 January 2025**, **Sullurpeta, Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh**, returning after five years.
- Birdwatching/eco-tourism at **Nelapattu**, **B.V. Palem**, **Atakanithippa**, **Sri City** and nearby wetland sites; **Pulicat** landscape links Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. The source's 'over 200 bird species' is broad event-region richness, not a promise every visitor sees 200 species.
- Cultural programmes, arts/crafts, biodiversity awareness and community participation; source says eligible local infrastructure work supported through **MGNREGA**, not that the entire festival is an MGNREGA scheme.
## Mains balance
- Benefits: habitat awareness, local businesses/livelihoods and cultural exchange.
- Risks: disturbance to birds, waste, overbuilding and exclusion of marginalised communities.
- Response: carrying-capacity limits, habitat buffers, waste control, ecologically suitable access and transparent local benefit sharing; conservation outcomes matter alongside tourist numbers.

topics.title: Revenue, DIPAM and disinvestment
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Ministry of Finance: who does what?
| Department | Core role |
| --- | --- |
| Revenue | Direct/indirect tax administration/policy; **CBDT** and **CBIC**; income tax, customs, Union GST/central excise remit |
| **DIPAM** | Government equity investment and disinvestment/public-asset management within assigned remit; strategic/minority stake sales and investor/capital-market interface |
| Public Enterprises | Public-enterprise policy/performance matters; distinct from DIPAM |
- State GST administration and all government non-equity assets are not automatically controlled solely by DoR/DIPAM.
- **Minority disinvestment**: sell a stake while retaining control. **Strategic disinvestment**: transfer substantial stake/management control as applicable. **Privatisation**: control transferred to private owners; not every stake sale is privatisation.
- Restructuring, efficiency, fiscal proceeds and public-interest valuation; consider competition, worker protection and transparency.
## Dated appointments
- **8 January 2025**, ACC approval: **Tuhin Kanta Pandey → Revenue Secretary**, **Arunish Chawla → DIPAM Secretary**, with temporary additional charges cited for **Public Enterprises and Culture**.
- Retain as January 2025 context preceding Budget preparation, not current officeholders.

topics.title: Road safety, cashless care and hit-and-run compensation
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Treatment ≠ compensation
| Provision | Distinction |
| --- | --- |
| Cashless road-accident treatment | **Up to ₹1.5 lakh per victim, maximum 7 days** at designated hospitals under scheme conditions |
| Hit-and-run compensation | Separate **₹2 lakh for death; ₹50,000 for grievous injury**, 2022 scheme |
- Source January 2025 discussion follows **2024 pilot**. Pan-India **Cashless Treatment of Road Accident Victims Scheme, 2025** notified **5 May 2025**, guidelines **4 June**; do not backdate nationwide formal notification to January. [MoRTH clarification](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2153890&lang=2&reg=48), [2022 compensation notification](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1801656&lang=2&reg=48).
- Statutory basis: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 **section 162**, inserted through **2019 amendment**. Eligible accidents caused by use of motor vehicles; 'all accidents without conditions' is too broad.
- **NHA IT platform**, police, designated hospitals and state authorities; **eDAR = electronic Detailed Accident Report** supports verification/reporting. Not identical to AB-PM-JAY beneficiary insurance.
## Why and how
- **Golden hour**: first hour after injury, rapid appropriate trauma care can improve survival; emergency transport/referral and blood/trauma capacity matter.
- Good Samaritans need protection, awareness and straightforward assistance procedures.
- Official **2023** report: **1,72,890 fatalities; ages 18–45 = 66.4%**. PDF's **1.8 lakh / 18–34 = 66%** mixes rounding/age groups. [MoRTH report](https://morth.nic.in/sites/default/files/Road-Accident-in-India-2023-Publications.pdf).
- Implementation: rural access, ambulance/hospital capacity, public awareness, prompt reimbursement, coordination, fraud controls and sustainable funding; prevention complements post-crash care.
## 15 May: prevent crashes through a Safe System
- Source’s **2022 ~1.68 lakh fatalities/~460 per day** is a dated baseline. Its road-network 6.3 millionkm, Japan/UK fatality-rate comparisons and 2047 urban-share 50% require matching dates/definitions; the latter is a projection, not a present fact.
- **Safe System:** humans make mistakes → road/vehicle/speed design should prevent fatal consequences → shared responsibility among authorities, designers, manufacturers and users. Protect pedestrians, cyclists, two-wheelers, children/older people and transit users.
- **Engineering:** footpaths, protected cycle lanes, refuge islands, raised crossings, clear markings and appropriate speed design. **Enforcement:** helmets/seatbelts, speed cameras. **Education:** sustained public/driver training. **Emergency care:** ambulances/trauma capability in the golden hour.
- Source initiatives include black-spot rectification, national-highway audits and vehicle standards; **over 5000 blackspots** means identified/targeted, not proven all rectified. District driver-training/fitness-centre coverage is a goal, not achieved universal infrastructure.
- Editorial proposes **automakers direct 100% CSR to road safety for 20–25 years**; this is not enacted CSR law. Proposed uses: trauma care, R&D, awareness, blackspots and driver education.
- Article 21 links protection of life to State prevention/emergency duties; the article’s safe-travel-right language does not mean every collision automatically establishes a constitutional violation.
- Source economic estimates **US$109 billion over 10 years to halve fatalities, loss~3% GDP and ₹4 benefit per₹1 invested** are study/scenario figures, not annual budget commitments or universal investment returns. Integrate prevention with equitable urban planning and SDGs 3.6/11.

topics.title: Anaemia and AnemiaPhone
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mechanism and causes
- **Anaemia**: low haemoglobin/oxygen-carrying capacity for the relevant group; iron deficiency is a major cause, **not the only cause**.
- Other contributors: **B12/folate deficiency**, poor intake, infections, blood loss and inherited blood disorders; nutrition and access inequalities matter.
- Fatigue, weakness, breathlessness, impaired function; severe cases can be life-threatening. Pregnancy risks include prematurity/low birthweight; signs alone do not establish the cause.
## AnemiaPhone: point-of-care iron assessment
- **Cornell University** technology licensed to **ICMR** for public-health use; announced **December 2024**, discussed in January 2025 notes. Integrates into anaemia/women's/maternal-child-health programmes; transfer is not proof of universal rollout.
- Finger-prick blood → **test strip + portable reader** → result in minutes → phone/tablet/computer-connected clinical record; source describes Bluetooth/Wi-Fi-enabled readers.
- Enables decentralised **iron-status screening**, potentially before clinical anaemia, and appropriate referral/differential diagnosis; not symptom-only smartphone diagnosis. [Cornell](https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2024/12/new-cornell-tech-evaluate-anemia-be-used-across-india).
## NFHS-5 and programme recall
- **2019–21 survey**: pregnant women 15–49 **52.2%** anaemic; children **6–59 months 67.1%**; all women 15–49 **57%**. PDF's general '50–70% pregnant / 50% children' should not replace specified survey figures. [Health Ministry](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1795421&lang=2&reg=48).
- **Anaemia Mukt Bharat, 2018**, life-cycle approach: supplementation, testing/treatment, diet/behaviour change and attention to non-nutritional causes; public-health support does not justify self-prescribing iron for every anaemia.
- Clinical workup may use CBC/haemoglobin, iron indicators and other cause-specific tests. Digital screening needs quality control, trained workers, reliable supply chains, follow-up and privacy.
## May 2025: preconception prevention
- Begin screening/nutrition and cause-specific treatment **before pregnancy**, supported by ASHA/Anganwadi outreach, families and affordable follow-up. NFHS-5 **57% women 15–49 anaemic** does not establish that all were undiagnosed/untreated. Source's MMR 93 is a maternal-health indicator, not an anaemia-specific death rate.
- Iron deficiency, B12/folate deficiency, blood loss, inflammation/infection, inherited disorders and thyroid-related conditions need differential assessment. Inset also highlights heavy menstrual/pregnancy blood loss and parasites. Source's **49% B12 deficiency** comes from an unspecified study, not a verified all-India census.
- Low haemoglobin/iron deficiency can be associated with prematurity, low birthweight, impaired development and reduced tolerance of delivery blood loss; anaemia is not proof it directly caused every listed complication, including pre-eclampsia.
- WHO 2024 thresholds at relevant reference conditions: non-pregnant women **<12 g/dL**; pregnancy **<11 g/dL first/third trimester, <10.5 g/dL second**. Altitude/clinical context and measurement matter. [WHO guideline](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK602183/?report=reader).
## Treatment and policy caution
- Oral iron/folic acid can be limited by gastrointestinal effects, adherence and absorption; **hepcidin** regulates iron availability. **IV ferric carboxymaltose** bypasses intestinal absorption and can be considered by clinicians for indicated iron deficiency/intolerance or inadequate response; it is not a universal first-line treatment or blanket first-trimester recommendation. Infusion supervision and adverse-effect assessment remain necessary. [WHO-hosted clinical discussion](https://cdn.who.int/media/docs/default-source/anaemia/areacop-webinar---21-april-2020/2020-areacop-webinar-michaelauerbach-presentation-21apr_258fe697-a9e2-4d81-af25-1f6aed1a86f4.pdf?sfvrsn=51f40924_5).
- B12/folate replacement and thyroid/metabolic screening depend on individual indications; gestational diabetes is distinct from anaemia. Article's proposal for injectable B12+IV iron for everyone should not become standard self-treatment advice.
- Proposed standardised/subsidised preconception care complements antenatal services and reproductive autonomy. **SDG 3.1 global MMR<70/100,000** requires comprehensive obstetric/health-system improvements; anaemia prevention alone does not guarantee it. Supplied 250-word 15-mark question is undated practice.

## Anaemia Mukt Bharat PYQ recap
- **Iron–folic acid**, not prophylactic calcium, is the supplementation intervention. Delayed cord clamping, periodic deworming and attention to non-nutritional causes (malaria, haemoglobinopathies, fluorosis) are included. Supplied **2023 answer: only three (c)**; statements2,3,4 are correct.

topics.title: UAPA: security powers and safeguards
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Statutory distinctions
- **Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967**, MHA: unlawful activities/associations and terrorist offences; amendments include **2004, 2008, 2019**. TADA lapsed **1995**, POTA repealed **2004**; separate histories.
- Terrorist acts, financing, proceeds/property and organisational activity; law has specified extraterritorial application, not limited only to citizens inside India.
- **Unlawful-association declaration**, **terrorist-organisation listing** and **individual terrorist designation** are different processes. **2019** enabled individual designation; administrative designation is **not itself criminal conviction or an automatic detention order**.
- NIA investigates scheduled offences under its own Act; state police also have roles. Source graphic: 2019 permits **NIA Inspector-or-above** investigation in relevant circumstances and **NIA DG** approval for seizure/attachment where NIA investigates; not DGP-only for every case. [India Code](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/1470?sam_handle=123456789%2F1362).
## Custody and rights traps
- UAPA prosecution/remand is **not the same legal framework as preventive detention**. Court may extend the relevant investigation period **from 90 to 180 days subject to conditions**; not automatic indefinite custody or extensions beyond 180 merely 'after informing court'.
- Strict bail conditions, including **section 43D(5)** for relevant terrorist offences; punishments vary by offence and consequences. Graphic's 'death/life for all' and 'absolute government powers' are overstatements.
- **Article 22(1)** and written grounds of arrest: the graphic reports a police argument, not settled law. Supreme Court affirmed written grounds in **Prabir Purkayastha, 2024**; see its reaffirmation in [Supreme Court judgment](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2024/56321/56321_2024_9_1502_65444_Judgement_06-Nov-2025.pdf).
## Mains evaluation
- Need: terrorism/secession threats and disrupted financing; risks: lengthy incarceration, vague application, chilling speech and misuse allegations.
- Treat allegations involving activists/journalists/students as allegations; peaceful dissent is not by itself proof of terrorism.
- Safeguards: precise statutory grounds, evidentiary scrutiny, lawful arrest/remand, independent oversight, timely trials, reasoned review and accountability. Security and fundamental rights require effective institutions.

topics.title: India–Maldives cooperation
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 defence engagement
- **8 January 2025, New Delhi**: Rajnath Singh and Maldivian Defence Minister **Mohamed Ghassan Maumoon**; India's readiness for capability support aligned with Maldivian priorities, **Neighbourhood First** and **SAGAR**.
- Defence equipment/stores handed over on request; training, platforms, maritime security and first-responder role. [Defence Ministry](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2091162&lang=2&reg=48).
- Source discusses **Ekatha Harbour**, MNDF Coast Guard, **Sifavaru repair facility**, grant assistance and ship refit.
## Geography, partnership and interests
- Low-lying Indian Ocean coral archipelago, **~1,200 islands**, near major shipping/energy routes; climate/sea-level and disaster vulnerability.
- **Operation Cactus, 1988**: India intervened against attempted coup to support President Gayoom's government. Do not describe that government's democratic credentials uncritically as the source does.
- Defence/coast-guard capacity, anti-piracy, counterterrorism/radicalisation, humanitarian/disaster response; maritime security serves both countries.
- Food, construction materials, medicines/petroleum trade; housing, water/sanitation and infrastructure projects; tourism, education/medical travel, diaspora and cultural ties.
- **SAARC** partner; India among first to recognise independence **1965**, embassy/mission **1972** according to embedded historical graphic.
## Political context: use correct dates
- Yameen-era China ties; relations improved after **2018** change to Solih, rather than universally worsening after that election.
- **Muizzu elected 2023**, India Out debate and Indian personnel issue; subsequent rapprochement should not be described as a new leadership change after his election.
- Maumoon visit here is **January 2025**, not the text's stray 2024; Muizzu's India engagements in **2024** should not be backdated to 2023. 'China Out' phrase in source is confused.
- Embedded Yameen-era graphic's **70% debt owed to China, 25,000 Indians, 6% tourists** are undated older claims, not January 2025 statistics.
- Policy approach: respect sovereignty, reliable project delivery, people-to-people benefits and transparent financing while managing strategic competition.

topics.title: Henley Passport Index and mobility
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Methodology
- **Henley & Partners**, began **2006** as Visa Restrictions Index; based on **IATA Timatic** data and additional research.
- Source scope: **199 passports, 227 destinations**; score measures destinations accessible **without a prior visa**, not passport holders' wealth, democracy or military power.
- Distinguish ordinary visa-free access, visas on arrival and relevant electronic authorisations from **prior-approved visas/e-visas**; immigration checks still apply. A 'destination' can be a territory, not necessarily a sovereign country. [Methodology explanation](https://www.henleyglobal.com/publications/global-mobility-report/2025-january/henley-passport-index-visa-free-travel-defined).
## January 2025 snapshot
- Source **India 85th, 57 destinations**, from a cited earlier **80th**; multiple updates during a year mean different 2024/2025 releases can show different ranks.
- **Singapore 1st, 195; Japan 2nd, 193**. Source **UAE 10th** and China's longer-term **94th → 60th** are dated comparisons, not current figures. [Publisher's January release](https://www.henleyglobal.com/newsroom/press-releases/henley-global-mobility-report-january-2025%C2%A0).
- Visa rules change, and ranking depends on other passports too: a rank change does not by itself establish a proportionate change in diplomacy or geopolitical influence.
- Pandemic restrictions affected mobility after **2020**; source's 'COVID impact from 2015' is chronologically wrong.
- Mains use: mobility inequality, diaspora/business travel, bilateral visa facilitation and regional cooperation; travel ease is one indicator, not a complete measure of national power.

## 22 July 2025 Henley release
- **India 77th, 59 destinations**, up from **85th/57 in January 2025**, an eight-place rise despite only two additional destinations. The PDF's “85th in 2024” misdates the baseline. **Singapore 1st/193; Japan and South Korea joint 2nd/190; seven EU passports joint 3rd/189**. [Publisher's July release](https://www.henleyglobal.com/newsroom/press-releases/henley-global-mobility-report-july-2025).
- Source names Philippines/Sri Lanka as recent access additions and Malaysia, Indonesia, Maldives, Thailand as examples; entry conditions, visit purpose and prior-authorisation rules still require destination-specific checks. Rankings measure destinations accessible without a prior visa, not unconditional entry rights.

topics.title: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas and the Indian diaspora
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Date, origin and institutions
- **9 January** marks Gandhi's return from South Africa **9 January 1915**. First convention: **2003, New Delhi**, under Atal Bihari Vajpayee; recommendations of **L. M. Singhvi committee**, report January 2002.
- Day observed annually; major conventions **biennial since 2015**. **MEA**, host state and partner organisations; CII participation does not make it the permanent sole organiser.
- **18th convention: 8–10 January 2025, Bhubaneswar, Odisha**; PM inaugurated 9 January. Theme: **Diaspora's contribution to a Viksit Bharat**.
- Chief guest **Christine Carla Kangaloo**, President of Trinidad and Tobago, addressed virtually. [MEA overview](https://www.mea.gov.in/pravasi-bharatiya-divas.htm).
## Samman and dated examples
- **Pravasi Bharatiya Samman Award**, highest honour for overseas Indians; President confers it on eligible NRIs/PIOs and their organisations for relevant contributions.
- Source January 2025: **27 awardees across 24 countries**. Examples: **Lekh Raj Juneja, Japan—science/technology; Robert Masih Nahar, Spain—community service**, Indian-origin Spanish senator since 2017 and cricket promotion; **Syed Anwar Khursheed, Saudi Arabia—medical service**, royal-protocol physician. [MEA award overview](https://www.mea.gov.in/pravasi-bharatiya-samman.htm).
- Source diaspora snapshot **over 3.5 crore**; USA **54 lakh**, UAE **35 lakh**, Canada **28 lakh**, Saudi Arabia **24 lakh**. Reference dates unspecified; not current population counts.
- Source remittance estimate **$125 billion in 2023**; distinguish remittances from foreign investment and diaspora headcount.
## Diaspora → contribution → policy
- Remittances, trade/investment, innovation, skills, philanthropy, cultural networks and public diplomacy; **Howdy Modi, Texas, 2019**, with Donald Trump, illustrates outreach.
- PM's January 2025 themes: developed India **2047**, humanity-first approach, Global South, African Union's G20 inclusion, Ashoka/Dhauli and Buddhist peace heritage.
- Preserve **Girmitiya/indentured-labour histories** through research and databases; historic Mandvi–Muscat commercial links described as about **250 years old**. Cultural memory complements present-day economic ties.
- Policy balance: consular protection, worker welfare, diaspora participation and host-country sovereignty; overseas Indian identity does not automatically confer Indian citizenship or voting rights.

topics.title: Wildfires: drivers, impacts and management
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## California: January 2025 case
- Los Angeles-region fires included **Palisades, Eaton and Sunset**; source maps highlight coastal/urban areas around Malibu, Los Angeles and Hollywood.
- Source's developing-news snapshot: **7 deaths and over 10,000 structures affected/destroyed**; an earlier embedded report cites **2 deaths and about 70,000 evacuations**. Different report times, not final totals or numbers to add together.
- Dry vegetation, low rainfall, drought conditions and strong **Santa Ana winds** intensified spread; dry downslope winds warm through compression and rapidly carry embers. Hilly terrain can accelerate uphill spread.
- [CAL FIRE's 11 January Eaton update](https://www.fire.ca.gov/incidents/2025/1/7/eaton-fire/updates/a1fb81e4-a242-45d9-b001-0dc25f174d01) describes dry northeast winds and Red Flag conditions.
## Fire triangle and amplification
| Required factor | Examples / control |
| --- | --- |
| Heat / ignition | Lightning, electrical faults, careless burning or deliberate arson; ignition control |
| Fuel | Dry grass, shrubs, forest litter and buildings; defensible space/fuel management |
| Oxygen | Air; wind also transfers heat/embers and changes fire behaviour |
- **Arson is intentional**, not accidental. General possible ignitions do not establish the investigated cause of a particular fire.
- Climate conditions influence fire weather and fuel dryness; attributing any single fire entirely to climate change requires evidence. Urban expansion into the **wildland–urban interface** increases exposure.
## Impacts and response
- Deaths/displacement, homes/infrastructure lost, habitat damage, soil erosion and polluted runoff; smoke particulates aggravate respiratory and cardiovascular illness. Insurance affordability/availability and livelihood recovery are policy concerns.
- **Before**: satellite/drone detection, fire-weather warning, power-line safety, zoning/building codes, fuel breaks and professionally planned prescribed burns.
- **During**: evacuation routes, accessible warnings, trained crews, water/retardants with environmental safeguards; protect responders and vulnerable residents.
- **After**: safe return, ash/water monitoring, erosion control, habitat restoration, transparent relief and resilient reconstruction.
- Mains: prevention + land-use planning + preparedness + ecosystem-sensitive recovery; emergency suppression alone is insufficient.
## Pink aerial retardant: January 2025
- **Phos-Chek** is a brand of long-term fire retardants, generally ammonium-phosphate/polyphosphate-based formulations. Pink colour marks treated ground; it is not the extinguishing mechanism.
- Water carrier evaporates → retardant remains → vegetation combustion/spread slowed → supports ground response. Weather, flight safety and placement limit performance; an aerial drop is not guaranteed to extinguish a severe wildfire.
- Source's Los Angeles death figure rose to **24** by its January 13 reporting; earlier figure stays dated, not a contradictory final toll.
- Some formulations tested contain **chromium/cadmium and other toxic metals**; exposure/aquatic risk differs by product and dose. A study estimated **850,000 pounds of metals** released in the western US **2009–2021**, not all retardant chemicals globally since 2009. [USC research summary](https://viterbischool.usc.edu/news/2024/10/toxic-metals-found-in-wildfire-suppressants/).
- Balance emergency protection with safer formulations, waterway protection, careful application and environmental monitoring; don't generalise one tested product to every Phos-Chek formulation.

topics.title: Sonamarg / Z-Morh tunnel
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Location and purpose
- **Gagangir–Sonamarg, Ganderbal, Jammu and Kashmir**, on **Srinagar–Leh NH-1**. Name **Z-Morh** refers to a Z-shaped road stretch; terrain above **8,500 feet**, prone to snow/avalanches.
- Main tunnel **6.4 km in official release**; source rounds to **6.5 km**. Project includes an **egress tunnel and approach roads**, approximately **12 km overall**.
- Source specifications: two-lane road, designed around **1,000 vehicles/hour**, **80 km/h**; cites **4.26-km escape** and **0.6-km ventilation** components. Escape passage is for emergencies, not ordinary parallel traffic.
- **11 January 2025** announcement: inauguration scheduled **13 January**; subsequently inaugurated that day. [PMO announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2092091&lang=2&reg=48), [inauguration](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2092468).
## Corridor recall
- **Srinagar → Gagangir → Sonamarg → Zoji La → Drass/Kargil → Leh**. Distinct from **Banihal–Jammu NH-44**.
- Sonamarg tunnel enables all-weather access to Sonamarg; alone it does **not** complete year-round access across every Ladakh bottleneck.
- Separate **Zojila tunnel**, source **14.15 km**, planned eastward connection across the pass; do not confuse its length/completion with Sonamarg.
- Benefits: winter tourism, local livelihoods, rescue and defence logistics near sensitive northern/eastern frontiers; monitor ecological disturbance, avalanche risk and emergency ventilation/egress.
## Practice-test trap
- The 19 January key overstates year-round access to all of Ladakh. **Sonamarg access ≠ completion of the separate Zoji La tunnel**; check the specific section of the route.

topics.title: Workplace ethics, overwork and duty of care
topics.subject: Ethics
topics.markdown:
## Case and ethical questions
- Source discusses **Anna Sebastian Perayil, 26, EY employee**: her mother's allegations of excessive work pressure and insensitive organisational response. Treat alleged causation/responsibility as allegations, not a proved medical or judicial finding.
- Long hours, unrealistic expectations, fear of retaliation and insecure performance assessment can erode dignity and health; wellness branding must match daily management practices.
- Relevant values: **duty of care, empathy, fairness, integrity, accountability, dignity and confidentiality**. Credit misappropriation and silencing grievances undermine trust.
## Claim → evidence → judgement
- Source debate over **18 hours/day for 4–5 years** and demands for **70-hour weeks**: productivity cannot be assumed proportional to hours; fatigue, error, inequality and health costs matter.
- Entrepreneurial autonomy/reward and salaried employees' bargaining power differ; entrepreneurship is not automatically a safe or feasible remedy for overwork.
- **WHO–ILO study published 2021** estimated **745,000 deaths in 2016** from stroke/ischaemic heart disease attributable to **≥55 working hours/week**, globally—not India alone or a count of every cause of overwork death. [WHO–ILO findings](https://www.who.int/news/item/17-05-2021-long-working-hours-increasing-deaths-from-heart-disease-and-stroke-who-ilo).
## Ethical management flow
- **Identify excessive demand → assess health/workload risks → redistribute or resource work → protect rest and grievance access → review outcomes**.
- Leaders: realistic deadlines, adequate staffing, fair credit/compensation, confidential counselling, non-retaliation, documented escalation and empathetic support after crises.
- Employees: communicate constraints, record concerns, seek support and use safe reporting channels; individual resilience cannot replace organisational duty.
- Evaluate actual workload, grievance resolution, turnover and wellbeing rather than counting wellness events. Voluntary overtime/pay does not remove the need for safe conditions.
- Mains conclusion: success includes health and dignity; reconcile performance with sustainable work and accountable leadership.
## Industrial labour and innovation, February 2025
- Ludhiana source reports **11–12-hour days** and precarious work; extending hours is not the same as raising output per hour.
- Source PLFS2023–24 **21.7% regular salaried** share; many regular jobs still lack written contracts, leave/social security. Regular status is not guaranteed decent work.
- Outsourcing to small/informal enterprises can shift risk down supply chains; delayed MSME payments restrict investment. Formal factory contract workers and informal-enterprise workers are distinct categories.
- Source **70% informal manufacturing /56% of new factory workers contractual since2011–12 /profit share31.6%→46.4% /garment export share3.1%** use different denominators/periods; they do not prove wage suppression alone caused all profit growth.
- International weekly-hours comparisons require comparable worker populations; source India46.7/US38/Japan36.6 are dated cited values, not mandated working hours.
- Improve technology/R&D, management, worker skills, timely supplier payment, safe conditions and predictable fair wages; protect displaced workers during automation.
- Productivity gains, worker dignity and stronger purchasing power can reinforce each other. Cheap labour alone cannot guarantee export competitiveness; market access/logistics/quality also matter.

topics.title: Gaddi dog and indigenous breed conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Himalayan guardian
- **January 2025**: **ICAR–National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources**, Karnal, recognised Gaddi as a registered indigenous dog breed; source calls it the **fourth** after **Rajapalayam, Chippiparai (Tamil Nadu)** and **Mudhol Hound (Karnataka)**. This is a dated registration count.
- Named after **Gaddi shepherds, Himachal Pradesh**; guards sheep/goats against predators. Nicknames **Indian Panther Hound / Indian Leopard Hound** reflect guarding ability, not a taxonomic relationship with cats.
- Mainly Himalayan; predominantly **black**, occasional white feet/tail/trunk, strong arched neck and muscular, moderately long body.
- Registration documents breed characteristics and supports conservation, suitable breeding and avoidance of genetic erosion; no automatic wildlife protection schedule follows from breed registration.

topics.title: Soapstone / steatite
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Rock → mineral → formation
- **Soapstone / steatite**: talc-rich **metamorphic rock**; **talc is a mineral**, not every soapstone specimen is pure talc. Soft, dense and heat-resistant; talc contributes the soapy feel.
- Associated minerals vary: **mica, chlorite, amphibole, quartz, magnesite and carbonates**.
- Heat/pressure and alteration of **peridotite, dunite or serpentinite**; chemically active hot fluids can alter **siliceous dolostone**, an example of **metasomatism**. Convergent settings favour metamorphism; not the only formation setting.
- Graphic recall: temperature/pressure change existing rocks without requiring complete melting; melting and solidification would instead produce igneous rock. [NPS rock classification](https://home.nps.gov/subjects/geology/metamorphic.htm).
## Locations, uses and regulation
- January 2025 source: Uttarakhand High Court scrutiny of unregulated mining in **Bageshwar**, cited **over 160 mines**; slope stability, river pollution and compliance are governance concerns.
- Source lists **China, India, Brazil, USA and Finland** among producers; Indian Bureau of Mines reserve snapshot **Rajasthan 57%, Uttarakhand 25%**, reference year unspecified; not current market shares.
- Slabs: countertops, sinks, hearths and sculpture. Processed talc: ceramics, paint, roofing, cosmetics/pharmaceutical formulations, lubricating/filling/thickening uses.
- Source describes talc/corn-starch powders; this is an industrial-use fact, not advice to apply mineral dust to infants. Product purity and inhalation/contamination risks require appropriate standards.

topics.title: Sonobuoys and undersea domain awareness
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 cooperation
- India–USA **co-production of sonobuoys** for Indian Navy **Undersea Domain Awareness (UDA)**; complements submarine tracking and anti-submarine warfare.
- **Expendable electro-mechanical acoustic sensors**; aircraft/helicopters deploy canisters in patterns. Surface float/radio antenna communicates while **hydrophone/sensors descend to a selected depth**.
- **Deploy → listen/emit → transmit → analyse contacts → locate/track**. Multiple measurements improve localisation; detection is not automatically a perfect position fix.
| Type | Function |
| --- | --- |
| Passive | Listen to target/environment sounds; no active sonar pulse |
| Active | Emit acoustic energy and analyse returning echoes |
| Special purpose | Measure temperature, ambient noise and other environmental conditions |
- Components: buoyant housing, sensors/hydrophone, battery/power and radio/data link to aircraft/ship.
- Applications: detect/classify and support engagement of adversarial submarines/ships; oceanographic/environmental research and marine-mammal acoustic monitoring.
- Prelims trap: **sonar uses sound**, not radar radio waves to travel through deep water; radio link is generally above-water communication.

topics.title: UJALA and efficient lighting
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Design
- **Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All**, launched **5 January 2015**; earlier **Domestic Efficient Lighting Programme (DELP)**. Energy efficiency, not a renewable-generation scheme.
- **EESL with DISCOMs**, Ministry of Power; large-scale **zero-subsidy** LED distribution, bulk procurement/e-procurement and competitive pricing.
- Source eligibility: households with metered electricity connections; upfront payment or instalment arrangements where offered; **SHGs** participate in distribution.
- LED price cited **₹300–350 → ₹70–80** through scale and market transformation; programme-era comparison, not a current retail quote.
## 6 January 2025 snapshot
| Indicator | Source / official snapshot |
| --- | --- |
| Distributed LED bulbs | **36.87 crore** |
| Annual electricity saved | **47,883 million kWh** |
| Annual monetary saving | **₹19,153 crore** |
| Peak demand reduced | **9,586 MW** |
| Annual CO₂ reduction | **3.87 crore tonnes** |
- [Power Ministry's ten-year review](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2090639&lang=1&reg=1). Savings estimates are annual, not cumulative generation.
- Source's **85 lakh kWh / 15,000 tonnes CO₂** target lacks a usable timeframe and is inconsistent in scale with reported achievements; don't memorise it as the national annual target.
- **77 crore conventional bulbs** is a replacement ambition; **3.5 crore streetlights** belongs to the separate street-lighting programme, not household bulbs already distributed under UJALA.
- Mains mechanism: pooled demand → lower unit cost → wider adoption → lower electricity demand/bills/emissions; verify quality, disposal and access.
## Practice-test trap
- UJALA household bulbs and the **Street Lighting National Programme (SLNP)** are separate programmes. Do not attribute cumulative streetlight replacements to UJALA merely because both use LEDs.

topics.title: Toda: society, livelihood and embroidery
topics.subject: Anthropology
topics.markdown:
## Nilgiri community
- **Nilgiri Hills, Tamil Nadu**; hamlet **mund**. Source describes a language without a traditional script; oral language does not mean absence of linguistic complexity.
- **Patrilineal descent**; source's two endogamous divisions **Tharthazoll and Theveioll**. Clan names given: **Paiki, Pekkan, Kuttan, Kenna and Todi**; transliterations vary.
- Traditional council **Noim**, headman **Monegar**, social regulation/dispute settlement; do not interpret traditional authority as unlimited legal power overriding Indian law.
- Buffalo pastoralism and embroidery; sacred buffalo/dairy associations make livelihood and ritual closely connected.
- **Red-and-black embroidery on white cloth**, GI-protected **Toda Embroidery, Tamil Nadu**. [GI register](https://search.ipindia.gov.in/GIRPublicSearch/Application/Details/135).
- **Modhweth**, New Year/buffalo festival; source places observance on last Sunday of December or first Sunday of January.
- Anthropology recall: **descent ≠ residence ≠ marriage rule**; patriliny alone does not establish every household's residence practice. Preserve culture with community participation, livelihood security and language transmission.
## Practice-test correction
- The 19 January Noim answer letter contradicts its own explanation. Recall **traditional council/social dispute resolution**, with authority subject to Indian law; reject claims of unrestricted powers.

topics.title: Kalpeni atoll and coral formation
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Map and landforms
- **Lakshadweep, Arabian Sea**; **southeast of Kavaratti**, between **Andrott and Minicoy**, about **287 km / 155 nautical miles from Kochi**.
- Official/source area **2.79 km²**; north–south alignment; lagoon maximum width **about 2.8 km**, not its total area.
- **Kalpeni + Tilakkam + Pitti + northern Cheriyam** form an atoll; **Cheriyam** described as uninhabited, not Kalpeni itself. [Administration geography](https://lakshadweep.gov.in/islands/kalpeni/), [atoll constituents](https://lakshadweep.gov.in/tourist-place/kalpeni/).
- **Volcanic island/fringing reef → subsidence with upward coral growth → barrier reef/lagoon → ring-like atoll**: classic schematic, not proof each island has an identical geological history.
- Coral reefs shelter lagoons and support diverse marine life; tourism includes snorkelling/diving; Kerala-like maritime monsoon climate.
## January 2025 news and correction
- Divers reported wreckage possibly from a **17th/18th-century European warship**; identity/date were provisional, not an authenticated archaeological conclusion.
- Source's **Maliku community** label confuses Kalpeni with **Minicoy/Maliku**; administration distinguishes Malayalam-speaking islands from Minicoy's **Mahl** language. [Lakshadweep islands](https://lakshadweep.gov.in/islands/).
- Protect reefs and wreck sites: scientific investigation, visitor limits, waste control and community livelihoods; avoid souvenir removal or unverified heritage claims.

topics.title: Garudakshi: digital forest-crime management
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Karnataka pilot: January 2025
- Forest Department online forest-offence/FIR system, developed with **Wildlife Trust of India**; encroachment, illegal felling, poaching and unauthorised entry.
- Pilot divisions: **Bengaluru Urban, Bhadravathi, Sirsi and Male Mahadeshwara Wildlife Sanctuary**; not nationwide implementation.
- Modules: **legacy case registration → online offence registration → investigation → reporting/analytics**; generates report/complaint formats, public complaints via mobile/email.
- Source says portal registration compulsory on implementation; digitisation supports enforcement under applicable forest/wildlife laws without automatically changing their substantive offences.
- Benefits: standard records, faster tracking, pattern detection and accountability; safeguards: data quality/security, trained staff, access for people without smartphones and verification of complaints.

topics.title: Vultures and toxic veterinary drugs
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Nimesulide: correct regulatory scope
- **NSAID**, pain/inflammation medicine. Veterinary exposure can damage vulture kidneys; **visceral gout** indicates uric-acid deposition associated with renal failure.
- **Medicated livestock → contaminated carcass → scavenging vulture → kidney injury → gout/death**; highlights indirect ecological effects of pharmaceuticals.
- **S.O. 5633(E), 30 December 2024**, section **26A, Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940**: **nimesulide/formulations for animal use** prohibition. **20 February 2025** CDSCO circular sought enforcement. [CDSCO record](https://www.cdsco.gov.in/opencms/opencms/en/Notifications/Gazette-Notifications/), [enforcement circular](https://cdsco.gov.in/opencms/resources/UploadCDSCOWeb/2018/UploadPublic_NoticesFiles/Nimesulide%20and%20its%20formulatin.pdf).
- January source's blanket assertion that this makes all human administration banned/unsuitable is unsupported; human-use safety restrictions are a separate issue. No medical-use recommendation follows from this note.
- Source lists earlier veterinary use in cattle/pigs/horses and human pain/fever indications; these describe usage, not endorsed prescribing.
- Conservation: enforce veterinary-drug restrictions, monitor carcass exposure, safe alternatives under professional guidance and vulture-population recovery; scavengers provide ecosystem sanitation services.
## Long-billed vulture and habitat
- Indian/long-billed vulture: **Gyps indicus**, Critically Endangered; cliff-nesting across much of central and peninsular India.
- Ramadevarabetta near Ramanagara, Karnataka, established in 2012, is an important vulture sanctuary; “first” should not become “India's only sanctuary forever”.
- Protect nesting cliffs, safe food and habitat connectivity; address quarrying, disturbance, electrocution and collision risks.
- Veterinary diclofenac harms vultures through renal failure. The 2006 veterinary prohibition differs from 2015 restrictions on large multidose human formulations; all human medicinal use was not banned.
- Vulture Safe Zones, captive breeding and monitored reintroduction complement drug regulation. Scavenging reduces carcass accumulation and associated disease risks; it does not sterilise every pathogen.

topics.title: GenomeIndia: reference genomes and precision medicine
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Programme and January 2025 milestone
- **DBT-funded multi-institution consortium**, initiated **2020**; large-scale sequencing to represent Indian genetic diversity. January 2025 data milestone builds on earlier sequencing announcements. [PMO address, 9 January 2025](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2091506&lang=2&reg=48).
- Earlier supplied programme reporting describes **10,074 samples across 99 ethnic groups** and an analysis subset of **5,750**; the **8 April 2025 consortium paper** reports 10,074 individuals sequenced from **83 population groups**, with **9,772** retained after quality control. Keep these differently defined reports distinct; use the published paper for the April dataset.
- Data housed at **Indian Biological Data Centre, Faridabad, Haryana**; research access requires appropriate safeguards, not unrestricted release of named individuals' medical records.
## What the reference enables
| Objective | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Variation catalogue | Common, low-frequency and rare variants; **SNPs** and structural variants |
| Haplotype reference | Variants inherited together; supports statistical imputation of missing variants |
| Genome-wide arrays | Affordable research/diagnostic tools suited to represented populations |
| Biobank | Stored **DNA/plasma** for approved future research |
- **Sample → sequence → quality checks/joint genotyping → reference database → validated research/clinical applications**.
- Potential: disease-risk research, pharmacogenomics, precision medicine and host susceptibility to infections; association does not guarantee diagnosis or cure.
- Ethics: informed consent, privacy, secure access, representative sampling, benefit sharing and avoiding caste/ethnic determinism or genetic discrimination.
## 8 April 2025: published reference dataset
- The GenomeIndia consortium’s *Nature Genetics* paper distinguishes **10,074 individuals sequenced** from **9,772 genomes retained after quality control**, representing **83 population groups** (30 tribal, 53 non-tribal). The source’s 99-group description belongs to earlier programme reporting and should not replace this paper’s sample definition.
- Preliminary calling yielded approximately **180 million raw variants**; further checks yielded about **130 million autosomal variants**. These are different processing stages, not interchangeable totals. After excluding singletons/doubletons, about 65% of variants were ultra-rare (minor-allele frequency below 0.1%).
- The paper describes consented sampling, population representation, coordinated quality control, and data at IBDC, Faridabad. The supplied 5,750-sample analysis is an earlier subset, not the April paper’s final call-set.
- Revision implication: larger, representative reference panels improve imputation, rare-disease investigation and drug-response research, with clinical validation and safeguards still required. [GenomeIndia consortium paper, published 8 April 2025](https://home.iitm.ac.in/sinha/pdf/Bhattacharyya_2025_NatGenet.pdf).

## Gujarat tribal-genome initiative: July 2025
- Source reports a tribal-focused project implemented by **Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre**, under the Tribal Development Department: planned **2,000 individuals across 17 districts**, building a reference database for genetic-risk research and precision healthcare.
- Focus includes sickle-cell disease and other disease susceptibilities. Sequencing can inform research and validated prevention/treatment; predisposition is not destiny or a guaranteed cure.
- Representative consented sampling, privacy, cultural sensitivity, non-discrimination and returning accessible health benefits are central. A state tribal reference initiative is distinct from nationwide GenomeIndia.

topics.title: International Organization for Migration
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Institution
- Founded **1951**, headquarters **Geneva, Switzerland**; intergovernmental migration organisation, **UN related organisation**. Not interchangeable with UNHCR's refugee-protection mandate.
- Humane/orderly migration, cooperation, practical migration management and humanitarian assistance to migrants, including displaced/refugee populations where relevant.
- Coordinates **UN Network on Migration**; source says 'coordinator for Secretary', which should not be memorised as the formal role.
- Labour mobility/human development work: policy and operations, diaspora-development links and integration. Supported **Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration, 2018**; the compact is not a binding refugee convention.
- Source membership **175 members, 8 observers** is an undated snapshot; membership changes. Publications: **World Migration Report**, **Migration Health Annual Report**.
## January 2025 Syria appeal
- Expanded earlier **$30 million** appeal to **$73.2 million**, response period **December 2024–May 2025**; humanitarian funding requested, not money already received. [IOM flash appeal](https://mena.iom.int/sites/g/files/tmzbdl686/files/documents/2025-01/iom-flash-appeal-for-syria-dec-2024-may-2025.pdf).
- Mains: reconcile dignity/protection, host capacity, safe mobility, integration and international burden sharing.

topics.title: Polar vortex and cold-air outbreaks
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Concept and distinctions
- Broad polar **low-pressure/cold-air cyclonic circulation**. Distinguish **stratospheric polar vortex** from upper-tropospheric circulation/jet patterns; they interact but are not one identical vertically uniform feature.
- Winter strengthens the stratospheric vortex; summer weakening/breakdown is part of its seasonal cycle. Source's 'always exists unchanged from tropopause through mesosphere' is too sweeping across both definitions.
- Normal cyclonic circulation: **anticlockwise in Northern Hemisphere**, **clockwise in Southern Hemisphere**; not anticlockwise at both poles.
- **Jet streams**: narrow fast winds in upper troposphere near tropopause; source approx **30,000 feet / 9.1 km**, height varies.
## Strong containment → disturbance → possible surface effects
- Strong circulation helps contain polar air; disturbances/weakening/displacement can alter jet patterns and favour some midlatitude cold outbreaks.
- A stratospheric disruption is **not required for every cold spell**, nor a guarantee all regions turn cold; coupling, timing and local weather matter. [NOAA distinctions](https://prod-01-asg-www-climate.woc.noaa.gov/news-features/blogs/enso/polar-vortex-going-make-you-put-sweater-be-afraid-be-very-afraid), [NWS cold-air explanation](https://www.weather.gov/safety/cold-polar-vortex).
- Source January 2025 US cold outbreak; Europe/Asia also affected in relevant events. Southern circulation tends to be more symmetric, with ocean-dominated surroundings; Southern Hemisphere cold outbreaks still occur.
- Impacts: hypothermia/frostbite, transport disruption, agricultural losses and energy demand; forecasts and protection for vulnerable people matter.
## Precision trap
- The **stratospheric** polar vortex is principally a winter feature; the tropospheric circulation persists year-round. Avoid an undifferentiated claim that every polar vortex remains equally strong in every season.

topics.title: Ebola: transmission, prevention and treatments
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Disease recall
- Severe viral disease; **Orthoebolavirus genus, Filoviridae**. First recognised **1976**, outbreaks in **Yambuku, now DRC**, and **Nzara, now South Sudan**; Ebola River gave the name.
- Fruit bats, particularly **Pteropodidae**, implicated as natural hosts; humans and other primates can become ill.
- Infected animal exposure → spillover; human transmission through **direct contact with infected bodily fluids/tissues**, sick/dead persons or contaminated materials. Not principally mosquito-borne or ordinary airborne transmission.
- Incubation **2–21 days**; fever, weakness, vomiting/diarrhoea and sometimes bleeding; bleeding is not universal. Average case-fatality **about 50%**, varies widely by outbreak/access to care.
## Correct the treatment claim
- Source's 'no fully tested treatments' conflicts with established therapies: **Inmazeb / REGN-EB3** and **Ebanga / ansuvimab / mAb114**, monoclonal-antibody treatments for **Zaire/Ebola virus disease**, recommended by WHO in **2022**.
- These do not constitute an approved treatment for every orthoebolavirus disease. Licensed vaccines also target particular viruses; **Ervebo** is not a universal all-strain Ebola vaccine. [WHO treatment guidance](https://www.who.int/news/item/19-08-2022-who-makes-new-recommendations-for-ebola-treatments-----calls-for-improved-access), [WHO disease distinctions](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/ebola-disease).
- Early supportive care, fluids/electrolytes and symptom management improve survival; blood products used when clinically appropriate, not compulsory for every patient.
- Source reports **nanobody-based inhibitors** as research; experimental discovery is not proof of approved population-wide therapy.
- Response: detection/testing, isolation with safe care, contact tracing, PPE/infection control, safe dignified burials and vaccination where relevant; survivors need follow-up and non-stigmatising support.

topics.title: Anji Khad Bridge and USBRL
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Map and engineering
- **India's first cable-stayed railway bridge**, **Reasi, Jammu and Kashmir**, between **Katra and Reasi**, over **Anji River, Chenab tributary**.
- Part of **Udhampur–Srinagar–Baramulla Rail Link (USBRL)**; Kashmir Valley connection across difficult Himalayan geology. Indian Railways with IIT Roorkee/Delhi site investigations.
- Asymmetric cable-stayed design: cables transfer deck loads to **main pylon/foundation**, not a self-supporting arch like the nearby Chenab railway bridge.
| Dimension / design figure | Source value |
| --- | --- |
| Overall length | **725.5 m** |
| Main pylon | **193 m** from foundation |
| Height above riverbed | **331 m** |
| Wind design | **213 km/h** |
| Train design speed cited | **100 km/h** |
| Reasi approach viaduct | **120 m** |
| Katra approach bridge | **38 m** |
| Cable-stayed section | **473.25 m** |
| Connecting embankment | **94.25 m** |
- January source describes completed construction; don't equate that with full public train-service inauguration at that date. [Official infrastructure overview](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2133723&lang=2&reg=48).
- Seismicity, fragile rock, wind and maintenance demand site-specific engineering; resilient connectivity supports livelihoods, access and strategic logistics.
## Chenab rail bridge: June 2025
- **Bakkal–Kauri, Reasi, Jammu and Kashmir**, USBRL: steel railway arch bridge **359 m above Chenab riverbed**, total **1,315 m**, principal arch **467 m**; distinguish riverbed clearance from structural height or arch-span length. “World's highest railway arch bridge” concerns elevation, not the world's longest arch.
- **6 June 2025:** inauguration of Chenab and Anji bridges/USBRL connectivity; the issue's clipping anticipates that day's programme. These milestones differ from earlier completion/trials. [Official overview](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressNoteDetails.aspx?ModuleId=3&NoteId=154553&id=154553&lang=2&reg=48).
- Source engineering: **17 spans**, concrete-filled steel arch boxes, **93 deck segments ~85 tonnes each**, **120-year design life**, wind design **266 km/h**, high-seismic/blast-resistance provisions. These are design/fabrication specifications, not a guarantee against every earthquake, blast or maintenance failure.
