- IIT structural input, DRDO blast studies and GSI geological assessment illustrate cross-disciplinary engineering in difficult rock/terrain. **Arch:** loads transfer through arch towards supports; **Anji cable-stayed bridge:** loads carried via stays/pylon—different structural systems.
- Improved Valley access supports passengers, freight, tourism, local livelihoods and strategic logistics; potential gains depend on reliable operations, complementary facilities and resilient maintenance.

## Chenab basin map
- **Chandra + Bhaga meet at Tandi, Lahaul–Spiti, Himachal Pradesh → Chandrabhaga/Chenab → Jammu region → Pakistan Punjab → Panjnad → Indus → Arabian Sea**. Sutlej joins the downstream combined system; Chenab does not flow directly to the sea as an independent coastal river.
- Source length **974 km** is an approximate convention, not uniquely established by every geographic source. Tributaries include **Miyar, Thirot, Bhut, Marusudar and other Himalayan streams**; basin networks matter for floods/hydropower.
- Treaty **western river**, alongside Indus/Jhelum; allocation/use rights and April 2025 abeyance developments remain in the common Indus Treaty topic. India's bridge inauguration does not amend water allocations.

topics.title: Siachen: geography, strategic control and altitude risks
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Map and historical anchor
- **Karakoram, northern Ladakh**; glacier near India–Pakistan–China territorial interfaces, **Saltoro Ridge** to its west, **Nubra Valley** connection southward.
- Source's 'largest glacier outside polar regions' is incorrect: NASA describes Siachen as **second-longest midlatitude glacier**, not the world's largest non-polar glacier. [NASA geography](https://eol.jsc.nasa.gov/Collections/EarthObservatory/articles/SiachenGlacier.htm).
- Source approximately **75 km** refers to glacier/sector length, not a surveyed joint 75-km India–Pakistan–China border; avoid conflating glacier length with boundary length.
- **Operation Meghdoot, 13 April 1984**, secured strategic glacier/Saltoro heights ahead of anticipated Pakistani action; not simply reclaiming territory after an already-completed Pakistani occupation. [Defence Ministry account](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2017834&lang=2&noshow=1&reg=48).
## Cold + altitude + logistics
- High posts may reach **20,000–23,000 feet**; glacier's entire length is not uniformly at these elevations. Extreme winter/source range **−20°C to −60°C** varies by place/time.
- Falling pressure → **lower oxygen partial pressure** → hypoxia; oxygen's atmospheric percentage stays broadly similar, not progressively replaced by another gas.
- Risks: altitude illness, cold injury, snowstorms/avalanches, sleep disturbance, appetite/weight loss, impaired memory and difficult casualty evacuation.
- Response: acclimatisation, suitable clothing/shelter, nutrition, medical monitoring, oxygen/evacuation capacity and reliable logistics; claiming survival is universally impossible without acclimatisation is too absolute.
- Source's recovered **Malkhan Singh**, aircraft crash **7 February 1968**, illustrates prolonged ice preservation and recovery challenges; the crash story is separate from Operation Meghdoot and Siachen's border history.

topics.title: Gulf of Mexico: map, resources and naming
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Map recall
- Atlantic marginal sea on southeastern North America; bordered by **USA, Mexico and Cuba**, world's largest gulf; sometimes called **Mediterranean of the Americas**.
| Connection | Passage |
| --- | --- |
| Gulf ↔ Atlantic | **Straits of Florida**, between Florida and Cuba |
| Gulf ↔ Caribbean | **Yucatán Channel**, between Yucatán Peninsula and Cuba |
- Rivers: **Mississippi**, **Rio Grande**. Tropical/subtropical climate, hurricanes and severe thunderstorms; substantial continental-shelf petroleum/natural gas, fisheries and maritime trade.
## Dated naming development
- January 14 source: President-elect Trump proposed **Gulf of America**.
- **20 January 2025 executive order** subsequently directed US federal geographic-name changes for the described US continental-shelf area and agency references. It does not itself redraw maritime boundaries or impose nomenclature on Mexico/Cuba. [Executive order](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/01/restoring-names-that-honor-american-greatness/).
- Prelims trap: **Florida → Atlantic; Yucatán → Caribbean**, not the reverse. A political naming change does not alter physical geography.

topics.title: WMO and the 2024 temperature record
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Institution
- **World Meteorological Organization**, **UN specialised agency**, founded **1950**; predecessor **International Meteorological Organization, 1873**. Headquarters **Geneva, Switzerland**.
- International cooperation in meteorology, hydrology, climatology and related geophysics; atmosphere–ocean interactions, climate and water resources.
| Body | Role |
| --- | --- |
| World Meteorological Congress | Supreme policy body, normally four-year cycle |
| Executive Council | **36 members**, annual sessions, implements Congress decisions |
| Secretariat | Administration; Secretary-General appointed for **four-year term** |
- Source **193 members = 187 States + 6 Territories**, January 2025 snapshot; members are not all sovereign states.
## 2024 record: interpret carefully
- January 2025 WMO synthesis of **six international datasets**: **2024 warmest year on record**, global mean near-surface temperature **about 1.55°C ± 0.13°C above 1850–1900**.
- A **single calendar year above 1.5°C** does not itself establish that the Paris Agreement's long-term warming threshold has been permanently crossed. Dataset differences and natural variability affect yearly estimates.
- Distinguish **weather event**, **annual anomaly**, and **long-term climate warming**; base period must accompany a temperature anomaly. [WMO announcement](https://wmo.int/news/media-centre/wmo-confirms-2024-warmest-year-record-about-155degc-above-pre-industrial-level).
- Mains: emissions mitigation, adaptation/early warning and climate-resilient water, food, health and infrastructure policy.

topics.title: Project Veer Gatha
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Education and civic values
- Launched **2021**, associated with **Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav**; joint **Ministry of Defence + Ministry of Education** initiative.
- Students learn gallantry awardees' bravery and life stories; essays/paragraphs about role models link **courage, public service, responsibility and patriotism**.
- **Fourth edition, Veer Gatha 4.0**, January 2025 Republic Day context; wider participation than earlier editions, no exact total supplied here.
- Source topics include **Rani Laxmibai**, **1857 uprising** and **tribal resistance**; these are curriculum examples, not proof every historical figure received a modern gallantry award.
- Ethics/governance use: experiential civic education and inclusive examples of service; participation counts alone do not measure learning outcomes.

topics.title: Pangolins and Indo-Burmese taxonomy
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Species proposal: January 2025
- ZSI-associated research described **Manis indoburmanica**, Indo-Burmese pangolin, as distinct from **Chinese pangolin (M. pentadactyla)** and **Indian pangolin (M. crassicaudata)**.
- Source locations: **Arunachal Pradesh/Assam**, possible Nepal, Bhutan and Myanmar extension; **180–1,830 m**; dark/olive-brown scales, pinkish face. A predicted range is not confirmed presence everywhere.
- Source reports **8% genetic difference** and **3.4-million-year divergence**; metrics/methods not supplied, so don't treat these as definitive universal figures.
## Later taxonomic clarification
- **1 July 2026** genomic/morphological study revalidated **Manis aurita Hodgson, 1836**, treating **M. indoburmanica** as a junior synonym under naming priority; estimated separation from M. pentadactyla **about 1.8 million years**.
- Keep **2025 proposal** separate from **2026 revision**: lineage evidence, species delimitation and the oldest valid scientific name are related but different questions. [Primary research](https://www.nature.com/articles/s42003-026-10314-9), [Mammal Diversity Database](https://www.mammaldiversity.org/taxon/1006934/).
## General recall and conservation
- **Order Pholidota, family Manidae**; Africa/Asia; unique mammalian **keratin-scale armour**. Curl into a ball; long sticky tongue; **myrmecophagous**, ants/termites.
- Many dig burrows; **fossorial ≠ arboreal**, and behaviour varies across pangolin species.
- Source's traditional **8 species: 4 African + 4 Asian** count predates/does not resolve newer taxonomic revisions; avoid adding the new name to eight without checking whether it replaces an older taxon.
- Severe trafficking for scales/meat and habitat loss; scale demand in traditional medicine is not evidence of medicinal effectiveness.
- Graphic's traditional Asian species: **Indian, Chinese, Sunda and Philippine**; African: **giant, Temminck's ground, white-bellied and black-bellied**.
## Trafficking disruption: April–May 2025
- **Wildlife Justice Commission, Disruption and Disarray (2015–24):** recorded major disruption of large-scale pangolin-scale/ivory trafficking after **2020**, reflecting pandemic restrictions, enforcement and changing criminal methods. Reduced seizures/visible shipments do **not** establish an equivalent population recovery or elimination of demand; smuggling routes may adapt. [WJC report](https://wildlifejustice.org/wildlife-justice-commission-report-reveals-major-disruption-in-pangolin-scale-and-ivory-trafficking/).
- Habitat extends across forest, grassland and agricultural mosaics, varying by species. Ant/termite consumption contributes to pest regulation; burrowing contributes to soil turnover/aeration. Habitat loss and hunting near settlements remain threats.
- **Indian pangolin: IUCN Endangered; Chinese pangolin: Critically Endangered**; both receive **Schedule I** protection under India's Wildlife (Protection) Act. Indian pangolin range includes India, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh; occurrence is not uniform across every habitat.
- Traditionally recognised eight pangolins were moved to **CITES Appendix I**, effective **2017**, prohibiting international commercial trade in wild-taken specimens; exceptional permitted transactions and domestic protection are separate legal questions. Preserve the existing notes' newer taxonomy qualifications. [CITES](https://cites.org/eng/new_CITES_trade_rules_come_into_effect_as_2017_starts_02012017).
- Priorities: intelligence-led enforcement and financial investigations, border cooperation, scale identification, habitat/community protection and demand reduction. Traditional medicinal use of scales is not evidence of efficacy.

topics.title: National Youth Festival and Young Leaders Dialogue
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Dates and programme
- **12 January**, Swami Vivekananda's birth anniversary, **National Youth Day**; source notes Youth Week observance from **1985**. Do not confuse Youth Week with the festival's specific dates each year.
- National Youth Festival: youth integration, cultural competitions/non-competitive events, conventions/**Suvichar**, exhibitions and adventure; linked to **National Programme for Youth and Adolescent Development**, national-integration component.
- **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, host State/UT partnership in the conventional format; not invariably one fixed venue or unchanging 12–16 January schedule.
## 2025 reimagined event
- **Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue, 10–12 January 2025**, **Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi**; PM interaction **12 January**.
- **3,000 selected participants**, not the source's generic **7,500** festival-delegate figure: **1,500 Viksit Bharat Track + 1,000 Traditional Track + 500 Pathbreakers**.
- Ten development themes; innovation in science/technology is one component, not the event's only overarching theme. Selection: quiz → essay → State Vision Deck; cultural programmes, mentoring and youth-policy dialogue. [Youth Affairs release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2091554&lang=2&reg=48).
- Source practice answer that treats a fixed annual 12–16 January schedule and a sole science/technology theme as correct is unreliable.
- Mains: civic participation, skills, inclusion and youth-led solutions; evaluate representation and follow-through beyond a one-off event.

topics.title: Foot-and-mouth disease
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 outbreak
- **Water buffalo near Berlin, Brandenburg, Germany**; first German occurrence since **1988**, officially notified **10 January 2025**, not an unspecified exactly 40-year interval. [WOAH statement](https://www.woah.org/en/statement-on-recent-foot-and-mouth-disease-fmd-outbreak-in-germany/).
## Pathogen, hosts and spread
- Highly contagious **Aphthovirus, Picornaviridae**, livestock disease; cattle, pigs, sheep, goats and other susceptible **cloven-hoofed animals**. Horses/dogs/cats are not usual susceptible hosts.
- **Seven serotypes: O, A, C, SAT1, SAT2, SAT3, Asia1**; immunity/vaccines are not universally interchangeable across serotypes or all strains.
- Animal secretions/excretions, aerosols, direct contact and contaminated equipment/clothing; people can mechanically carry virus without having the livestock disease.
- Fever, mouth/tongue/lip/teat/interdigital blisters → lameness, salivation, poor intake; weight loss, growth retardation and persistent milk-production loss. Adult deaths generally low; young animals may die from severe disease/myocarditis.
- Transboundary disease: trade restrictions and major production losses. Source **77% of world livestock** refers to population in areas where disease circulates, not a measured 77% simultaneously infected.
## Prevention and traps
- Matched vaccines, surveillance/rapid notification, biosecurity, movement controls, outbreak response and appropriate official disease-status procedures; first disease for which WOAH established official status recognition.
- **Livestock FMD ≠ human hand-foot-and-mouth disease**; not ordinarily a human-health/food-safety threat. [WOAH disease information](https://www.woah.org/en/disease/foot-and-%20mouth-disease/).
- Intensive husbandry can amplify spread; traditional breeds are not automatically immune. Graphic **Futvac** is a vaccine example, not a universal vaccine name for all serotypes.
## Precision trap
- **Seven serotypes** does not mean only seven viral strains: multiple strains/subtypes occur within serotypes.

topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Facts from the embedded PYQ-recall graphic
| Disease / organism | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| Viruses | Require living host cells for replication; cannot multiply in a cell-free artificial culture medium like suitable bacteria/fungi |
| Common cold | Multiple viruses; adenoviruses can cause some cases |
| HIV/AIDS | HIV is a **retrovirus** |
| Hepatitis B / C | **B has a vaccine; C has no licensed vaccine**—graphic reverses this distinction |

| Viral hosts | Viruses infect animals, plants, bacteria and fungi; bacteriophages infect bacteria |
| Foot-and-mouth disease / cowpox | Infectious conditions relevant to animal-health recall; pathogens differ |
| Athlete's foot | **Fungal** infection |
- Graphic labels UPSC years **2021, 2019, 2017, 2016, 2005 and 2001**, but supplies facts/fragments rather than complete question statements/options. Full questions must be recovered before adding them to common PYQ JSON; year labels alone do not justify inventing questions.

topics.title: Desert National Park and Great Indian Bustard
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Location and ecosystem
- **Thar, Rajasthan, Jaisalmer and Barmer districts**; **about 3,162 km²**, source rounds to over 3,160. [Rajasthan protected-area record](https://forest.rajasthan.gov.in/content/raj/forest/en/aboutus/departmental-wings/wildlife/details-of-protected-area-.html).
- Arid landscape: rocky outcrops, salt-lake bottoms, interdunal areas, fixed dunes and open desert grass/scrub; **dunes about 20%**, not 50%. Source **under 100-mm annual rainfall** is not a universal park-wide climatic threshold.
- **Human settlements occur within the landscape**; conservation must account for pastoral/local livelihoods.
- **Great Indian Bustard**, critically endangered; source sighting of **12** is a local observation, not a national population estimate or by itself proof of population recovery.
- Other source fauna: **chinkara, desert/Bengal fox, Indian wolf, desert cat, hare, spiny-tailed/monitor lizards, saw-scaled viper**. Broad reptile lists do not prove every species equally abundant at every site.
- **Khejri, Prosopis cineraria**, ecological/cultural importance, including Bishnoi conservation traditions; regional fossil-rich geological heritage, Jurassic-era deposits cited.
## Correct misplaced park details
- **Rajbagh, Malik Talao and Padam Talao** are associated with **Ranthambore**, not lakes to memorise for Desert National Park. Source's **Dhok/Ronj/Salai/palm** list also mixes generic/other-park flora; prioritise desert vegetation and verified local records. [Ranthambore management plan](https://forest.rajasthan.gov.in/content/dam/raj/forest/ForestDepartment/PDFs/Department%20Wing/Wildlife/tigerconservationplan/TCP%20RTR.pdf).
- GIB conservation: habitat connectivity, low-disturbance breeding areas, safe power-line planning and community partnership; balance infrastructure with bird survival.
## UPSC Prelims 2020
- Statements: **(1) spread over two districts—correct; (2) no human habitation—incorrect; (3) natural habitat of GIB—correct**. Answer **(c) 1 and 3 only**; full question in common Environment PYQ-Prelim JSON.

topics.title: Crude oil imports and energy security
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## December 2024 source snapshot
- Pre-February 2022: Iraq/Saudi Arabia major suppliers; after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, discounted Russian crude reshaped sourcing.
- Source explanation for December shift: Russian refinery utilisation after maintenance and domestic/seasonal demand constrained exports; West Asian supplies gained share.
| Supplier | December 2024 imports | Change / basket share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Russia | **1.48 million barrels/day** | **−17%**; share **38% November → 31.5% December** |
| Iraq | **1.13 million b/d** | **+29%**; **18.7% → 24%** |
| UAE | **530,000 b/d** | **+22.1%**, 32-month high; **9.2% → 11.2%** |
| Saudi Arabia | **649,000 b/d** | **+4.4%**; **13.8% December** |
- Differentiate **supplier's volume** from **share of India's import basket**; these are source-period data, not today's shares.
## Prices → sourcing → macro effects
- Source **Urals about $5.5/barrel below Arab Light**, **Basrah Medium about $0.80 above Dubai benchmark**; different grades/benchmarks, time-specific spreads.
- Landed cost includes freight, insurance, sanctions/payment constraints and refinery suitability; the largest discount alone does not determine supply.
- Source India **over 85% import dependence**, third-largest oil consumer; distinguish crude-import dependence from all-energy dependence.
- Oil prices/import bill → current account, rupee, inflation, fiscal/subsidy pressures and transport/industrial costs. Diversification, strategic reserves, efficiency and cleaner alternatives strengthen energy security.
- Source predicts weak Russian supplies early 2025 and possible **March–April 2025** rebound during refinery maintenance; forecasts, not verified subsequent outcomes.
## Ballia: exploration is not a proven oilfield
- March 2025 reporting concerned ONGC exploratory work near Sagarpali, **Ballia, Uttar Pradesh**. ONGC lists environmental clearance for **two exploratory wells** in the district's OALP-VI block. [ONGC clearance register](https://ongcindia.com/en/web/eng/sustainability/environment/environment-clearance).
- An exploration lease/drilling plan, a geological indication, a resource estimate and a commercially recoverable reserve are separate stages. Do not label the location a confirmed “massive” producing field from the news alone.
- Exploration may help supply diversification but economics, reservoir assessment and environmental/community safeguards determine feasibility. Import-dependence percentages require a specified reporting year and denominator.

## Brent and WTI: benchmark revision
| Feature | Brent | West Texas Intermediate |
|---|---|---|
| Origin/reference | North Sea-derived international benchmark | US crude; Cushing, Oklahoma delivery reference |
| Quality | Light/sweet; indicative source sulphur about 0.37% | Generally lighter/sweeter; indicative source sulphur about 0.24% |
| Uses | International price reference | Major US/global traded benchmark |
- **Higher API gravity means lighter crude**; sweet means relatively low sulphur, **not sulphur-free**. Grade specifications can vary; a single sulphur percentage is not universal for every blend. [EIA quality explanation](https://www.eia.gov/TodayinEnergy/detail.php?id=33012).
- Freight, pipeline/storage bottlenecks, refinery compatibility, supply/demand and contracts shape differentials. “WTI always costs more to ship” or “Brent always determines every OPEC sale” are oversimplifications; many Asian sour grades use **Dubai/Oman** references.
- **India's crude basket blends Brent Dated with Dubai/Oman sour grades**; it is not purely Brent. WTI can matter through US supply and interconnected markets. [Government methodology](https://www.data.gov.in/resource/month-wise-details-average-international-crude-oil-prices-indian-basket-2017-18-2022-23).
- **One petroleum barrel = 42 US gallons ≈158.99 litres ≈159 litres**; volume does not specify mass without density.
- Supplied Brent question is labelled **2011**; answer **1 and 2 only**, since sulphur is present. Barrel question **2008** answer **159 litres**. Retain all statements/options when authenticated rather than using the PDF's answers as automatic official verification.

## June 2025: West Asian escalation
- Israel–Iran hostilities raised risks of oil-price spikes, disrupted **Strait of Hormuz** traffic and longer Red Sea/Suez shipping routes; distinguish direct purchases from Iran from indirect global price exposure.
- Higher landed oil costs can widen the trade/current-account deficit, pressure the rupee, raise transport/input inflation and weaken investment/consumption. Tax cuts/subsidies can protect consumers but reduce fiscal space; none of these responses is automatic.
- **Current account includes goods, services, primary and secondary income**; a merchandise import surplus alone is the trade deficit, not the full definition of CAD. Reserves do not necessarily fall because a CAD exists.
- Supplier diversification, reserves, energy efficiency and producer diplomacy improve resilience; route disruption can also increase Indian exporters' freight/time costs.

## June23 supplier reporting
- Source reports India increasing Russian and US purchases amid West Asian instability. Supplier diversification can reduce one-country exposure while leaving exposure to global prices, freight and chokepoints.
- PDF's **88.2% import dependence vs87.6%** is labelled **FY2025 first half vs FY2024 first half**, not a new June monthly/full-year figure. Producer/consumer rankings require a year and a defined measure (crude vs all liquids); India is a major third-ranked oil consumer/importer, not the second-largest as its practice distractor states.

## Oil reserves versus production
- **Proved reserves** are estimated economically recoverable volumes under specified conditions; **production** is a flow per unit time. Venezuela's **over 300 billion barrels**, largely extra-heavy crude, illustrate why large reserves do not ensure high output: sanctions, finance, refining technology and infrastructure matter. Canada's oil sands and US shale similarly show technology/economics shape supply.
- Source table (rounded **billion-barrel reserve snapshots**, without common reference year): Venezuela **303**, Saudi Arabia **267**, Iran **209**, Canada **163**, Iraq **145**, UAE **113**, Kuwait **102**, Russia **80**, US **74**, Libya **48**. Its embedded graphic gives conflicting figures/order (e.g. Iran ~155/Russia ~107/Canada >170), includes **Qatar and Brazil**, and mixes gas reserves: **do not memorise this as a harmonised current ranking**. Libya has Africa's largest proved oil reserves.
- **Reject the “annual billion barrels” production table**: the magnitudes/units are inconsistent and no comparable year/series is supplied. The US is a leading producer and Saudi Arabia/Russia are major suppliers, but reserve rank ≠ production rank; crude-only versus all-liquids definitions differ.
## OPEC/OPEC+ revision
- **OPEC:** founded **September 1960, Baghdad** by **Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Venezuela**; headquarters **Vienna**. Coordinates petroleum policies, market stability, producer returns and reliable consumer supplies.
- **June 2025 twelve members:** Algeria, Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Libya, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Venezuela. Angola left **January 2024**; Ecuador/Qatar/Indonesia are former members or suspended participants, not current members.
- **OPEC+ / Declaration of Cooperation (2016)** adds Azerbaijan, Bahrain, Brunei, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Mexico, Oman, Russia, Sudan and South Sudan. Distinguish the **2016 Declaration** from the later **2019 Charter of Cooperation**; participation in the Charter or voluntary cuts is not identical to OPEC membership.
- Output targets, conformity monitoring and additional voluntary adjustments influence Brent/WTI and importing countries' inflation/current accounts. Saudi/Russian influence is substantial but non-OPEC growth (US, Brazil, Guyana), demand, sanctions and compliance constrain coordination; market shares depend on year and crude/all-liquids denominator.
- Correct source's generic “cuts extended into mid-2025”: by **31 May 2025**, eight members had agreed another **411,000 b/d July increase** while unwinding part of voluntary restraint. This was announced future supply, not July output already produced. [OPEC May announcement archive](https://www.opec.org/opec_web/en/publications/498.htm).
- **2024 Venezuela PYQ: (d)**—large reserves do not imply rapid crisis recovery or halted emigration. Economic distress and migration persisted in the question's context.

## July 11: Russian-oil tariff risk
- Embedded clipping reports Trump's threat of a **500% tariff** against countries importing Russian oil, alongside a claim that trade talks with India were nearing agreement. Treat this as a source-period political threat/proposal, **not an enacted tariff already applying to every Indian export**.
- Such secondary pressure can affect supplier choice, payment/shipping costs and India–US negotiations even where Russian discounts lower the crude purchase price. Existing FY2025-first-half import-dependence figures remain historical comparisons.

## July revision and reporting-period qualifications
- PDF reports **88.2% crude-import dependence in H1 FY2024–25**, versus 87.6% a year earlier; preserve that period rather than label it all-FY2025. India is a major net crude importer despite its substantial refining/export industry.
- Oil-price increases can raise import bills, cost-push inflation and fiscal pressures where taxes/subsidies buffer consumers; outcomes depend on volumes, exchange rates and policy. **Current account includes goods, services, primary and secondary income**, not merely imports minus exports.
- Repeated Brent/WTI chart and PYQs add no new core facts: sweet crude still contains sulphur; one oil barrel is about 159 litres. Existing common PYQ bank already contains 2011 Brent and 2008 barrel questions.

topics.title: Election records, transparency and public trust
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## What changed in December 2024?
- **Conduct of Elections (Second Amendment) Rules, 2024**, **S.O. 5517(E), 20 December 2024**; made under **Representation of the People Act, 1951, section 169**, after consultation with ECI.
- **Rule 93(2)(a)**: inserted **“as specified in these rules”** after “papers”, narrowing the category open to inspection under that provision. This is an ordinary statutory-rule amendment, **not a constitutional amendment**. [Gazette text](https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2024/259568.pdf).
- Debate concerns non-prescribed electronic records such as CCTV/webcasting. Do not equate it with abolition of **Form 17C**, which is prescribed, or cancellation of copies supplied to polling agents under the applicable rules.
- **Form 17C** records votes at a polling station; polling agents receive copies. Public online access, candidate-agent access and judicial access are distinct questions. [ECI explanation](https://www.eci.gov.in/evm-faqs).
## Competing considerations
- Transparency/accountability and voter confidence versus voter privacy, ballot secrecy, security and risk of decontextualised disclosure.
- Source raises turnout-revision concerns in **Odisha, Haryana, Maharashtra** and invokes **Chandigarh mayor election**, litigation and **2024 electoral-bonds judgment**; allegations/editorial conclusions are not findings that manipulation occurred in each named election.
- **Article 324**: ECI's supervision/direction/control; neutral administration and reasoned disclosure bolster trust. A challenge being filed does not itself invalidate the rule or establish a final court outcome.
## Mains response
- Publish timely, reconciled aggregate data and explain provisional/final differences; preserve auditable records and candidate safeguards.
- Clearly define access categories/retention, protect identities/ballot secrecy, provide secure redacted access where lawful, independent review and grievance remedies.
- Evaluate amendment through proportionality, statutory authority and constitutional values; distinguish reform recommendations from existing enforceable disclosure duties.

topics.title: PM-KISAN: income support and eligibility
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Scheme recall
- **Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi**, launched **February 2019**, effective from **December 2018**; **Central Sector**, 100% Union funding, **Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare**.
- **₹6,000 annually in three ₹2,000 instalments**, direct transfer to eligible **landholding farmer families**; States/UTs identify eligible beneficiaries and verify land records.
- Initially small/marginal farmer scope; expanded irrespective of holding size **subject to exclusion criteria**. Source's 'all landholding farmers' without exclusions is incomplete. [Official scheme](https://pmkisan.gov.in/), [2019 expansion](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1576233&lang=2&reg=48).
- Institutional landholders and specified higher-income categories excluded; tax-paying/professional/public-office categories assessed under scheme guidelines. Tenancy without qualifying recorded land ownership does not automatically create entitlement.
- Objective: supplement input/household liquidity and reduce distress borrowing, not reimburse the full cultivation cost or provide crop insurance.
- Issues: land-record errors, exclusion of vulnerable cultivators, timely transfer, grievance resolution and real value of assistance; DBT does not by itself resolve eligibility inequity.

topics.title: Plasticisers and esterase bioremediation
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Research recall
- **EstS1 esterase**, from soil bacterium **Sulfobacillus acidophilus**: laboratory research on breakdown of **phthalate plasticisers**; enzyme structure studied by **X-ray crystallography**. Reported activity over roughly a month concerns tested conditions, not guaranteed field performance.
- Plasticisers are **additives** that impart flexibility/durability; removing them is different from destroying the plastic **polymer backbone**. Exposure can occur through leaching from products, food/contact materials and personal-care items; health effects depend on substance, dose and exposure.
- **DEHP: bis(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate** → ester hydrolysis → **MEHP: mono(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate + 2-ethylhexanol**. A monoester intermediate may remain harmful; first-step hydrolysis is not complete detoxification/mineralisation.
- Other bacterial enzymes, including research on **Comamonas testosteroni**, can take intermediates through **phthalate → hydroxylated intermediates → protocatechuate → central metabolism**, eventually CO₂/water under suitable conditions. Multiple steps/organisms may be needed.
- Source suggests polymer-binding could help remove contaminants from water. Do not infer demonstrated complete **polypropylene biodegradation** from binding or plasticiser degradation. [EstS1 primary research](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0969212624004969).
## Persistence graphic: approximate estimates
| Item | Source estimate |
| --- | --- |
| Plastic bag / coffee cup | **20 / 30 years** |
| Straw / six-pack ring | **200 / 400 years** |
| Bottle / plastic cup | **450 years** |
| Coffee-mixing pod / disposable nappy / toothbrush | **500 years** |
- These are illustrative environmental-persistence estimates, not fixed experimentally universal lifetimes. Sunlight, temperature, oxygen and medium matter; fragmentation into **microplastics ≠ complete biodegradation**.
- Mains: source reduction, safer substitutes, segregated collection, producer responsibility and verified treatment; enzymes complement rather than replace waste prevention.
## Practice-test correction
- EstS1 is linked to **plasticiser degradation**, not methane absorption. The 19 January printed answer points to the wrong listed application.

## Endocrine disruption and plastic-related exposure
- **EDCs can mimic/block hormones or alter their production/signalling**. BPA in polycarbonate/epoxy uses, phthalates (DEHP/DBP) in flexible plastics/personal-care products, and selected PFAS in water/oil-resistant products illustrate chemicals with different uses/risks; not every plastic or PFAS has identical effects.
- Research associations include reproductive/developmental, thyroid/metabolic, immune and some cancer risks; low-dose/chronic exposure and sensitive developmental windows matter. **Chemical additives ≠ microplastic particles (<5 mm)**. Detection in blood, placenta, semen, lungs or other samples does not itself prove a particular disease. [NIH fact sheet](https://www.niehs.nih.gov/health/materials/endocrine_disruptors_508.pdf).
- Source **80% Dutch blood samples/89% Indian blood samples** are study-specific, not population prevalence; testicular-tissue findings must not be silently assigned to every Indian study. **“3× breast-cancer risk”, “30% sperm decline over 20 years”, ₹25,000-crore annual cost** lack adequate references/denominators here; do not memorise them as causally established national estimates.
- **9.3 million tonnes/year** concerns modelled plastic pollution emissions, not all plastic waste generated; retain the metric distinction.
- **Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016**, later amendments, segregation, EPR and specified single-use controls address waste. Chemical-exposure control also needs biomonitoring, longitudinal research, safer chemical design, worker protection and enforcement. Avoid blanket claims that no laws protect children/pregnant women or that biodegradable means non-toxic.
- Awareness options: follow food-contact container/heating instructions, use suitable materials, protect waste workers and validate filtration. “BPA-free” does not certify every chemical risk; an antioxidant diet is not a proven antidote. **BPA 2021 PYQ: polycarbonate**, already banked.

topics.title: UN committee on big data for official statistics
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Institution and purpose
- India joined **UN Committee of Experts on Big Data and Data Science for Official Statistics (UN-CEBD)** in **January 2025**.
- Established **2014**, initially chaired by **Australia**; supports official-statistics innovation, including **2030 SDG monitoring**. Reports to the **UN Statistical Commission**; not the UN Chief Executives Board.
| Structure | Function |
| --- | --- |
| Advisory Board | Strategic management; source describes roughly four meetings/year |
| Bureau | Continuing operational coordination |
| Task teams | Methods, applications and capacity building |
- Priorities: data sources/technology, training and experience-sharing, international/cross-border cooperation, advocacy and public trust. [UN Statistics mandate](https://unstats.un.org/bigdata/about/index.cshtml).
- Big data can improve timeliness/detail, but coverage bias, privacy, security, reproducibility and quality need safeguards; it does not automatically replace representative surveys/censuses.

topics.title: Blue Flag beaches
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Certification
- Voluntary international eco-label run by **Foundation for Environmental Education (FEE), Denmark**; beaches, marinas and sustainable tourism boats.
- Origin **France, 1985**; expanded beyond Europe **2001**. Four pillars: **water quality; environmental management; environmental education/information; safety/services**.
- January 2025 report: **Kappad, Kozhikode + Chal, Kannur, Kerala**. Kappad had earlier certification; this is not proof its first-ever recognition occurred in 2025. Award depends on compliance/renewal, not permanent protected-area status. [Kerala Tourism](https://www.keralatourism.org/newsletter/news/2025/blue-flag-certification-for-keralas-kappad-and-chal-beaches/2284).
## Source beach-map recall
| State / UT | Beaches |
| --- | --- |
| Gujarat / Diu | **Shivrajpur / Ghoghla** |
| Karnataka | **Kasarkod, Padubidri** |
| Kerala | **Kappad; Chal** in this development |
| Andhra Pradesh / Odisha | **Rushikonda / Golden** |
| Andaman & Nicobar | **Radhanagar** |
| Tamil Nadu / Puducherry | **Kovalam / Eden** |
| Lakshadweep | **Minicoy Thundi, Kadmat** |
- **Kovalam here is Tamil Nadu**, not the famous Kerala destination. This combines the source's older 12-beach list with Chal; do not use it as today's national total.
- Governance link: wastewater control, safe bathing, waste management, accessibility and local livelihoods; label alone does not resolve coastal carrying capacity.

topics.title: Organ donation, NOTTO and donor leave
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Organisation and law
- **National Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisation (NOTTO)**, under **DGHS, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare**; apex coordination of donation/transplant networks and donor/recipient registries under the national programme.
- **Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 1994**, amended **2011** to incorporate tissues and related regulation; consent, lawful allocation and prevention of commercial exploitation matter.
| Division | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| National Human Organ and Tissue Removal and Storage Network | Network/coordination and information functions |
| National Biomaterial Centre / National Tissue Bank | Tissue banking, quality and demand–supply coordination |
- Donation recall: **kidneys, liver, heart, lungs, pancreas, intestine**; tissues such as **cornea, skin, bone, heart valves and blood vessels**. Living donation and deceased donation differ; not every organ can be donated by a living person.
## Leave: dated rule
- **DoPT order, 25 April 2023**: up to **42 days special casual leave** for eligible **Central Government servant organ donors**, subject to medical recommendations and prescribed conditions.
- January 2025 awareness report does not create a new NOTTO law, automatic recipient entitlement or a rule covering every private employee. [Official donor-leave order](https://notto.mohfw.gov.in/WriteReadData/Portal/News/871_1_Grant_of_special_casual_leave_to_organ_donors.pdf).
- Ethics: informed consent, donor welfare, equitable waiting lists, transparent allocation and anti-trafficking enforcement.
## Registry compliance and transplantation ethics
- NOTTO under DGHS/Health Ministry maintains transplant data with the ROTTO/SOTTO network; THOTA **1994**, amended to include tissues, and implementing rules regulate transplantation/commercial dealings.
- March reporting highlighted hospital failure to update data; the directive sought registration/details within **48 hours of transplant** and regular reporting. This does not replace pre-transplant authorisation requirements.
- Reliable donor/recipient/hospital records support allocation, audit and research, but require confidentiality, access control and correction mechanisms.
- Allocation depends on applicable organ-specific priority/medical criteria; foreigners, living donation and deceased-organ lists have distinct rules. Missing data are a compliance risk, not automatic proof of trafficking.
- Low deceased-donor rates, public awareness, clinical capacity, transport and equitable access require action alongside enforcement; pledging alone does not guarantee an organ becomes available.

topics.title: Trichophyton indotineae and antifungal resistance
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Pathogen and transmission
- **Dermatophyte fungus**, named **Trichophyton indotineae in 2020**, following study of isolates from India/Nepal. A geographic name does not establish where all infections originated.
- Causes itchy, inflamed **tinea/ringworm** skin lesions, often widespread across groin, buttocks, trunk or face; dermatophytes as a group can affect skin, hair and nails. **Ringworm is fungal, not a worm**.
- Contact with affected skin and contaminated towels/clothes; source reports detection in over **40 countries** and renaming advocacy by over **30 dermatologists in 14 countries**, January 2025 figures.
## Resistance and public health
- Often **terbinafine-resistant**; not every isolate resists every antifungal. Misuse of topical steroid–antifungal–antibiotic combinations can mask/worsen infection and contributes to the problem.
- Correct diagnosis, species/resistance surveillance, appropriate clinician-led treatment and antifungal stewardship; avoid treating a source regimen as personal medical advice. [CDC investigation](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/72/wr/pdfs/mm7219a4-h.pdf).
- Naming ethics: precise scientific communication without stigmatising a country/community.

topics.title: Hattee community and Boda Tyohar
topics.subject: Anthropology
topics.markdown:
## Community and geography
- **Boda Tyohar**, major annual festival of the **Hattee/Hatti**, **Trans-Giri, Sirmour district, Himachal Pradesh**.
- Name associated with selling agricultural/wool produce at a **haat**. Related communities across **Jaunsar-Bawar, Uttarakhand**; **Giri and Tons**, Yamuna-system rivers; Tons forms sections of the Himachal–Uttarakhand boundary.
- Traditional community council **khumbli**; ceremonial white headgear; agriculture and cash crops. Do not relocate the community to Kinnaur/Lahaul-Spiti because a generic Himachal economy paragraph mentions those districts.
- Source **2011 population about 2.5 lakh**, later roughly **3 lakh** estimate without a specified census year: preserve dates/estimate status.
## Scheduled Tribe status
- **Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Second Amendment) Act, 2023**, inserted **“Hattee of Trans Giri area of Sirmour district”** in Himachal's list; geographic scope matters. It is an ordinary Act amending the ST Order, not a numbered constitutional amendment. [Gazette Act](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/repealedfileopen?rfilename=A2023-14.pdf).
- Source contrasts **Jaunsar-Bawar recognition in 1967**; don't assume every group using a similar name everywhere automatically has identical legal status.

topics.title: Vice-Chancellor appointments and federalism
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 draft
- **Draft UGC teacher/academic-staff qualification and higher-education standards Regulations, 2025**, released **6 January 2025**. These notes describe the **proposal**, not assume it is today's operative rule.
- Proposed eligibility: **ten years** as professor, senior research/academic administrator, or senior industry/public administration/public policy/PSU professional with significant academic/scholarly contributions.
| Proposed search committee | Nominating authority |
| --- | --- |
| Chairperson | **Visitor / Chancellor** |
| Expert | **UGC Chairman** |
| Expert | **University apex body**, e.g. Senate/Syndicate/Executive Council |
- Visitor/Chancellor constitutes committee and appoints from its **3–5-name panel**. Independence, conflicts/recusal and transparent selection matter. [Official draft, section 10](https://www.ugc.gov.in/pdfnews/3045759_Draft-Regulation-Minimum-Qualifications-for-Appointment-and-Promotion-of-Teachers-and-Academic-Staff-in-Universities-and-Colleges-and-Measures-for-the-Maintenance-of-Standards-in-HE-Regulations-2025.pdf).
## Existing framework versus proposal
- Earlier UGC norms call for eminent higher-education experts and a **panel of 3–5 candidates**; this panel size is not automatically the number of committee members.
- University Acts/statutes differ: President is Visitor of many central universities; Governor commonly Chancellor of state universities by **statute**, not an automatic constitutional power over every university. Source central/State/private examples are not a uniform all-India committee formula.
- Source conflicts: **Kerala** reappointment/Chancellor replacement; **West Bengal** interim VCs and Supreme Court-linked search process; **Tamil Nadu** search nominees and appointment Bills; **Karnataka** proposed changes for six universities; **Maharashtra** reversal of earlier restrictions. Legislative/court positions are dated January 2025, not current outcomes. Kerala's earlier controversy involved **Arif Mohammed Khan**; avoid calling him its January 2025 Governor.
## Federal balance: mains frame
- Union **List I Entry 66**: coordination/determination of higher-education standards; **Concurrent List Entry 25**: education, subject to relevant Union entries. Education shifted to Concurrent List by **42 nd Amendment, 1976**.
- National quality/merit and wider talent pool versus State autonomy, local accountability and financing; centrally nominated members do not automatically prove political misconduct.
- Consult States; clarify statutory authority; independent expert selection, recorded reasons, disclosure of conflicts and timely appointments; assess NEP 2020 goals alongside federal safeguards.
## Statutory power and precedent: January 2025 debate
- **UGC Act, 1956, section 26** authorises regulations within the Act's purposes. Whether specific VC rules adequately relate to educational standards is a legal question; an editorial claim of overreach is not itself a judgment invalidating the draft.
- **Suresh Patilkhede**, Bombay High Court (source labels **2011**): cited for doubts about applying UGC VC criteria to State statutory appointments; distinguish High Court reasoning from the full Supreme Court line of authority.
- **Kalyani Mathivanan v. K.V. Jeyaraj, 2015**: source incorrectly describes blanket mandatory application to all State universities. The ruling distinguished the 2010 framework's mandatory central/institutional operation from its directory character for relevant State institutions pending State adoption; Tamil Nadu had not adopted the scheme. Do not extrapolate this mechanically to every later regulation. [Supreme Court's subsequent discussion, paragraph 35 onward](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2024/45256/45256_2024_8_1501_62293_Judgement_14-Jul-2025.pdf).
- **Articles 246/254** and legislative competence/repugnancy must be read alongside **Entry 66, List I** and **Entry 25, List III**. A State law versus delegated central rule dispute is not settled simply by saying either government always wins.
- UGC prescribes standards/selection norms; **final appointment authority arises from applicable university law**, commonly Chancellor/Visitor. A UGC search nominee is not direct UGC appointment of every VC.

##2025 draft and federalism
- Draft UGC2025 regulations proposed a three-membersearch committee:Chancellor/Visitor nominee, UGCChair nominee, universityapex-body nominee; broader eligibility included senior industry/public policy/administration roles.
- **Draft is not already operative law**. UGC sets applicable standards; it does not personally appoint every university VC. Constituting committees and appointing VCs follow relevant Acts/rules.
- Education Concurrent List Entry 25 coexists with Union Entry 66 coordination/standards; fiscal funding alone does not override lawful national standards.
- Gambhirdan Gadhvi judgment is 2022, not source 2019; other Sreejith/Kannur/West Bengalcases turn on theirstatutes, facts andimproperinterference, not a blanket rule that every State academic nominee is prohibited.
- Governor's Chancellor role comes fromuniversity law, not automatically fromconstitutional Governor status. State Bills changingit need assent/commencement; disputes andpending Bills are source-era snapshots.
- Balance transparent merit, independent academic selection, State voice andinstitutionalautonomy; concern overpoliticisation is an argument, not proofevery proposedappointee is biased.

topics.title: Denotified and nomadic communities: SEED and inclusion
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Categories and exclusion
| Category | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **DNT** | Communities denotified after colonial criminal-tribe labelling |
| **NT** | Nomadic livelihoods/mobility |
| **SNT** | Semi-nomadic, periodically mobile |
- **Criminal Tribes Act, 1871** imposed collective stigma; denotification/repeal **1952**. Mobility and denotification are different criteria; categories overlap.
- Communities may be classified **SC, ST, OBC or none** depending on State/list; examples **Kanjar, Nat, Pardhi, Sapera**. Neither all STs nor all nomads are automatically DNTs.
- Identity/address documentation and certificates, insecure housing/livelihoods, interrupted schooling, healthcare access, stigma and limited representation; source's claim that none ever owned land/property is overbroad.
## Commissions: timeline recall
- **1947 Criminal Tribes Inquiry**; **1949 Ananthasayanam Ayyangar committee**; **1953 Kalelkar Commission**, first Backward Classes Commission.
- **Mandal** appointed **1979**, report **1980**; **NCRWC 2002** examined stigma; **Renke** constituted **2005**, report **2008**; **Idate** decision **2014**, report titled **2017**, submitted **8 January 2018**.
- Source lists **1,526 communities, 269 unclassified**; a 2022 official summary lists **1,262**. Different catalogues/counts should not be treated as one consistent current census. Population claims **25 crore**, **10%**, **10–12 crore**, and **150 DNT/500 NT groups** also differ in scope/period and are estimates, not settled present census totals.
## SEED and welfare
- **Scheme for Economic Empowerment of DNTs**, launched **February 2022**, Social Justice and Empowerment Ministry; planned **₹200 crore over five years from 2021–22**.
| Component | Delivery link |
| --- | --- |
| Competitive/professional entrance coaching | Education/employment access |
| Health insurance | **PM-JAY** |
| Livelihoods | **NRLM / State Rural Livelihood Missions** |
| Housing | **PMAY** |
- **DWBDNC**, registered society, established **21 February 2019**, rather than a permanent statutory commission. [Board record](https://dwbdnc.dosje.gov.in/index.php/content/about-us).
- **Dr Ambedkar pre/post-matric scholarships** and **Nanaji Deshmukh hostel scheme**, **2014–15**, source focus on DNT students outside SC/ST/OBC coverage. Eligibility/overlapping benefits require scheme-specific checks.
- Idate recommendations: permanent commission; State welfare departments; detailed survey; classification of unclassified groups; legal safeguards, including proposed additional SC/ST atrocities-law schedule. **Recommendations are not enacted protections by themselves**. [Official SEED background](https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2022/feb/doc202222519501.pdf).
## Mains response and PYQs
- Documentation camps/portable entitlements → accurate identification → accessible education, healthcare, housing and livelihoods → anti-stigma enforcement → participation and outcomes audit. Avoid treating mobility as criminal propensity.
- **Prelims 2014, Changpa**: primarily **Ladakh**, rear **pashmina goats**, **ST**; statements **2 and 3**, answer **(b)**. This comparison does not classify all Changpa as DNTs.
- **Mains 2017** asks for two major post-Independence legal initiatives addressing ST discrimination (**250 words, 15 marks**). Full questions are in the common subject PYQ files; welfare schemes and enforceable anti-discrimination laws must be distinguished.
## January 29 implementation focus
- Repeat coverage highlights certificate denial, poorly classified communities, outreach delays, overlapping-benefit checks and limited representation. Source's **“29 states”** and absence of a full-time board chair are dated claims, not verified universal present conditions.
- Prioritise mobile documentation camps, State-specific classification, community participation and transparent SEED uptake; distinguish catalogue estimates from census totals.

## Habitual-offender laws and inherited stigma
- Criminal Tribes Act **1871**, expanded/reworked in 1924, imposed collective colonial criminalisation; repeal in **1952** denotified communities. Criminality cannot be inherited from community identity.
- State habitual-offender laws generally use repeated conduct/convictions, but discriminatory definitions, prison manuals and enforcement can reproduce earlier stigma. Wording and safeguards differ by State.
- *Sukanya Shantha v. Union of India*, **3 October 2024**, rejected caste-based prison discrimination and addressed misuse of habitual-offender categorisation—not October 2023. [Supreme Court judgment](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2023/51059/51059_2023_1_1502_56228_Judgement_03-Oct-2024.pdf).
- Budhan Sabar's **1998** custodial death became a mobilisation anchor; reform advocacy involved Mahasweta Devi/G. N. Devy, NHRC, CERD and commissions including Renke (2008) and Xaxa (2014).
- Source NCRB 2022 classification rates describe recorded convicted prisoners, not the proportion of an entire community committing crime. No recent cases under a law does not mean formal repeal.
- Review discriminatory statutes/manuals; require individual evidence, due process and oversight; combine legal aid, documentation and non-stigmatising inclusion rather than community-based surveillance.

## August 2025: permanent commission demand
- A New Delhi national conference renewed the demand for a **permanent national commission for DNT/NT/SNT welfare**, and urged Parliament to address classification and inherited stigma. This repeats an Idate recommendation; it does not mean a new statutory commission was created.
- Source SEED eligibility: family income **up to ₹2.5 lakh/year**, subject to exclusion of overlapping equivalent benefits. Existing notes retain the scheme's coaching, health, livelihood and housing components and distinguish the **2019 welfare board** from a permanent commission.

topics.title: Hollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary and NBWL
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Sanctuary and primates
- **Jorhat, Assam**; approximately **100–120 m** altitude; terrain gently slopes southeast → northwest. **Bhogdoi River** supports waterlogged/semi-hydrophytic habitat at its border.
| Forest layer | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| Upper canopy | **Hollong** |
| Middle canopy | **Nahar** |
| Lower layer | Evergreen shrubs/herbs |
- Hoolock gibbons: India's only wild **apes**, **family Hylobatidae**, arboreal/diurnal, long arms and **brachiation**; territorial calls and pair bonding. Male dark with pale brows, female generally brown/buff. **Not monkeys**.
- Source graphic's traditional species: western **Hoolock hoolock**, **Endangered**; eastern **H. leuconedys**, **Vulnerable**, CITES **Appendix I**, dated graphic categories. Traditional range includes Northeast India/Myanmar and, for western, Bangladesh; species boundaries/ranges can be revised. Graphic's **20 gibbon species / 25-year lifespan** are approximate dated recall, not immutable counts.
- **Bengal slow loris**, Northeast India's nocturnal primate; not the only nocturnal primate everywhere in India.
- Source fauna: elephants, tiger/leopard, jungle cat, wild boar, civets, squirrels; **stump-tailed, northern pig-tailed, rhesus and Assamese macaques**, capped langur. Presence list is not a current population census.
## January 2025 exploration approval
- **Standing Committee of NBWL** approved proposed oil/gas **exploration in the sanctuary's eco-sensitive zone**, not unrestricted commercial production inside the sanctuary. Environmental, wildlife and other required clearances remain distinct. [Parliamentary explanation](https://eparlib.sansad.in/bitstream/123456789/2989605/1/lsd_18_IV_06-02-2025.pdf).
- **NBWL: section 5A, Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**, chaired by **Prime Minister**, Environment Minister vice-chair; source membership **47**.
- **Standing Committee: section 5B**, chaired by **Environment Minister**. Do not give the two bodies the same chair.
- Habitat diversion, protected-area boundary changes and relevant tourism proposals face statutory safeguards; tiger-reserve changes also involve **NTCA** and applicable legal processes. NBWL does not alone erase every safeguard.

topics.title: Cockfighting: law, tradition and animal ethics
topics.subject: Ethics
topics.markdown:
## Issue and law
- Cockfighting pits roosters against each other, sometimes with sharp blades/spurs; injury/death and associated unlawful betting. Source discusses Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala; customary popularity does not confer legal exemption.
- **Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960**, notably **section 11(1)(m)/(n)** provisions concerning entertainment involving fighting and organising places for animal fights. [Act text](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/7233/1/awbi01.pdf).
- Source cites **IPC 428/429**: these dealt with mischief by killing/maiming animals, not every unnecessary-pain offence. For January 2025, IPC references are historical: **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, section 325**, operates from **1 July 2024**, subject to offence facts. [BNS](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/20062/1/a202345.pdf).
- Source's 2017 Supreme Court narrative concerns enforcement of the Andhra Pradesh prohibition; avoid reading it as an independently verified blanket new national ruling on every animal sport.
- **PETA = People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals**; PETA India and its expanded name are not two unrelated organisations.
## Ethics: values → action
| Competing claim | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Cultural continuity / livelihoods | Respect communities; provide lawful alternatives |
| Animal welfare | Prevent avoidable suffering and lethal entertainment |
| Rule of law | Consistent enforcement, fair procedure, curb unlawful gambling |
| Public responsibility | **Article 51A(g)**: compassion for living creatures |
- Engage local leaders, run awareness campaigns, support nonviolent festival competitions and alternative livelihoods, and enforce anti-cruelty laws without selective tolerance.
- Tradition is relevant context, not a sufficient ethical defence of cruelty; evaluate harm, legality, compassion and practical alternatives together.

topics.title: Trade deficit and external-sector resilience
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Concepts: keep the balances separate
- **Merchandise trade balance = goods exports − goods imports**; negative means a merchandise deficit. Goods + services balance differs; **current account** also includes primary income and transfers/remittances. **Trade deficit ≠ fiscal deficit ≠ current-account deficit**.
- Causes: crude oil dependence (**over 85%**), electronics/semiconductor inputs and pharmaceutical **APIs**, notably from China; domestic investment/demand, relative prices, competitiveness and global demand.
- Imported capital/intermediate goods can raise productivity/exports; consumers gain choice, competition can stimulate efficiency. Benefits of imports do not prove that any size of persistent deficit is sustainable.
## Dated December 2024 data
| Merchandise | December 2024, USD bn |
| --- | --- |
| Exports | **38.01**, about **−0.99%** year-on-year |
| Imports | **59.95** |
| Deficit | **21.94**, rounded to 22 in graphic |
- Source graphic April–December exports **316.6 → 322.5**, imports **506.6 → 540.3**, deficit **190 → 217.8**, USD bn; these differ from the revised official January release: **exports 321.71, imports 532.48, deficit 210.77** for April–December 2024. Use matching revised series, not a mixture. [Commerce Ministry release](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/archiveContent.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=266125).
- Embedded graphic December growth: imports **gold +55.39%, petroleum +2.21%, silver +210.97%, electronics +9.60%**; exports **petroleum products −28.62%, gems/jewellery −26.51%, chemicals −2.93%**, non-oil exports **+5.05%**. Period/base matter; these are dated source figures.
## Effects: conditional, not automatic
- Import competition can displace some jobs; inputs can create others. Persistent external imbalances may pressure rupee/import prices and create financing risk.
- **FDI/equity inflows, borrowing or reserves** can finance external imbalances; a trade deficit does not automatically mean foreign borrowing or reserve depletion. Services/remittances can offset goods deficits. [RBI balance-of-payments framework](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/PublicationsView.aspx?id=9479).
- Source's emphasis on lost **export-duty revenue** is misleading as a general fiscal mechanism: most exports are not subject to export duty. Broader growth/tax effects vary.
## Policy and mains structure
- Competitive logistics/ports, reliable power, quality/innovation, skills and diversification; domestic capability in critical inputs; export-market access through negotiated FTAs, including **India–UAE CEPA**.
- Public procurement and carefully targeted import substitution can help; blanket high tariffs can raise input costs, harm exports and invite retaliation. FTA benefits depend on rules of origin/utilisation, not automatic bilateral balance.
- Answer sequence: define correct balance → explain composition/drivers → weigh productive imports against vulnerability → address competitiveness, energy diversification and stable financing.
- The source's daily mains prompt is **coaching practice**, not a dated UPSC PYQ.
## Accounting distinctions
- Merchandise trade deficit: goods imports exceed goods exports. Goods-plus-services balance differs; the current account additionally includes primary and secondary income such as remittances.
- A bilateral deficit is not automatically India's overall current-account deficit. Importing capital goods or intermediate inputs can support future production and exports.
- Financing can involve FDI, portfolio/debt flows and reserves. A deficit does not inevitably mean immediate reserve collapse or borrowing of the same amount.
- Risks depend on composition, persistence, exchange rates and financing stability. Rupee depreciation can raise import costs, but export responses depend on imported inputs and demand.
- Improve competitiveness, logistics, skills, quality standards and market diversification. Higher import tariffs can also raise exporters' input costs; assess value chains and sector effects.
- Export duties are not generally India's main fiscal-revenue source; avoid confusing trade balance with government budget balance.

## 16 May: April 2025 release
- **April 2025 goods+services estimates:** exports **US$73.80 billion**, imports **US$82.45 billion**, deficit **US$8.65 billion**. The clipping’s 84.9 bn headline needs reconciliation with official exports; do not mix total imports with goods exports. **Merchandise:** exports **US$38.49 billion**, imports **US$64.91 billion**, deficit **US$26.42 billion**. [15 May Commerce release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2128909&lang=2&reg=48).
- Services figures are provisional/estimated pending RBI release. Source explanatory December chart is recycled earlier data already recorded above, not April 2025.
- Energy/API/electronics inputs, benefits/risks and policy responses are covered above. Export-duty fiscal losses and automatic foreign-borrowing/reserve-depletion claims remain misleading; assessment must distinguish productive imports, financing stability and overall current account.

## April–June 2025: services offset the goods gap
- Embedded clipping reports Q1 FY2025–26 goods-plus-services exports **US$210.31 billion**, imports **US$230.62 billion**, deficit **US$20.31 billion**, down **~9.4%** year-on-year. Exports grew **5.94%**, imports **4.38%**; earlier-year totals **US$198.52/220.94 billion**.
- Services exports approximately **US$98.1 billion**, versus **US$88.5 billion** earlier, helped offset merchandise weakness; goods exports **US$112.17 billion** grew **1.92%**. Services estimates are provisional, not final RBI outcomes. [Commerce Ministry July 15 release](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2144870&lang=2&reg=48).
- Therefore the clipping concerns an **overall trade deficit**, not simply deficits with each named trading partner. The explanation repeats existing energy/API dependence and competitiveness measures; its automatic external-debt/reserve-depletion and export-duty-revenue claims remain misleading. Daily mains question is practice, not PYQ.

## Q1 FY2025–26 and June 2025 source snapshot
- April–June merchandise exports **$112.17 billion (+1.92%)**, estimated services exports **$98.13 billion (about +11%)**; goods deficit **$67.26 billion**, versus about $62.1 billion a year earlier. Services helped reduce the combined goods/services deficit by about **9.4%**; distinguish this measure from merchandise balance and the whole current account.
- June growth: electronics **46.93%**, tea **32.64%**, meat/dairy/poultry **19.7%**, marine products **13.33%**. US-bound goods rose about **23.5%**; front-loading ahead of tariff uncertainty may affect interpretation.
- Source Russian crude share around **36%**, petroleum about **15% of goods exports**, US about **17.7% of exports**: dated shares with different denominators, not permanent ratios. Diversify export products/markets and energy suppliers; improve value addition/logistics while negotiating market access. Secondary-tariff threats were July risks, not proof every threatened measure was already operative.

topics.title: Robotic MULES and military autonomy
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Platform and purpose
- **MULE: Multi-Utility Legged Equipment**, quadrupedal unmanned ground robot associated with **AeroArc/ARCV**, Delhi; displayed at **77th Army Day, Pune, 15 January 2025**. Theme **Samarth Bharat, Saksham Sena**. Army Day recalls **K. M. Cariappa's command takeover, 1949**.
- Legs traverse stairs, slopes and debris; sensors/thermal cameras support reconnaissance/perimeter security, light supply carriage, hazardous-material handling and possible bomb-disposal support. Payload options are not proof every deployed unit has every attachment or weapon.
| Technical recall | Qualification |
| --- | --- |
| Weight / payload / top speed | **51 kg / 12 kg / 3 m/s** |
| Computing / protection | **NVIDIA Xavier / IP67** |
| Endurance | **About 3 hours walking**, **20–21 hours standby**, not 20 hours continuous movement |
| Temperature | Product page gives **−40°C to +55°C** in narrative, **−45°C** lower limit in feature list; tested specification/version needs checking |
- Manufacturer lists modular cameras, robotic arm, chemical/radiation detection and weapon-system options. [AeroArc product specifications](https://aeroarc.in/products/). The **100-km command range** in coaching text lacks supporting product specification here.
## Dated procurement claims and evaluation
- Source places delivery of **100 units in June 2023** before its stated **September 2023 order**; inconsistent sequence, not a verified procurement timeline. It cites emergency procurement ceiling **₹300 crore**, which is not evidence of actual contract value.
- Pune was a first Pune parade, not the first ever outside Delhi; source merges parade and Southern Command investiture contexts. [Official Army Day report](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2093060&lang=2&reg=3).
- Benefits: reduce human/canine exposure, carry small loads, improve situational awareness; potential disaster-response/search-and-rescue uses.
- Limits: endurance, payload, communications loss, terrain reliability, cyber security and maintenance. An armed autonomous-capable robot requires human accountability, lawful targeting and appropriate control; autonomy does not establish independent lethal deployment.
- Indian assembly/vendor presence alone does not establish wholly indigenous hardware, software or IP.

topics.title: Jallikattu: culture, welfare and law
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Tradition and debate
- Tamil Nadu **Pongal**, January harvest festival; bull-taming event. **Jalli**: coins; **kattu**: tied—traditional prize associated with the bull's horns.
- Agrarian identity, bravery, human–animal relationships; supporters link breeding value to indigenous **Kangayam, Pulikulam, Bargur** cattle. Conservation benefit is an argument to evaluate, not proof every event protects biodiversity.
- Risks: bull stress/injury, tail twisting/poking/drugging, participant/spectator injury; rural livelihoods and cultural continuity must be weighed against preventable harm.
## Legal timeline: correct the source
| Year | Development |
| --- | --- |
| **2014** | **AWBI v A. Nagaraja**: Supreme Court prohibited Jallikattu under the then law; highlighted animal welfare/compassion |
| **2017** | Tamil Nadu amended the **Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960**, with rules permitting regulated Jallikattu |
| **18 May 2023** | Constitution Bench upheld relevant Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Maharashtra amendments concerning Jallikattu, Kambala and bullock-cart racing |
- January 2025 source incorrectly calls constitutional validity still undecided. The 2023 decision requires statutory safeguards; it is not blanket permission for cruelty. [Supreme Court judgment](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2016/1216/1216_2016_3_1501_44624_Judgement_18-May-2023.pdf).
- **Article 51A(g)** compassion; **48** animal husbandry, **48A** environmental/wildlife protection; cultural claims invoke **29**. Do not treat source's Article 21 reference as an unqualified holding that animals have the same enforceable fundamental rights as persons.
- Wildlife protection legislation is not the central regulating statute for a domestic bull sport. Mains: cultural participation with independent welfare inspection, veterinary checks, safety barriers, accountability and enforcement.
## Breed trap
- **Gir is indigenous to India (Gujarat)**. A breed being outside the typical Tamil Nadu Jallikattu breed list does not make it foreign to India.

## May 2025 cultural additions and comparison
- Also **Eruthazhuvuthal**; variants **Vadi manjuvirattu, Veli virattu, Vatam manjuvirattu**. Popular districts: Madurai, Tiruchirappalli, Theni, Pudukkottai and Dindigul; **Pulikulam**, associated with Sivagangai, is an important native breed. Participant prize and owner prestige are cultural features, not a universal competition rule.
- Ancient Tamil bull-embracing traditions have literary associations; the source's purported **Mohenjo-daro seal chronology/continuous Jallikattu lineage** and unqualified **“Silappadikaram is Sangam-era”** claim should not be treated as established dating. Artefact interpretation does not prove uninterrupted modern practice.
- **Concurrent List entry 17: prevention of cruelty to animals**. The **2023 Constitution Bench** upheld regulated statutory amendments but did not itself certify Jallikattu as an “essential cultural practice” or give animals all human Article 21 rights. [Supreme Court judgment](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2016/1216/1216_2016_3_1501_44624_Judgement_18-May-2023.pdf).
| Comparison | Recall |
|---|---|
| Kambala | Coastal Karnataka buffalo racing in wet paddy tracks |
| Bullock-cart racing | Maharashtra and other States; Maharashtra amendment included in 2023 judgment |
| Cockfighting | Associated with Sankranti in Andhra Pradesh; cruelty/betting concerns; tradition is no blanket legal exemption |
| Camel racing | Rajasthan fairs including Pushkar; permission/safety depend on applicable rules |
| Dhirio | Goa bull fights, distinct from bull-embracing Jallikattu; legality cannot be inferred from Tamil Nadu's amendment |

topics.title: Nagarahole, chital and prey–predator balance
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Reserve map
- **Mysuru and Kodagu, Karnataka**; landscape connectivity with **Wayanad Sanctuary, Kerala**, south, and **Bandipur**, southeast; Western Ghats/Nilgiri forest landscape.
- Scrub and deciduous forests with other moist habitats. Calling the Western Ghats a UNESCO site does not mean every site/entire reserve is automatically a listed component.
- Fauna: tiger, leopard, dhole, sloth bear; **chital, sambar, gaur, four-horned antelope, elephant**; southwestern langur.
## Dated population interpretation
- January 2025 report: **28 chital/km²**, source **142 tigers**, described as third-highest reserve population in a 2023 release. Keep survey area/method/year distinct; these are not today's counts.
- Adequate prey supports predators, but density alone does not establish a perfectly balanced/healthy ecosystem. Food/water, habitat, disease, grazing pressure, seasonal change and survey uncertainty matter.
- Habitat diversity/grass availability, controlled livestock grazing and protection can support prey; camera-trap and other systematic monitoring inform management. Tigers outside core areas may imply landscape use/conflict risk, not automatically beneficial overflow.
## Chital recall
- **Axis axis**, spotted deer, native to the Indian subcontinent, **Least Concern** in source. Reddish-brown coat/white underparts, persistent white spots; social herds, source typical **10–50**.
- Males larger; males carry **three-tined antlers**, shed annually; antlers differ from permanent horns.
- Source approximate size **35 inches/89 cm**, **187 lb/85 kg**, antlers near **3 ft/91 cm**; dimensions vary with sex/age/population. The printed **20–30-year lifespan** should not be treated as a verified typical wild lifespan.
- Distribution graphic lists India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Bhutan and small Pakistan occurrence; distinguish native range, introduced populations and locally extinct occurrences.

topics.title: Kashi Tamil Sangamam and Agasthyar
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Edition 3.0, 2025
- **15–24 February 2025**, **Namo Ghat, Varanasi**, during the wider Maha Kumbh period; Kumbh's main venue **Prayagraj**, not Varanasi.
- Theme: **Sage Agasthyar's legacy**—Tamil language/literature, philosophy, knowledge and health traditions; strengthen cultural/intellectual ties between Tamil Nadu and Kashi.
- Source planned **1,200 delegates**, five groups: students/teachers/writers; farmers/artisans; professionals/small entrepreneurs; women; startups/innovation/edtech/research. Separate **200 Tamil-origin Central-university students**, youth participation encouraged. [Education Ministry programme](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2102893&lang=2&reg=48).
## Links: history versus tradition
- Agasthyar's foundational role in Tamil knowledge is a **traditional attribution**, not a precisely dated proof of sole authorship of a language.
- **Brahmanda Purana** narrative of Dasharatha seeking Kamakshi's blessings at Kanchipuram: religious tradition, not independently established chronology.
- Source **15th-century Parakrama Pandya** and Sivakasi temple story; **Kasi Viswanathar Temple, Tenkasi** recalls north–south religious links. Distinguish temple history from journey legends.
- **Varanasi–Kanchipuram silk trade** and pilgrimage support people-to-people exchange. Evaluate inclusion, multilingual learning and sustained exchanges rather than only delegate numbers.

topics.title: Blue Ghost, Resilience and commercial lunar missions
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## One rocket, two missions
- **15 January 2025**, **SpaceX Falcon 9**, Kennedy Space Center, Florida: **Firefly Aerospace Blue Ghost (USA)** and **ispace Resilience (Japan)** rideshare launch.
| Lander | January plan |
| --- | --- |
| Blue Ghost | Roughly **45-day journey**, **10 NASA instruments**, **Mare Crisium near Mons Latreille**, northeastern near side |
| Resilience | Roughly **4–5 months**, **Mare Frigoris**, northern lunar region; **Tenacious micro-rover**, ispace-Europe |
- Blue Ghost is a **NASA CLPS** delivery, supporting science/technology and Artemis goals; sharing its launcher does not make the Japanese mission itself a NASA CLPS contract.
- Investigations: dust, lunar interior, Earth magnetosphere interactions, radiation-tolerant navigation/computing; rover/regolith handling for Resilience. [NASA payloads](https://science.nasa.gov/lunar-science/clps-deliveries/to19d-firefly/).
## Landing and dated outcomes
- Essentially no atmosphere → **parachutes cannot provide Earth-like braking**; powered descent/navigation must avoid rocks/craters. Rideshare saves launch cost but does not guarantee landing success.
- Later: **Blue Ghost landed 2 March 2025**; **Resilience's June 2025 attempt failed**, communication lost/no successful landing. Keep launch intentions separate from outcomes. [ispace update](https://www.ispace-inc.com/2025/06/06/status-update-on-ispace-mission-2-smbc-x-hakuto-r-venture-moon/).
- **Intuitive Machines** achieved the first commercial soft landing in **2024**; commercial providers complement national agencies, not eliminate their role in science/funding/regulation.
## Country recall
- **Intuitive Machines is American**, not Chinese; Blue Ghost → Firefly/USA, Resilience → ispace/Japan. Nationality of company differs from launch provider.

topics.title: Natural catastrophe losses and insurance resilience
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Hazard × exposure × vulnerability
- Swiss Re report cited: India **2023 economic losses about US$12 bn**, versus **US$8 bn annual average over the prior decade**. Economic loss differs from insured claims; more exposed assets can increase losses without a matching increase in hazard frequency.
- Source attributes roughly **63%** of annual catastrophe economic losses over two decades to floods; **Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu 36.8% industrial output** cited, baseline unspecified. Industry concentration raises exposure, not identical risk everywhere.
