- **Kalari**: training ground/gymnasium; **payattu**: martial practice. Integrates physical conditioning, armed/unarmed combat and mind–body coordination; one of India's longstanding martial traditions.
| Training stage | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| **Maippayattu** | Body conditioning |
| **Kolthari** | Wooden weapons: sticks/staves |
| **Angathari** | Metal weapons |
| **Verumkai** | Bare-hand fighting; anatomical knowledge |
- Northern/Malabar styles named: **Vattenthirippu, Arappukkai, Pillathangi**.
- **Parasurama origin story is tradition**, not verified historical founding. Bodhidharma/Shaolin transmission narrative is disputed; source **fifth-century / Thanjavur once part of Kerala** claim should not be learnt as settled history.
- January controversy: role in **38th National Games, Uttarakhand**, beginning **28 January 2025**; demonstration status and competitive-medal inclusion are distinct.
## Regional martial-art map
- **Huyen Langlon/Thang-ta, Manipur**: sword/spear armed practice and **Sarit Sarak** unarmed combat.
- **Lathi Khela, Bengal**: staff; **Gatka, Punjab**: Sikh martial practice with sticks/swords, linked to **Guru Hargobind** and later Sikh tradition; source federation **2018** is an organisational date, not origin of the art.
- **Silambam, Tamil Nadu**: staff/other weapons, Tamil diaspora including Malaysia; deity/sage origin accounts are traditional.
- **Kathi Samu, Andhra Pradesh**: sword practice in **garidi**, stick practice as preparation; **Paika Akhada, Odisha**: warrior training with rhythmic performance/drums.
- **Pari Khanda, Bihar/eastern tradition**: sword–shield; links to Chhau practice do not make every local martial form separately UNESCO-listed.
- **Thoda, Himachal Pradesh**: archery-based sport/performance, Baisakhi and Mahabharata-themed groups; **Mallakhamb, Maharashtra/Madhya Pradesh**: gymnastic pole/rope practice, malla = wrestler, khamb = pole.
- **Kalaripayattu, Mallakhamb, Gatka, Thang-ta** inducted into Khelo India Youth Games programme in the source's historical account; not proof all described arts are medal events in every competition.

topics.title: National Board for Wildlife and statutory safeguards
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Legal identity
- **Section 5A, Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972**, introduced by **Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act 2002**, **Act 16 of 2003**. Source **2022 creation** is wrong; predecessor **Indian Board for Wildlife, 1952**.
- **Prime Minister chair; Environment Minister vice-chair**, senior government representatives, institutions, NGOs, nominated conservationists/ecologists and rotating State/UT representatives. Source **47 members** is a reported composition count, not the safest substitute for statutory categories.
- Member-secretary: **Additional Director General of Forests (Wildlife)/Director of Wildlife Preservation**.
- **Section 5B Standing Committee**: vice-chairperson, member-secretary **plus no more than ten nominated Board members**; not “ten total” and not an independent external regulator. [Amendment text](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/6199/1/wild_act_2002.pdf).
## Roles and limits
- Advises on policy, conservation and protected-area assessment; Standing Committee exercises delegated functions/project scrutiny.
- Statutory safeguards cover protected-area habitat diversion/destruction, relevant tourism development and boundary changes; tiger-reserve denotification requires **NTCA recommendation + NBWL approval**, with applicable State/central procedures.
- NBWL recommendation **does not replace every forest/environment clearance** or permit all activity automatically. Applicable protection differs by sanctuary, national park, tiger reserve and eco-sensitive area.
- January report: refusal of **soapstone mining proposal near Kedarnath Wildlife Sanctuary, Uttarakhand**; compare mineral extraction, habitat/hydrology and site-specific legal constraints.

topics.title: NASAMS and networked air defence
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## System
- **National Advanced Surface-to-Air Missile System**, **Kongsberg (Norway) + Raytheon (USA)**; ground-based short/medium-range **networked air defence**, fielded by Norway **1994**.
- Radar/sensors → **Fire Distribution Centre** → distributed launchers; **AIM-120 AMRAAM** adapted for ground launch, with configuration-dependent other missiles. Aircraft, helicopters, cruise missiles and drones are typical targets.
- Modular open architecture, active radar and passive electro-optical/IR inputs; distributed components improve survivability/interoperability, not immunity to jamming.
- Source **75 km radar / 30 km engagement**, **six missiles per launcher**, **three launchers / 72 targets** combine configuration-specific claims. **Detection range ≠ missile range; launcher inventory ≠ simultaneous target capacity**. [Manufacturer description](https://www.kongsberg.com/what-we-do/defence-and-security/integrated-air-and-missile-defence/nasams-air-defence-system/).
## January context
- Taiwan reported planned **north/Taipei deployment** of purchased systems; procurement, delivery and deployment dates differ.
- Users source lists Norway, Spain, US, Finland, Hungary, Netherlands, Australia, Indonesia, Qatar, Oman and Lithuania; **13-country count** is dated/incomplete, not a permanent membership list. US capital-region protection since **2005**.
- Practice's “Canada never uses NASAMS” distractor requires date/end-user distinction; Canada's procurement for Ukraine differs from Canadian domestic operational deployment. Do not memorise a timeless negative.

topics.title: Antimicrobial resistance: containment and research
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## January research finding
- **Southern Cross University**, oyster **haemolymph** proteins: laboratory antibacterial activity and improved action of conventional antibiotics against selected bacteria.
- **Antimicrobial proteins/peptides** are innate defences against microbes in marine habitats; potential drug leads require isolation, mechanism, toxicity, dosage and clinical validation. **Not an approved human treatment or evidence eating oysters cures resistant infection**. [University's 21 January account](https://www.scu.edu.au/news/2025/video---oyster-blood-proteins/).
## Biology traps
- **Mollusca → Bivalvia**; two irregular calcified shell valves, marine/brackish filter feeders drawing algae/particles across gills.
- Filtration depends on size, species and conditions; source **1.3 gallons/hour** is not a universal fixed rate. Many reproduce by broadcast spawning, with sex change in some species.
- Oysters have **nervous ganglia**, despite lacking a vertebrate-like brain/spinal cord. That alone does not establish a definitive capacity/absence of pain.
- Source **eyes all over body** confuses oysters with eye-bearing bivalves such as scallops; shell closure/sensory response does not require that anatomy.
- University describes **Sydney rock oyster** proteins disrupting/preventing bacterial **biofilms**, one reason for improved antibiotic action in laboratory work.

## AMR: public-health framework, April 2025
- **Antimicrobial resistance:** microbes—bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites—become less responsive to relevant medicines; infection becomes harder to treat and can spread, cause severe illness or death. **The microbe becomes resistant, not the patient's body**. Antibiotic resistance is the bacterial subset. [WHO](https://www.who.int/health-topics/antimicrobial-resistance).
- Bacterial resistance emerges through mutation and **horizontal gene transfer**; antimicrobial exposure selects resistant organisms. Drivers: inappropriate prescribing, self-medication and unnecessary broad-spectrum use; livestock/aquaculture misuse; inadequate WASH, infection prevention and diagnostic access; poor-quality medicines and environmental contamination.
- Resistant infections jeopardise routine treatment and care dependent on effective infection control—surgery, transplants, cancer therapy and neonatal care. High infectious-disease burden, uneven surveillance/diagnostics and hospital infection control magnify India's vulnerability. TB/malaria resistance requires disease-appropriate drugs; antibacterial antibiotics do not treat every pathogen.
- **Burden correction:** the study published in **2022**, covering **2019** across 204 countries/territories, estimated **4.95 million deaths associated with bacterial AMR**, including **1.27 million attributable to resistance**. Associated deaths and attributable deaths are different counterfactual measures; this was not a 2021 mortality count. Western sub-Saharan Africa had particularly high mortality rates and South Asia a substantial burden. [Original study](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(21)02724-0).
- Source's **60,000 neonatal deaths/year in India** is an older, inadequately dated estimate, not a verified April 2025 annual count. India has surveillance systems; describe coverage/data gaps rather than their total absence.

## Stewardship of newer antibiotics: 25 April clipping
- Infectious-disease specialists urged **DCGI** to establish clear regulatory pathways for rational use of newer antibiotics. The clipping reports inappropriate community/broad-spectrum use of **ceftazidime–avibactam**, intended for targeted resistant gram-negative infections, and resistance even when combined with **aztreonam**. Treat this as expert concern, not a quantified national failure rate.
- **Cefiderocol** and **cefepime–zidebactam** are described as forthcoming options in this dated report; do not infer universal Indian approval, market availability or efficacy against every resistant isolate.
- Use culture/susceptibility testing where indicated, appropriate prescribing and review/de-escalation, hospital stewardship and surveillance. Education should accompany enforceable prescribing/dispensing controls; reserve agents should not become indiscriminate first-line substitutes.

## Indian response and One Health priorities
- **National Action Plan on AMR launched April 2017**: awareness, surveillance, infection prevention, optimised antimicrobial use, R&D/investment and multisectoral coordination. **Delhi Declaration** supports coordinated action across ministries and stakeholders. NCDC/ICMR networks provide resistance surveillance; India joined **WHO GLASS in 2017**. [NCDC programme](https://ncdc.mohfw.gov.in/includes/About/CentresAndDivision/amr.php).
- **One Health:** link human health, animal husbandry, food systems and the environment. Extend monitoring to community/rural settings, animals and effluents; improve sanitation, vaccination, diagnostics and healthcare infection control.
- Free Diagnostic Services and **Kayakalp** can strengthen diagnosis and facility hygiene; neither automatically ensures appropriate prescribing. Affordable access to effective medicines must accompany restrictions on misuse.
- R&D priorities: antibiotics, rapid diagnostics, vaccines and validated alternatives; finance development and sustainable supply while preserving access. Source suggestions for an international funding mechanism or patent-pooling arrangements are **proposals**, not proof of an established AMR-specific global fund or a patent pool covering all antibiotics.

## International comparison and mains structure
- US **2020–25** plan: prevent emergence/spread; strengthen surveillance; advance rapid diagnostics; accelerate R&D; improve international coordination.
- UK **2019–24** framework emphasised reducing need/exposure, optimising use and innovation/access. It was succeeded by **2024–29** national action plan, published **8 May 2024**; do not present the earlier plan as the current April 2025 framework. [UK plan](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/uk-5-year-action-plan-for-antimicrobial-resistance-2024-to-2029).
- Use international examples to compare measured stewardship, surveillance and access, not assert success merely because a country has a plan.
- **250-word practice answer:** definition/burden → India-specific drivers → government response → remaining gaps → funded One Health implementation, diagnostic-led stewardship, infection prevention, R&D and accountable monitoring. The supplied daily question is practice, not a dated UPSC PYQ.

## May 2025: antibiotic innovation and access
- The issue revisits **Nafithromycin**, Wockhardt/BIRAC-supported indigenous oral antibacterial for **community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP)**, marketed as **Miqnaf**. Public scientific launch **20 November 2024** differs from regulatory clearance and later commercial rollout; company reports commercial launch **27 May 2025**, after this issue. [PIB research announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2075174&lang=1&reg=3), [company rollout statement](https://www.wockhardt.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/press-release-q2-fy26.pdf).
- Proposed/labelled course **once daily for three days** and reported **97% clinical cure** concern studied CABP patients, not every resistant infection or guaranteed individual cure. PIB describes **14 years** of development (source rounds to 15). “First of its class in three decades” must not be expanded into “no new antibiotic class anywhere for 30 years”.
- **2050 projections**: **1.91 million annual deaths attributable to bacterial AMR**, **8.22 million associated**; model forecasts with uncertainty, not present mortality. **2019 global 1.27 million** is attributable, not the full associated burden. Source India **297,000** is an attributable estimate rather than every infection-associated death. [Original forecast study](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(24)01867-1).
- Source's **70% antibiotic use in animals/agriculture** has no clear geography/measure; it is not a verified universal Indian consumption share. India's **2019 colistin prohibition** covers its use in food-producing animals, poultry, aquaculture and animal feed supplements, not simply poultry growth promotion.
- Delayed/poor-quality susceptibility testing, understaffing, high caseloads, self-medication and indiscriminate new-agent use undermine stewardship. Existing ceftazidime–avibactam resistance reinforces culture-guided use, infection prevention and review/de-escalation, not reflexively broader treatment.
- New-drug research needs rigorous trials/regulatory evidence, affordable access and sustainable supply alongside restrictions on misuse. One Health implementation links human/veterinary/agricultural/environmental surveillance, public education and accountable dispensing; AMR is microbes resisting treatment, not humans becoming resistant.

topics.title: Mount McKinley–Denali and Alaska geology
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 naming context
- **20 January US executive direction** to restore **Mount McKinley** name for **Denali**, **North America's highest peak**, **Alaska Range, south-central Alaska**. Mountain renaming differs from renaming **Denali National Park and Preserve**.
- Two summits, higher southern summit; mainly granitic massif with tectonic uplift/erosion. Not a volcano and not on the US–Canada boundary.
- Source uplift history **about 60 million years** describes long tectonic history, not instantaneous formation of the present summit.
- Large vertical relief above surroundings, source **~5,500 m**; **relief is not summit elevation above sea level**. Snow/ice feed **Kahiltna, Muldrow, Peters, Ruth, Traleika** glaciers.
## Denali Fault
- Major **strike-slip fault system**; long-term horizontal movement rearranges geological units. Source study correlates three formerly connected **terminal-suture-zone** sites and estimates **~483 km displacement over millions of years**, not one earthquake or annual movement.
- **Suture**: zone of past terrane/plate joining; later strike-slip offsets can separate once-contiguous features. Map locations and differentiate vertical mountain uplift from lateral fault displacement.

topics.title: Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis after tuberculosis
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Disease distinction
- **CPA**, chronic lung disease caused by **Aspergillus**, often **A. fumigatus**, an environmental mould in soil/dust/decaying vegetation; spores inhaled, not ordinarily person-to-person transmission.
- **Pre-existing lung cavities/damage**, especially post-TB, COPD or sarcoidosis, predispose. Severe immunosuppression is particularly important for **invasive aspergillosis**; CPA can occur without it. Do not collapse all Aspergillus syndromes into one.
- Persistent **three-month-plus respiratory symptoms**, cough/haemoptysis, weight loss, fatigue/breathlessness; fungal ball **aspergilloma** or chronic cavitary changes. **Post-TB symptoms ≠ automatically recurrent bacterial TB**.
- Diagnosis combines imaging and **Aspergillus IgG/other microbiology** with clinical context; antibody positivity alone is not the same as confirmed CPA. [CDC overview](https://www.cdc.gov/aspergillosis/about/index.html).
## Assam study
- January **2025**, Dibrugarh tea-community study: **128 tea gardens screened**, selected symptomatic sample **177**; clipping **17.8% CPA**, **18.5% among TB patients**, **48.9% among those who completed TB treatment**. These are study/subgroup estimates, not Assam-wide population percentages. [Original research](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pntd.0012756).
- Poverty, nutrition, occupational exposure and diagnostic access compound vulnerability. Clipping cites Assam TB **217 per lakh**, national prevalence survey **2019–21**, and CPA **60 per lakh** estimate; keep disease/period/estimate distinct.
- Source **1.2 million globally annually** is not an adequately defined current all-CPA incidence estimate; post-TB estimates and total disease prevalence must not be conflated.
## Care and policy
- Specialist **antifungals** such as itraconazole/voriconazole, selected surgery for serious fungal-ball bleeding and nutritional/underlying-disease support; treatment depends on form, resistance and patient assessment.
- Follow up TB survivors, train clinicians, improve affordable imaging/serology and antifungal access; better nutrition/living conditions support health, but ventilation alone cannot remove ubiquitous mould exposure.

topics.title: SANJAY battlefield surveillance system
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 flag-off
- **24 January**, **Indian Army + Bharat Electronics Limited**, indigenous automated **Battlefield Surveillance System (BSS)**, **Buy (Indian)**; **₹2,402 crore**.
- Planned phased induction into **brigades, divisions, corps**, **March–October 2025** in three phases. Flag-off and a planned induction schedule do not prove all units were deployed in January. [Defence Ministry](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2095712&lang=2&reg=48).
## Data to decisions
- Ground/aerial sensor inputs → integration and removal of duplicate observations → **Common Surveillance Picture** → secure Army data/satellite networks → commander assessment.
- Improved border/intrusion awareness, network-centric coordination and decision speed in conventional/sub-conventional operations; technology absorption/domestic industry benefits.
- Surveillance system **does not itself guarantee correct identification or replace command responsibility**. Sensor quality, interoperability, resilient communications, cybersecurity and operator training determine performance.

topics.title: Indo-Pacific: geography, interests and cooperation
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Concept and map
- Connects **Indian and Pacific Ocean** strategic/economic systems; boundaries differ by country. India's broad vision extends from **African shores to the Americas**, rather than one universally fixed treaty region.
- **Hormuz**, Persian Gulf approach; **Malacca**, Indian Ocean–South China Sea route; sea lanes carry energy/trade. **South China Sea is a sea, not a strait/chokepoint**.
- Source **60% maritime trade / 60% GDP / two-thirds growth** are broad region/period-dependent estimates, not comparable exact annual shares without definitions.
## Issues
- US–China competition, Chinese maritime claims/artificial-island activity and BRI influence; diverse countries' interests cannot be reduced to identical blocs.
- South China Sea claims involve **China, Vietnam, Philippines, Malaysia, Brunei**, with **Taiwan** also relevant; East China Sea **Senkaku/Diaoyu** dispute. Maritime rights/navigation governed by applicable international law, not merely influence over trade routes.
- Piracy, illegal fishing, arms/drug trafficking; climate hazards, sea-level rise, coral loss and marine pollution; militarisation and unequal infrastructure/capacity.
## India and regional mechanisms
- **Act East, ASEAN centrality, free/open/inclusive cooperation**, strategic autonomy and international law; security alongside connectivity, blue economy and disaster resilience. [India's 2018 policy address](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=179711).
| Mechanism | Distinction |
| --- | --- |
| **Quad** | India, USA, Japan, Australia; partnership, not a formal defence alliance |
| **AUKUS** | Australia, UK, USA; India is not a member |
| **IPEF** | Economic cooperation framework, not identical to a free-trade agreement |
| **IONS / Malabar** | Maritime dialogue / naval exercise, respectively |
- **Andaman–Nicobar Command**, naval capacity, partner exercises; island partnerships **Sri Lanka, Maldives, Seychelles**. **Sagarmala** domestic port-led development; **Chabahar** Iran connectivity project—different functions/locations.
- Balance partnerships, protect commerce and support smaller States' choices; technology/finance/infrastructure, readiness and environmental cooperation matter as much as declarations.

topics.title: Guillain–Barré syndrome and post-infection nerve injury
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mechanism and symptoms
- Rare **immune-mediated peripheral nerve disorder**: immune attack damages myelin and/or nerve fibres → weakness, tingling/numbness, reduced reflexes and sometimes paralysis.
- **Not contagious**; an antecedent infection may be transmissible. **Peripheral nervous system ≠ brain/spinal cord**. All ages affected, more often adults/men; background incidence roughly **1–2 per 100,000/year**, population-dependent.
- Common progression: legs → arms/face, impaired walking/coordination; swallowing/respiratory muscles may be affected. **Autonomic dysfunction** can disturb heart rate/blood pressure; weakness need not remain mild/temporary.
## Triggers and Pune context
- Often follows gastrointestinal/respiratory infection, notably **Campylobacter jejuni**, and **EBV/CMV**, among others. **Mycoplasma pneumoniae** is another recognised association; not every urinary infection causes GBS.
- Surgery and rare associations with particular vaccines occur; **infections carry greater GBS risk than their relevant preventive vaccines**. Source's broad “trauma/stress” list is not evidence ordinary emotional stress is an established routine cause.
- **January 2025 Pune cluster**, central/State teams investigating; clipping reports **73 cases / 14 ventilated as of 25 January**, a dated snapshot, not final outbreak totals or proof a specific water source caused every case.
## Treatment and recovery
- **IVIG**, pooled donor immunoglobulins, or **plasma exchange** can modify the immune attack; respiratory/cardiac monitoring, supportive care and rehabilitation matter.
- Antivirals are not the main treatment for the immune disorder; management of an identified antecedent infection is a separate decision.
- Many recover over weeks/months, sometimes much longer, with persistent disability in some; no instant curative treatment. Rapidly progressive weakness/breathing difficulty requires urgent clinical assessment. [WHO explanation](https://www.who.int/en/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/guillain-barr%C3%A9-syndrome).

topics.title: Dhanauri wetland and Sarus crane conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Location and notification
- **Dhanauri, near Dankaur/Greater Noida**, **Gautam Buddha Nagar, Uttar Pradesh**, near Jewar airport; wider **Yamuna floodplain/basin**, source about **15 km from Yamuna**, with Okhla/Surajpur regional wetland connections.
- **Yamuna is within the larger Ganga drainage system**. Practice key's absolute “not Ganga Basin” is overdrawn: distinguish the immediate **Yamuna sub-basin** from the overarching Ganga basin.
- January **NGT** direction for State's wetland-notification status in **four weeks**; direction/proposal **does not itself notify the wetland or designate a Ramsar site**. **Important Bird Area ≠ Ramsar designation**.
- Embedded historical graphic: identification **2014**, Centre sought Ramsar proposal **2019**; State forest proposal **January 2022**, consent issue **February**, **YEIDA NOC for 112 ha, June 2022**. Those steps precede the January 2025 status inquiry; retain chronology without assuming final approval.
## Birds and ecology
- Marsh habitat important for **Sarus crane, Antigone antigone**, **world's tallest flying bird**, source IUCN **Vulnerable**.
- Three recognised living regional subspecies: **Indian, Eastern, Australian**; Indian is generally largest/heaviest. IUCN threatened category differs from the legal status of a particular wetland.
- Source birds: **common teal, mallard, northern pintail, greylag/bar-headed geese; woolly-necked, black-necked and painted storks; Eurasian marsh harrier**. Great Indian Bustard is principally dry grassland/semi-arid habitat, not this marsh's flagship.
- Protect habitat, drainage, water quality and feeding/breeding areas; land-use/airport development requires transparent assessment and bird/habitat safeguards.

topics.title: Typhon missile system and regional deterrence
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Ground-launched system
- **US Army Mid-Range Capability (MRC), Typhon**, **Lockheed Martin system integration**; mobile ground launchers, operations/command centre and reload/support vehicles; reported battery **four launchers**.
- Fires **SM-6 and Tomahawk**; missiles are associated with **Raytheon**, which differs from identifying the Typhon system integrator. [Manufacturer account](https://www.lockheedmartin.com/en-us/news/features/2023/keeping-the-us-army-ahead-of-ready-with-next-generation-launch-systems.html).
- **SM-6** has naval air/surface roles; **Tomahawk** cruise missile has land-attack and maritime variants. A missile's broader family roles **do not prove this deployed Army configuration provides every naval air-defence function**.
- Source **500 km SM-6 / 2,500 km Tomahawk** are reported variant-dependent estimates, not universal official ranges. **Patriot is a different system**, not a Typhon round; ground launcher is not submarine-launch infrastructure.
## January 2025 context
- Reported relocation **within Philippines** to improve mobility/survivability; Chinese/Russian objections and regional deterrence debate. Distinguish relocation from first deployment or a transfer of US missiles into Philippine ownership.
- Regional security balance versus escalation/host-country concerns; deployable strike capability differs from a standing military alliance's political commitments.

topics.title: Eurodrone and India’s observer status
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Programme identity
- **Medium Altitude Long Endurance Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (MALE RPAS)**; **Germany, France, Italy, Spain**, managed by **OCCAR—Organisation for Joint Armament Cooperation**, Germany lead nation.
- Industrial prime **Airbus Defence and Space, Germany**; partners **Dassault Aviation, France; Leonardo, Italy; Airbus Spain**. **UK is not one of the four programme States**.
- **21 January 2025, India observer status**, joining Japan as an observer; **observer ≠ full programme partner, procurement order or operational deployment**. [OCCAR programme announcements](https://occar.int/news?cat=13).
## Planned capability
- **Twin-turboprop**, maximum mission payload **2.3 tonnes excluding fuel**, endurance **up to 40 hours** under relevant configuration/conditions. Maximum payload and maximum endurance need not occur simultaneously.
- **ISTAR = intelligence, surveillance, target acquisition, reconnaissance**, possible maritime missions; source ASW/early-warning roles require appropriate mission sensors/configuration, not automatic capability of any airframe.
- Designed with **civil-airspace integration/certification** in mind; manufacturer's superiority/first claims are promotional comparisons, not universal proof. [Airbus specification](https://www.airbus.com/en/products-services/defence/uas/eurodrone).
- European capability/industrial autonomy and reduced reliance on imported Reaper/Heron platforms; India's observation supports familiarity and cooperation without implying a signed purchase.

topics.title: KaWaCHaM and last-mile disaster warnings
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Kerala system
- **Kerala Warnings Crisis and Hazards Management System**, **KaWaCHaM**, Malayalam shield; functional **1 April 2024**, formally inaugurated **21 January 2025**.
- **National Cyclone Risk Mitigation Project**, NDMA/World Bank-supported early-warning infrastructure; **NCRMP is a programme, not a separate international funding organisation**. [Kerala SDMA](https://sdma.kerala.gov.in/kawacham/).
- **126 sirens**, strobe lights/cameras, public-building/tower/school sites; source **eight loudspeakers**, reach **up to 1,200 m**, lights **red/orange/yellow**. Reach depends on terrain/noise and must not be mistaken for guaranteed audibility everywhere.
## Warning to action
- Inputs from **IMD, INCOIS, CWC**, relevant agencies and validated situational reports; social-media information needs verification.
- **State Emergency Operations Centre**, district/local/taluk coordination; multi-hazard alerts for **coastal impacts, intense rain, strong wind, extreme heat**.
- Hazard assessment → authorised alert → siren/voice/light and other channels → evacuation/safe shelter instructions → coordinated response and monitoring.
- Pre-recorded messages, camp/safety information, accessible languages/formats, regular tests and community drills. Source “world's fastest” is not a measured universal ranking; warning value depends on **timely receipt, understanding and action**.

topics.title: Chinar trees and digital heritage conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Tree identity
- **Platanus orientalis, Oriental plane**, family **Platanaceae**; Kashmir **Booun/Boueen**, J&K heritage/state tree.
- **Maple-like leaves do not make it an Acer maple**; poplars are also a different group. Source's “only Platanaceae species in India” needs cultivated/native scope rather than an exhaustive botanical claim.
- Large spreading **deciduous** tree, around **30 m** height, old trunks **10–15 m girth** in source; green summer foliage → red/amber/yellow autumn. Growth **30–50 years to mature height / ~150 full size** is approximate/site-dependent.
- Cultural links to landscape, literature, **papier-mâché/embroidery/wood carving**; source Bhavani-associated local-name tradition and Persian **“che na(r) ast”** etymology are traditions, not verified sole origins.
- Timber/lacewood for furniture; source traditional leaf/bark use and dye-making from twigs/roots are **reported uses, not clinical efficacy claims**.
## Tree Aadhaar
- **J&K Forest Research Institute/Forest Department** tree census, coordinates and **QR-linked unique ID**, recording **25 parameters** such as location, estimated age, girth/height and health.
- January clipping: **28,560 surveyed/geotagged**, estimated regional total **32,000–33,000**, Kashmir and Chenab region; interim census estimates, not all surveyed on a single day.
- Monitor health/removal risks, legal protection and changing condition; permissions remain relevant even on private land.
- Source claims some trees **over 1,000 years**: **geotagging records an age estimate; it does not itself date wood or prove that age**. Credible age evidence and repeat inspections matter.

topics.title: Technology clusters, FDI and inclusive urban growth
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Hyderabad example
- January 2025 source describes Google's planned **Hyderabad campus**, **3 million sq ft / 7.3 acres**, billed as its largest outside the US. Embedded graphic projected **early 2026 completion / capacity for 18,000 employees**; projections are not proof construction or hiring was completed.
- **Gachibowli** IT corridor; institutions **ISB, IIIT Hyderabad**; Telangana **TS-iPASS**, industrial project approval/self-certification system, illustrates facilitation alongside infrastructure and skills.
- Source's blanket claims that Amazon, Microsoft and Facebook each have their “largest campus” here require company-specific comparison; Hyderabad is a major cluster without relying on those superlatives.
## Benefits, risks and response
| Channel | Benefit | Conditions / risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Investment + jobs | Construction, IT/services and suppliers | Jobs/capital inflows must be measured; office size alone is not FDI or GDP |
| Knowledge links | R&D, startup collaboration, global networks | Technology transfer is not automatic |
| Urban growth | Transport, housing, services | Congestion, unaffordable housing, water/power demand and construction pollution |
| Sector concentration | Scale and skilled-worker networks | Global downturn/visa exposure; diversify industries |
- Align transit, affordable housing and civic services with expansion; sustainable buildings, reliable utilities, satellite centres where suitable, industry-linked training in **AI/cloud/data**, and university–firm research.
- Source's **$5 trillion by 2025–26** is a dated ambition, not an achieved GDP statistic. Coaching Mains prompt: investment benefits → distribution/infrastructure constraints → sustainable cluster governance.

topics.title: Diplomatic capacity, MEA funding and development partnerships
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Resources behind foreign policy
- Aspirations in the neighbourhood, Global South, Quad, ASEAN engagement and **International Solar Alliance** require missions, trained diplomats, project delivery and policy research. India engages ASEAN; it is not an ASEAN member.
- **FY 2024–25 MEA Budget Estimates: ₹22,154.67 crore**, including missions, cooperation, passport services and other heads; allocation ≠ expenditure. [MEA annual report, finance chapter](https://www.mea.gov.in/Images/CPV/140725MEAAnnualReport2024English.pdf).
- January editorial: roughly **0.4% of Union budget**, committee recommendation **1%**, suggested staged **0.6–0.8%**. These are dated shares/recommendations; compare like-for-like BE/RE/actuals, including reserve transfers.
- Source comparisons: average **4% annual rise, 2017–2023**, later **23% spike**; training **+30%**, missions/training/cultural heads **+7%**, Nalanda/South Asian University **20–22% cuts**. Different heads and comparison bases; not a single uniform change.
## Grants, loans and implementation
- **Grant** need not be repaid; **loan/Line of Credit** creates repayment/project terms. Aid can support hydropower, connectivity and crisis response; repayment risk and delivery delays matter.
- Source snapshots: aid **−10%**, foreign-government loans **+29%**; Bangladesh allocation **₹200 → ₹120 crore**, Sri Lanka **+63%**; Bhutan largest aid recipient. Bangladesh cumulative LoCs **$7.86 billion**, neighbourhood share **45%**: stocks differ from annual budget flows/disbursements.
- Connectivity through **BBIN/BIMSTEC**, energy interdependence and trusted partnerships; competition with China's BRI does not make every project a zero-sum contest.
## Reform priorities
- Expand recruitment/training and regional expertise; coordinate ministries, monitor costs/time/outcomes, assess loans and local needs, protect fiscal priorities.
- **Track 1** official diplomacy; **Track 2** academic/nonofficial dialogue. Fund research, archive digitisation and lawful declassification to improve institutional memory, with appropriate confidentiality safeguards.
- Mains chain: ambitions → capacity gap → prioritised resources → delivery/accountability → durable influence. Source prompts are coaching questions.

topics.title: Child marriage: substantive equality and annulment
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Ages and remedies
- **PCMA 2006, section 2(a)**: child = **female below 18 / male below 21** for marriage. **Majority Act** adulthood generally **18 for both**; source's “men attain majority at 21” confuses marriage age with general majority.
- **Section 3**: child marriage generally **voidable at the child party's option**, not automatically void in every case; specified circumstances under **sections 12/14** differ. A minor applies through guardian/next friend with Child Marriage Prohibition Officer.
- Section 3(3) allows filing before completing **two years after attaining majority**; interpretation of male limitation has been contested. [Act](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/2055/4/a2007-06.pdf).
## Judgment: reasoning versus outcome
- **T. Sivakumar (Madras HC, 2011)** interpreted male filing limit as **23**; **Independent Thought (SC, 2017)** includes observations relevant to that approach.
- **Sanjay Chaudhary v Guddan, Allahabad HC, 25 October 2024** reasoned for an equal majority-based limit and questioned advantage to adult men. **However, its final decision followed binding Supreme Court precedent, accepted this man's filing before 23 and allowed the appeal**. The PDF's “rejected extension” does not capture that outcome. [Court's published judgment, paragraphs 69–76](https://allahabadhighcourt.in/ILR/ilr-2024/Oct2024.pdf).
- Do not treat the discussion as a nationwide enacted rule abolishing the male 23-year interpretation.
## Substantive equality debate
- **2021 Amendment Bill** proposed women's marriage age **21**; lapsed with dissolution of the 17th Lok Sabha. Proposal ≠ enacted amendment.
- Higher common age: potential schooling, delayed pregnancy and formal equality; concerns: adult **18–21** autonomy, privacy, selective enforcement and criminalisation of consensual relationships.
- Source **49.4% self-initiated marriages**, Enfold/Civic Data Lab 2024 study: sample-specific, not a national prevalence estimate.
- Options debated: equal age **18**, clearer/equal extended annulment periods, accessible legal aid and timely courts. Suggested **3–5 years** is a reform proposal.
- Pair protection from forced marriage with education through 18, livelihoods/social security, safe healthcare/contraception, sexuality education, counselling and survivor support. Formal equal wording must deliver real agency and access to remedies.
## Prevalence and prevention
- **Women aged 20–24 married before 18**: **47.4% (NFHS-3, 2005–06) → 26.8% (NFHS-4, 2015–16) → 23.3% (NFHS-5, 2019–21)**. The latest interval represents **3.5 percentage points**, not a 3.5% relative reduction. It is a retrospective age-cohort indicator, not the fraction of all marriages occurring in 2025. [Health Ministry annual report](https://www.mohfw.gov.in/sites/default/files/FinalforNetEnglishMoHFW040222_1.pdf).
- NFHS-5 source comparisons: West Bengal, Bihar and Tripura exceed **40%**; Madhya Pradesh **23.1%**, Rajasthan **25.4%**, compared with **32.4%** and **35.4%** in NFHS-4 respectively. Date the data; a recycled global-programme committee visit is not evidence of a new April 2025 visit.
- Poverty, gender norms, school discontinuation, insecurity and weak livelihood options reinforce early marriage. Consequences include curtailed education/employment, reduced agency, violence risk and early pregnancy; adolescent maternal and child nutrition/health require support rather than stigma.
- **SDG target 5.3:** eliminate child, early and forced marriage and female genital mutilation by **2030**. The source's approximately **12 million girls married annually worldwide** is an annual flow, not the stock of all women married as children. [UNICEF data](https://data.unicef.org/topic/child-protection/child-marriage/).
## Measures and limits
- **PCMA 2006** and **POCSO 2012** provide legal protection; combine timely prevention, Child Marriage Prohibition Officers, safe reporting, legal aid and survivor support with schooling, social protection and livelihoods. The source's 2021 proposal to raise women's marriage age to 21 **did not become law**; retain the existing legal-age discussion above.
- **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (2015):** addresses discrimination and girls' survival, protection and education; **Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (2015):** savings for girls' education/future needs, not an unconditional cash grant. Source-listed **Balika Samriddhi Yojana** links assistance with girls' schooling; distinguish an older scheme example from proof of current universal delivery.
- Source image highlights safety/violence, educational loss, reproductive health, psychological burden and violation of childhood rights. Child-help services support rescue/referral; an old **1098** image should not be treated as a complete description of present emergency-response integration.
- **Mains framework:** scale and causes → law/enforcement → education and economic agency → health/social protection → community engagement → implementation gaps and measurable outcomes. The source's 250-word question is undated practice.

topics.title: Milk, dairy cooperatives and nutritional inequality
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Production does not ensure access
- India is the world's largest milk producer; **White Revolution / Operation Flood**, cooperative organisation and **Verghese Kurien** transformed supply and rural livelihoods.
- Milk supplies protein, calcium and micronutrients in many diets; nutritional security also needs dietary diversity, safe food and access. Milk is not compulsory for every person or suitable for every age/allergy.
- January editorial consumption estimates: richest decile **3–4 times** poorest decile; poorest **30% of households consume 18%**. Household surveys can miss consumption outside home; estimates are not the same as national per-capita availability.
- Higher consumption examples **Rajasthan/Punjab/Haryana**, lower **Chhattisgarh/Odisha/West Bengal**; affordability, regional diets and access matter. Source **300 g/day** is a dietary reference, not a universal entitlement.
## Inclusive nutrition policy
- Prioritise children, pregnant/lactating women and vulnerable elderly; locally appropriate supplementary nutrition under **POSHAN/Anganwadi services (ICDS)**. Existing programmes do not guarantee universal daily milk everywhere.
- Reliable State funding, cold chains, quality testing, diversified nutrition, SHG/community engagement; CSR/social bonds are proposed financing additions, not substitutes for public accountability.
- Avoid excess sugar in flavoured milk/processed foods; food choice, lactose intolerance and allergies need consideration. Overnutrition cannot be inferred merely from a person's income.
- Mains: production success → unequal consumption → affordability/service gaps → targeted access and monitoring.
## Question-label caution
- Printed **2012/2018 Prelims** dairy questions and **2014–2023 Mains** list lack confirmed official matches; held for review. The alleged **2019 PM Matsya Sampada** question is especially suspect because the scheme launched in 2020. Do not memorise these as verified PYQs or accept the milk-availability comparison without a year/source.

## Operation Flood and dairy value chains
- **NDDB, 1970**, **Anand cooperative pattern**, **Verghese Kurien**: village procurement → chilling/processing → urban markets; producer incomes and milk self-sufficiency.
| Phase | Historical summary |
|---|---|
| I, 1970–1980 | Donated European milk-powder/butter-oil sales financed infrastructure; 18 milksheds linked to cities |
| II, 1981–1985 | 136 milksheds, 290 urban markets; 43,000 cooperatives, 4.25 million producer members |
| III, 1985–1996 | Procurement, chilling, transport, feed, veterinary care and artificial insemination; 173 milksheds by 1988–89 |
- **Milk and Milk Products Order 1992**, Essential Commodities Act 1955, is historical regulation; do not treat every old provision as the current food-safety regime. Liberalisation expanded private participation; quality testing matters across ownership types.
- Source dairy exports **2022–23: 67,573 tonnes, US$284.65 million**. Its 24% global share (2021–22), 60% decadal production growth, 40% per-capita availability increase and 6% annual growth versus 2% globally are dated estimates. Rajasthan-first state ranking is not timeless.
- Schemes: **AHIDF**, National Programme for Dairy Development, livestock **KCC**, **Rashtriya Gokul Mission**, National Livestock Mission and food-processing infrastructure support; eligibility and sector scopes differ.
- Low yields, feed/veterinary gaps, FMD/Black Quarter, cold chains, adulteration and low producer margins require animal health, scientific breeding, testing, producer bargaining, processing and market access.
- **2015 Mains PYQ:** rural non-farm income/employment potential; include women/smallholders and sustainable husbandry.
- Embedded news trigger: dairy/agriculture market-access differences complicated India–US trade negotiations; producer livelihoods and food standards require attention alongside export opportunities.

## August production update and Gokul Mission recall
- Embedded report: **2023–24 milk output 239.3 million tonnes**; cows **53.12%**, buffaloes **43.62%** of total. Uttar Pradesh led, followed by Rajasthan; the adjacent Rajasthan-first list uses an older ranking. Do not combine years. [DAHD/PIB production confirmation](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2101854&lang=2&reg=48).
- **Rashtriya Gokul Mission** supports scientific development/conservation of indigenous cattle and buffalo breeds and higher productivity; small/marginal farmers and landless households hold many low-yielding animals. **2025 PYQ: both statements (c)**; the image supplies the complete question although text extraction omits it.
- **2015 Mains** livestock question: link non-farm employment/income to feed, veterinary care, breeding, credit, cooperatives, processing and remunerative markets. Operation Flood phases, historical MMPO and dairy constraints repeat existing notes.

topics.title: DR Congo: critical minerals and the resource curse
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Map and minerals
- **Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), capital Kinshasa**, Central Africa; distinguish **Republic of Congo, Brazzaville**. Neighbours: **Angola, Zambia, Tanzania, Burundi, Rwanda, Uganda, South Sudan, Central African Republic, Republic of Congo**; short Atlantic outlet.
| Mineral | Main use / issue |
| --- | --- |
| Cobalt | Many EV/lithium-ion cathodes; aerospace alloys; not every battery chemistry uses cobalt |
| Copper | Wiring, grids, motors |
| Coltan, columbite–tantalite | Tantalum/niobium ore; tantalum capacitors |
| Gold / diamonds | Jewellery, investment / industrial uses; illicit trade risks |
| Tin / tungsten | Solder / hard alloys and specialist industries |
- Source roughly **70% of world cobalt output**; **2023 PYQ says about three-fourths**. Production shares are dated, not fixed reserves or a prediction.
## Conflict and supply chains
- January 2025 eastern DRC conflict around **Goma**, M23 advances; other armed actors include **ADF and Mai-Mai**. Distinguish eastern conflict-mineral networks from all copper/cobalt mines across DRC.
- External ownership, smuggling, weak revenue governance and armed-group finance can create a **resource curse**: wealth fails to deliver welfare. Child labour/unsafe artisanal mining, displacement, forest loss and water/soil pollution require safeguards.
- China-linked firms have major mining/processing interests; US/EU seek diversified clean-tech supply. Responsible Indian partnerships need due diligence and community benefit.
- **Dodd–Frank section 1502** concerns **tin, tantalum, tungsten, gold (3TG)** and covered issuers' disclosure/due diligence; not a generic ban on all DRC minerals or automatic inclusion of cobalt.
- Transparency **EITI**, traceability, accountable royalties, responsible sourcing, regional/UN cooperation, value addition and economic diversification.
## PYQ recall
- **2023** cobalt: DRC **(c)**; Congo Basin country: Cameroon **(a)**. The latter question's other options are Nigeria/South Sudan/Uganda; answer should not imply Uganda is one of the six commonly listed Congo Basin forest countries.
- **2022** news-pairs: Guinea, Lebanon and Tunisia correctly matched; Chad–Chinese permanent base wrong → **only three pairs (c)**.

## August 2025: African resource nationalism
- Governments/civil society seek higher local value, skills, infrastructure, environmental safeguards and transparent revenues from critical-mineral investment. **Sicomines** exemplifies DRC resources-for-infrastructure exchange; tax concessions, delivery and commodity-linked returns require scrutiny.
- Source examples: Zimbabwe's **2022** raw-lithium restrictions; Namibia's **2023** unprocessed-critical-mineral restrictions; mining/environment controversies in **Hwange(Zimbabwe), Kafue River(Zambia), Lobé–Kribi(Cameroon)** and allegations concerning Namibia's **Xinfeng**. Distinguish allegations, project decisions and nationwide bans; do not treat all African countries as one legal regime.
- Local **beneficiation** needs reliable energy/transport, processing technology, finance and skills, plus accountable contracts/community safeguards. Raw-export bans alone can strand projects rather than guarantee manufacturing.
- Source DRC **~80%global cobalt**, Chinese control **~80%of DRC output**, **US$132 million2024 tax loss**, and **32%→70% State stakes** lack common denominators/project identification. Keep these as source claims requiring verification; do not infer a completed nationwide ownership change. Existing dated cobalt-share notes remain qualified.
- India: diversify battery/clean-tech inputs through joint processing, capacity building and responsible South–South investment; competition, political risk, pollution and community consent matter.
- **2025 PYQ:** **Botswana–diamond; Chile–lithium; Indonesia–nickel** all match→**(c)**. Botswana's **Orapa/Jwaneng** mines, Chile's **Atacama** brines/Lithium Triangle and Indonesian downstream nickel policy aid map recall. The daily250-word15-mark Africa prompt is practice.

topics.title: NavIC, NVS-02 and satellite navigation
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Navigation fundamentals
- **NavIC, Navigation with Indian Constellation**, previously **IRNSS**; regional **position/velocity/time** services over India and roughly **1,500 km beyond**.
- Original architecture **7 satellites: 3 geostationary + 4 inclined geosynchronous**. All geostationary orbits are geosynchronous; inclined ones do not stay above one ground point. Design count ≠ number healthy/operational on any date.
- **SPS** civilian and **Restricted Service** authorised/strategic; stated service-area accuracy **better than 20 m**, timing **better than 40 ns**, under specified conditions.
- Other systems: **GPS—US; GLONASS—Russia; Galileo—EU; BeiDou—China; QZSS—Japan**. Interoperability ≠ all systems having identical coverage.
## January 29 launch and later clarification
- **GSLV-F15** inserted **NVS-02**, second NVS-series satellite, into intended **geosynchronous transfer orbit**, on **29 January 2025**, **100th launch from Sriharikota** (not ISRO's 100th mission overall).
- GSLV three stages, indigenous upper cryogenic stage; **Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Andhra Pradesh**. Agency established **15 August 1969**, roots in **INCOSPAR 1962**, Bengaluru HQ.
- Source **1979 SLV-3 experimental flight** failed to reach orbit; first successful SLV-3 orbital launch **18 July 1980**. Sriharikota launch history is wider than SLV-3 alone.
- **2 February 2025 ISRO update**: launch successful, but oxidiser valves did not open for orbit raising; satellite in elliptical orbit, alternative strategies considered. Launch insertion ≠ operational placement in final slot. [ISRO mission and update](https://www.isro.gov.in/GSLV-F15_NVS-02_Mission.html).
## PYQ traps
- **2023** own satellite-navigation system among Australia/Canada/Israel/Japan → **Japan (d)**.
- **2018 IRNSS**: statement 1 correct; **5,500 sq km** boundary claim and promised worldwide coverage by mid-2019 wrong → **1 only (a)**, correcting source key **(b)**.
- Printed **2007 Galileo**: EU multi-satellite navigation project; full official wording/year retained for verification before JSON inclusion.

## July 2025 replenishment plan
- **23 July parliamentary reply**: **NVS-03 planned by end 2025**, NVS-04/05 at approximately six-month intervals. Source's 2026 completion was a schedule expectation, not evidence all launches occurred. [Space Department reply](https://www.pib.gov.in/Press Release Page.aspx?PRID=2147284&lang=2&reg=48).
- Source snapshot: **11 launched including IRNSS-1 H launch failure**, one retired, four navigation-capable, four usable for one-way messaging, plus NVS-02 orbit-raising problem. Constellation design, satellites launched and satellites providing navigation are different counts. Atomic-clock health affects ranging; message broadcasting can remain useful for disaster alerts.
- GPS timing synchronises **mobile networks, banking transactions and power grids** in addition to locating users;2018 applications PYQ includes all three. Old infographic's constellation sizes/accuracy are historical, not a fresh 2025 global inventory.

topics.title: Critical minerals, processing and supply-chain security
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Criticality and uses
- Critical = economic/strategic importance plus supply vulnerability; lists vary by country/time. Mineral occurrence, inferred **resource**, economically recoverable **reserve**, mined output and refining capacity are different.
| Mineral / material | Uses |
| --- | --- |
| Lithium, cobalt, nickel | Many battery chemistries; chemistry-specific demand |
| Graphite | Common lithium-ion anodes |
| Neodymium, dysprosium | Permanent magnets for some EV motors/wind turbines |
| Copper | Electricity networks/electronics |
| Vanadium | Steel alloys / flow batteries |
| Aluminium | Transport/construction/aerospace; strategic use alone does not automatically put it on India's critical list |
- China's extraction and especially processing concentration creates exposure; it does **not** dominate mining of every mineral. DRC cobalt and Australia/lithium-brine countries illustrate different mining locations.
- India has **rare-earth-bearing monazite and other mineral resources**; source's blanket absence of domestic rare earths/cobalt/lithium is misleading. Reasi lithium **inferred resource** is not an operating mine or proven commercial reserve; unverified Rajasthan reserve headlines require caution.
## Response across the value chain
- Explore and assess geology; efficient permitting with social/environmental safeguards; domestic refining/separation and skilled workforce; diversify contracts/overseas assets; strategic stockpiles; recycling/e-waste recovery and material substitution.
- **29 January 2025 NCMM approval**, **2024–25 to 2030–31**: government outlay **₹16, 300 crore**, expected PSU/other investment **₹18, 000 crore**. Cover exploration → mining → processing → recovery, including overseas partnerships and reserves. Expected investment ≠ public budget already spent. [Cabinet release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2097309&lang=2&reg=48).
- **30 minerals** identified in India's 2023 report; legal schedule categories and that policy list are distinct. FTAs/Quad cooperation can support access, but source's January discussion of EU FTA should not be read as an agreement then in force.
## Beach minerals and PYQs
- **Ilmenite / rutile → titanium**; **monazite → rare earths + thorium**, not present in all Indian coastal sand. **2023 titanium (d)**; **2022 monazite statements 1, 2, 4 (b)**.
- Monazite's radioactivity invokes special controls; question's legal position is tied to exam year. Source's lithium question labelled 2023 has no confirmed paper match and is held for review.
## Ukraine mineral negotiations
- February 2025 US–Ukraine minerals arrangement was under negotiation; agreement was signed later, 30 April 2025. A resource deal does not automatically provide a defence guarantee.
- Distinguish geological resources from economically recoverable reserves, and mining shares from refining shares. Occupied-resource valuations in the source are dated estimates.

## Exploration licences: March 2025
- Auction launch covered 13 exploration blocks; the exploration-licence framework arose from the 2023 amendment to MMDR Act 1957.
- It covers specified deep-seated minerals, including copper, zinc, platinum-group minerals and diamonds; it is not limited to rare earths.
- Licence areas may extend up to 1,000 sq km under the framework. **Exploration permission is not automatic permission to mine**; subsequent leases, environmental approvals and applicable land/forest requirements remain separate.
- Auctions and revenue-sharing incentives can mobilise risk capital; transparent information, competition, local interests and ecological safeguards determine outcomes.

## April 2025: Kazakhstan rare-earth exploration
- **Kuirektykol, Karaganda region, Kazakhstan:** reported exploration estimates of roughly **one million tonnes** of rare-earth metals; the wider Zhana Kazakhstan area's potential was projected at about **20 million tonnes**. These are reported resource/potential estimates, **not certified economically recoverable reserves** or proof of the world's largest operating deposit.
- Identified elements include **cerium, lanthanum, neodymium and yttrium**. The reported average concentration was about **700 g/tonne**; richer zones reached approximately **0.25%**. Grade, recovery, costs and environmental constraints determine commercial viability. [Karaganda regional government](https://www.gov.kz/memleket/entities/karaganda/press/news/details/967871?lang=ru).
- **Rare earths = 15 lanthanides + scandium + yttrium (17)**. They need difficult separation/refining; geological occurrence alone does not create a reliable supply chain.
- Uses include electronics, catalysts, defence systems and permanent magnets in some EV motors/wind turbines. **Lithium is not a rare earth; not every battery or renewable technology uses rare earths.**
- Kazakhstan's significance is prospective supply diversification. Foreign investment, processing technology, infrastructure and responsible extraction remain essential; discovery does not immediately displace China's established processing role.
- India–Kazakhstan uranium/civil-nuclear links provide a base for mineral cooperation. India's coastal monazite resources also contain rare earths; distinguish domestic resources from processing scale and usable supply.

## 4 April 2025: Chinese rare-earth export controls
- **MOFCOM/Customs Announcement No.18 of 2025**, effective 4 April, introduced licensing for specified medium/heavy rare-earth-related items: **samarium (Sm), gadolinium (Gd), terbium (Tb), dysprosium (Dy), lutetium (Lu), scandium (Sc), yttrium (Y)** and listed forms/products.
- It was an **export-control/permit regime**, not a blanket prohibition on all 17 rare earths, nor a measure confined to shipments to India. The source's “2024” date is incorrect. [Official announcement](https://english.mofcom.gov.cn/Policies/AnnouncementsOrders/art/2025/art_0dd87cbee7b045bf93fabe6ab2faceee.html).
- Delayed authorisations and concentrated separation/magnet production expose vehicle, renewable-energy and defence supply chains even where alternative ores exist. India's strategic task includes usable separated materials and components, beyond geological resources alone.
- Source's coastal example mixes coasts: **Kerala is on India's western coast**; Tamil Nadu and Odisha include eastern-coast monazite deposits. Avoid treating all domestic reserves as readily available heavy-rare-earth supply.

## April 23 revision additions: implementation and applications
- GSI's **1,200 critical-mineral exploration projects for 2024–25 to 2030–31** are a mission target, not completed discoveries or producing mines. [PIB, 9 April 2025](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressNoteDetails.aspx?ModuleId=3&NoteId=154178&lang=1&reg=3).
- Rare-earth uses also include catalysts, specialist alloys and medical technologies: **gadolinium** in some MRI contrast agents and particular isotopes of **yttrium/lutetium** in treatment. Application is element-, isotope- and technology-specific; “all REEs used in all semiconductors/solar panels” is too broad.
- Source's **2,270-tonne 2023–24 imports** and **6% reserve share** need defined commodity/year denominators; do not equate mineral/compound import weight with separated elemental supply or economic reserves with total resources.
- Japan's response to the **2010 supply shock** offers a diversification lesson: alternative sourcing, recycling/substitution and stockpiles; source's exact “months-long” buffer is not a universal adequacy rule.

## May 2025: germanium supply and export-control chronology
- Indian Embassy in Beijing told the source it was engaging China through communications/meetings on **germanium** restrictions; the RTI response identified that particular industry concern. It does not establish successful supply restoration or absence of every rare-earth risk.
- **Germanium (Ge), atomic number 32:** metalloid; **gallium (Ga), 31:** soft post-transition metal, melting near room temperature. Neither is one of the 17 rare earths. Discovery recall: **Ge—Clemens Winkler, 1886; Ga—Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran, 1875**.
- Ge/GeO2: optical-fibre glass preforms, infrared optics/night vision, specialised semiconductors and space-grade solar cells. GaAs/GaN: RF/power electronics, LEDs, radar/communications; gallium also enters CIGS photovoltaics. Do not infer every ordinary solar module or every green-hydrogen plant requires these materials.
- Generally recovered as by-products: **Ge from zinc-processing and some coal-related sources; Ga from bauxite/alumina processing and some zinc routes**. Supply hinges on recovery/refining, not only standalone mines; China's concentration creates vulnerability. Source's crustal abundance/production shares mix definitions/years and should not be memorised as current refining totals.
- **3 July 2023 announcement, effective 1 August 2023:** China introduced licensing for listed Ga/Ge-related exports—not 2022. [MOFCOM](https://english.mofcom.gov.cn/News/PressConference/art/2023/art_36fb2d80e4b4453891bb8fc83e2b3c4e.html).
- **3 December 2024, Announcement 46:** tightened listed dual-use exports to **US**, including in-principle nonpermission for Ga/Ge/antimony/superhard-material exports and stricter graphite review. This is not a late-2023 worldwide ban applying identically to India. [Official notice](https://www.mofcom.gov.cn/zwgk/zcfb/art/2024/art_3d5e990b43424e60828030f58a547b60.html).
- Source reports Indian import reliance/UAE sourcing and higher costs; transshipment country is not necessarily country of primary production. Its blanket “no domestic production” needs commodity-specific confirmation. Foxconn personnel/equipment delays do not establish officially confirmed retaliation.
- Diversify suppliers and contracts, assess domestic by-product recovery/recycling, strategic buffers and substitution, and deepen processing skills/technology partnerships. Listed potential supplier countries do not prove immediately available export capacity or signed deals.
- Existing **NCMM approved January 2025** supersedes the source's “critical-minerals strategy merely proposed” wording. Do not retrospectively label a future **Quad Critical Minerals Initiative** as already launched in May; general Quad/iCET cooperation is separate.

## June 2025: rare-earth applications and constraints
- **Europium/terbium/yttrium compounds** form display phosphors; lanthanum enters optical glass and petroleum-refining catalysts; cerium enters catalytic converters/polishing and selected water-treatment materials. Lanthanum alloys occur in **nickel-metal-hydride batteries**, not every EV battery.
- **Mischmetal** commonly contains cerium, lanthanum, neodymium and praseodymium; used in alloys/steelmaking. **Bastnaesite, xenotime and loparite** complement monazite as REE-bearing minerals.
- Indian deposits are predominantly light rare earths; coastal monazite occurrences are geographically uneven, with inland occurrences too. IREL (India) Ltd under DAE undertakes mining/separation; downstream magnet capacity remains a constraint.
- The June source reports instructions to prioritise domestic rare-earth needs over sales to Japan. Its **China 90–95% production** wording confuses stages: mining and separation/processing are distinct; do not memorise it as mined-output share. Its universal **2,000 tonnes toxic waste per tonne REE** lacks a defined process/system boundary and is held for review.
- 2025 PYQ: rare-earth phosphorescent properties explain display applications (**a**). 2022 monazite: statements **1,2,4 (b)**; monazite is not distributed throughout all Indian coastal sands.

## Rare-earth permanent magnets
- **NdFeB (neodymium–iron–boron):** high magnetic strength, widely used in motors/electronics. **SmCo (samarium–cobalt):** useful where high-temperature stability/corrosion resistance matter. These are permanent-magnet families, not interchangeable names for all rare-earth minerals.
- Dependence on Chinese separation/processing and magnet manufacture can disrupt auto-component and clean-technology supply chains. Industry proposals for stockpiles, domestic processing and incentives require environmental safeguards and viable production links; a proposal is not an operational stockpile.
- Medical-imaging examples need qualification: some MRI designs use permanent magnets, while many use superconducting electromagnets. China's processing dominance must not be confused with exclusive worldwide mineral occurrence.

## Rajasthan rare-earth reporting: July 2025
- Source identifies **Balotra and Jalore** occurrences and REE-bearing **bastnaesite, britholite and xenotime**. Balotra is a separate Rajasthan district created from Barmer; “Balotra in Barmer district” is administratively outdated.
- Exploration indications/auction proposals are not certified commercially recoverable reserves or immediate magnet supply. Ore grade, separation technology, infrastructure, investment and radioactive/waste safeguards determine viability.
- PDF's **₹1,000-crore rare-earth-magnet incentive** should be treated as a July proposal/report, not an established operational PLI scheme on this evidence. Geological reserves ranking, mining share and processing share must be tied to year/definition; they are not interchangeable.

topics.title: Major and minor minerals: classification and map recall
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Legal distinction
- **MMDR Act 1957, section 3(e)** defines minor minerals: building stones, gravel, ordinary clay, ordinary sand except prescribed uses, and others notified by Centre. It is a **legal classification**, not simply low output/value or a small mine. [Act](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/20096/1/a1957-67.pdf).
- State rules regulate minor-mineral concessions under **section 15**; central notification determines additional minor minerals. Source's attribution solely to **MCR 1960** and inclusion of all gemstones/asbestos as minor are unreliable; diamond is not minor just because it is a gemstone.
- **As at January 2025** mica/quartz/barytes were minor. **20 February 2025 notification** subsequently moved **barytes, felspar, mica, quartz to major**; preserve that date when revising. [Ministry announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2105215&lang=2&reg=48).
## Mineral–location–use recall
| Mineral | Key examples | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Coal | Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal, MP, Telangana | Power/steel |
| Iron ore | Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Goa | Steel |
| Bauxite | Odisha, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Maharashtra, MP, Chhattisgarh | Aluminium |
| Manganese | Odisha, MP, Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka | Steel/batteries |
| Limestone | Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, AP, Gujarat | Cement/flux |
| Copper | Rajasthan–Khetri; MP–Malanjkhand; Jharkhand–Singhbhum | Conductors |
| Gold | Karnataka–Hutti; AP and other occurrences | Jewellery/investment |
| Lead/zinc | Rajasthan, including Zawar | Batteries/galvanising |
| Salt | Gujarat, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, AP | Food/chemical industry |
| Chromite | Odisha–Sukinda | Stainless-steel ferrochrome |
| Mica | Jharkhand/Bihar/Rajasthan | Insulation/electronics |
| Marble | Rajasthan, MP, Gujarat | Decorative stone |
| Barytes | AP–Mangampeta | Drilling-fluid weighting |
- Sand/gravel construction; clay bricks/tiles; kaolin ceramics; talc cosmetics/filler; garnet abrasive/filter; quartz glass/electronics; chalk writing/industry; perlite expanded volcanic glass for horticulture/insulation. Asbestos fibres pose serious inhalation hazards; industrial use does not imply safety.
- State lists indicate important examples/occurrences, not exclusive locations, present mining status or equal production shares.

topics.title: Fiscal Health Index and State finances
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Index structure
- **NITI Aayog, inaugural FHI 2025**, released **24 January 2025** by 16th Finance Commission chair; covers **18 major States**, using **FY 2022–23** and CAG data, not every State/UT or the current fiscal year. [Release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2095974&lang=2&reg=48).
| Pillar | Recall indicators |
| --- | --- |
| Quality of expenditure | Development/capital spending; social/economic services |
| Revenue mobilisation | Own tax/non-tax revenue and own-revenue financing |
| Fiscal prudence | Fiscal/revenue deficit patterns |
| Debt index | Debt burden and interest commitments |
| Debt sustainability | Growth–interest relation and debt trajectory |
## FY 2022–23 ranking in 2025 report
- **Achievers**: Odisha **67.8**, Chhattisgarh **55.2**, Goa **53.6**, Jharkhand **51.6**, Gujarat **50.5**.
- **Front-runners**: Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Telangana, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka.
- **Performers**: Tamil Nadu, Bihar, Rajasthan, Haryana.
- **Aspirational**: Kerala **25.4**, West Bengal **21.8**, Andhra Pradesh **20.9**, Punjab **10.7**; latter worst, Haryana **27.4** just above this group.
- Report-relative category ≠ permanent State label. Improve own revenues, expenditure quality and credible debt management; comparisons need structural context, not a single rank.
- Practice trap: 18 major States / CAG / five pillars, not all UTs or exclusively Finance Ministry data. Index source year matters when later editions are added.

topics.title: Pangsau Pass, Stilwell Road and border culture
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Location and heritage
- **Patkai Hills, India–Myanmar border**, near **Nampong, Changlang district, Arunachal Pradesh**; source altitude about **1,136 m / 3,727 ft**. Named after nearby Myanmar village Pangsau.
- Route connects Assam plains toward Myanmar; **Lake of No Return** lies on Myanmar side. Difficult terrain gave nicknames **Hell Pass / Hell Gate**.
- Associated with the reputed route of **13th-century Ahom migration into Assam**, not an independently proved modern border route for every historical account.
- **World War II Stilwell/Ledo Road**, associated with General **Joseph “Vinegar Joe” Stilwell**, connected Allied supply routes toward China after Japanese occupation of Burma.
- **Pangsau Pass International Festival**, Nampong: India–Myanmar cultural contact, tourism and trade; source calls it annual, but recurrence does not prove it was held uninterrupted every year.
- Map recall: Arunachal → Patkai border pass → Myanmar → Lake of No Return; not Western Ghats/Aravallis.

topics.title: Blue carbon and coastal wetland protection
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Carbon storage
- Carbon captured/stored by ocean/coastal ecosystems; key **coastal vegetated sinks: mangroves, salt marshes, seagrass meadows**. Carbon stored in vegetation and especially sediments. [NOAA](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/bluecarbon.html).
- Source's **10-times terrestrial-forest rate** describes a comparison of relevant coastal habitats, not a universal rate for all oceans/reefs or equal carbon stocks everywhere.
- Coral reefs are biodiversity-rich but **not included among the standard three coastal blue-carbon habitats** in the practice question; carbon sequestration and carbonate formation differ.
## Services and threats
- Climate mitigation + coastal protection + nurseries/fisheries/food security + adaptation.
- Conversion for aquaculture/agriculture, destructive harvesting, pollution and urban/industrial reclamation threaten stored carbon and livelihoods; degradation may release carbon.
- Protect existing habitats, restore suitable hydrology, prevent pollution and measure long-term carbon/benefits; poorly placed plantations do not replace functioning seagrass or marsh ecosystems.

topics.title: Deep Ocean Mission and Samudrayaan
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mission and components
- **Ministry of Earth Sciences**, multi-institutional Central Sector mission, Cabinet-approved **2021**, estimated **₹4,077 crore**, two phases over initial **2021–2026** period.
- Six components: **deep-sea mining/submersible/robotics; ocean climate advisories; biodiversity exploration/conservation technology; deep-ocean survey; ocean energy/freshwater; advanced marine station for ocean biology**.
- **Samudrayaan** manned-submersible component: **Matsya 6000**, intended **three people to 6,000 m**, scientific sensors. Design/testing milestone ≠ completed crewed 6-km operational dive.
- Supports **blue economy** knowledge/technology; living and non-living resource assessment must consider fragile deep-sea habitats, sediment plumes and international rules.
- Graphic contrasts shallow human diving and deep engineering; pressure rises with depth, requiring a strong pressure sphere, life support, communications and recovery systems. Mission is wider than mineral extraction alone.

topics.title: Paraquat: herbicide toxicity and regulation
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Toxicity
- **Paraquat**, methyl viologen, commonly paraquat dichloride; herbicide for weeds/grass, also agricultural desiccation in permitted uses. Not a fertiliser.
- **WHO hazard Class II**, source “moderately hazardous”; classification does **not** make swallowing safe. Regulatory restriction differs from a toxicological class.
- Ingestion can cause severe mouth/GI injury and lung, kidney, liver/heart damage, seizures and respiratory failure. Longer/stronger skin exposure, especially broken skin, can poison; inhalation/eye exposure also harms. [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/chemical-emergencies/chemical-fact-sheets/paraquat.html).
- **No proven antidote/cure**; urgent specialist treatment and supportive care. Source mentions charcoal haemoperfusion/immunosuppression as clinical approaches, not guaranteed effective cures or self-treatment instructions.
## Regulation and January context
- January 2025 Kerala poisoning-case sentencing brought attention to access and handling; trial judgment ≠ proof appeal outcomes are final.
- Source says banned in **70+ countries**; country counts/date/meaning of ban vary. EU/China restrictions and **US restricted-use licensing** illustrate different regimes; source's “banned in India” practice distractor is false in its January account.
- Safe storage, access control, training, labelling and poisoning surveillance matter; occupational and intentional exposures require distinct prevention measures.

topics.title: Titan arum: corpse-flower pollination
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Identity and life cycle
- **Amorphophallus titanum**, correcting PDF **“titanium”**; Titan arum / **Bunga bangkai**, native to **Sumatra, Indonesia**, IUCN **Endangered**. January Sydney flowering specimen **Putricia** drew large crowds.
- **Inflorescence**, not one giant individual flower: **spadix** bears many small flowers, enclosed by a purple **spathe**. May reach about **3 m**; bloom brief, roughly **24–48 hours**, interval variable and sometimes many years.
- Underground **corm** stores energy built through leaf cycles; bloom needs adequate reserves, not a fixed once-yearly/once-decade clock.
- Female flowers receptive **before male pollen release**, reducing self-pollination; carrion smell/heat attracts **flies and beetles**, encouraging pollen transfer. [US Botanic Garden](https://www.usbg.gov/gardens-plants/corpse-flowers).
- Source volatile list: **dimethyl disulfide/trisulfide, methanethiol, methyl thioacetate, 3-methylbutanal, isovaleric acid**; odour is a mixture, not a single compound.
- Botanical propagation/pollen exchange helps conserve genetic diversity; rare garden bloom does not imply natural population recovery.

topics.title: IWAI and inland-waterway infrastructure
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Institution and routes
- **Inland Waterways Authority of India Act 1985**; IWAI established **27 October 1986**, HQ **Noida**, **Ports, Shipping and Waterways Ministry**. Develops/maintains navigation infrastructure on national waterways.
- **23 January 2025**, Varanasi sub-office upgraded to Regional Office for **NW-1, Ganga** and Uttar Pradesh waterways; sixth Regional Office alongside **Guwahati, Patna, Kochi, Bhubaneswar, Kolkata** in source snapshot. [Ministry release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2095758&lang=2&reg=48).
- Source jurisdiction: **Betwa, Chambal, Gomti, Tons, Varuna**, parts of **Gandak, Ghaghra, Karamnasa, Yamuna**, coordination with UP State IWT Authority. Naming a river ≠ every reach already commercially navigable.
- Benefit depends on fairway depth, terminals, last-mile freight, seasonal flows and ecological safeguards; inland shipping is not automatically feasible on every tributary.

topics.title: White-naped tit and dry scrub habitat
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Identification
- **Machlolophus nuchalis**, family **Paridae**, passerine; endemic to India, source IUCN **Vulnerable**.
- Disjunct northwestern (**Gujarat/Rajasthan and source Haryana**) and southern (**AP/Karnataka/Tamil Nadu**) distribution; **dry thorn scrub** habitat.
- Black upperparts, white nape/upper-mantle patch, white cheeks/underparts with central black band, white wing patch; pairs/small groups, identifiable calls.
- January report first documented occurrence in **Kappatagudda hills, North Karnataka**; new local record ≠ new species or first record anywhere in Karnataka.
- Habitat loss/fragmentation matters; do not substitute wetland/evergreen-rainforest habitat in recall questions.

topics.title: Epicoccum indicum and plant-pathogenic fungi
