- Invest in skills, rigorous research, hardware validation and post-quantum cryptographic transition; count useful logical performance, not physical qubits alone.
- **2022 PYQ: “qubit” →quantum computing**, not cloud, visible-light or wireless communication.
- [Cabinet approval of NQM](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1917888&lang=2&reg=48) confirms outlay and2023–31 period.

topics.title: Global talent shortages and India’s skilled-migration opportunity
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Opportunity and projections
- Source study forecasts **85.2 million global skilled-worker shortfall /US$8.45 trillion unrealised annual revenue by2030**; scenario estimates, not a guaranteed market India can capture in full.
- GCC: construction/manufacturing/healthcare; Europe/UK: healthcare/services; Australia: technology/services/resource efficiency. Demand depends on sector, qualifications, language and immigration policy.
- Skills shortages can coexist with domestic unemployment when competencies/locations differ; a young population does not automatically imply ready internationally employable workers.
## Barriers and safeguards
- Qualification/licence recognition, visas, language, recruitment costs and employer exploitation/trafficking; source blanket “no hostility abroad /Australia always open” is unreliable.
- Mutual-recognition agreements do not automatically license every profession; health professionals need applicable country standards.
- **Skill India, NSDC, PMKVY**, bilateral mobility/worker-protection agreements and transparent recruitment systems can support lawful placement.
- Train to verified demand, regulate recruiters, provide clear contracts/consular assistance, expand language/professional preparation and track placement/earnings.
- Circular migration/remittances and returnee skills can help; balance overseas opportunity with domestic healthcare/skill needs and avoid brain-drain assumptions without evidence.
- Source **US$6.5–9 trillion India GDP2030** is an economic forecast attributed to a speaker, not an achieved outcome or assured benefit from overseas labour demand.

topics.title: Unapproved drug combinations and pharmaceutical-export ethics
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Action and correction
- **Tapentadol:** opioid analgesic; **carisoprodol:** centrally acting muscle relaxant. Individually approved products do **not** make their fixed-dose combination approved.
- February 2025 action followed reports of Aveo exports to West Africa: stop activities, withdraw export NOCs and act on unauthorised manufacturing permissions. **Joint audit21–22 February 2025**, not PDF's2024. [Health Ministry23 February release](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/erelcontent.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=267822).
- Official source reports **~1.3 crore tablets/capsules /26 API batches** and wider inspections **905 units /694 actions**; separate seizure from concluded criminal guilt and inspection from permanent closure.
- Addiction/misuse and combined CNS effects are public-health concerns; whether a drug is listed under NDPS is different from whether it is regulated under drug law.
## Institutions and ethics
- **CDSCO**, national regulator under **MoHFW**, New Delhi; headed by **DCGI**. New drugs/trials/imports/standards and specified categories involve central powers; State regulators have important manufacturing/sale enforcement roles.
- **Drugs and Cosmetics Act1940 /Rules /New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules2019**; devices use their relevant framework. No single officer personally issues every drug licence in India.
- Safe exports require approvals/quality, traceability, importing-country coordination and ethical marketing. Weaker enforcement abroad does not justify exporting unsafe/unapproved combinations.
- Risk-based joint inspections, authentic supply-chain data, recalls/enforcement with due process and international alerts protect patients and India's pharmaceutical credibility.
- Proposal to add substances to NDPS is not proof notification occurred; do not confuse action against this combination with a blanket ban on every lawful standalone product.

topics.title: Source segregation and the municipal waste chain
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Segregation and treatment
- **Source segregation:** separate wet/biodegradable, dry/recyclable and **domestic hazardous** waste; special biomedical/e-waste streams follow appropriate rules.
- Keep streams separate in collection/transport; segregating at home achieves little if mixed again in the truck.
| Stream | Appropriate route |
| --- | --- |
| Suitable wet organics | Composting/biomethanation with contamination controls |
| Dry recyclables | Recovery/recycling through authorised systems |
| Non-recyclable high-calorific residues | Suitable controlled energy recovery, not indiscriminate burning |
| Hazardous/inert/process residues | Appropriate authorised treatment/engineered disposal |
- Benefits: less landfill methane/leachate, better recycling, safer workers and resource recovery; treatment may still generate residues/emissions.
## Rules and programmes
- Source-era **SWM Rules2016**, **Plastic Waste Rules2016/EPR**, **SBM-U2.0** and **SATAT** compressed-biogas support. **2022 SUP ban targets listed products**, not every single-use plastic object.
- Producers' responsibility and municipal obligations differ; blanket plastic/e-waste EPR cannot be attributed solely to SWM Rules.
- **Indore** collection/biogas, **Pune SWaCH** waste-picker integration, **Alappuzha** decentralised composting illustrate approaches; source's30,000-Pune-worker and100%-zero-waste claims require verification.
## Data and governance
- Source **~160,000 tonnes/day generated /79,000 processed /3,159 dumpsites /14 WTE plants**, composition and city segregation shares are mixed dated estimates; not a harmonised current national inventory.
- Sweden's “99% recycling” often conflates material recycling with energy recovery; international segregation, treatment and landfill percentages are different metrics.
- Awareness plus reliable separate collection, ULB capacity, user fees/enforcement, EPR accountability, decentralised organics treatment and dignified waste-worker inclusion.
- WTE is not an automatic answer for high-moisture mixed waste; technology choices need feedstock, pollution control, costs and maintained operation.

topics.title: Social protection, informal workers and the ILO
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Coverage and dimensions
- Source **24%→49%** rounds the reported **24.4%2021 →48.8%2024** coverage under **at least one social-protection benefit**; not proof everyone covered has comprehensive protection. [Official clarification](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2115391&lang=2&reg=3).
- **Social insurance**: contributory risk protection; **social assistance**: tax-financed support; labour-market programmes support income/work. Adequacy, timely payment and actual access matter with enrolment.
- **e-Shram2021**, worker database; registration is not automatic pension/insurance entitlement. DBT can improve delivery but is **not inherently leakage-free** or free from exclusion.
- **PM-KISAN₹6,000/year**, eligible **PM-JAY** hospital cover, **APY** contributory pension and **MGNREGA100 days per rural household demanding unskilled work**—not100days guaranteed to every individual regardless of demand.
- February 2025 Labour Codes enacted but not all implemented; recognition of gig/platform workers did **not automatically make every gig worker an insured ESIC beneficiary**. Scheme announcement, registration and benefit receipt differ.
## ILO recall
- **1919, Treaty of Versailles; Geneva; UN specialised agency1946**. India member since **28 June 1919**, correcting PDF's1920. [ILO country profile](https://normlex.ilo.org/dyn/nrmlx_en/f?p=NORMLEXPUB%3A11110%3A0%3A%3ANO%3A%3AP11110_COUNTRY_ID%3A102691).
- **Tripartite: governments, employers, workers**; International Labour Conference sets standards; Governing Body executive oversight.
- Reports: **World Employment and Social Outlook, Global Wage Report, World Social Protection Report2024–26, India Wage Report2018**.
- India ratified **C100 equal remuneration, C138 minimum age, C182 worst child labour**; source-era **C87/C98** not ratified. Ratification and domestic implementation are distinct; total convention count changes with time.
- Source187members/DG **GilbertF.Houngbo** are dated institutional facts, not permanent constitutional rules. Cross-country49/70/90/100coverage table lacks comparable definitions.
## Reform
- Informal earnings, digital barriers, gender gaps and portability complicate coverage; reliable funding, outreach, grievance redress and linked schemes are needed.
- Measure effective benefits, adequacy/equity and shock resilience; protect workers through formalisation without assuming informal work means no employment.

topics.title: Right to Information: transparency, privacy and implementation
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Statutory framework: revision points
- The right to know is derived from **Article 19(1)(a)**; *State of UP v Raj Narain* was decided in **1975**, not 1976. **RTI Act 2005** supplies the request/disclosure machinery.
- **Section 2(h):** constitutional/statutory/notified public authorities; bodies owned, controlled or substantially financed by government, including substantially financed NGOs. Not every private organisation is directly covered.
- **Section 4:** record management/proactive disclosure; **6:** request procedure; **7:** response timelines; **8:** exemptions/public-interest balance; **19:** first and second appeals; **20:** penalties; **23:** statutory court bar.
- Ordinary request normally **30 days**, life/liberty **48 hours**. Information Commission may impose **₹250 per day, maximum ₹25,000**, on the PIO under section 20 after the statutory process; penalty is not automatically deducted whenever a reply arrives late.
- Applicant need not explain why information is wanted. RTI covers existing information/records rather than requiring officials to create a new analysis or answer hypothetical questions.
- Exemptions include protected national-security/foreign-relations material, commercial confidence/IP where competitive interests would be harmed, confidential sources, investigation impediments and specified Cabinet records. These are qualified statutory tests—not a blanket exemption for every document touching those subjects.
- **Section 8(2)** permits disclosure where public interest outweighs protected harm, notwithstanding the Official Secrets Act/exemptions; **section 10** allows severing exempt portions.
- Appeal within the department → **CIC/SIC** second appeal; commissions also have complaint functions. PIOs/public authorities give information in the first instance, not only commissions.
- Section 23 does not eliminate constitutional judicial review: **Supreme Court Article 32 / High Court Article 226**, not Article 225. [DoPT RTI Act](https://rti.dopt.gov.in/).
## Disclosure–privacy balance
- **CBSE v.Aditya Bandopadhyay2011:** recognised access to evaluated answer-books while discussing practical limits; not a judgment simply eliminating transparency or every student's access.
- **Girish Ramchandra Deshpande2012:** personal/service information and demonstrated larger public interest; disclosure debate needs facts and applicable law, not an assumption no public official has privacy.
- Source-era parliamentary-information proviso matters, but does not justify skipping all other statutory/contextual analysis.
## Amendments: specify status
- **2019 amendment** changed service-condition control for Information Commissioners; institutional-independence concerns differ from content exemptions.
- **DPDP Act2023 section44(3)** legislated replacement of8(1)(j)'s personal-information wording; **not operative in February 2025 merely because enacted**. Distinguish that historical discussion from later commencement/notifications.
- Reforms proposed in the editorial—reverse amendments, strengthen penalties/new protection laws—are proposals, not existing provisions.
## Improve access
- Timely transparent appointments, diverse expertise, digitised records and accessible tracking; publish reasons, enforce existing non-compliance penalties and protect applicants.
- Proactive disclosure reduces repetitive requests; exemptions must be lawful/proportionate and appellate oversight timely. Compare case-disposal figures cautiously; different institutions have unlike case complexity.

topics.title: PUNCH: mapping the solar wind
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mission recall
- **Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere**, NASA; four small spacecraft in low Earth orbit: one Narrow Field Imager coronagraph and three Wide Field Imagers.
- Polarised sunlight scattered by electrons helps reconstruct the corona–solar-wind transition in 3D; track coronal mass ejections and space-weather evolution.
- Complements Parker Solar Probe's in-situ measurements and Aditya-L1 observations; a remote map is different from directly sampling plasma.
- February launch plans changed: launched with SPHEREx on 11 March 2025 California time, 12MarchUTC. [NASA](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-launches-missions-to-study-sun-universes-beginning/).

topics.title: Maternity benefits and delivery gaps
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Law and schemes
- **NFSA2013 section 4:** maternity benefit of not less than₹6, 000, subject to specified exclusions; statutory entitlement and actual scheme design must be distinguished.
- **PMMVY:** first living child₹5, 000 in two instalments; under PMMVY2.0, second child if a girl₹6, 000 in one instalment. Eligible JSY payments can supplement support;₹6, 000 is not automatically paid to every first-child beneficiary. [WCD](https://www.wcd.gov.in/offerings/pradhan-mantri-matru-vandana-yojana).
- Maternity Benefit Act's 26-week provision applies where the woman has fewer than two surviving children; otherwise 12 weeks. It does not describe every worker's access.
## Implementation
- Source expenditure₹2, 700 crore 2018–19→₹870 crore 2023–24 and coverage 36%→9% are dated reported estimates, not universal measures of all maternity support.
- Tamil Nadu₹18, 000/Odisha₹10, 000 are source-era scheme amounts with eligibility conditions; compare coverage using matching denominators.
- Aadhaar/bank linkage, documentation and software failures can exclude eligible women. Simplify access, publish payments/denials, provide grievance redress and assess inflation-adjusted adequacy.

topics.title: Prohibitory orders, begging and lawful prosecution
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Distinguish legal stages
- **BNSS163** replaces CrPC144: urgent orders to address nuisance/danger must satisfy statutory conditions and reasons.
- **BNS223** concerns disobedience of a duly promulgated public-servant order; it is different from BNSS223's complaint procedure.
- **BNSS215 /former CrPC195:** court cognizance of specified offences requires the prescribed written complaint by the relevant public servant or authorised superior. Do not convert this into a universal prohibition on every FIR or investigation into independent offences.
- C.Muniappan 2010 and Daulat Ram/Mata Bhikh lines emphasise the complaint requirement; Jeevanandham 2018 is Madras High Court guidance, not a nationwide Supreme Court ruling on every investigation.
## Begging restrictions
- An Indore prohibitory order and editorial criticism are not themselves a final judicial finding of guilt or invalidity.
- Poverty, homelessness and exploitation need rehabilitation and social protection; restrictions require lawful, proportionate enforcement and due process. Donating to a person is not automatically a crime everywhere.

topics.title: RS-24 Yars and ballistic-missile terminology
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Recall
- Russian three-stage solid-fuel intercontinental ballistic missile, related to Topol-M; silo and road-mobile versions; entered service around 2010.
- Common NATO designation **SS-27 Mod 2**; source's SS-29 label is unreliable. Reported length~22.5 m, diameter~2 m, mass~49 tonnes and range~10, 500 km are approximate variant-dependent specifications.
- **MIRV:** independently targeted re-entry vehicles; differs from multiple vehicles without independent targeting. Source 300kilotons describes explosive yield, not warhead mass; warhead-count claims vary.

topics.title: Slender-billed gull and Pallikaranai
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Species and habitat
- **Chroicocephalus genei**, slender-billed gull; IUCN Least Concern. Mediterranean and north-western Indian Ocean coastal wetlands/lagoons; migratory movements extend to India and North Africa.
- Pale body, long slender reddish bill/legs, pale yellow iris and black wing tips; length~37–40cm, wingspan~90–102cm. Eats fish and invertebrates; proportions vary with habitat.
- Chennai sighting is a distribution/observation record, not discovery of a new species.
- **Pallikaranai**, Chennai, Ramsar site 2022; fresh/brackish marsh, flood storage and biodiversity. Its wider catchment connects through Okkiyam Madavu/Buckingham Canal towards the coast; catchment wetlands are not all inside its protected boundary.

topics.title: Spices Board and export quality
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Institution
- Statutory **Spices Board Act 1986**; Board established 1987 by merger of Cardamom Board and Spices Export Promotion Council. **Commerce and Industry Ministry; Kochi headquarters.**
- Export development for 52 scheduled spices and development of small/large cardamom; quality testing, market promotion, research and exporter support.
- Food-safety regulation and export promotion are distinct functions; FSSAI and other competent agencies retain their respective roles.
- Traceability, pesticide residues, ethylene oxide and importing-country standards influence market access. Testing must connect to corrective action across the supply chain.
## Value addition
- Source 2030 US$10 billion export target/~70%value-added share is an ambition; reported US$4.5 billion, 1.5 million tonnes, 48%processed share use dated/possibly different denominators.
- Raw spices→seasonings/extracts/essential oils→branding/standardisation; global seasoning-market share differs from India's overall spice-export share.
- FPOs, storage, packaging, traceability, IPM and farmer training; ICAR/seed-spice research supports disease/climate-resilient varieties.
- Nutraceutical/pharmaceutical opportunities require evidence, quality and applicable approvals; traditional use alone does not establish clinical efficacy. Extending PLI is a recommendation, not automatic existing eligibility.

## SPICED and commodity-board recall: May 2025
- Spices Board constituted **26 February 1987**, merging **Cardamom Board (1968)** and **Spices Export Promotion Council (1960)**. **Indian Cardamom Research Institute** undertakes small/large cardamom research; the Board's scheduled-spice export work differs from general food-safety regulation. [Board constitution](https://www.indianspices.com/about-us/constitution.html).
- **SPICED: Sustainability in Spice Sector through Progressive, Innovative and Collaborative Interventions for Export Development**. Supports productivity/quality, cardamom rejuvenation, post-harvest processing, GI/organic/value-added exports, food-safety/phytosanitary compliance, capacity building and MSME/startup market access.
- May issue describes **2025–26 implementation**; SPICED already operated in **2024–25**, so this is not proof of a first-ever May 2025 launch. Approved through the remaining Fifteenth Finance Commission period to FY 2025–26. Programme objectives do not demonstrate every supported plantation/export project is complete. [Board programmes](https://www.indianspices.com/box5_programmes_schemes.html), [2024–25 report](https://www.indianspices.com/sites/default/files/Spices%20Annual%20Report%202024-25%20final%20%282%29%20%281%29.pdf).
| Commodity board | Headquarters / statutory anchor |
| --- | --- |
| Coffee | Bengaluru; Coffee Act 1942 |
| Rubber | Kottayam; Rubber Act 1947, Rules 1955 |
| Tea | Kolkata; Tea Act 1953 |
| Tobacco | Guntur; Tobacco Board Act 1975, constituted 1 January 1976 |
| Spices | Kochi; Spices Board Act 1986 |
- All five fall under **Commerce and Industry**, not Agriculture. **2008 matching PYQ: A–1, B–3, C–4, D–2 → (b)**. **2022 Tea Board PYQ: statements 1 and 4 → (d)**. Overseas-office statements must be read in their exam-year setting; the source's expanded five-city list/50% export assertion is not a verified current network or trade statistic.

topics.title: Selenium: essential nutrient and excess exposure
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Essential versus excessive
- **Se, atomic number 34**; essential trace element. Selenoproteins support antioxidant defence, thyroid-hormone metabolism and reproduction; examples glutathione peroxidases, thioredoxin reductases and selenoproteinP.
- USNIH reference intake: adults 55, pregnancy 60, lactation 70 **micrograms/day**, not milligrams. Food content depends on soil; sources include seafood, meat and Brazil nuts. [NIH](https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Selenium-HealthProfessional/).
- Excess can cause **selenosis**: hair loss, brittle/lost nails and gastrointestinal symptoms; deficiency and toxicity are different problems.
- Buldhana hair-loss reports linked suspect wheat/selenium exposure: an investigated hypothesis is not proof all ration wheat or every Punjab/Haryana crop is unsafe. Establish exposure through food/soil testing and clinical/epidemiological assessment.

topics.title: Black plastic, recycled e-waste and food-contact safety
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Risk pathway
- Poorly controlled recycling of electronic plastics can transfer flame-retardant chemicals into other products. **Colour alone does not establish contamination** in every black utensil.
- Bromine detection is a screening clue, not identification of every chemical or proof of illness. Migration depends on material, temperature, use and dose.
- Widely circulated exposure claims from a 2024 study were subject to a calculation correction; do not memorise the original headline as an established daily toxic dose.
- Carbon-black pigments can impede conventional near-infrared sorting. Segregate e-waste, enforce traceability and food-contact standards, and improve sorting/authorised recycling.

topics.title: Spinal muscular atrophy and prenatal research
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mechanism and care
- Common 5qSMA: **autosomal recessive SMN1 defect on chromosome 5**→low survival motor neuron protein→motor-neuron loss→progressive weakness, often proximal, with respiratory/nutritional complications.
- SMN2 copy number can modify severity; types 0–4 reflect age/severity patterns rather than completely separate diseases.
- Disease-modifying treatments include nusinersen, risdiplam and onasemnogene abeparvovec; physiotherapy is not the only treatment. Respiratory, nutritional and orthopaedic support remain important.
- February 2025 prenatal risdiplam report concerned **one case**, not an established universal prenatal cure. [NEJM report](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMc2300802).
- Research requires informed consent, maternal/fetal safety monitoring and long-term follow-up; access and costs raise equity concerns.

## June 20 revision
- Source estimates SMA at roughly **1 in 10,000 births**. Its prenatal-treatment story repeats the single-case research report; it does not establish a prenatal cure.
- **PYQ 2021:** mitochondrial replacement can be performed before fertilisation (maternal spindle transfer) or after fertilisation (pronuclear transfer); mitochondrial inheritance is maternal. Both numbered statements are correct. This mitochondrial mechanism differs from SMN1-related SMA.

topics.title: Textiles: value chains, competitiveness and sustainability
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Value chain and clusters
- Fibre→yarn→fabric→processing→garments/home textiles; cotton and man-made fibres face different input/market conditions.
| Cluster | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| Tiruppur | Knitwear |
| Surat | Man-made textiles |
| Ludhiana | Hosiery/woollens |
| Bhiwandi | Powerloom weaving |
- Reported~4.5 crore employment refers to the broader textile sector, not cotton farming alone; around 60lakh cotton farmers is a separate dated estimate. MSMEs are important throughout the chain.
## Source-era trade and policy
- SourceFY2023–24 textile/apparel exports~US$34.1 billion versusUS$33.4 billionFY2019–20; garment and cotton/home-textile segments moved differently. Values, volumes and growth periods must match.
- Raw-material availability/cost, quality-control orders, logistics, skills and preferential trade access affect competitiveness; QCOs need quality benefits balanced with input availability.
- Traceability, cleaner processing, renewable power, water efficiency and recycling help respond to buyer sustainability requirements. PMMITRA infrastructure and production incentives require implementation/results assessment.
-2030 global fibre-demand figures and projected market values are forecasts, not achieved production.
## Circular fashion
- Source examples: **Panipat** textile recycling, **Bengaluru** waste-management innovations and **Tiruppur** cleaner production/wastewater work.
- Repair → reuse/rental → upcycling → fibre recycling, where feasible; match each route to material quality and demand.
- Mixed fibres, sorting, dyes, water/energy and transport affect actual benefits. Recycled textiles are not automatically impact-free; support worker safety, viable markets and responsible collection.

## June 2025: competitiveness debate and targets
- Industry report says export value has remained around **US$37–42 billion**, with volume shrinking; **US$100 billion exports/US$350 billion industry by 2030** are ambitions, not realised output. Source's **17% CAGR** and **US$100 billion capacity investment** are industry calculations/estimates, dependent on base year and scope.
- Raw-material/power/labour/finance costs, lead times, fragmented inter-State fibre-to-fashion chains and detailed compliance limit scale. Compare productivity, quality and logistics, not wages alone. **Cotton-price stabilisation fund, cheaper MSME loans, freer input trade and labour-compliance reform** are recommendations in this issue, not newly enacted schemes.
- Recall **PM MITRA**, textile **PLI**, **TUFS** and **SAMARTH** have differing mandates/status; programme name does not prove every firm receives incentives or every park is operating. QCOs support quality but can constrain competitively priced polyester/viscose imports.
## Complementary source data: keep dates/definitions
- **4.5 crore employment** concerns the broad textile sector, not only cotton; **60 lakh cotton growers** separate. Graphic cites **130.61 lakh ha/40% world cotton area**, world **324.16 lakh ha**; undated area estimates do not establish June production share or yield. India cultivates **Gossypium arboreum, herbaceum, barbadense, hirsutum**; cotton zones broadly north/central/south.
- **24% cotton share/second-largest producer**, **second MMF producer**, MSME **80%**, MMF consumption **3.1 kg/person** versus China **12/North America 22.5**, all-fibre **5.5 vs global 11.2** are source-era figures with unspecified matching reference years. **Reliance—polyester; Grasim—viscose**; “sole domestic viscose producer” is product/category-dependent.
- Source growth **FY2015–19 textiles 0.4% CAGR/apparel 7.7%; FY2020–24 −1.8%/−8.2%** lacks an explicit volume/value series. Its **2/2.3% GDP, 11/12% exports, 13% industrial output** use mixed snapshots; do not combine as one current measure.
- FY2020→FY2024 source exports: **apparel US$15.5→14.5 billion; cotton/home textiles US$10.2→12.3 billion**; total **33.4→34.1** already recorded. US/EU major markets; brand examples **JCPenney/Gap/Decathlon**, home-textile firms **Welspun/Trident**. Claimed **Vietnam US$40 billion apparel (2023)** may conflate apparel with wider textiles.
- Sustainability: traceability, clean power, recycling and responsible sourcing; source **16 EU rules in 2021–24** needs instrument-level verification. Recycling-market **India US$400 million/global US$7.5 billion**, **148 million tonnes waste by 2030** and **under 25% recycled** are projections/undefined-scope estimates, not guaranteed outcomes. Assist MSMEs with standards/finance while measuring actual environmental performance.

topics.title: Kalakkad–Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Map and biodiversity
- Southern Western Ghats, **Tamil Nadu**, across the Tirunelveli–Tenkasi–Kanyakumari landscape near Kerala; not a reserve divided equally between the two States.
- Tiger reserve 1988, combining Kalakkad/Mundanthurai landscapes; part of Agasthyamalai region, headwaters important to the **Tamirabarani** basin.
- Evergreen/semi-evergreen forest, moist/dry deciduous forest, thorn habitats and grasslands; plantations are not equivalent to natural forest.
- Tiger, leopard, elephant, gaur, sambar, sloth bear, Nilgiri/langurs, lion-tailed macaque, slender loris and small cats; flora includes Cullenia, Hopea and **Paphiopedilum druryi**.
- Western Ghats is a biodiversity hotspot; source 18-world-hotspot count is outdated. Hotspot status concerns endemism and habitat loss, not tiger density alone.

topics.title: Honduras: map recall
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Location
- Central America: borders **Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua**; Caribbean coast on Gulf of Honduras, Pacific access through **Gulf of Fonseca**.
- Capital **Tegucigalpa**; highland terrain, highest peak Cerro Las Minas. Rivers Coco, Patuca and Ulúa; Lake Yojoa and Caratasca lagoon.
- Forest, mineral/agricultural resources and hurricane/flood exposure; source Indian 26-tonne aid report followed Tropical Storm Sara, a dated humanitarian event.

topics.title: Time use, unpaid care and the care economy
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Reading Time Use Survey 2024
- NSO survey records a 24-hour activity diary; 2019 and 2024 comparisons require matching ages, activity categories and **participant versus all-person averages**.
- Source employment participation, ages 15–59: women 21.8%→25%, men 70.9%→75%; these measures are not interchangeable with PLFS annual LFPR.
- Unpaid domestic work remains strongly gendered; reported female 15–59 participant time 305 minutes/day versus 315 in 2019. Do not present participant minutes as time spent by every woman.
- Caregiving, learning, leisure and self-care have different age/participation denominators; one table's numbers cannot be applied to all ages. [NSO release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2106113&lang=2&reg=48).
## Care and policy
- **Recognise→Reduce→Redistribute** unpaid care; represent care workers in decisions and provide fair reward/conditions in paid care.
- Water access, reliable energy, nearby childcare/Palna, elder care and transport reduce time burdens; a registered tap is not proof reliable daily supply.
- Unpaid household care generally falls outside GDP's production boundary; unpaid work in a family enterprise/agriculture is a different category and cannot all be called excluded care.
- Gender Budget 2025–26₹4, 49, 028.68 crore/~8.86% of expenditure is an allocation classification, not money entirely dedicated to childcare or proof all women benefit.
- Bogotá care blocks illustrate linked neighbourhood services. Measure service quality, time saved and women's choices, not merely facility counts.

topics.title: Avalanches: triggers and risk reduction
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Process
- Snow mass descends a slope when gravity exceeds stability; slab failure often combines a weak layer and loading from snowfall/wind, warming or rain.
- Types: slab, loose-snow, wet-snow and powder-snow avalanches; ice/rock avalanches are related mass movements, not all identical snow processes.
- Many snow avalanches occur on~30–45° slopes; terrain, snowpack and weather interact, so angle alone is not a prediction.
## Reduce exposure
- February 2025 Mana-region disaster highlights risks to mountain workers and routes. Map runout zones, monitor weather/snowpack, issue actionable warnings and close exposed work/routes when necessary.
- DGRE expertise, Army/ITBP/NDRF coordination, trained rescue and appropriate shelters/equipment support preparedness; remote sensing cannot guarantee exact event prediction.
- Combine disaster planning with changing mountain climate and infrastructure siting; do not treat all snowfall as equally dangerous.

topics.title: India’s high-income2047 pathway
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Conditional scenario
- World Bank February 28, 2025 report: average realGDP growth~**7.8%** over 22 years could support high-income status by 2047; this is a reform scenario, not a guaranteed forecast. [World Bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2025/02/28/india-accelerated-reforms-needed-to-speed-up-growth-and-achieve-high-income-status-by-2047).
- Suggested investment/GDP~33.5%→40% by 2035; labour-force participation 56.4%→65%, women's participation 35.6%→50%; improve productivity and human capital.
- High-income classification uses **GNI per capita**, not aggregateGDP rank. Real growth, population, exchange rates and the classification methodology matter.
- More jobs/skills, productive cities, infrastructure, competitive firms/trade, State reforms and inclusion; climate resilience must accompany investment.
## GDP size versus living standards
- The source's US$2.1 trillion (2015) to US$4.3 trillion (2025) comparison mixes a historical value with a dated **projection**; future rankings were not achieved outcomes at publication.
- **Nominal US-dollar GDP**, real domestic-currency growth and purchasing-power-parity GDP measure different things. Dollar values change with inflation and exchange rates; country comparisons need consistent bases.
- Large total GDP does not itself establish high income per person or inclusive prosperity. Assess employment, real wages, productivity, inequality and human development.
- GST, IBC, digital payments, infrastructure and investment can support growth; attributing all observed growth to one policy/leader exceeds the evidence.
- Demographic dividend requires skills, health and productive jobs; a young population is an opportunity, not automatic growth. Forecast dates for overtaking Japan/Germany remain vintage-specific scenarios.

topics.title: Aditya-L1 and Lagrange points
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mission
- ISRO solar observatory: **PSLV-C57 launch 2 September 2023; halo-orbit insertion 6 January 2024**, near Sun–EarthL1~1.5 millionkm from Earth. It does not travel to the Sun's surface.
- Seven payloads: **VELC, SUIT, SoLEXS, HEL1OS** remote solar observations; **ASPEX, PAPA, magnetometer** in-situ particles/fields.
- Study corona, heating, flares, solar wind and space weather; complements other observatories rather than duplicating every instrument.
## Lagrange points
- Five points in the rotating two-body system; L1–L3 unstable and need station-keeping; L4/L5 can be stable under appropriate mass-ratio conditions.
- Balanced effective forces do not mean zero gravity or no fuel requirement. Halo orbit provides useful observing geometry.
- Source claims of ISRO's first-ever PSLV restart are incorrect; earlier restart demonstrations preceded this mission.

topics.title: Naval Anti-Ship Missile–Short Range
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Trial and technology
- **DRDO/Indian Navy test 25 February 2025**, Sea King helicopter off Chandipur; **NASM-SR means Short Range**, despite source long-range/hypersonic wording. [Defence release](https://www.pib.gov.in/pressreleasepage.aspx?lang=2&prid=2106482&reg=48).
- Sea-skimming flight; imaging-infrared seeker, fibre-optic-gyro inertial navigation, radio altimeter and two-way data link.
- **Man-in-the-loop** allows target selection/retargeting via live seeker imagery; demonstrated direct hit and relevant control modes.
- DRDO laboratory collaboration includes RCI/DRDL/HEMRL/TBRL. Successful trial is not proof every unit is operationally inducted or an export contract exists.

topics.title: Border Roads Organisation
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Institution and role
- **Raised 7 May 1960**, under Ministry of Defence; builds/maintains strategic roads, bridges, tunnels and airfield-related infrastructure in border areas and certain overseas projects.
- Border connectivity supports defence mobility, disaster response and civilian access; BRO is not the Ministry of Home Affairs' Border Management Department.
- Mountain terrain, weather, environmental impacts and maintenance require integrated planning; road length alone does not establish year-round connectivity.

topics.title: Kandla–Gorakhpur LPG pipeline
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Project
-~2, 800 km LPG pipeline from Kandla through Gujarat/Madhya Pradesh/Uttar Pradesh to Gorakhpur; associated distribution can serve wider regions without every State lying on the main route.
- **IHB:** IndianOil 50%, BPCL25%, HPCL25%; reported capacity~8.25 million tonnes/year and project cost~₹10, 000 crore are source-era estimates.
- March 2025 commissioning schedules were plans, not proof the whole pipeline was already operational.
- LPG is principally propane/butane; LNG is mainly methane. Pipeline transport can reduce road-tanker exposure and logistics costs but retains leak/fire/maintenance risks.
- PNGRB standards, monitoring, emergency plans and maintenance matter. It does not automatically cut consumer prices or end import dependence; cited Jaipur tanker disaster occurredDecember 2024, not 2023.

topics.title: Three-language policy and foundational learning
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## NEP2020
- Three-language approach retains flexibility: choices involve States/regions/students; **at least two languages native to India**; no language is to be imposed. [NEP](https://www.education.gov.in/sites/upload_files/mhrd/files/NEP_Final_English_0.pdf).
- Tamil Nadu's two-language position raises federal, identity and implementation debates; Hindi is not India's constitutionally designated national language.
- Mother-language familiarity can support early learning; multilingual benefits depend on teaching quality, exposure and resources.
## Learning priorities
- Source ASER claim about Class 3 inability to read a Class 2 passage concerns a specific rural reading benchmark, not absence of every literacy skill among all Indian children.
- Foundational literacy/numeracy, teacher vacancies, materials and training need attention alongside language policy; salary spending shares do not alone measure teaching quality.
- Flexible sequencing and local consultation can reduce overload. AI translation is a useful aid, not a substitute for language learning or reliable classroom teaching.
## Medium versus language subjects
- NEP recommends home/mother/local/regional medium **wherever possible until Grade 5, preferably Grade 8 andbeyond**; choice of medium differs from learning three language subjects.
- NCERT2024 languages initiative included primers in 104 languages/dialects, not necessarily full translated science/maths curricula in 104 languages.
- Teacher/material shortages, parental Englishpreferences and State linguistic choices affect implementation. Older AISES2002–09 percentages cannot establish a current 2025 trend.
- Classical-language learning and foreign-language options differ from formalgovernmentclassicalstatus; Sanskrit/Tamil/Telugu/Kannada/Malayalam/Odia/Pali/Prakrit and Persian references must not imply identical notified status.

## Maharashtra withdrawal
- Maharashtra withdrew its **16 April and 17 June 2025 orders** concerning the three-language policy in Classes 1–5 after opposition over Hindi and regional-language concerns; a **Narendra Jadhav committee** was to examine sequencing, the earlier Mashelkar report and public views, with a three-month report period.
- The issue incorrectly mandates a foreign language: NEP requires **at least two of three languages native to India**, with flexible State/region/student choice and no imposed language. The source's 20-student arrangement should not be attributed as a universal NEP rule. [NEP paragraph 4.13](https://dsel.education.gov.in/sites/default/files/update/NEP_Final_English.pdf).
- Education is in the **Concurrent List**. Mains balance: multilingual learning/national communication alongside linguistic identity, federal choice, teacher availability, materials and foundational learning. Reciprocal opportunities to learn non-Hindi Indian languages and consultation matter; the policy's text alone cannot prove uniform outcomes.
- Source diagram: **5+3+3+4 structure** = foundational (ages 3–8), preparatory (8–11), middle (11–14), secondary (14–18), including three preschool years and twelve school years.

topics.title: Fisheries: livelihoods, sustainability and governance
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Sector
- Marine capture, inland capture and aquaculture are distinct; source's production rank is dated and should not be treated as a permanent ranking.
- Fisheries support food, exports and millions of livelihoods. Estimated resource potential is not a sustainable annual catch entitlement.
- Constitution: State List 21 covers fisheries; Union List 57 covers fishing/fisheries beyond territorial waters.
## Policies and constraints
- **PMMSY2020; National Policy on Marine Fisheries 2017. National Fisheries Policy 2020 was a draft**, not automatically a final enacted framework.
- Cold chains, landing/processing facilities, credit, skills and traceability support value addition; fishers' safety/social protection matter with export growth.
- Climate change, habitat degradation, illegal/unreported/unregulated fishing, bycatch and excessive effort need ecosystem-based management.
- Bottom trawling and deep-sea fishing are not synonymous; assess gear, habitat and stock impacts. Neighbouring-country maritime disputes require lawful coordination.

topics.title: Blue Ghost lunar landing
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mission
- Firefly Aerospace **Blue Ghost landed 2 March 2025 in Mare Crisium**; launched 15 January on Falcon 9. NASA CLPS delivery carried 10 NASA instruments.
- Payload themes: heat flow/drilling, regolith/plume interactions, lunar navigation signals, magnetic fields, dust mitigation, retroreflection and Earth/space observations.
- Commercial delivery still involves government funding/payloads. Odysseus 2024 preceded it as a commercial lunar landing but tipped; specify the basis of any “first” claim.
## India connections
- India joined **Artemis AccordsJune 2023**, not still awaiting a first invitation inMarch 2025.
- Chandrayaan 3 landed near 69°south, not exactly at the geographic south pole. Chandrayaan 4/LUPEX concern different exploration objectives; Gaganyaan is a human-spaceflight programme, not itself an announced lunar landing.

topics.title: Academy Awards and Indian cinema
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Awards recall
- **97th Oscars, 2 March 2025**, Dolby Theatre, Los Angeles; Anora won five awards, Sean Baker four.
- Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences founded 1927; first awards 1929. Cedric Gibbons design/George Stanley sculpture; statue's five spokes represent original branches.
| Indian recognition | Year |
| --- | --- |
| Bhanu Athaiya, Gandhi costume design; first Indian winner |1983|
| Satyajit Ray, honorary award |1992|
| AR Rahman, score/song; Gulzar, song; Resul Pookutty, sound, Slumdog Millionaire |2009|
| Naatu Naatu: MM Keeravani/Chandrabose; The Elephant Whisperers: Kartiki Gonsalves/Guneet Monga |2023|
- Mother India was a 1957 film nominated at the 1958 ceremony; film year and award year differ.
- Statue materials changed historically, including wartime plaster and later production methods; recognition is not an objective ranking of every national cinema.

topics.title: Mob lynching: law and prevention
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Legal recall
- **BNS103(2):** murder by a group of five or more acting in concert on specified identity-related grounds attracts death or life imprisonment and fine; source's blanket “no provision” claim is outdated forMarch 2025.
- **Tehseen S.Poonawalla 2018**, not 2017: Supreme Court preventive, remedial and punitive directions, including nodal officers, prompt response/investigation, victim relief and accountability.
- Articles 14/15/21 support equality and protection of life; rumours, hate mobilisation and impunity do not justify violence.
- State anti-lynching Bills require assent/commencement checks; passage alone does not make every proposal operative law.
## Prevention
- Local intelligence, prompt action against incitement, accurate public communication, impartial policing and timely prosecution; victim/witness protection and compensation.
- Separate evidence of individual/group acts from stereotypes about whole religious communities. Accountability must cover official failure as well as perpetrators.

topics.title: Ganges river dolphin
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Species
- **Platanista gangetica**, Susu; National Aquatic Animal 2009, IUCN Endangered, CITESAppendix I and Wildlife Protection Act Schedule I.
- Ganges and Indus dolphins are now recognised as distinct species; older subspecies nomenclature persists in older sources.
- Reduced vision; echolocation supports navigation/prey detection in turbid rivers. Confluences/deeper channels are important habitats.
## Population and protection
- First national estimation, surveys 2021–23/report March 2025: **6, 327 river dolphins overall**, distinguished from 6, 324 Ganges and 3 Indus dolphins; do not label the entire combined count Ganges-only.
- Project Dolphin 2020; Vikramshila sanctuary, Bihar. First satellite tag in Assam 18 December 2024. [Official tagging account](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressNoteDetails.aspx?ModuleId=3&NoteId=153834&lang=2&reg=3).
- Pollution, dams/flow fragmentation, entanglement and poaching threaten survival; protect ecological flows, reduce bycatch and monitor connected river habitat.
## Survey interpretation
- Source State totals:UP2, 397; Bihar 2, 220; West Bengal 815; Assam 635; Jharkhand 162; Rajasthan/MP95; Punjab 3. River-basin totals are a different classification, not inconsistent State totals.
- Boat visual observations plus acoustic/hydrophone methods and statistical modelling address brief surfacing/detection probability; acoustic detection is not automatically unique identification of every animal.
- First national baseline does not alone prove a stable population trend. Dolphins can leave genetic evidence in water; “no DNA evidence possible”is wrong.
- Bycatch, oil/blubber use, pollution and flow fragmentation need community-linked measures; reported annual 4–5%mortality is study-specific, not a universally verified national rate.

topics.title: Cities Coalition for Circularity
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Initiative
- **C3 announced 3 March 2025, Jaipur**, during 12th Regional 3R/Circular Economy Forum. [MoHUA](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2107712&lang=2&reg=48).
- City cooperation, shared knowledge, digital coordination, private participation and resource-efficient urban systems; proposed collaborative mechanism, not a binding international treaty.
- **Reduce→Reuse→Recycle**; also design for durability/repair and recover suitable materials through safe systems.
- CITIIS2.0's reported₹1, 800 crore/18 cities/14States is a separate programme context, not proof the entire amount finances C3.
- Track material recovery, lifecycle impacts and waste-worker inclusion; a digital platform alone does not make a city circular.

topics.title: SPHEREx: infrared all-sky survey
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mission
- NASA **Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer**; infrared all-sky survey across 102 spectral bands.
- Study galaxy distribution/cosmic inflation, the history of collective cosmic light, and interstellar water/organic ices relevant to planet formation.
- Survey targets include hundreds of millions of galaxies and~100 million stars; planned repeated maps are mission goals, not all completed observations at launch.
- March 4 launch date in source was a schedule: launched with PUNCH11 March 2025 California time/12MarchUTC. [NASA](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-launches-missions-to-study-sun-universes-beginning/).
- Detecting ingredients associated with life does not establish extraterrestrial life; infrared observations infer early-universe processes rather than photographing the Big Bang itself.

topics.title: Parandur airport: infrastructure and wetland trade-offs
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Proposal and concerns
- Proposed second Chennai airport at **Parandur, Kanchipuram**, site chosen 2022. Source₹29, 144 crore/ultimate 100 million passengers and 2028 phase targets are planning figures, not completed capacity.
- Reported 13affected villages include Ekanapuram; displacement, farm livelihoods and water-body/wetland networks require transparent assessment and fair rehabilitation.
- Parandur is not automatically a Ramsar-listed site. Wetland Rules 2017 definitions/exclusions, other water/land laws and project clearances must be examined separately.
- Basin hydrology, Kamban canal links, flood storage and cumulative effects matter; elevating a runway alone does not resolve downstream flood risk.
## Decision framework
- Assess demand/site alternatives, environmental impacts and public consultation; disclose clearances, acquisition terms and compensation/R&R.
- Pair connectivity/economic gains with ecological limits, meaningful grievance redress and monitored mitigation; projected jobs are not proof all displaced households gain.

topics.title: India–Belgium defence manufacturing
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Collaboration
- John Cockerill Defence/Electro Pneumatics & Hydraulics joint venture, reported 60:40, to produce turrets in India; technology transfer/local production differ from fully indigenous intellectual property.
- DRDO–L&T **Zorawar light tank** development responds to high-altitude mobility needs following 2020 Ladakh tensions; trial stage is not fleet induction.
- Source 700 tank requirement and anticipated 2025 Mo U are reported plans, not signed orders or completed deliveries.
- Combine specialised foreign technology with Indian manufacturing/electronics, testing, spares and lifecycle support; local assembly alone does not remove every import dependency.
## Wider bilateral relations and dated figures
- Diplomatic ties **1947**; Modi's Brussels visit **2016**, King Philippe/Queen Mathilde India visit **2017**, regular Foreign Office Consultations. The 2017 visit was not the first Belgian royal State visit in four decades: King Albert II visited in 2008. [Embassy bilateral brief](https://indianembassybrussels.gov.in/pdf/Bilateral%20 Brief%20 July%202025.pdf).
- Correct source's **over US$19 billion trade in FY2023–24**: Embassy gives **US$15.074 billion**, Belgium **fifth-largest EU trading partner** in that year. Calendar/FY data, currencies and trade scope must be consistent.
- **Antwerp** diamond trade links with Indian firms; chemicals/pharmaceuticals/machinery/IT and port logistics diversify ties. Source **500+ diamond firms / 20,000+ PIOs** are dated estimates, not an exact current registry. Examples **Solvay, UCB, AB InBev; TCS, Infosys** illustrate business presence, not all investment.
- Renewable energy/clean technology, space-launch collaboration and university research/student exchanges (**KU Leuven, Ghent; IITs/IISc**) accompany ICCR/cultural links. Belgian firms' defence-exhibition participation does not itself constitute signed procurement.
- UN/ISA/FATF engagement and reported UNSC reform support coexist with separate treaty/forum membership. Avoid inferring automatic agreement on every policy or an established bilateral cyber/maritime programme from generic cooperation claims.
## Map and institutions
- **Kingdom of Belgium**, federal constitutional monarchy; **Brussels** capital. Borders **Netherlands north, Germany east, Luxembourg southeast, France south/southwest; North Sea coast**.
- **Flanders—predominantly Dutch; Wallonia—predominantly French; German-speaking community east**. Brussels is a bilingual region; linguistic Communities and territorial Regions are distinct.
- Founding member of EEC/EU institutional predecessors, NATO, OECD and WTO; euro-area participant. Brussels hosts **European Commission, Council of EU, European Council, NATO headquarters**.
- European Parliament's official seat/plenary is **Strasbourg**, committees/additional sessions **Brussels**, Secretariat **Luxembourg**: correct the PDF's simple “two seats” account. [Parliament organisation](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/news/en/faq/3/which-languages-are-in-use-in-the-parliament).

topics.title: Healthcare financing and household costs
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Correct denominator
- **NHA2021–22**, released September 2024: out-of-pocket spending **39.4% of total health expenditure**, ~1.51%GDP; government health spending~1.84%GDP. Source 47%/2.3% uses older/mismatched figures. [Health Ministry](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2058791&lang=2&reg=48).
- Union health-budget allocation is not total Centre+State public health spending. Budget 2023–24 figures are historical, not March 2025 current spending.
- Reduce **household financial burden**, while increasing efficient public provision; cutting all health spending would undermine access.
## Reforms
- Prevention, primary care, affordable drugs/diagnostics, referral systems and usable insurance reduce catastrophic costs; coverage enrolment is not guaranteed effective access.
- National Health Policy public-spending target 2.5%GDP; source proposed cost commission is a recommendation, not an established regulator.
- Clinical Establishments **Act 2010 /Central Rules 2012**, not source's 2010 Rules; applicable regulation and fair rates need enforcement/State-context checks.
- HAQ rank 145/195 and poverty/medical-inflation estimates are dated study results; distinguish medical-price indices and forecasts from general inflation.

topics.title: Astra MkIII, Gandiva and ramjet propulsion
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Concepts and status
- Astra family: beyond-visual-range air-to-air weapons; reported Mk III/Gandiva development involves **Solid Fuel Ducted Ramjet**, not source's “dual-fuel” expansion. [DRDO SFDR demonstration](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=179682).
- Ramjet draws atmospheric oxygen; sustained thrust can improve engagement energy. BVR engagement still needs detection, tracking, guidance and aircraft integration.
- Source 340 km/190 km envelopes, Mach ranges and manoeuvre angles are reported development specifications, not universally demonstrated combat performance or proof of global superiority.
- Ground/technology trials, captive carriage, separation, live firing and operational induction are distinct. Planned Su-30 MKI/Tejas integration is not completed fleet-wide integration.

## July 11 indigenous-seeker flight tests
- DRDO and IAF flight-tested Astra with an **indigenous RF seeker from Su-30 MKI off Odisha**, with two launches against high-speed unmanned aerial targets under different range/aspect/platform conditions. This is the development reported in the July 12 clipping. [Defence release](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2144118&lang=2&reg=48).
- **BDL** manufactures Astra. Source Mk-I recall: approximately **3.6 m, 178 mm, 154 kg, Mach 4.5**, head-on envelope **80–110 km** versus shorter **20–40 km** tail chase; these are indicative configuration/engagement figures, not every-shot guarantees. Mid-course inertial guidance and terminal active radar homing perform different tasks.
- **LOBL** acquires a lock before launch; **LOAL** acquires it after launch. All-weather capability does not remove targeting/network limitations. Mk-II and SFDR-based Mk-III development should be separated from Mk-I induction; ramjet propulsion alone does not establish a hypersonic operational weapon. Meteor is a multinational MBDA programme, not simply a French missile.

topics.title: Eklavya Model Residential Schools
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Recall
- Began 1997–98 for quality residential education for Scheduled Tribe children; historical grants under **Article 275(1)**, later central scheme framework.
- Coeducational Classes VI–XII, usually 480 students/equal boy–girl seats, free education/CBSE curriculum, local culture, sport and skills. Non-ST admission up to 10% is subject to scheme rules.
- **NESTS**, autonomous society under Tribal Affairs Ministry, coordinates EMRS; State societies support operation.
-2018–19 expansion criterion: blocks with over 50%ST population and at least 20, 000 ST residents. Original 2022 target is not proof universal completion.
-15-acre site requirement can be difficult in hills/Northeast/conflict areas; dispersed tribal populations may miss density thresholds. Teacher vacancies, contractual staffing and variable quality need attention; source July 2022 staff figures are historical.

## 2025 entrance examinations
- Tribal Affairs Ministry reported **596 EMRS students across 12 States** qualifying in engineering/medical entrance examinations: **218 JEE Mains, 34 JEE Advanced and 344 NEET**; qualification does not itself establish admission. The Ministry planned scholarship and application support.
- Correction: **NESTS was established in April 2019**, distinct from the 2018–19 policy expansion. Its 2022 teacher-shortage example is historical, not proof no national recruitment rules existed in July 2025. [NESTS anniversary release](https://nests.tribal.gov.in/WriteReadData/RTF1984/1743750388.pdf).

topics.title: Deocha–Pachami: basalt, coal and land
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Project and trade-offs
- **Birbhum, West Bengal**; thick basalt overburden must be addressed to access coal. Basalt is volcanic igneous rock, useful in aggregates/construction.
- Reported coal 1, 240 million tonnes/basalt 675 million tonnes and 100–350 m basalt thickness are project estimates; ranking “Asia's second largest mine” confuses resource/block potential with operating output.
- Initial 326-acre work, proposed additional 50 acres, 71.5%revenue sharing and ₹5, 000 crore expected basalt revenue are source-era plans/contracts/forecasts.
- Land consent/acquisition, rehabilitation, environmental permissions, waste/air/water management and technical feasibility govern outcomes. Basalt permission does not automatically clear the entire coal project.
- State Investment Synergy Committee, chaired by Chief Secretary, coordinates approvals; political claims about jobs/elections are not measured project benefits.

topics.title: Kedarnath and Hemkund Sahib ropeways
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Approved proposals
| Route, Uttarakhand | Source approval figures |
| --- | --- |
| Sonprayag–Kedarnath, Rudraprayag |12.9 km; ₹4, 081.23 crore; ~36 minute planned journey|
| Govindghat–Hemkund Sahib, Chamoli |12.4 km; ₹2, 730.13 crore|
- Parvatmala framework, PPP; monocable/tricable detachable gondola technologies. Approval is not completed construction or operating safety certification.
- Better access for elderly/disabled pilgrims and tourism livelihoods; links to Valley of Flowers region, not a ropeway constructed inside every part of the UNESCO park.
- Himalayan slope stability, forest impacts, carrying capacity, waste/water, weather evacuation and construction disruption need assessment; lower journey time does not itself prove lower lifecycle emissions.

topics.title: Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Revision
- Source 2024–25/2025–26 outlay ₹3, 880 crore, including ₹75 crore **Pashu Aushadhi** component for affordable generic veterinary medicines.
- Vaccination, surveillance and Mobile Veterinary Units; medicine distribution via eligible PM-Kisan Samriddhi Kendras/cooperatives.
- FMD, brucellosis, PPR and **CSF=Classical Swine Fever**, not cerebrospinal fluid; lumpy skin disease is another animal-health concern. [Animal Husbandry portal](https://pashuaushadhi.dahd.gov.in/).
- Healthy livestock protects income/food supply; One Health links animal/human/environment surveillance, but not every livestock disease is zoonotic.

topics.title: Space debris: responsibility and liability
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Treaty distinction
- Non-functional human-made orbital/re-entering objects create collision/re-entry risks. Identifying origin and responsible launching States can be difficult.
- **Outer Space Treaty 1967 Article VI:** State responsibility for national activities, including private operators; authorisation/continuing supervision.
- **Liability Convention 1972:** launching State absolute liability for damage on Earth's surface/to aircraft in flight; fault-based liability for damage to another space object elsewhere. Components are included in “space object”; debris is not automatically outside the Convention. [UNOOSA](https://www.unoosa.org/oosa/en/ourwork/spacelaw/treaties/liability-convention.html).
- Launching State includes launch/procurement and territory/facility connections; several States may be involved. Absolute liability still requires attributable damage and applicable claims procedures.
## Examples and reform
- Cosmos 954 fell in Canada 1978; negotiated settlement illustrates attribution/compensation. Kenya December 2024 metal object was initially suspected debris, not conclusively assigned to an operator by appearance alone.
- Source Long March July 2024 date, 100, 000 satellite forecast and 30%compliance are not a verified uniform inventory; distinguish planned constellations from satellites already launched.
- Better tracking, registration, disposal/re-entry plans, passivation and collision avoidance; voluntary guidelines differ from domestic licence rules.
- Tribunal/penalty proposals are reforms, not existing universal powers. Reusable launchers/on-orbit servicing can help but do not inherently create zero debris.
## 10 May 2025: Kosmos 482 re-entry
- Soviet **Venera-programme** Venus probe launched **1972**, failed to escape Earth orbit owing to a launcher failure; the surviving descent capsule remained about **53 years**. Source **~495 kg, ~1 m**, robust titanium design intended for Venus's high-temperature/high-pressure environment.
- **Uncontrolled re-entry10 May 2025**; source “11 May 2024” is erroneous. Russia reported Indian-Ocean descent, but **precise time/location and surviving wreckage were not independently established**. The source's Bay-of-Bengal splashdown is too definite. ESA's 10 May update inferred re-entry after a radar non-detection and reported no direct visual/ground-impact observations. [ESA tracking updates](https://blogs.esa.int/rocketscience/2025/05/07/reentry-prediction-soviet-era-venera-venus-lander-cosmos-482-descent-craft/comment-page-1/).
- Capsule toughness made survival plausible, not proven. **~242 km/h** intact-impact estimate attributed to Marco Langbroek is conditional, not measured impact velocity. After decades, parachute/battery usefulness cannot be assumed; this was not a controlled functioning landing system.
- Atmospheric drag depends on solar activity/density, orbit and object's orientation; prediction windows narrow with radar/other tracking but retain uncertainty. Low individual risk does not erase accountability or the need for responsible disposal and transparent alerts.
- **Outer Space Treaty Article VIII** retains ownership of objects/components despite return to Earth; **Rescue Agreement Article 5** governs notification/recovery/return on request with relevant conditions and expenses. **Liability Convention** addresses damage, not an automatic transfer of ownership or blanket immediate duty for any finder to ship debris. [UNOOSA Rescue Agreement](https://www.unoosa.org/oosa/en/ourwork/spacelaw/treaties/rescueagreement.html).
- Tracking cooperation, registration, passivation, planned disposal and end-of-life licensing complement liability rules; legacy debris shows that mission failure can leave enduring safety responsibilities.

topics.title: AI in education and critical thinking
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Learning design
- AI can support feedback, coding and exploration; uncritical reliance can weaken independent reasoning. Effects depend on task, student and how learning is assessed.
- Match permitted use to learning objectives: independent fundamentals, then assisted exploration, verification and explanation of choices.
- Train teachers/students to check errors, bias and sources; require appropriate disclosure and protect personal data/intellectual property.
- Institutional rules, safety audits and accessible training; a blanket ban or blanket adoption cannot replace course-specific decisions.
- Future of Jobs 2025 highlights analytical thinking/adaptability/AI skills; does not establish traditional programming has no value. India's general laws still apply even without a single comprehensive AI Act.

topics.title: AIKosha and IndiaAI compute access
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Data and infrastructure
- **AIKosha**, India AI datasets platform, launched March 2025; supports datasets/models for researchers, startups and public applications, including Indian-language work.
- India AI Mission approved 2024, ~₹10, 372 crore; Compute Portal expands shared/subsidised GPU access. Source 316 datasets/14, 000 GPUs are launch-era counts, not permanent inventory. [Meit Y launch](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2108961&lang=1&reg=1).
- Data.gov.in already aggregates open government data; AIKosha is not India's first public-data portal. Departmental Chief Data Officers support sharing.
- Data quality, licences, consent/privacy, re-identification risk, security and representative languages matter; “non-personal” is not a guarantee all processing is unrestricted.
- Gopalakrishnan non-personal-data committee was constituted 2019, not 2018; recommendations do not create an automatic compulsory private-data sharing law.
## AI compute: 28 April 2025 editorial
- **Training** develops model parameters; **inference** runs trained models. Both require suitable chips, memory, networking, dependable electricity and data centres; GPU counts alone do not measure usable capacity or domestic chip manufacture.
- IndiaAI uses empanelled private providers and subsidised shared access to reduce barriers for startups/researchers. Official January 2025 announcement described **18,000+ GPUs** and **40% subsidy**; the issue's roughly **19,000** is an April-era estimate, not a permanent installed inventory. Source cites approximately **₹4,500 crore over five years for compute**, distinct from the whole mission's roughly ₹10,372 crore. [January announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx/PRID=2097709).
- Policy rationale: stimulate nascent demand, widen access, support public-priority applications and domestic capability, and prevent vendor concentration. “Sovereign compute” requires control/access/security arrangements; foreign GPUs or privately hosted infrastructure do not automatically mean sovereign hardware production.
- Editorial critique: lowest-bid matching can depress sustainable margins, quality and R&D; eligibility/application friction burdens small users; subsidies/price controls can distort private demand; limited scale and narrow application focus may constrain frontier research. The claim that only 25% of H100 demand is domestic is an **unverified editorial estimate**, not a census of India's compute market.
- Reform proposals: assess reliability/performance and innovation alongside price; simplify access; combine compute support with model/R&D grants and talent; scale public-private investment; adapt procurement to inference as well as training; improve chip imports and sustainable power/data-centre capacity.
- Balance affordability against fiscal efficiency, utilisation, competition and future hardware obsolescence. Source comparisons with Meta spending are illustrative and not like-for-like public programme budgets. These are policy arguments, not proof the mission has failed or that all proposed reforms were implemented.

## Strategy before implementation: editorial argument
- The editorial calls for an updated, democratically debated national AI strategy linking missions to **strategic autonomy, data control, jobs, inclusion, public-service accountability and environmental costs**. Mission execution and national strategic priorities serve different functions.
- “India has no AI strategy” is too absolute: **NITI Aayog published its National Strategy for AI discussion paper in June 2018**. The article seeks a more comprehensive Cabinet-backed/parliamentarily debated framework, not discovery that no prior policy work existed. [2018 official account](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=181007).
- Risks: foreign model/compute dependence in sensitive uses; platform/data concentration; opaque healthcare, police/welfare decisions; unequal access to gains. Protect privacy/consent, representative data, contestability and independent oversight.
- Source **65,000 jobs cut at TCS/Infosys/Wipro in 2024** is an employment-change claim, not proof AI caused all reductions. **26% workforce exposure** estimates potential task exposure, not realised job loss or certain replacement.
- Proposals: Cabinet strategy presented to Parliament, dedicated parliamentary oversight, national study of sector/region/group employment effects, reskilling and social protection. These were recommendations, not newly established institutions; Global South/GPAI leadership needs domestic credibility.

topics.title: Pelicans and painted storks
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Identification
| Bird | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| Great white pelican, Pelecanus onocrotalus |Pelecanidae; large pouch; IUCN Least Concern|
| Dalmatian pelican, P.crispus |Pelecanidae; source Near Threatened|
| Spot-billed pelican, P.philippensis |Pelecanidae; source Near Threatened; southern breeding colonies|
| Painted stork, Mycteria leucocephala |Ciconiidae; yellow-orange bill, pink tertials; tactile feeding in shallows|
- Pelicans scoop prey with expandable pouches; some fish cooperatively. Storks probe/sweep the bill; no pelican-like pouch.
- **Kokkare Bellur, Karnataka; Vedanthangal, Tamil Nadu; Ranganathittu, Karnataka; Keoladeo, Rajasthan**: important breeding/wetland examples; each bird is not equally present at every site.
## Conservation
- Maintain wetland water regimes, food availability and nesting trees; reduce pollution, disturbance and persecution; community stewardship matters.
- Source blanket “all pelicans Near Threatened” contradicts its great-white entry. Conservation assessment and legal schedule must be species/date-specific; old Schedule IV labels cannot be copied after 2022 schedule restructuring.
- Ramsar designation recognises a wetland, not automatic protection of every habitat occupied by these birds.
## Status correction
- **Painted stork: Least Concern since 2023**, replacing Near Threatened in the older notes/source. [Bird Life assessment update](https://www.birdlife.org/news/2023/12/12/the-2023-red-list-update-reveals-hope-for-birds-in-crisis/).

topics.title: India–Sri Lanka relations
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Links and cooperation
- Maritime neighbours across Palk Strait; cultural/Buddhist/diaspora ties, trade, tourism, investment and development cooperation.
- India provided~US$4 billion support during 2022 economic crisis; financial assistance, financing assurances and debt restructuring have different roles.
- India–Sri Lanka FTA operational 2000; ETCA discussions are not proof agreement is already implemented. UPI-enabled tourist payments differ from replacing Sri Lanka's currency/payment system.
- BIMSTEC/SAARC and maritime cooperation; strengthen infrastructure, training, education and reliable project delivery.
## Frictions
- Fisher arrests, destructive bottom trawling and livelihoods; 1974/1976 maritime agreements/Katchatheevu questions require precise rights distinctions, not assumed general fishing permission.
- Hambantota/Chinese engagement, smuggling and regional competition; Sri Lanka retains sovereign choices, rather than being an Indian “point of control”.
- Dated tourism/export shares should not be treated as current permanent rankings. Work on sustainable fishing, legal channels and broader people-to-people ties.
## Fisheries dispute
- **1974 Palk Strait and 1976 Gulf of Mannar/Bay of Bengal agreements** are maritime-boundary anchors. Cross-border fishing is not an unrestricted traditional entitlement.
- Bottom trawling damages seabed habitats and Northern Sri Lankan fishers' livelihoods; Sri Lanka banned it in 2017. Tamil Nadu's nearshore restriction concerns mechanised vessels, not a blanket ban on all fishers within three nautical miles.
- Combine bilateral Joint Working Group/ministers' dialogue, humane treatment/release processes, enforceable sustainable fishing and economically viable alternatives.
- Deep-sea transition needs vessel finance, training, fuel/logistics and market access; it is not automatically affordable or ecologically sustainable.

## Katchatheevu: geography and rights
- Small, uninhabited island in the **Palk Strait**, between Tamil Nadu and northern Sri Lanka; St Anthony's shrine sustains shared pilgrimage/fisher-community ties. Avoid the unsupported claim that it was formed by volcanic activity.
- **1974 maritime delimitation** placed Katchatheevu on the Sri Lankan side; **1976 agreements** further defined boundaries and cross-border fishing restrictions.
- India's official position treats sovereignty/boundary as settled. Political/legal challenges to the agreements are distinct from that executive position; do not describe every constitutional question as already finally adjudicated.
- Government statements distinguish traditional access for **resting, drying nets and pilgrimage** from a right to fish in Sri Lankan waters. Access to the island is not an unrestricted fishing licence. [Official parliamentary answer](https://rsdebate.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/235467/1/PQ_162_23031992_U3277_p84_p85.pdf), [MEA account](https://meacms.mea.gov.in/Images/pdf/India-foreign-relation-2011.pdf).
- Solutions require sustainable fishing and protection of livelihoods on both shores: bilateral dialogue, humane handling of detainees, viable vessel/skill support and alternatives to destructive bottom trawling. Proposed joint-fishing arrangements require agreement; they are not existing blanket permission.

topics.title: Bangus Valley and community ecotourism
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Map and proposal
- **Kupwara, north Kashmir, near Lo C**; two meadow bowls amid mountains/forest, reported~10, 000 feet/~100 km from Srinagar.
- March 2025 plan emphasised modest shelters, toilets, signage, waste systems and registered homestays, rather than large hotels; source 19 registered stays is a snapshot.
- Diversifies pressure away from Pahalgam/Gulmarg/Sonamarg; potential benefits to shepherds, nomadic communities and local artisans.
- Carrying capacity, waste/water, habitat disturbance, local consent and border security need coordination; PARIVESH is a clearance portal, not automatic permission.
- The source's National Tourism Policy 2022 reference concerns a draft; do not treat every proposed national policy as enacted.

topics.title: Women’s freedom in public spaces
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Inclusion beyond necessary travel
- Mobility supports work, health, politics and leisure; harassment, fear, patriarchal restrictions and victim blaming reduce autonomy.
- **Why Loiter?2011**, Phadke/Ranade/Khan: women need freedom to occupy public spaces without proving a compulsory purpose.
- Source NFHS4 market 54%/health 50%/outsidecommunity 48%unaccompanied mobility are dated survey measures, not universal travel rules.
- Source Women, Peaceand Security Index 2023 rank 128/177 is a dated composite; it is not solely a street-crime ranking.
## Action
- Lighting, accessible toilets, benches, parks, reliable transport and safe last-mile routes; women participate in design/audits.
- Enforce harassment laws, provide responsive complaint systems and accountability; CCTV/segregated transport alone cannot secure equality.
- Nirbhaya Fund/Safe City initiatives need utilisation/results assessment; surveillance must respect privacy.
- Source PLFS2023–24 female LFPR35.6%does not match the usual-status 15+annual 44.5%; cite age/status/year together. Employment, mobility and unpaid-care barriers interact.
## Shishtachar squads: safety with safeguards
- Delhi Police's district squads target street harassment/stalking and assist reporting; announced at least two per district under ACP-level Crime Against Women supervision.
- Source team design: Inspector, one Sub-Inspector, five male and four female personnel, with technical support. Deployment details are administrative plans, not proof every district already has identical functioning capacity.
- Hotspot patrols, public-transport coordination, plain-clothes observation and quick response can help; surveillance proposals need lawful use, privacy safeguards and oversight.
- **Prevent harassment without moral policing** of consensual relationships or restricting women's freedom. Train personnel, make complaints accessible and assess safety/outcomes rather than only arrests.
- UP Anti-Romeo squads and Hyderabad SHE Teams are comparison examples, not interchangeable legal frameworks.

## Institutional safety: July 2025 debate
- Balasore college student's death after alleged harassment highlighted failures in complaint handling and institutional accountability. Schools, campuses and workplaces need credible preventive systems, accessible reporting, support and fair investigation.
- POSH Act 2013: Internal Committees apply at workplaces with **10 or more workers**; Local Committees cover specified cases including smaller establishments and complaints against employers. The PDF's claim that every workplace must have its own committee ignores this distinction.
- Source NCRB **2022** snapshot: **4,45,256 registered crimes against women**, about 4% above 2021; cruelty by husband/relatives 31.4%, assault on modesty 18.7%, rape 7.1%. Registered cases do not measure all prevalence or prove a specific trend within campuses.
