- Audit committee functioning, train staff on consent/reporting, prevent retaliation, provide counselling/legal aid and hold administrators accountable through lawful procedures. Criminal-law references require date awareness: BNS replaced IPC for offences committed from July 2024.

topics.title: Women in STEM: recognition, retention and leadership
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Concepts
- **Matilda effect:** women's scientific contributions overlooked/credited to men.
- **Leaky pipeline:** attrition across career stages; **chutes/ladders:** structural barriers and supports that shape progression/re-entry.
- Biased hiring/promotion/grants, harassment, unequal care, poor mentoring and conference exclusion restrict advancement; do not attribute structural inequality merely to low confidence.
- Source 17%women faculty across 98 institutions is a study sample, not every Indian STEMinstitution.
## Supports
- Transparent recruitment/funding, pay equity, harassment redress, childcare, parental flexibility and fair career-break/re-entry criteria; mentoring and leadership representation.
- **DSTGATI2020, WISE-KIRAN/Women Scientists programmes, Bio CARe** support institutional change/research re-entry; ICMR initiatives have their own eligibility.
- Bias Watch India tracks inequities; measure retention, decision-making and credit, not only admission counts. Diversity improves opportunities without guaranteeing every team identical outcomes.

## World Youth Skills Day, July 15
- Editorial cites women as **~43% of Indian STEM graduates** versus **~27% of STEM workforce**; these are source-reported differently defined education/employment indicators, not a single cohort's measured transition rate. Retention, career progression and safe work need industry participation alongside education.
- **PLFS 2023–24, usual status, age 15+: female LFPR 41.7% overall, 47.6% rural, 28.0% urban**. Source's urban **25.4%** belongs to **2022–23**, not the same year. Participation is not identical to secure salaried technical employment. [MoSPI annual results](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2057970&lang=2&reg=48).
- Source's **WeSTEM** example brings UN Women, Madhya Pradesh/Gujarat and Micron Foundation together for technical skills, workplace safety, mentoring, role models and family/community engagement. Partnerships must address hiring, care transitions, pay, safety and leadership as well as training.
- Source Budget 2025–26 gender allocation **₹4.49 lakh crore/~8.8%** concerns gender-responsive budgeting; it should not be interpreted as money exclusively spent on women-only STEM schemes. GDP gains cited for greater women's employment are scenarios, not realised growth.

topics.title: India–US energy trade and diversification
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Security and trade
- India imports over 85%of crude requirements in source-era data; diversify among Russia, West Asia, US and other suppliers based on landed cost, refinery compatibility, reliability and geopolitics.
- February 2025 USvisit discussed expanded energy purchases and US$500 billion bilateral trade ambition; pledge is not a fixed executed procurement contract.
- Source Russia~40%share and US357, 000 barrels/day figure are period-specific, not constant shares. Imports do not inherently lower overall import dependency.
- Natural-gas share 15%goal and IEA2030~103 bcm forecast are targets/projections; LNGterminals, pipelines, pricing and demand determine absorption.
- Gas may have lower combustion CO₂than coal but remains fossil fuel; methane leakage affects climate benefits. Clean power, efficiency and electrification complement supply diversification.
- IEAassociation/support for membership is different from completed full membership. Maintain strategic autonomy and commercially viable sourcing.

topics.title: India–Mauritius: diaspora, development and maritime ties
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Relationship
- March 11–12, 2025 visit around Mauritius National Day 12 March; ~70%Indian-origin population, including descendants of indentured workers, alongside diverse communities.
- Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam/Indianfreedom links; Mahatma Gandhi Institute, cultural cooperation and World Hindi Secretariat; engage all communities, not only diaspora.
- Source FY2022–23 US$554 million trade is dated; DTAA/investment links and **CECPA2021** require rules/anti-abuse safeguards, not assumed automatic tax exemption.
- Mauritius is an African Union/Af CFTAmember; using it as an Africanbusiness hub does not automatically grant every Indian export duty-free access—rules of origin apply.
## Maritime cooperation
- Large EEZ, coastal radars, Agaléga infrastructure, hydrographic surveys and IFC-IORinformation links support capacity and maritime awareness.
- Colombo Security Conclave includes India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius, Bangladesh at sourcecheckpoint; it is not simply a military alliance directed at one country.
- Respect Mauritiansovereignty, transparent projects and blue-economy/climate needs; competition with China is one dimension of a wider relationship.
## March 2025 visit
- The 11–12 March visit expanded training, policing, financial-crime cooperation, local-currency trade and development partnerships.
- The cited development allocation is **500 million Mauritian rupees**, not ₹500 million Indian rupees. Announced police-academy, information-sharing and cultural projects are not all completed facilities.
- Cooperation supports Indian Ocean maritime security, capacity building and diaspora ties; sovereignty and local priorities remain central.

topics.title: Dual-luminescent security ink
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Material and mechanism
- INSTMohali/BARC research: **Sr₂Bi F₇, strontiumbismuthfluoride nanoparticles, dopedwitherbium/ytterbium**; coprecipitation, mixed into PVCink, screenprinted.
- Reported emissions:365 nm UV→blue; 395 nm→magenta; 980 nmnear IR→orange-red. UV/downconversion and IR/upconversion give different authentication cues.
- Potential banknotes, passports, identity documents, packaging; multilayersecurity includes visible, tactile andmachine-detectable features.
- Laboratory stability/cost claims need production validation; offset/intaglioprocess compatibility, persistence andverification devices matter. Research is not proof RBI has adoptedthisink or that counterfeiting becomes impossible.

topics.title: Shingles: latent virus and prevention
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mechanism
- **Varicella-zoster virus** causes chickenpox, remains latent in sensory ganglia and can reactivate as herpes zoster/shingles; age and impaired immunity increase risk, but cases are not confined to over 50 s.
- Pain/tingling followed by usually one-sided band-like blisters; **postherpetic neuralgia** can persist after rash resolution.
- VZV exposure from an affected person can cause chickenpox in a susceptible contact, not directly transmit “shingles” as the same clinical condition.
- Eye/neurological complications can be serious; rare deaths occur, so source “never life-threatening” is incorrect. [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/vaccines/hcp/current-vis/shingles.html).
## Public health
- **Shingrix is recombinant, non-live**; vaccination helps prevent shingles/complications. US recommendations include adults 50+ and specified immunocompromised adults 19+; national programmes/eligibility differ.
- Early clinical assessment and antiviral treatment can reduce disease severity; source “no treatment/cure” must not obscure effective management.
- Awareness, affordability and older-adult access matter; 90%prior-virus exposure/56.6%unawareness are source survey claims, not inevitable disease prevalence or nationally representative facts without methodology.
- Adding vaccination to India's programme is a proposal in this source, not proof universal rollout.

topics.title: Forum for India–Pacific Islands Cooperation
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Members and summits
- India plus 14 Pacific island partners; established 2014; complements Act East/Indo-Pacific and South–South cooperation.
- **Cook Islands, Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Nauru, Niue, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu.** Australia/New Zealand are not members; Cook Islands/Niue are not UNmember States, so not all 14 have a UNvote.
-2014 Suva, Fiji; 2015 Jaipur; 2023 Port Moresby, PNG. Source US$200 million 2015 grant claim is wrong: annual grant-in-aid was US$200, 000 **per country**, increased from US$125, 000. [President's 2015 address](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=126188).
## Cooperation
- Climate/disaster resilience, renewables, health, digital skills, education, maritime resources and fisheries; Fiji diaspora supports links but countries have distinct priorities.
- Distance/connectivity, limited capacity, project delivery and geopolitical competition constrain engagement; not every partner is uniformly debt-trapped.
- Large EEZs do not mean unrestricted mining rights for outsiders; sustainability, sovereignty and relevant marine law matter. Turn pledges into reliable locally requested projects.

topics.title: SIPRI arms transfers2020–24
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Report and metric
- SIPRI, founded 1966, Stockholm: independent institute researching conflict, armaments, disarmament; **not a UNagency**.
- March 2025 report covers **2020–24 versus 2015–19**; trend-indicator value(TIV) measures major-arms transfer volume, not market price or every defence import. [SIPRI](https://www.sipri.org/publications/2025/sipri-fact-sheets/trends-international-arms-transfers-2024).
- India second-largest importer after Ukraine, 8.3%global share; imports down 9.3%. Russia 36%of Indiaimports versus 55%priorperiod/72%2010–14; India took 28%of French exports.
- US43%global exports; France second 9.6%; Russia exports down 64%. Pakistan imports up 61%, China 81%ofits imports. Period-specific figures do not describe every later year.
## Implications
- Supplier diversification, domesticproduction and delayeddeliveries shape trends; lower TIValone does not prove every import substituted domestically or all capability gaps closed.
-36 Rafales andsource-era 26 navalvariant negotiations differ from completed naval delivery. CAATSA risk is not proofsanctionsalready imposed.
- Strengthen R&D, engines/components, private/DPSUmanufacturing, testing, spares andtimely delivery. Quad is a cooperation grouping, not a mutual-defencealliance; HALispublicsector, not a private firm.
- Exporttargets vary bydate/currency; draft DPEPP2020 is not an operative policy merelybecause named in thesource.

topics.title: India–US trade negotiations and WTO rules
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Legal distinctions
- bilateral trade agreement negotiations are not a signed FTA. A label“BTA”does not itself exempt preferential tariffs from WTO obligations.
- **MFN:GATTArticle I(goods); GATSArticle II(services)**; relevant exceptions differ. Non-discrimination is not a requirement everycountryset identicaltariffs.
- **GATTXXIV** permits qualifyingcustomsunions/FTAs covering substantiallyalltrade; interimagreements need aplan/schedule. Understanding ordinarilylimits reasonabletransitionto 10 years, with exceptionalcases explained.
- **Enabling Clause 1979** supports specified developing-country preferences/GSP and developing-country regional arrangements; it does not broadly authorise a reciprocal India–USselectiveagreement.
- **GSP** is a preferencescheme operating through applicable legal basis, not a separate treatyarticle identicalto XXIV.
## Negotiation trade-offs
- market access, services, supply chains andtechnology opportunities; farming/dairy sensitivities, standards andpolicy space need assessment.
- bound tariffs are ceilings; applied rates can differbelowthem. Demandforreciprocalrates does not automatically prove a breach—actual measures, bounds, MFN/exceptions matter.
- Safeguard WTOcompatibility andtransparent sectoral impact analysis; potentialbenefits are not guaranteedby announcement.
## WTO relevance and reform: April 2025 debate
- **Established 1 January 1995** following the Uruguay Round: wider coverage than GATT, including services/IP, negotiations, dispute settlement, trade-policy monitoring and capacity building. WTO members account for about **98% of world trade**; membership share is not proof 98% of transactions comply with every WTO rule. [WTO profile](https://www.wto.org/english/thewto_e/whatis_e/who_we_are_e.htm).
- **Doha Round launched 2001:** prolonged disagreement over agriculture, subsidies, market access and development; do not infer it produced no outcomes except fisheries. **Trade Facilitation Agreement** was concluded at Bali **2013** and entered into force **22 February 2017**. [WTO TFA](https://www.wto.org/englIsh/tratop_e/tradfa_e/tradfa_e.htm).
- **Appellate Body unable to hear new appeals since December 2019**, following blocked appointments. Panels, consultations and arbitration continue; appeals into an unavailable appellate process can obstruct finality. This serious impairment is not the complete disappearance of dispute settlement or enforcement. [WTO Appellate Body](https://www.wto.org/english/tratop_e/dispu_e/appellate_body_e.htm).

## Pressures and legal qualifications
- Unilateral tariff measures, geopolitical rivalry, subsidy/state-enterprise concerns, overcapacity and opaque notifications strain predictability. US **Section 232** steel measures and **Section 301** China measures are examples; WTO compatibility depends on the specific measures, obligations and claimed exceptions. Trump was President again in April 2025; historical Biden policies belong to an earlier administration.
- Regional arrangements such as **RCEP/CPTPP** can fragment rules and divert negotiating attention; qualifying FTAs are recognised exceptions within WTO law, not automatically breaches of MFN. WTO disciplines on subsidies/state trading exist; the challenge is adequacy, transparency and enforceability, not a total absence of rules concerning state-led economies.
- Source's “India may subsidise agriculture only up to 10%” is misleading: **10% de minimis** applies to relevant trade-distorting product-specific/non-product-specific support; Green Box, specified developing-country measures and other qualifying exemptions differ. Historical AMS entitlements and public-stockholding/food-security concerns create asymmetries. [WTO agriculture explanation](https://www.wto.org/english/tratop_e/agric_e/ag_intro03_domestic_e.htm).
- India seeks food-security safeguards, a durable public-stockholding solution and meaningful special/differential treatment. Labour/environment provisions negotiated in particular bilateral agreements do not create a universal Indian acceptance or rejection of all such provisions in the WTO.
- Transparency duties and committee scrutiny matter; weak/incomplete notifications and enforcement do not mean reporting obligations do not exist.

## Value, outcomes and reform priorities
- A common rules framework, negotiated tariff commitments, transparency and a negotiating forum matter especially to smaller/developing economies. Formal member equality does not eliminate differences in bargaining power, legal capacity or market size; decisions usually use **consensus**.
- **MC12, June 2022:** Geneva Package included fisheries-subsidy disciplines, pandemic response, a targeted COVID-19 vaccine TRIPS decision, food security and protection of WFP humanitarian food purchases. The IP outcome was not a blanket waiver of all intellectual property. Fisheries adoption in 2022 and entry into force are different milestones; do not assume the agreement was already operative in April 2025. [WTO Geneva Package](https://www.wto.org/english/thewto_e/minist_e/mc12_e/geneva_package_e.htm).
- Reform: restore effective appellate review, improve notifications/monitoring and dispute access, address subsidy/market-access concerns, and reconcile new issues with development and food security. Negotiated proposals are not enacted reforms.
- Mains balance: institutional dysfunction weakens WTO credibility, but abandoning its common framework can leave weaker economies more exposed to unilateral power. Assess negotiation, adjudication and monitoring separately; pursue reform with transparent, inclusive implementation.

## Dairy certification and India–US negotiations: July 2025
- “Non-veg milk” is a debate label for milk from animals fed certain animal-origin ingredients, not a distinct biological milk category. Market access involves feed certification, cultural preferences, sanitary regulation and small-producer livelihoods.
- India's veterinary certification has restrictions on source-animal feed; the published certificate refers to internal organs, blood meal and ruminant-origin tissues, and also animal rennet in products. Check the applicable certificate rather than generalise every animal-derived ingredient identically. [DAHD certificate](https://www.dahd.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-07/OMdated10August2020onVHCforimportofMilkandMilkProducts.pdf).
- US regulation prohibits specified mammalian proteins in ruminant feed to prevent BSE, with exemptions and additional high-risk-material controls. It is misleading to imply US cattle universally or unrestrictedly eat other cattle. [FDA feed rules](https://www.fda.gov/animal-veterinary/bovine-spongiform-encephalopathy/feed-ban-enhancement-implementation-questions-and-answers).
- Source **239.3 million tonnes Indian milk output, 2023–24**; producer-income/price-loss scenarios from import opening are estimates, not realised losses. Balance negotiation gains with livelihood impacts, credible certification and food safety; July deadline discussions did not establish a signed deal.

topics.title: Balochistan and the CPEC corridor
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Region and conflict
- The Baloch cultural region spans Pakistan, Iran and Afghanistan. Pakistan's largest province by area has copper, gold, coal and gas, but sparse population and uneven development.
- Kalat's disputed accession in 1948 and the centralising One Unit arrangement (1955–70) are historical background; the entire present province was not one uniform independent kingdom.
- Resource distribution, political representation, disappearances and alleged abuses fuel grievances. Distinguish peaceful civil protests from armed separatist violence, including the March 2025 Jaffar Express hijacking.
- **CPEC connects Kashgar in Xinjiang to Gwadar** on the Arabian Sea. Port concessions are commercial arrangements, not a transfer of Pakistani sovereignty to China.
- Infrastructure can improve connectivity; fishing livelihoods, local participation, security and accountability determine whether benefits reach residents.
## 22 May 2025: rights protests and resource governance
- Source highlights women-led demands against **enforced disappearances**, alleged extrajudicial killings and marginalisation; distinguish allegations requiring investigation and peaceful civic activism from **BLA armed violence**. The clipping's claim about the “most prominent” separatist group is descriptive, not grounds to equate all Baloch activism with terrorism.
- Map: **Quetta**, provincial capital; western Pakistan borders **Iran/Afghanistan**, with Arabian Sea coast/Gwadar. CPEC's Kashgar–Gwadar road/rail/energy links pass through **Gilgit-Baltistan/Pakistan-administered territory claimed by India**, giving the corridor a sovereignty dimension; map colours do not settle disputed boundaries.
- Fisheries concerns, jobs, education/healthcare and unequal returns from copper/gold/gas resources underpin opposition. Source **5% Pakistan GDP** has no year/series and should not be memorised. Claims of Chinese trawler exploitation need specific evidence rather than attributing all fisheries pressure to one nationality.
- A reported **40-year Gwadar operating concession** is not transfer of sovereignty or proof of an established Chinese military base. Assess actual infrastructure/agreements, local participation, environmental impacts and security arrangements; feared militarisation is a risk claim.

topics.title: Srinagar Tulip Garden
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Location and significance
- Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden: Zabarwan foothills overlooking Dal Lake, Srinagar; opened in 2007, formerly the Model Floriculture Centre.
- Roughly 30 hectares, with seven terraces; varieties and bloom dates vary by season. Its size recognition is not UNESCO World Heritage status.
- **Tulipa belongs to Liliaceae**; native chiefly to Central and south-central Asia. Spring flowering, cup-shaped flowers and varied colours support floriculture and tourism; the Netherlands is a major commercial centre.
- The spring Tulip Festival links horticulture, livelihoods and Kashmir tourism. Climate and flowering windows affect visitor planning.

topics.title: Urine recycling and percarbamide fertiliser
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Waste to resource
- Research uses porous graphitic carbon electrodes to reduce oxygen into hydrogen peroxide; interaction with recovered urea produces **percarbamide, a urea–hydrogen peroxide crystalline adduct**.
- Urea, CO(NH₂)₂, supplies nitrogen. It is not by itself a complete nitrogen–phosphorus–potassium fertiliser.
- Urine contains recoverable nutrients; the source estimates an adult's annual output at 450–680 litres, about 4 kg nitrogen and 0.3 kg phosphorus. Values vary with diet and collection.
- Reported near-100% product purity is an experimental result, not proof of commercial viability. Porosity and surface chemistry assist adsorption and reaction.
- Benefits: nutrient recovery and reduced wastewater nutrient loads. Test energy cost, pathogen/contaminant control, variable feedstock, crop response and environmental life-cycle performance before scale-up.

topics.title: Disease names, scientific precision and stigma
topics.subject: Ethics
topics.markdown:
## Naming principles
- Geographic labels can wrongly imply origin and stigmatise communities. Spanish flu describes reporting history, not an established Spanish origin; legacy examples include Delhi boil and Madura foot.
- WHO's 2015 guidance for **new common human disease names** avoids places, persons, animals and offensive terms. It does not govern scientific pathogen taxonomy or require every legacy name to change. [WHO guidance](https://www.who.int/news-room/detail/08-05-2015-who-issues-best-practices-for-naming-new-human-infectious-diseases).
- *Trichophyton indotineae* is a dermatophyte fungus associated with difficult, often terbinafine-resistant ringworm; its name does not establish where it originated.
- Mpox naming illustrates stigma reduction. Reactive arthritis replacing Reiter's eponym also reflects concerns about the person's Nazi associations; this was not simply a WHO order.
- Ethical test: scientific clarity → neutral communication → public trust → cooperation with surveillance and treatment. Criticise nomenclature without blaming patients or populations.

topics.title: Household debt and consumer credit
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Debt, assets and demand
- RBI Financial Stability Report figures cited in the source: household debt/GDP rose from **36.6% in June 2021 to 42.9% in June 2024**.
- Household financial assets/GDP fell from 110.4% to 108.3% in the cited comparison. This excludes much physical wealth; a falling ratio does not prove absolute assets declined.
- Prime/subprime classifications measure credit risk, not income classes exactly. Source estimates link more super-prime borrowing to asset creation and more subprime borrowing to consumption; their scope and date matter.
- Unsecured personal loans, credit cards and BNPL can smooth consumption but raise debt-service stress. Existing repayments can reduce disposable income and future demand; effects depend on household circumstances.
- NPA classification follows applicable borrower-wise rules within a bank; every late payment does not automatically make every loan across all banks an NPA.
- Better underwriting must consider aggregate obligations, transparent charges, affordability, grievance redress and financial literacy while avoiding indiscriminate exclusion.

topics.title: Dubai greenfield FDI and Indian investment
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Read the ranking correctly
- Dubai ranked first in **greenfield project count** for a fourth consecutive year in 2024, and fourth in greenfield capital attracted—not first in every measure of FDI.
- India supplied 21.5% of estimated greenfield FDI capital in the cited ranking; US 13.7%, France 11%, UK 10%, Switzerland 6.9%. [Dubai's official results](https://www.dubaidet.gov.ae/en/newsroom/press-releases/dubai-top-destination-for-greenfield-fdi-for-fourth-year).
- Greenfield investment establishes new operations; brownfield investment uses/acquires existing operations.
- Connectivity between Asia, Europe and Africa, business services, talent mobility and India–UAE CEPA support investment. A favourable tax environment does not mean every business pays zero corporate tax.
- Lawful outward FDI is not automatically panic-driven capital flight. Evaluate market access, diversification and networks alongside domestic investment needs and financial flows.

topics.title: Phased-array radar and strategic early warning
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## How it works
- Electronic phase control across antenna elements steers a beam rapidly without mechanically rotating the whole antenna. It can track multiple targets and support ballistic-missile early warning.
- Detection is not interception. Range depends on frequency, power, target characteristics, height, terrain and Earth's curvature; a claimed 5,000 km range does not imply detection of every low-flying aircraft at that distance.
- The source reports a Chinese long-range radar in Yunnan; its operational performance claims require independent verification.
- US **PAVE PAWS**: PAWS means Phased Array Warning System; PAVE is a programme code name. The source's expanded PAVE wording is incorrect.
- Advanced radar capabilities are not confined to the US, Russia and China; India and other countries also operate relevant systems.
- Strategic implications: tracking and warning, intelligence about tests, and requirements for resilient communications and survivable deterrence. APJ Abdul Kalam Island is off Odisha.

topics.title: APAAR student identity and educational records
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Purpose and safeguards
- **Automated Permanent Academic Account Registry**: a 12-digit lifelong student identifier, linking educational records through DigiLocker and the Academic Bank of Credits.
- ABC stores academic credits for transfer, not money. Identity infrastructure does not by itself make credentials accurate or ensure credit acceptance by every institution.
- Participation and informed consent, including parental consent for minors, matter. A saturation target should not turn a voluntary identifier into a condition for access to education.
- Privacy chronology: Puttaswamy privacy judgment **2017**; Aadhaar judgment **2018**. DPDP Act was enacted in 2023, although its main provisions were not operative in March 2025.
- Risks: mismatched records, exclusion, unnecessary Aadhaar linkage, profiling and breaches. Encryption alone cannot prevent misuse.
- Safeguards: purpose limitation, minimum data, clear consent/alternatives, correction, access controls, independent audit and accessible grievance redress.

topics.title: Mission Amrit Sarovar and pond restoration
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Mission and implementation
- Launched on **24 April 2022**, with the initial objective of developing/rejuvenating at least 75 ponds per district; Ministry of Rural Development coordinates convergence across programmes and ministries.
- MGNREGA, community participation and local institutions can support construction and maintenance. Original 2023 milestones and later 2025 proposals refer to different phases.
- Railways' proposed use of desilted material for embankments links water restoration to infrastructure; suitability and contamination require testing.
- Potential benefits: storage, recharge, livelihoods and biodiversity. Recharge depends on local geology and hydrology, not merely excavation.
- Choose appropriate sites, prevent encroachment, preserve drainage, monitor water quality and finance long-term maintenance; avoid treating completion counts as proof of ecological recovery.

topics.title: Small modular reactors and India's nuclear mission
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Reactor distinctions
| Concept | Key point |
|---|---|
| SMR | Usually up to 300 MWe per module; modular manufacture and deployment |
| Bharat Small Reactor (BSR) | Existing 220 MWe pressurised heavy-water reactor approach |
| BSMR-200 | Developing 200 MWe pressurised **light-water** reactor; not a PHWR |
- **3 April 2025 DAE answer:** concept design complete, detailed engineering underway; erection/start-up expected about **six years after financial approval**, regular operation by the end of the **seventh year**. These are approval-dependent estimates. BARC/NPCIL lead development; competitive private component/EPC supply does not imply unrestricted private reactor ownership. [DAE clarification](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2118377&lang=2&reg=48).
- Slightly enriched uranium is an option; do not assume every Indian reactor uses natural uranium. Passive/engineered safety systems require independent licensing; **nuclear is non-fossil, not renewable**.
## Policy and deployment
- **Budget 2025–26**, not Budget 2024: ₹20,000 crore Nuclear Energy Mission for SMR R&D and at least five indigenous SMRs targeted by **2033**. Funding is not solely for one reactor. **100 GW by 2047** is a capacity ambition, not achieved output.
- Potential uses: captive power for steel/cement/aluminium, smaller grids and suitable remote demand, and assessed reuse of coal-plant land/grid infrastructure. Cooling water, safety zones, security, waste, licensing and viable demand still matter.
- Factory fabrication, standardisation and staged investment may reduce construction/financing burdens; cheaper electricity, rapid delivery and accident immunity are **not guaranteed** before commercial replication.
- Fleet map: **Tarapur—Maharashtra; Rawatbhata—Rajasthan; Kakrapar—Gujarat; Narora—UP; Kaiga—Karnataka; Kalpakkam/Kudankulam—Tamil Nadu**. Indigenous 700 MWe PHWRs form the larger-reactor route alongside SMRs. Use the dated fleet snapshot in Nuclear power for capacity/counts, rather than the source's inconsistent totals.
## Fuel cycle and Mains assessment
- Three-stage strategy: natural-uranium PHWRs → plutonium fast breeders → thorium/U-233 systems. Reprocessing recovers usable uranium/plutonium but does not eliminate waste, cost, security or proliferation concerns.
- Assess fuel/enrichment supply, vendor capability, financing/offtake, independent oversight, liability, emergency planning and long-term spent-fuel management. Supplier participation and proposed legal amendments must be distinguished from operative ownership/licensing rules.

topics.title: Tamil rupee logo and linguistic federalism
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Identity and constitutional context
- Tamil Nadu's 2025–26 Budget logo used **ரூ**, associated with the Tamil word for rupee. It did not replace RBI-issued currency or the national currency symbol.
- **₹**, adopted in 2010 and designed by D. Udaya Kumar, combines Devanagari र and the Latin R.
- Tamil is one of the 22 Eighth Schedule languages. The banknote language panel has 15 languages, with Hindi and English elsewhere—not only 15 languages on the whole note.
- Article 345 concerns State official-language adoption. Article 347 concerns a Presidential direction recognising a language where a substantial proportion demands it; these are distinct powers.
- Evaluate regional cultural representation, communication and federal accommodation. Political claims about legality are not automatically judicial findings.

topics.title: PM-JAY coverage and fraud control
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Scheme and accountability
- Launched on 23 September 2018; National Health Authority and State agencies administer cashless hospital coverage of **₹5 lakh per family per year** for eligible secondary/tertiary care, with portability.
- Original socio-economic eligibility was expanded in 2024 to people aged **70 and above regardless of income**. It is not universal hospital insurance for every age group.
- Source committee figures on suspensions, de-empanelment and penalties are dated enforcement information; allegations, recommendations, final penalties and criminal convictions are distinct.
- Risks: ghost claims, inflated bills, unnecessary procedures, identity misuse and denial of eligible care. Administrative errors should not automatically be labelled fraud.
- Combine claim analytics with clinical review, beneficiary feedback, medical-necessity checks, due process and recovery/penalties where established.
- Digital trails help audits; blockchain cannot make false input true. Protect patient privacy and preserve accessible appeals and timely legitimate payments.
## June 2025: enforcement figures and audit
- Source repeats a committee account: **600 hospitals recommended for suspension, 1,113 removal, ₹122 crore penalties on 1,504**. March **12, 2025** report and recommendations are distinct from final implementation; do not add categories as necessarily unique hospitals.
- **4 April 2025 parliamentary reply** reported actions: **549 suspended, 1,114 de-empanelled, ₹122 crore penalties on 1,504**, based on States/UTs. Different snapshot/stage explains why the figures differ; de-empanelment is not proof of criminal conviction. [Lok Sabha record](https://eparlib.sansad.in/bitstream/123456789/2990875/1/lsd_18_IV_04-04-2025.pdf).
- **₹5 lakh/family/year** covers eligible secondary/tertiary hospital care; source **12.37 crore families/bottom 40%** describes socio-economic coverage, not universal insurance for all citizens. The separate **70+ income-independent expansion** is already recorded.
- Detect ghost patients, inflated/fake bills, eligibility misuse and medically unnecessary procedures through claim analytics, clinical audits, beneficiary feedback and verification. Higher fraudulent claims threaten public budgets/quality/trust; this does not mechanically mean every beneficiary pays higher premiums.
- Recommendations: coordinated Centre–State anti-fraud units, transparent due-process suspension/de-empanelment/recovery, accessible grievances, provider compliance and timely genuine payments. AI flags need expert review, explanations and privacy; **blockchain cannot make a false diagnosis/input true** or guarantee tamper-proof administration.
- PDF's NHS/US/Australia examples are broad comparisons, not a verified universal protocol or requirement for biometric authentication in all Australian healthcare.

topics.title: Hantavirus: transmission and disease forms
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Revision facts
- Current family: **Hantaviridae**, order Bunyavirales; Bunyaviridae is an older classification.
- Infection commonly follows inhalation of material contaminated by rodent urine, droppings or saliva; contact and bites can also transmit infection.
- **HPS** predominates in the Americas and affects the lungs; **HFRS** predominates in Asia/Europe and involves haemorrhagic/renal illness. Fatality differs substantially by virus and setting.
- Person-to-person spread is uncommon, but **Andes virus is an exception**; “never transmitted between humans” is incorrect.
- HPS may progress from fever, muscle aches and gastrointestinal symptoms to severe respiratory illness. Management is clinical supportive care; severe cases may need respiratory or renal support.
- There is no US-licensed HPS vaccine or specific curative treatment. This narrower statement must not be converted into “no vaccine for any hantavirus disease anywhere”. [CDC overview](https://www.cdc.gov/hantavirus/hcp/clinical-overview/hps.html).
- Prevention centres on rodent exclusion and safe cleanup; avoid dry sweeping contaminated material. Risk follows exposure, not a universal age-based rule.

topics.title: H1N1 influenza
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Essential distinctions
- Influenza A subtype **H1N1**: haemagglutinin type 1 and neuraminidase type 1. The 2009 pandemic strain, A(H1N1)pdm09, now circulates seasonally.
- Human seasonal infection does not require contact with pigs. Respiratory particles are important; “swine flu” is an imprecise label for all current infections.
- Fever, cough, sore throat, myalgia and fatigue may occur; pneumonia and respiratory failure are possible complications. Influenza B is a separate type, not H1N1-B.
- **Seasonal influenza vaccines include an H1N1 component**; the source's no-vaccine claim is false. Antiviral treatments exist, with clinical decisions based on risk and severity. [CDC vaccine composition](https://www.cdc.gov/flu/about/season/vaccine-selection.htm).
- India's first confirmed pandemic H1N1 cases were reported in May 2009. Prevention combines vaccination, ventilation, respiratory hygiene and appropriate clinical care.

topics.title: North Sea geography and shipping risks
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Map anchors
- A shallow continental-shelf sea of the north-eastern Atlantic, between Great Britain and north-western continental Europe.
- Coastal countries: UK, Norway, Denmark, Germany, Netherlands, Belgium and France. It opens northward to the Atlantic and south-westward through the Dover Strait/English Channel.
- Skagerrak–Kattegat–Danish straits connect toward the Baltic. Important river systems include Rhine–Meuse–Scheldt, Elbe, Weser, Ems, Thames and Humber.
- Oil/gas, fisheries, shipping and offshore energy are major uses. Approximate area estimates vary with boundaries.
- The March 2025 Solong–Stena Immaculate collision off eastern England illustrates fuel-spill, fire, shipping-safety and coastal-ecosystem risks; early reports do not establish final pollutant fate.

topics.title: Sarus crane conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Identification and habitat
- **Antigone antigone**; older synonym *Grus antigone*. Tallest flying bird, roughly 1.5 m tall, with grey plumage and a conspicuous red head/upper neck.
- Found in South/South-East Asia and Australia; Indian strongholds include the Gangetic plains and eastern Rajasthan.
- Wetlands, marshes, flooded fields and agricultural landscapes support feeding and nesting. Generally resident with local movements; nesting pairs and seasonal social behaviour vary.
- **IUCN Vulnerable; CITES Appendix II**. Older statutory schedules in source material should not be treated as current after India's wildlife-law amendments.
- Wetland loss, drainage, disturbance and agricultural intensification threaten breeding. Protect nesting habitat and work with farming communities; very long lifespan claims about cranes generally should not be assigned to this species without evidence.

topics.title: Exercise Khanjar and India–Kyrgyzstan cooperation
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## March 2025 edition
- The 12th India–Kyrgyzstan joint special-forces exercise was scheduled for 10–23 March 2025 in Kyrgyzstan.
- Began in 2011 at Nahan; hosting alternates. Indian Para Special Forces and Kyrgyz Scorpion Brigade train in counter-terrorism, mountain operations and interoperability.
- Defence engagement builds skills and bilateral trust; an exercise is not a mutual-defence treaty.
- Nowruz is a regional spring festival celebrated across several societies, not exclusively a Kyrgyz festival.

topics.title: Lunar surface temperatures and accessible ice
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Measurement versus inference
- Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander carried **ChaSTE**, developed by PRL and VSSC, to probe approximately the upper 10 cm of lunar regolith near 69.37°S—not at the exact South Pole.
- Measurements ran during the lunar day, 24 August–2 September 2023. Reported surface temperatures differed strongly between nearby sites, illustrating slope-related thermal variation.
- A quoted night temperature near −181°C is a model estimate, **not ChaSTE's direct overnight measurement**.
- Modelling indicates pole-facing slopes steeper than about 14° at suitable high latitudes can permit shallow stable ice. This is not direct proof of ice at every such site. [ISRO research account](https://www.isro.gov.in/ISRO_EN/India_Bags_Credit_First-Ever_In-Situ_Measurement.html).
- Water could support life support and fuel/oxygen production through in-situ resource utilisation; abundance, extraction, energy and engineering feasibility still require investigation.
- Chandrayaan-1's water-molecule evidence and Chandrayaan-3's thermal measurements answer different questions. India joined the Artemis Accords in 2023.
## ChaSTE instrument and exam traps
- **Chandra's Surface Thermophysical Experiment** on Vikram used a controlled probe with **10 temperature sensors**, reaching roughly **10 cm** into regolith; its deployment and thermal measurements inform instrument/material design.
- ChaSTE at **69.37°S** measured high southern-latitude temperatures; this is not the exact geographic pole. Slope/illumination and shallow insulating regolith cause strong local variation.
- Temperature-based conditions for possible stable ice are **not direct detection of water ice**. Permanently shadowed cold traps and illuminated lander-site measurements must not be conflated. [ISRO research account](https://www.isro.gov.in/ISRO_EN/India_Bags_Credit_First-Ever_In-Situ_Measurement.html).
- “First” applies to this regional/surface measurement achievement; Apollo 15 and 17 already deployed lunar heat-flow experiments. [NASA records](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20150004428). ChaSTE is not the first successful thermal probe anywhere on the Moon.
- Other worlds present different penetration challenges: InSight's HP3 mole lacked adequate regolith friction; Philae's limited hammer penetration on its comet does not establish one deployment method universally superior.
- Thermal data support future habitat, power-system and resource-use planning; they do not themselves establish commercially extractable ice or a completed lunar base.

topics.title: Jalantheeswarar Temple at Thakkolam
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Heritage anchors
- Thakkolam, Ranipet district, Tamil Nadu; associated with the historical name Thiruvooral and Shiva worship.
- Pallava origins, subsequent Chola expansion and later Nayak contributions illustrate layered temple patronage; not every visible structure belongs to the founding period.
- The sand lingam is associated with **Theenda Thirumeni**, worship without direct touching. A tiered gopuram and granite enclosure are prominent architectural features.
- One of the **Paadal Petra Sthalams** celebrated in Tevaram hymns; associated with Sambandar's seventh-century devotional tradition.
- Inscriptions, architecture and ritual practice are complementary historical evidence. Conservation status should not be assumed to be ASI protection without a verified notification.

topics.title: Bar-headed goose and Himalayan migration
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Identification and adaptation
- **Anser indicus; IUCN Least Concern**. Pale grey/white body, two dark bars on the head and orange-yellow bill/legs; sexes look similar, with males generally larger.
- Breeds around high-altitude lakes in Central Asia and winters in South Asia, including India. A March 2025 Arunachal sighting is an occurrence record, not proof of a newly established breeding range.
- Himalayan migration is aided by efficient oxygen uptake, circulation and flight physiology. Very high maximum flight reports do not describe every bird's routine route.
- Threats include wetland degradation, hunting and disturbance; secure breeding and wintering habitats along the migratory network.

topics.title: T-72 tanks and engine upgrades
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Upgrade rather than new fleet
- A March 2025 contract with Rosoboronexport, reported at US$248 million, concerns **1,000 horsepower engines** replacing existing 780 HP engines; 1,000 is the power rating, not the number ordered.
- Supply and technology transfer involve fully built and knocked-down configurations, with work at Heavy Vehicles Factory, Avadi.
- T-72 is a Soviet-origin tank family; variant-dependent features include a 125 mm smoothbore gun, autoloader and machine guns.
- More engine power can improve mobility; outcomes depend on transmission, reliability, maintenance and terrain. Local assembly and technology transfer are not identical to wholly indigenous components or intellectual property.

topics.title: US travel restrictions and vetting proposals
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## March 2025 proposal
- Reports described a draft covering 41 countries: possible full restrictions, partial restrictions and conditional compliance reviews. **A reported draft is not an operative travel ban**.
- Afghanistan, Iran, Syria, Cuba and North Korea appeared among proposed full-restriction examples; Myanmar and Haiti among partial examples; Pakistan among conditional-review examples.
- The January 2025 vetting direction, 2017 executive orders and the 2018 *Trump v. Hawaii* judgment concern different instruments and periods.
- Assess security screening alongside family separation, refugee protection, non-discrimination and diplomatic effects. Predictions of retaliation or economic loss are not already observed outcomes.
## June 4 proclamation: draft versus adopted measure
- PDF juxtaposes a **March 2025 reported 41-country draft** with the new **4 June 2025 proclamation**. Its “2024 proposal” table label is wrong; the March memo was not the June final list.
- June measure, effective **9 June 2025, 12:01 a.m. EDT**: full entry restrictions for **Afghanistan, Myanmar/Burma, Chad, Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Eritrea, Haiti, Iran, Libya, Somalia, Sudan, Yemen**; partial restrictions for **Burundi, Cuba, Laos, Sierra Leone, Togo, Turkmenistan, Venezuela**.
- Scope generally covers designated nationals **outside the US and without a valid visa at the effective date**, with exceptions/waivers including permanent residents, qualifying dual nationals, official categories and specified family/sporting/SIV cases. Partial restrictions target immigrant and specified visitor/student/exchange categories, rather than an identical ban on every visa. [White House proclamation](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/06/restricting-the-entry-of-foreign-nationals-to-protect-the-united-states-from-foreign-terrorists-and-other-national-security-and-public-safety-threats/).
- Older draft breakdown **10 full /5 partial /26 conditional**, including proposed 60-day vetting reviews, is not a completed June rule for all 41. Pakistan/Syria/North Korea examples in that draft must not be inserted into the June 19-country list.
- Claimed justification: identity/vetting gaps, information sharing, security and overstays; these are administration rationales, not a conclusion that every affected citizen is dangerous.
- **2017 seven-country orders**, subsequent revised proclamation and **2018 Trump v. Hawaii** judgment have separate dates/scope; earlier judicial approval is not automatic adjudication of the June 2025 instrument.
- Mains: security screening versus proportionality, families/refugees/students/business mobility and diplomatic reciprocity; possible challenges or retaliation are scenarios, not already established results.

topics.title: Uniyala keralensis and Western Ghats endemism
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Discovery and conservation
- *Uniyala keralensis*: Asteraceae shrub with light-purple flowers, roughly 1–3 m tall; reported from Agasthyamalai slopes in south-western India, around 700–1,400 m elevation.
- Collected in 1998 by E. S. Santhosh Kumar and S. M. Shareef; initially mistaken for a related taxon. The genus honours botanist B. P. Uniyal.
- Larger leaves, longer petioles and fewer lateral veins distinguish it from compared relatives. Source field estimates describe about 5,000 individuals in four populations; these are survey results, not a permanent population total.
- Authors' suggested Data Deficient status is **not automatically a formal IUCN listing**; Data Deficient does not mean safe.
- Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve spans Kerala and Tamil Nadu and joined UNESCO's biosphere network in 2016. Biosphere recognition differs from the Western Ghats World Heritage serial property.

topics.title: Melioidosis and environmental exposure
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Organism and public health
- Caused by **Burkholderia pseudomallei**, a bacterium in soil and water. Entry can occur through skin inoculation, inhalation or ingestion; it is not a mosquito-borne disease.
- Manifestations range from skin infection to pneumonia and severe sepsis. Diagnosis and prolonged treatment require clinical expertise; confusion with other bacteria can delay care.
- An Odisha study of 144 cases during 2015–23 linked case patterns with environmental/weather conditions. Association does not establish that every weather variable independently causes infection.
- Modelled global burden is distinct from laboratory-confirmed reported cases. The source's inconsistent India-versus-South-Asia percentage should not be memorised as a verified national share.
- Improve laboratory identification, exposure awareness and surveillance, particularly around monsoon conditions and occupational contact with soil/water.

topics.title: Chandrayaan-5 and lunar polar exploration
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Missions and goals
- March 2025 reporting described approval for the India–Japan **LUPEX/Chandrayaan-5** lunar polar mission: ISRO lander and JAXA rover roles, investigating water and regolith.
- A reported approximately 250 kg rover was a design-stage figure, not final delivered hardware; Chandrayaan-3's Pragyan was approximately 26 kg.
- Chandrayaan-4 is a separate sample-return programme approved in September 2024. Proposed launch dates are targets.
| Mission | Milestone |
|---|---|
| Chandrayaan-1 | Launched 22 October 2008; water-molecule evidence |
| Chandrayaan-2 | Launched 22 July 2019; orbiter science continued despite landing failure |
| Chandrayaan-3 | Launched 14 July 2023; soft landing 23 August 2023 |
- Polar-region landing is not landing at the exact geographic pole. Larger payload capacity does not itself prove ice extraction capability.
## 13–14 May 2025 : technical coordination
- ISRO/JAXA technical-interface meeting **TIM 3, Bengaluru**, addressed **Chandrayaan 5/LUPEX**. Source reports JAXA’s H 3-24 Llauncher and Japanese rover; **ISROlander** and Indian instrument contributions; payloads from ISRO, JAXA, ESA, NASA to study water/volatile distribution and subsurface regolith.
- Named planned instruments **MIR, APXS**, a sampler and thermal/material studies support resource characterisation; design meetings do not mean hardware launch or commercial ice extraction.
- Chandrayaan 4 is a separate sample-return programme. Clipping’s “2027–28 ” is a planning timeline, not an accomplished launch.

topics.title: Yemen, Houthis and Red Sea shipping
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Conflict and geography
- Houthis/Ansar Allah emerged from northern Yemen's Zaidi Shia context; took Sana'a in 2014. Saudi-led intervention began in 2015. Yemen is not under one uncontested national authority.
- **Bab el-Mandeb links the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden**, between Yemen and the Djibouti/Eritrea side of the African coast.
- US strikes on 15 March 2025 and Houthi retaliation were reported; early casualty figures and claims of hits require attribution and later verification.
- Iranian support does not establish identical control over every aligned group. Hamas is Sunni; the loosely described “Axis of Resistance” is not uniformly Shia.
- Shipping reroutes via the Cape of Good Hope raise journey time, insurance and freight costs, affecting Indian trade and energy supplies.
- Self-defence claims under UN Charter Article 51 require analysis of necessity and proportionality; invoking the Article is not a final ruling that every strike is lawful. Civilian protection remains essential.
## Movement and regional context
- **Ansar Allah** means “Partisans of God”; the Houthi movement developed in the **1990s** in northern Yemen's Zaidi Shia setting, with armed conflict against the government beginning in **2004**. Zaidism differs from Twelver Shiism; Yemen's war involves political, tribal and regional interests as well as sectarian identity.
- Arab Spring upheaval in **2011** weakened the existing political order. Houthi control of Sana'a in **2014**, Saudi-led intervention and Iranian support internationalised the conflict. Anti-US/anti-Israel rhetoric is part of the movement's political messaging; territorial shares vary and do not measure population control.
- **Land neighbours:** Saudi Arabia to the north and Oman to the east. Across surrounding waters lie **Djibouti, Eritrea and Somalia**. Red Sea → Bab el-Mandeb → Gulf of Aden → Arabian Sea is the maritime sequence.
- India’s **Operation Rahat (2015)** evacuated Indians and foreign nationals from Yemen. Protecting seafarers, diaspora and trade corridors remains relevant alongside humanitarian relief and diplomacy. [MEA Operation Rahat](https://www.mea.gov.in/Images/amb1/lu1509_aneexr.pdf).

topics.title: Mangrove ecosystems and restoration
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Ecology and distribution
- Salt-tolerant intertidal forests of tropical/subtropical coasts, estuaries and deltas. Pneumatophores, stilt roots, salt filtering/excretion and vivipary vary among species; not every mangrove has every adaptation.
- Indian examples: Sundarbans, Gujarat's coast/Kutch, Bhitarkanika, Pichavaram and Andaman–Nicobar. West Bengal has the largest State extent.
- ISFR 2021 reported about **4,992 sq km**, roughly 0.15% of India's geographical area; 2023's 4,991.68 sq km is essentially the same rounded scale, not a large national doubling.
- Functions: fish nurseries, shoreline stabilisation, carbon storage in biomass/soil and wave-energy reduction. They cannot guarantee complete cyclone protection.
## Restoration and interpreting studies
- Restore tidal hydrology and suitable native communities, not merely plant saplings anywhere. Control invasive vegetation while avoiding damage to existing habitat.
- Tamil Nadu study estimates of 4,500 ha in 2021 and 9,039 ha in 2024 use their own survey/mapping scope; do not equate them automatically with an official FSI series.
- **Carbon stock is not annual sequestration**, and tonnes of carbon differ from tonnes of CO₂. Compare methods, pools, area and dates.
- CRZ regulation and community stewardship support protection. Mangrove Alliance for Climate is a voluntary initiative, not a binding treaty.
- Carbon credits need credible baselines, additionality, permanence and safeguards for local rights.
## PYQ recall
- The combination of mangrove, evergreen and deciduous forests points to **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**; distinguish biome combinations from a single species' range.

## Swaminathan and restoration
- **M. S. Swaminathan**, founder-president of **International Society for Mangrove Ecosystems (ISME), established 1990 in Okinawa**, promoted mangroves for coastal protection, salinity-related food security and research on salt tolerance. ISME developed knowledge networks/manuals and **GLOMIS** information sharing.
- **Charter for Mangroves** was submitted to UNCED in **1992** as an annex to the World Charter for Nature; do not misdate the original World Charter for Nature itself to 1992. [ISME history](https://mangrove.or.jp/img/newsletter/ISMENews 33.pdf).
- MSSRF's **fishbone canal** approach restores tidal flushing/hydrology in degraded mangroves, tested along Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and West Bengal; complemented by **Joint Mangrove Management** and community participation. Clear-felling can alter drainage/salinity, so degradation must not automatically be attributed to local people.
- Source recalls coastal buffering in the **1999 Odisha supercyclone** and **2004 tsunami**; protection varies with forest width, health, terrain and event intensity. Invasive **Prosopis juliflora**, aquaculture, construction and pollution remain pressures.
- **ISFR 2023:4,991.68 km²,0.15%** of geographical area. The PDF's “+16.68 km² since 2019” does not establish the latest two-year trend; keep comparable assessment baselines distinct. [Mo EFCC statement](https://www.pib.gov.in/Press Release Iframe Page.aspx?PRID=2115836&lang=2&reg=48).
- Graphic additions: **26 July**, International Day for Conservation of the Mangrove Ecosystem; **MISHTI**, Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes, Budget 2023–24. **Mangrove Alliance for Climate**, launched by UAE/Indonesia at COP 27 in 2022, includes India; voluntary conservation cooperation, not an enforceable treaty.

topics.title: India–New Zealand relations
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## March 2025 engagement
- Diplomatic ties date to 1952; Commonwealth links, education, migration, tourism and diaspora connect the countries.
- PM Christopher Luxon's visit and relaunch of FTA negotiations occurred in **March 2025**, not 2024. Earlier negotiations began in 2010. Negotiations in this update are not a signed FTA. [Joint statement](https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/india-new-zealand-joint-statement/).
- Trade opportunities: Indian pharmaceuticals, engineering, textiles and services; New Zealand horticulture, wool, wood and other products. Dairy sensitivities, farmer interests and standards require negotiation.
- Defence cooperation, maritime security and counter-terrorism featured alongside mobility. Distinguish peaceful expression from violence/incitement; political allegations do not prove criminality.
- New Zealand is an **IORA dialogue partner**, not a member; it belongs to APEC, while India does not. Common participation in other forums must be checked individually.
- President Pranab Mukherjee visited in 2016; the source's Kovind/2018 attribution is incorrect. Diaspora/student totals require year and definition rather than merging incompatible estimates.

topics.title: Satellite broadband, licensing and digital inclusion
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Network and economics
- Starlink uses many low-Earth-orbit satellites, user terminals, gateways and inter-satellite links. Lower orbital height can reduce latency compared with geostationary systems.
- Performance depends on coverage, congestion, obstructions, weather and power; advertised speeds/latency are not guaranteed at every location.
- March 2025 Jio/Airtel distribution announcements were **conditional on regulatory approvals**, not proof that Indian commercial service had launched.
- Terminal/subscription estimates in reports were not final officially announced Indian tariffs. Affordability and reliable power can limit inclusion even where geographic coverage exists.
## Regulation and public interest
- DoT licensing, security requirements, spectrum allocation and relevant IN-SPACe authorisations are separate functions; Home Ministry clearance is not the sole licence.
- Telecommunications Act 2023 provides administrative allocation for listed satellite services. The 2012 natural-resources advisory opinion did not make auction the sole constitutional method for every resource.
- Safeguard lawful interception, privacy, secure gateways, fair competition and emergency resilience; commercial coverage is not automatically a secure military network.
- Orbital debris, collision avoidance and sustainable spectrum/orbit use accompany digital-inclusion benefits.
## Starlink licence: 6 June 2025
- **DoT granted Unified Licence** authorisations for **GMPCS, Commercial VSAT CUG and ISP Category A** to **Starlink Satellite Communications Private Limited on 6 June**. This advances approval beyond the March distribution announcements; separate spectrum, relevant space authorisation, security/testing and commercial rollout stages still matter. [Official parliamentary confirmation](https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/268/AU3216_S4YKT2.pdf?source=pqars).
- Source describes Starlink as **third after OneWeb/Jio Satellite**; **Amazon Kuiper awaiting approval** in this dated snapshot. June 7 practice answer **(b),1,3,4** concerns licensing status at that time, not universal current service availability.
- Proposed **trial spectrum within 15–20 days** was an expectation, not a confirmed allocation/delivery deadline; security obligations include lawful interception.
- Diagram compares **LEO/MEO/GEO**: lower altitude generally reduces propagation delay but needs constellation/handover support; **Starlink uses LEO**. Existing notes retain affordability, gateway/power/coverage and debris qualifications.

## Orbit comparison and dual use
| Orbit | Approximate altitude | Communications trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **LEO** | Below 2,000 km | Lower propagation delay; many satellites, tracking and handovers |
| **MEO** | Between LEO and GEO | Wider footprints than LEO; constellation still required (e.g. O3b) |
| **GEO** | ~35,786 km above equator | Appears fixed; broad footprint, high propagation delay, poorer polar coverage |
- A GEO satellite can see roughly one-third of Earth geometrically; usable coverage depends on elevation/beam/service constraints. Illustrative source latency **LEO20–40 ms, MEO150 ms, GEO600 ms** is end-to-end/system dependent, not a universal orbital constant.
- Remote mountains/islands/deserts can have high terrestrial cost per user; satellite links support ships/aircraft, telemedicine, farming and disaster recovery. Ground gateways, terminals, power and backhaul remain necessary network elements.
- **Dual use:** civilian and military communications, drone/support networks and remote-border backup; also potential illicit-device use. Secure access, control, interception/privacy rules and resilience matter.
- Source **US$500 terminal +US$50/month** is an illustrative overseas/report estimate, not an announced Indian tariff. Direct-to-device technology, scale and competition may lower costs; predicted price convergence is not assured. Practice: **all three (D)**; the explanation's “statement4” means its third statement.

topics.title: India–China relations and border normalisation
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Distinguish disengagement and normalisation
- Galwan violence in 2020 damaged relations. October 2024 arrangements concerning Depsang and Demchok preceded the Modi–Xi meeting at **Kazan on 23 October 2024**, not 2023.
- Disengagement at specified points is not complete de-escalation, border settlement or restoration of trust. “Stable” and “normal” reflect different assessments.
- Flights, visas, pilgrimages and journalist access were diplomatic agenda items; announcements do not prove every channel was already restored.
- Long cultural/commercial contact coexists with the **1962 war** and later clashes; “no history of conflict” is incorrect.
- India's April 2020 Press Note 3 imposes approval requirements for relevant land-border-country investment; it is not a universal ban on all Chinese FDI.
- Trade asymmetry, CPEC through Pakistan-occupied territory and Indian Ocean competition accompany cooperation in multilateral forums. Quad cooperation is not automatically a mutual-defence alliance.
## Recall correction
- The LAC is a disputed line of actual control, **not an agreed, fully demarcated international boundary**. India fought China in 1962.
- “Largest trading partner” depends on year and whether goods or goods-plus-services are measured; a dated ranking must not become a timeless statement.

topics.title: India–Australia defence policy cooperation
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Ninth Defence Policy Talks
- Held in New Delhi on **17 March 2025**; covered maritime awareness, information-sharing, industry/science cooperation and interoperability. [Defence Ministry account](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2111839&lang=2&reg=48).
- The 2020 Mutual Logistics Support Arrangement enables agreed support/access; it does not grant unlimited ownership of each other's bases.
- Malabar/Quad participation differs from **AUKUS**, of which India is not a member.
- ECTA became operational in 2022; broader CECA negotiations are a separate process. Procurement ideas and cooperation proposals are not completed hardware contracts.
- Balance maritime security and technology opportunities with strategic autonomy, domestic capacity and regulatory safeguards.
## 4 May 2025: Australian election
- **3 May federal election:** Anthony Albanese’s **Labor Party** won reelection; he claimed a second term. The clipping reports opposition Liberal leader **Peter Dutton** conceded and lost his seat. Early majority projections are distinct from final certified seat totals. [Prime Minister’s election-night speech](https://www.pm.gov.au/media/election-night).
- Campaign priorities included renewable energy, housing and healthcare; Dutton advocated lower migration and nuclear energy. These were political platforms, not completed policy outcomes. Australia’s parliamentary election returns MPs; voters do not directly elect the Prime Minister.

topics.title: Construction workers and portable welfare
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Coverage and access barriers
- BOCW Act 1996 and its cess framework support State welfare boards; construction cess is generally **1% of construction cost** under the notified rate.
- Registration eligibility includes age 18–60 and at least **90 days of construction work in the preceding 12 months**, not necessarily continuous work for one employer.
- Migrant mobility, fragmented registration, proof requirements, informal contracts and low awareness impede benefits. Heat, pollution-related stoppages, unsafe work and unpaid wages compound vulnerability.
- Source figures on accumulated/unspent cess are dated estimates; funds collected do not automatically translate into benefits delivered.
- **e-Shram has existed since 2021** as a national unorganised-worker database. Registration alone does not make every State BOCW benefit automatically portable.
- Link records with safeguards, simplify lawful proof, offer worksite registration/help desks, improve interstate coordination and grievance redress, and publish outcome-based spending information.

topics.title: Free speech: public attitudes and constitutional protection
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Survey interpretation
- *Who in the World Supports Free Speech?*, Future of Free Speech: October 2024 survey, published in 2025; India ranked **24th of 33**, score **62.6**.
- In this sample, 37% of Indian respondents supported government prevention of criticism of government policies; abstract support for speech can differ from support for controversial speech. [Report](https://futurefreespeech.org/who-supports-free-speech-findings-from-a-global-survey/).
- It measures **public attitudes**, not a global ranking of legal protection or actual press freedom. Country/sample coverage, question wording and index construction limit generalisation.
- Article 19(1)(a) protects citizens' expression. Article 19(2) permits reasonable restrictions on specified grounds: sovereignty/integrity, State security, friendly foreign relations, public order, decency/morality, contempt, defamation and incitement to an offence.
- Criticism alone is not a constitutional ground for censorship. Assess legality, necessity, proportionality and procedural safeguards; media literacy and civic education support informed disagreement.

topics.title: Gig work, algorithmic management and labour rights
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Opportunity and precarity
- Platforms match workers and customers; flexible entry and demand aggregation coexist with uncertain earnings, unpaid waiting, expenses and weak social protection.
- Ratings, task allocation, pricing and deactivation can create employer-like control despite the label “partner”. **Legal employment status depends on law and facts**, not branding alone.
- The source's low-cost instant domestic-work example raises dignity, safety and bargaining-power concerns; advertised customer price is not necessarily workers' net hourly pay.
- Code on Social Security 2020 recognises gig/platform workers, but enactment, commencement and actual benefit delivery are distinct. Rajasthan's 2023 legislation provides a welfare framework; draft Karnataka proposals in March 2025 were not already implemented law.
- International rulings vary by jurisdiction and category: UK's “worker” status is not identical to full employee status; do not generalise one rule to all platforms.
- Reform priorities: clear earnings/fees, safety and insurance, portable welfare, access to relevant personal work data, fair deactivation appeals, representation and collective bargaining.
- Protect privacy when increasing algorithmic transparency; assess net earnings and coverage rather than registrations alone.
## 16 May 2025 : workers’ roundtable
- **15 May Delhi meeting**, organised by **Janpahal/Gig Workers Association**, sought **minimum earnings, social security and legal protection**, plus State/Central tripartite welfare boards including workers, platforms and government. Recommendations were to be forwarded to policymakers; these are demands, not newly enacted rights.
- Workers described blocked IDs/deactivation without notice/remedy, payment/per-task reductions, platform surcharges, poor support and resistance to organising. Testimonies illustrate alleged practices rather than adjudicated findings against every platform.
- They also sought an explicit Central policy; evaluate effective earnings after costs/unpaid waiting, worker representation, transparent deductions and accessible appeal systems.

## Visibility in PLFS
- Gig/platform workers can be counted as employed in **PLFS** while remaining indistinguishable in published broad categories such as self-employment, own-account work or casual labour. **Inclusion in total employment≠separate identification**.
- Multi-platform work, task rates, algorithmic allocation/deactivation, unpaid waiting, net costs, income volatility and access to protections need survey modules/identifiers. Legal employment status cannot be decided by a survey label or universally denied to every platform worker.
- **Code on Social Security 2020** definitions/framework, e-Shram registration and Budget 2025 ID/health-cover announcements are relevant; the Code's provisions for boards/funds are not proof all were already notified, operational and paying benefits by July 2025.
- The **January 2025 PLFS redesign** broadens frequency/rural coverage, but frequency alone does not create gig-specific classifications. Improve occupation/platform questions, multiple-job reporting and benefit/contract data with privacy safeguards; reconcile survey and administrative records rather than equate registrations with all active workers.

topics.title: IUCN Green List and effective conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## What is certified?
- Voluntary global standard for **protected and conserved areas**, administered by IUCN; not a UNEP programme or mandatory status for every park.
- Four pillars: **good governance; sound design/planning; effective management; successful conservation outcomes**. It assesses how well an area works, not merely whether it has legal designation.
| January 2025 additions | Country |
|---|---|
| Sharaan Nature Reserve | Saudi Arabia |
| King Abdulaziz Royal Nature Reserve | Saudi Arabia |
| Aqaba Marine Reserve | Jordan |
| Sir Bu Nair Protected Area | UAE |
- These additions were announced in January, rather than first occurring in March. [IUCN account](https://iucn.org/story/202501/2025-kicks-growth-four-new-sites-added-iucn-green-list-and-three-relisted).
- IUCN **Red List** assesses species extinction risk; Green List assesses area conservation performance. Neither is UNESCO inscription.
- Aichi Target 11's 17% terrestrial/10% marine goals were for 2020. The current global framework's Target 3 seeks effective conservation of 30% of land/inland waters and marine/coastal areas by 2030.
- Community rights, equitable management and measurable ecological outcomes matter as much as coverage statistics.

topics.title: CAG: independence, appointment and public audit
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Constitutional framework
| Article | Provision |
|---|---|
| 148 | Appointment by President; independence and removal safeguards |
| 149 | Duties/powers prescribed by Parliamentary law |
| 150 | Form of Union/State accounts prescribed by President on CAG's advice |
| 151 | Reports to President/Governor for laying before respective legislature |
- Appointment is by warrant under the President's hand and seal; no statutory selection collegium was established in the March 2025 source period. A PIL/notice does not enact the proposed reform.
- **Six years or age 65, whichever earlier**, comes from the CAG's 1971 service law, not an express tenure clause in Article 148. Further office under Union/State governments is prohibited after leaving office. [CAG framework](https://cag.gov.in/en/page-constitutional-provisions).
- Removal follows the same manner/grounds as a Supreme Court judge: proved misbehaviour/incapacity and special-majority parliamentary process. Salary and specified service rights cannot be varied to disadvantage after appointment; office expenses are charged expenditure.
## Scope and reform
- Audits receipts/expenditure and bodies according to law, ownership, financing and entrustment provisions. It does **not automatically audit every private firm**, nor are all PPPs/NGOs automatically exempt.
- CAG reports support PAC scrutiny; audit findings are not themselves criminal convictions or orders to spend money.
- Reforms proposed: transparent merit-based selection, protection from conflicts, skilled timely audits, accessible reports and stronger legislative follow-up. Safeguard independence while avoiding interference in ordinary executive policy choices.

topics.title: Prime Minister Internship Scheme
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## March 2025 pilot design
- Ministry of Corporate Affairs; launched in 2024 following the Budget announcement. Overall ambition: **one crore internships in top 500 companies over five years**, not one crore already trained.
- Pilot eligibility: age **21–24**, not in full-time education or full-time employment; other qualification/exclusion criteria apply. It is not a programme automatically open to every current full-time student.
- **12-month internship**, ₹5,000 monthly assistance and ₹6,000 one-time grant; at least six months of relevant professional experience. [MCA pilot account](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2104914&lang=2&reg=48).
- Mobile app improves access/application management. Internship selection is not a guaranteed permanent job; overall top-500 ambition differs from actual participating-company counts in a pilot round.
- Evaluate mentorship, meaningful tasks, safe workplaces, travel/living costs, equitable selection, completion and subsequent employment. Proposed incentives are not automatically enacted tax benefits.

## July 2025 pilot uptake
- Image clipping reports **over 50,000 accepted of 1.53 lakh offers** across two rounds; **over 8,700 joined** in the first round. Around 6% is a rounded joined/all-offers comparison, **not acceptance rate**; second-round acceptance/joining was ongoing. First-round offers over 82,000 to over 60,000 candidates; about 28,000 acceptances. Multiple offers per candidate mean offers and persons are not interchangeable.
- Monthly assistance split **₹4,500 government viaDBT + ₹500 companyCSR**; ₹6,000 joining support and government-paid **PMJJBY/PMSBY** insurance.
- Pilot exclusions include specified elite-institute graduates/professional or higher qualifications, prior/current specified government training, and regular government employees in defined family. Official rule excludes when **any family member's FY 2023–24 income exceeds ₹8 lakh**; source **≥₹8 lakh family income** is imprecise. Family means self, parents, spouse. [Pilot rules](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2061909&lang=2&reg=3).
- Quality mentorship, meaningful work, digital access, living/travel costs and post-internship transition are key to uptake; an internship is not guaranteed employment or automatic eligibility for every MSME as host.

topics.title: Government assurances and OAMS
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Parliament to implementation
- **Online Assurances Monitoring System**, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs: records and tracks ministerial assurances made during questions/debates.
- An assurance is an undertaking to provide information or take specified action; not every political promise becomes a parliamentary assurance automatically.
- Normally expected within three months; extensions and requests for dropping assurances undergo the appropriate process. Delay is not proof every assurance automatically lapses.
- Ministry/department follows up → implementation report → parliamentary Committee on Government Assurances scrutiny.
- Digital tracking supports visibility and coordination but cannot ensure fulfilment without accurate updates, responsible officers and committee follow-up. AI-based prioritisation is a recommendation, not the source of legal accountability.

topics.title: Bodo identity and the 2020 peace accord
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Identity and agreement
- Bodos/Boros are a major tribal ethnolinguistic community of Assam, within the Bodo-Kachari group; not Assam's largest ethnolinguistic group overall.
- Bodo belongs to the Tibeto-Burman branch; included in the Eighth Schedule by the **92nd Amendment, 2003**.
- Third Bodo accord signed **27 January 2020** among Union/Assam governments and Bodo representatives, including NDFB groups and ABSU. Earlier accords: 1993 and 2003.
- BTAD nomenclature changed to **Bodoland Territorial Region**, within Assam; **no new State** was created. BTC autonomy derives from the Sixth Schedule; ST recognition is distinct from Fifth/Sixth Schedule area administration.
- Provisions: stronger council powers, boundary review through the prescribed mechanism, ₹1,500 crore development package over three years, cultural/educational support and rehabilitation of surrendered cadres.
