| Mamostong Kangri | 7,516 m | Rimo Muztagh, Karakoram |
| Rimo I | 7,385 m | Rimo Muztagh, Karakoram |
| Hardeol | 7,151 m | Kumaon/Milam region |
| Chaukhamba I | 7,138 m | Garhwal/Gangotri massif |
| Trisul I | 7,120 m | Kumaon Himalaya |
- **Nanda Devi is in Kumaon**, not Garhwal. Kanchenjunga is a boundary peak, not wholly inside India.
- **K2 (8,611 m)** lies in territory claimed by India and administered by Pakistan. A list based on territory under Indian administration is different from one using India's territorial claim.
- Heights vary slightly by survey; the source list is not a definitive ranking of every subsidiary summit.

topics.title: ATF and sustainable aviation fuel
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Fuel and emissions
- Conventional **ATF** is jet fuel, generally kerosene-based. **SAF** uses approved waste/biomass or synthetic pathways and certified blends; arbitrary bio-oils cannot be put directly into aircraft.
- SAF can reduce **life-cycle emissions**; combustion still emits CO₂. Feedstock, land/water use, renewable energy, transport and processing determine net savings.
- Challenges: cost, reliable sustainable feedstock, competing uses, certification, scale and refinery/airport compatibility.
- India's announced **indicative international-flight blending targets: 1% in 2027, 2% in 2028, 5% in 2030**, not 1% in 2025. CORSIA concerns international aviation emissions; a target is not evidence all flights already comply. [Civil Aviation Ministry](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2255021&lang=1&reg=3).
- Mains: combine efficient aircraft/operations, credible life-cycle accounting, domestic SAF scale-up and safeguards against food/land competition.
## 1 June 2025 price report and taxation
- Clipping reports Delhi ATF reduction **₹2,414.25/kilolitre (2.82%, rounded 3%) to ₹83,072.55/kl**, third monthly cut after April/May; city/tax/date-specific price, not a permanent nationwide rate. Commercial **19-kg LPG** cut **₹24**, a separate product.
- Jet A-1 is a kerosene hydrocarbon mixture with energy-density, freezing-point and thermal-stability requirements. Source **30–40% airline operating-cost share /VAT up to 30%** are variable snapshots. ATF inclusion in GST is a **proposal**, not proof already operative.
## SAF pathways and PYQ traps
- **SAF is not exclusively bio-derived**: approved biomass/waste and synthetic power-to-liquid pathways qualify subject to lifecycle/certification criteria. Combustion still emits CO2; savings **up to94% /fourfold cost** are pathway/market-specific claims, not universal properties.
- **Corn grain → ethanol → alcohol-to-jet (ATJ)**; **HEFA** processes oils/fats, not grain directly. Agricultural/wood residues may undergo gasification/Fischer–Tropsch or other routes; sludge-derived fuels need appropriate processing/certification. [ICAO pathways](https://www.icao.int/SAF/saf-rules-of-thumb).
- Feedstock eligibility does not establish every batch sustainable: food/land competition, electricity/carbon inputs and traceability matter. Approved blend limits apply; “drop-in” does not mean any unblended alternative liquid suits all existing aircraft.
- **2024 PYQ: all four feedstocks—agricultural residues, corn grain, wastewater-treatment sludge, wood-mill waste—answer(c)**. Corn can be an eligible feedstock despite food-security concerns.
- Indicative **1% in 2027, 2% in 2028, 5% in 2030** targets relate to **international flights**; the PDF mislabels 2030 as broader aviation. ICAO net zero by 2050 is an aspirational goal; CORSIA has separate implementation rules.
- ATF also emits NOx/CO/particulates; aviation's climate effects include CO2 and non-CO2 processes. “Ozone depletion” alone is an oversimplified description—NOx chemistry depends on altitude and atmospheric conditions.

## Panipat SAF project: planned commercial output
- August report: **IndianOil's Panipat refinery, Haryana**, planned commercial SAF output by **December 2025**, **35,000 tonnes/year** capacity, using **used cooking oil** and **ISCC CORSIA certification**. This records the announced plan at the issue date, not proof of completion or production already underway.
- Feedstock collection is easier from organised hotels/restaurants than dispersed eateries/households; traceability, consistent quality, logistics, certification and high cost constrain scale. Source's threefold/fourfold price and up-to-94% emissions-saving claims vary by pathway and market.
- IOC also explores **ethanol → alcohol-to-jet**. Corn-derived ethanol belongs to ATJ, not direct corn-to-HEFA. CORSIA certification and an approved fuel specification/blend limit address different requirements; **50% is not a universal limit for every pathway**.
- Retain indicative international-flight targets **1% in 2027, 2% in 2028, 5% in 2030**, correcting source table's broader-sector label. Repeat **2024 PYQ: C, all four feedstocks**; unyearred practice **B, used cooking oil + forestry residues + sludge**, excluding coal as renewable SAF feedstock.

topics.title: PM-AASHA: farmer price support and consumer stability
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Integrated scheme
- **Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay SanraksHan Abhiyan**, launched 2018; September 2024 continuation integrated farmer/consumer price interventions, with **₹35,000 crore through 2025–26**. [Cabinet decision](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2055990&lang=2&reg=48).
| Component | Function |
|---|---|
| PSS: Price Support Scheme | Physical procurement of notified pulses/oilseeds/copra at MSP under conditions |
| PSF: Price Stabilisation Fund | Buffers and releases to moderate essential-commodity price volatility |
| PDPS: Price Deficiency Payment Scheme | Compensates an eligible price gap for notified oilseeds; no physical government purchase |
| MIS: Market Intervention Scheme | Market intervention for qualifying perishable horticultural produce |
- PSS normal ceiling: **25% of national production** from 2024–25; **tur, urad, masur exempted for 2024–25**, with 100% procurement provision. This is a dated, conditional procurement policy, not automatic purchase of every farmer's entire crop.
- NAFED **eSamridhi** and NCCF **eSamyukti** facilitate pre-registration. State requests, crop quality, operations and storage affect access.
- PDPS coverage was enhanced to **40% of State oilseed production**, implementation period to four months, in the September decision.
- MSP support to growers and affordable consumer prices require different tools. Improve registration access, prompt payment, transparent stocks and diversification without unlimited fiscal/storage burdens.

topics.title: Contempt of court and legitimate criticism
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Law and limits
- **Articles 129 (SC) and 215 (HC)**: courts of record with contempt powers. **Contempt of Courts Act, 1971** defines and regulates contempt.
- **Civil**: wilful disobedience of a court order or wilful breach of an undertaking. **Criminal**: specified scandalising/lowering authority, prejudicing proceedings or obstructing justice.
- Fair and accurate reporting and fair criticism of a judicial act have statutory protection. **Truth may be a defence**, when public interest and bona fides satisfy section 13, amended in **2006**.
- Criticism is not contempt merely because a judge dislikes it; protect justice administration while permitting accountability and expression. Context, interference and statutory safeguards matter.
- Parliament can legislate on contempt within constitutional competence; statutory definitions do not mean SC/HC constitutional powers originate only in the Act.
- PYQ 2022: statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct. Statement 3 is false: the **Act**, not the Constitution, defines civil and criminal contempt.

topics.title: LCH Prachand: high-altitude attack helicopter
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Platform and procurement
- HAL's **Light Combat Helicopter, Prachand**: armed high-altitude operations; Kargil experience highlighted the capability need. First flight **2010**; IAF induction **3 October 2022**.
- Twin **Shakti** engines, developed through HAL–Safran cooperation; relates to indigenous rotary-wing experience but differs from Dhruv utility transport and heavy-lift helicopters.
- High-altitude performance depends on load/weather; manufacturer altitude claims do not guarantee identical capability in every configuration.
- **28 March 2025 contracts: 156 helicopters—66 IAF, 90 Army—₹62,700 crore excluding taxes**, including training/associated equipment. The source's older proposed number is outdated. [MoD](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2116411&lang=2&reg=48).
- Order, phased production, delivery, training and operational induction are distinct; local supply chains and maintenance matter alongside indigenous design.

topics.title: Drones and Indian UAV programmes
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Uses and regulation
- UAVs support surveillance, mapping, agriculture, infrastructure inspection, deliveries and disaster response; FPV means the operator sees a camera feed, not necessarily autonomy or permission for beyond-visual-line-of-sight flight.
- **Drone Rules 2021**, amended in 2022: remote pilot certificate terminology. Exemptions cover **nano**, and **micro for non-commercial use**, not every micro flight. [2021 rules summary](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1749154&lang=2&reg=48).
- Green-zone flights normally need no prior airspace permission within conditions; yellow/red zones require relevant permissions. Check the applicable map and operational restrictions; military systems have a distinct regulatory scope.
- **₹120 crore drone/component PLI**, three-year scheme; **Drone Shakti** announced in Budget 2022 encourages drone services. Neither announcement grants universal flight permission.
## Programme distinctions
| Name | Correct category |
|---|---|
| ABHYAS | High-speed **expendable aerial target**; not a piloted fighter trainer or missile |
| Lakshya | Pilotless aerial target; not a cruise-missile strike system |
| SWiFT | Autonomous flying-wing technology demonstrator; not an anti-tank missile |
| CATS | **Combat Air Teaming System**, manned–unmanned teaming concept |
| Rustom / TAPAS | UAV surveillance programmes; TAPAS is a MALE platform, not a light combat aircraft |
| Nishant | Tactical surveillance UAV |
| Netra UAV | Small quadrotor; distinct from manned **Netra AEW&C** on EMB-145 |
| Imperial Eagle, Golden Hawk, Pushpak | Small UAV programmes/demonstrators; do not label them passenger transports or piloted trainers |
- The source classification table mislabels multiple programmes. [DRDO ABHYAS](https://drdo.gov.in/drdo/en/offerings/products/high-speed-expendable-aerial-target-abhyas).
- Benefits need indigenous components, skilled operators and viable services; manage collision, privacy, cyber security and misuse risks with proportionate rules and counter-UAS capabilities.
## 10 June 2025: evolving warfare
- Source examples: **Operation Sindoor**, Ukraine's **Operation Spider Web**, Azerbaijan's loitering-munition warfare and Myanmar resistance's improvised/3 D-printed drones. They illustrate surveillance/strike, low-cost adaptation and reach; drones do not by themselves explain victory or eliminate personnel/civilian risk.
- Low-altitude flights can exploit radar coverage gaps; multiple cheap drones can saturate defences. **Autonomy/AI navigation, electronic-warfare resistance and coordinated swarming are capabilities of selected systems**, not every commercial UAV. Jamming/spoofing, kinetic interception, weather, endurance/payload and communications remain constraints.
- India needs affordable manufacture and resilient components, training/logistics and layered detection/soft-kill/hard-kill counter-UAS for military and lawful civilian protection. 3 D printing accelerates some airframe/part manufacture but does not print every sensor/engine/control system.
- Infographic examples **Heron TP, MQ-9, Harpy, Nagastra-1** have different roles; source Rustom-II weapon carriage and **AURA 3,000-km/5–6-hour** specifications are not verified operational capability. Compare configuration and demonstrated integration, not a generic “all drones armed” list.
- Regulatory weight bands: **nano ≤250 g; micro >250 g–2 kg; small >2–25 kg; medium >25–150 kg; large >150 kg**. Source incorrectly labels small/medium; civil Drone Rules permissions are distinct from defence use. [Drone Rules 2021](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1749154&lang=2&reg=48).
- **2020 drone applications PYQ: all three (d)**, spraying, volcano inspection and whale breath sampling. **2025 UAV PYQ: none (d)** of universal vertical-landing, hovering and battery-only claims. Fixed-wing, rotary, hybrid VTOL and fuel-powered architectures differ; hovering is not exclusive to multirotors.

## Reported MALE procurement proposal
- July 10 clipping reports a proposed **87 locally manufactured MALE UAVs**, about **₹20,000 crore**, with a **minimum 60% indigenous-content requirement**; trials had assessed proposed designs and final clearance was pending. These are procurement plans, not delivered aircraft.
- Stated requirement: **over 30 hours endurance and at least 35,000 ft**, all-weather intelligence/surveillance/reconnaissance and combat capability. Generic MALE altitude bands are descriptive, not a universal 30,000-ft ceiling.
- Examples: **TAPAS BH-201/Rustom-II (DRDO)**; **Hermes 900/Drishti 10**; armed **Bayraktar TB2**. Performance varies by payload/configuration. Remote operation removes the onboard pilot's exposure but does not eliminate civilian or ground-personnel risk.

## ULPGM-V 3 flight trial
- **25 July 2025**, DRDO tested **UAV-Launched Precision Guided Missile-V 3** at **National Open Area Range, Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh**; enhanced from V 2. This is a munition carried/launched by UAV, not a new UAV airframe.
- Official release: **dual-channel high-definition seeker**, day/night and plain/high-altitude operation; **two-way data link permits post-launch target/aim-point updates**. Modular warheads: **anti-armour (including ERA-protected targets), penetration-cum-blast/anti-bunker, pre-fragmentation**.
- Indigenous UAV integration and partners **Adani Defence, BDL, MSMEs/startups/Dc PPs** strengthen precision-strike production. Source's **4 km day/2.5 km night,12.5 kg, dual-thrust propulsion** are reported specifications, not substantiated by this official trial release; do not substitute them for verified V 3 performance. [DRDO/PIB trial](https://www.pib.gov.in/Press Release Page.aspx?PRID=2148320&lang=2&reg=48).
- Existing PYQs:2020 drone applications all three;2025 universal VTOL/hovering/battery-only claims none. **Hovering is not exclusive to multirotors**; some other rotorcraft/VTOL designs can hover.

topics.title: Regional Rural Banks: inclusion and financial health
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Institutional anchors
- Began under a **1975 ordinance**, followed by **RRB Act, 1976**, on Narasimham working-group recommendations: combine rural familiarity with commercial-bank resources.
- Original ownership **Union 50% : sponsor bank 35% : State 15%**; later amendments permit capital flexibility, so this historical structure should not be treated as an immutable prohibition on other capital.
- **RBI regulation; NABARD supervision**. Lending/deposits and government-payment delivery serve rural households, farmers, artisans and small enterprises.
- Priority-sector target: **75% of ANBC or credit-equivalent off-balance-sheet exposure, whichever is higher**, not an undefined 75% of all assets.
## Read ratios carefully
| Indicator | Meaning / caution |
|---|---|
| CRAR | Capital relative to risk-weighted assets; resilience measure |
| Credit–deposit ratio | Loans relative to deposits; higher is not always safer/better |
| NPA ratio | Asset-quality stress; decline may reflect recovery, write-offs or denominator growth |
| Profit | Sustainability; FY 2023–24 aggregate ₹7,571 crore is a dated result |
- Challenges: geographic concentration, technology/cyber capacity, operating costs, staff and local credit appraisal. Consolidation may improve scale but must preserve last-mile service and accountability.

topics.title: Money Bills and Financial Bills
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Three categories
| Category | Introduction and recommendation | Rajya Sabha / joint sitting |
|---|---|---|
| Money Bill, **110** | Only listed money matters and incidental provisions; LS only, President's recommendation | RS recommends within **14 days**; LS may reject recommendations; no joint sitting |
| Financial Bill I, **117(1)** | Money matters plus other substantive provisions; LS only, President's recommendation for introduction | Ordinary bicameral passage; joint sitting possible on deadlock |
| Financial Bill II, **117(3)** | Involves Consolidated Fund expenditure without being 110/117(1); either House | President's recommendation needed before consideration/passage; normal bicameral procedure |
- Speaker certifies under **110(3)**; “final” does not mean wholly immune from constitutional judicial review.
- Taxation, borrowing, Consolidated/Contingency Funds, appropriation and specified account/audit matters are Article 110 anchors. Fines, fees or local taxation alone do not make a Money Bill.
- Finance Bill title is not itself conclusive; examine contents. Demands for grants, Appropriation Bill and taxation legislation perform different budget functions.
- Mains: efficient fiscal legislation must retain bicameral scrutiny and federal checks; classification disputes concern substance, not labels.

topics.title: Vikramshila and the Pala Buddhist learning network
topics.subject: Ancient and Medieval India
topics.markdown:
## Historical anchors
- **Vikramshila Mahavihara**, founded by Pala king **Dharmapala**, late eighth/early ninth century; remains at **Antichak, Bhagalpur, Bihar**.
- Important centre of Buddhist learning, especially Vajrayana, alongside grammar, logic and philosophical debate; linked to scholarly exchanges and Sanskrit–Tibetan translation.
- **Atisha (c. 980/982–1054)** is associated with the institution and transmission of Buddhist teaching to Tibet. Approximate birth-year traditions differ.
- Monastic complex with a central shrine and cells; institutional patronage, disciplined study and cross-regional networks are key themes.
- Destruction/decline around **1200/early thirteenth century**, commonly associated with Bakhtiyar Khalji; do not convert an uncertain date into an exact late-twelfth-century event.
- Pala network: Nalanda, Vikramshila, Odantapuri, Jagaddala and Somapura. **Somapura at Paharpur, Bangladesh** became a UNESCO World Heritage site in **1985**.
- A modern university proposal near the site is not proof that the ancient monastery has been reconstructed or a new institution already operates.

topics.title: Türkiye: borders, straits and river systems
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Map recall
- Transcontinental: **Anatolia** in Asia and **Eastern Thrace** in Europe; capital **Ankara**, major city **Istanbul**.
- Eight land neighbours: Greece, Bulgaria, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan (**Nakhchivan exclave**), Iran, Iraq and Syria.
- Seas: Black north, Marmara between the straits, Aegean west, Mediterranean south.
- **Black Sea → Bosphorus → Marmara → Dardanelles → Aegean → Mediterranean**. Straits have major trade/security significance.
- Tigris and Euphrates originate in Türkiye and ultimately join as the **Shatt al-Arab**, flowing to the Persian Gulf.
- Kızılırmak: longest river wholly within the country; **Mount Ararat (~5,137 m)** in eastern Türkiye.
- Location connects Europe, Caucasus and West Asia; map proximity does not determine identical diplomatic positions on every conflict.
## 15 May 2025 : travel boycott context
- The clipping reports Indian travellers cancelling Türkiye/Azerbaijan bookings after their perceived support for Pakistan during the conflict. These are consumer/travel-industry reports, **not an announced Indian government travel ban**. Mapping facts above remain the key prelims content.
- Turkish is official; Kurdish and Arabic are also spoken. The source’s “over 99% Muslim” is an unsourced demographic estimate, not a necessary precise current census fact.

topics.title: Rocket propellants and ISRO’s semi-cryogenic engine
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Three propulsion categories
| Type | Typical propellant anchor | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| Earth-storable liquid | Vikas: UH25 fuel + nitrogen tetroxide oxidiser | Easier long storage, but toxic/corrosive handling |
| Semi-cryogenic | Liquid oxygen (LOX) + kerosene | Dense fuel and high thrust; LOX still needs cryogenic handling |
| Cryogenic | LOX + liquid hydrogen (LH₂) | High specific impulse; very cold storage and bulky low-density hydrogen |
- Approximate normal boiling points: **LOX −183°C; LH₂ −253°C**. Fuel and oxidiser are different; rocket engines carry oxidiser because space provides no atmospheric oxygen.
- LOX–kerosene need not have higher specific impulse than LOX–hydrogen. Density, thrust, tank size, handling and stage role create engineering trade-offs.
## March 28, 2025 milestone
- LPSC's **SE2000, 2,000 kN-class** engine will power proposed **SC120**, replacing LVM3's **L110 liquid core**; LVM3's solid S200 boosters and cryogenic upper stage are different components.
- **Mahendragiri**: Power Head Test Article hot-fired for **2.5 seconds**, validating ignition/bootstrap operation and integrated pre-burner, turbopump, start/control subsystems. This was an intermediate test, **not a complete engine's flight qualification**. [ISRO](https://www.isro.gov.in/ISRO_achieves_breakthrough_in_Semicryo_engine_development_Mar_2025_Final.html).
- Repeated tests, full engine/stage qualification and flight integration remain distinct milestones. Payload enhancement is an intended result; a development announcement does not mean the upgraded stage already flew.
- Importance: heavy payloads, deep-space/human-spaceflight capacity, domestic propulsion and launch competitiveness; challenges include combustion stability, turbopumps and thermal control.

## August 2025 launch target
- ISRO chairman's source-period target: first LVM3 flight with **semi-cryogenic core in Q1 2027**; planned cryogenic upper-stage propellant increase **28→32 tonnes**. These are development/integration targets, not an already-flown configuration.
- Existing SE2000/SC120 notes establish **2,000 kN (~200-tonne-force)**, LOX–kerosene and replacement of **L110**; replacing a stage is not simply swapping one 80-tonne Vikas for a completed flight-qualified engine. Higher thrust/density and cost are design trade-offs, not proof higher specific impulse than LOX–hydrogen.
- Embedded cryogenic graphic's caption **'73.55 kN vacuum thrust'** conflicts with modern LVM3 CE20's roughly 200-kN class; do not transfer older cryogenic-engine specifications to CE20. **December 2014 experimental suborbital flight** differs from first orbital developmental flight in **2017**.
- Verified anchors: [ISRO LPSC propulsion FAQ](https://www.lpsc.gov.in/faq1.html), [ISRO launch history](https://www.isro.gov.in/ISRO_EN/LVM3_Launchers.html).

topics.title: Xenotransplantation: pig organs, safety and ethics
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Definition and milestones
- Transplantation/implantation/infusion of living animal cells, tissues or organs into humans; also includes relevant ex-vivo exposure procedures. Distinct from human-to-human allotransplantation.
- **2021** pig-kidney work in a brain-dead recipient; **2022** gene-edited pig-heart transplant in a living patient; **16 March 2024, Massachusetts General Hospital**: first genetically edited pig kidney transplanted into a living human. It was not a new first in March 2025. [Hospital](https://www.massgeneral.org/news/kidney-xenotransplant-faqs?cid=sur4433i).
- Baby Fae's **1984 baboon-heart** case was an earlier landmark, not the first-ever xenotransplant attempt in history.
- Pigs offer comparatively suitable organ size/physiology and breeding scale; genetic changes aim to reduce immune incompatibility. A transplant's technical completion differs from long-term success.
## Benefits and safeguards
- Potential to relieve donor shortages, but rejection, immunosuppression effects, cross-species infection (including concern over porcine endogenous retroviruses) and uncertain durability require follow-up.
- Informed consent, transparent trials, biosafety surveillance, animal welfare, affordability and fair allocation are central.
- Religious/cultural preferences differ among individuals; a dietary pork prohibition does not establish universal rejection of a medically necessary transplant.
- Waiting-list numbers from one country cannot be relabelled as the global total. Experimental promise does not mean routine organs are universally available.

topics.title: Parker Solar Probe and solar storms
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mission and corrected timeline
- NASA probe launched **12 August 2018**, Delta IV Heavy; studies the **corona and solar wind**. Venus flybys reduce heliocentric orbital angular momentum, enabling close perihelia.
- **24 December 2024** record approach: about **6.1 million km from the Sun's surface**. **22 March 2025**, 23rd close approach, matched this distance and roughly **692,000 km/h** speed—not March 2024 as printed. [NASA March update](https://science.nasa.gov/blogs/parker-solar-probe/2025/03/25/nasas-parker-solar-probe-completes-23rd-close-approach-to-sun/).
- Carbon-composite heat shield about 4.5 inches thick; low-density coronal plasma has high temperature but transfers far less heat than dense matter at the same temperature.
## Four instrument suites
| Suite | Measures |
|---|---|
| FIELDS | Electric and magnetic fields |
| IS☉IS | Energetic particles |
| SWEAP | Solar-wind electrons, alpha particles and protons |
| WISPR | Images of corona/solar wind |
- **Faraday/Solar Probe Cup is part of SWEAP**, not a fifth suite. [NASA instruments](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/parker-solar-probe/parker-solar-probe-instruments/).
- Research: coronal heating, Alfvén waves, magnetic switchbacks, wind acceleration and near-Sun dust depletion. These are active investigations, not proof every heating question is solved; dust sublimation is important near the Sun.
## Space weather
- **Flare**: electromagnetic radiation release; **CME**: large plasma/magnetic-field eruption. They can occur together but are not identical or inseparable.
- Flare classes **A, B, C, M, X** classify soft-X-ray flux in decade bands; numeric suffixes specify strength within a class.
- Solar storms can disrupt GPS/HF radio, affect satellite orbits, damage grids and cause widespread auroras; they do not cause equatorial tsunamis or global forest fires simply by arriving.
- Aditya-L1 observes from around Sun–Earth L1 (~1.5 million km from Earth); complements close in-situ Parker observations.

topics.title: Uranium isotopes, reactor fuel and safeguards
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Conceptual recall
- Natural uranium: about **99.3% U-238, 0.7% U-235**, plus trace U-234. U-235 is fissile; U-238 is fertile and can produce plutonium-239 through reactor processes.
- **Enrichment increases U-235's proportion by isotope separation**; it does not chemically turn U-238 into U-235. Centrifuges exploit small mass differences; uranium isotopes have essentially the same chemistry.
- Light-water reactor fuel typically has roughly **3–5% U-235**; India's conventional **PHWRs use natural uranium**. HALEU means enrichment above 5% and below 20%; reactor designs vary.
- Do not infer that every nuclear reactor requires enriched uranium or that civilian fuel use equals a weapons programme.
## Governance
- IAEA safeguards verify relevant nuclear-material commitments and peaceful-use arrangements. NPT governs non-proliferation obligations; **India is not an NPT party**.
- CTBT concerns nuclear explosive testing, not ordinary reactor-fuel enrichment; **India has not signed it**, and the treaty has not entered into force.
- India–US civil nuclear cooperation and designated civilian-facility safeguards differ from blanket safeguards on all Indian facilities.
- Mains: energy security, fuel supply, safety, waste management and non-proliferation; distinguish physical fuel concepts from international legal obligations.

## June 2025 revision
- Centrifugation uses the small mass difference between uranium isotopes, rather than different chemistry. The schematic force relationship is **F = m r ω²**; high-strength rotor materials withstand large mechanical stresses.
- 2023 PYQ: India's coal dependence is correct; the assertion that electricity generation requires **at least 60% enriched uranium is incorrect (c)**. Conventional Indian PHWRs use natural uranium, while typical LWR fuel is around 3–5% U-235.

topics.title: Education governance: federalism, access and autonomy
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Reading the “three Cs” critique
- Source editorial argues **centralisation, commercialisation and communalisation** threaten education. These are analytical claims, not a court ruling that NEP 2020 is unconstitutional.
- Education is in the Concurrent List; CABE, Centre–State consultation, school funding and university governance matter. Proposed UGC rules and final operative regulations must be distinguished.
- Samagra Shiksha funding linked to PM SHRI participation raised federal concerns; parliamentary recommendations for release are not themselves binding disbursement orders.
- **RTE Act enacted 2009, commenced 2010**; Article **21A** protects free compulsory education for ages **6–14**. Neighbourhood-school distances arise from rules, not a universal constitutional kilometre limit.
## Assess evidence and reform
- School closures reported since 2014 cannot all be caused by a policy adopted in 2020; distinguish mergers, access impacts and comparable data series.
- HEFA provides capital-financing loans with differing repayment arrangements; one reported student-fee burden cannot describe every financing window.
- NAAC/NTA integrity issues, academic appointments and textbook changes need institution/edition-specific evidence; preserve critical inquiry, diversity and academic autonomy while ensuring accountability.
- Priorities: predictable equitable funding, transparent recruitment/accreditation, State participation, accessible public schools and meaningful outcome monitoring.
## May 14 editorial: education, employability and research outcomes
- Core argument: enrolment/degrees need **disciplinary depth, adaptable skills and meaningful employment**, with equity and quality pursued together. Atal Tinkering Labs, coding and inclusion measures cannot alone establish an educational renaissance; NEP implementation needs financing, teachers and evidence of outcomes.
- Historical context: **University Education Commission/Radhakrishnan 1948–49; Education Commission/Kothari 1964–66; NPE 1968, 1986 (modified 1992); NEP 2020**. Source's unnamed **“Officers' Commission 1985”** is not sufficiently identifiable for exam recall.
- NEP's flexible entry/exit, mother-tongue learning, Indian Knowledge Systems and curricular flexibility raise implementation/quality questions. Claiming they **caused low-quality e-commerce jobs** requires causal evidence; degrees do not guarantee employment, but employment also depends on labour demand and economic structure.
- The claim **“no industry stakeholders involved”** overstates the evidence: Ministry records wide stakeholder/public/state consultation. Assess participation and uptake rather than asserting none. [Ministry consultation record](https://www.education.gov.in/nep/about-consultation).
- Source's **42.6% employability in 2025 /44.3% in 2023**, **11.72% knowledge-intensive employment**, **11 QS top-500 universities** and **CNCI rank 16 among G20** need the original surveys, populations and years. They are not interchangeable with PLFS unemployment or all-graduate job-placement rates. A separate India Skills Report 2025 assessment reports **54.81%**, illustrating incompatible measures. [Report partner](https://taggd.in/industry-reports/isr/india-skills-report-2025/).
- **GII 2024: India 39, Malaysia 33, Türkiye 37**; Bengaluru **56th S&T cluster**. Rankings differ between country innovation, cluster size and research intensity; one patent assignee's prominence does not prove an absence of domestic innovation. [WIPO country results](https://www.wipo.int/web-publications/global-innovation-index-2024/en/gii-2024-at-a-glance.html), [cluster ranking](https://www.wipo.int/web-publications/global-innovation-index-2024/en/cluster-ranking.html).
- Source questions outcomes of **CSIR-NMITLI, Aakash tablet and IMPRINT**; demand programme-specific delivery/audit evidence rather than claiming no public outcome documentation exists. Vannevar Bush analogy and blanket dismissal of Indian startups are editorial judgments; service ventures and deep-tech ventures coexist.
- Reform priorities: practical curriculum/apprenticeships, employability and tracer studies, research quality and reproducible outcomes, transparent funding/audits, industry–academic links and academic freedom. Equity does not logically require sacrificing excellence.

## Early childhood care and education
- NEP 2020 foundational stage includes **three preschool years 3–6**, then grades 1–2; **Balvatika I/II/III** may serve 3–4, 4–5, 5–6. Provision varies; all government schools have not already implemented every level.
- **Play, stories, art, movement, exploration** support holistic development; avoid premature formal drills/ “schoolification”. School readiness must retain care, nutrition and health. [KVS](https://bsfbagafa.kvs.ac.in/en/bal-vatika/).
- Source case: preschool expansion in **Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu** drew some 4–6-year-olds from Anganwadis to schools; not a national order to remove all 3–6-year-olds from Anganwadis.
- Proposed opportunity: release worker capacity for **0–3 children, pregnant/lactating mothers, home visits**, while strengthening educational work via **Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi**. Anganwadis already had preschool education responsibilities.
- **First 1,000 days=conception to age 2**, different from 0–3. Early stimulation, parent support, nutrition and health interact; Perry Preschool/Odisha studies illustrate early intervention, not identical interventions at every age.
- Implementation: Education–Women and Child Development coordination, Samagra Shiksha budgets, ECCE-trained teachers/workers, recruitment, age-appropriate spaces, home-visit time and quality monitoring. 14 lakh Anganwadis is a rounded infrastructure reference.

topics.title: Phase-change materials and thermal energy storage
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mechanism
- PCMs absorb/release **latent heat** during a phase transition; near the transition temperature they can buffer temperature changes. They **store energy**, not generate it or automatically become renewable energy.
- **Charging: heat absorbed → melting. Discharging: solidification → heat released.** Ice/water around 0°C is a familiar example; other materials select different operating temperatures.
| Type | Examples / cautions |
|---|---|
| Organic | Paraffins, fatty acids; often low conductivity/flammability concerns |
| Inorganic | Hydrated salts; possible corrosion, phase separation or subcooling |
| Eutectic | Mixtures formulated for a selected transition temperature |
| Bio-based | Feedstock-derived materials; performance varies by formulation |
## Applications and limits
- Cold-chain food/pharmaceutical transport; temperature-buffering building walls/roofs; solar thermal storage; battery/electronics thermal management.
- Each vaccine has its own validated storage requirements; **not all vaccines require 2–8°C**. PCM capacity is finite and requires proper charging/containment.
- Check leakage, cycling durability, thermal conductivity, fire safety, cost and lifecycle benefits. Source percentage savings are case-specific, not universal guarantees.
- Logistics, clean-energy and efficient-building policies may support these applications; do not infer every cited scheme mandates PCM use.

topics.title: Superconductors: nickel oxides and the LK-99 claim
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Properties
- Below relevant critical temperature/field/current limits: **zero electrical resistance** and **Meissner effect** (magnetic-field expulsion). Perfect conductivity alone is not the full definition.
- Kamerlingh Onnes observed mercury superconductivity in **1911**. Bednorz–Müller's cuprate work began in **1986**, rewarded with **1987 Nobel Prize**.
- “High temperature” is relative to other superconductors; **40 K ≈ −233°C**, still very cold, not room temperature.
## March 2025 nickelate result
- NUS synthesised **(Sm–Eu–Ca)NiO₂**, copper-free oxide with transition near **40 K at ambient pressure**, reporting zero resistance **above 30 K**. It extends oxide superconductivity beyond cuprates, not the first copper-free superconductor of any kind. [NUS](https://news.nus.edu.sg/nus-physicists-copper-free-high-temperature-superconducting-oxide/).
- Onset temperature and fully zero-resistance temperature are different. Interlayer interactions and predictive material models guide research; bulk device production remains a separate engineering challenge.
## LK-99: failed replication
- Copper-substituted lead-apatite claim arose in **2023**, not as a confirmed 2025 breakthrough. Independent studies did **not establish room-temperature superconductivity**. [Replication study](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acsomega.3c06096).
- Levitation or an apparent resistance change alone is insufficient; reproducible resistance, magnetic response and sample purity matter.
- Applications: MRI magnets, maglev, selected quantum circuits and power equipment. Cryogenic cost, critical limits and alternating-current losses mean entire devices are not automatically loss-free.

topics.title: Waqf administration and the 2025 reform debate
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Basic distinctions
- Waqf: permanent dedication for religious, pious or charitable purposes recognised by Muslim law; includes public and eligible family-benefit forms. **Waqif creates; mutawalli manages; statutory Board supervises**—the manager is not the personal owner.
- Major national statutory anchors: **1954 Act**, **1995 Act**, **2013 amendments**; Central Waqf Council established **1964**. “1955 Act” in the heading is erroneous. [Historical overview](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2118415&lang=2&reg=48).
- Registration, surveys, accounts, adjudication and legal challenge operate under law; not every disputed ownership claim is finally established waqf property.
- The source incorrectly suggests a two-thirds Board vote permits sale/gift/mortgage: **2013 section 104A prohibits sale, gift, exchange, mortgage or transfer**; leases have separate rules. [2013 Amendment](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/repealedfileopen?rfilename=A2013-27.pdf).
## Legislative timeline and debate
- **1 April 2025 issue** discusses the pending amendment process originating in 2024; draft provisions are not already law on that date. Passage and commencement followed later in April, so this is a historical debate snapshot.
- Proposed reforms concerned verification/registration, administrative accountability, composition and government-property disputes. Women representation was **already required in 2013**; do not say it first appeared in the 2024 proposal.
- Arguments for reform: transparent records, safeguarding beneficiaries/property and accountable management. Concerns: minority participation, excessive executive intervention, due process and religious autonomy.
- Articles **14, 25, 26 and 300A** frame equality, religious freedom/institutional rights and lawful property deprivation; freedoms operate with constitutional limits, not immunity from all regulation.
- Property-count/land-area estimates require registry date/definition; the “third-largest landowner” claim is not a reliable comparable ranking from the source alone.
- Evaluate final statutory text and court orders separately from the old draft. The undated 15-mark essay is practice, not a verified UPSC PYQ.
## 14 April 2025: Murshidabad unrest and constitutional duties
- The issue reports **three deaths and over 150 arrests** during violence associated with protests against the Waqf (Amendment) Act in Murshidabad, West Bengal. These are contemporaneous reported figures, not permanent totals. Reports identify Suti/Samsherganj and Ghospara, attacks on personnel, vehicles and railway property; individual allegations require investigation.
- The source reports Calcutta High Court intervention for central-force deployment and reinforcements including BSF companies. The newspaper clipping describes **17 CAPF companies overall**; BSF subset counts vary with deployment time and should not be confused with the total.
- **The Act was already public:** presidential assent/publication **5 April 2025**, commencement **8 April 2025**. The claim that details were yet to be released is incorrect. [Act Gazette](https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2025/262316.pdf), [commencement notification](https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2025/262340.pdf).
| Provision/institution | Revision distinction |
|---|---|
| Public order and police | Primarily State List responsibilities; governments must protect life, property and peaceful expression |
| Article 355 | Union duty to protect States against external aggression/internal disturbance and ensure constitutional governance; assistance does not itself replace the State government |
| Article 356 | Separate constitutional process for failure of constitutional machinery; central-force deployment does **not** automatically imply President's Rule |
| BSF/CAPFs | Border forces may assist internal security under lawful arrangements; assistance and takeover of State administration are distinct |
| Criminal procedure | BNSS has operated since 1 July 2024, subject to savings/transitional rules; do not cite the old CrPC as the universal current framework |
- Judicial oversight, proportionate policing, impartial investigation, relief and rehabilitation, verified communication and protection of fundamental rights are complementary. Violence by individuals must not be attributed collectively to a religious community.
- Distinguish peaceful constitutional disagreement about waqf administration from criminal acts during unrest. Articles 14, 21, 25 and 26 remain relevant to equal protection, life and religious freedoms.

topics.title: Tiger Triumph and tri-service disaster response
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## April 2025 plan
- Fourth India–US **tri-service HADR** exercise, planned **1–13 April 2025**; harbour phase **Visakhapatnam, 1–7 April**, sea phase **8–13 April**.
- Shared procedures, logistics/medical response and a **Combined Coordination Centre** improve joint-task-force interoperability. At publication it was starting, not completed.
- Distinguish **Yudh Abhyas (Army), Cope India (Air Force), Malabar (naval/multilateral)** from tri-service Tiger Triumph.
- Cooperation rests alongside LEMOA **2016**, COMCASA **2018**, BECA **2020**; access/logistics agreements do not create an automatic treaty alliance or identical policies.
- HADR readiness needs timely communications, host consent, rapid supplies, medical support and local coordination—not military deployment alone.

topics.title: Tourism: infrastructure, arrivals and sustainable growth
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Infrastructure programme
- FY **2024–25**: **40 projects in 23 States, ₹3,295.76 crore**, approved under **SASCI—Development of Iconic Tourist Centres to Global Scale**. Approval differs from completion. [Tourism Ministry](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2099157&lang=2&reg=3).
- Special capital assistance includes long-term interest-free State loans; tourism selection considers connectivity, carrying capacity, utilities, sustainable management and local value.
- **Swadesh Darshan 2.0**: sustainable destinations; **PRASHAD**: pilgrimage/heritage infrastructure; **RCS-UDAN**: regional connectivity. Travel for LiFE promotes responsible behaviour; skill programmes support hospitality/local enterprise.
- Adopt a Heritage amenities partnerships do not transfer monument ownership. A **draft National Tourism Policy** is not automatically a final enacted policy.
## Read statistics correctly
- **TTDI 2024: India 39th**, WEF. **2023 international tourist arrivals 18.89 million** include **9.52 million foreign tourist arrivals plus NRI arrivals**; the two totals are not synonyms.
- GDP estimates depend on direct versus total tourism contributions and methodology; avoid equating a single industry estimate with the official satellite-account measure.
- Tourism creates jobs, foreign exchange and local demand, but seasonal overcrowding, safety, scams, waste, water pressure and habitat damage can undermine benefits.
- Develop lesser-known destinations within carrying capacity; improve transport/accessibility, reliable sanitation, local skills, fair community benefits and outcome-based maintenance.

topics.title: Bipolar disorder: episodes, recognition and inclusion
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Distinct episodes
- Bipolar disorder involves episodes of marked mood/energy/activity change, beyond ordinary moodiness. **Mania** may involve high/irritable mood, reduced sleep, racing thoughts and risky behaviour; depression involves low mood, loss of interest and impaired functioning.
- **Bipolar I**: at least one manic episode; depression often occurs. **Bipolar II**: hypomania plus major depression, with no manic episode. Cyclothymia involves less severe recurring symptoms. [NIMH](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/bipolar-disorder).
- Genetics are polygenic and interact with environment; a heritability estimate describes population variation, not a percentage of an individual's illness “caused by genes”.
- Stress/HPA-axis and circadian disruption are associated with illness; direction of causation can be uncertain, not one proven universal mechanism.
## Public-health relevance
- Initial depression and overlooked hypomania can delay diagnosis. Clinical assessment considers lifetime episodes, family history, substances and medical alternatives; family history alone does not diagnose the condition.
- Appropriate ongoing treatment, psychosocial support, sleep/routine management and reduced stigma can support productive lives. This is revision content, not a self-diagnosis checklist.
- **World Bipolar Day: 30 March**. Awareness and accessible mental healthcare matter; an ongoing survey is not already a published national prevalence result.

topics.title: AI image generation: privacy, consent and safeguards
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Photos, AI and consent
- Uploading a portrait shares identifiable personal data; facial images can enable impersonation, profiling or deepfakes. A stylised output does not automatically anonymise the original input.
- Risks include unclear retention/training practices, third-party sharing, unauthorised reuse and security breaches. These are risk pathways, not evidence that a named service has suffered a breach or violated GDPR.
- Processing an image to fulfil a request, retaining it, and reusing it for training are different purposes. Check the applicable service, account settings and terms; do not assume every upload is used for training or that deletion guarantees immediate removal from every model.
## Governance and practical safeguards
- Privacy principles: clear notice and lawful basis; purpose limitation; data minimisation; retention limits; access security; meaningful user control and grievance redress.
- India's **Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023** provides the statutory framework for digital personal data. Enactment and commencement/implementation are separate; do not treat all provisions as operational on 2 April 2025 merely because the Act was passed.
- Protect children's and bystanders' privacy; avoid unnecessary identity documents or sensitive backgrounds. Consent to a photograph is not automatically consent to every AI reuse.
- Transparent policies, usable controls, privacy by design, audits and public digital-literacy campaigns can preserve creative benefits while reducing misuse. AI ethics proposals are not themselves binding law.
- **Mains balance:** creativity and accessibility ↔ privacy, autonomy, cybersecurity and accountability. Assess actual processing and safeguards rather than assuming innovation is inherently unlawful.
- Statutory reference: [DPDP Act, 2023, official Gazette](https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2024/02/Digital-Personal-Data-Protection-Act-2023.pdf).

topics.title: Disinformation: democratic trust and safeguards
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Distinctions and risks
- **Misinformation:** false information without necessarily intending deception. **Disinformation:** deliberately deceptive information. Genuine material used maliciously is sometimes termed malinformation.
- AI-generated text/images/video, coordinated amplification and attention-driven recommendation systems can increase the speed and scale of deception. Deepfake ≠ automatically false or unlawful; context, impersonation and deception matter.
- Consequences: polarisation, communal tension, distorted elections/public debate, fraud, health misinformation, reduced institutional trust and foreign information manipulation/interference (**FIMI**).
- **WEF Global Risks Report 2025:** misinformation/disinformation ranked first over the **two-year** horizon in respondents' risk assessment; armed conflict led the separate immediate-2025 concern. This is a perception survey, not a measured count of every harm. [WEF report](https://www.weforum.org/publications/global-risks-report-2025/).
- The supplied ISB–CyberPeace study summary reports political 46%, general 33.6% and religious 16.8% of its studied disinformation. Treat these as sample-dependent findings, not shares of all Indian online content; missing methodology prevents national extrapolation.
## Response: verify → explain → correct → review
- Check provenance, original date/context and independent evidence before forwarding; teach digital/media literacy in schools and public campaigns.
- Platforms: proportionate risk assessments, transparent moderation rules, researcher access, independent fact-checking and accessible appeals; provenance labels help but are not proof that an unlabelled item is authentic.
- AI developers: safety testing and abuse monitoring; public agencies: timely trustworthy information, cybersecurity capacity and evidence-based corrections.
- Protect journalists/fact-checkers, support cross-border cooperation and investigate coordinated fraud/illegal activity within applicable law.
- **Trade-off:** Article 19(1)(a) expression and legitimate dissent require protection; restrictions must meet Article 19(2) and due process. “False” alone does not create unlimited censorship authority.
- Automated verification can make errors; moderator bias, low trust, linguistic diversity, cross-border attribution and commercial/political incentives complicate implementation.
- A proposed Indian Digital Services Act, national deepfake policy or AI oversight council in the article is a recommendation, not an established institution/law. EU policy cannot be described as already adopted by India.

topics.title: Defence exports: production, innovation and strategic autonomy
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Dated figures: keep the measures separate
| Measure | Period and figure |
| --- | --- |
| Defence exports | **FY 2024–25: ₹23,622 crore**, up **12.04%** over FY 2023–24 |
| Private-sector exports | FY 2024–25: ₹15,233 crore |
| DPSU exports | FY 2024–25: ₹8,389 crore; growth 42.85% |
| Export authorisations | FY 2024–25: 1,762, against 1,507 previously |
- Exports measure sales abroad; **production** measures output, and the defence **budget** measures government allocation. They cannot be interchanged. [MoD, 1 April 2025](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2117348).
- FY 2023–24 production was about **₹1.27 lakh crore**; exports were ₹21,083 crore. CareEdge's FY24–FY29 growth rates in the source are forecasts, not realised growth or government guarantees. [MoD background](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2114546).
- **₹50,000 crore exports by 2029** is a target. Source recipient percentages and a fixed 60:40 private/DPSU split lack a compatible current denominator; do not memorise them as FY 2024–25 facts.
## Why it matters
- Domestic design/manufacturing can strengthen supply security, strategic autonomy, jobs, skills and foreign-exchange earnings; export partnerships can support defence diplomacy.
- Electronics, metallurgy and precision engineering gain spillovers. Domestic assembly does not by itself eliminate dependence on imported engines, sensors, components or intellectual property.
## Verified policy tools
- Simplified online export-authorisation processing; indigenisation through **SRIJAN** and positive indigenisation lists; innovation through **iDEX** and DRDO's **Technology Development Fund**.
- Defence industrial corridors: **Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu**; strategic partnerships aim to develop domestic capability through selected collaborations.
- Defence FDI: up to **74% automatic route** for companies seeking new industrial licences; above that and up to 100% through government approval subject to conditions. Investment ceilings do not waive security review or export controls. [Parliamentary reply](https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/254/AU669.pdf?source=pqars).
- **TUFS is a textile-sector scheme**, not a general defence modernisation scheme. The source's “India Defence Mart”, generic “SPDE” and defence “Export Promotion Council” labels should not replace verified official mechanisms.
## Constraints and way forward
- Long testing/procurement cycles, finance and working-capital constraints, limited critical technologies, certification and after-sales support challenge expansion.
- Invest in R&D, predictable procurement, start-up/MSME finance, quality assurance, competitive supply chains and lifecycle maintenance; improve coordination between defence and industrial-policy institutions.
- Judge success by indigenous technology depth, reliability and sustainable customer support, alongside export value; published forecasts and start-up counts need dates and definitions.

topics.title: Chile: geography, resources and India ties
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Map recall
- Long, narrow country on **South America's Pacific coast**; land neighbours **Peru (north), Bolivia (northeast), Argentina (east)**; Andes form much of the eastern boundary. **Santiago** is the capital.
- **North → south:** Atacama Desert → central Mediterranean-climate zone → temperate southern forests and Patagonia. The Valdivian region supports temperate rainforest.
- **Humboldt/Peru Current** flows northward along western South America. Cold water, subtropical subsidence and the Andes rain shadow help explain Atacama aridity; nutrient-rich upwelling supports fisheries.
- **Drake Passage** separates southern South America from Antarctica; Cape Horn lies in Chile's far south. Chile's southern ports are gateways for Antarctic research/logistics.
## Resources and economic geography
- Important copper producer; **Chuquicamata** is a major copper mining complex, not an unqualified permanent “world's largest open-pit mine” ranking.
- **Salar de Atacama:** lithium-bearing brines. Copper and lithium connect Chile to electricity infrastructure and battery supply chains; mining has water/ecosystem trade-offs. [USGS Chile](https://www.usgs.gov/centers/national-minerals-information-center/chile).
- Historical **sodium nitrate (NaNO₃)** deposits: fertilisers/explosives; other resources include gold, silver and iron ore.
- Wine, fruits such as grapes/apples/berries, forestry products and fisheries diversify exports; Atacama's high solar resource supports renewable-energy opportunities.
## India–Chile trade: correct the timeline
- Original **PTA signed 8 March 2006**, effective **September 2007**. Expansion signed **6 September 2016**, effective **16 May 2017**; 2016 was not the original agreement year. [Commerce Ministry](https://www.commerce.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/MOC_636338205640368585_Expansion_India-Chile_PTA.pdf).
- Mineral supply cooperation, pharmaceuticals, textiles, vehicles, renewables and Antarctic science offer complementarities. Preferential tariff concessions are narrower than an unrestricted free-trade regime.

topics.title: Betavoltaic nuclear batteries
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Electricity from decay
- **Betavoltaic:** beta particles from a radioisotope interact with a semiconductor to generate electricity directly. **Radioisotope thermoelectric generator (RTG):** decay heat → thermoelectric conversion. Neither requires a controlled reactor chain reaction.
- **Nickel-63 → stable copper-63** through beta decay; BV100 uses a diamond semiconductor. Radioactive decay is an energy source, not rechargeable chemical storage.
- Betavolt's **50-year life**, temperature range **−60°C to +120°C** and high energy-density figures are manufacturer claims. Long life does not mean constant output forever: activity declines as the isotope decays.
- The manufacturer’s **8 January 2024** announcement reports BV100 output of **100 microwatts at 3 V**, far below ordinary smartphone/drone power requirements. A proposed one-watt model is a development target; combining cells adds material, volume and cost. [Betavolt announcement](https://www.betavolt.tech/646785-646785_2562735.html).
## Opportunities and limits
- Best conceptual fit: ultra-low-power remote sensors, microelectronics and difficult-to-service aerospace systems; medical implants require device-specific safety/clinical approval. Not every implant or AI device can run on such low power.
- Advantages: long operation without charging, compactness and potential performance where solar/chemical batteries are impractical. **High total energy density ≠ high instantaneous power.**
- Isotope supply, semiconductor cost, containment, radiation protection, licensing, damage scenarios and end-of-life management matter. A stable decay product does not remove radioactive-material obligations during service or permit ordinary disposal.
- City Labs develops **tritium-based** betavoltaics; carbon-14/diamond research is another approach. These are different isotopes/platforms, not proof every announced product is commercially ready. [City Labs technology](https://citylabs.net/technology-overview/).
- Indian R&D opportunities: sensors, space/defence applications, materials and reliable packaging, with appropriate nuclear regulatory oversight. Do not infer India has no research merely from limited coverage.
## Practice recall
- Direct conversion of **beta-particle energy**, not heat, sunlight or a chemical reaction, identifies betavoltaic technology. The supplied multiple-choice exercise has no exam year and is practice, not an authenticated UPSC PYQ.

topics.title: Jacaranda tree
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Identify
- **Jacaranda mimosifolia**, family **Bignoniaceae**, order **Lamiales**: subtropical ornamental tree, violet-blue trumpet flowers, bipinnate fern-like leaves and woody flattened seed capsules.
- Kew records the native distribution as **Bolivia, northwestern Argentina and Paraguay**; do not list Brazil as this species' confirmed native range merely because the genus occurs widely in South America. [Kew POWO](https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/130936-2).
- Widely planted beyond its native range, including India, Australia and South Africa. Introduced ornamental presence is different from native/endemic status.
## Urban ecology
- Shade, amenity and flowering habitat can benefit cities; site choice should consider water, soil drainage, branch safety, litter and local biodiversity.
- Naturalisation/invasiveness is **location-dependent**; assess competition with native vegetation rather than treating it as invasive everywhere.
- Traditional medicinal uses are not proof of clinically effective or safe treatment. Timber/ornamental use and cultural associations do not define its ecological origin.

topics.title: Damselflies and Euphaea wayanadensis
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Wayanad discovery
- **Euphaea wayanadensis**, family **Euphaeidae**, order **Odonata**, suborder **Zygoptera**: new species described in **ENTOMON 50(1), 2025**, from the Wayanad landscape, Western Ghats, Kerala.
- Distinguished from closely similar **E. pseudodispar** by hindwing black patch, thoracic stripes and male terminal/genital structures. The study includes **morphology and mitochondrial COI molecular analysis**, with 12.9% nucleotide divergence and phylogenetic evidence—not morphology alone. [Research paper](https://www.entomon.ambadi.org.in/index.php/Entomon/article/download/1416/716).
- The daily compilation reports Kerala's **191st** and Western Ghats' **223rd** recorded odonate; these are dated checklist counts, not permanent totals.
- Rocky forest-stream habitats link terrestrial forest protection with freshwater conservation. Restricted known records are not proof of a formal threatened-category assessment.
## Damselfly versus dragonfly
| Feature | Damselflies | Dragonflies |
|---|---|---|
| Suborder | Zygoptera | Anisoptera |
| Typical build | Slender | More robust |
| Wings | Fore/hind pairs generally similar | Hindwings usually broader at base |
| Eyes | Widely separated | Usually meet/close; exceptions occur |
| Resting wings | Usually folded together; exceptions | Usually held open |
- Aquatic immature stages → winged terrestrial adults; both are predators and part of food webs. Habitat/species assemblages can indicate freshwater condition, but one sighting does not certify pollution-free water.
- Threats: stream alteration, riparian clearing, water pollution and climatic stress. Protect streams and vegetation, monitor water and conduct targeted taxonomic surveys; not all damselflies are restricted to stagnant or slow water.

topics.title: BIMSTEC and Bay of Bengal cooperation
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Members and evolution
- **Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation**; established by the **Bangkok Declaration, 6 June 1997**.
- **Seven members:** Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, Sri Lanka; Myanmar and Thailand. Nepal/Bhutan are landlocked members—Bay of Bengal cooperation does not require every member to have a coast.
- BIST-EC began with Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka and Thailand; Myanmar joined in 1997. Bhutan and Nepal joined in 2004, producing the present grouping/name.
- Bridges South/Southeast Asia through trade, technology, energy, transport, security and development cooperation. Overlap with SAARC/ASEAN is different from formally replacing either.
## April 2025 summit and India
- India's PM visited Thailand **3–4 April 2025**; the **sixth summit took place 4 April in Bangkok**, not throughout both days. Charter entered into force **20 May 2024**. [BIMSTEC summit declaration](https://bimstec.org/images/content_page_pdf/1743841366_6th%20BIMSTEC%20Summit%20Declaration.pdf).
- Supports India's **Neighbourhood First** and **Act East** policies: connectivity, maritime cooperation, resilient supply chains and regional public goods.
- **MAHASAGAR:** Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions; articulated during the **March 2025 Mauritius visit**, not created for the first time at the Thailand summit. [MEA briefing](https://www.mea.gov.in/outoging-visit-detail.htm?39163).
- BIMSTEC FTA negotiations/framework are not evidence of a fully operational free-trade area. Implementation, political instability, infrastructure gaps and non-tariff barriers matter alongside declarations.

## 2025 PYQ
- Seven members as of January 2025; **Bangkok Declaration 1997**, not Dhaka 1999; founders Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Thailand; Nepal joined 2004.
- **Tourism led by Nepal**, not India; therefore **I only (d)**. This sector-leadership fact complements common membership notes.

topics.title: Axiom-4, Gaganyaan and the International Space Station
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mission and India’s role
- **Ax-4:** fourth private astronaut mission to the ISS, organised by **Axiom Space**, using SpaceX transport with NASA/partner coordination. Commercial low-Earth-orbit activity complements public space programmes.
- **2 August 2024:** ISRO announced **Shubhanshu Shukla—prime mission pilot; Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair—backup** from its Gaganyaan astronaut pool. Training covered spacecraft operations, emergencies, microgravity experiments and astronaut health. [ISRO selection](https://www.isro.gov.in/ISRO%20Press%20Release-SFA%20Signing.html).
- **4 April 2025:** mission was still forthcoming; the PDF’s “launched in August 2024” is incorrect. August 2024 concerned selection/training, not launch.
- **Later development—25 June 2025:** launched aboard SpaceX Dragon/Falcon 9 from Kennedy Space Center. Shukla became the first Indian to visit the ISS; the completed stay was **18 days**, rather than the initial approximately fortnight-long plan. Returned **15 July 2025**. [ISRO mission outcome](https://www.isro.gov.in/Axiom04_mission_successfully_concluded_return_ISRO_Gaganyatri_ShubhanshuShukla.html).
## ISS quick recall
- International microgravity laboratory in **low Earth orbit, approximately 400 km high**; NASA, Roscosmos, ESA, JAXA and CSA partnership.
- First modules **1998**; continuous human presence since **2 November 2000**. Typical crew about seven, with temporary variation during handovers/visiting missions.
- Approximately **7.7 km/s**, one orbit about **90 minutes**: roughly 16 orbits/sunrise–sunset cycles daily. Research: biology, medicine, materials, fluid physics and technologies for longer missions. [NASA ISS facts](https://www.nasa.gov/international-space-station/space-station-facts-and-figures/).
## Link to Indian human spaceflight
- **Ax-4 experience → operational skills and microgravity research → Gaganyaan capability → longer-duration missions.** Participation does not itself constitute an independently launched Indian crewed mission.
- **Gaganyaan:** indigenous human-spaceflight programme; uncrewed tests, escape systems and crew safety must precede crewed flight. Successful independent crewed launch would place India alongside the Soviet/Russian, US and Chinese capabilities; distinguish ambition from achievement.
- **Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035** was a programme target, not an already operational station. Avoid treating an early 20-ton concept or old launch forecast as a final configuration/date.
- Benefits: space diplomacy, commercial participation, scientific collaboration and training; constraints: cost, life support, radiation, microgravity health effects and reliable emergency recovery.
## 21 May 2025: planned outreach and research
- Source's **8 June 2025** launch date was a forecast subsequently revised; **Falcon 9 is the rocket, Dragon the spacecraft**. Approximately **14 days at ISS** was the initial plan; completed mission details are recorded in the existing outcome section.
- Clipping adds planned **ISRO–NASA public downlink/student interaction**, student events across two Indian locations and amateur-radio contact, plus **five joint human-research investigations**. These are distinct from ISRO's **seven shortlisted Indian microgravity experiments**, announced **28 April 2025**; neither count is a claim that all work was completed by May. [ISRO research portfolio](https://www.isro.gov.in/Indian_microgravity_research_Axiom4_mission.html).
- Crew included US commander **Peggy Whitson**, Indian pilot **Shubhanshu Shukla**, Polish **Sławosz Uznański-Wiśniewski** and Hungarian **Tibor Kapu**; Poland/Hungary's first ISS visits do not mean their first citizens ever in space. [Axiom May science briefing](https://www.axiomspace.com/mission-blog/ax4-science-press-conference).
- **2008 THEMIS PYQ: (c)**, high-latitude auroral displays; Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms investigates magnetospheric substorms.
- **2016 MOM PYQ: (c), statements 1 and 3**. Correct the source explanation: ISRO was the **fourth space agency**, after Soviet programme, NASA and ESA, to achieve Mars orbit, not second after the USA; India succeeded at its first attempt. [ISRO MOM](https://www.isro.gov.in/MarsOrbiterMissionSpacecraft.html).

## June 27 headline
- The issue reports Shubhanshu Shukla reached space/ISS and calls him the **634th person in space**. Such ordinal counts depend on the definition/boundary and tracking list; the durable milestone is **first Indian to visit ISS**, after launch on **25 June 2025**, not first Indian ever in space.

## In-flight biological experiments reported July 10
- Shubhanshu Shukla photographed **fenugreek and green-gram sprouts in petri dishes** and stored samples in an ISS freezer to study microgravity effects on germination/early growth. The sprouts experiment involves **University of Agricultural Sciences, Dharwad and IIT Dharwad**; multigeneration post-flight work will examine genetic, microbial and nutritional changes.
- Clipping also reports microalgae deployment/storage for potential food, oxygen and biofuel applications; imaging of six crop-seed varieties for later multigeneration studies; and stem-cell recovery/repair research. These are experiments/potential applications, not demonstrated space-farming self-sufficiency or proven clinical therapy.

## Crop seeds: post-flight research
- **IIST Space Biology Lab + Kerala Agricultural University** study dry seeds exposed aboard Ax-4: rice **Jyothi, Uma**; horse gram **Kanakamani**; tomato **Vellayani Vijay**; sesame **Thilakathara**; brinjal **Soorya**. Dry exposure differs from germinating sprouts on ISS.
- Compare **space-returned, Earth-stored control and fresh seeds** for germination, growth, morphology, flowering/fruiting, yield and genetic changes over subsequent generations. Space radiation/microgravity may alter biology; beneficial mutations or higher yields are hypotheses, not demonstrated outcomes.
- Collaboration involves ISRO/HSFC, IIST and KAU; source identifies project lead **K.G. Sreejalakshmi** and May 2025 MoU. The issue anticipates receipt of seeds after landing; completed mission return is recorded separately.

## Gaganyaan forecast reported August 2025
- Source plans **first uncrewed December 2025, two more 2026, crewed early 2027**: then-announced schedules, not completed flights/guarantees.
- Orbital-module development, crew-escape testing and launch-vehicle human-rating are separate requirements; one qualification claim does not establish total mission readiness.

topics.title: Geographical indications: protection and producer livelihoods
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Meaning and legal anchors
- **GI:** identifies goods whose quality, reputation or other characteristic is essentially attributable to their geographical origin. Covers agricultural/natural/manufactured goods, handicrafts and food products.
- **GI Act, 1999**, effective **2003**; Registry **Chennai**; Registrar is the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks, under the DPIIT/Commerce and Industry framework.
- Registration lasts **10 years**, renewable. Registered proprietors and authorised users have statutory protection; authorised-user registration matters for producer rights. GI is a collective origin-linked right, not an individual transferable brand. [IP India FAQs](https://ipindia.gov.in/pages/gi/learn/faqs).
- **Darjeeling Tea:** India’s first registered GI (2004–05). Global framework: industrial-property protection under the **Paris Convention (1883)** and GI provisions of **WTO TRIPS**. Indian registration does not automatically confer identical protection in every foreign jurisdiction.
## April 2025 development and examples
- **Kannadippaya (bamboo mat), Kerala:** tribal handwoven craft featured in the April 4 clipping; the official GI list confirms its name and registration. Protect skill, authentic production and community benefit, alongside sustainable bamboo supply. [GI Registry list](https://www.ipindia.gov.in/writereaddata/Portal/Images/pdf/Total_Registered_GI_details_of_GI_Application_in_India_15_05_2025.pdf).
| Region | Examples highlighted in the source |
|---|---|
| Uttar Pradesh | Pilkhuwa hand-block printing; Banaras metal casting; Bareilly cane/bamboo craft; Tharu embroidery; Banaras Tirangi Barfi |
| Assam | Bodo Aronai; Bodo Napham (fermented fish); Bodo Jou Gwran (beverage) |
| Andaman and Nicobar | Nicobari Hodi/canoe craft; Andaman Karen Musley Rice; Nicobari virgin coconut oil |
| Gujarat | Kutch Ajrakh textile printing |
| Other recall | Alphonso mango—Maharashtra; Kashmir Pashmina—J&K; Madhubani painting—Bihar; Dharwad Peda—Karnataka; Firozabad glass—UP |
- **Basmati:** GI region covers Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Delhi and specified areas of western UP/J&K. A geographical claim/dispute does not itself extend registration to Madhya Pradesh. [APEDA](https://apeda.gov.in/BasmatiRice).
- **22 January 2025:** Commerce Minister announced a **10,000 GI tags by 2030 target**, with an oversight committee proposed. It is not achieved registration. The PDF’s **605 in July 2024** is a dated count; state rankings depend on date and counting method. Avoid comparing national registrations with foreign jurisdictions’ protection totals as identical measures. [PIB](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2095279&lang=2&reg=48).
## Turning recognition into income
- **Origin and skill → registration + authorised users → quality control and traceability → branding/market access → producer value.** A tag alone does not guarantee premiums or exports.
- Problems: imitation/misuse, weak awareness, unequal regional registration capacity, boundary disputes, fragmented producers and poor post-registration marketing; an imitation’s infringement depends on the protected indication and legal facts, not simply machine production.
- Responses: producer collectives, registration assistance, authentic labelling, enforcement, quality standards, affordable logistics, digital selling and benefit-sharing with artisans/tribal communities.
- GI logo/tagline **“Invaluable Treasures of Incredible India”** supports recognition. APEDA facilitates agricultural exports: Naga Mircha, Manipur black rice and Assam lemon are cited examples.
- **ODOP ≠ GI:** district product promotion may support registered products, but ODOP selection is not a GI certificate. ONDC can improve digital market access; neither guarantees global sales.
- Mains value: rural entrepreneurship, cultural preservation and export differentiation; ensure premiums reach original producers rather than only intermediaries.

## June 27: artisan recognition and differentiated craft
- News list records **Kolhapuri chappal makers' objection to Prada's “replica” sandals**. Kolhapuri chappal is a **2019 GI**, a traditional leather-footwear craft linked to Maharashtra/Karnataka; the headline is a dispute, **not an adjudicated finding of infringement**. [Official craft account](https://handicrafts.nic.in/crafts/All_Crafts/Craft_Categories/Leather/Leather_footwear/Kolhapuri_Chappal/KolhapuriChappalWebPage.html).
- Repeated Kannadippaya clipping adds its distinctive **soft inner reed-bamboo layers and mirror-like patterns**, associated with winter warmth/summer cooling; tribal craft skills and producer benefit matter alongside registration. Named communities include **Oorali, Mannan, Muthuva, Malayan and Kadar**, in Idukki, Thrissur, Ernakulam and Palakkad districts; do not treat GI as restricted to a single household or as proof therapeutic effects.
- Existing 10,000-by-2030 target, legal duration, authorised users, examples and marketing constraints cover the repeated body.

## Prada–Kolhapuri dispute and overseas protection
- The July discussion develops the earlier Prada–Kolhapuri dispute into a distinction between **cultural attribution and territorial legal rights**.
- Protection is **territorial**: domestic registration alone creates no universal international monopoly over a design. Overseas national applications, mutual-recognition agreements and appropriate certification/collective marks can help. The **WIPO Lisbon system** facilitates protection among contracting parties; India is not a member in this issue's timeframe. [WIPO GI explanation](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/geographical-indications).
- Paris Convention, WTO TRIPS and India's GI Act supply distinct international/domestic legal layers. Right to prevent misleading origin claims differs from a patent over an invention or a design right.
- **Traditional-knowledge patent examples:** turmeric wound-healing patent revoked after prior-art challenge; neem antifungal patent revoked in Europe; RiceTec/Basmati controversy concerned patent claims and naming issues. Avoid describing all as identical GI disputes or implying the RiceTec patent was wholly cancelled.
- Responses: searchable authentic-product databases, producer/authorised-user capacity, foreign-market registration where useful, enforcement, ethical brand–artisan collaboration and benefit-sharing. The issue's 658 GI figure lacks a clear matching date/count definition; do not replace the existing dated registry figures with it.

topics.title: NATO: membership and collective defence
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Formation and membership
- **North Atlantic Treaty/Washington Treaty: 4 April 1949.** Political-military alliance initially formed in the Cold War security context; headquarters **Brussels**, Allied Command Operations/SHAPE **Mons, Belgium**.
- Twelve founders: **Belgium, Canada, Denmark, France, Iceland, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, UK and USA**.
- **32 members by April 2025**. Finland joined **4 April 2023**; Sweden **7 March 2024**—both had already joined, rather than merely expressing interest. [NATO membership](https://www.nato.int/en/what-is-nato), [Sweden accession](https://www.nato.int/en/news-and-events/articles/news/2024/03/07/sweden-officially-joins-nato).
| Accession | Members |
|---|---|
| 1952 | Greece, Türkiye |
| 1955 | West Germany; reunited Germany continued membership in 1990 |
| 1982 | Spain |
| 1999 | Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland |
| 2004 | Bulgaria, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia |
| 2009 | Albania, Croatia |
| 2017 / 2020 | Montenegro / North Macedonia |
| 2023 / 2024 | Finland / Sweden |
- **France:** left integrated military command in **1966**, retained NATO membership, rejoined command structures in **2009**. Command participation and treaty membership are distinct.
