- Automate suitable NOCs using geospatial/geotagged data (e.g. airport height restrictions); mining/forest/rail/defence approvals have distinct safety/environmental mandates and cannot be reduced to automatic permission in every case.
- Gig-work framework should recognise flexible work while securing dignity/social protection. The source's claim that States uniformly classify gig workers as full-time employees is too broad; welfare obligations do not automatically create that legal status.
- Reform administrative incentives towards lawful facilitation, published reasons and accountability. Contrast **1991 macro liberalisation** with today's proposed micro-level institutional reform; the source's **8%+ growth for 2047** is an ambition/scenario, not an assured outcome.
- Evaluate turnaround time/compliance cost alongside safety, environment, fair competition and worker protection; streamlined regulation needs credible enforcement, not merely fewer forms.

topics.title: S-400 Triumf and layered air defence
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## System and operational limits
- Russian **Almaz/Almaz-Antey S-400 Triumf**, mobile surface-to-air missile system against aircraft, UAVs, cruise missiles and selected ballistic threats. Command centre, acquisition/engagement radars (including **91N6E**), launchers and transport/reload units operate as a network.
- Source missile-family recall: **40N6 ~400 km; 48N6 variant ~250 km; 9M96E2 ~120 km; 9M96E ~40 km**. Maximum advertised range depends on missile variant, target altitude/profile and configuration; it is not a guaranteed interception radius against every target.
- Source advertises radar detection **up to 600 km**, engagement **up to 80 targets** and Mach **14–15**. Treat these as configuration-specific headline claims; detection, tracking and engagement differ, and maximum target speed is not automatically every interceptor's speed. “Anti-stealth” does not establish assured detection/destruction of all low-observable aircraft.
## India and strategic autonomy
- **October 2018** contract, roughly **US$5.43 billion**, five systems; initial deliveries **2021**. Source's full delivery “expected by 2025” is a forecast, not proof all five had arrived by May 9. Initial Punjab-sector deployment is source-reported; avoid reconstructing sensitive present locations.
- Supports layered protection of infrastructure/airspace and complements other systems; integration with indigenous sensors/command networks, logistics, maintenance, ammunition and Russian supply dependence affect effectiveness.
- **CAATSA: Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act** creates sanctions risk for significant Russian defence transactions. India's purchase reflects defence needs/Russia ties and strategic autonomy; risk is not proof sanctions had been imposed on this purchase.
- Comparators have different missions: **Patriot PAC-3** terminal missile defence, **THAAD** high-altitude terminal ballistic interception, **India–Israel Barak-8** land/naval air defence. Source's Patriot ~160-km number mixes interceptor families; do not rank all systems using a single unqualified “maximum range”.
## June 3: delivery forecast and defence PYQ recall
- Contents heading says **remaining S-400 units expected by 2026**, while generic body repeats **2025**. Treat the former as this issue's updated **reported timetable**, not proof of delivery; no detailed supporting clipping is reproduced. Existing range, speed, configuration and CAATSA qualifications apply.
- **2025 aircraft pairs: (b), only two**—Dornier-228 maritime patrol and C-17 Globemaster III military transport; **IL-76 is military transport, not supersonic combat**.
- **2024 fighter-generation question: (d), none**—Rafale, MiG-29 and Tejas Mk-1 are not fifth generation; spelling “Rafael” in this PDF is an error.
- **2018 THAAD: (c), American anti-missile system**, terminal ballistic-missile interception; distinguish THAAD from general aircraft defence.
- **2008 Barak purchase: (a), Israel**; historic acquisition question is not the same as later India–Israel jointly developed Barak-8. **2016 INS Astradharini: (c), torpedo launch/recovery vessel**. **2008 Dhruv: (c), advanced light helicopter**.

## June 27 delivery headline
- Source's news list reports Russia's Defence Minister **Andrei Belousov assured timely delivery of S-400 systems**. Its generic body still says completion expected “2025”; retain the earlier **2026 reported timetable** as a forecast and avoid presenting assurances as completed delivery.
- Graphic's network sequence: **surveillance radar → command vehicle → engagement radar/launcher → guided interception**. Acquisition range, target speed and engagement envelope are different measures; previous qualifications and six defence PYQ explanations apply.

topics.title: Maternal mortality: indicators, trends and prevention
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Definition and denominator
- **Maternal death:** during pregnancy or within **42 days** of termination, irrespective of pregnancy duration/site, from a cause related to/aggravated by pregnancy or its management; excludes accidental/incidental causes.
- **MMR = maternal deaths ÷ live births × 100,000** in the same period. It differs from maternal mortality rate, lifetime risk and absolute deaths.
## UN estimates 2000–2023: published 7 April 2025
- Global deaths **443,000 → 260,000**; MMR **328 → 197**, about **40% reduction**. Annual reduction slowed from about **2.2% (2000–2023)** to **1.6% (2016–2023)**.
- Sub-Saharan Africa: about **70%** of deaths and MMR **454**; Central/Southern Asia **112**, Oceania excluding Australia/New Zealand **173**, Australia/New Zealand around **3**. Different regional boundaries matter. [UN inter-agency report](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240108462).
- India 2023 estimate: MMR about **80** and **19,000 deaths (~7.2% world total)**, among the largest absolute contributors; DRC ~7.2%, Pakistan ~4.1%. Population size and MMR measure different burdens.
- Source gives India **384 (2000), 103 (2020), 80 (2023)**: this series implies roughly **79% reduction since 2000**. Separate official comparison: **86% India vs 48% global reduction during 1990–2023**, not during 2000–2023. Modelled UN estimates must not be interchanged with India's multi-year **SRS** estimates. [Official clarification, published 10 May](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2128024&lang=2&reg=48).
## SDG and implementation
- **SDG 3.1:** global MMR **below 70 by 2030**; required 2024–30 annual reduction around **14.8%**, much faster than recent progress. A target is not an achieved result.
- India programmes: **JSY** institutional-delivery incentives; **PMSMA** antenatal assessment; **LaQshya** labour-room/maternity-care quality; **Poshan Abhiyaan** nutrition; skilled midwifery services.
- Address unequal rural/tribal access, higher-burden States, anaemia/nutrition, adolescent reproductive health, antenatal/postnatal continuity, timely referral, emergency obstetric care, respectful treatment and trained personnel. Institutional delivery alone does not establish safe high-quality care.

## June issue: programme and indicator distinctions
- Source revisits UNFPA's recognition of India at **50 years of partnership**; do not treat the commemorative occasion as necessarily newly held in June 2025.
- **SUMAN** seeks free, dignified maternal/newborn care and zero denial at public facilities; complements PMSMA antenatal services and skilled midwifery. The source's 90,000-midwives/90%-services wording describes an ambition, not a verified completed workforce.
- Source historical indicators: institutional deliveries about **79% (NFHS-4, 2015–16) → 89% (NFHS-5, 2019–21)**; IMR **39 (2014) → 28 (2020)** per 1,000 live births. Keep reference periods distinct.
- **MMR 97** belongs to **SRS 2018–20**, not simply calendar 2020 or a UN estimate of 70% decline ending at 97. MMR means maternal mortality **ratio**, with live births as denominator; retain the separate UN/SRS series already explained above.

## SRS 2019–21 and the three delays
- **SRS MMR 93** maternal deaths per 100,000 live births. Selected State ratios: **Madhya Pradesh 175, Assam 167, West Bengal 109, Haryana 106; Karnataka 63, Gujarat 53, Jharkhand 51, Tamil Nadu 49, Maharashtra 38, Kerala 20**. Keep this series distinct from UN modelled estimates. Assam is often grouped with EAG States for analysis but is not itself one of the eight EAG States.
- **Three delays:** deciding to seek care → reaching a suitable facility → receiving timely appropriate care. Poverty, gender inequality, transport/referral failure and shortages of trained staff/blood/operating facilities can act at different stages.
- Major preventable pathways: postpartum haemorrhage (often uterine atony), obstructed labour, hypertensive disorders/eclampsia, sepsis and unsafe abortion; anaemia, TB and malaria can contribute indirectly. Unsafe abortion and illegal abortion are not synonyms.
- Strengthen antenatal registration/nutrition, emergency obstetric first-referral units and specialist teams, maternal-death review and postpartum mental-health care. The article proposes **four FRUs per two million population**; its **66% specialist vacancy** figure lacks a current reference period and is not a July 2025 census.
- **Kerala Confidential Review of Maternal Deaths** illustrates learning from each death. Uterine artery clamps/suction techniques are clinical tools requiring trained teams. **JSSK** provides free public-facility maternity/newborn services; **PMMVY**'s second-child benefit is conditional on the child being a girl, not unconditional payment for every second birth.

topics.title: UNHCR and refugee protection
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Institution and mandate
- **United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees**, established by UNGA **1950**, began work **1951** following European WWII displacement; headquarters **Geneva, Switzerland**. Nobel Peace Prize **1954 and 1981**.
- Protection/legal assistance, shelter and other emergency aid, government capacity and durable solutions: **voluntary repatriation, local integration, third-country resettlement**. Works with refugees, stateless people and displaced populations according to relevant mandates; not every internally displaced person automatically has refugee status.
- **1951 Refugee Convention/1967 Protocol:** international refugee framework. India is party to **neither**, but cooperates with UNHCR. Refugee recognition/documentation by UNHCR and domestic immigration status are distinct.
- Funding is **almost entirely voluntary**, mainly governments plus individuals/private donors; a small UN regular-budget contribution makes the source's “entirely” incorrect. [UNHCR funding](https://www.unhcr.org/us/about-unhcr/planning-funding-and-results), [regular-budget evidence](https://reporting.unhcr.org/global-report-2023/income).
- Syria, Afghanistan, Rohingya and Ukraine illustrate different crises. Funding shortfalls, host-country political resistance, uncertain legal identity and protracted displacement complicate protection. Distinguish statelessness from merely lacking an identity document.

topics.title: Nipah virus and zoonotic surveillance
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## May 2025 Kerala report
- Embedded clipping reports a **42-year-old woman** testing positive in **Malappuram**, treated at **Perinthalmanna**; health authorities traced contacts and imposed surveillance/restrictions around her Valanchery residence. Initial seven close-contact tests were negative. The infection source was **unknown**; investigating local-fruit exposure did not establish a confirmed transmission route.
## Pathogen and transmission
- **Nipah (NiV): RNA virus, Paramyxoviridae, Henipavirus**; related to Hendra. Identified in **1998–99 Malaysia/Singapore** outbreaks involving pigs; pigs were amplification hosts, **Pteropus fruit bats** the natural reservoir. Other domestic animals can be infected.
- Bat-secretions-contaminated food, including **raw date-palm sap**, and infected-animal exposure can transmit infection. Close contact with infected patients/fluids, including healthcare exposure, supports human-to-human spread; bat urine/saliva contamination is especially relevant.
- Clinical spectrum: fever/headache, drowsiness/confusion and severe **encephalitis/coma**, sometimes acute respiratory illness. Case fatality typically **40–75%**, varying by outbreak/care; source's ~70% is not universal. [CDC clinical overview](https://www.cdc.gov/nipah-virus/hcp/clinical-overview/index.html).
- **RT-PCR** and serology support diagnosis. No licensed specific antiviral/vaccine in the source period; intensive supportive care is central. Experimental candidates are not approved routine treatment.
- Kerala outbreaks since **2018**; India also has earlier West Bengal outbreaks. ICMR/NIV diagnostics, human/animal surveillance, rapid isolation/contact follow-up, PPE, hospital infection control and food-safety awareness are priorities. Avoid contaminated/partly eaten fruit and unprotected sap collection; protecting bat habitats is compatible with reducing risky exposure.
- WHO priority R&D disease: zoonotic spillover, severe disease and limited countermeasures support a **One Health** approach; priority status is not evidence a pandemic has begun.

topics.title: Chikungunya: vectors, disease and vaccines
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Disease and vector control
- **CHIKV: RNA Alphavirus, Togaviridae**; identified in **southern Tanzania, 1952**. Kimakonde name refers to a bent posture from severe joint pain.
- Infected female **Aedes aegypti/Aedes albopictus**, mainly daytime biters, transmit disease; these also transmit dengue/Zika. Ae. aegypti is an important yellow-fever vector, but do not equate both species' vector roles for every disease.
- Sudden fever, severe/prolonged joint pain, joint swelling, headache, muscle pain and rash; dengue/Zika overlap complicates diagnosis. Africa/Asia/Americas predominate, with outbreaks in Europe/Pacific; travel, vector suitability and climate affect spread.
- PCR early/serology later; no specific antiviral. Symptomatic treatment, rest/hydration; **paracetamol initially**, delay aspirin/NSAIDs until dengue is excluded because of bleeding risk. [WHO, 14 April 2025](https://www.who.int/en/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/chikungunya).
- Reduce container/stagnant-water breeding, improve sanitation, repellents/clothing and appropriate nets; community surveillance and early reporting complement clinical care. National vector-borne programme covers **malaria, dengue, chikungunya, lymphatic filariasis, kala-azar and Japanese encephalitis**, now coordinated through NCVBDC.
## Vaccines: distinguish dates and safety
- **Ixchiq**, Valneva, single-dose intramuscular **live-attenuated** vaccine: FDA first approval **9 November 2023**, adults **18+** at increased exposure risk. US approval does not establish Indian approval/universal routine use.
- **9 May 2025:** FDA/CDC recommended pausing Ixchiq for **60+** while reviewing serious postmarketing neurologic/cardiac reports. Reported events are not automatically proved vaccine-caused; source's “only mild symptoms” understates recognised risk. [FDA dated safety communication](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/safety-availability-biologics/fda-and-cdc-recommend-pause-use-ixchiq-chikungunya-vaccine-live-individuals-60-years-age-and-older).
- **Vimkunya**, non-live virus-like-particle vaccine, FDA approval **14 February 2025**, **12+**: by May 2025 Ixchiq was no longer the only approved product. [FDA product/approval letter](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/vimkunya). Vaccines supplement vector control; availability and recommendations remain jurisdiction-specific.

topics.title: Public health governance and workforce education
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## May 2025 editorial: prevention and interdisciplinary capacity
- **World Health Day, 7 April 2025:** “Healthy beginnings, hopeful futures”. Public health combines medicine/epidemiology, engineering/sanitation, nutrition, social sciences, communication and community engagement; it extends beyond hospitals/doctors.
- **State List entry 6:** public health/sanitation, hospitals/dispensaries; Union responsibilities include port quarantine, census and international functions. Concurrent responsibilities include drugs/poisons, population control/family planning, food adulteration and interstate infectious-disease prevention. Do not infer a neat exclusive ministry allocation from the source's simplified list.
- Fragmentation among health, water/sanitation, food-safety and municipal agencies impedes coordination. Tobacco-health control versus cultivation promotion illustrates conflicting policy incentives; the colonial-legacy explanation is editorial analysis.
## MPH education and careers
- Editorial identifies variable **Master of Public Health** admission criteria/curricula, uneven field exposure, weak public-health engineering, applied nutrition, behavioural science/social marketing and health technology assessment.
- Two-year programmes combine epidemiology, policy, economics, behaviour, operational research, fieldwork and thesis; compressed coverage may reduce practical depth. The assertion of “no national baseline curriculum” is too absolute: distinguish existing model guidance from **uniform mandatory implementation/accreditation**.
- Insufficient public-health cadres and stable posts can underuse graduates in temporary projects/NGOs. Avoid treating every State/programme as equally deficient.
- Proposed reforms: coordinated minimum competencies with interdisciplinary entry, practical placements, technical/behavioural/HTA training, modular flexibility, recognised public-health career pathways and sustained preventive funding. These are recommendations, not reforms already implemented in this issue.
- Mains chain: **clear interdepartmental responsibility → trained multidisciplinary workforce → prevention/surveillance → timely outbreak response and equitable maternal/community health**.

topics.title: UP-AGREES: agricultural productivity and rural enterprises
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## 9 May 2025: Uttar Pradesh launch
- **Uttar Pradesh Agriculture Growth and Rural Enterprise Ecosystem Strengthening (UP-AGREES)** launched by CM Yogi Adityanath during World Bank President Ajay Banga's Lucknow visit; inset identifies **28 Bundelkhand/Purvanchal districts**. Aim: productivity, farmer incomes, agricultural diversification, digital/climate-resilient practices, finance, market linkages and rural enterprises.
- Source's yield increase **10 → 14–15 quintals/acre** is a stated ambition without a specified crop/baseline; not an achieved statewide yield improvement. Value addition, post-harvest facilities and enterprise opportunities can improve incomes if implementation succeeds.
- **World Bank approval, 12 December 2024: US$325.10 million IBRD loan**, planned benefit to **one million farmers**, with intended **US$15 million private-finance mobilisation**. Final maturity **33.5 years**, including **6-year grace period**; a six-year implementation/grace figure is not a six-year loan maturity. Source's ₹2,737 crore figure is a rupee-equivalent report, not verified funding separately allocated to AI Pragya. [World Bank approval](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/12/12/world-bank-supports-project-to-modernize-agriculture-systems-in-india-s-uttar-pradesh-state-benefiting-1-million-farmers).
- UP is a major wheat, rice, potato, fruit/vegetable producer; smallholders face investment/technology and post-harvest gaps. Source's **75% cultivable land, 15% vegetables, 11% fruits, 23% foodgrains, 16–17% population**, and blanket first-place list (wheat,potatoes,mangoes,guavas,peas,mushrooms,watermelons,honey) lack common reference year/definitions; retain as source-reported context rather than verified contemporary rankings. Inset's **US$1-trillion UP economy** is an aspiration, not achieved size.

topics.title: AI Pragya: digital skills in Uttar Pradesh
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## 9 May 2025: programme announcement
- **AI Pragya**, source expansion: *Artificial Intelligence Programme for Resourcefulness, Awareness, Growth and Youth Advancement*, targets **10 lakh citizens/youth** trained in AI, ML, cybersecurity, data analytics and emerging technologies. It is a training target, not a completed beneficiary total.
- Source identifies **Centre for e-Governance, UP IT & Electronics Department** as nodal agency; collaboration across education, health, agriculture and rural development. Partners listed: **Microsoft, Intel, HCL, Amazon, Google and Wadhwani Foundation**; each partnership's exact obligations require programme documents. [UP IT department presentation](https://uplc.up.gov.in/policy/Department-of-IT-and-Electronics-2025.pdf).
- Goals: digital literacy, employability, rural–urban inclusion and startup capability, including Noida's ecosystem. Source's **14,000+ DPIIT startups/US$8.6 billion since 2014** are dated reported counts/funding estimates without verified cutoff, not programme achievements.
## Distinguish funding and programmes
- UP-AGREES IBRD support should not be described as a verified joint loan earmarked equally for AI Pragya. National **IndiaAI Mission approved 7 March 2024: ₹10,371.92 crore**, over five years; source's **₹2,000 crore** is not its total approved outlay. [Cabinet decision](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2012357&lang=2&reg=48).
- The issue lists **PMKVY 4.0** AI training, Digital India future-skills support, **₹500 crore AI education CoE** and State examples **Telangana T-AIM/Tamil Nadu AI for Youth**. These are separate programmes/allocations; unverified **19,000 trained/₹1,000 crore skilling** must not be conflated with AI Pragya reach.
- Evaluate access/connectivity, curriculum quality, trainers, cybersecurity/ethical literacy, certification and actual placements; training announcements alone do not prove employment or bridging the digital divide.

topics.title: Food systems: nutrition, access and sustainability
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Triple burden and indicator caution
- Food security includes nutritious affordable diets, not cereal output alone: **undernutrition, micronutrient deficiencies and overweight/obesity** can coexist. Climate stress, biodiversity loss, low incomes and poor storage compound inequity/NCD risks.
- **NFHS-5 (2019–21), under 5:** stunting **35.5%** (low height-for-age), wasting **19.3%** (low weight-for-height), underweight **32.1%** (low weight-for-age). Source lists adult overweight/obesity **women 24%, men 22.9%**, and anaemia **57% women 15–49**. These are distinct indicators/cohorts, not proportions all suffering the same condition. [Official NFHS nutrition figures](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1779258&lang=2&reg=3).
- Source's **194 million undernourished** is not an NFHS national calorie-undernourishment count; it needs a separate FAO estimate/year. **GHI 2024: 105/127** is a composite rank, not a direct census of hunger or every nutritional condition.
- Article cites **55.6% unable to afford healthy diet in 2022 at PPP US$3.36/day**; dollar-PPP diet cost is not a nominal exchange-rate rupee price, and affordability estimates depend on methodology/reference year. Global **US$12 trillion/year food-system costs** are an estimated hidden-cost concept, not India's fiscal spending or an audited invoice.
## Transformation priorities
- **Nutrition-sensitive agriculture:** diverse/biofortified crops, nutrition goals in farm policy, better storage/processing and locally suitable foods; supplementation/fortification complements dietary diversity rather than replaces it.
- **Nutrition-Sensitive Community Planning:** connect food with WASH, soil/water conservation and healthcare. Source's **Nutri-Pathshala** model combines nutrition education, biofortified grains and local sourcing to support small farmers; programme examples are not proof every implementation succeeded.
- Diversify PDS and **PM-POSHAN (mid-day meals)** appropriately; strengthen safety nets and healthy-diet behaviour campaigns. Private sector: understandable labels, responsibly fortified foods, suitable plant alternatives and digital/QR education; innovation needs nutrition/equity safeguards.
- Climate-smart, gender-inclusive farming and rural opportunities; nutrition literacy via interactive tools (source example **MyPlate Blast Off**) and radio for remote areas.
- Source's **TERI–FOLU Himalayan model:** region-specific micronutrient-rich crops, local food networks and decentralised processing; assess measured outcomes rather than asserting universal success. Integrate nutrition/health expertise with planning; links **SDG 2, 3, 12**. [FAO dietary guidance](https://www.fao.org/nutrition/education/dietary-guidelines/regions/india/en/).
## Gender justice and nutrition: May 2025
- **NFHS-5, 2019–21:** anaemia affects **57% of women 15–49**, versus about **25% of men 15–49**; roughly **18.7% of women** have low BMI. Women's anaemia rose from **53% in NFHS-4 (2015–16)**. These are different indicators; anaemia is not identical to calorie undernutrition and can have multiple causes. [Official health statistics](https://www.mohfw.gov.in/sites/default/files/Publication%20Health%20and%20Family%20Welfare%20Statistics%20in%20India%202023.pdf).
- Unequal intra-household food allocation, women eating last, unpaid care, weak income control, poverty and low bargaining power can limit adequate diets despite food availability. Employment alone does not ensure safe work, fair wages or control over earnings.
- **POSHAN Abhiyaan (2018)** sought phased reductions in stunting/undernutrition and anaemia, not literal elimination of every form of malnutrition by 2022. **Saksham Anganwadi/POSHAN 2.0** integrates relevant services; before/after survey comparisons alone cannot isolate programme causality. [Official objectives](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1602195&lang=2&reg=48).
- Source **69% fund utilisation in 2022–23**, **49% lacking control over own income** and **53% self-employed earnings gap** lack complete denominator/accounting/method details. Do not present them as universal statistics for every Indian woman; distinguish access to personal money from sole/joint decisions over cash earnings.
- **PLFS female LFPR, usual status, age 15+: 23.3% in 2017–18 →32.8% in 2021–22**. Rounded source 23→33 is consistent, but LFPR includes those seeking/available for work and is not the employment rate; unpaid family work/informal employment requires job-quality analysis. [Official PLFS series](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2004075&lang=2&reg=48).
- **Proposals:** link nutrition with **NRLM, MGNREGS, SHGs, skills, credit/financial literacy** and maternal healthcare; make Anganwadis accessible hubs for nutrition, literacy and livelihood referrals without overburdening workers.
- Measure dietary/health outcomes alongside income control, job security/pay equity and service use; coordinate health, WCD and rural-livelihood departments. **Jan Andolan** awareness complements actual food/health access; neither awareness nor larger allocation alone guarantees consumption/outcomes.
- Mains: nutrition problem → gendered resource/power structures → programme gaps → accountable services plus social/economic empowerment. The source's 250-word question is practice, not a PYQ.

## India–UK CETA: commercial determinants of health
- **24 July 2025:** India and UK signed **Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement**. Signature is distinct from ratification/entry into force and phased tariff concessions; the editorial's “tariff-free access” should not be read as all HFSS tariffs already zero on July24. [Official agreement and chapters](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/comprehensive-economic-and-trade-agreement-between-the-united-kingdom-of-great-britain-and-northern-ireland-and-india).
- Editorial concern: cheaper/more marketed **high-fat, sugar and salt (HFSS)** foods may raise unhealthy consumption/NCD risk, especially in children. **HFSS is a nutrient-profile classification; ultra-processed is a processing classification**—overlap is not identity. Trade does not by itself prove a specified rise in disease.
- Commercial determinants include pricing, promotion, lobbying and food availability. Source quotes **13.3% annual growth in UPF sales, 2011–21**; distinguish nominal sales value from volume/individual intake and from all HFSS products.
- Recommended safeguards: health-impact assessment in negotiations, preserve legitimate health regulation, transparent industry conflicts, clear front-of-pack warnings, child-marketing controls, healthier school environments and public-health participation. Warning labels and star ratings are different designs; source favours Chile-style warnings, while India's **2022 star-rating proposal was a draft**.
- India already has **2020 school-food restrictions**; “no child HFSS framework” is too broad. Mexico's **2014 sugary-drink tax** and later warning-label regime are different dates, not one 2014 measure.
- **UK date correction known before this issue:** legal TV-before-9pm/paid-online less-healthy-food advertising restrictions had been deferred to **5 January 2026**; industry voluntary compliance was expected from **1 October 2025**. Source presents October as the legal start. [Government update, 4 June 2025](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/less-healthy-food-or-drink-advertising-and-promotions-restrictions).
- Mains structure: economic gains → food-environment/inequality risks → existing regulatory gaps → proportionate health safeguards. Printed 250-word India–UK question is contemporary practice, with no verified exam year.

topics.title: NOTAMs: aviation hazards and operational notices
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Purpose and terminology
- **NOTAM:** aeronautical notice disseminating time-critical establishment, condition or changes in facilities/services/procedures or hazards essential to flight operations. Issued through authorised aeronautical-information systems; informs pilots, controllers and airport/other personnel.
- Source singular **“Notice to Air Mission”** is imprecise. The FAA used **Notice to Air Missions**, then reverted to **Notice to Airmen on 10 February 2025**; nomenclature is jurisdiction-specific, not proof of a universal ICAO rename. [FAA definition/history](https://www.faa.gov/about/initiatives/notam/what_is_a_notam).
- Typical triggers: restricted airspace/military exercises/VIP movements, runway/taxiway closures, failed navigation aids/lights, cranes/temporary obstacles, airshows/parachuting/glider operations and urgent hazards. Do not mistake every NOTAM for complete airspace closure.
## Format and use
- **NOTAMN new; NOTAMR replaces; NOTAMC cancels**. Encoded identifiers, location, validity times, vertical limits and explanatory text require trained interpretation; source graphic categories **aerodrome/en-route/navigation warning** describe operational grouping, not an exhaustive universal letter code. Printed sample is illustrative, not a live restriction.
- Distributed quickly via NOTAM databases and electronic flight-planning/briefing channels; safety preparation combines applicable notices with weather, route, airport and other information. Check start/end times and replacement/cancellation before flight; stale/incomplete review can cause delays, hazards or airspace violations.

topics.title: Arnala: shallow-water anti-submarine warfare craft
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## 8 May 2025: delivery
- **Arnala**, first of **eight GRSE ASW shallow-water craft**, delivered to Navy at **L&T Kattupalli**; GRSE designed/built under PPP collaboration, to **Indian Register of Shipping classification rules**. Delivery is distinct from commissioning/operational induction; May 10 issue should not imply commissioning already occurred.
- Named for **Arnala Fort off Vasai, Maharashtra**; length **77 m**; largest Indian naval warship powered by **diesel engine–waterjet combination**, not largest Navy warship overall. **Over 80% indigenous content**, not necessarily 80% counted components under a specified denominator.
- Roles: shallow/coastal underwater surveillance and ASW; search/rescue, **Low Intensity Maritime Operations**, advanced mine-laying. Shallow-water platforms complement other fleet assets and improve littoral security; announced roles are not evidence of a completed combat deployment.
- Indigenous design/supply chains and public/private shipbuilding cooperation support self-reliance and maritime readiness. Eight refers to this GRSE contract, not necessarily the total national ASW-SWC programme. [MoD delivery announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2127729&lang=2&reg=48).

topics.title: Tapti Basin Mega Recharge Project
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## 10 May 2025: inter-State MoU
- **Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra** signed an MoU in Bhopal for the proposed **Tapti Basin Mega Recharge Project**. The newspaper clipping identifies **Mohan Yadav** as MP Chief Minister and **Devendra Fadnavis** as Maharashtra Chief Minister; the summary's “Deputy CM” designation is wrong for this event.
- **Tapti/Tapi** rises near **Multai, Betul district**, in the Satpuras, flows west south of the Narmada, and reaches the **Gulf of Khambhat/Arabian Sea**. Length about **724 km**; basin covers MP, Maharashtra and Gujarat. [CWC basin record](https://www.cwc.gov.in/sites/default/files/admin/9_N%26TBO_Gandhinagar_WestFlowingRivers_SYB_2015-16.pdf).
- **31.13 TMC** planned water use: **11.76 TMC MP + 19.37 TMC Maharashtra**. The source’s 19.36 is inconsistent with the Chief Minister’s release. TMC means thousand million cubic feet.
- Proposed irrigation: **123,082 hectares in MP (Burhanpur/Khandwa)** and **234,706 hectares in Maharashtra (Jalgaon/Akola/Buldhana/Amravati)**. The plan includes a dam at **Khariya Guti Ghat** and an estimated **₹19,244 crore cost at 2022–23 prices**.
- **Nagpur’s long-term drinking-water benefit concerned the separate Jamghat project discussed at the same meeting**, not a verified Tapti recharge allocation to Nagpur. [Chief Minister’s 10 May release](https://www.devendrafadnavis.in/press-release/tapi-mega-recharge-prakalpababat-maharashtra-aani-madhyapradeshat-aitihasik-karar/).
- MP's land requirement reported at **3,362 hectares**, with officials claiming no village displacement/rehabilitation needed. This is a project claim requiring social-impact verification, not an independently established guarantee of no livelihood effects.
- Leaders sought **national-project recognition and 90% central funding**; these were requests/expectations, not confirmed sanction or money released. The MoU was finalised after an inter-State Control Board meeting reportedly held for the first time in **25 years**; the concept dates to the **1990s**.
- “World's largest recharge project” is an attributed political claim, not an independently verified global ranking. Signing an MoU does not mean recharge/irrigation benefits have already materialised.
- Assess aquifer geology, recharge rates, water quality, downstream/environmental flows (including Gujarat), hydrological climate variability, EIA/SIA, community participation, financing and regular joint-board oversight. Ken–Betwa and Parvati–Kalisindh–Chambal illustrate cooperation, not identical project design.

topics.title: BrahMos: supersonic cruise missile
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## System and distinctions
- **Brahmaputra + Moskva** gives the name; **DRDO–Russia's NPOM** joint venture. **Supersonic cruise missile**, not a ballistic missile or hypersonic BrahMos-II.
- Two stages: **solid booster → liquid-fuel ramjet** sustained flight; approximately **Mach 2.8**. Original **~290-km** range differs from extended-range tested variants; specify variant instead of treating one range as universal.
- Land/ship/air versions; air launch from modified **Su-30MKI**. Submarine version was tested from a **submerged platform on 20 March 2013**; demonstration is not proof operational fit on every Indian submarine. [BrahMos test](https://brahmos.com/press-release/166).
- All-weather/day-night and fire-and-forget guidance; no continuous operator command does **not** mean no onboard guidance. Mission planning, sensors, target profile and platform configuration affect precision; avoid absolute “fastest in world” claims.
- Tactical strike/deterrence, indigenous capability with international collaboration and defence-export diplomacy. The clipping's “missile triad” means land/sea/air launch modes, **not India's nuclear triad**.
- **Philippines first delivery, 19 April 2024**, already preceded this issue: source incorrectly groups it with merely prospective exports. Vietnam discussions do not establish a signed/delivered sale. [BrahMos delivery](https://www.brahmos.com/brahmos-in-media/114).
## 16 May 2025 : export interest
- Source reports heightened interest following Operation Sindoor. **Philippines: confirmed US$375 million contract for three coastal-defence batteries**, with deliveries beginning in 2024. Indonesia/Vietnam/Malaysia and other listed Asian, Latin American, Gulf, African and European markets are **reported discussions/interest**, not signed/delivered sales.
- DRDO–NPOM ownership **50.5%–49.5%**; first test **12 June 2001**. Source warhead 200–300 kg, speed Mach 2.8–3 and extended 500–800 km ranges are variant/configuration-dependent, not specifications of every exported missile. Submerged-platform tests do not establish operational submarine deployment.
- Brah Mos-II is a **hypersonic development ambition**, distinct from existing supersonic Brah Mos. Export opportunities depend on approvals, financing, integration, training and support; commercial interest alone is not export revenue.

## Practice wording correction: May 2025
- Worksheet statement 1 is false: **supersonic DRDO–Russia NPOM collaboration**, not subsonic India–Israel. Statement 2, land/air/sea launches, is correct.
- Statement 3's unqualified “range limited to 290 km due to MTCR” is ambiguous/stale: **original variant about 290 km; extended-range variants existed before this issue**. Source answer **(b) 2 and 3** works only if explicitly referring to the original configuration; **(a) 2 only** fits an assertion that every present variant is still capped. Do not silently endorse the latter claim. [Manufacturer extended-range test](https://www.brahmos.com/press-release/207).

## 22 May 2025: export graphic caution
- Repeated post-Sindoor export-interest table does not establish new contracts: source Indonesia **$200–350 million**, Vietnam **$700 million**, and Malaysia/Thailand/Singapore/Brunei, Brazil/Chile/Argentina/Venezuela, Egypt/Saudi Arabia/UAE/Qatar/Oman, South Africa/Bulgaria are **reported prospects**, not verified completed sales. Philippines contract/deliveries are separately established in existing notes.
- Source height **15 km/10 m** and warhead/range figures describe configurations/flight profiles, not universal parameters of every missile. Operational performance cannot be inferred solely from promotional specifications.
- Graphic wrongly implies MTCR membership permits development above thresholds but categorically forbids exports. MTCR is an **export-control arrangement**, with a strong presumption of denial for qualifying Category I systems capable of delivering **≥500 kg to ≥300 km**; it is not a universal domestic-development ban or automatic ban on every missile exceeding 300 km. Hypersonic **Mach ≥5** is distinct from BrahMos's supersonic speed; BrahMos-II remains a development ambition.
- Export-control details: [US State Department MTCR FAQ](https://2021-2025.state.gov/remarks-and-releases-bureau-of-international-security-and-nonproliferation/missile-technology-control-regime-mtcr-frequently-asked-questions/).

topics.title: Women, land rights and environmental governance
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## May 2025 editorial: agency without authority
- Adivasi, Dalit and rural women organise environmental/anti-displacement resistance yet may lack title, consultation influence, compensation eligibility and formal leadership. Examples: **Sijimali, Odisha** bauxite; **Jharkhand coal-mining resistance**; **Kudankulam, Tamil Nadu** fishing communities/nuclear plant; **Phulbari, Bangladesh** open-pit mining; **Narmada Bachao Andolan/Medha Patkar** dam displacement. The rewritten source's **“Dewas, Jharkhand”** is geographically unreliable; Dewas city/district is in Madhya Pradesh, so retain only the supported Jharkhand example without inventing a corrected village.
- **Free, prior and informed consent (FPIC)** demands timely, understandable information and freedom from coercion; presence in a male-dominated meeting does not prove meaningful influence. Women's ecological knowledge can be dismissed as emotional while title/household-head rules obscure unpaid work and resource dependence.
## Legal safeguards and limits
- **Forest Rights Act 2006**: individual rights registered jointly for married spouses; **FRA Rules** require women's representation in Forest Rights Committees and Gram Sabha quorum. Implementation and actual voice still need monitoring. [Tribal Ministry framework](https://tribal.nic.in/FRA.aspx), [Rules](https://tribal.nic.in/downloads/acts-and-rules/FRARulesBook.pdf).
- **PESA 1996** protects Scheduled-Area Gram Sabha/community powers; distinguish consultation and consent requirements under particular laws rather than claiming every development project has identical FPIC procedure.
- **Hindu Succession Amendment 2005** grants equal daughter coparcenary rights within its applicable framework; **Section 2(2)** generally excludes Scheduled Tribes absent a Central notification. It cannot be assumed to replace all tribal customary inheritance. [Act](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1713/1/AAA1956suc___30.pdf).
- Nepal joint-ownership and Bangladesh **khas-land distribution** are comparative arrangements cited by the editorial, not uniform guaranteed individual entitlements for every woman.
## Climate justice and reform proposals
- Resource depletion can increase water/fuel collection, care work and livelihood insecurity; exposure differs by caste, class, community and place. **Ecofeminism** links domination of women/nature as an analytical lens, not a substitute for evidence.
- Accessible local-language/translated technical information, safe meeting spaces/timing, legal literacy/aid and skilled facilitation; women-only preparatory consultations where helpful, followed by meaningful authority in legally required decision bodies.
- Joint/individual titles, compensation recognising independent livelihood and non-titleholder losses, inclusion of single women/widows/caregivers, representative negotiation/rehabilitation boards and funded leadership training. These are recommendations; assess actual consent, influence and benefit distribution rather than attendance alone.

topics.title: Kerala waste management and the Vruthi campaign
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Campaign and changing waste
- **Malinya Muktham Nava Keralam**, Waste-Free New Kerala: State/local-government mobilisation for source segregation, treatment and responsible disposal. **Vruthi 2025 Clean Kerala Conclave**, **9–13 April, Kanakakkunnu, Thiruvananthapuram**, showcased waste-management practices; it is associated with the campaign rather than the campaign's formal name. [Kerala LSGD](https://lsgd.kerala.gov.in/en/latest_news/vruthi-2025-the-clean-kerala-conclave/).
- Consumption/urbanisation increased plastic and mixed/non-biodegradable waste beyond older household composting/manure practices. Source agriculture share “<10% GDP” is a broad State-economy context, not a measured waste-generation share.
- **Haritha Karmasena**, local self-governments, schools/colleges/youth, residents/business/worker groups; culture/arts and local competition seek sustained **“My Waste, My Responsibility”** behaviour. Reported sanitation-worker canal death in Thiruvananthapuram, dog bites/zoonotic risks and **Brahmapuram, Kochi, 2023 fire** illustrate health/occupational/ecological stakes; sanitation failure is not the sole proven cause of every disease.
## Centralised/decentralised: choose by waste stream
- Central facilities can deliver scale/professional treatment; **Guruvayur** is source's positive example. Brahmapuram failure shows governance/operation risks, not proof every central facility fails. Local processing supports participation but needs expertise, space and funding; use appropriate hybrid systems with collection/transport links.
- The source caricatures **Swachh Bharat** as only top-down toilet building: **SBM-U 2.0**, launched 2021, explicitly targets **garbage-free cities**, scientific solid-waste processing and sustained sanitation. Kerala's emphasis on local mobilisation can complement national policy. [SBM-U 2.0](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1780913&lang=2&reg=48).
- Priorities: segregation and reliable collection, safe wet-waste processing, material recovery/recycling and hazardous-stream separation; avoid transferring dumping burdens to marginalised communities.
- Strengthen **Extended Producer Responsibility**, verified recycling/end-market links, worker safety/tools/training, professional local capacity and transparent monitoring. State-driven campaign momentum/garbage-free declarations need sustained service-quality evidence; a 100% aspiration is not proof all litter/dumping ended.
- Kerala Urban Policy Commission's professionalisation recommendation and participatory awareness require implementation, finance and accountability to survive beyond a publicity campaign.

topics.title: Boron and nuclear criticality safety
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Boron: established science and May 2025 rumours
- **Boron-10** strongly absorbs neutrons; boron-bearing materials/solutions help control reactor reactivity and prevent inadvertent criticality in appropriate fuel-handling systems. Effectiveness depends on concentration, geometry and validated engineering, not merely delivery of raw boron. [IAEA criticality safety](https://nucleus.iaea.org/sites/nss-oui/Published%20Chunks/m_50d5ac40-0b83-46c9-9192-223620d551fe/c_bee262ad-39f1-4966-ba74-b09dd92b8558__10_0.Html).
- The May 13 PDF links a purported **11 May Egyptian aircraft visit (EGY1916)** to possible boron delivery after India–Pakistan exchanges. **No confirmed cargo, nuclear accident or remediation operation is established**. Flight-tracker interpretation and reports of Nile Delta soil boron do not demonstrate shipment or make Egypt a proven strategic supplier.
- Historical use of neutron absorbers during emergencies, including Chernobyl, does not corroborate this particular rumour. Alleged Kirana Hills tunnel area, stored weapons and radiation damage remain unverified in this material; do not memorise the supplied 68 sq km as an established nuclear inventory.

topics.title: DGMO: military operations and crisis communication
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Role and dated officeholders
- **Director General of Military Operations**, a senior Indian Army appointment normally held by a **Lieutenant General**, in Army Headquarters, New Delhi; military operations planning, operational readiness, intelligence coordination and advice within the Army/COAS command system.
- May 2025 briefing team: **Lt Gen Rajiv Ghai (Army DGMO), Air Marshal A.K. Bharti (Director General Air Operations), Vice Admiral A.N. Pramod (Director General Naval Operations)**. These are distinct service appointments, not three officers holding the Army DGMO post. Pakistan's counterpart in the source is **Maj Gen Kashif Abdullah**. [Official briefing collection](https://www.pib.gov.in/EventDetail.aspx?ID=1206&lang=1&reg=3).
- Source dates Ghai's appointment **25 October 2024**; officeholder recall is tied to May 2025 and must not be presented as permanently current.
## Operations, coordination and hotline
- Links planning, readiness, border/LoC operations, intelligence inputs, military policy advice and inter-service liaison. Other commanders and service headquarters retain their responsibilities; DGMO is not the independent commander of every tri-service action.
- Hotline communication conveys violations, clarifies intentions and supports de-escalation/confidence-building. Regular calls and crisis calls are distinct; the PDF's **1990 origin / weekly schedule** needs institutional-history corroboration.
- **10 May 2025** understanding to halt military actions followed DGMO communication; **12 May** talks addressed continuation and avoiding firing/aggressive action and reducing border troop concentrations. A cessation understanding is not a peace treaty or settlement of underlying disputes.
- Historical recall: **Kargil 1999, surgical strikes 2016, Pulwama–Balakot 2019** illustrate operations/crisis-coordination contexts; Balakot was an Air Force action, not simply an Army DGMO operation.
- **Pahalgam attack: 22 April 2025**, correcting the source's isolated April 2024 typo. Source's detailed branches/agency liaison list is illustrative, not a verified complete organisational chart.

topics.title: Lactase persistence and gene–culture coevolution
topics.subject: Anthropology
topics.markdown:
## Concepts and the March 2025 study
- **Lactase** breaks milk sugar **lactose → glucose + galactose**. Activity usually falls after weaning; adult persistence varies genetically. Malabsorption may cause gas/bloating/diarrhoea but is distinct from milk allergy and not every low-lactase individual has identical symptoms.
- Different regulatory variants supporting the same adult trait illustrate **convergent evolution**. Dairying can alter selection pressures: **gene–culture coevolution**; adoption of livestock and spread of alleles need not occur simultaneously in every population.
- **PNAS, 10 March 2025:** identified an East Asian-specific **Neanderthal-derived haplotype near LCT**, apparently positively selected before dairying. **It does not prove that this haplotype causes East Asian lactase persistence**; phenotype samples were unavailable and regulatory/immune-cell associations are indirect. Immune-function selection is a hypothesis. [Original study](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2404393122).
- Study estimates selection timing varied: approximately **24,500–27,000 years ago in Han populations**, later in the analysed Vietnamese group; the source's blanket **“over 30,000 years”** is inaccurate. Ancient DNA includes an **Amur-region individual ~14,000 years old**. Reported **28.9%** denotes **haplotype carriers**, not a demonstrated milk-tolerance rate.
- Introgression = genetic material entering a population through interbreeding. Neanderthal ancestry varies; blanket “Africans have zero” and a universal **80,000–120,000-year admixture date** oversimplify complex evidence. Do not equate age of a sequenced Neanderthal individual with date of admixture.
- Takeaway: natural selection at a locus can reflect multiple functions; physiological adaptation, haplotype frequency and cultural practices require separate evidence. The finding complicates, rather than disproves, gene–culture coevolution.

topics.title: Himalayan plastic waste and packaging accountability
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Himalayan Cleanup: 2024 audit reported in May 2025
- **The Himalayan Cleanup (THC)**, active since **2018**, led by **Zero Waste Himalaya (Gangtok)** and **Integrated Mountain Initiative (Dehradun)** with local partners; waste/brand audits help identify upstream packaging sources.
- Audit: **121,739 collected items; 106,857 plastic (~87.8%)**; food/beverage packaging **84.2%** of audited plastics. The audit is a sampled collection, **not a census of all Himalayan waste**. [IMI original newsletter/report account](https://www.mountaininitiative.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/IMI-NEWSLETTER-OCT-2024.pdf).
- Source reports around **70% of plastics non-recyclable**, and **71% of food packaging**; multilayer packaging/cartons often have poor local recovery economics. “Not locally recyclable/no resale value” does not imply every composite carton is technically impossible to recycle anywhere.
- Collection counts: **Sikkim 53,814 (~44% of all items); Darjeeling 36,180**; Ladakh, Nagaland and Uttarakhand also participated. Higher collected counts may reflect coverage/effort as well as pollution; they do not prove a standardised region-wide ranking.
- Risks: litter near rivers, schools, tourism sites and protected areas threatens water, landscapes and biodiversity. Mountain transport/remoteness constrain viable collection/recycling.
## Beyond cleanup
- Reduce unnecessary single-use packaging; reusable/refill systems and appropriate redesign; segregated collection and material tracking; enforce producer responsibility and brand accountability.
- Tourism/local-government coordination and community participation support prevention, but responsibility cannot rest solely on consumers. Assess alternatives across their full lifecycle; biodegradable labels are not permission to litter.
- Graphic persistence estimates are approximate environmental illustrations, not universal decomposition deadlines; fragmentation into microplastics is not complete biodegradation.

topics.title: Ecology as the foundation of economic prosperity
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## “Ecology is the permanent economy”
- Idea associated with **Sunderlal Bahuguna**: livelihoods, water, soil fertility, biodiversity and durable prosperity depend on functioning ecosystems. GDP can rise while natural capital and wellbeing decline; ecological health belongs in development decisions.
- Science supplies evidence and modelling; ethical stewardship adds intergenerational responsibility, respect for limits and attention to communities bearing environmental costs.
- Restore forests/wetlands and protect biodiversity, but **nature-based solutions cannot compensate indefinitely for continuing destructive extraction or fossil emissions**. Prevention, sustainable production/consumption and enforceable policy accompany restoration.
- The PDF's “climate change is natural” is misleading for today's warming: human greenhouse-gas emissions have unequivocally caused modern global warming. [IPCC synthesis](https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/syr/summary-for-policymakers/).
- Personal emotional/cultural connection with nature can motivate conservation and mindful lifestyles; collective institutions, incentives and structural change remain necessary. Avoid romantic universal claims that early humans never overused ecosystems or that only humans anticipate future needs.
- Mains: ecological dependence → depletion/externalities → stewardship and fair development → measurable ecosystem/livelihood outcomes. Treat ecology as productive infrastructure, not an automatic prohibition of all development.

topics.title: Right to repair and the Repairability Index
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## May 2025: proposed transparency framework
- **3 May 2025:** DoCA committee submitted Repairability Index framework report; initial category **smartphones and tablets**. **September 2024** committee chaired by **Bharat Khera**; submission/recommendations are not proof of universal mandatory labelling already operating for all electronics.
- Proposed **five-point index**, OEM self-declaration; six parameters: **disassembly depth, repair information, spare-part availability, software updates, tools, fasteners**. Display proposed at physical/e-commerce purchase points and through packaged-product QR codes. [Official report announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2126409).
- **Right to Repair Portal India, 2022:** information in automobiles, mobiles/electronics, consumer durables and farming equipment. Information access is not automatically a comprehensive enforceable right to independent repair.
## Consumer and environmental case
- Affordable spares, manuals/diagnostics, repairable construction and continued software support can extend product life, cut e-waste and build local repair jobs. Planned obsolescence is deliberate shortening of useful life; not every failure or update ending proves it.
- Consumer advocates, including **Pushpa Girimaji** in the source, seek independent/third-party repair choice; manufacturer-only repair can restrict access and increase costs.
- Evaluate safety, cybersecurity, IP and product responsibility alongside affordability and competition. Self-declaration needs clear criteria and credible verification; parts availability and realistic cost matter beyond a score.
- Source contrasts confrontational US campaigns with India's cooperative approach; US legal rules vary by jurisdiction/product, and tone is an editorial comparison. Circular-economy policy should include repair/reuse before material recycling.

## Right to remember: informal repair knowledge
- Editorial extends repairability to **tacit knowledge**: diagnosis/skills learned by observation, practice, apprenticeship and trial, often undocumented. Markets such as **Karol Bagh, Delhi, and Ritchie Street, Chennai** preserve knowledge for older/discontinued devices.
- Sealed designs, rapid replacement, unavailable diagnostics/spares and exclusion from formal training can erode this expertise. Merely improving recycling does not preserve repair livelihoods or skills.
- Proposals: recognise prior learning, community apprenticeships, technician participation in policy, safe documentation/digital repositories, design for disassembly and repairability in procurement. Link eligible workers to social protection; **e-Shram is a worker database/registration platform, not itself a skilling course**.
- PMKVY/NEP/e-waste-policy gaps are the author's assessment, not proof those frameworks categorically prohibit repair training. AI-assisted codification needs practitioners' participation and knowledge rights; not all tacit skill is fully captured in manuals.

topics.title: Aluminium industry: production, energy and recycling
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Value chain and uses
**Bauxite → alumina refining → electrolytic smelting → primary aluminium → fabricated/alloy products; scrap → secondary aluminium.**
- India is a major primary producer, officially described as **second globally** in the source period. [Mines Ministry, August 2024](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2039988).
- **Hindalco (Aditya Birla Group), NALCO (PSU) and Vedanta** are key firms. Source's capacities **1.3/2 Mt**, **FY2022–23 ~4.1 Mt output** and **1.4 Mt exports** need matching company/product/year definitions; do not use its “Hindalco largest” statement as an unqualified present ranking.
- Products: ingots, sheets, foil, conductors and alloys; packaging, construction, aerospace/vehicles and electrical applications. EV lightweighting, enclosures and components can raise demand; aluminium is not necessarily the active battery material in every chemistry.
- Smelting is electricity-intensive; power cost/emissions, responsible bauxite mining, land/ecological safeguards and refining residues constrain growth. Scrap collection, segregation and quality control can reduce demand for primary production and energy.
- **National Mineral Policy 2019** is a general policy framework, not automatic approval for any mine. The source's dedicated **aluminium PLI** and blanket government power-subsidy claims lack verification; official 14-sector PLI list includes **specialty steel**, not a general aluminium PLI. [Official PLI review](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2114011&lang=1&reg=46).
## Bauxite: ore, landscape and dated statistics
- **Primary aluminium ore**, a mixture dominated by hydrated aluminium oxides/hydroxides; commonly residual/lateritic caps on hills/plateaux, with lower/coastal deposits including Gujarat/Goa. **Bayer process → alumina**, followed by smelting; ore is not already aluminium metal. [USGS ore account](https://www.usgs.gov/centers/national-minerals-information-center/bauxite-and-alumina-statistics-and-information).
- Demand links construction, transport, packaging and electronics. India's principal Eastern Ghats resources include **Odisha/Andhra Pradesh**; mining economics depend on grade, accessibility, permissions and environmental/community costs.
- Source's historical world-reserve total **~30 billion tonnes (2015)** and shares **Guinea 25%, Australia 20%, Vietnam 12%, Brazil 9%, Jamaica 7%, Indonesia 4%, China 3%** are an older series, not June 2025 inventory. Its production shares **Australia 29%, China 19%, Guinea 18%, Brazil 10%, India 7%** have no matching explicit year; reserve/production shares differ and should not be treated as current rankings.
- Source India share table labelled **2019**: Odisha **51%**, Andhra Pradesh **16%**, Gujarat **9%**, Jharkhand **6%**, Maharashtra **5%**, MP/Chhattisgarh **4% each**; it may conflate **resources with economically defined reserves**. Odisha production **71%** is source **2020** data. Keep reference year/metric rather than merge these with latest mine output.

## Rayagada mining dispute: June 5, 2025
- Embedded clipping reports police preventing **Medha Patkar and other activists** from entering/remaining in **Rayagada, Odisha**, for a World Environment Day public meeting about **Sijimali bauxite mining**. Officials invoked tension/order concerns; activists disputed the exclusion. These are reported positions, not a judicial finding that a project is lawful/unlawful or that protests caused violence.
- Mains: aluminium supply/value addition versus forest/water impacts, displacement, recognition of FRA rights and lawful consultation/clearances; independent impact assessment, fair compensation and transparent grievance redress support legitimate development.

## PYQ revision: Chhattisgarh
- **2008 answer (d): all four—bauxite, dolomite, iron ore, tin—occur naturally.** **Bailadila, Dantewada** is the key iron-ore recall; **Bastar** has tin occurrences. Do not infer Chhattisgarh is the only place with any natural tin occurrence from its tin-concentrate production role.
- Source's claim that dolomite is mainly in Bastar/Dantewada is an inadequately supported district ranking; natural occurrence, mine output and reserve dominance are separate tests.

## Aluminium Vision Document: 4 July2025
- Mines Minister **G.Kishan Reddy**, Hyderabad conference on sustainable/responsible mining and mine closure: roadmap to **sixfold aluminium output by2047**, **150million tonnes/year bauxite production capacity**, **double national recycling rate**, low-carbon technology and stronger raw-material security.
- These are targets, not delivered capacity. Stakeholders included **NALCO, Hindalco, Vedanta, JNARDDC**, producer/recycling associations. Supports clean-energy systems, electric mobility, infrastructure, jobs and resource security; mining/smelting impacts and electricity emissions still need safeguards. [Mines Ministry release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2142184&lang=2&reg=48).
- Source's second-largest producer/~6% global-output description is a period-specific snapshot; bauxite capacity, primary metal output and recycling rate measure different stages.

topics.title: Jute cultivation and Jute Corporation of India
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Crop and geography
- **Golden fibre**, natural bast fibre; warm humid conditions, roughly **25–35°C**, abundant rainfall **150–250 cm**, fertile well-drained alluvial soils. Ganga–Brahmaputra delta supports cultivation; retting separates fibres, requiring appropriate water/processing.
- **India** is a leading raw-jute producer; **Bangladesh** a major exporter. West Bengal dominates Indian cultivation, with **Bihar and Assam** important. Source's **99% three-state share /55% global share /75% Bangladesh versus 7% Indian exports /₹5,500-crore annual exports** lack consistent years/product coverage; do not equate raw-fibre, jute-products and government-purchase measures.
- Uses: sacking/gunny bags, yarn, rope, mats, carpets, crafts and geotextiles; value addition and diversified demand can support farmer/mill livelihoods.
## JCI and 2025–26 support
- **Jute Corporation of India, 1971**, Government enterprise under **Textiles Ministry**, headquarters **Kolkata**; nodal price-support procurement agency protecting growers from distress sales. **JCI implements MSP, it does not independently determine Cabinet MSP policy.** [JCI](https://jutecorp.in/).
- **22 January 2025 CCEA approval:** raw jute **TD-3 MSP ₹5,650/quintal for 2025–26**, **₹315** above ₹5,335 in 2024–25; corresponding grades differ. Price-support losses reimbursed by Centre. May clipping's “minimum selling price” wording should not replace **Minimum Support Price**. [Cabinet decision](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2095068).
- May article reports applicability from the crop season beginning **1 July**, asks growers to use procurement access instead of below-MSP distress sale, and describes **Jute Commissioner's ISRO collaboration/remote sensing** for soil, moisture, production and environmental data. This is not proof JCI itself has launched every listed satellite technology.
- Market support needs accessible centres, prompt payment, quality assessment and improved retting/productivity. Promotion/export/industry-modernisation roles across JCI, Jute Commissioner and other agencies should not all be assigned to JCI alone.

topics.title: Nuclear transmutation: lead into gold at the LHC
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## ALICE result: 8 May 2025
- CERN's **ALICE** measured electromagnetic transmutation during **ultra-peripheral lead-ion interactions**: nuclei pass close without a head-on nuclear collision; intense electromagnetic fields induce photon–nucleus excitation and nucleon emission.
- **Lead Z=82 → gold Z=79 requires emission of THREE protons**, correcting the PDF's one/two-proton claim. One proton gives thallium; two mercury. Neutron emission changes isotope/mass number; illustrated **Pb-208 minus 3p and 2n → Au-203**.
- **Zero-degree calorimeters** register forward nucleon signals to identify channels. Newly produced nuclei rapidly leave the beam and strike accelerator components; fleeting survival is not evidence they all instantaneously radioactively decay or become collectible gold metal.
- Tiny yields and accelerator energy/cost make commercial production impractical. Measurements test electromagnetic-dissociation models and help understand beam-loss behaviour. [ALICE/CERN announcement](https://alice-collaboration.web.cern.ch/2025-alice-lead-to-gold).
## Chemistry versus nuclear physics
- Element identity depends on **proton number**. Chemical reactions rearrange electrons/bonds and cannot turn lead into gold; nuclear processes can alter nuclei.
- Alchemy's historic gold-making aspiration differed from modern experimental nuclear transmutation. This is measurement of a particular high-energy mechanism, not the first-ever artificial gold or validation of ordinary alchemical chemistry.

topics.title: Genome-edited rice: varieties, regulation and farmers’ rights
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## May 2025 release
- **4 May:** government launched **DRR Dhan 100 (Kamala)** and **Pusa DST Rice 1**. ICAR-IIRR Hyderabad developed Kamala from **Samba Mahsuri/BPT 5204**; ICAR-IARI developed Pusa DST Rice 1 from **MTU 1010**. [ICAR press note](https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/ICAR_Genome_Edited_Rice_04052025.pdf).
- Kamala: source trial yield **5.37 versus 4.5 tonnes/ha**, maturity about **130 days/20 days earlier**, improved resource-use traits/strong stalk. Pusa DST: inland/coastal salinity and alkalinity tolerance; reported **9.66–30.4% yield gains under specified stress conditions**. Trial performance is not guaranteed on every farm.
- Shorter crop duration can save water/fertiliser and reduce methane; actual benefits depend on management/conditions. Food security, climate resilience and input efficiency link SDGs 2/13 ; increased yield does not automatically double net farmer income.
## Editing and regulatory distinction
- **SDN 1 :** targeted cut followed by repair without a repair template; **SDN 2 :** targeted small template-directed change; **SDN 3 :** larger sequence insertion, potentially foreign DNA. Editing changes DNA even when it introduces no transgene; “not genetically modified” is regulatory shorthand rather than absence of genetic change.
- India’s **2022 exemption for qualifying SDN 1/SDN 2 plants free of exogenous introduced DNA** concerns specified Rules 1989 provisions; it does not abolish all safety/release requirements. Traceability and developer documentation matter.
- Government’s “world first” describes its public rice-variety launch; do not turn it into a claim that rice had never been genome-edited in research anywhere. Foreign examples include edited tomato/soybean/fish, with different regulatory frameworks.
- **PPVFR Act 2001** recognises farmers’ rights to save/use/sow/resow/exchange/share/sell farm produce including seed, **excluding branded seed sale of protected varieties**. Source Article 21 food/seed-sovereignty framing is an argument, not an unlimited standalone seed-IP exemption.
- Evaluate intellectual-property access, public breeding, seed affordability, transparent trials and agronomic/ecological performance alongside innovation.

## Phosphate-use efficiency in japonica rice
- NIPGR's **Nipponbare (japonica)** study targeted a **30-bp W-box region in the OsPHO1;2 promoter**, where repressor **OsWRKY6** binds. It did not simply delete 30 bp from the WRKY6 gene. Removing WRKY6 entirely caused unwanted effects; promoter editing reduced repression of root-to-shoot phosphate transport.
- Study reports approximately **20% yield gain under full phosphate and 40% gain at 10% recommended phosphate**, with more panicles/seeds under experimental conditions. Foreign editing DNA was segregated away. Off-target prediction is not proof no unintended change can ever occur.
- Potential benefits: phosphorus-use efficiency, lower fertiliser dependence and runoff; translation to Indian indica varieties and farmer-scale performance still require testing. A study does not establish immediate national DAP-import savings. [Plant Biotechnology Journal](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/pbi.70165).

topics.title: World Food Prize and sustainable soil microbiology
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## 2025 laureate
- **Mariangela Hungria**, Brazilian microbiologist, named 2025 World Food Prize laureate for biological nitrogen fixation/soil-microbiology advances and deployment of microbial inoculants. Soybean/bean symbiosis and beneficial microbes in other crops support yield with lower synthetic-fertiliser needs; not every inoculant fixes nitrogen equally in every crop. [Foundation laureate](https://www.worldfoodprize.org/en/laureates/20202026_laureates/2025_hungria/).
- Potential: lower input costs, fertiliser emissions and water pollution, healthier soils. Productivity gains do not by themselves prove reduced Amazon deforestation or that Brazil’s entire soybean leadership was caused by one technique.
## Prize recall
- Conceived by **Norman Borlaug**, established 1986 ; **M.S.Swaminathan first laureate 1987**. Des Moines, Iowa-based Foundation recognises improvements in food’s quality, quantity or availability across agriculture, nutrition, technology and rural development.
- Annual international award; “Nobel Prize for Food and Agriculture” is an informal description. The source’s **US$250,000** is outdated for 2025 : the prize increased to **US$500,000**. Announcement and later award ceremony are distinct events.
- Source associates ceremony with October/World Food Day and a Saul Bass sculpture; scheduling is year-specific, not always 16 October.

topics.title: Colombia: geography and Belt and Road cooperation
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## May 2025 cooperation and map
- Colombia signed a **Belt and Road cooperation plan with China during President Gustavo Petro’s May visit**. Infrastructure/finance opportunity and US–China influence competition form the context; signing does not mean all promised projects are financed/completed. [Colombian Foreign Ministry plan](https://www.cancilleria.gov.co/en/node/30761).
- **Northwest South America**, capital **Bogotá**, Spanish, Colombian peso; borders **Panama, Venezuela, Brazil, Peru, Ecuador**. Caribbean north and Pacific west: the only South American State with both these coasts; Caribbean is part of Atlantic.
- Andes split into three cordilleras; Amazon region; **Magdalena River**, **Putumayo River** along part of Peru border. Bogotá eastern Andes; Medellín industrial hub; Cali salsa; Cartagena/Barranquilla Caribbean ports/culture.
- Pacific Alliance participation and anti-narcotics cooperation matter. Source’s UNASUR membership is date-sensitive and should not be assumed continuously operative. Pan-American route has the **Darién Gap** between Panama/Colombia rather than an uninterrupted motor highway.
- BRI partnerships should be assessed for viability, debt/transparency, environmental effects and strategic autonomy; geography does not by itself establish alignment against the US.

topics.title: Paediatric cough–cold FDC restriction and drug safety
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## 16 May 2025 : restriction and implementation
- **S.O.1717 (E),15 April 2025**, under Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940 section 26 A: restricts manufacture/sale/distribution of **chlorpheniramine maleate + phenylephrine hydrochloride** FDC subject to a **“shall not be used in children below four years” warning** on labels/package insert/promotional literature. This is an age-related restriction, not a blanket prohibition on every cough syrup for every patient. [Gazette](https://cdsco.gov.in/opencms/resources/UploadCDSCOWeb/2018/UploadGazette_NotificationsFiles/S.O.%201717%28E%29%20dt%2015.04.2025.pdf).
- Chlorpheniramine: first-generation antihistamine, sedation risk; phenylephrine: vasoconstricting decongestant, cardiovascular concerns. Regulatory concern is risk/benefit in young children, not proof every properly used medicine inevitably causes respiratory arrest.
- Source says Delhi HC applied the notification prospectively and companies must communicate the restriction; its **15 April 2024 stock cutoff is inconsistent with the 2025 notification**. Do not learn it as a verified rule permitting all old stock to be administered to under-fours.
- Most uncomplicated childhood colds are viral/self-limiting; indiscriminate FDC use may obscure diagnosis or expose children to unnecessary medicines. The source’s second-generation antihistamine examples are not substitutes appropriate for every age/illness.
- **Honey is unsuitable for infants under 12 months**; omit the source’s unqualified honey recommendation. Public-health priorities: responsible prescribing, label enforcement, pharmacist/parent information, clinician continuing education, adequate inspectors and clear stock-management instructions. A recommended recall is distinct from an actual mandatory recall order.

topics.title: Childhood hypertension and school food literacy
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## May 2025 school-health argument
- Source cites **CNNS 2016–18 :7.3% adolescents with hypertensive readings, urban 9.1%**, and **NFHS 5 :12% aged 15–19 with elevated BP**. Different thresholds, age samples and measurement protocols mean these cannot alone prove a rising clinical-hypertension trend. Paediatric diagnosis requires age-appropriate assessment/repeated readings; one high reading is not definitive diagnosis.
- Risks: obesity, inactivity/screen-heavy routines and salty highly processed diets; underlying kidney/endocrine conditions also matter. Source **over 8 g salt/day** lacks a national survey baseline. WHO’s adult limit is less than 5 g/day; children’s allowance is lower and energy-adjusted.
- **PM POSHAN** can combine balanced locally appropriate meals with food literacy and safe student participation. Source scale~120 millionchildren/1.27 millionschools is an undated programme-era figure, not verified current coverage.
- Japan’s **Shokuiku** food education and Vietnam examples illustrate learning about food sources/meal preparation; source claims of reduced obesity do not establish the programme alone caused all changes.
- Reform proposals: fresh diverse menus, healthier food environments, activity, nutrition education, family engagement and BP/health follow-up. Do not assume school meals are every child’s sole nutrition source or that educating pupils alone treats clinical hypertension.

topics.title: NOTA and uncontested elections
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Background and 16 May debate
- **PUCL v Union of India,2013 :** secret expression of rejection through **None of the Above**. First used in 2013 Assembly polls in Chhattisgarh, Mizoram, Rajasthan, Delhi, MP, then 2014 Lok Sabha.
- In parliamentary/Assembly elections, NOTA is **not a binding right to reject/restart**: candidate with highest votes wins even if NOTA exceeds individual candidates. **RPA 1951 section 53** governs uncontested declaration; absence of a poll differs from excluding an option on a contested ballot.
- Source reports **Vidhi Centre PIL** seeking NOTA even when only one candidate remains; EC opposed the change as unnecessary for rare uncontested elections and requiring law/rule amendments. This is a litigation position, not a completed reform/judgment.
- Source historical counts **nine unopposed since 1952/six since 1971**, and NOTA shares~1% nationally, Bihar 2015 ~2.48%, Gujarat 2017 ~1.8%, are dated claims requiring election-series context, not fixed present totals.
- Arguments: voter dissent, secrecy and pressure for candidate quality versus election cost, representation/vacancy and uncertain practical effect. Threshold victory, binding NOTA and reruns with fresh candidates are **proposals**, not current national rules. Local-body frameworks may differ.
## May 2025 practice: indirect elections
- **2018 Supreme Court ruling** disallowed NOTA in **Rajya Sabha** elections; direct popular voting and indirect proportional-representation elections differ.
- Source practice answer **(b), statements 3 and 4**, captures its intended freedom-of-expression/direct-election comparison; statement 4’s **“only Lok Sabha and Assembly”** is overbroad if it excludes all local-body polls. Preserve the question for review rather than memorise it as an exhaustive list of NOTA applications. Existing notes retain the 2013 PUCL origin and absence of an automatic national rerun.

topics.title: IAEA: safeguards, nuclear cooperation and India
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Institution and limits
