- **1957, Vienna**; independent international organisation related to UN, “Atoms for Peace and Development”; **2005 Nobel Peace Prize jointly with Mohamed El Baradei**. Peaceful nuclear science supports energy, health, agriculture and water.
- **Safeguards** verify non-diversion of nuclear material under applicable agreements; **safety** protects against accidents/radiation, **security** against malicious acts. These are related but distinct functions.
- Reports to UNGA; safeguards non-compliance can be reported to UNSC. Membership alone does not allow inspection of every military/civil facility; mandate depends on agreements and authority.
- Source clipping reports India’s call to put Pakistan’s nuclear arsenal under IAEA oversight following conflict. This is **a diplomatic proposal**, not evidence Pakistan’s weapons became subject to inspection or a nuclear accident was established.
- India: IAEA member, **not NPT party**; civilian separation and India-specific safeguards enable international civil-nuclear cooperation. Additional Protocol increases agreed information/access duties; not automatic NSG membership or inspection of military installations.
- **DPRK:** IAEA has had no inspectors there since 2009 ; remote monitoring/assessment must not be described as regular current onsite inspection. [IAEA 2009 safeguards statement](https://www.iaea.org/sites/default/files/es2009.pdf).
## PYQ revision
- **2020 : answer(b)**, imported versus domestic uranium, in the question’s intended civil-cooperation context. Actual safeguards status follows designated facilities/material agreements; domestic fuel does not automatically exempt an already safeguarded reactor.
- **2018 : answer(a)**, civilian-reactor safeguards. India’s specific Additional Protocol obligations must not be generalised from the broad model protocol for NPT comprehensive-safeguards States.
## UN status: practice distinction
- IAEA is an **autonomous organisation related to the UN, not a UN specialised agency**. Its verification/reporting differs from Security Council enforcement; the undated worksheet’s correct statements are 2 and 3, answer **(c)**. Nobel and reporting facts are recorded above. [IAEA/UN relationship](https://www.iaea.org/sites/default/files/nobel2005.pdf).

## Institutional recall
- IAEA Statute approved **23 October 1956** and entered into force **29 July 1957**. Its annual General Conference sets policy/budget; the **35-member Board of Governors** handles major decisions and safeguards; the Secretariat runs implementation.
- **2020 PYQ: (b)** remains the imported/domestic uranium distinction intended by the question. Do not infer all domestically fuelled civil facilities are exempt, or that NPCIL operates every Indian research or breeder installation.

topics.title: Mahadayi river dispute and Kalasa–Banduri diversion
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Basin and proposal
- **Mahadayi/Mhadei/Mandovi:** Western Ghats, Karnataka/Bhimgad region → Goa → Arabian Sea near Panaji; basin includes Maharashtra. Source 111 km length/~76 km Goa is an approximate river-length account; basin membership does not prove the main channel traverses every State identically.
- **Chorao Island/Salim Ali Bird Sanctuary**, estuarine habitats and Western Ghats biodiversity. Source tributaries Rogaro, Kushavati, Nanorem, Nanuz, Valvota, Mapusa require local naming/reach distinctions rather than assuming every listed watercourse is identical in hydrology.
- **Kalasa–Banduri:** divert tributary water toward **Malaprabha basin**, drinking-water needs in Karnataka’s Belagavi, Dharwad, Bagalkot, Gadag. Canals/barrages require hydrological and ecological appraisal.
## Tribunal and federal dispute
- **MWDT constituted 2010 ; award 2018 :** source allocations **Karnataka 13.42 TMC, Goa 24 TMC, Maharashtra 1.33 TMC**. Allocation rights differ from diversion components/conditions; award ≠ all construction clearances. [Tribunal report](https://www.jalshakti-dowr.gov.in/static/uploads/2024/05/MAHADAYI-WATER-DISPUTES-TRIBUNAL-Report-Vol.-VII.pdf).
- Goa challenged the award and argues downstream ecological-flow harm. Source’s **2020 “in-principle environmental approval”** is too vague to prove every forest/wildlife/environmental approval is final/operative.
- Embedded clipping reports Goa controversy over a study of diversion impacts; one claimed projection does not establish realised river damage. **Article 262/Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956** provide the adjudication framework; interstate cooperation, transparent flow data and enforceable environmental conditions remain essential.
## Practice wording: main river versus basin
- The undated worksheet asks which States the river “passes through”, but its Karnataka/Maharashtra/Goa answer identifies **basin/dispute States**. The main channel flows through Karnataka and Goa; the basin also includes Maharashtra.
- As literally worded, the worksheet lacks a Karnataka+Goa-only option. Review its wording rather than memorise basin membership as a false main-channel route.

topics.title: Syria: transition, sanctions and regional geography
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## 16 May 2025 : new beginning and risks
- Embedded editorial concerns **Ahmed al-Sharaa’s post-Assad transitional government**, **14 May meeting with US President Trump** and US announcement to lift sanctions. Source table saying “Damascus controlled by Assad” is **outdated**: Assad’s government fell in December 2024.
- **13 May sanctions announcement** was a policy commitment, not proof every sanction legally vanished that day. Later measures implemented relief; keep future effective dates separate. [White House account of chronology](https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2025/06/fact-sheet-president-donald-j-trump-provides-for-the-revocation-of-syria-sanctions/).
- Editorial advocates demobilising armed groups, minority protection and an inclusive constitutional order; cites March violence against Alawites and Israeli strikes/security pressures. These are transition challenges, not proof stability was achieved. Al-Sharaa’s former HTS/jihadist background does not justify collective blame of religious communities.
## Map and historical recall
- **Damascus, West Asia**; neighbours Türkiye, Iraq, Jordan, Israel, Lebanon; Mediterranean coast. **Euphrates/Orontes**, northeastern Tigris border area; Anti-Lebanon/Mount Hermon; Syrian Desert and fertile river valleys.
- **Aleppo, Homs, Idlib, Raqqa** have different civil-war histories; older maps of Assad/rebel/ISIS control cannot serve as a May 2025 battlefield map. Raqqa was ISIS’s self-styled capital; Golan occupied by Israel since 1967.
- Sunni majority; Alawite, Kurdish, Christian, Druze, Armenian communities with differing identities—not uniform political blocs. Tartus has strategic Russian naval facilities; the claim of a secure continuing Iranian corridor must be reassessed after regime change.
- Chemical-weapons allegations/investigations involve **OPCW**, a distinct institution from IAEA. India supports UN-led peaceful resolution and has provided aid/training through ITEC; source embassy statements are dated, not verification of all current operations.
- Reconstruction requires inclusive institutions, security, service delivery and credible rights protections alongside sanctions relief/investment.

topics.title: Nursing leadership and advanced-practice reform
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Beyond International Nurses Day
- **12 May**, Florence Nightingale’s birthday: recognition should accompany safe work, fair pay, professional autonomy and policy representation. Source nurses/midwives 47% workforce needs dataset/year before treating as current headcount.
- Advanced-practice **Nurse Practitioners** can improve primary/critical care where trained/licensed; diagnosis/prescription authority differs by jurisdiction and role. Global examples include Australia, US, UK, South Africa, Botswana, Brazil, Thailand, Zambia.
- National Health Policy 2017 supports mid-level providers. **INC NPcritical-care regulations date 2016**, qualifying the source’s 2017-only initiation; primary-care/midwifery initiatives are distinct programmes, not universal independent-prescribing authority. [INC regulations](https://www.indiannursingcouncil.org/uploads/pdf/1625822647112267150560e815b7cf2af.pdf).
- **National Nursingand Midwifery Commission Act 2023** sets reform framework; passage alone does not establish all new bodies/roles fully operational. Concerns: unclear scope/title/licensing and employment pathways, weak training oversight, resistance to expanded roles, hierarchy/gender undervaluation and limited collective voice.
- Stoma care/diabetes education illustrate specialist work; “no national recognition anywhere” is too absolute. International claims of comparable NP/physician outcomes depend on patient group, scope and study design—not identical competence for every procedure.
- Priorities: accredited practical education/faculty, ethics/leadership, enforceable defined scope and accountability, career/pay progression, team-based care and nurse participation in policymaking. Australia illustrates role/title protection, rural-access objectives and nurse-led services; these are lessons to assess, not reforms automatically copied into Indianlaw.

topics.title: EOS-09 and PSLV-C61 mission
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## 16 May 2025 : planned launch
- **PSLV-C61/EOS-09** planned for **18 May**, First Launch Pad, Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota; source says 5.59 am. Earth-observation satellite with **C-band synthetic-aperture radar**, intended all-weather/day-night surface imaging and surveillance. Launch preparation/mobile-service-tower transfer is not orbit insertion. [ISRO mission plan](https://new1.isro.gov.in/ISRO_HINDI/Mission_PSLV_C61_EOS_09.html?timeline=timeline).
- **Later 18 May outcome:** mission **not accomplished**; keep this separate from the 16 May forecast. [ISRO launch register](https://www.isro.gov.in/ISRO_EN/PSLV_Launchers.html). Radar capability of intended payload does not establish delivered operational service.

## Failure review: August 2025 report
- After **18 May PSLV-C61** failure, issue reports committee analysis completed, submission to PM pending. **Third-stage anomaly**, not demonstrated EOS-09 payload malfunction; no root cause can be inferred from “small issue” or confidential report.
- Practice conflates **geostationary orbit** with **geosynchronous transfer orbit(GTO)**. PSLV can place suitable smaller payloads into GTO; this is not direct insertion into final geostationary orbit. Its explanation cites nonexistent statement 3. Failed orbit insertion delivered no operational radar service.

topics.title: Al-Ayyala: Gulf performing heritage
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Performance and safeguarding
- **Oman and UAE** traditional performing art, inscribed on UNESCO's **Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage, 2014**; not a built World Heritage Site.
- Chanted poetry, drumming and synchronised movement evoke battle, pride and unity: **two facing rows of men** carry thin **bamboo sticks** representing weapons; drums, tambourines and cymbals accompany movement. Approximate row sizes vary, not a fixed rule of precisely 20.
- UAE performances include **young girls** in front moving their long hair; the source's generic “women” description misses UNESCO's age-specific account. The lead performer directs rhythm/movement; skill passes through community/family participation, with public teaching supporting preservation. [UNESCO](https://ich.unesco.org/en/RL/al-ayyala-a-traditional-performing-art-of-the-sultanate-of-oman-and-the-united-arab-emirates-01012).
- Weddings, festivals and official welcomes sustain social identity. **May 2025:** performance welcomed Donald Trump in Abu Dhabi during a Gulf tour including Saudi Arabia, Qatar and UAE; source links tour to defence, investment and AI cooperation.
- **Soft power:** hospitality and living heritage communicate identity; compare India's cultural diplomacy through yoga/classical dance without assuming cultural performance itself establishes a defence or investment contract. Safeguarding requires practitioners and intergenerational transmission, not inscription alone.

topics.title: Methanol poisoning and illicit liquor regulation
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Chemistry and public-health risk
- **Hooch:** illicit/spurious liquor outside reliable licensed production; toxic contamination can arise from deliberate industrial-alcohol diversion or unsafe production. Not all illicit alcohol contains the same methanol concentration.
- **Methanol CH₃OH**, wood alcohol: colourless, volatile, flammable, water-miscible industrial alcohol; solvents, formaldehyde/chemical manufacture, antifreeze and fuel uses. Modern synthesis uses **syngas—CO/H₂**, potentially from natural gas, coal or biomass; industrial production is not necessarily wood distillation.
- **Ethanol C₂H₅OH** is the principal beverage alcohol and a CNS depressant; beverage presence does not make unlimited consumption safe. Smell/appearance cannot establish liquor safety.
- **Methanol → formaldehyde → formate/formic acid**: metabolic acidosis, optic-nerve injury/blindness and neurological/organ damage; early symptoms may resemble intoxication, with deterioration after a delay. Source's **10 mL blindness /30 mL fatality** figures are illustrative toxic exposures, not dependable safe/lethal thresholds for every person.
- Suspected exposure requires **urgent emergency assessment**; antidotes such as fomepizole and other hospital interventions block toxic metabolism/treat complications. These are clinician-directed treatments, not an instruction to self-administer ethanol. [CDC/NIOSH](https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/ershdb/emergencyresponsecard_29750029.html).

## Governance: May 2025 revision
- **FSSAI Alcoholic Beverages Regulations 2018** prescribe product-specific methanol limits; no single limit applies identically to every beverage. **MSIHC Rules 1989**, State excise controls and poison/industrial-chemical rules address distinct parts of production, storage and sale. [FSSAI compendium](https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Alcoholic_Beverages_Regulations_30_06_2022.pdf).
- **Poisons Act 1919** provides enabling powers/rules, not an identical blanket national ban on every industrial use. Gujarat/Bihar prohibition does not imply all lawful industrial methanol handling is absolutely prohibited; permissions/exemptions and applicable State law matter.
- Drivers: illegal manufacture, industrial diversion, poor traceability, enforcement corruption/gaps, limited consumer awareness and weak health–excise–police coordination.
- Response: licensed supply-chain records and inspections, chemical traceability, inter-State intelligence, rapid outbreak identification, accessible emergency treatment and targeted awareness. The source's comprehensive new central law is a **recommendation**, not an enacted May measure; evaluate existing-law enforcement as well as legislative gaps.

## June 20 PYQ revision
- Ethanol-production question (2025): **United States produces more ethanol than Brazil**; US feedstock is principally corn, Brazil's principally sugarcane. Statement I is false and II true (d); source production volumes are dated approximations.
- Source CDS explanation mistakenly calls “methanal” a typo for formaldehyde: **methanal is formaldehyde**. Methanol metabolism proceeds through formaldehyde to formate; formate chiefly drives acidosis and optic injury. Preserve that distinction from the source's oversimplified protoplasm explanation.

topics.title: Multi Agency Centre and intelligence coordination
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Revamp inaugurated: 16 May 2025
- Home Minister inaugurated upgraded **MAC, North Block, New Delhi**: IB-led counter-terrorism **intelligence fusion/sharing mechanism**, in existence since **2001**, providing continuous coordination between central and State agencies.
- Official account: revamp **over ₹500 crore**, **28 organisations**, connectivity expanded to **all police districts**. A connected district is not proof every threat is detected instantly; source's “₹500 crore” is rounded. [MHA announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2129141&lang=2&reg=48).
- Participants include intelligence agencies, armed forces, State police and CAPFs; **BSF is itself a CAPF**, so do not count it as a wholly separate institutional category when describing the total.
- Fusion combines information across agencies, identifies links and disseminates actionable intelligence; benefits for counter-terrorism, borders, insurgency and organised-crime networks depend on analysis and operational follow-through.
- Speech cited **Operation Sindoor** and anti-Naxal action in **Karreguttalu hills, Chhattisgarh–Telangana border**, as coordination examples. These do not prove the newly inaugurated network alone caused earlier operations' outcomes.
- Mains priorities: timely verified information, common standards, secure access controls, accountable intelligence use, district-level capacity and feedback from operations; avoid silos, duplication, cyber compromise and indiscriminate data accumulation.

topics.title: Rajon ki Baoli: stepwell conservation
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Conservation completed: 16 May 2025
- **Rajon ki Baoli**, sixteenth-century **Lodhi-era** stepwell, **Mehrauli Archaeological Park, Delhi**; Lodhi dynasty **1451–1526**. Stepped access supported traditional water storage and groundwater use; baolis combine hydraulic, architectural and social functions, not simply one generic rainwater tank design.
- **ASI + World Monuments Fund India Association + TCS Foundation** announced completed conservation/rejuvenation. Part of WMF's **Climate Heritage Initiative launched 2024**, connecting water heritage/local knowledge and adaptation. Completion of works is not a guarantee of indefinite water quality or maintenance. [Project partners' announcement](https://www.wmf.org/press-releases/restoration-rajon-ki-baoli).
- **ASI:** established **1861**, associated with **Alexander Cunningham**; Ministry of Culture, HQ New Delhi. Archaeological research, excavation, documentation and centrally protected monument/site conservation under **AMASR Act 1958** and associated law. Source “over 3,600” is an approximate administrative count, not all India's heritage sites.
- **WMF**, founded **1965**, New York-based conservation organisation; Indian arm supports expertise, fundraising, advocacy, skills and community participation. It is **not UNESCO** and does not confer World Heritage status. Donations/grants/CSR help, but legal custodianship and public accountability remain distinct.
- Mains: compatible traditional materials plus scientific assessment, restored drainage/water function, community access and maintenance; evaluate structural stability, water quality and sustainable stewardship alongside visual restoration.

topics.title: RBI economic capital, risk buffers and surplus
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Framework and fiscal link
- **Economic Capital Framework (ECF)** assesses RBI financial risks and appropriate equity/provisions; surplus available for transfer follows income, expenditure and provisioning, not an unrestricted government claim to every reserve.
- **Contingent Risk Buffer (CRB)** cushions monetary/financial-stability, credit and operational risks. **Realised equity/provisions** differ from unrealised revaluation gains; changing a buffer ratio does not turn every accounting gain into cash.
- **Bimal Jalan committee constituted 2018; report/framework adopted 2019**: recommended CRB **5.5–6.5% of balance sheet**, subject to the framework. The source's “2018 recommendations” conflates constitution and adoption.
- RBI transfer is Union **non-tax revenue**; it can ease borrowing/deficit pressure or permit spending depending on budget choices. More revenue alone is not necessarily a fiscally expansionary policy, and it does not automatically finance a specified defence programme.

## May 2025 review: stages and interpretation
- Source reports RBI's ECF review alongside an internal Finance Ministry assessment and speculation about larger dividends amid defence needs. That is **reported motivation/analysis**, not proof political direction had changed provisions or determined the payout.
- **15 May 2025:** RBI Board reviewed ECF; subsequent official disclosure confirmed approval of a revised framework at that meeting. Keep **later-publicised details and eventual dividend decision** separate from the issue's incomplete snapshot. [RBI's dated Board statement](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/reservebankofindia_the-615th-meeting-of-the-central-board-of-activity-7330543243010437122-aZFY).
- Source recalls a large 2019 transfer; its accounting period and fiscal-year receipt must be distinguished. Capital-release decisions and recurring annual profit transfers are different components.
- Balance adequate buffers/central-bank credibility with legitimate fiscal accountability, transparent risk assessment and predictable transfer rules. This primarily concerns **Union–RBI institutional governance**, not inherently a Centre–State water/federal dispute.
- Mains: explain risk provisions → surplus calculation → fiscal trade-off → safeguards for transparent, independently reasoned capital management. A lower buffer may increase distributable surplus in a given calculation, but risk capacity and future shocks matter.
## 23 May 2025: revised framework and surplus decision
- RBI approved the revised ECF on **15 May**, effective for **FY2024–25**. The new **CRB range is 4.5–7.5% of the balance sheet**, replacing the 2019 framework’s 5.5–6.5% band.
- At its **23 May Board meeting**, RBI maintained CRB at **7.5%** and approved **₹2,68,590.07 crore surplus transfer for accounting year 2024–25**. The decision occurred in the Union’s FY2025–26; approval and actual receipt are distinct. [RBI’s Board release](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=60514), [revised ECF highlights](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=60513).
- The repeated review article in the 24 May PDF is stale: it does not establish that review remained unfinished or that the old CRB band was still operative. Core risk-buffer and fiscal distinctions are explained above.

topics.title: Neeraj Chopra and the 90-metre javelin milestone
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Doha result: 16 May 2025
- **Doha Diamond League 2025**, correcting repeated PDF **2024** labels: **Neeraj Chopra 90.23 m**, Indian record and first Indian beyond 90 m, **second** to Germany's **Julian Weber 91.06 m** in the final round. A personal/national milestone does not necessarily win that competition. [World Athletics result](https://worldathletics.org/competitions/diamond-league/news/weber-chopra-doha-diamond-league-2025).
- Source describes Chopra as **third Asian /25th male athlete** to join the 90-metre club at this milestone; these are dated achievement counts, not a permanent ranking. **Kishore Jena eighth, 78.60 m** in the source result; Paris 2024 “preparation” is stale in a May 2025 issue.
- **Wanda Diamond League:** annual elite track-and-field meeting series, qualification points leading to a final; meeting placing differs from Olympic/world-championship medals.
- Chopra: **Tokyo Olympic gold (Games held 2021)**, first Indian Olympic athletics gold; **World Championships silver 2022 /gold 2023**; coach **Jan Železný**, world-record holder, whose record had not been broken by 90.23 m.
- Training, biomechanics, coaching and athlete-support pathways matter; the source's weather/wind explanation is not proof a single factor caused the improvement.

topics.title: Gyan Bharatam and manuscript conservation
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Budget announcement and May 2025 status
- **Union Budget 2025–26:** survey, documentation and conservation covering **over one crore manuscripts** and a **National Digital Repository of Indian knowledge systems**. Intended coverage is not manuscripts already digitised or publicly available. [Budget highlights](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2025-26/doc/bh1.pdf).
- **Ministry of Culture** initiative builds on **National Mission for Manuscripts (NMM), established 2003**, with resource/conservation/partner-centre networks. Source reports annual allocation **₹3.5 crore →₹60 crore**; annual budget is distinct from later multi-year mission outlays.
- Page-one clipping **anticipated a June 9 launch** and considered an autonomous preservation body; these were plans, not proof of a completed May launch. It reports metadata for **52 lakh manuscripts**, around **three lakh digitised**, and roughly one-third of those uploaded—different stages and source snapshots, not one universal completed digital-access count.
- Scope includes museums, universities, libraries, temples/mutts and private collections; central cataloguing, conservation facilities, digitisation, transcription/research and access require institutional/custodian cooperation.

## What counts as a manuscript?
- Handwritten compositions on **paper, palm leaf, birch bark, cloth** and other media, with historical/scientific/literary/aesthetic significance. NMM's **75-year age criterion** is a programme definition, not a universal linguistic definition prohibiting newer handwritten manuscripts.
- Printed books, lithographs and photographic reproductions are not original handwritten manuscripts in this classification. **Language ≠ script**: a language can be written in different scripts; the source incorrectly lists “Maithili” generically as an ancient script (the language's historic script is **Tirhuta/Mithilakshar**).
- Themes: religion/philosophy, literature/grammar, medicine, astronomy, mathematics, history/genealogy, arts and agriculture. Source's **80 scripts /75% Sanskrit** need a dataset and reference date; do not assume a verified full inventory exists.
- **Bakhshali**, birch-bark mathematical manuscript using a zero placeholder: source's blanket **third–fourth-century** date is obsolete/disputed. Oxford's **2024 revised radiocarbon study** models production across approximately **799–1102 CE**, with uncertainty; material dating is not automatically the date a mathematical idea originated. Avoid an unqualified “world's earliest zero” claim. [Oxford primary report](https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid%3A5a6d1dd7-f20c-4209-adb6-33849f5b08f4).

## Institutions, constitutional links and implementation
- **National Library, Kolkata**, and **Asiatic Society, founded 1784 by William Jones**, contribute to textual heritage. Source's 3,600-library-manuscript count is an approximate collection snapshot.
- **Article 29(1)** protects any section of citizens with a distinct language/script/culture, not minorities alone. **Article 49** concerns protected monuments/objects of national importance; **Article 51A(f)** is the duty to preserve composite heritage. The source supplies no specific judgment establishing a universal standalone **Article 21 entitlement to every cultural asset**.
- Digitisation enables research/access but does not replace physical conservation; preserve provenance, metadata, rights/consent, backup formats, script-reading expertise and scholarly verification. Scans alone do not validate every scientific/medical claim in a historic text.
- Mains: protect fragile diverse knowledge → catalogue and conserve originals → accurate digitisation/translation → equitable research access and community stewardship. Global soft power and curricula are potential uses, not automatic outcomes.

topics.title: UN peacekeeping: principles, mandates and India
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Mandates and core principles
- Military, police and civilian personnel support peace processes; **Security Council** establishes mandates, with UN organs/member States providing administration, finance and personnel. Peacekeeping is **not expressly named in the Charter**; practice draws on Charter powers, including Chapters VI/VII as relevant. **Capstone Doctrine** articulates operational principles.
- **Consent of main parties; impartiality; non-use of force except self-defence/defence of mandate**. Impartiality means even-handed mandate enforcement, **not neutrality/inactivity towards violations**; robust authorised action differs from unrestricted warfighting. [UN principles](https://peacekeeping.un.org/en/principles-of-peacekeeping).
- Tasks can include ceasefire monitoring, **DDR**, civilian protection, police/rule-of-law support, human rights, electoral assistance and confidence building; exact authority/resources vary by mandate.
- **UNTSO, 1948**, first operation, Middle East. Source's **11 active operations in May 2025** is consistent with the Berlin ministerial account. Examples: **UNMISS—South Sudan; MINUSCA—CAR; MONUSCO—DR Congo; UNIFIL—Lebanon; UNMIK—Kosovo**. **MINUSMA—Mali closed 31 December 2023**, so it was not an active May 2025 mission. [Mission closure](https://minusma.unmissions.org/en/node/48431).

## Berlin ministerial: 13–14 May 2025
- Ministerial involved over **130 member States/international partners**; **74 States made pledges**, including capabilities and support. UN account: over **61,000 military/police** plus over **7,000 civilians** across 11 operations. Pledges are not proof every unit already deployed. [UN outcome](https://peacekeeping.un.org/en/node/132178).
- Embedded clipping reports India's proposed **quick-reaction company, male CRPF formed-police unit, women-led formed-police unit, counter-explosive/IED-disposal unit, dog unit and SWAT police unit**, plus training partnerships/courses for observers, commanders and uniformed personnel. These are offered capacities pending implementation/confirmation; India–US training of African peacekeepers is a partnership example.
- Clipping reports **5,375 Indians /fourth-largest contributor**, whereas accompanying prose says **5,424 across nine missions**. Rankings/headcounts require an exact monthly snapshot and personnel scope; do not merge these into one audited figure. **0.16% assessed-budget share** is inadequately dated in the PDF, distinct from troop contribution and not a secure current rate.

## India, achievements and limitations
- Indian contribution began with a **medical unit in Korea, 1950**; distinguish medical support, later neutral-repatriation responsibilities and combat formations. Women serve in **UNISFA, Abyei**; source reports 150 Indian UNMISS personnel receiving service medals, not necessarily individual gallantry “medals of honour”.
- **Major Radhika Sen**, MONUSCO in DRC (**March 2023–April 2024**), received **2023 Military Gender Advocate of the Year award in 2024**. Award year and presentation year differ. [UN award account](https://peacekeeping.un.org/en/press-releases/indian-peacekeeper-wins-2023-military-gender-advocate-of-the-year-award).
- UN peacekeepers received **Nobel Peace Prize 1988**; operations supported transitions in Namibia, Cambodia, Mozambique, El Salvador and Tajikistan.
- Failures: **Rwanda genocide 1994** killed around 800,000, mainly Tutsi and also moderate Hutu; **Srebrenica 1995**, over 8,000 Bosniak men/boys. Limited mandates, resources, political will and civilian-protection failures matter; not all Rwanda victims were Tutsi.
- Gaza/Ukraine deployment proposals face mandate, Council politics, consent and feasibility barriers; no existing peacekeeping force there can be assumed merely from the UN's general peace role.
- Mains: achievable mandates, political settlements, trained/equipped contingents, women’s participation, civilian protection, accountability and clear exit strategies; military deployment alone cannot solve political conflict.

topics.title: Kandha communities: identity, rights and gender change
topics.subject: Anthropology
topics.markdown:
## Identity and livelihood
- **Kandha/Khond/Kondh** communities concentrated in Odisha—**Kandhamal, Rayagada, Koraput, Ganjam, Kalahandi**—with related communities in neighbouring States. **Kui/Kuwi** are Dravidian languages; subgroup geography/language varies rather than one uniform identity.
- Scheduled Tribe identification operates under **Article 342**, through State/UT-specific notified lists; the Article does not by itself provide one universal all-India community entry.
- Forest produce (**mahua, sal seeds, honey, tamarind**), farming, livestock and historically **podu/shifting cultivation** support livelihoods; MGNREGS/other employment diversify income. Not all households practise shifting cultivation or traditional hunting.
- Source reports **~1.4 million /17% of Odisha ST population** as Census 2011 but provides no precise notified-category table; treat as an unverified demographic claim rather than memorise the mismatched rounded baseline. Education/health disadvantages need subgroup- and sex-disaggregated data.

## Tattooing: local oral history and transformation
- **May 2025 Kandhamal/Daringbadi case study:** older women describe painful geometric facial tattooing near **age ten**, undertaken by experienced older women, with needle injury, infections and lengthy recovery. The newspaper records one survivor's **two-month recovery**; not a standard medical duration for every case.
- Community recollections explain the practice as deterrence against exploitation by landlords/rulers/colonial agents; over time it became associated with womanhood, marriageability and belonging. This is **reported oral history**, not a proven uniform origin for every Kandha subgroup.
- Ear-rim silver ornaments also communicate marital/community identity in the described locality. Source describes patriarchal/patrilineal norms, indigenous medicine/folklore and worship of **Dharani Penu**, earth deity; **Kedu** ritual and historic **Meriah** practices vary and should not stereotype contemporary communities.
- Decline since **mid-1990s**, linked to education, awareness and sustained family counselling; report says facial tattoos are rare below age 40 in the community surveyed. It does not prove the practice is extinct across all communities.
- Older survivors welcome younger girls' freedom from coercive tattooing; modern voluntary fashion tattoos have a different consent/social context. **Preserve cultural identity while protecting bodily autonomy and child welfare**; community-led reform need not erase language, folklore or collective belonging.

## Rights and development
- Risks: land alienation, mining/project displacement, forest degradation, exploitative credit/intermediaries, weak health/education/sanitation and climate-sensitive livelihoods. **Niyamgiri issues particularly involve Dongria Kondh**; do not equate every Kandha community with one subgroup or project.
- **FRA 2006:** recognition of qualifying individual/community forest rights; **PESA 1996:** Gram Sabha powers in **Fifth Schedule areas**, not automatically every place inhabited by tribal people. Tribal-development earmarking and **Odisha Tribal Empowerment and Livelihood Programme** support development; statutory schemes do not themselves prove secure title or service delivery.
- Priorities: consent-sensitive services, girls' education, recognition of rights, fair market/credit access, habitat protection and community participation. Avoid framing a living community solely through historic sacrifice or traumatic customs.

topics.title: Amrit Bharat Station Scheme: phased redevelopment
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Scheme and design
- **Ministry of Railways**, long-term station master plans and **phased redevelopment**. Official policy announced **27 December 2022**, correcting PDF's blanket **February 2023 launch**. Needs, passenger use, funds and priorities determine implementation. [Railways policy](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1886884&lang=2&reg=3).
- Amenities: cleaner waiting areas/toilets, accessible facilities for persons with disabilities, food outlets, legible multilingual signage; improve circulation with entry/exit arrangements, parking, footpaths and roads.
- Intermodal links to buses/taxis/autos support last-mile travel; efficient lighting, rainwater harvesting and green spaces improve sustainability. Roof plazas/commercial/public spaces can connect stations with the city; these are long-term design elements, not identical requirements already finished at every station.
- The source links ballastless track with reduced noise/vibration; actual vibration/noise performance depends on design and mitigation, so do not treat slab track as a universal noise cure.

## West Bengal progress: May 2025 clipping
- **Kalyani Ghoshpara**, near **AIIMS Kalyani**, upgraded with passenger/safety amenities; clipping cites **over ₹3 crore** invested and redevelopment of stations in the **Sealdah Division**.
- Clipping inconsistently says Kalyani Ghoshpara “and 18 other stations” while also counting it among **18 selected Division stations**; retain the named station/region, not the contradictory subtotal.
- National **103-station inauguration on May 22** was **scheduled**, not already completed on May 18. Station works, opening ceremony and future master-plan phases are distinct milestones.
- Mains: accessibility and safety → circulation/intermodal connectivity → maintainable amenities and urban integration; test passenger outcomes, upkeep, costs and local needs rather than infer redevelopment always produces a thriving commercial city centre.

topics.title: Fiscal deficit, defence spending and fiscal space
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Correct deficit arithmetic
- **Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − (revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts)**; indicates net financing requirement. PDF's “expenditure minus revenue receipts” formula omits **loan recoveries/disinvestment and other non-debt capital receipts**.
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Revenue receipts | Taxes net to Centre plus non-tax revenue, including dividends/fees |
| Capital receipts | Include borrowings and non-debt receipts; borrowings finance rather than reduce fiscal deficit |
| Revenue deficit | Revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts |
| Primary deficit | Fiscal deficit minus interest payments |
- Expressing deficits as **% GDP** supports scale comparisons; a ratio can change with either rupee deficit or nominal GDP. Deficit is an annual flow; public debt a stock.
- Drivers: expenditure/income choices, tax buoyancy, subsidies, interest costs, slowdowns and shocks. Deficit-financed productive investment differs from recurrent spending; assess growth/interest and expenditure quality, not one ratio alone.

## Defence fiscal-space debate: May 2025
- **FY2025–26 Budget Estimate fiscal-deficit target: 4.4% GDP**, versus **4.8% FY2024–25 Revised Estimate**. Target ≠ final outturn. **FRBM Act 2003** and fiscal statements provide the framework; the historic 3% ambition is not the operative 2025–26 Budget target. [Budget fiscal statement](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2025-26/doc/frbm1.pdf).
- Source reports Defence Ministry **expected to seek ~₹50,000 crore additional allocation through Supplementary Demands for Grants**. Expectation is not an approved/appropriated addition or actual spending; parliamentary authorisation and financing follow.
- Article argues larger RBI surplus, lower oil prices, tax receipts and reprioritisation could absorb extra defence spending while maintaining target. This is a **conditional fiscal assessment**, not a guarantee; lower oil prices affect subsidy/import/inflation channels but do not automatically yield equal budget savings.
- RBI **FY2023–24 surplus ₹2,10,874 crore**, about **141% above ₹87,416 crore**, was transferred/received in **FY2024–25**. The source conflates surplus year with government-receipt year. A higher next transfer was still an expectation at the issue date, not the later Board payout already realised. [CAG government-receipt table](https://saiindia.gov.in/uploads/download_audit_report/2026/6of2026UGEng-069ce496f1158e0.22682438.pdf).
- More non-tax revenue can reduce borrowing or finance spending; RBI risk provisions must remain prudent (see common economic-capital topic). Spending cuts across revenue heads can affect welfare/services; “revenue” does not automatically mean wasteful.

## Historical comparison: avoid causal/date errors
- **1971 war**, **Kargil 1999**, **Parliament attack 2001**, **Mumbai 2008**, **Uri 2016**, **Pulwama 2019** belong to different fiscal years/economic settings. PDF wrongly associates **2000–01/2001–02** deficit figures with Kargil.
- The **2008 global crisis** and later stimulus, revenue slowdown and accounting changes must be separated from security costs. COVID affected the final days of **FY2019–20** and especially **FY2020–21**; do not explain the entire earlier year's deficit solely by pandemic response.
- Source historic **3→3.45%** and **5.3→6.1%** figures omit a reconciled official series; avoid treating them as causal estimates of the cost of war. Deficits can rise/fall for many simultaneous reasons.
- Mains: spending need → revenue/financing options → trade-offs for welfare/capex → transparent supplementary appropriations and credible debt/deficit monitoring. Macroeconomic tailwinds help but do not eliminate fiscal risk.
## 30 May 2025 provisional FY 2024–25 outturn
- Embedded clipping reports fiscal deficit **₹15.77 lakh crore/4.8%GDP**, matching revised target; total non-borrowing receipts **₹30.78 lakh crore**, **97.8%RE**; total spending **₹46.55 lakh crore**, **97.8%RE**. These are provisional fiscal accounts with the then GDP denominator, not audited final accounts.
- Corporation-tax receipts **₹9.87 lakh crore**, around **0.7% above RE**; income-tax **₹11.83 lakh crore**, around **6% below RE**. Disinvestment **₹10,131.32 crore**, non-debt capital receipts **52.1%RE**: different receipt headings must not be conflated.
- **FY 2025–26 target 4.4%** is separate from achieved/provisional FY 25 ratio. Repeated defence **~₹50,000 crore supplementary request** remains an expectation, not parliamentary approval.
- Repeated formula is corrected in common core: **expenditure − revenue receipts − non-debt capital receipts**; source omitted non-debt receipts. Revenue deficit/primary deficit differ.
- Repeated article calls higher RBI transfer prospective, reflecting an earlier report, not necessarily status as at 31 May. Do not redate its historical₹2.1 lakh-crore surplus or claim every oil-price reduction translates into budget saving. Fiscal flexibility remains conditional on receipts, spending and buffer prudence.
- Historical source again misdates **Kargil 1999** to 2000–02; macroeconomic crises/accounting changes confound security-cost comparisons. Capital investment and necessary revenue services both have value; assess opportunity costs and transparent appropriations.

topics.title: e-Passports and biometric document security
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## May 2025 rollout and design
- An **e-passport remains a physical booklet**, with contactless **RFID chip/antenna**, personal particulars and biometric information, plus digitally signed data. A gold e-passport symbol identifies it. MEA's system uses **public-key infrastructure (PKI)** to verify data integrity and origin. Phased issuance does not invalidate existing ordinary passports before expiry. [Passport Seva FAQ](https://services1.passportindia.gov.in/psp/FaqEPassport).
- The source's “over 120 countries” is an issue-date approximation. ICAO travel-document standards support interoperability, not automatic visa-free access or guaranteed expedited entry.
| Security concept | Function |
|---|---|
| Basic Access Control | Restricts chip access and protects chip–reader communications using document-derived keys |
| Passive Authentication | Checks issuer signature/data integrity; does not alone detect cloning |
| Extended Access Control | Further controls access to sensitive biometrics where implemented |
- Facial image is the interoperable primary biometric; **fingerprints and EAC should not be assumed mandatory in every Indian passport** merely from generic international capabilities. A chip is not by itself tamper-proof; cryptography, inspection and key management work together. [ICAO Doc 9303](https://www.icao.int/publications/pages/publication.aspx?docnum=9303).
- Potential gains: harder forgery, authenticatable identity, compatible e-gates and efficient processing. Benefits depend on destination infrastructure; no system guarantees elimination of identity theft.
- The issue's **“address no longer printed, stored only digitally”** claim is not established by MEA's cited technical definition; avoid presenting this or universal fingerprint storage as verified new Indian policy. Protect privacy through controlled access, secure systems and lawful use, alongside Digital India/service modernisation.

topics.title: Sansad Ratna Awards and parliamentary performance
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Award and May 2025 selection
- Instituted **2010**, inspired by **A.P.J. Abdul Kalam**; organised by **Prime Point Foundation**, a civil-society initiative, **not a Government of India or Parliament award**. Recognises parliamentary performance and encourages accountability. [Organiser](https://www.sansadratna.in/p/about-sansad-ratna-award.html).
- May clipping reports selection of **17 MPs and two Parliamentary Standing Committees** for 2025; selection precedes presentation. Named examples: **Bhartruhari Mahtab, Ravi Kishan, Supriya Sule, N.K. Premachandran and Shrirang Appa Barne**; jury chaired by **Hansraj Ahir**.
- Core reported quantitative measures: participation in debates, questions and **Private Members' Bills**, using parliamentary/PRS data and an expert jury. Do not assume the PDF's attendance, MPLADS use, debate duration/quality and generic retired-judge membership are each confirmed components of the organiser's scoring method.
- Participation counts aid scrutiny but cannot alone measure policy quality, constituency work, inclusiveness or outcomes. Distinguish a private-member Bill being introduced from its passage into law.

topics.title: National Council of Science Museums
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Institution and outreach
- **NCSM**, autonomous society under **Ministry of Culture**, registered **4 April 1978**; headquarters **Kolkata**. Promotes public science awareness and scientific temper through national/regional/district science centres, interactive exhibits, training, demonstrations, publications and workshops. [NCSM FAQ](https://ncsm.gov.in/resources/faq).
- **Central Research and Training Laboratory, Kolkata** supports exhibit development, research and professional science communication. **Mobile Science Exhibitions** extend outreach to rural/remote communities.
- International work cited: **Rajiv Gandhi Science Centre, Mauritius**, and India's Buddhism gallery at the **International Buddhist Museum, Sri Lanka**; travelling exhibitions in US/Russia/China/France/Bangladesh/Bhutan/Trinidad and Tobago/Guyana/Bulgaria. Examples do not imply a science centre already exists in every district.
## May 2025: Saroj Ghose
- Embedded obituary: **Saroj Ghose died 17 May 2025 in Seattle**, aged **89**; NCSM announcement **18 May**. Architect of India's decentralised, interactive science-centre movement; led NCSM **1979–1997**, later museum adviser and former ICOM president. **Padma Shri 1989; Padma Bhushan 2007**. [NCSM/PIB tribute](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2129474&lang=2&reg=48).
- Science museums link accessible informal education with curiosity, evidence and public understanding; measure reach and engagement rather than buildings alone.

topics.title: New Caledonia: decolonisation and political status
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Geography and historical anchors
- **Sui generis French collectivity**, not an independent country; capital **Nouméa**. Southwest Pacific/Coral Sea: east of Australia, south of Vanuatu, west of Fiji, northwest of New Zealand. Main island **Grande Terre**, **Loyalty Islands** (Ouvéa, Lifou, Maré), **Isle of Pines**, **Bélep Islands**; important nickel resources and extensive barrier reef.
- Graphic chronology: **1774 James Cook arrival; 1853 French annexation; 1984 FLNKS election boycott; 5 May 1988 Ouvéa cave assault; June 1988 Matignon Accord; 1998 Nouméa Accord**. France annexed in 1853; establishment of the later penal colony should not be conflated with the exact annexation date.
- Indigenous **Kanak** rights, colonial dispossession and uneven political/economic power underpin independence demands. **FLNKS = Kanak and Socialist National Liberation Front**.
- **Nouméa Accord 1998** recognised colonial trauma, provided autonomy, local citizenship/electoral safeguards and progressive transfers of competence; citizenship is not already independent nationality. Referendums **2018, 2020, 2021** officially rejected independence; pro-independence boycott of 2021 left its legitimacy contested.
- The infographic's population **278,500 (2017)**, ethnic shares **39.1% Kanak/27.1% European/33.8% other**, GDP **€8 billion (2015)**, unemployment **14.6% (2014)** and nickel output **12.237 million wet tonnes (2017)** are dated background, not May 2025 data. Avoid confusing ore output with refined nickel.
## May 2025 political impasse
- Proposed electoral-roll expansion was opposed as diluting Kanak influence; **May 2024 unrest** caused a reported **14 deaths** and extensive damage. North/Loyalty Islands and South Province have differing political majorities; Kanaks are not an absolute territory-wide majority merely because they predominate in some areas.
- **Manuel Valls' May 2025 talks** explored sovereignty in partnership/shared powers with France; loyalist opposition and a proposed territorial partition blocked agreement. The PDF's **8 May 2024 collapse** is a year error: this negotiation round ended **8 May 2025**. [French government May 2025 account](https://www.info.gouv.fr/conseil-des-ministres/compte-rendu-du-conseil-des-ministres-du-15-05-2025).
- Partition proposal: association for North/Loyalty Islands, closer French integration for South; rejected by independence representatives and France's territorial-integrity position. These were proposals, not implemented boundaries.
- Provincial elections anticipated for **November 2025** were a dated scheduling expectation, not proof they would proceed unchanged. Dialogue must reconcile self-determination, indigenous rights, democratic legitimacy and protections for all communities.

topics.title: Urban fire safety and building-code enforcement
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## 18–19 May 2025: urban fire reports
- Embedded Hyderabad clipping reports **17 family members killed, including eight children**, near Charminar; **17 rescued**. Cause was **under investigation** in that report, not a proven electrical fault. A separate Maharashtra garment-unit clipping reported **eight deaths**.
- PDF cites NCRB ADSI **2022: 7,435 deaths from over 7,500 fire accidents**; keep as a source-reported dated statistic pending table-level confirmation, not a current annual total.
## Rules, institutions and corrections
- **BIS National Building Code 2016**, first published **1970**, is a **model code** adopted through enforceable building/fire regulations and other applicable instruments. **Part 4 = Fire and Life Safety**; requirements depend on building occupancy/height/risk. [BIS NBC](https://www.bis.gov.in/standards/national-building-code/?lang=en).
- **Twelfth Schedule item 7** covers municipal fire services; it is **not the Seventh Schedule State List**, as the PDF claims. State/local law, municipal building controls and fire services share implementation responsibilities.
- **Model Building Bye-Laws 2016** guide adoption by States/UTs; NDMA preparedness guidance complements local enforceable rules. Codes on paper do not establish inspection/NOC compliance.
- Three layers: **prevention** (safe electrical/gas systems, fire-resistant construction/compartmentation, zoning); **life safety** (clear protected exits, occupant-load planning, signage/emergency light, smoke control and drills); **protection** (appropriate alarms, sprinklers/mist, risers/water supply and maintained firefighting systems). [BIS user guide](https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Booklet-Guide-for-Using-NBC-2016.pdf).
- Do not universalise every listed system or two-hour staircase requirement across every building type. **Metal sheets are not inherently highly flammable**; heat transfer, structural behaviour and combustible contents matter. Generic “smog-control devices” cannot substitute for engineered smoke management.
## Compliance failures and response
- Unsafe alterations/combustibles, blocked escape routes, absent/expired NOCs, irregular audits, staff/training shortages, ageing equipment, poor planning and weak public preparedness create preventable risk. PDF's Rajkot example is a reported case, not proof every allegation was adjudicated.
- Adopt/enforce appropriate norms, risk-based mandatory audits of high-rises/schools/hospitals/malls, transparent NOCs, penalties, independent checks and accountable maintenance. A **uniform binding national code** is a reform proposal in this issue, not already enacted law.
- Invest in trained firefighters, suitable vehicles/equipment, water access, GIS dispatch, inspections and learning from incidents; integrate planning with emergency access.
- Practise evacuation, keep exits clear, use designated stairs, protect children/elderly/disabled occupants; avoid ordinary lifts, re-entry and panic. Smoke exposure can be lethal before direct burns.
## Mains practice framework
- Introduce the enforcement gap → organise causes into legal/institutional/building/community failures → recommend enforceable standards, audits/capacity, maintained detection/suppression and public drills → conclude with accountable prevention and urban resilience. The **250-word/15-mark** question supplied is **undated coaching practice**, not an authenticated PYQ.

topics.title: Harappan civilisation: chronology and urban features
topics.subject: Ancient and Medieval India
topics.markdown:
## Revision anchors
- Broad Harappan sequence approximately **3300–1300 BCE**; distinguish **Mature urban phase c. 2600–1900 BCE** from early/late phases. Spread covered present Pakistan and northwestern/western India beyond only the main Indus banks.
- **Harappa—Punjab, Pakistan; Mohenjo-daro—Sindh**; **Dholavira/Lothal—Gujarat; Kalibangan—Rajasthan; Rakhigarhi—Haryana**. Harappa's excavation supplied the conventional name; Mohenjo-daro's Great Bath illustrates public works.
- Planned settlements, drainage, bricks, craft production, standardised weights, bronze tools and beads; agriculture, exchange networks and maritime links supported complex urban economies. Lothal's interpreted dock/water structure and trade role should not imply every inference is uncontested.
- Script remains undeciphered; archaeological evidence does not establish a complete political hierarchy or prove no religion existed merely because clearly identified palaces/temples are absent.
- Environmental/climatic changes, river shifts and regional settlement/economic reorganisation feature in decline explanations. **Invasion is an older hypothesis, not an established general cause**; urban decline did not mean every population disappeared. [NCERT historical overview](https://www.ncert.nic.in/dgs/pdf/KGBV-HistoryENGLISH.pdf).
- Floodplains/resource access facilitated settlement; contemporary Mesopotamia/Egypt illustrate separate early civilisations. Study planning, technology and exchange through evidence rather than projecting modern institutions onto ancient towns.

topics.title: Mullaperiyar Dam and interstate safety governance
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Dam and dispute
- **Idukki, Kerala**, on **Periyar near Mullayar confluence**; Tamil Nadu operates/maintains it under interstate arrangements for diverted water supporting irrigation/drinking supply and power. Completed **1895**; “126 years old” is stale for 2025. Source dimensions **53.66 m height/365.85 m length** need engineering datum consistency.
- **Periyar: about 244 km**, Kerala's longest river, Sivagiri/Western Ghats headwaters; tributaries **Mullayar, Muthirapuzha, Cheruthoni, Perinjankutti**; reservoir/river landscape within Periyar protected area. Source categorically locates origin in Tamil Nadu without adequate boundary evidence; use geographic headwaters rather than assert that State label. [Kerala statistics](https://ecostat.kerala.gov.in/publication-detail/compendium-of-environment-statistics-kerala-2013).
- **1979** safety concerns lowered level from **152 ft to 136 ft** while strengthening. Supreme Court **2006/2014** allowed **142 ft**, with **2014 supervisory mechanism**. Kerala seeks replacement/decommissioning for safety; Tamil Nadu argues strengthening/continued supply and eventual 152-ft restoration. Demands are not automatically permitted operational levels.
## 19 May 2025: repair directions
- Kerala to forward tree-felling application/recommendations **within two weeks**; Union **MoEFCC sanction within three further weeks**, subject to conditions. **No felling before formal sanction**.
- Material transport: Kerala had consented for six of nine repairs; remaining permissions **within one week**, with Kerala Executive Engineer present. **Vallakadavu Ghat Road** repairs: Kerala executes with ecologically suitable materials/Tamil Nadu engineer; Tamil Nadu pays; **four-week** completion direction.
- Dormitory repairs permitted under supervision; second boat conditional on **Inland Vessels Act 2021/Wildlife Protection Act 1972** compliance. Supervisory Committee addresses remaining matters **within six weeks** and grouting recommendations **within four weeks**.
- These are **court directions**, not proof works finished or environmental statutes waived. [Supreme Court order](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2006/8520/8520_2006_2_301_61943_Order_19-May-2025.pdf).
- Cooperative engineering assessment, transparent monitoring, downstream preparedness and predictable access are necessary; nearby landslides alone do not establish imminent structural failure.

topics.title: India, Türkiye and Azerbaijan: diplomacy and economic links
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## May 2025 backlash and relationships
- Following Türkiye/Azerbaijan support for Pakistan in the Pahalgam/India–Pakistan crisis, the issue reports **tour-operator cancellations, trader boycott resolutions and suspension of institutional MoUs including IITs/JNU**. These are organisational/public responses, **not proof of a comprehensive Indian government trade or travel ban**.
- Türkiye–Pakistan defence/diplomatic ties include Kashmir/Cyprus positions and artillery/armoured-platform transfers; Türkiye supported Azerbaijan in **2020 Nagorno-Karabakh war**. India–Armenia defence exports include surface-to-air missiles and multiple rocket launchers. SIPRI records cover **major conventional arms**, so absent records are not proof of zero trade in every defence item.
- Source data: Türkiye/Azerbaijan combined **under 1% of India's crude imports (2018–2023)**; India **third-largest Azerbaijani oil buyer in 2023**. Türkiye's machinery share around **1%** is a dated product-category claim, not import dependence across every sector.
- Indian arrivals: **under 1% of Türkiye tourists (2024)**; Azerbaijan **roughly 10% (2024), about 6% (2023)**. Combined students reportedly **777 by January 2024**, versus under 100 in 2017. Tourism, students, commodity trade and armaments have separate datasets; “limited aggregate exposure” does not guarantee no firm/person suffers boycott costs.
## Azerbaijan map and Karabakh correction
- **South Caucasus; capital Baku on western Caspian shore**; borders **Russia (Dagestan), Georgia, Armenia, Iran and Türkiye via Nakhchivan**. Nakhchivan is Azerbaijani **exclave** separated from mainland, directly bordering Türkiye/Armenia/Iran—not an indirect Turkish border.
- **Kura River → Caspian; Greater Caucasus north; Ganja, Nakhchivan City, Shusha** recall. Caspian is the largest enclosed inland water body; **Russia/Azerbaijan/Iran/Turkmenistan/Kazakhstan** are littoral States.
- Azerbaijan restored control over Karabakh **2023**; the PDF's present “mainly Armenian population” is misleading after **over 100,000 fled to Armenia**. Historical Armenian-majority/separatist administration is not the same as current demographic reality. [UNHCR](https://www.unhcr.org/am/en/refugee-response-and-coordination-0).
- **BTC oil pipeline: Baku–Tbilisi–Ceyhan**; **TANAP/TAP gas routes** connect to Europe; Azerbaijan participates in western INSTC connectivity. An interest in BRI is not proof every corridor/project is complete.
## Türkiye map recall
- Transcontinental: **Anatolia in Asia + eastern Thrace in Europe**; **Ankara capital, Istanbul largest city**. **Black Sea north, Aegean west, Mediterranean south**.
- **Bosporus: Black Sea ↔ Marmara; Dardanelles: Marmara ↔ Aegean**. Eight land neighbours: **Bulgaria, Greece, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Iran, Iraq, Syria**.
- Turkish official language; Kurdish/Arabic spoken; majority-Muslim society. The source's **over 99%** religion share is an undated estimate, not necessary exact contemporary census fact. Diplomacy should assess security positions, business exposure and long-term engagement distinctly.

topics.title: Jarosite and luminescence dating on Mars
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## 21 May 2025 research report
- **Jarosite**, yellow-brown hydrous iron sulphate, ideal formula **KFe₃(SO₄)₂(OH)₆**; forms in acidic oxidising aqueous environments. Opportunity detected it on Mars in **2004**: evidence relevant to past water chemistry, not proof of life.
- Six terrestrial samples from **Kachchh, Gujarat**, a dry/saline Martian analogue, were tested as potential luminescence dosimeters/chronometers. Radiation stores energy in mineral traps; heating or suitable light releases a measurable signal. **Age ≈ accumulated dose / dose rate**, provided initial resetting, stability and environmental dose are understood.
- Source laboratory procedure: weak-acid washing, controlled irradiation and repeated heating/cooling; thermoluminescence peaks near **100, 150, 300 and 350°C**, persisting after **450°C** annealing. This supports instrument-development potential, not a demonstrated operational Martian rover clock.
- Source gives saturation **590–2,600 Gy**, dose rate **65 mGy/year = 65 Gy/ka**, and a possible dating window of **~25,000 years**. The later published paper reports **700–2,600 Gy** for the relevant saturation measures and stresses different signal stability/fading. Do not derive a universal precise maximum age from one saturation value. [Primary study, published July 2025](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/maps.70021).
- Proposed applications: recent sediment transport/dust storms, flood deposits and volcanic layers using compact heaters/LEDs. Actual Martian validation and dose/resetting calibration remain necessary; a ~25 ka method does not date all billion-year-old water events.

topics.title: Potato cultivation, productivity and food security
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## 21 May 2025: CIP outlook
- Scientists associated with **International Potato Center (CIP / Centro Internacional de la Papa), Peru**, projected Indian potato production could reach **100 million tonnes annually by 2050**, potentially overtaking China. India was described as **second-largest after China**; projection is not an achieved ranking.
- Context: symposium on **Root and Tuber Crops Research and Development in India and South Asia**, and **50 years of India–CIP cooperation**; source quotes board chair Helen Hambly Odame. Research, improved seed, storage and processing support food security and livelihoods; growth must remain climate/resource-resilient.
## Crop and geography
- Potato is botanically a **modified underground stem tuber**, not a root. Primarily **rabi** in Indian plains; cooler hill/southern conditions allow other seasons, including limited kharif production in source-listed Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra.
- **UP and West Bengal** lead; other producers include Bihar, Gujarat, MP, Punjab, Haryana, Assam, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh. Source 2021–22 figures: UP **161 lakh tonnes**, West Bengal **124 lakh**, India **533 lakh**: combined **~53.5%**, rather than exactly 50%.
- Source series **1991–92 → 2020–21**: area **11 → 22 lakh ha**; output **181.95 → 561.72 lakh tonnes**; yield **~16 → 25 tonnes/ha**. Keep these dated rounded figures together; do not compare them directly to a forecast as actual growth.
- Cool conditions favour tuberisation; heat stress reduces yield. Source indicative day **18–29°C**, night **13–18°C**, growth optimum **~24°C**, tuber development **~20°C**: cultivar and stage matter, so “above 30°C tuberisation always stops” is too absolute.
- Loose, well-aerated, organic-rich loam/sandy loam and good drainage aid tuber growth; salinity/alkalinity and waterlogging constrain it. Adequate light matters; the source's six-hour rule is a general horticultural guide, not a universal agronomic threshold.
## Value chain and PYQ links
- Quality disease-free seed, extension, water management, cold storage, processing and export access can lift supply and income. More output alone does not guarantee better prices/net income; post-harvest losses and gluts require market planning.
- **2023 India–China agriculture PYQ: (b), only two**—India has more arable area and a higher irrigated proportion, but not higher average productivity; compare like-for-like land definitions.
- **2019 rice exporter: India (b)** in the question's five-year context, not a permanent ranking guarantee. Source rice export shares/destination lists are period-dependent; policy is not invariably export-friendly.
- **2011 lower Gangetic plain: paddy and jute (c)** fit humid, warm, alluvial conditions. Wheat is still cultivated in eastern India; cotton can grow beyond black soils, so alternative-option explanations should not become blanket impossibility claims.

## June 25 Cabinet approval: Agra research centre
- Cabinet approved **CIP South Asia Regional Centre (CSARC), Singna, Agra, Uttar Pradesh**, serving India/South Asia. Approved establishment is distinct from an already operating completed facility.
- **₹171 crore total**: India **₹111.5 crore**, CIP **₹60 crore**; UP provides **10 hectares**. Research on climate-resilient/disease-free **potato and sweet potato**, quality seed, storage/post-harvest systems, processing/value addition, technology transfer and farmer livelihoods. [Cabinet decision](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2139496&lang=2&reg=48).
- **CIP**, established **1971**, headquarters **Lima, Peru**; works on potato, sweet potato and Andean roots/tubers; India cooperation since **1975**. Access to germplasm and better domestic seed can reduce import dependence and support food/nutrition security.
- CIP's China Asia-Pacific centre at **Yanqing, Beijing (2017)** is another regional institution. The source calls CSARC India's second such international agricultural regional centre after IRRI-SARC; **IRRI-SARC, Varanasi was inaugurated in 2018**, so its “established 2017” shorthand should not replace the inauguration date. [2018 inauguration](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1557772&lang=2&reg=48).
- Existing crop requirements, source 1991–2021 growth series, UP/West Bengal leadership and conditional **2050** forecast cover the repeated cultivation section. “Third most consumed food” depends on crop/measure definition; avoid equating fresh potato tonnage with cereal calorie contribution.

## July 2025 research: ancient hybrid origin
- Cell study traced potato lineage to **hybridisation between ancestral tomato and Etuberosum lineages about 8–9 million years ago**, not potatoes descending directly from today's cultivated tomato. All belong to **Solanum/Solanaceae**; neither ancestral parental lineage had potato tubers.
- Combined inherited genetic machinery enabled tuber development, vegetative reproduction and diversification into cold/dry Andean habitats; source cites **107 wild potato species** and roughly **40% tomato-like/60% Etuberosum-like ancestry** as study summaries, not a recipe for crossing modern crops.
- Evolutionary insight may aid breeding for resilience; an inferred ancient origin does not itself establish a new released climate-proof cultivar. [Participating Natural History Museum, 31 July 2025](https://www.nhm.ac.uk/press-office/press-releases/scientists-reveal-the-origins-of-the-potato-and-find-the-key-to-.html).

topics.title: DGFT and foreign-trade administration
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Institutions and trade facilitation
- **DGFT**, attached office under the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**, headquarters **New Delhi**; evolved from Chief Controller of Imports and Exports during post-1991 reforms. Implements Foreign Trade Policy, authorisations, notifications, norms and exporter obligations alongside its facilitation role.
- Source describes **24 regional offices**, also documented in a June 2024 DGFT circular; this is a dated administrative count, not an immutable number.
- **IEC** is the importer-exporter identifier issued online by DGFT, aligned with PAN. Generally required for goods trade **subject to exempt categories**; services/technology have specified requirements including FTP-benefit eligibility. Source's “mandatory for all importers/exporters” omits exemptions. [FTP 2023](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/61d61bc2-272e-4880-b96c-c8f685a3b244/Foreign%20Trade%20Policy%202023.pdf).
## 17 May restrictions; 21 May garment-industry response
- **Notification 07/2025–26**, effective immediately: Bangladesh ready-made garments barred through land ports; imports permitted through **Nhava Sheva and Kolkata seaports**. Other specified products face specified land-port restrictions; this is **not a blanket ban on all Bangladesh trade**. [Commerce Ministry notification summary](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2129380&lang=2&reg=48).
- Clipping: Indian/Tiruppur garment MSMEs hoped higher logistics costs and lead times would shift orders domestically; importers' response and realised order gains were still uncertain. Source estimates imported garments **12–15% cheaper**, land-to-sea shift could add **~10% costs**, imports **$634 million in 2024/~19% ten-year CAGR**, and overall 2024 textile/apparel trade **India→Bangladesh $3.2 billion vs reverse $1.07 billion**. These are industry/trade-data claims with distinct denominators, not realised benefits of the notification.
- Mains: trade facilitation and border regulation must weigh domestic manufacturing/inputs, consumer costs, logistics, lawful origin verification and neighbouring-country relations; alleged rerouting of Chinese fabric is an industry concern requiring evidence.

topics.title: Trachoma elimination and avoidable blindness
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## WHO milestone and disease
- **WHO validated India's elimination of trachoma as a public-health problem on 8 October 2024**, the third South-East Asia Region country after Nepal and Myanmar. The May 2025 issue revisits this achievement; its “2023 elimination” table should not replace the official validation date. [WHO announcement](https://www.who.int/news/item/08-10-2024-elimination-of-trachoma-as-a-public-health-problem-in-india).
- **Chlamydia trachomatis** bacterial eye infection; spreads through infected eye/nasal discharge, hands, shared materials and eye-seeking flies. Repeated infection → eyelid scarring → inward-turning lashes (**trichiasis**) → corneal injury/blindness.
- **SAFE:** Surgery for trichiasis; Antibiotics against infection; Facial cleanliness; Environmental improvement including water/sanitation. **NPCBVI**, a centrally sponsored programme, supports avoidable-blindness reduction through eye care/screening and surgery; cataract surgery itself is not treatment for trachoma infection.
## Exact elimination criteria
- WHO thresholds: trichiasis **unknown to the health system <0.2% in adults ≥15 years**, follicular inflammation **<5% in children 1–9 years** in every formerly endemic district, sustained for at least two years without ongoing antibiotic mass treatment, plus a funded system able to detect/manage incident trichiasis. **Not merely “blindness below 1%”.** [WHO criteria](https://www.who.int/en/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/trachoma).
- Source historical blindness shares **5% in 1971 → below 1%** describe a burden trend with unclear denominators, not the validation test. Maintain surveillance and accessible eye/WASH services after elimination.
## PYQ disease distinctions
- **2014: smallpox alone (b)** among diphtheria, chickenpox and smallpox. Smallpox (Variola virus) globally eradicated in **1980**; last naturally acquired case **Somalia, 1977**. Diphtheria is bacterial (**Corynebacterium diphtheriae**), controlled through vaccination including DPT; chickenpox is **varicella-zoster viral** infection, not eradicated. Varicella vaccine availability differs from inclusion in India's UIP.
- **2001 athlete's foot: fungus (b)**; **tinea pedis**, commonly dermatophytes such as Trichophyton, causes itching/peeling/cracks and spreads through contaminated surfaces/materials. Moisture facilitates growth; hygiene/dry feet and appropriate antifungals matter.
- **Eradication** means permanent worldwide reduction to zero incidence; **elimination of transmission** concerns a defined geographical area; **elimination as a public-health problem** meets disease-specific thresholds. Endemic means continuing occurrence, not necessarily controlled disease.

topics.title: Neglected tropical diseases and integrated public health
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## NTD framework
- Diverse diseases concentrated in poor/marginalised tropical/subtropical settings; neglect reflects limited resources/attention and stigma. **Not all are communicable:** snakebite envenoming is toxin injury.
| Group | Examples |
|---|---|
| Helminthic | Taeniasis, lymphatic filariasis |
| Protozoal | Leishmaniasis/kala-azar |
| Viral | Rabies, dengue |
| Bacterial | Leprosy, trachoma, yaws |
| Fungal | Mycetoma/chromoblastomycosis and other deep mycoses |
| Ectoparasitic | Scabies |
| Non-infectious | Snakebite envenoming |
- **India guinea-worm-free certification: 2000**; yaws national elimination declared **2006**, WHO verified interruption/free status **2016**; **trachoma validation 2024**, not 2023. These national milestones do not mean all three diseases eradicated worldwide. [NCDC yaws timeline](https://ncdc.mohfw.gov.in/includes/About/CentresAndDivision/yep.php).
- Global instruments: WHO NTD **2021–2030 road map**, **Global NTD Annual Reporting Form (GNARF)** for monitoring, **Global Vector Control Response 2017–2030**, **Kigali Declaration 2022** political commitments. Different diseases require prevention/control/elimination/eradication targets; declarations are not achievements.
- Indian vector-borne programme covers malaria, dengue, chikungunya, kala-azar and lymphatic filariasis; **malaria is not itself on WHO's NTD list** simply because it shares control infrastructure. Swachh Bharat, Jal Jeevan Mission and health-system access support prevention through WASH, surveillance and care; one intervention cannot eliminate every NTD.

topics.title: International Booker Prize and Heart Lamp
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## 20 May 2025 award
- **Heart Lamp**, **Banu Mushtaq**, translated from **Kannada by Deepa Bhasthi**, published by **And Other Stories**, won at **Tate Modern, London**. First short-story collection and first Kannada-language winner; Bhasthi first Indian translator to win. Mushtaq is the second Indian author winner after Geetanjali Shree's **Tomb of Sand (2022)**.
- Twelve stories centre women's everyday struggles and resilience in southern Indian Muslim communities, engaging gender, religion, class/caste and power; the author's **Bandaya Sahitya** association links protest literature with marginalised voices. Translation makes regional literature accessible while preserving linguistic/cultural texture. [Official winner announcement](https://thebookerprizes.com/media-centre/press-releases/heart-lamp-wins-the-international-booker-prize-2025).
- Prize established **2005**; current annual translated-book format began **2016**. Eligible fiction translated into English and published in **UK/Ireland**. **£50,000 split equally author/translator**; source shortlisted author/translator award **£2,500 each**.
- Longlist **12–13**, shortlist **six**; selection dates vary by year, so source March/April/May calendar is not an immutable rule. Distinguish this translation prize from the separate Booker Prize for English-language fiction.

topics.title: Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Science honour and PYQ
- **2009 Prelims answer (c), Science**. Named after CSIR's founding Director **Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar**; recognises outstanding fundamental/applied scientific research, mainly work done in India.
- First award year **1958**; CSIR-HRDG describes institution in **1957**, whereas source simply gives 1958. Distinguish establishment from first award. Historical eligibility: Indian citizens **up to 45 years** as of **31 December of the preceding year**. [CSIR prize history](https://www.csir.res.in/en/shanti-swarup-bhatnagar-prize/shanti-swarup-bhatnagar-prize-science-and-technology-1958-1998), [HRDG institutional account](https://www.csirhrdg.res.in/Home/Index/1/Default/1887/8).
- Seven historical disciplines: **biological; chemical; earth/atmosphere/ocean/planetary; engineering; mathematical; medical; physical sciences**. Preserve the historical prize question without assuming its rules automatically describe every later national science-award category.

topics.title: Asiatic lions and conservation translocation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Range, status and habitat
- India's surviving wild Asiatic lions occupy the **Gir/Saurashtra landscape, Gujarat**, including areas outside Gir's protected boundaries; historically extended across West Asia. **Panthera leo persica** is the traditional name; modern taxonomy includes Indian lions within **P. l. leo**, with **P. l. melanochaita** covering southern/eastern African populations. “Asiatic vs all African” is not an exact two-subspecies division.
- **2020 population estimate: 674**, source landscape **~30,000 km², nine districts/53 talukas**; these are 2020 figures, not a May 2025 count. Growth does not eliminate genetic/disease risks. [Gujarat Forest Department](https://girlion.gujarat.gov.in/Documents/Uploads/NewsUpdates/WorldLionDay2020_report_final.pdf).
