- **Correction:** lion species **P. leo is Vulnerable**, but species-wide status must not be passed off as proof that Asiatic lions were downgraded from Endangered to Vulnerable after 2008. Historical Asiatic assessment was Endangered; taxon/assessment dates differ. Indian protection **Schedule I**, Indian population **CITES Appendix I**; other lion populations generally Appendix II. [IUCN Cat Specialist Group](https://www.catsg.org/living-species-lions).
- Gir National Park/Wildlife Sanctuary established **1965**, source combined protected area **~1,412 km²**; separately cited buffer **470 km²** should not be treated as the national park's own area. Dry deciduous/thorn/scrub habitats; **Girnar Sanctuary, 2008, Junagadh**, extends protection in the hills, with teak/dhak/acacia and leopards, chinkara/chousingha and birds. Source bird count >300 needs defined geographical scope.
- Typical Asiatic identification includes a less-developed mane and abdominal skin fold; body size/social systems vary, so source's male-pride contrast is not an absolute rule.
## Threats and translocation
- Restricted range and isolation → disease catastrophe, inbreeding and environmental-disaster risk; habitat/prey loss, roads/open wells/electric fencing and human-lion conflict require landscape protection, veterinary surveillance and community participation.
- **2017 PYQ: Kuno-Palpur Wildlife Sanctuary, MP (b)** proposed second lion population. This is the historic site name/status; proposal/court direction does not establish completed translocation. Geographic separation spreads risk but does not automatically increase genetic diversity without managed founders/exchange.
- Do not retain source's unsupported claims that Sariska lost lions through recent poaching or that Kuno's African-cheetah project was an earlier completed Asiatic-cheetah reintroduction.
- **2019 PYQ: Asiatic lion alone (a)** exclusively naturally found in India today. Greater one-horned rhino **India/Nepal**, not a confirmed current wild population in Bhutan/Bangladesh. Bactrian camels occur beyond India; distinguish domesticated Ladakh camels from the separate wild camel **Camelus ferus** of China/Mongolia. A Rajasthan dromedary is not proof of a natural wild population.

## 2025 estimate visible in the issue's graphics
- The **16th lion population estimation (May 2025): 891**, compared with **674 in 2020**, about **32.2% increase**. Issue graphic records landscape **~35,000 km² across 11 districts**. These are survey-period estimates; the prose's 674/nine districts remains the older 2020 snapshot.
- Embedded reporting stresses expansion outside protected Gir into satellite habitats/corridors. Conservation needs landscape connectivity and conflict/disease monitoring beyond park boundaries. [Later official confirmation of the 2025 count](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2223755&lang=1&reg=1).

topics.title: Cholera and waterborne-disease control
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Infection and prevention
- Acute diarrhoeal infection from **Vibrio cholerae**, transmitted by contaminated water/food. Epidemic disease chiefly **O1/O139**, with **O1 responsible for recent outbreaks**; infection ranges from asymptomatic to severe rice-water diarrhoea, vomiting, cramps and rapidly fatal dehydration.
- Timely **oral rehydration**, IV fluids for severe dehydration and appropriate antibiotics for severe cases save lives. Safe water, sewage treatment, hygiene, surveillance/rapid response and oral vaccination work together; vaccination cannot replace WASH. [WHO disease facts](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/cholera).
## Historical trend versus the May 2025 issue
- Source refers to **2022**, not new May cases: WHO reports **472,697 cases versus 223,370 in 2021**, more than double. Countries/regions including Africa and Asia, Lebanon, Syria and Afghanistan experienced outbreaks; inconsistent reporting means notifications are not the full incidence burden. Source Nigeria/25%-share comparisons need matching regional denominators. [WHO 2022 report](https://iris.who.int/bitstream/handle/10665/372993/WER9838-431-43.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1).
- **Ending Cholera: global roadmap to 2030**, launched **2017** by the **GTFCC** partnership: target **90% reduction in deaths by 2030**; targeted multisectoral control/elimination in countries is not a claim of completed worldwide eradication.
## Vaccine correction
- Source list **Dukoral, Shanchol, Euvichol-Plus** is outdated: **Euvichol-S prequalified 12 April 2024**; Shanchol production stopped in **2022**, last doses distributed **2023**. [WHO vaccine record](https://extranet.who.int/prequal/vaccines/p/euvicholr-s), [WHO 2023 annual report](https://cdn.who.int/media/docs/default-source/dco/wer_36_2024_cholera-annual-report-for-2023_bilingual-proof.pdf).
- Standard full adult protection generally uses two doses; **single-dose outbreak regimens since October 2022 during supply shortage** give shorter-term protection. Source “all require two doses” omits this policy and age/product differences. Track prequalification, production, availability and campaign schedule separately.

topics.title: Golden Dome and layered missile defence
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## May 2025 proposal
- President **Donald Trump** outlined **Golden Dome on 20 May 2025**, following **27 January 2025 Executive Order 14186**. A planned US homeland missile-defence system, not an operational shield or a geographical copy of Israel's Iron Dome. Space Force General **Michael Guetlein** was selected to lead the effort.
- Planned architecture integrates space/ground sensors, tracking, interceptors and command-and-control against **ballistic, cruise and hypersonic missiles**, including conventionally or nuclear-armed threats. Space-based detection and proposed interceptors could permit earlier engagement; satellite numbers, autonomous operation and universal interception capability remain design claims, not demonstrated facts. [US DoD, 20 May](https://www.defense.gov/News/Releases/Release/article/4193417/secretary-of-defense-pete-hegseth-statement-on-golden-dome-for-america/).
- A distributed real-time network must detect → classify → track → assign interception → assess results. Coverage, discrimination of decoys, saturation, survivability, cost and integration are challenges. Source's “nuclear drones” wording should not be confused with a confirmed category of nuclear-powered drones being intercepted.
## Strategic and treaty debate
- Russian/Chinese objections concern weaponisation of space, arms racing and strategic stability; sensor satellites and weapons stationed in space are distinct issues.
- **Outer Space Treaty 1967, Article IV** prohibits nuclear weapons/other WMD in orbit or stationed in space; celestial bodies must be used exclusively for peaceful purposes, without military bases, weapons testing or manoeuvres. It **does not expressly prohibit every conventional Earth-orbit interceptor**. Treaty legality cannot be inferred merely from the word space; UN Charter obligations and due regard remain relevant. [UN treaty text](https://www.unoosa.org/oosa/en/ourwork/spacelaw/treaties/outerspacetreaty.html).
## Systems and PYQ recall
| System | Country / distinction |
| --- | --- |
| Iron Dome | Israel; short-range rockets/artillery threats |
| David's Sling | Israel; medium-range layer |
| Arrow-2 / Arrow-3 | Israel; ballistic-missile defence, including high-altitude/exo-atmospheric interception |
| S-400 Triumf | Russia; long-range surface-to-air system |
| THAAD | US; Terminal High Altitude Area Defense, terminal-phase ballistic interception |
| HQ-9 | China; long-range air defence; range differs by variant, source's 125 km not universal |
| Golden Dome | US; proposed multilayer homeland architecture |
- **2018 PYQ: THAAD → American anti-missile system, (c)**; deployment in South Korea began in 2017. **2008 PYQ: Barak purchase → Israel, (a)**. Original Barak shipborne point defence must be distinguished from later jointly developed India–Israel Barak-8/MRSAM; the purchase question does not establish original Barak was jointly developed.

topics.title: Gallantry awards: order and eligibility
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Two principal orders
| In the face of the enemy: conventional wartime label | Not in the face of the enemy: conventional peacetime label |
| --- | --- |
| **Param Vir Chakra** — highest | **Ashoka Chakra** — highest |
| **Maha Vir Chakra** — second | **Kirti Chakra** — second |
| **Vir Chakra** — third | **Shaurya Chakra** — third |
- President confers awards for gallantry/courage/self-sacrifice under each award's conditions. “Wartime” does **not require a formally declared war**; the criterion is action in the face/presence of the enemy. “Peacetime” is not a ban on recognising dangerous counter-terrorism, counter-insurgency or rescue acts.
- PVC: most conspicuous bravery or daring/pre-eminent valour/self-sacrifice in the face of enemy; MVC/VC recognise respective degrees of gallantry in enemy presence, on land, sea or air. Ashoka Chakra recognises exceptional courage/self-sacrifice other than in enemy presence; Kirti/Shaurya follow in order.
## Dates and eligible persons
- **26 January 1950**: PVC, MVC and VC instituted, effective retrospectively from **15 August 1947**. **1952**: Ashoka Chakra Classes I, II and III instituted, likewise retrospective; **January 1967** renamed Ashoka, Kirti and Shaurya Chakra.
- Eligibility includes Army/Navy/Air Force, territorial/reserve and other lawfully constituted forces under award rules. **Civilians, police and paramilitary personnel** can receive the not-in-enemy-presence awards; civilian eligibility should not be assumed identical for every decoration.
- Service medals **Sena Medal, Nao Sena Medal, Vayu Sena Medal** recognise service-specific gallantry or distinguished devotion to duty, depending on the award category; awards can arise in wartime or peacetime. They are distinct from the six Chakra awards.

topics.title: Financial Action Task Force and compliance lists
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Mandate and membership
- **FATF**, intergovernmental standard setter established at **1989 G7 Paris summit**; Secretariat in **Paris**, hosted by OECD. Combats **money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing** through standards, mutual evaluations and implementation monitoring; does not investigate/prosecute individual criminal cases.
- India became a full member in **2010**. Source's **39 members /37 jurisdictions +2 organisations** is outdated after Indonesia's **October 2023** accession: FATF counts **40 members**, including **European Commission and Gulf Cooperation Council**; Russia's membership was suspended **24 February 2023**. Membership total and active participation differ. [FATF network](https://www.fatf-gafi.org/en/countries.html), [Indonesia accession](https://www.fatf-gafi.org/en/countries/detail/Indonesia.html).
## Lists: status relevant to May 2025
| List | Meaning / consequence |
| --- | --- |
| **Jurisdictions under increased monitoring**, grey list | Strategic deficiencies with agreed corrective action; greater monitoring, possible reputational/financing costs; not an automatic FATF sanctions order or instruction to sever every relationship |
| **High-risk jurisdictions subject to a call for action**, black list | Significant deficiencies; enhanced due diligence and, for the most serious cases, countermeasures; measures vary by jurisdiction |
- **21 February 2025 high-risk list: DPRK, Iran and Myanmar**. Source omits Myanmar. DPRK/Iran attracted countermeasure calls; Myanmar required proportionate enhanced due diligence, with humanitarian flows/remittances protected. The old **NCCT** label is not the current official list title, and listing does not prove every government deliberately funds terrorism. [Dated FATF statement](https://www.fatf-gafi.org/en/publications/High-risk-and-other-monitored-jurisdictions/Call-for-action-february-2025.html).
- Pakistan was removed from increased monitoring in **October 2022**; May clipping reports India considering/pushing for renewed scrutiny, not proof Pakistan had been re-listed. Review national AML/CFT effectiveness and evidence, not nationality alone. Financial restrictions derive from competent jurisdictions/UN rules; FATF recommendations and sanctions are different instruments.

## June2025 list check
- India advocating renewed scrutiny of Pakistan is a diplomatic proposal, **not a June2025 re-listing**. Pakistan did not appear on the **13 June2025 increased-monitoring list**. [Dated list](https://www.fatf-gafi.org/content/fatf-gafi/en/publications/High-risk-and-other-monitored-jurisdictions/increased-monitoring-june-2025.html).
- **13 June2025 high-risk list:** DPRK, Iran, Myanmar; countermeasure calls differ from Myanmar's proportionate enhanced due diligence. This repeats and confirms the corrected May distinction, rather than the PDF's two-country list. [FATF statement](https://www.fatf-gafi.org/en/publications/High-risk-and-other-monitored-jurisdictions/Call-for-action-june-2025.html).

topics.title: Border Security Force: mandate and capabilities
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Origin and role
- **BSF raised 1 December 1965** after the India–Pakistan war; central border-guarding force under **MHA**, governed by **BSF Act 1968**. “First line of defence”; motto **Duty Unto Death**.
- Guards primarily **India–Pakistan and India–Bangladesh international borders**, prevents infiltration/smuggling/transnational crime and supports the Army in war; deployments also include LoC duties alongside Army and internal-security/anti-Naxal assignments. CAPF is not interchangeable with the regular military Armed Forces.
- Logo: National Emblem, grain ears and BSF lettering/motto. Source calls it one of seven CAPFs: MHA listings often group **CAPFs, Assam Rifles and NSG**, while narrower classifications differ; name the force rather than infer all seven have identical command structures.
## Capability and legal limits
- Air/water wings, artillery and specialised units support varied terrain; camel/dog units aid border operations. **Tear Smoke Unit** produces riot-control munitions. Leadership is a **Director General**, normally an IPS officer.
- Source **186 battalions /2.57 lakh personnel** is an older snapshot, not a May 2025 verified strength: official parliamentary broadcaster's **December 2023** description gives **193 battalions including four disaster-management battalions, over 2.65 lakh personnel**; sanctioned and deployed strengths differ. [Sansad TV profile](https://sansadtv.nic.in/episode/national-security-border-security-force-03-december-2023).
- Notified powers include specified **arrest/search/seizure** under relevant passport, customs, NDPS and arms laws; scope depends on law, notification and geography. They do not confer unlimited nationwide policing or replace State police responsibility for ordinary crimes.
- May issue links BSF's border role to India–Pakistan escalation; preparedness, locally informed surveillance, force coordination and accountable law enforcement matter alongside infrastructure. Avoid assigning a precise contemporary troop deployment from a general profile.

topics.title: Medical oxygen access and health-system resilience
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Essential medicine and measured access gap
- **Medical oxygen**, WHO essential medicine, treats hypoxaemia in pneumonia/acute respiratory disease, neonatal distress, severe systemic illness and surgery/anaesthesia. Reliable access requires a **service ecosystem**, not only possession of cylinders or a PSA plant.
- **Lancet Global Health Commission 2025** estimates over **5 billion people** lack safe, affordable, quality oxygen-service access. Acute medical-patient coverage gaps: **South Asia 78%**, **East Asia/Pacific 74%**; these are not proportions of all residents or all surgical/chronic patients. **Sub-Saharan Africa 91%** is higher, so the source's “highest gaps worldwide” claim for the Asian regions is wrong. [Commission presentation](https://stoppneumonia.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Lancet-Commission-Official-Deck-9.pdf).
- In **LMIC general hospitals**, pulse oximeters available in about **54%**, oxygen therapy in **58%**; corresponding tertiary-hospital values **83% /86%**. Source omits facility types and incorrectly implies the figures describe every hospital uniformly. [Commission paper](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/11865010/).
- Additional financing to close LMIC coverage gaps: about **US$6.8 billion annually**, including **US$2.6 billion for South Asia**; commission's **US$34 billion 2025–30** estimate is a programme-cost calculation, not an already funded global commitment. Source's unqualified “$6.8 billion globally” loses geography and time unit. [Commission policy brief](https://stoppneumonia.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Policy-Brief-English-1.pdf).
## Equipment → sustained safe service
- Challenges: missing pulse oximetry/delivery devices, poor distribution, rural inequity, unstable electricity, scarce biomedical engineers/technicians and unfunded maintenance; installed equipment can be nonfunctional.
- **PSA** separates oxygen from air through pressure-dependent adsorption; concentrators support smaller-scale supply. Cryogenic production/liquid oxygen is a different supply route. Cylinders, booster pumps, community supply hubs and transport networks support delivery; purity, fire safety and quality standards are essential.
- Solar power with adequate storage/backup may improve reliability in remote settings; Ethiopian/Nigerian examples illustrate adaptation, not guaranteed uninterrupted operation or universal savings. Use clinical demand, local energy conditions and maintenance costs to choose systems.
## Governance and equity
- **WHA resolution 76.3 (2023)** urges increased access; **WHO Director-General** reports implementation progress to WHA in **2026, 2028 and 2030**, rather than a blanket direct reporting deadline imposed on every individual facility. [Resolution](https://apps.who.int/gb/ebwha/pdf_files/WHA76/A76_R3-en.pdf).
- National scale-up plans should fund lifecycle operation, trained staff, local manufacture where feasible, procurement/production/storage/transport standards and emergency reserves within **UHC**. A proposed access scorecard supports monitoring; distinguish planning/reporting tools from proven local implementation.
- WHO's **2022 South-East Asia lessons report** stresses sustained investment beyond COVID surges. Source's Nepal–Bhutan technician training/PSA collaboration offers a regional-cooperation example, subject to project-specific verification.
- Digital demand forecasts, supply inventories and real-time equipment monitoring; research on affordable context-suitable systems; public/private/civil-society coordination. **SDGs 3 and 10** link oxygen security to health and equitable access. Donation counts alone do not establish patient access or clinical quality.

topics.title: Integrated theatre commands and jointness
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Purpose and existing structures
- Theatreisation integrates Army/Navy/Air Force assets under a theatre commander for operational planning/application in a defined area; joint intelligence, logistics, communications and training aim to reduce duplication and improve response.
- Source baseline **17 single-service commands: Army 7, Navy 3, Air Force 7** includes operational/support commands, not 17 identical geographical theatres. **Andaman and Nicobar Command (2001)** is joint; **Strategic Forces Command (2003)** manages strategic nuclear forces under the nuclear-command framework, distinct from conventional geographical theatreisation.
- Kargil **1999** exposed coordination gaps; subsequent Kargil-review/Group of Ministers, Naresh Chandra and Shekatkar reform discussions support jointness with differing recommendations. Do not attribute every CDS/theatre proposal identically to all committees.
- US/Chinese unified commands offer comparators; **China's Western Theatre Command** covers the India-facing region. Other countries' joint arrangements are not identical structures simply labelled theatre commands.
## May 2025 proposal: not three operational new commands
- Issue reports proposals for **Pakistan-facing Western (Jaipur)**, **China-facing Northern (Lucknow)** and **Maritime (Coimbatore)** commands. Maritime locations, previously Karwar and other southern sites, have varied in reporting; source's Coimbatore is a **reported proposal, not a verified final notified headquarters**.
- Proposed **four-star Vice CDS**, **three-star Deputy CDS**, theatre operational control and service chiefs' **Raise, Train and Sustain** roles remain organisational ideas subject to final decisions. Source's prospective defence-minister-led **National Defence Committee** is likewise not an established operational body.
- Cross-posting, common training/logistics and headquarters restructuring are steps towards integration. **Joint Logistics Nodes at Mumbai, Guwahati and Port Blair operational since 2021**; source's claim Mumbai was already designated the first common defence station in 2024 conflates reported plans with completion. [MoD jointness account](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressNoteDetails.aspx?ModuleId=3&NoteId=154490&lang=2&reg=3).
## Law and implementation
- **Inter-Services Organisations (Command, Control and Discipline) Act 2023**, effective **10 May 2024**, empowers specified joint commanders to exercise disciplinary/administrative control over personnel from different services while respective service laws remain applicable. It supports future joint structures; it does **not itself create all proposed theatres**.
- Allocation of scarce air assets, clear theatre/service-chief authority, interoperable intelligence/communications, logistics, training/career culture and manpower-neutral restructuring are central challenges. Resource savings and faster decisions are aims to test, not assured merely by renaming headquarters.
- Jointness strengthens deterrence and coordinated two-front/sea responses; indigenous technology complements organisation but theatreisation does not automatically make imported weapons indigenous.

topics.title: Project Kusha and indigenous air-defence development
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## May 2025 development stage
- **Project Kusha**, DRDO-led long-range surface-to-air defence development, aims to protect against aircraft, missiles and UAV threats; often compared with Russia's S-400, but analogy is not proof of identical design/performance or completed induction.
- **BEL** is a development-cum-production partner for radars/control subsystems. Its **20 May 2025 earnings call** says overall system integrator was **not yet finalised**. **₹40,000 crore** is a potential order opportunity conditional on integration/procurement allocation, **not sanctioned total project cost or an order already awarded to BEL**. [BEL official transcript](https://bel-india.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/दिनांक-20.05.2025-को-आयोजित-कॉन्फ्रेंस-कॉल-की-प्रति.pdf).
- Source's **12–18 months prototype /12–36 months trials** are expectations requiring technical trials, user evaluation and procurement; not completed milestones or a binding delivery promise. Technological performance, reliability, timely qualification, domestic supply chains and integration with **IACCS** determine utility.
## Related systems and procurement distinctions
- **QRSAM**, DRDO-led quick-reaction low-level air-defence programme, has BEL as production agency; expected **₹30,000 crore combined Army/Air Force order** discussed by BEL remained a **future expectation in May**, not contract receipt. BEL partnership does not replace DRDO's development role.
- Source **S-400 400 km** describes an advertised **missile engagement range for a particular interceptor**, not a universal radar-detection radius. India contracted five systems in **2018** for roughly **US$5.4 billion**; source **three delivered/two pending** is a dated delivery account, not proof all arrived.
- Operation Sindoor revived attention to layered defence, including S-400, Akash and Barak-8; **BrahMos is a strike cruise missile, not a SAM interceptor**. Source's “over 300 Pakistani drones neutralised” cannot be inferred merely from reported drone numbers or assigned to each named system without verified operational evidence.
- Indigenous air-defence R&D supports strategic autonomy and reduced import dependence; fielded range/accuracy, availability, interoperability, replenishment and lifecycle maintenance matter beyond comparison slogans.

topics.title: Coastline measurement and the coastline paradox
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Why measured length increased
- India’s reported coastline was reassessed from **7,516.6 km to 11,098.81 km**, without equivalent territorial gain. The source associates reassessment with December 2024; a later official reply dates promulgation to the **29 April 2025 MoPSW circular**, based on NHO/Survey of India work. [Official clarification](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2198800&lang=1&reg=6).
- **Richardson’s coastline paradox**, developed in Mandelbrot’s fractal analysis: smaller measuring intervals trace more creeks, estuaries and irregularities → longer measured perimeter. A natural coast is fractal-like over relevant scales, not infinitely self-similar at every physical scale.
- Source maps **1:4,500,000 → 1:250,000**; larger-scale mapping captures finer detail. GIS analyses spatial data; LiDAR uses laser ranging for terrain; GPS positions, drones/aerial imagery and electronic navigation charts provide complementary information. The source’s list does not establish every technology was used in the official calculation; satellite altimetry mainly measures surface height/sea level.
## State and island comparison
| State/UT | Old km | Revised km |
|---|---:|---:|
| Gujarat | 1,214.70 | 2,340.62 |
| Tamil Nadu | 906.9 | 1,068.69 |
| Andhra Pradesh | 973.7 | 1,053.07 |
| West Bengal | 157.5 | 721.02 |
| Kerala | 569.7 | 600.15 |
| Andaman and Nicobar Islands | 1,962.00 | 3,083.50 |
| Puducherry | 30.60 | 42.65 |
- Gujarat remains longest **State** coastline; Tamil Nadu now exceeds AP. West Bengal’s estuarine complexity produces a large percentage revision; Kerala’s reported increase is about 30 km. The source’s Puducherry “−4.9 km due to erosion” is **not supported by the official comparison**, which shows an increase. Changes in measurement are not by themselves physical erosion/accretion.
## Policy and geomorphology
- Better spatial detail supports coastal surveillance, safe navigation, cyclone/tsunami evacuation, fisheries/port planning and mangrove/coral/estuary conservation. It reveals existing geography rather than automatically creating new ports, resources or patrol area.
- **EEZ is not proportional to measured coastline length**: UNCLOS rights depend on lawful baselines, distance rules and delimitation. A longer ruler-derived perimeter does not automatically enlarge maritime jurisdiction.
- **CRZ boundaries depend on demarcated High Tide Line and applicable notification**, not the national total; official clarification says this reassessment does not change CRZ jurisdiction. High-water/HTL definitions require tidal and regulatory context, not simply the highest wave ever recorded.
- Emergence: relative land uplift/sea-level fall; submergence: subsidence/sea-level rise. Raised beaches versus drowned valleys/rias are diagnostic examples; beaches, spits/lagoons can occur under several processes. Avoid the source’s blanket classification of all Kerala as emerging or every west-coast segment as tectonically submerged.
- Coast borders **Arabian Sea, Indian Ocean and Bay of Bengal**; nine States plus four coastal UTs. Current UT name is **Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu**, alongside Puducherry, Lakshadweep and A&N. Proposed ten-year measurement updates are a source-reported plan, not evidence every past decade was revised.

## June 28 map and clipping additions
- Embedded **1990–2016 shoreline-change map** distinguishes erosion, stable coast and accretion. It is **not the date range of the coastline remeasurement**, nor proof that every longer reported State shoreline physically accreted land.
- Newspaper table additionally gives revised **Maharashtra 877.00 km, Karnataka 343.30 km, Goa 193.85 km, Odisha 574.71 km, Lakshadweep 144.80 km and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu 54.38 km**. These complete the already recorded source comparison; keep State totals separate from islands/UTs.
- Clipping reports **2014 Surveyor General count 1,382**, other agencies/States **1,334**, then reconciled offshore islands **1,298 +91 lake islands =1,389**. The heading’s **seven-island increase** compares **1,382→1,389**, not 1,334. These counts exclude the many river islands; better identification/standardisation is **not evidence seven islands geologically formed**.
- Repeated text's Puducherry decline/EEZ proportionality/Kerala blanket emergence errors are already corrected above. Andhra port examples **Ramayapatnam, Krishnapatnam and Kakinada Gateway** illustrate maritime planning, not ports automatically created by a perimeter revision.

topics.title: Elephants: ecology, conservation and conflict
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Species and ecological role
- **Asian elephant: Elephas maximus**, found across 13 Asian range countries; India has the largest wild population. Source global **50,000–60,000/India over 60%** are approximate background estimates with varying denominators, not a new 2025 global census.
| Species | IUCN status |
|---|---|
| Asian elephant | Endangered |
| African savanna elephant | Endangered |
| African forest elephant | Critically Endangered |
- Asian elephant: Indian **Schedule I** protection; keystone/ecosystem engineer through seed dispersal, vegetation modification and habitat diversity.
- Herds are generally matriarchal; adult males often solitary/in bachelor groups. Gestation about **22 months**, calving intervals often **4–5 years**; reproduction can continue beyond 40. Tusks are modified incisors and do not regrow after complete loss; tusklessness occurs in some Asian males, so “only males have tusks” is not “all males are tusked”. Trunk muscle-count graphic is approximate, not a fixed anatomical census.
## Counts and conservation programmes
- **2017 India estimate: 29,964**, Karnataka highest, followed in the source by Assam/Kerala; do not label these as a completed May 2025 national estimate.
- **23–25 May 2025** embedded clipping: synchronised southern count concluded, using block/direct count, line transects and waterhole observation; rain affected final-day detection. Karnataka sites included Bandipur, Nagarahole, BRT, Bhadra, Cauvery and adjoining forests. A count exercise concluding is not publication of a final population; non-sighting at one site does not prove absence.
- **Project Elephant, 1992:** habitat/corridors, population assessment, conflict mitigation and State support. Elephant reserves may encompass protected forests and other lands; designation is not identical to a national park’s statutory regime.
- Source **32 reserves/latest Agasthyamalai** is stale: official **December 2023 counted 33**; Terai, UP, was another addition alongside Agasthyamalai, Tamil Nadu. [MoEFCC/PIB](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1986211&lang=2&reg=48).
- **MIKE = Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants**, CITES programme; roots in **1997** decisions and implementation from **2001**, rather than universally “launched 2003”. Source cites ten Indian sites, including Kaziranga/Nagarahole/Wayanad. [CITES programme](https://cites.org/eng/prog/mike/index.php/portal).
## Conflict and PYQ recall
- Habitat conversion and roads/rail/mining fragment corridors; crop attraction and blocked movement drive dangerous encounters, losses and retaliatory killing. Source “over 500 human deaths annually” is a dated broad burden claim, not an exact fixed annual total.
- Protect connected habitat, retrofit crossings/rail operations, early warnings, rapid response, compensation and community participation; control ivory/body-part trade and monitor disease.
- **2020 PYQ: (a) 1 and 2 only**—female herd leadership and gestation up to 22 months; 40-year-only calving cutoff false; Karnataka, not Kerala, led the relevant population estimate.
## June 2025: Kumki management and corridor correction
- **Kumki** means trained **captive Asian elephants**, working with mahouts in professionally managed capture/rescue, conflict response, veterinary support/patrol and training. They are not a separate species or a genetically domesticated elephant lineage.
- Source recalls **2024 Andhra Pradesh–Karnataka MoU** for deployment, expert teams, mahout training, veterinary SOPs, nutrition/health and knowledge exchange; Karnataka's **62 transfers** is a source-reported cumulative count, not proof all were newly deployed to AP or that conflict was solved.
- Embedded capture illustration depicts multiple elephants assisting veterinary-controlled restraint/transport, with named example **Khaleem** and **Madukkarai Maharaj**; its **7–8-year training** is illustrative, not a universal age/duration. Capture/relocation require animal welfare, trained staff, veterinary judgment and continued habitat/community measures.
- Correct repeated population **2017: 29,964**, not PDF **27,312**. Corridor count: **150 across 15 range States**, ground-validated in 2023 report, not source 138. [MoEFCC corridor report](https://moef.gov.in/uploads/2023/11/PE-Elephant-Corridor-of-India-2023.pdf).
- Graphic's “four main species” conflates Asian subspecies with species: **Indian/Sumatran are Asian elephant populations/subspecies; African savanna/forest are separate species**. Existing topic lists conservation statuses/gestation/ecology; no new completed national census is established here.
- Infographic recall: **Gaj Sochna app 2022, Gaj Yatra 2017, Haathi Mere Saathi 2011**, source **National Elephant Corridor project 2005**; names/years are source background, not proof statutory protection or nationwide success. **MIKE** timing correction already recorded.
- **IUCN**, membership union headquartered **Gland, Switzerland**; RedList threatened categories **Vulnerable, Endangered, Critically Endangered**. Old pink/green page conventions are not contemporary legal protection schedules.

topics.title: Schistura densiclava and Meghalaya cave biodiversity
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## May 2025 species description
- **Schistura densiclava**, freshwater stone loach, **Nemacheilidae**, described from **Krem Mawjymbuin, East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya**, in *Journal of Fish Biology*. Team included **D.K.B. Mukhim and Kangkan Sarma**; newly described does not mean newly evolved. [Primary description](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jfb.70092).
- **Troglophile:** cave-associated organism capable of living/reproducing in surface (**epigean**) environments; distinguish an obligate cave specialist/troglobite.
- Clipping reports collection about **60 metres inside** in a cold, flowing stream, approximately **18°C**, with low oxygen. Retains eyesight/pigment; pale yellow-green body, **14–20** grey-to-black bars and a thick dark dorsal-fin-base stripe reflected in its name.
- Reported sexual dimorphism: slimmer males, puffier cheeks/irregular markings; sturdier females with more consistent markings. Genetic/morphological evidence supports species distinction.
- Known distribution is limited to the cave system in this report; ability to survive above ground does not prove a broad wild surface distribution. Protect cave hydrology/water quality and carefully assess limestone extraction, disturbance and tourism. Endemism increases vulnerability without automatically assigning an IUCN category.

topics.title: Bharat Forecast System and local weather prediction
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Launch and resolution
- The May 26 issue previews launch “today”; MoES later confirmed **official launch 26 May 2025**. **Bharat Forecast System (BharatFS)**, developed by **IITM Pune under Ministry of Earth Sciences**, supports real-time numerical weather prediction. [MoES Parliamentary reply, 31 July](https://www.moes.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/08/d5741b4be405d5b111e04ea32d760b08.pdf).
- **6 km horizontal grid**, versus previous **GFS T1534 ~12 km**; **Triangular Cubic Octahedral (TCo)** dynamical grid improves terrain representation/filtering/conservation. Forecast cells can serve village/panchayat **clusters**, not a guarantee of an independently exact forecast for every household.
- “Highest resolution globally” concerns the announced **global operational model** comparison, not all regional/weather research models—some regional grids are finer than 6 km. More grid points do not by themselves ensure every small storm/fog event is correctly predicted.
## Infrastructure and use
- Source says **Arka installed 2023**: correction—**Arka at IITM Pune and Arunika at NCMRWF Noida were inaugurated September 2024**. IITM facility **11.77 petaflops**, NCMRWF **8.24**; HPC supports intensive modelling/data assimilation. [MoES inauguration](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2059397&lang=2&reg=48).
- Forecasting combines observations/satellite and real-time inputs, assimilation, atmospheric models and evaluation. Uses: local rainfall/temperature/wind advisories, crop/irrigation/harvest planning, reservoir management, transport/health preparedness and extreme-event warning.
- Cyclone/heavy rain/thunderstorm prediction supports flood/landslide risk assessment; a weather model is not itself a complete flood or landslide model. Last-mile alerts, local response plans, uncertainty communication and verification turn improved forecasts into safety benefits.
## May 27 clipping: forecast horizons
- The embedded report says improvements are largely visible in **short/medium-range rainfall forecasts (3–7 days)**; they do not automatically change month-ahead seasonal forecasts or ensure prediction of every sudden severe thunderstorm. Radar observations and specialised models remain important. Existing common notes cover launch, resolution and infrastructure.

topics.title: Mosura fentoni and Cambrian arthropod evolution
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Fossil and anatomy
- **Mosura fentoni**, radiodont described in **2025** from **Burgess Shale, British Columbia, Canada**; fossil age about **506 million years**, not automatically 540 million simply because it belongs to the Cambrian. Radiodonts are extinct early arthropod relatives, distantly related to modern insects, crustaceans and arachnids.
- Small, roughly **1.5–6 cm**, with **three eyes**, grasping/spiny jointed frontal appendages, toothed circular mouth and swimming flaps; source describes **26 trunk segments** differentiated into neck/mesotrunk/posterotrunk, six broad swimming-flap-bearing middle segments and up to **16 tightly packed gill-bearing posterior segments**.
- A **tagma** is a functionally specialised grouping of segments. Respiratory posterior region resembles solutions in horseshoe crabs/other arthropods through **evolutionary convergence**, not proof it is their direct ancestor or that horseshoe-crab tails themselves collect oxygen.
- Relationship near basal hurdiid radiodonts and specialised segmentation illustrate early diversity/flexibility in arthropod body organisation. Respiratory efficiency/habitat explanations remain hypotheses.
## Why Burgess Shale matters
- Exceptional soft-tissue preservation reveals nervous/digestive/circulatory anatomy; Mosura fossils preserve an **open circulation** with body cavities/lacunae. Collections comprised **61 specimens**, many collected decades before description. [Research museums’ announcement](https://www.rom.on.ca/news-releases/manitoba-museum-and-rom-palaeontologists-discover-506-million-year-old-predator), [primary paper](https://doi.org/10.1098/rsos.242122).
- Cambrian diversification around the early Cambrian produced many animal body plans; this later Cambrian animal helps investigate that evolutionary radiation, without moving all arthropod origins to one exact fossil date.

topics.title: Tamil Nadu Space Industrial Policy
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Policy status and aims
- **Tamil Nadu Space Industrial Policy 2025**; Cabinet approval **17 April 2025**, correcting the source’s **2024** label. Source describes it as the third State policy after Karnataka/Gujarat. Aim: **₹10,000 crore investment and 10,000 direct/indirect jobs over five years**—targets, not realised investment/jobs. [Official policy](https://storage.investingintamilnadu.com/Guidance/Uploads/Others/indus_policy.pdf), [official policy listing](https://www.investingintamilnadu.com/business-in-tamil-nadu/policy-notifications/tamil-nadu-space-industrial-policy-2025).
- Manufacturing/R&D, launch/satellite systems, space-grade electronics and services; supports startups/NGEs within **Indian Space Policy 2023** framework. IN-SPACe promotes/authorises non-government activity; ISRO research and NSIL commercial roles remain distinct.
## Why the State has an industrial base
- **ISRO Propulsion Complex, Mahendragiri, Tirunelveli:** storable/cryogenic engine and stage testing/development. **Kulasekarapattinam, Thoothukudi:** forthcoming second spaceport, not already fully operational in this issue.
- Existing precision-engineering/electronics vendor ecosystem, source **over 250 ISRO vendors**; **Space Technology Incubation Centre at NIT Tiruchirappalli**; **TIDCO–IN-SPACe MoU** links firms/startups and space-grade component manufacture.
- Local startups span launch/reusable-launch technology, refuelling, data fusion and satellite applications; examples do not prove all capabilities have completed flight qualification.
## Source-listed incentive tools and applications
- Payroll subsidies for R&D/global-capability centres; **Space Bay** districts with special packages for projects below **₹300 crore**; industrial housing support **10%, up to ₹10 crore**; green capital support **25%, up to ₹5 crore**. Eligibility/conditions govern entitlement, not automatic payment to every firm.
- Training for space-grade manufacturing/electronics/data systems; applications in agriculture, fisheries, disaster management, health, urban/revenue administration and transport.
- Assess targets against actual project commitments, skilled jobs, testing infrastructure, supply-chain quality, regulatory safety and research outcomes. The source’s “Aerospace and Defence Policy 2021” reference needs title/version checking rather than a new unquestioned historical anchor.

topics.title: India–Africa digital cooperation and public infrastructure
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Africa Day and development partnership
- **Africa Day, 25 May:** OAU founded **1963**; African Union’s **Digital Transformation Strategy 2020–2030** advances inclusive digital services/governance and capacity. [AU strategy](https://www.au.int/en/documents/20200518/digital-transformation-strategy-africa-2020-2030).
- Editorial proposes a new **India–Africa digital compact**, complementing lines of credit, infrastructure, scholarships and technical training with co-development/social enterprises. It is a recommendation, not a new continent-wide agreement already concluded.
- Indian examples: **Aadhaar** identity, **UPI** payments, **CoWIN** vaccination and **DIKSHA** education. DPI includes technology, institutions, standards and safeguards; it is incorrect to assume every component of every named Indian system is open-source merely because some reusable platforms are.
## Agreements versus deployment
| Partner | Initiative and qualification |
|---|---|
| Togo | **MOSIP = Modular Open-Source Identity Platform**, MoU with **IIIT Bangalore**, not “IIT Bangalore”; modular national-ID support, not Indian Aadhaar enrolment abroad |
| Zambia | Source reports **CDPI/IIIT-B collaboration with Smart Zambia**, co-creation and public-service digitisation; cooperation is not proof every system is nationally deployed |
| Namibia | **2 May 2024 NIPL–Bank of Namibia agreement** to develop a **UPI-like** instant payment system; local platform differs from simply linking to Indian UPI |
| Ghana | **May 2024** agreement sought operationalisation on **GhIPSS within six months**; target/announcement alone does not prove completed integration by May 2025 |
- [MOSIP Togo MoU](https://www.mosip.io/news_events/the-government-of-the-togolese-republic-sign-an-mou-with-iiit-b-on-mosip), [NIPL Namibia agreement](https://www.npci.org.in/PDF/npci/press-releases/2024/NPCI-International-Partners-with-Bank-of-Namibia-for-Deploying-India%E2%80%99s-UPI-Stack-in-Namibia.pdf), [Ghana dated announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2019724&lang=2&reg=48).
- **IIT Madras Zanzibar**, first overseas IIT campus, inaugurated **6 November 2023**, offers data science/AI education; scholarships/industry partnerships support skills rather than automatically resolving the continent’s workforce gap. [IIT Madras](https://www.iitm.ac.in/happenings/press-releases-and-coverages/iit-madras-zanzibar-campus-inaugurated-his-excellency-dr).
## Conditions for inclusion and sovereignty
- Expensive devices/data, rural and gender access gaps, unreliable power and limited skills impede uptake. Reliable energy/connectivity, local-language access, training and sustainable operations accompany software.
- Open standards and adaptable platforms can reduce vendor lock-in and enable local control; they do not automatically eliminate surveillance, privacy or exclusion risks. Consent/legal safeguards, cybersecurity, accessible offline alternatives and public accountability matter.
- Co-design with African institutions, interoperability and durable local capacity can strengthen healthcare, education, payments and governance. Avoid portraying all African countries as one market or all competing models as necessarily surveillance-heavy.

topics.title: ONGC discoveries and hydrocarbon development
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## May 2025: Mumbai Offshore discoveries
- ONGC announced **Suryamani**, OALP-VI block **MB-OSHP-2020/2**: initial tested oil **2,235 barrels/day**, gas **45,181 m³/day**; **Vajramani**, OALP-III block **MB-OSHP-2018/1**: oil **2,122 barrels/day**, gas **83,120 m³/day**. These are discovery/well-test rates, not assured sustained commercial production or reserve volumes. Suryamani zones reported as **Basal Clastics/Mukta Formation**. [Parliamentary confirmation of discovery tests](https://www.sansad.in/getFile/annex/268/AS81_Uc8uMN.pdf?source=pqars).
- Source additionally reports **Yandapalli-1**, **Malleswaram petroleum mining lease**, onshore Krishna–Godavari basin, depth **3,958 m**. Appraisal and development economics still determine recoverable reserves and production timing.
- Mumbai Offshore includes **Mumbai High, Bassein, Heera, Neelam, Panna–Mukta**; map places these in the Arabian Sea west of Maharashtra. Source shares **35% oil/18% gas** lack a reference year; do not treat as current fixed national contributions.
## Policy and implications
- **HELP/OALP** permits companies to identify acreage and submit expressions of interest; identified blocks are then offered through **competitive bid rounds**. “Bid anytime” wrongly conflates EOI submission with unrestricted continuous auctioning. [DGH process](https://www.dghindia.gov.in/assets/downloads/67bc6bc3dfe6fiews.pdf).
- Potential benefits: domestic supply, foreign-exchange savings, investment/employment and infrastructure. Source's **~85% crude/~50% gas import dependence** are indicative dated ratios, not all-energy dependence.
- **Discovery → appraisal → development approval/investment → infrastructure → production**. No clear source development timetable; slower ramp-up is an analyst assessment, not a demonstrated failure. Financial-results/dividend announcement does not establish project commercial readiness.

topics.title: Marine oil spills: Kerala response and pollution control
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## 25–27 May 2025: MSC ELSA 3
- Liberian-flagged **MSC ELSA 3**, Vizhinjam → Kochi, sank **25 May** off Kerala. Source reports oil/chemical risks, nine containers reaching Kollam/Alappuzha beaches, **643 containers including 13 calcium-carbide containers**, and local fishing/shoreline restrictions. Calcium carbide reacts with water to release flammable acetylene; do not handle washed-up cargo.
- Different location descriptions occur: PDF **38 nautical miles off coast**; **26 May Coast Guard release about 15 nautical miles southwest of Alappuzha**. Retain attribution rather than invent one reconciled position. Oil sheen and hazardous cargo risk do not imply every stored tonne/chemical had leaked. [ICG response](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2131395&lang=2&reg=48).
## Effects and institutions
- Oil pollution: uncontrolled petroleum release from ships, drilling, pipelines/operational discharges or disasters. **Deepwater Horizon 2010** illustrates offshore failure; source cites Uran pipeline spill 2013 without detailed verification.
- Oil coats/smothers organisms, affects light/photosynthesis, habitats and reproduction; birds/mammals lose insulation, fish suffer toxic/gill effects. Seafood/surface-contact risks, fisheries/tourism losses, cleanup costs and port/shipping exposure matter particularly for India’s long coastline and coastal livelihoods.
- **MARPOL 1973/1978 annexes:** I oil; II noxious liquids in bulk; III harmful packaged substances; IV sewage; V garbage; VI air pollution. **OPRC 1990** concerns preparedness/cooperation; **CLC 1992** concerns qualifying tanker persistent-oil damage, not every container-ship spill. **Bunkers Convention 2001** concerns ship-fuel liability; source's “India ratified 2015” is unverified and must not be learned as fact. [IMO treaty information](https://www.imo.org/en/KnowledgeCentre/ConferencesMeetings/Pages/MARPOL.aspx).
- **NOS-DCP 1996**, updated including 2015: ICG national coordination; ports/oil facilities and States have defined local/shoreline roles. Merchant Shipping Act 1958, environmental law and port rules underpin relevant duties. Pollution-response resources at Mumbai/Chennai/Port Blair/Vadinar, vessels/aircraft, **INCOIS trajectory/online oil-spill advisories** and drills support response. [Response arrangements](https://www.itopf.org/knowledge-resources/countries-territories-regions/india/).
- **NATPOLREX-IX 2023, Vadinar/Gulf of Kutch:** contingency-plan validation, inter-agency capability and environmental protection. Source's “annually since 2009” should not be assumed without event-series verification. **SACEP** regional cooperation applies to South Asian seas; **Nairobi Convention** is Western Indian Ocean regional framework, not automatically India's regional treaty.
## Control: distinguish recovery from degradation
| Method | Function/constraint |
|---|---|
| Booms | Contain floating oil; waves/currents limit effectiveness |
| Skimmers/sorbents | Mechanically recover or absorb oil; disposal/handling required |
| Dispersants | Break slick into droplets; transfer exposure into water column and require case-specific assessment |
| Bioremediation | Microbes degrade hydrocarbons; temperature/oxygen/nutrients affect performance |
| Shoreline cleanup/surveillance | Protect responders; monitor trajectories and avoid damaging sensitive habitats |
- **TERI Oilzapper** is a bacterial consortium; claimed 2017 Chennai deployment is source-reported, not proof of universal success. **IIT Guwahati superhydrophobic cotton/MOF composites** are **oil–water separation/sorption**, not themselves biological degradation. IIT's related 2023 silica-coated cotton work illustrates the mechanism. Cold-adapted bacteria such as **Cycloclasticus/Paraperlucidibaca** illustrate research possibilities, not a ready treatment for every spill. [IIT separation research](https://www.iitg.ac.in/iitg_press_details.php?p=68%2Fiit-guwahati-develops-an-eco-friendly-method-to-mitigate-dual-environmental-hazards-biomass-burning-and-marine-oil-spills).
- **PYQ 2023:** define oil pollution → ecological mechanisms → India's livelihood/coastal-economy vulnerability → prevention, rapid response, liability and restoration.

## 9–11 June: MV Wan Hai 503 fire
- Separate from MSC ELSA 3: **Singapore-flagged Wan Hai 503** suffered explosions/fire on **9 June 2025**, about **88 nautical miles off Beypore, Kozhikode**; drifting vessel, hazardous cargo and floating containers created fire, navigation and marine-pollution risks.
- June 11 PDF reports **157 hazardous-cargo containers**, including resin solution, benzophenone, alcohol-wetted nitrocellulose and printing ink. Its approximate **2,000 tonnes marine oil + 240 tonnes diesel** should not be confused with a verified quantity released; official June 11 response reports **2,128 metric tonnes of fuel** onboard.
- **11 June:** Coast Guard winched five salvage personnel and an aircrew diver onto the burning vessel to prepare towing. Salvage, firefighting, search/rescue and pollution prevention are distinct but coordinated tasks. [Coast Guard update](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2135826&lang=2&reg=48).
- IMDG recall: **Class 3 flammable liquids; 4.1 flammable solids; 4.2 substances liable to spontaneous combustion; 6.1 toxic substances**. Radioactive material is Class 7. Source's drift speeds are transient incident estimates, not fixed properties of the vessel.
- MARPOL diagram dates: Annexes I/II entered into force **2 October 1983**, III **1 July 1992**, IV **27 September 2003**, V **31 December 1988**, VI **19 May 2005**; adoption of a convention differs from entry into force.

topics.title: Arms transfers: diversification and supplier dependence
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Changing South Asian procurement
- India has diversified historically substantial USSR/Russian procurement towards France, Israel/US and domestic manufacture; Pakistan increasingly depends on China, with Turkish UAVs alongside Chinese air systems. Source cites Pechora/OSA-AK, SkyStriker and PL-15 in recent operations; procurement origin is distinct from independent verification of battlefield performance.
- Embedded charts concern particular **decades/categories**; never mix shares of air-power transfers, all arms imports, recipient imports and exporter destinations. Source's Russian 75%, Pakistan–China 95%, US global 65%, China<2% lack stable common periods and should not replace verified 2020–24 figures.
- **SIPRI 2020–24:** Russia **36%** of India's major-arms imports (55% 2015–19,72% 2010–14); China **81%** of Pakistan's imports. Global export shares **US 43%, Russia 7.8%, China 5.9%**. SIPRI major-arms transfer-volume measures are not total defence spending or invoice values. [SIPRI 2024 transfer report](https://www.sipri.org/publications/2025/sipri-fact-sheets/trends-international-arms-transfers-2024).
- France/Rafale, US/GE-F414 and Israeli drone/surveillance cooperation illustrate diversification; agreements and technology-transfer ambitions are not completed domestic production. Legacy Russian equipment still needs spares/maintenance; new import shares do not equal installed-inventory shares.
- Strategic implications: supply resilience, interoperability, quality, lifecycle costs, sanctions/export controls and strategic autonomy. Ukraine-related Russian constraints are one factor, not the sole cause of all historical shifts. Indigenous capability/defence diplomacy complements diversified supply.
- Undated practice answer supplied **B(2 only)**; statement 3's unbounded air-power claim and supporting percentages need category/year clarification, so retain as practice with caveat, not official PYQ.

topics.title: Electric freight locomotives and Dahod manufacturing
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## 26 May 2025: Dahod milestone
- PM inaugurated Dahod locomotive manufacturing plant/flagged off the first **9,000 HP** locomotive, Siemens technology partnership. Source names **D9**, and reports~90% technology made in India and component facilities at Nashik, Aurangabad/Mumbai; technology sourcing is not automatically audited local-value content. [PM event](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2131273&lang=2&reg=48).
- Graphic programme targets: **1,200 locomotives over 11 years; 9,000 HP; 120 km/h maximum speed; 4,500 tonne haulage illustration; 35 years maintenance**. Targets/design ratings do not mean all delivered or routine operation at maximum speed; load depends on route/gradient and operating conditions.
- **“India's most powerful electric freight engine” is false unqualified:** **12,000 HP Madhepura locomotives** operated commercially from 18 May 2020. D9 is a powerful six-axle category; distinguish from double-section WAG-12B. [Railways 2020 announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1625158&lang=2&reg=48).
- Benefits: freight capacity/productivity, domestic manufacturing/employment, predictive maintenance and potential shift from road to lower-emission rail. Electrification reduces direct exhaust; total emissions depend on electricity mix. National Rail Plan freight-share ambition **45%** is a target, not achieved share; PM Gati Shakti promotes integrated logistics.
- Undated example's supplied answer A relies on incorrect “most powerful” statement 1; on its wording, only statement 3 is supported and **no offered option is valid**. Do not copy A into official PYQs.

topics.title: AMCA: fifth-generation fighter development
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## 27 May 2025: execution model approved
- Defence Minister approved **Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) programme execution through industry partnership**. **Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA)** executes the programme; public/private Indian companies may compete independently or in consortia, with equal opportunity. **HAL is not the automatically selected manufacturer**; collaboration model does not mean HAL and every private bidder already won contracts. ADA to issue an expression of interest for development partners. [MoD approval](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2131528&lang=2&reg=48).
- Source reports **March 2024 CCS development approval, roughly ₹15,000 crore**; first prototype **2028–29**, induction **2034** are projected milestones, not completed aircraft or assured delivery dates.
## Design concepts and technology
- Intended **twin-engine, 25-tonne class fifth-generation stealth fighter**, internal weapons bay, low-observable shaping/materials, diverterless supersonic intake and advanced avionics/sensor integration. Internal weapons reduce radar signature; external carriage adds payload while compromising stealth. Stealth reduces detection probability, not invisibility.
- Source indicative load figures **1,500 kg internal weapons/5,500 kg external/6,500 kg internal fuel**; load configuration and fuel are not interchangeable categories. Inset includes **17.6 m length,11.13 m wingspan,25,000 kg maximum takeoff weight, ~Mach 2.15,20,000 m ceiling,1,620 km combat-range claim**: development-design figures need configuration/testing confirmation, not operational specifications.
- **Mk 1 planned GE F414 engines**; higher-thrust indigenous/co-developed engine envisaged for Mk 2. Source's **Safran** collaboration is an option/discussion, not a final delivered co-developed engine. Generation labels (including inset's fourth/4.5/fifth examples) are broad capabilities shorthand, not a universal legal classification.
## Strategic assessment
- China's J-20/FC-31/J-35 developments motivate capability planning; source's Pakistan J-35 “acquisition” should not imply verified delivery/operational induction as of this issue.
- Opportunities: aerospace R&D, skilled employment, supplier ecosystem, composites/avionics/propulsion learning, dual-use spillovers and reduced long-term import dependence. Foreign engines still create supply/technology dependencies.
- Challenges: engine maturity, stealth integration, testing/certification, funding, transparent procurement and public/private production capability. Stage-gated milestones, realistic timelines, sustained R&D and carefully structured technology collaboration matter.
- **Undated practice:** statements 1 and 3 supported; statement 2 wrong because ADA leads, with competitive industry partnership—answer **(c) 1 and 3 only**.

topics.title: Dugongs and seagrass conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Species, habitat and status
- **Dugong dugon**, sea cow: herbivorous marine mammal, related to manatees; depends on shallow sunlit coastal **seagrass**, unlike manatees that also inhabit freshwater. Long-lived (recorded 73 years), slow reproduction makes small populations vulnerable. **IUCN Vulnerable; Wildlife (Protection) Act Schedule I**; regional Indian threat descriptions differ from global Red List category. [CMS species facts](https://dugong.cms.int/about/faq-dugong).
- Indian distribution: **Gulf of Mannar/Palk Bay, Tamil Nadu; Gulf of Kachchh, Gujarat; Andaman and Nicobar**—not the entire coastline. Inset estimates India~250 and Australia~85,500/Arabian Gulf~7,300 without matching survey dates; avoid treating these as current exact counts.
- Seagrasses (**Cymodocea, Halophila, Halodule, Thalassia**) are **flowering plants, not seaweeds**. Stabilise sediments, shelter fish/turtles and store blue carbon. Source's dugong intake **20–30 tonnes/day is an obvious unit error**; retain feeding dependence without this figure. “Low nutrients” alone is not a complete dietary-selection explanation.
- Grazing can affect meadow renewal/carbon dynamics, but “farmers of the sea” is a metaphor, not proof every grazing intensity increases carbon sequestration. Source **516.59 km² national seagrass/434.9 tonnes CO₂/km²/year** needs survey/method qualification; distinguish carbon stock from annual uptake.
## Protection and community response
- **India's first Dugong Conservation Reserve**, notified **21 September 2022**, **~448 km² Palk Bay** off Thanjavur/Pudukkottai. Source's 448.3 and 122.5 km² healthy-seagrass figures are more precise reported estimates, not the reserve's universal habitat coverage. TN Forest Department, WII/OMCAR conservation work supports mapping, monitoring and fishers' participation. [Tamil Nadu notification account](https://www.dugongseagrass.org/media/2022/09/2022-09-21-PalkBay-Dugong-Reserve-Govt.-Press-Release.pdf).
- India **CMS party since 1983**; signed **Dugong MoU 28 May 2008**. MoU originated 2007; distinguish India's signature date from instrument creation. [CMS signatories](https://dugong.cms.int/signatories-and-range-states).
- Threats: dredging/ports/reclamation and turbid polluted runoff destroy meadows; gillnets/trawling cause bycatch/drowning; hunting, boat strikes, contaminants and climate-related disturbance compound risk. Persistent mercury/organochlorine exposure is a source concern, not proof every Indian dugong is contaminated.
- Recommended: map/restore seagrass, regulate damaging fishing/boating/development, support alternative livelihoods, train fishers in sightings/strandings, community education/ecotourism safeguards, research/population/genetic monitoring and appropriate tracking/drone/citizen-science tools. Source's blanket gillnet/trawl ban is a recommendation, not proof a nationwide ban enacted.
- **PYQ 2015 answer (c) 1 and 3:** herbivorous marine animal + Schedule I protection; entire-coast statement false.

topics.title: Phosphoric acid: fertilisers and battery supply chains
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## May 2025: proposed plant
- Embedded clipping: **Caitlyn India Private Ltd**, not Cairn, proposes **₹400 crore,50,000 tonnes/year integrated phosphoric-acid plant** in a port-accessible southern Indian industrial zone. Site under evaluation; **30–50 acres**, proposed **FY 2027 commissioning**, hemihydrate–dihydrate process and captive sulphuric-acid unit; initially fertiliser supply, possible future own NPK facility. Rock imports envisaged from **Morocco, Jordan, Egypt**. This is an announced investment/commissioning plan, not an operating plant or achieved output.
## Chemistry and uses
- **H₃PO₄**, colourless inorganic acid, non-combustible but corrosive/irritating at relevant concentration. Phosphorus **atomic number 15**; allotropes have different structures, so inset's single body-centred-cubic descriptor should not be generalised to all elemental phosphorus.
- Usually produced from phosphate rock by wet acid treatment; purification/thermal routes yield different grades. Plant phosphorus is essential for roots, energy transfer and reproduction.
- Uses: phosphate fertilisers (including downstream DAP/NPK), feed supplements, phosphate/polyphosphate industrial chemicals, detergents/cleaning/metal-treatment and food-grade acidulant/dental applications. Industrial acid is not automatically food/battery grade.
- **LFP—lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO₄)** cathodes need phosphorus feedstock; battery-grade purification demand may compete for supply, but acid is not itself the entire battery/cathode and not every EV uses LFP.
## Resources and policy
- Major phosphate resources are **sedimentary marine phosphorites**, with significant **igneous deposits** too; source's all-organic-seafloor definition is incomplete. **Morocco** holds the largest reported reserves; reserve, resource and annual production ranks differ. [USGS phosphate summary](https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2023/mcs2023-phosphate.pdf).
- Source cites Indian production mainly **Rajasthan/Madhya Pradesh**, limited supply and acid imports from **Jordan, Morocco, Senegal, Tunisia**; exact shares require year/product definitions.
- Manage fertiliser affordability/food security alongside battery supply diversification, domestic processing/purification, resource efficiency/recycling and safe handling. Growing battery demand creates a potential allocation/price pressure, not evidence an actual fertiliser shortage caused by this proposed plant.

topics.title: PFAS: persistence and bioaccumulation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## 2024 PYQ revision
- **Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS)** are a large group of synthetic chemicals used in many products/processes, valued for resistance to water/oil/heat. Carbon–fluorine bonds make many highly persistent; “forever chemicals” is shorthand for slow environmental breakdown, not literal infinite lifetime.
- PFAS can contaminate drinking water, food and food packaging; continued exposure can cause accumulation of certain PFAS in people/animals. Persistence, mobility, bioaccumulation and toxicity vary across compounds; do not attribute identical risk to every member. **Phosphoric acid is not PFAS**—the source places an unrelated chemistry PYQ after its section. [EPA explanation](https://www.epa.gov/pfas/pfas-explained).
- **PYQ 2024 answer (d) 1, 2 and 3:** widespread occurrence, not easily degraded, and persistent exposure can lead to animal bioaccumulation. Consider exposure controls, source substitution, monitoring and suitable water/waste treatment.

## Exposure and regulation
- Additional source examples: non-stick cookware, stain-resistant textiles/carpets, food packaging and firefighting foams; industrial use includes aerospace, automotive, construction and electronics. Water, food and airborne particles can transmit exposure.
- PFOS and PFOA are listed under the **Stockholm Convention**. Different PFAS have different persistence, accumulation and toxicity profiles; avoid treating every compound as equally toxic.
- The issue's “nearly 20 bacteria break down PFAS” claim is unsubstantiated here. **Binding/bioaccumulation is not chemical degradation**; do not infer a proven bacterial cure or safe disposal method. The 2024 PYQ's three statements about occurrence, persistence and bioaccumulation are all correct.
- Health associations for studied PFAS include reproductive/developmental effects, hormonal/immune disruption, raised cholesterol and some cancers; associations depend on compound and exposure, rather than every exposure causing disease. Pollution pathways can include industrial waste, firefighting foam and maternal transfer via placenta/breast milk; prevention focuses on sources and exposure monitoring.

topics.title: Urban overnutrition and prevention of metabolic disease
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Study evidence and indicator corrections
- **Scientific Reports,24 March 2025**: cross-sectional sample of **345 Hyderabad IT employees**, recruited voluntarily, assessed during **July 2023–July 2024**; **84.06% liver fat/MAFLD,70.72% obese** under the study's Asian BMI criteria. Associations with sedentary work, diet/sleep and metabolic risk support workplace prevention, but not a representative estimate for all IT workers or India, nor proof one factor caused disease. **MAFLD is the paper's terminology; common MASLD note explains the current nomenclature.** [Original study](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-91482-2).
- Undernutrition and overnutrition can coexist in any income/location group; source's rural poor/urban affluent contrast is illustrative, not exhaustive. Food environments, activity, sleep, stress and access matter alongside individual behaviour.
- Source NFHS figures **~7% younger men→~32% men 40–49** concern **overweight or obesity**, not necessarily obesity alone. **46.1% urban men/43.1% urban women** are cited for **high waist-to-hip ratio**, not BMI-defined urban obesity; do not conflate measures. Wealthiest~37% vs poorest~10% is source-reported overweight/obesity gradient requiring age/sex cohort.
- Source Tamil Nadu STEPS 2023–24: **94.2% low fruit/vegetable intake,31.6% overweight,14.2% obese**, and **16% hypertensive patients on care controlled** needs precise denominator. These State/cohort indicators are not national rates. WHO **74% global deaths in 2019 from NCDs** is dated; premature mortality threatens SDG 3 and working-age productivity.
## Integrated prevention
- Workplace routines: activity breaks, healthy food choices, sufficient rest, appropriate screening/referral; urban design: walkability, parks and active commuting. Improve labelling/marketing safeguards, nutrition education, and surveillance without stigma.
- **Tamil Nadu Makkalai Thedi Maruthuvam** doorstep chronic-disease services; clipping reports **3.79 lakh workers screened 2024**. Health walk/Eat Right activities are associated initiatives, not proof all screened patients controlled disease.
- **FSSAI Eat Right India/Aaj Se Thoda Kam** promote safer healthier intake. **Front-of-pack health star rating** is a proposed/debated regulatory approach; do not present a nationwide notified mandatory scheme as implemented. Existing labelling/advertising rules mean “unrestricted marketing” is too absolute.
- Saudi comparator includes source-reported **100% energy drink/50% sweetened drink excise**, calorie disclosure, sodium limits and trans-fat measures. Assess fiscal/regulatory mix and implementation, not automatic transfer of all Saudi outcomes. [Saudi tax framework](https://zatca.gov.sa/en/RulesRegulations/Taxes/Documents/Commodities%20Subject%20to%20Excise%20Tax_ENG_v.01.pdf).
- Nutrition tax, mandatory workplace checks, urban surveillance and stronger HFSS labelling are editorial recommendations. Source's **450 million overweight/obese adults in 2050** is a projection, not current count; **244% rise/121% future childhood growth** need matched periods/cohorts. Claimed WHO/PHFI quotation attributions are unverified; do not use as authenticated quotes.

topics.title: India–Germany relations and strategic cooperation
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Partnership timeline and priorities
- **Strategic partnership since 2000 →25th anniversary in 2025**, not 2024. **1974 S&T intergovernmental agreement →50 years in 2024**; keep the two anniversaries separate. **7th IGC 25 October 2024, New Delhi**, co-chaired by Modi/Scholz; source May 2025 editorial reflects continued cooperation amid German leadership transition. [Joint statement](https://www.auswaertiges-amt.de/en/newsroom/news/2681720-2681720).
- **Innovation and Technology Partnership Roadmap** covers renewable energy, startups, semiconductors, AI/quantum, climate risk/resource management/agroecology, with space cooperation potential. **IGSTC** funds collaborative research; **WISER—Women in Science and Engineering Research** supports participation. Source 49 priority projects is a dated programme count, not universal current total.
- **Green and Sustainable Development Partnership 2022:** German **€10 billion commitment through 2030**, not all already spent; solar/renewables, green hydrogen, agroecology and urban mobility cooperation. **ISA/CDRI** engagement supports climate/disaster resilience.
## Economic, people and security links
- Germany is a major European trade/investment partner; source **US$33.33 billion 2023 trade, US$14.5 billion FDI April 2000–December 2023/9th rank** are historical snapshots, not May 2025 current shares. Verify goods/services and equity/total FDI definitions before comparisons.
- Skills/student/migration links and India’s market support cooperation; Germany's China exposure motivates diversification, but “China+1” is not complete economic disengagement. Clipping notes roughly 2,000 German companies/750,000 jobs and 50,000 Indian students without common latest cutoff; treat as reported context.
- **Defence cooperation agreement 2006**; naval/air exercises **MILAN, PASSEX, TARANG SHAKTI** and industrial dialogue. **Project-75I interest** concerns potential collaboration for six conventional submarines, not a concluded delivered deal. Cyber/counterterrorism and classified information/MLAT cooperation deepen institutional ties.
## Challenges and options
- EU CBAM exposure, tax/regulatory predictability, supply-chain risks, China ties and Ukraine-policy differences affect cooperation; source's human rights concerns require specific attributed evidence rather than a blanket indictment.
- **June 2024 Chinese EV tariff 38.1%** was a provisional-era source figure, not a timeless final tariff. India–EU FTA was under negotiation at this issue; do not treat recommendation as completed agreement.
- Priorities: conclude balanced trade arrangements, facilitate mobility/research, expand sustainable technology and Indo-Pacific cooperation, diversify semiconductor/pharma/EV supply chains while preserving strategic autonomy.

topics.title: Nurdle spills and marine plastic pollution
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Kerala spill: 29 May 2025
- The embedded clipping links pellets on Thiruvananthapuram beaches to the sunken **MSC ELSA 3**; local observations identified mainly **LDPE/HDPE**. Volunteers, drone surveys and State pollution-control rapid-response teams were mobilised; crew rescue did not remove the continuing environmental risk.
- **Nurdles** are pre-production plastic pellets, commonly about **1–5 mm**; used for packaging, containers, pipes, films and other products. Polyethylene, polypropylene, polystyrene and PVC pellets differ chemically and in buoyancy; not every pellet floats.
- Losses during manufacture, handling/storage and transport enter drains → rivers → sea; shipping accidents can create concentrated coastal deposits. The **2021 X-Press Pearl disaster off Sri Lanka** illustrates large-scale pellet loss; the issue quotes about **1,680 tonnes** as a contemporary estimate.
- Pellets are **primary microplastics**; further fragmentation generates smaller micro/nanoplastics rather than complete biodegradation. They contaminate habitats, may be ingested by wildlife and can carry additives or sorbed pollutants. Injury, reduced feeding and toxic exposure depend on species, dose and conditions.
- The source's **230,000 tonnes/year, 11.5 trillion pellets, 220 species, second-largest source after tyre dust and 600 pellets/bottle** figures lack a consistent methodology/year. Retain the pollution mechanism rather than treating these as universal measured constants.
- Finding microplastics in human samples does not establish they came from this spill, or prove a quantified disease burden/inevitable biomagnification. Nurdles' physical and chemical hazards matter even when the base polymer is not inherently acutely toxic.
- Prevention is essential, but early shoreline containment and carefully supervised cleanup remain useful; “cleanup is impossible/prevention is the only solution” is too absolute. Protect nesting/feeding habitats and avoid harming organisms during recovery.
- The source's “no IMO rules” is misleading: **MEPC 81 approved 2024 recommendations** on packaging, declaration and stowage of pellets in freight containers. These were **non-binding recommendations**, distinct from a comprehensive mandatory pellet-specific regime; wider container-safety requirements already existed. [IMO guidance](https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/oceans-default.aspx).
- Response priorities: spill/source inventory, shoreline/drift monitoring, safe collection/disposal, wildlife and food-safety assessment, transparent public communication, shipper accountability and stronger loss-prevention standards.
## PYQ revision
- **2019 microbeads:** **(a)** marine-ecosystem harm. Microbeads used in some personal-care products differ in intended use from industrial nurdles, although both contribute to microplastic pollution.
- **2022 PET:** **(a), 1 and 3**—polyester fibres can blend with wool/cotton; bottles can be recycled. “Any alcoholic beverage” is too sweeping, and PET incineration produces greenhouse gases. Suitability depends on food-contact standards and conditions rather than a universal alcohol threshold.

topics.title: Wild boar, vermin declarations and conflict management
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Kerala request and legal distinctions
- The May issue reports **Kerala's request** for wild-boar vermin notification and greater decentralisation of wildlife-control authority to Chief Conservators of Forests. A State request is not a Union notification or completed statutory amendment.
- **Wild Life (Protection) Act, section 62:** the Union may notify a **Schedule II** wild animal as vermin for a **specified area and period** under the revised schedules; relevant protection changes only within that notification's scope. The PDF's **Schedule III wild-pig** reference uses the older schedule arrangement. [Current Schedule II](https://upload.indiacode.nic.in/schedulefile?aid=AC_CEN_16_18_00007_197253_1517807324579&rid=760).
- Do not conflate section 62 with **section 11 authorisation** for a specific dangerous/diseased animal, or read either as unlimited permission to kill any wildlife. The Chief Wildlife Warden/authorised officers must follow statutory conditions, reasons and safeguards; mere apprehension is insufficient.
