- Wild boar **Sus scrofa**, family **Suidae**: adaptable omnivore, native to Eurasia/North Africa; rooting, crop-raiding and potential attacks create forest-fringe conflict. Widely introduced/feral populations can damage ecosystems outside the native range; activity can be nocturnal or vary with disturbance. IUCN global status **Least Concern** does not remove Indian statutory protection.
- **Sus scrofa cristatus** is the Indian wild-boar form; the source incorrectly equates it with both the **Andamanese pig** and **Moupin pig**. Do not treat those names as interchangeable. Sariska, Bandhavgarh, Corbett and Ranthambore are useful occurrence examples, not an exhaustive distribution.
- The map distinguishes historical notifications in parts of **Uttarakhand/Bihar** from requests in **Gujarat/Maharashtra/Himachal Pradesh**; these are not proof every old authorisation remains operative in 2025. Check species, place and expiry of each notification.
- Pair evidence-based population/conflict assessment with fencing, crop protection, compensation, habitat/waste management, community reporting and humane legally authorised intervention. Broad culling needs ecological and effectiveness scrutiny.
## PYQ revision
- **2022 wildlife-law question: (b), 2 only**, correcting the source's **(a)**. Protection follows a protected animal outside a sanctuary; section **39**, not section 3, deals with specified government-property circumstances, so “all wild animals are sole government property” is overbroad. Mere apprehension of danger does not justify capture/killing.
- **2020 musk deer: (a), Askot and Gangotri** in the Uttarakhand Himalaya. **Kishanpur** is Uttar Pradesh's Terai and **Manas** Assam's foothills; neither is the best natural-habitat match for this question. Musk deer are **Moschus** species, distinct from wild boar.

topics.title: Dholes and cooperative carnivore conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Species and May 2025 zoo context
- **Dhole/Asiatic wild dog: Cuon alpinus**, family Canidae; native to Asia, with Indian populations in suitable forest landscapes. Social packs hunt cooperatively, including medium/large ungulates; their ecological role involves prey regulation, alongside interactions with tigers/leopards and other carnivores.
- **IUCN Endangered**; major pressures include habitat fragmentation, prey depletion, persecution/conflict and infection from domestic dogs. Protect connected habitat/prey, monitor populations and manage dog-related disease interfaces.
- The clipping highlights specialised dhole enclosures at **Indira Gandhi Zoological Park, Visakhapatnam**, describing the largest Indian **zoo/captive** collection at the time. This does not mean the zoo contains India's largest wild population; numbers/rank are dated reports. Breeding/awareness complement in-situ protection rather than replace it.
- Under the revised Act schedules, dhole appears in **Schedule I**, correcting the PDF's present-tense Schedule II claim. The older Schedule II Part II system also should not be collapsed into today's two-animal-schedule structure. [Current Schedule I](https://upload.indiacode.nic.in/schedulefile?aid=AC_CEN_16_18_00007_197253_1517807324579&rid=759).
- **2017 tortoise PYQ: (a), same statutory protection level as tiger**. Schedule I listing does not mean extinct in the wild, captive-only or endemic. Statutory listing and IUCN assessment are separate systems; lawful exceptions remain governed by the Act.

topics.title: Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Constitutional office and May 2025 vacancy
- The issue notes no Deputy Speaker throughout the **17th Lok Sabha (2019–24)** and continued vacancy in the **18th Lok Sabha as of May 2025**. **Article 93** obliges the House to choose a Speaker and Deputy Speaker as soon as may be; there is no specified numerical deadline, but prolonged vacancy raises constitutional accountability concerns.
- **Election:** Lok Sabha members choose one of themselves by the ordinary voting majority; **Rule 8** lets the **Speaker fix the date**. No separate oath beyond the MP's oath is prescribed. Deputy Speaker is an independent constitutional officer, not the Speaker's subordinate.
- **Article 94:** ceases on losing membership; resigns to the **Speaker** (Speaker resigns to Deputy Speaker); removal requires a majority of **all the then members**, an **effective majority excluding vacant seats**, with **at least 14 days' notice**. Correct the PDF's “absolute majority of total sanctioned membership”.
- **Article 95(1):** during Speaker-office vacancy, Deputy Speaker performs duties; if **both offices are vacant, the President appoints a Lok Sabha member** for that purpose. **95(2)** addresses absence from a sitting, with provision for other authorised/House-chosen members. Thus vacancy does not create the PDF's claimed absolute inability to preside.
- **Article 96:** presiding officers cannot preside over consideration of their own removal. **Articles 178–180** are State Legislative Assembly counterparts; **180(1) does not govern Lok Sabha**. [Constitution, Part V](https://www.mea.gov.in/Images/pdf1/Part5.pdf), [Lok Sabha FAQ](https://sansad.in/ls/faq).
- When presiding, the Deputy Speaker has the same procedural powers as Speaker; constitutional voting provisions and removal proceedings still require their own distinctions. Speaker's survival in office until immediately before the first sitting after dissolution should not be automatically attributed to Deputy Speaker.
- Committee roles depend on rules: Deputy Speaker heads a committee when appointed to it under the relevant chairmanship rule; **Rules Committee is chaired by the Speaker**, so “Deputy Speaker automatically chairs the Rules Committee” is wrong. [Lok Sabha Rules](https://sansad.in/uploads/Rules_of_Procedures_E_9d8fd0f4c3.pdf?updated_at=2022-).
- Opposition occupancy is a convention promoting bipartisan trust, **not a constitutional eligibility rule**, and historical practice has exceptions. Electing the office supports continuity, balanced procedure and impartiality; allegations of a precise motive for delay are editorial inference, not a judicial finding.
- Historical recall: **Sachchidananda Sinha**, first Central Legislative Assembly Deputy President (**1921**); **M. Ananthasayanam Ayyangar**, first elected Lok Sabha Deputy Speaker (**1952**). After Mavalankar's death (**1956**), Ayyangar performed Speaker duties and was elected Speaker during the **first** Lok Sabha, then continued in the second—not first elected only in the second.

topics.title: Keeladi archaeology and Sangam literature
topics.subject: Ancient and Medieval India
topics.markdown:
## Site and dating
- **Keeladi/Keezhadi**, **Sivaganga district, Tamil Nadu**, near Madurai on the **Vaigai**: excavated by ASI and subsequently the Tamil Nadu archaeology department. Brick buildings, wells, pottery, beads, metalworking evidence and inscribed sherds illuminate settlement, crafts and literacy.
- The State department reports carbon samples dated to about **580 BCE (sixth century BCE)**, earlier than the PDF's blanket fifth-century-BCE start. A dated organic sample establishes its archaeological context; it does not directly date every inscription, structure or the entire site to one year. Link stratigraphy, sample association and independent tests. [Tamil Nadu archaeology account](https://www.tnarch.gov.in/node/1257).
- Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions and graffiti are different evidentiary categories; graffiti should not automatically be read as deciphered writing. Urbanisation, craft production and exchange are supported by material finds, but literacy rate, every literary event and specific Roman links require their own evidence.
- The map also distinguishes **Porunai/Tamiraparani** sites **Sivagalai and Adichanallur**, near Tirunelveli, from Vaigai-basin Keeladi. Its Sivagalai offering-pot paddy/husk result is reported as about **3,200 years old**, approximately **1200 BCE**, not the same date as Keeladi. ASI excavated Adichanallur earlier; State work in these southern sites began in **2020** according to the graphic.
## Read the literature critically
- Early historic/Sangam Tamilakam is conventionally studied around **third century BCE–third century CE**, with debated composition/compilation dates and earlier archaeology; this is an approximate literary-period framework, not a uniform lifespan of every site/text.
- Traditions describe **three Sangams** under Pandyan patronage: first **Madurai**, second **Kapadapuram**, third **Madurai**. Treat these as later literary tradition, not three independently verified historical academies with securely established dates.
- **Tolkappiyam**, traditionally attributed to **Tolkappiyar**, is an early surviving Tamil grammatical/poetic work: **Ezhuttu (letters), Col (words), Porul (subject matter/poetics)**. Its date/layers are debated; the tradition linking it to the second Sangam is not settled archaeological fact.
- **Ettutogai (Eight Anthologies): Ainkurunuru, Natrinai, Akananuru, Purananuru, Kuruntokai, Kalittokai, Paripatal, Patirruppattu**. **Akam** treats interior/love themes; **puram** public life, warfare, generosity and fame.
- **Pattuppattu (Ten Idylls)** includes **Tirumurukarruppatai, Perumpanarruppatai and Maduraikkanchi**. **Patinenkilkanakku** comprises eighteen mainly didactic works, generally associated with the post-Sangam tradition; **Tirukkural**, Thiruvalluvar: **aram, porul, inbam** (virtue, wealth/polity, love).
- **Silappatikaram — Ilango Adigal; Manimekalai — Sattanar**: later Tamil epic traditions, not securely contemporaneous eyewitness accounts of all Sangam events. Religions, ethics, social ideals and economy can be studied through them with critical dating.
- **Chera, Chola, Pandya**, smaller chiefs, cultivation, crafts and trade appear in literature; women poets and varied social roles are significant, but do not infer universal gender equality or a hierarchy-free society. Much poetry concerns everyday life, yet “entirely secular” is too sweeping given religious themes.
- Combine textual genres and archaeological evidence; the literary geography of Tamilakam should not be reduced to every territory south of Krishna/Tungabhadra or projected as today's State boundaries.

## June 27 news listing
- Source flags a **Keeladi controversy** but provides no substantive accompanying report in this issue. Keep dating/stratigraphic qualifications above; a contents question alone does not establish a new archaeological finding.

topics.title: Meerkats and cooperative behaviour
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Species recall
- **Suricata suricatta**, mongoose family **Herpestidae**, order **Carnivora**; small diurnal mammal, not a rodent. Global IUCN status **Least Concern** does not imply every local population is free of pressures.
- Southern African dry/open habitats, especially **Botswana, Namibia and South Africa**, extending into southwestern Angola; **Kalahari** is a key landscape. The PDF's Lesotho occurrence should not be memorised without a supported range record. [San Diego Zoo species account](https://animals.sandiegozoo.org/animals/meerkat).
- Social groups/mobs show cooperative care, grooming and sentinel calls during foraging; group size varies, often around the source's **20–30** example. Sentinel behaviour is useful in studying cooperation/kin selection, but describing it as pure self-sacrifice oversimplifies benefits and risks.
- Burrows provide shelter, escape and thermal buffering. Mainly insectivorous, with scorpions, small vertebrates and plant material also eaten; **Carnivora taxonomy** does not imply an exclusively meat diet.
- Resistance to some venom and handling skills are not immunity to every snake/scorpion toxin. Habitat degradation and inappropriate pet trade are concerns; sight, alert communication and group vigilance help predator detection.

topics.title: Tobacco affordability, taxation and cancer prevention
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Dated burden and affordability
- **GATS-2, India 2016–17, adults 15+: 42.4% men, 14.2% women, 28.6% overall** currently used tobacco. These are survey-period rates, not measurements made in May 2025. Smoking and smokeless products have different patterns; the source's global **70% smokeless-user share** needs a defined dataset/year. [WHO factsheet](https://cdn.who.int/media/docs/default-source/ncds/ncd-surveillance/data-reporting/india/gats/gats-india-2016-17-factsheet.pdf?download=true&sfvrsn=59fbdbff_2).
- WHO-supported study estimates **₹177,341 crore** economic costs from tobacco-attributable disease/deaths among people **aged 35+ in 2017–18**, about **1.04% of GDP**: roughly **74% smoking/26% smokeless**. Direct care, morbidity/productivity and premature mortality costs are included. This is neither a measured 2025 annual loss nor the cost of all cancer alone. [WHO account](https://www.who.int/india/news-room/detail/09-02-2021-india-loses-1-of-its-gdp-to-diseases-and-early-deaths-from-tobacco-use-finds-who-study).
- Low unit prices, single-stick/sachet sales, rising purchasing power, product substitution and tax undershifting can sustain affordability. Prices by pack, stick and sachet are not interchangeable; source **₹1–₹5**, **₹5–₹95**, **87% vendors**, **450-million middle class** and **88-country ban** claims lack a consistent national sample/year.
- Tobacco causes oral, lung and other cancers and cardiovascular/respiratory disease; second-hand smoke harms non-users. **India is not first worldwide for all male cancer incidence/mortality**—the source conflates site-specific oral-cancer burden with all cancers.
## Tax and wider policy
- WHO benchmark **at least 75% of retail price in total taxes** is a tax-*share* indicator. A proposed **35% GST slab** is an ad-valorem rate with a different denominator and ignores other taxes/cess; the PDF's direct 35-versus-75 comparison is invalid. Proposal reporting does not establish enactment as of this issue. [WHO tax benchmark](https://www.who.int/europe/health-topics/tobacco/promoting-taxation-on-tobacco-products).
- Taxes should raise real prices faster than income growth, cover product substitutes, and limit evasion; assess burden alongside reduced disease/household spending and accessible cessation. Manufacturer price responses mean tax-rate change does not ensure equal retail-price change.
- Single-stick restrictions, plain packaging, stronger zoning and earmarking taxes are **recommendations here**, not all newly enacted universal rules. COTPA already restricts sales to minors and within **100 yards of educational institutions**; “near every tea stall” is not the existing nationwide statutory rule.
| MPOWER | Measure |
| --- | --- |
| M | Monitor tobacco use and prevention policies |
| P | Protect people from tobacco smoke |
| O | Offer help to quit |
| W | Warn about tobacco dangers |
| E | Enforce bans on advertising, promotion and sponsorship |
| R | Raise tobacco taxes |
- Combine tax, warnings, smoke-free enforcement, marketing controls, youth protection, cessation and surveillance. Protect policymaking from tobacco-industry interference; tobacco farming/export revenue and public-health harm are distinct policy dimensions.

topics.title: Sikkim: statehood and constitutional integration
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Fiftieth anniversary in May 2025
- Sikkim became India's **22nd State on 16 May 1975**, through the **Constitution (36th Amendment) Act, 1975**. The clipping reports a **29 May 2025** virtual golden-jubilee address advocating tourism/sport; a vision of becoming a global hub is not an achieved ranking. [Sikkim government account](https://www.sikkim.gov.in/media/news-announcement/news-info?name=Prime+Minister+Mr+Narendra+Modi+Virtually+Addresses+Sikkim%E2%80%99s+Golden+Jubilee%2C+Commends+State%E2%80%99s+Progress).
- Namgyal monarchy began in the **seventeenth century**, headed by the **Chogyal**. The **1890** Anglo-Chinese Convention recognised British protectorate arrangements; after independence, the **1950 India–Sikkim Treaty** formalised India's defence/external affairs/communications role while preserving internal autonomy. Do not treat 1947 alone as the treaty date.
- **1953 State Council** introduced limited representative governance; democratic agitation led by **Kazi Lhendup Dorji** and others culminated in the **1973** political crisis and tripartite arrangement. **Government of Sikkim Act, 1974** reshaped representative government.
- **35th Amendment Act, title year 1974**, received assent **22 February 1975** and commenced **1 March 1975**: added **Article 2A and the then Tenth Schedule**, association terms, one seat each in Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha and related **Articles 80/81** changes. The PDF's “associated State status/representation began in 1974” confuses the title year with legal commencement. [35th Amendment text](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/c7c27cef78844056fc4033c78c1131ea.pdf).
- **1975 referendum** supported ending the monarchy and integration; source's approximately **97%** refers to the reported vote share, not necessarily 97% of every resident. Preserve democratic/political context rather than treating the transition as an ordinary princely-State accession.
- **36th Amendment:** added Sikkim in the **First Schedule**, parliamentary representation, **Article 371F** special provisions; omitted **2A and the association-era Tenth Schedule** and removed related association references. This old Tenth Schedule is not today's **anti-defection Tenth Schedule**, inserted by the 52nd Amendment in 1985. [36th Amendment text](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/2a875dab390ddae1419f7f050ccd6ed0.pdf).
- Map: borders **Nepal, Bhutan and Tibet/China**, with **West Bengal** to the south. Himalayan connectivity, ecology, tourism and border stability support the strategic/federal relevance.

topics.title: Shangri-La Dialogue and Indo-Pacific defence diplomacy
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Singapore, 30 May–1 June 2025
- **22nd Shangri-La Dialogue**, organised by the **International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS)** in Singapore; annual ministerial/military/strategic dialogue begun in **2002**. It is an IISS-convened forum involving governments, not a treaty organisation or binding regional alliance. [IISS 2025 event](https://www.iiss.org/events/shangri-la-dialogue/shangri-la-dialogue-2025/).
- The 30 May issue reports **CDS General Anil Chauhan's planned participation** and bilateral engagement with military leaders from Australia, EU, France, Germany, Indonesia, Japan, Netherlands, New Zealand, Philippines, Singapore, UK and US. This pre-event itinerary is not proof every proposed meeting concluded. [Defence Ministry, 29 May](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2132230&lang=2&reg=48).
- Planned engagement with academia/think tanks included **future wars/warfare** and **defence innovation for future challenges**. Maritime security, cyber risks, terrorism, emerging technology and Indo-Pacific competition provide common discussion ground.
- Dialogue can clarify positions, build trust, sustain military contacts and identify cooperation; attendance does not itself settle territorial disputes or prove participants share identical strategies. India's maritime/Indo-Pacific partnerships can be presented without assuming a formal anti-China alliance.

topics.title: Civil-service recruitment and examination reform
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## 30 May 2025 editorial: two entry routes
- Newspaper-only clipping **“India Needs UPSC 2.0”**, by former RBI Governor **Duvvuri Subbarao**, proposes reducing entry-level age/attempt limits and creating an annual open competitive route into the IAS around **age 40–42**. These are **editorial proposals**, not announced UPSC rules.
- Argument: repeated preparation can create opportunity costs, financial/psychological stress and a **sunk-cost fallacy**; applicants continue because of past investment rather than current expected gains. Critique the incentive structure without assuming unsuccessful candidates lack ability or motivation.
- He recalls his **1972 batch**, approximately **80% first-attempt entrants**, as historical experience. This is not a representative measurement of today's cohort. His suggested **three attempts/age 27** differs from the current rules he discusses.
- **2025 ordinary/general-category framework:** age **21–under 32** on the prescribed reference date and **six attempts**, with category/disability relaxations. The clipping's “21–32” shorthand is not inclusive of attaining 32; eligibility depends on the official notification and category. [UPSC 2025 notice](https://upsc.gov.in/sites/default/files/Notif-CSP-2025-Engl-220125.pdf).
- Selection errors: potentially good administrators excluded and weaker performers selected; a competitive exam cannot perfectly predict decades of administrative performance. More attempts can reward exam technique as well as merit; tighter limits can disadvantage candidates with unequal education/resources or later opportunity.
- Proposed mid-career exam-based **permanent recruitment** would differ from small-number specialist **lateral-entry contractual posts**. Potential benefits: second chance, outside experience, diverse perspectives and reduced all-or-nothing early-career risk.
- Tradeoffs: fairness/reservation, assessable merit, seniority/training, career progression, recruitment capacity and representation. The author also credits young entrants' energy and past scheme innovations; reform should combine youthful talent with experience rather than assuming only one age group can govern well.

topics.title: Gene-edited sheep and CRISPR livestock research
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## May 2025 research milestone
- **SKUAST-Kashmir**, team led by **Riyaz Ahmad Shah**, reported India's first gene-edited sheep after four years of research. **CRISPR-Cas 9** targets **myostatin**, a brake on muscle growth; **~30% more muscle** is a reported/expected trait, not proof herd-wide commercial productivity or farmer-income gains. Similar muscling occurs naturally in **Texel** sheep. [University technology register](https://skuastkashmir.ac.in/TechnologiesDeveloped.aspx?id=Animal%2FFish).
- **CRISPR = Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats**; guide RNA directs **Cas 9 nuclease** to a DNA target, cutting it so cellular repair can disrupt/change sequence. Other tools include TALENs and zinc-finger nucleases.
- **Correction:** editing can delete, alter **or insert DNA**, including introduced sequences; “never foreign DNA” is false. Transgenesis is a particular genetic-modification route; gene editing is not scientifically outside all genetic modification. Crossbreeding combines inherited traits through mating and selection. [NHGRI](https://www.genome.gov/about-genomics/policy-issues/Genome-Editing/How-genome-editing-works).
- Somatic edits generally affect treated body cells; embryo/germline edits may be inherited. Off-target changes, mosaicism, animal welfare, heritability and food-safety require evaluation. No foreign gene does not automatically confer safety, consumer acceptance or exemption from regulation; **plant SDN exemptions cannot simply be applied to livestock**.
- Potential meat yield, disease resistance, wool/milk improvement and lower veterinary costs are broader research possibilities, not all traits demonstrated in this lamb. Research birth is distinct from authorised food-market release.
## Questions: revision corrections
- **2019 Cas 9 PYQ: (a)** molecular scissors.
- Source practice Q 2 marks “allows insertion of foreign DNA” false, but **can** insert DNA: as worded statements **1 and 2** are correct, answer **(A)** rather than supplied (B).
- Practice Q 3's blanket editing/modification divide is flawed; option (C) best matches source's intended non-transgenic case but is not a universal definition.

topics.title: GDP: measurement, growth and potential output
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Measurement
- GDP measures final production **within domestic territory** over a period. **Nominal** at current prices; **real** at constant prices; neither is a complete welfare measure.
- **GDP at market prices = GVA at basic prices + product taxes − product subsidies**. Output minus intermediate consumption is value added, requiring the tax/subsidy adjustment for GDP; income sums compensation/operating surplus/mixed income plus appropriate net taxes; expenditure **C + I + G + X − M**, with statistical discrepancies where reported.
- **NSO, MoSPI** quarterly/annual accounts. Informal production is estimated, **not wholly ignored**; coverage/measurement gaps persist. GDP does not directly show distribution, unpaid care, health, education or environmental depletion. Nominal growth may reflect inflation rather than additional real output.
## 30 May 2025 provisional estimates
- Source-series **2011–12 base**: **FY 2024–25 real GDP growth 6.5%; Q 4 7.4%**. Provisional release differs from later revised/base-year estimates. Annual slowdown can coexist with faster final-quarter growth. [NSO release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2132688&lang=2&reg=48).
- Embedded clipping: Q 4 agriculture **5.4%**, manufacturing **4.8%**; annual manufacturing **4.5%**, construction **9.4%**, Q 4 construction **10.8%**; annual household/PFCE growth **7.2% versus 5.6%** previous year. Compare annual with annual and quarter with quarter. Construction/consumption support contrasted with manufacturing weakness and global uncertainty.
## Potential GDP and PYQ reasoning
- Potential GDP = sustainable output at normal resource utilisation without persistent inflation pressure; labour/skills, capital, technology/productivity and institutional capacity determine it. Infrastructure, regulatory unpredictability, investment/finance, low farm productivity and skill deficits can constrain India; reforms must improve productive capacity, not only demand.
- **2015 GDP trends: (b)**: real growth rate did not steadily rise in the preceding decade, while nominal rupee GDP level did. Do not use post-2015 pandemic/demonetisation examples as evidence available to that question.
- Tax/GDP ratio is receipts relative to GDP; a fall can reflect rates/exemptions/compliance, composition or cyclical changes. It **does not logically prove slower growth or inequality**. Source's answer (a) is its given exam interpretation; avoid turning it into a universal economic identity. The question has no separate year label here, so held for review/practice rather than assigning a guessed year.
## June 2: fourth-largest economy claim and welfare
- May 2025 NITI Aayog statement refers to **IMF April 2025 projected nominal-dollar GDP**: India approximately **US$4.187tn**, narrowly above Japan **US$4.186tn** in the 2025 projection. **Forecast ≠ already completed national-accounts result**. Comparisons depend on fiscal/calendar conventions, exchange rates and revisions; PPP rankings are different. [IMF April database](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/weo/weo-database/2025/april).
- Total output helps assess market scale, but **per-capita GDP, distribution, job quality, health, education and ecological costs** determine living conditions. Embedded India/Japan/Poland charts compare agricultural versus industrial/service work, vulnerable employment, female participation, health and HDI; total-GDP rank does not imply corresponding welfare rank.
- Drivers: services/IT/telecom/finance; domestic demand; UPI/JAM/ONDC; investment/manufacturing facilitation through PLI, Gati Shakti, Make in India. Programme announcement is not proof every gain is caused by that programme.
- Constraints: large farm employment relative to value added, underemployment, skills/job mismatch, weak manufacturing depth, informal work, inequality and low research investment. Source shares **~45% farm employment/~18% GDP, ~16–17% manufacturing, >85% informal, youth UR15–18%** need year/age/reference definitions; farm share may be of GVA rather than GDP.
- **~$2,500 per capita/rank141/behind Bangladesh**, wealth shares **top1%=40% /bottom50%=3%**, and R&D international ratios are dated/source-specific estimates; do not mix income with wealth, or infer every comparison uses 2025. Its “2004–14 tripled /2014–24 doubled” nominal-dollar trajectory does not isolate real productivity or establish causes of slowdown.
- Source reports **~96% net FDI decline in FY2024–25**. Net flows deduct repatriation/disinvestment and outward investment; strong gross inflows can coexist with small net receipts. Repatriation need not mean only profit transfer or flight caused by policy uncertainty. [RBI annual report](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/AnnualReportPublications.aspx?ld=1247).
- Trade slowdown/tariffs, oil-import prices and financial uncertainty create external risks. Priorities: farm productivity/agro-processing, labour-intensive MSMEs/textiles/tourism, apprenticeships, health/education, competitive clusters/logistics, research and private R&D, predictable rules and efficient public investment.
- **UBI pilot** and subsidy/tax/land/labour reforms are editorial recommendations, not implemented national entitlements. Assess fiscal space, social protection and distribution alongside aggregate growth.

## July 2025 state-led growth forecast
- Source reports Morgan Stanley's **23 July 2025 “India's State-Led Economic Transformation”** forecast: India could become the **third-largest nominal-dollar economy by 2028**, reaching **$10.6 trillion by 2035** and contributing about **20% of global growth** over a decade. These are conditional forecasts, not achieved ranks. **$4.19 tn→$10.6 tn exceeds doubling**, correcting the PDF's arithmetic description.
- Reported leading state scorecard: **Maharashtra, Gujarat, Telangana**; most-improved over five years: **UP, MP, Chhattisgarh**. A projected **3–5 states above$1 tn GSDP by 2035** is distinct from an official realised GSDP estimate.
- Mechanisms: infrastructure/capital spending, supply-chain diversification, manufacturing/PLI, financial access and competitive federalism. Source's public capex comparison **1.6% GDP(FY 2014–15)→3.2%(FY 2024–25)** is its dated metric, not every government's combined expenditure.
- Risks: geopolitical/energy shocks, climate damage, insufficient quality jobs, inequality, volatile capital and poorly managed urbanisation. Existing notes' IMF projection qualification resolves the PDF's conflicting fourth/fifth-rank labels.

topics.title: Ahilyabai Holkar: rule, patronage and legacy
topics.subject: Modern Indian History
topics.markdown:
## Life, administration and cultural legacy
- **31 May 1725–1795**; Holkar ruler of **Malwa**, reign **1767–1795**, capital **Maheshwar** on the Narmada, not Pune. Married **Khanderao Holkar**; military/administrative training associated with father-in-law **Malhar Rao Holkar**; **Tukoji Rao Holkar** commanded forces.
- Reputation for public grievance hearings, justice, simple living and stable administration; supported childless widows' property rights and artisans/trade. The story that she executed her own son is **not sufficiently established here** and should not be memorised as documented history.
- Maheshwari weaving, support for women weavers, arts/literature; source lists **Moropant, Ananta Gandhi, Khushali Ram** as patrons' court associations. “Philosopher Queen” is a descriptive historical epithet, not a constitutional office or official investiture.
- Patronage of temples, ghats, roads and dharmashalas at **Kashi, Somnath, Gaya, Rameshwaram, Haridwar** and other pilgrimage sites. **Kashi Vishwanath reconstruction 1780** is a key architectural association; do not infer she built every original shrine.
## 300 th anniversary:31 May 2025
- Commemoration at **Jamburi Maidan,Bhopal**, jointly Culture Ministry/Madhya Pradesh; source announced PM attendance, exhibition and commemorative coin/stamp. Distinguish programme announcements from its historical biography. [Official announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2132707&lang=2&reg=48).
## Related social-reform PYQs
- **Vital-Vidhvansak,1888: Gopal Baba Walangkar**; Gandhi's Harijan 1933 and Ambedkar's Mooknayak 1920 are distinct.
- **Bethune/Hindu Female School,Calcutta 1849: secretary Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**. These questions relate to broader reform history rather than Ahilyabai's reign.
- Practice: Maheshwar was not a transfer from Pune; protect the difference between supported administrative facts and heroic anecdotes.

topics.title: Alternative investment funds and venture-capital migration
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Framework
- **SEBI (AIF) Regulations 2012**, privately pooled funds with a defined investment policy. **CategoryI:** venture capital, SME, infrastructure/socially beneficial funds; **II:** private equity/debt and other qualifying funds, generally no leverage except permitted operational purposes; **III:** complex/diverse strategies, potentially leverage/derivatives. **Category**, not “Type 1”, is the formal classification.
- AIFs may hold stocks/bonds; those securities are **not themselves AIFs**. Mutual funds and specified trusts/vehicles have separate frameworks. Industry body **IVCA** advocates for private-capital investors; it is not the regulator.
## Legacy VCF migration:May 2025 report
- **19 August 2024 SEBI circular** sets migration modalities for VCFs under **1996 rules** into the 2012 framework as **Migrated Venture Capital Funds**, a CategoryI sub-category. It is an **option under specified conditions**, not proof every existing fund was legally forced to migrate. [SEBI circular](https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/aug-2024/modalities-for-migration-of-venture-capital-funds-registered-under-erstwhile-sebi-venture-capital-funds-regulations-1996-to-sebi-alternative-investment-funds-regulations-2012_85914.html).
- Clipping reports **19 July 2025** deadline, simplified application/fee relief and low uptake; IVCA urges timely action to avoid last-minute liquidation/regularisation problems. Deadline is the then-reported window, not a completed migration count; benefits/requirements depend on applicable circular and scheme status.
## PYQ distinction
- Page 22 scanned investments question: **hedge funds and venture capital = two**; bonds/stocks are instruments. The handwritten “only three” marking is incorrect. **2025 year verified against official UPSC GS-I booklet, question 1** (the supplied clipping is question 31 in a different set). [Official paper](https://www.upsc.gov.in/sites/default/files/QP-CSP-25-GENERAL-STUDIES-PAPER-I-26052025.pdf).

## RBI investment directions: 29 July 2025
- For RBI-regulated entities investing in an AIF scheme: **individual contribution ≤10%** of scheme corpus; **all REs collectively ≤20%**. These are shares of the **AIF scheme corpus**, not of a bank's total assets. Effective **1 January 2026**, or earlier adoption through the RE's policy. [RBI directions](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=12886) (core July provisions; linked text later adds an October exemption, which is outside this issue period).
- Where an RE contributes **more than 5%** and the AIF has downstream **non-equity** investment in its debtor company, proportionate **100% provisioning** applies, capped at direct exposure under the rule. Purpose: curb evergreening and concentration while allowing legitimate investment; this is not a blanket AIF ban.
- AIFs raise funds **privately**, may be trusts/companies/LLPs; general minimum investment **₹1 crore**, with regulatory exceptions. Category label alone does not guarantee a fixed risk level.
- Repeated 2025 PYQ: **hedge funds + venture capital = two**; securities held by a fund are not themselves funds. **NBFC 2010 recall:** may acquire government securities, but cannot accept demand deposits; banking functions and permissions vary by NBFC category.

topics.title: Controller General of Accounts and government accounting
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Institution and functions
- **Principal accounting adviser**, **Department of Expenditure, Finance Ministry**; administers Union civil departmental accounting, distinct from constitutional **CAG external audit**.
- Official history locates departmentalisation/audit-account separation in **1976**, with the 1976 Act assented **8 April**; source “October 1975 established” is inaccurate. [CGA history](https://cga.nic.in/Page/History-of-Indian-Civil-Accounts-Organisation.aspx).
- Consolidates monthly/annual Union accounts; advises accounting principles/forms/manuals, receipt/payment administration, treasury/cash reconciliation with RBI and management accounting/fiscal analysis. Internal audit supports ministry financial control and scheme compliance; CAG/PAC scrutiny is a separate accountability channel.
- Audit-para/action-taken monitoring, **PFMS** financial information and civil-pension accounting/payment authorisation through relevant offices; not every central/defence/rail pension is directly disbursed personally by CGA.
- **Article 150:** President prescribes Union/State account form on CAG advice; Article 151 concerns audit-report submission. Do not turn CGA's administrative duties into an independent constitutional power overriding CAG.

topics.title: Bat organoids, cell models and pandemic preparedness
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## May 2025 experimental platform
- **Organoids:** self-organising 3 D cultures from stem/progenitor cells that reproduce selected tissue structures/functions; **not complete functioning organs**. **Cell lines:** maintained cell populations; not all are single-cell clones or immortal. Primary cultures have limited growth, while immortalisation permits sustained proliferation; **HeLa** and **Vero** illustrate established lines, not universally engineered immortalisation.
- **Kim and colleagues, Science, May 2025:** organoids from **five insectivorous bat species**, four organ types—**trachea, lung, kidney, intestine**—with mucus/goblet-cell and alveolar features. Species have wider Asian/European ranges, but sampled bats were captured in **South Korea**, not necessarily across both continents. [Original study](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.adt1438), [authors' account](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ctm2.70454).
- Tested **SARS-CoV-2, MERS-CoV, influenza A and Seoul orthohantavirus**; observed species/tissue-specific susceptibility and strong MERS replication in relevant models. Source reports SARS-CoV-2 infection enabled by introduced human **TMPRSS 2**, a cell-entry-related **protease**, not the main ACE 2 receptor. Results from selected cultures do not establish immunity of all bats or settle pandemic origins.
- Fecal-sample work identified **mammalian orthoreovirus and paramyxovirus**; detection/isolation in bats does not prove human pathogenicity or imminent pandemic spread.
- Separate **PLOS Biology study, 15 April 2025**, developed kidney/brain/liver/spleen lines from **Carollia perspicillata**, Seba's short-tailed **fruit bat**; tested MERS-CoV, vesicular-stomatitis and Andes orthohantavirus-related susceptibility/immune responses. **ATCC** distributes research biological resources. [Original study](https://journals.plos.org/plosbiology/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pbio.3003098).
## Applications, limits and India
- Disease/entry mechanisms, innate immunity, antiviral/toxicity screening and tissue-specific spillover assessment; organoids offer architecture while scalable lines support high-throughput experiments. Human intestinal/brain organoids also model disease and personalised treatment research.
- Bats support pollination, seed dispersal and insect control; some species host zoonotic viruses. **Nipah reservoir fruit bats** differ from the insectivorous study species; don't infer every bat carries every listed virus. COVID-19 origin and reservoir pathways are not conclusively determined by this experiment.
- Source India **120+ species**, limited virological data, Northeast **Ebola/Marburg-reactive antibodies** and an **April 2024 inter-ministerial initiative** are reported context; antibodies do not prove a local Ebola outbreak or exact infecting species/virus.
- Models reduce some live-animal handling but **infectious-virus culture still requires appropriate biosafety**, permissions and ethical oversight. Build One Health surveillance, BSL capacity, diagnostics and collaborative data sharing; laboratory susceptibility cannot alone predict future human transmission.

topics.title: Pulses: cultivation, imports and farmer incentives
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Crops and geography
- **Gram/chickpea/chana**, lentil/masoor and dry peas are chiefly **rabi**; **tur/arhar/pigeonpea**, moong and urad are important **kharif** crops, with cultivar/region-dependent summer/rabi cultivation. Gram and chana are the same crop, not separate pulse species.
- **Arhar also fixes atmospheric nitrogen** through root-nodule symbiosis: the source's exception is false. Pulse rotation can improve soil fertility, but actual fixation depends on plant–microbe/environmental conditions. [ICAR biofertiliser crop list](https://icar.gov.in/sites/default/files/2022-06/ICAR-technologies-Biofertilizers.pdf).
- Main producing States in source map: **Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka**. Its uniform **20–27°C / 25–60 cm rainfall** cannot describe every pulse/cultivar. India is a major producer/consumer/importer; map's **25% production/27% consumption/14% trade** are dated approximations with different denominators.
- **Yellow peas = dry Pisum sativum L.**, legumes used as dal substitutes/protein ingredients; rabi sowing approximately **Oct–Nov**, harvest **Mar–Apr**, well-drained loam. Source **15–25°C / 20–40 cm** indicative, **20–25% protein** approximate. Canada/Russia are important suppliers, with Ukraine, US, Australia, France/China also cited; exact producer rankings need year and dry-pea definition.
## 31 May 2025 yellow-pea extension
- Clipping announces free import **without minimum import price/port restrictions**, subject to online import-monitoring registration, for consignments with **bill of lading on/before 31 March 2026**; previous window ran to **31 May 2025**. This supersedes rewritten “February 2025/reimposed in 2024” account. Import-policy “free” and customs **zero duty** are distinct measures. [USDA report reproducing Indian notifications 31/2025 and 16/2025–26](https://apps.fas.usda.gov/newgainapi/api/Report/DownloadReportByFileName?fileName=India+Extends+Unrestricted+Imports+of+Yellow+Peas_New+Delhi_India_IN2025-0039.pdf).
- Source reports duty-free tur extended to **31 March 2026**; chickpea/urad/lentil decisions differ by notification/date. Do not treat its blanket “no decision yet” as a verified current status for every crop.
## Import–price trade-off and policy
- Source import totals **3.31 Mt (2023), 6.63 Mt (2024)** are stated all-pulse totals, not yellow peas alone; calendar/FY labels need reconciliation. Reported prices **urad down 25% from₹100/kg, turUS$1,400→800/t, yellow peasUS$700→450/t** are market/time-specific, not universal farmgate realisations.
- Imports may contain food inflation/bridge shortages yet depress local prices and planting incentives; cereal procurement/irrigation, rainfed vulnerability and weak seed/storage/processing can discourage pulses. Ethanol-driven maize competition is an incentive concern, not proof every farmer switched.
- **NFSM pulses:** demonstrations, seed production/hubs; source **28 States+2 UTs /150 hubs /343 varieties 2014–23** are programme-period claims, not new June achievements.
- **PM-AASHA/PSS** MSP procurement and price-support instruments have scheme-specific scope; listing PDPS/private procurement does not mean all apply identically to every pulse. **Budget 2025 six-year self-reliance mission** focuses **tur, urad, masoor**, resilient/productive seeds and procurement via **NAFED/NCCF**. Announcement/budget allocation differs from full field implementation.
- Recommended stable, consulted import policy, calibrated duties/quotas where justified, MSP access, storage/processing and location-specific R&D; weigh consumer affordability and farmer returns rather than assuming protection alone guarantees self-sufficiency.

## Green gram (moong)
- **Vigna radiata, Fabaceae**: short-duration pulse, commonly **60–75 days**, fitting rotations/intercropping with maize, sorghum, cotton or sugarcane. Kharif, rabi or summer/zaid cultivation varies by region.
- Warm conditions, well-drained loam/sandy loam; the source's **25–35°C, 600–750 mm rainfall and pH 6.2–7.5** are indicative agronomic ranges, not universal requirements. Waterlogging impairs growth/nodulation.
- Rhizobial fixation and residues can improve soil nitrogen; actual fertiliser savings depend on conditions. MSP/NFSM-pulses support is relevant; irrigation/organic programmes are complementary instruments, not a guarantee of doubled income.
- PYQ revision: urad can be both kharif and rabi; moong does **not** account for nearly half of Indian pulse output. The 2020 question's historical trend statement about declining rabi pulses is false; do not present its three-decade window as a newly measured July 2025 trend.

topics.title: IBBI and flexible corporate insolvency resolution
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## 26 May 2025 Fourth Amendment
- **IBBI (Insolvency Resolution Process for Corporate Persons) (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2025**, reported 30 May. **Resolution professional, with Committee of Creditors approval**, can invite expressions of interest for resolution of **the corporate debtor as a whole, sale of one/more assets, or both**. This facilitates parallel/part-wise options rather than waiting for value erosion; it does not guarantee every case resolves faster or authorise sale without process safeguards. [IBBI regulations/press-release register](https://ibbi.gov.in/en/).
- Potential broader bidding, viable-business preservation, realisation and flexibility; assess valuations, credible competition, creditor treatment, feasibility and actual timelines. EOI is a solicitation stage, not an approved resolution plan or completed sale.
## Institution and powers
- **Statutory IBC 2016 regulator**, established **1 October 2016**. Regulates insolvency professionals, professional agencies/entities and information utilities; registered-valuer oversight under delegated Companies-law framework. **NCLT adjudicates corporate cases**; IBBI does not personally adjudicate every insolvency or automatically apply every personal-insolvency provision universally.
- Board: chairperson; **three Central-government ex-officio members** representing Finance/Corporate Affairs/Law; **one RBI nominee**; **five nominated members, at least three whole-time**. Chairperson/other appointed-member tenure **five years or 65**, subject to statutory rules; do not apply it blindly to ex-officio representation.
- Distinguish **resolution** preserving viable value from **liquidation**, and regulator from professional/CoC/adjudicator. Better predictability/investor confidence are goals requiring evidence, not automatic consequences of notification.

topics.title: Osaka World Expo 2025 and Indian cultural diplomacy
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Expo and pavilion
- **13 April–13 October 2025**, Osaka/Kansai, Japan; theme **“Designing Future Society for Our Lives”**. World Expo organised as a six-month international exhibition, ordinarily on a five-year cycle; not every specialised Expo follows the same timing. “Living Lab”/co-creation approach links innovation and SDGs.
- India pavilion curated by **IGNCA**, autonomous Culture Ministry institution, narrates heritage/spiritual philosophy alongside contemporary scientific ambitions, inclusivity and sustainability. **Padmapani Bodhisattva from Ajanta**, lotus/Bodhi-tree imagery evoke compassion/mindfulness; the image is a cultural reference, not evidence Ajanta is in Japan. [Official pavilion](https://www.expo2025.or.jp/en/official-participant/india/).
- Source highlights space achievements and describes IGNCA as **sutradhar**, storyteller. Clipping **13,141 single-day visitors** is a dated footfall snapshot, not total Expo attendance. Curatorial responsibility differs from every construction/engineering contract.
## Soft power
- **Joseph Nye:** influence through attraction, culture/values and credible policy, distinct from coercion. Art, philosophy, cultural exchange, sustainability and scientific achievement can support international confidence.
- Exhibitions create contact/opportunity, not proof attitudes, investment or diplomacy changed. Assess accessible narration, plural heritage, contemporary relevance, visitor engagement and sustained partnerships.

topics.title: Confederation of Indian Industry
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Institution and June 2025 leadership
- **Non-government, not-for-profit, industry-led organisation**; roots in **Engineering and Iron Trades Association, 1895**; headquarters **New Delhi**. It collaborates with ministries but is **not a statutory body under Commerce Ministry**.
- **1 June 2025:** **Rajiv Memani**, EY India Chairman/CEO, became CII President **2025–26**, succeeding **Sanjiv Puri** of ITC. **R. Mukundan** president-designate; **Suchitra K. Ella** vice-president. These are dated officeholders, not permanently current. [CII announcement](https://www.cii.in/ResourceDetails.aspx?enc=fuONeJl+koEWm16Dm8dwCWaLLn+t+JiaJHKzW9AhyA4%3D).
- Functions: policy advocacy/industry consultations, competitiveness and entrepreneurship, skill/innovation platforms and centres of excellence, B2B/trade-investment missions, sustainability/CSR and inclusive development.
- Source's **300 partner organisations/100 countries** is a network snapshot, not treaty membership. Participation in WTO-related business dialogue does not make CII the sovereign trade negotiator. Its activities can intersect agriculture/consumer supply chains despite the PDF's overly absolute exclusion.

topics.title: Perito Moreno Glacier and Patagonian ice
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Map recall and change
- **Perito Moreno Glacier**, Patagonian Andes, **Santa Cruz, Argentina**, near **El Calafate**, terminates in **Lake Argentino**; part of **Los Glaciares National Park**, UNESCO World Heritage **1981**. Do not confuse it with the separately named Perito Moreno National Park. [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/145).
- Source dimensions **~30 km long /ice front ~60 m above water** are approximate; visible cliff height differs from total ice thickness. Southern Patagonian Ice Field contributes substantial freshwater storage; glacier dynamics include accumulation, flow and calving.
- The June source reports increasing ice loss after a long reputation for stability. Individual glacier trends require measurements and period-specific evidence; calving alone does not establish identical annual net loss everywhere.
- Source's “formed 18,000 years ago” is an unsupported exact age and misrepresents the long, fluctuating last glacial period. Preserve Ice Age landscape context without dating today's glacier to one universal formation year.
- Mains links: warming, freshwater systems, tourism and ecosystem management; climate trends and local geometry both influence retreat.

topics.title: Paraguay, MERCOSUR and India’s Latin American engagement
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## June 2025 visit and trade
- **Santiago Peña Palacios**, Paraguay President, began first State Visit to India **2–4 June 2025**. Diplomatic ties **1961**; resident Indian Embassy in **Asunción** opened **2022**. Discussed digital technology, critical minerals, energy, agriculture, health, defence, railways and space; proposed collaboration is not proof signed extraction projects or completed technology transfers. [MEA arrival](https://www.mea.gov.in/newsdetail1.htm?13564%2F=).
- **MERCOSUR = Mercado Común del Sur**, founded **Treaty of Asunción, 1991**; founders **Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay**. **Bolivia became a State Party in 2024**, with a transition to incorporate bloc rules; the source's pending-ratification label is stale. **Venezuela suspended**, not an active participating member. Secretariat **Montevideo**, Common Market Council includes foreign/economy ministers. [Official membership](https://www.mercosur.int/en/about-mercosur/countries).
- **India–MERCOSUR framework 17 June 2003; PTA signed 25 January 2004; entered into force 1 June 2009**, with negotiated annexes finalised later. **PTA means selected preferences, not comprehensive FTA/free movement with India**. [WTO treaty record](https://rtais.wto.org/UI/PublicShowRTAIDCard.aspx?rtaid=520).
- Diversify exports/markets, South–South cooperation and supply partnerships; tariff/non-tariff barriers, shipping/logistics and internal bloc differences matter. The source's GDP/population totals are dated and membership-dependent; Paraguay's supposed universally neutral foreign policy or readily available critical-mineral capacity is not established by a visit.
## Paraguay map
- **Landlocked South America**; neighbours **Brazil east/northeast, Argentina south/southwest, Bolivia northwest**, not Chile. **Asunción** on east bank of **Paraguay River**; river divides populous **Oriental east** from more sparsely populated **Gran Chaco west**.
- **Paraná River:** borders with Brazil and Argentina in respective stretches; **Itaipu** is Paraguay–Brazil hydropower project, **Yacyretá** Paraguay–Argentina. Do not place Itaipu on an Argentina-owned boundary merely because another Paraná stretch borders Argentina.
- River navigation links landlocked trade to neighbours/Atlantic; hydropower, soybean, beef and forestry feature in economy. **Lake Ypacaraí** near Asunción. Geographic partnership does not grant India automatic tariff-free access to the whole bloc.
## Map PYQ revision
- **2025 Andes: (c), four** among listed—Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Venezuela; not Brazil or Paraguay. Andes extend through western South America, also Peru, Chile and Argentina.

topics.title: Phytoplankton, iron deposition and ocean nutrient cycles
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Two different ocean studies
- **North Pacific transition zone, PNAS 2 June 2025:** anthropogenic atmospheric iron estimated at **39 ±9% of mixed-layer dissolved-iron sources** under studied spring conditions. East Asian emissions/westerly transport can stimulate blooms and advance nitrate/phosphate drawdown; **not 39% of all ocean iron everywhere**.
- Four **2016–19 expeditions**, trace-metal-clean sampling, iron isotopes, gene-expression/metatranscriptomics and satellite chlorophyll observations connect deposition to biological response. HNLC means **high nutrient, low chlorophyll**, often reflecting iron limitation. Chlorophyll is a biomass proxy, not direct proof of permanent carbon sequestration. [Original PNAS study](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2418201122).
- Separate **late 2019–early 2020 southeast-Madagascar bloom** linked to dust from drought-stricken southern African drylands, including Namib/Kalahari/Etosha source regions; atmospheric transport/deposition supplied nutrients. Do not transfer the North Pacific anthropogenic 39% estimate to this Indian Ocean event; source's **~2,000 km²** needs confirmation. [Original Madagascar study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11443548/).
- Warming-related stratification and nutrient supply interact; iron addition does not alone demonstrate that it directly causes all stratification. Changes in dust are region-specific, not proof storms must always become more frequent everywhere.
## Ecology and risks
- Phytoplankton include photosynthetic **diatoms, cyanobacteria and many dinoflagellates/algae**; primary producers supporting **phytoplankton → zooplankton → fish → predators**. Copepods and foraminifera are consumers in the exam distinction, although biological symbioses can occur.
- Marine photosynthesis contributes roughly **half global annual oxygen production**, not necessarily more than half the accumulated atmospheric oxygen stock. Much oxygen is consumed again by respiration/decay. Cyanobacteria are bacteria, not taxonomically true algae.
- Blooms may enhance food supply and carbon uptake; some species produce toxins, while decomposition can consume oxygen/hypoxia. **Not every bloom harmful**; durable sequestration depends on export/storage, not photosynthesis alone. Natural dust fertilisation is not automatically safe intentional geoengineering.
- **2012 PYQ: (a), statements 1/2**—destroying phytoplankton damages carbon sink and food chains, not drastically seawater density. Density chiefly varies with temperature/salinity/pressure. **2021 primary producers: (b), cyanobacteria and diatoms**.

topics.title: Subsea cables: digital connectivity and resilience
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Network and Indian geography
- Optical fibres carry encoded **light signals**; repeaters/support conductors maintain long-distance transmission. Nearshore armour/burial can reduce anchor/fishing damage; deep-sea design differs. Satellites complement rather than replace the bulk international backbone.
- Correct source's ambiguous **90% global data**: ITU describes **over 99% international data traffic** through submarine cables; this is not all domestic data. Source **$10tn financial flows /80% world trade** needs period/definition. [ITU February 2025](https://www.itu.int/en/mediacentre/Pages/PR-2025-02-27-submarine-cables-summit-nigeria.aspx).
- Mumbai/Chennai are major Indian gateways; **CANI Chennai–Andaman/Nicobar** and **Kochi–Lakshadweep** improve island connectivity. **17 international systems** is a legacy snapshot; systems, landing points, stations and traffic/capacity are different counts. Source **Mumbai 95% /1% stations /3% systems /6-km concentration** should not be treated as equivalent universal shares.
- **2Africa Pearls/SEA-ME-WE 6 landings** support new capacity, including planned **over 100 Tbps** for Pearls; landing does not mean all end-to-end links commercially active. [Airtel contemporaneous results](https://assets.airtel.in/static-assets/cms/investor/docs/quarterly_results/2024_25/Q4/Quarterly-IR-Pack-Bharti-Airtel-Consolidated.pdf).
## Resilience and strategic agenda
- Anchors, fishing, dredging, seismic events, route concentration and security threats can cause breaks. Source's attribution of **2024 Red Sea cable cuts specifically to Houthi sabotage is unproven here**; disrupted shipping/anchors and deliberate attack require separate evidence.
- Permitting, foreign repair-vessel dependence and storage/spares can delay restoration; **51+ approvals /3–5 months** are source case claims, not a fixed statutory count/service time.
- Proposed single-window clearance, diversified gateways **Visakhapatnam/Kochi/Thiruvananthapuram/Andamans**, domestic flagged repair vessels/depots, secure monitoring and PPP investment increase redundancy. These are recommendations, not all completed capacity.
- India–US/Quad partnerships can support trusted networks, cloud/data economy and Indo-Pacific links to Africa/Europe/Southeast Asia; assess data jurisdiction, provider diversity and emergency restoration. Ownership alone does not guarantee digital sovereignty.
- **38% demand growth in 2021–28** lacks CAGR-versus-total clarification; **$5 tn digital economy** is an ambition/source framing, not a verified realised sector size.

topics.title: Ladakh: domicile, reservation and local governance
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## 4 June 2025: new legal framework
- Following the **J&K Reorganisation Act 2019**, Ladakh is a UT without a legislature; J&K is a UT with a legislature. Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance have sought Sixth Schedule protection, employment/land safeguards and greater local autonomy; Sonam Wangchuk’s protests highlight tribal identity and fragile ecology.
- **2 June recruitment/reservation regulations; 3 June domicile procedure rules:** domicile routes include **15 years’ residence**, or **seven years’ study and appearance in Class 10/12 examination in Ladakh**; specified children of eligible long-serving Central-government personnel and family/spouse categories are covered. Exact categories/conditions follow the rules rather than an unlimited “any child/spouse” entitlement. Tehsildar issues certificates; Deputy Commissioner hears appeals; physical/electronic application. [Ladakh administration chronology](https://ladakh.gov.in/ut-administration-initiates-filling-vacant-posts-after-formalising-domicile-and-reservation-rules/).
- Reservation cap raised **50% → 85%**, with **10% EWS separate**, covering the prescribed recruitment/admission categories including professional institutions. Ceiling, category shares and implementation notifications are distinct; do not say 85% includes EWS or guarantees every applicant a post.
- **Official Languages Regulation:** English, Hindi, Urdu, **Bhoti and Purgi**; promotes **Shina, Brokskat, Balti and Ladakhi**. Official use is subject to the Administrator’s notified date; English continues for existing purposes. Recognition creates a legal framework, contrary to the source’s “without legal backing” phrase. [Gazette](https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2025/263538.pdf).
- **LAHDC amendment:** one-third seats in Leh/Kargil councils reserved for women by rotation. This does not convert councils into Sixth Schedule autonomous district councils.
## What remains unresolved
- Article **240** presidential regulations have **force and effect of parliamentary law**, not merely informal executive guidelines; they remain amendable and subject to constitutional review. They do not themselves entrench Sixth Schedule status or create a UT legislature.
- The package does not establish the comprehensive land/autonomy safeguards campaigners demand. Blanket assertions that every non-domicile may buy every parcel ignore existing land categories/restrictions; assess applicable law before claiming unrestricted access.
- Priorities: transparent recruitment/certificate delivery, funded multilingual administration, women’s participation, tribal/community consultation and ecological carrying capacity. Local job protection, land rights and constitutional autonomy are separate questions.

topics.title: Almatti dam and Krishna water sharing
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Project and dispute
- **Almatti dam, Krishna River, north Karnataka**, part of **Upper Krishna Project**; irrigation/storage and hydropower. It is not on Tungabhadra, which is a Krishna tributary.
- Upstream Karnataka’s height/storage increase raises downstream Andhra Pradesh water-availability concerns; reservoir operation, seasonal timing and allocations matter alongside physical height.
- Krishna basin spans **Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh**; distinguish basin membership from each stretch of main river. Do not extrapolate the source’s two-State Almatti focus into exclusion of Maharashtra/Telangana from the broader tribunal/legal dispute.
- **Article 262; Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956** support adjudication. An award on allocations/storage does not automatically supply all construction/environmental permissions; assess legal stage and implementation conditions.
- Comparators: Cauvery (including Karnataka/Tamil Nadu), Mahanadi (Chhattisgarh/Odisha), Ravi–Beas and Mullaperiyar (Kerala/Tamil Nadu, including dam safety). Shared rivers require dependable data, equitable use, drought coordination and transparent releases; every listed dispute has a different legal history.

topics.title: Nanozymes and experimental thrombosis prevention
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## 3–4 June 2025: IISc research
- **G. Mugesh’s IISc team** investigated **vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) nanozymes**, enzyme-like nanomaterials modulating reactive oxygen species. Physiological clotting limits bleeding; excess platelet activation/aggregation can contribute to thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.
- **Oxidative stress → excess ROS → platelet signalling/activation → aggregation**; antioxidant-enzyme mimic reduces triggers. This is **not direct thrombolysis of an existing clot**. Shapes/sizes were compared using isolated human platelets and agonists such as thrombin; spherical particles performed best in the source account.
- The published work also investigated **pulmonary embolism in mice**; human platelets in laboratory experiments are **not a human clinical trial**. [IISc announcement](https://www.iisc.ac.in/events/novel-nanozyme-prevents-excess-clotting/).
- Proposed next work on **ischaemic stroke** remains research. PTE, COVID-related clotting and stroke are potential disease contexts, not evidence of an approved drug curing each condition. Safety, biodistribution/dose and controlled efficacy studies precede clinical adoption; “non-invasive therapy” is not established merely by nanozyme chemistry.

topics.title: ECINET: integrated electoral digital services
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Development-stage platform
- **ECI announced ECINET on 4 May 2025**, envisaged after the March CEO conference: unify **40+ web/mobile applications** with simpler UI/UX and fewer logins, serving electors, officials, parties and civil society. This June issue describes **development/planned rollout**, not proof every service was already migrated. [ECI announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2126682&lang=2&reg=48).
- Includes **Voter Helpline, Voter Turnout, cVIGIL, Suvidha 2.0, Saksham, KYC, ESMS**; desktop/smartphone access envisaged. Officially authorised entry and primary legal records prevailing in a conflict aim to protect data integrity; integration alone cannot guarantee error-free data.
- Governing framework: **RPA 1950/1951, Registration of Electors Rules 1960, Conduct of Elections Rules 1961** and ECI instructions.
- Source estimated reach: about **100 crore electors**, **10.5 lakh BLOs**, **15 lakh BLAs**, **45 lakh polling officials**, **15,597 AEROs**, **4,123 EROs**, **767 DEOs**. These are announcement-era estimates, not proven active platform users; BLAs are party agents, not all government staff.
- Unified services should preserve accessibility, privacy, secure authentication, auditability and assisted/offline routes. Platform integration differs from conducting exit polls or itself altering substantive election law.
## 5 June 2025: proposed turnout reporting
- New clipping describes **presiding officers entering turnout every two hours directly into ECINET** on polling day, automatically aggregating constituency totals; planned use **before Bihar Assembly polls**. This is a rollout proposal, not proof it already operated in every election.
- Post-poll entry before officers leave aims to reduce previous four-to-five-hour reporting delays, subject to connectivity; offline entries should sync when service returns. Approximate turnout trends remain distinct from legally authoritative final records/counts.
- The June issue repeats other platform objectives/services/user estimates already covered in the preceding update. Timelier data needs clear revision rules, audit trails and secure authorised entry; technology does not change statutory record precedence.

topics.title: Polio vaccines and surveillance transition
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## 4 June 2025: network transition debate
- **WHO–India National Polio Surveillance Project began 1997**. Source reports phased NPSN reduction **280 units (2024–25) → 190 (2025–26) → 140 (2026–27)**, beginning June with lower funding and eventual integration into **IDSP**. These are reported transition plans, not evidence all closures happened on 4 June.
- WHO describes preserving essential functions and wider disease surveillance; Dr Jacob John argues withdrawal is premature given **Pakistan/Afghanistan WPV1 circulation**, importation risks and job insecurity. Staff transition and replacement capacity must be verified rather than treating assurances as completed implementation. [WHO transition framework](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/india-polio-transition-snapshot).
- Priorities: acute flaccid paralysis investigation, environmental/laboratory surveillance, high vaccination coverage, rapid response, trained workforce and sustainable financing. **Polio-free certification is not global eradication**.
## Disease and vaccine distinctions
- Poliovirus: **single-stranded RNA**, principally **faecal–oral/person-to-person** spread; mostly under-fives, but susceptible people of other ages can be infected. Many infections are asymptomatic; possible fever, fatigue, headache/vomiting/stiffness and irreversible paralysis. WHO approximate **1 in 200 infections paralysed; 5–10% of paralysed patients die when breathing muscles are affected**. No curative antiviral treatment; prevention and supportive/rehabilitative care remain essential.
- **Wild type 2 eradicated 2015; wild type 3 eradicated 2019; WPV1 remains. India’s last wild case 2011; WHO South-East Asia certification 2014**. Vaccine-derived viruses are a separate risk. [WHO polio facts](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/poliomyelitis).
| Vaccine | Distinction |
|---|---|
| **IPV/Salk** | Inactivated injected vaccine, strong protection against paralytic disease; cannot replicate/revert or cause VAPP. Less intestinal immunity than OPV is not simply “less potent” overall |
| **OPV/Sabin** | Live attenuated oral vaccine; strong gut/systemic response, easy mass administration; rare VAPP and, with prolonged circulation in poorly immunised populations, vaccine-derived-virus risk |
- **VAPP** is rare paralysis in a recipient/contact; **cVDPV** means evidence of community circulation of genetically evolved vaccine virus. Not all VDPV is type 2, and VAPP ≠ circulating outbreak. Source “40% of polio cases” lacks a denominator and “India does not classify VAPP as polio” should not erase real vaccine-associated paralysis. [WHO vaccine explanation](https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/poliomyelitis).
- Transition toward IPV/ultimate OPV cessation must be coordinated with eradication strategy; Dr John’s recommendation is not proof India stopped OPV in June. Both vaccine technologies require product-specific cold-chain/safety rules; no inactivated vaccine is automatically “risk-free”, and not every live vaccine is oral/nasal.
- Practice: **statement 1 only**; inactivated IPV cannot regain virulence, unlike replicating attenuated OPV-derived virus.

topics.title: Biohappiness, agrobiodiversity and opportunity crops
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Biodiversity → nutrition → livelihoods
- **M.S. Swaminathan’s “biohappiness”**: wellbeing from sustainable, equitable use of biological resources; **Evergreen Revolution** seeks enduring productivity without ecological harm. Agrobiodiversity includes crop/livestock/microbial diversity and associated knowledge.
- **Neglected and underutilised species (NUS), orphan/opportunity crops**: traditional foods with low research/market support. **Millets, jackfruit, amaranth, yams and tubers** offer dietary/resource-use opportunities, but resilience/nutrition vary by species and preparation.
- Source describes food/knowledge loss among **Nyishi/Apatani communities, Arunachal Pradesh**, and cash-crop shifts in **Kolli Hills, Tamil Nadu**. Crop concentration in rice/wheat/maize can reduce dietary and climatic resilience; it does not alone establish the cause of every NCD or unequal food distribution.
- India is one of **17 megadiverse countries**; portions of four hotspots: **Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats–Sri Lanka, Sundaland (Nicobar)**. Source rounded **2% land/8% biodiversity** uses species-based measures; “₹130 trillion/year forest services” lacks valuation baseline and should not be memorised as a realised annual income.
- **International Year of Millets 2023**, millet value chains/branding and **Odisha Millet Mission, including Koraput**, support producer-to-consumer links. “Shree Anna” is the policy label for millets; source “Shree Anna Yojana” should not imply one verified standalone national scheme with automatic benefits.
- Priorities: community seed systems, conservation/research of local varieties, women’s knowledge/participation, fair benefit sharing, appropriate inclusion of minor millets in PDS and nutrition programmes, processing/markets and soil health. Biodiversity science connects agriculture, ecology, nutrition and bioeconomy; potential jobs/health gains are not completed outcomes.

topics.title: Battery energy storage and clean-grid integration
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## BESS functions and units
- **BESS** combines rechargeable batteries, power-conversion/inverters, management/control and thermal/safety equipment; it is not simply an inverter. It stores electricity from grid/renewable sources and discharges for balancing, peak supply, backup and ancillary services.
- **MW = power; MWh = stored energy**. A **20 MW/40 MWh** system has about **two hours at rated power** before losses/reserves. Source “four hours daily” assumes separate charging/discharging cycles; this is not four uninterrupted hours at 20 MW from one charge.
- Lithium-ion is common; lead-acid/flow technologies have different cost/life/energy characteristics. Charging losses, degradation/cycle limits, capital cost, critical minerals, fire/thermal controls and recycling constrain deployment. Emissions benefits depend on charging mix; batteries do not create energy or automatically ensure cheap 24/7 electricity.
## Delhi project and policy chronology
- **Kilokri, South Delhi, BRPL project: 20 MW/40 MWh**, developed with **IndiGrid/AmpereHour and Global Energy Alliance** support. Source forecast “operational by March 2025” is old: project partner announced commercial operation/launch **8 May 2025**. The narrow claim is first utility-scale standalone commercial/distribution project, not India’s first battery installation of any kind. [Partner announcement](https://energyalliance.org/india-first-utility-scale-standalone-battery-energy-storage-system/).
- Source **12,000 low-income consumers** is a project-beneficiary estimate, not a guarantee each receives continuous backup from this battery alone. Renewable PPAs can provide charging energy; dispatch/settlement matters.
- **September 2023 VGF:** **4,000 MWh by 2030–31**, up to **40% capital support**; initial scheme outlay **₹9,400 crore includes ₹3,760 crore budget support**. Source conflates total outlay with grant support and gives conflicting 2026/2030–31 deadlines. [Cabinet decision](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1955112&lang=2&reg=48).
- **₹18,100 crore advanced-chemistry-cell PLI** supports manufacturing, distinct from deployment VGF. Source FY2023 **37 MWh** and **1.3 million tonnes annual avoided emissions** require scope/charging assumptions; neither proves current installed capacity or realised savings.

topics.title: Senior citizens: policy reform and assistive support
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## 4–5 June 2025: policy discussion
- **Fourth National Council for Senior Citizens meeting**, chaired by Social Justice Minister **Virendra Kumar**, discussed a new policy reflecting ageing, digital inclusion, NGO/senior associations’ involvement, elder-abuse redress, care-home standards and intergenerational/community bonds. It is **policy preparation**, not a newly implemented national policy. [Ministry meeting](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2133837&lang=2&reg=48).
- Source shares **8.23% (2011), projected 12.16% (2026), about 20% (2047)** require age definition/projection source; 2047 is a scenario estimate, not a Census finding. Plan health/care, income security, accessible services and representation without assuming all older people have identical needs.
- Council reviewed **RVY, Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSrC), Senior Citizen Portal**, quality/post-distribution support and coverage. Source “over five lakh beneficiaries” is a dated reported reach; do not also treat the same count as an unfulfilled target.
## Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana
- Launched **1 April 2017**, central-sector assistive-device scheme, Social Justice Ministry; **ALIMCO** implementation; source funding through Senior Citizens’ Welfare Fund.
- Eligible **60+** people with qualifying age-related impairments: BPL **or monthly income not exceeding ₹15,000**, correcting the source’s BPL-only summary. [Ministry eligibility](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1741927&lang=2&reg=48).
- Assessment-based free aids include walking sticks, elbow crutches/walkers, hearing aids, wheelchairs, dentures and spectacles. Devices improve functional independence; they do not replace clinical assessment, maintenance and accessible community infrastructure.

topics.title: Asian Development Bank: financing and safeguards
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Institution
- **Established 1966**, headquarters **Mandaluyong/Metro Manila, Philippines**; regional development bank supporting inclusive, resilient, sustainable development with loans, grants, equity and technical assistance. India collaboration: infrastructure, climate resilience, logistics, water/sanitation, health/education.
- **69 members: 50 Asia-Pacific, 19 nonregional**, correcting the body’s 49/20 split (its graphic gives 50/19). [ADB institution](https://www.adb.org/who-we-are/about).
- Embedded comparator: **AIIB, 2016, Beijing**, infrastructure; **African Development Bank, 1964, Abidjan**. Their memberships change; source AIIB110/AfDB81 counts are dated, not permanent totals.
## 5 June: Pakistan financing dispute
- Clipping reports India strongly opposed funding and sought safeguards/monitoring against resource diversion, citing fiscal/military-spending concerns. These are India’s reported objections, not proven findings that this package financed terrorism.
- ADB approved an **US$800 million package**, comprising **US$300 million policy-based loan + US$500 million guarantee**, for resource mobilisation/utilisation reforms. Guarantee ≠ an US$800 million immediate cash loan or grant. [ADB programme account](https://www.adb.org/multimedia/partnership-report2025/our-stories/unlocking-domestic-resources-and-private-capital-to-strengthen-fiscal-resilience/).
- Source cites Pakistan tax/GDP **13% (2017–18) → 9.2% (2022–23)** and regional~19% average, requiring matching definitions/years. Requested FATF review is separate from ADB’s lending decision; it does not prove automatic relisting.

topics.title: IIAS presidency and administrative-science cooperation
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## June 2025 election
- **V. (Voruganti) Srinivas**, DARPG Secretary, elected **IIAS President for 2025–28**; India nominated him in November 2024. Final vote on **3 June 2025** against Austria after candidates from South Africa/Bahrain were also considered. Election and assumption of the term are distinct milestones.
