[IIAS announcement](https://iias-iisa.org/news/shri-srinivas-voruganti-india-elected-president-of-the-iias-20252028/).
- **International Institute of Administrative Sciences** is a global federation for public-administration research/collaboration; not a formal UN body, though it cooperates with UN initiatives. Source membership **31 countries, 20 national sections, 15 academic centres** is an election-era snapshot, not fixed constitutional composition.
- India member since **1998**, represented through **DARPG**. Source’s assertion that the election occurred at **Bharat Mandapam** needs event-specific corroboration; presidency election should not be confused with a conference hosted there.
- Potential: comparative governance research, public-grievance systems, digital administration and professional networks. Election does not give India binding authority to prescribe other countries’ public policy or prove every domestic reform already succeeded.

topics.title: India and the Central Asian republics
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Region and June 2025 dialogue
- **Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan**: landlocked region linking Russia, China and Afghanistan; historical/cultural links, security and energy interests support India's engagement.
- **4th India–Central Asia Dialogue, New Delhi, 6 June 2025**, chaired by India's External Affairs Minister; accompanying Business Council discussions sought wider commercial cooperation. Connectivity, digital/fintech, financial links and partnerships were policy priorities, not all completed projects. [MEA joint statement](https://www.mea.gov.in/bilateral-documents.htm?dtl%2F39643=).
- **SCO/RATS** supports regional security dialogue; membership and cooperation differ across the five republics. Avoid implying every CAR is an identical SCO full member or that SCO is an Indian-controlled security alliance.

## Energy, trade and connectivity
- Kazakhstan uranium ties, oil/gas resources and possible long-term energy agreements diversify supply. **TAPI—Turkmenistan–Afghanistan–Pakistan–India** is a pipeline project, not gas already flowing to India; security, finance and transit conditions matter.
- **INSTC /Chabahar** seek alternative access around direct overland constraints; individual railway/port links have distinct operational and construction stages. Lack of direct geographic access, border friction, NTBs and transport costs inhibit pharmaceuticals/IT and other trade.
- Source **~US$2 billion annual India trade** and **China–CAR US$89.4 billion in 2023** need comparable periods/trade coverage; the disparity illustrates competition, not proof every CAR rejects Indian investment.

## Security and diplomacy
- Afghanistan instability, terrorism/extremism and **2022 Kazakhstan unrest** shape risk. Partnership should respond to CAR priorities and sovereignty rather than reduce all relations to countering China/Russia.
- **Dustlik—Uzbekistan; Khanjar—Kyrgyzstan**, training and intelligence cooperation; cooperation does not automatically authorise cross-border joint combat operations.
- PDF's unqualified **“India's military base in Tajikistan”** overstates public evidence: India historically helped renovate **Ayni** and maintained training cooperation; historical assistance is not proof of a continuously operating sovereign Indian overseas airbase in June 2025. [MEA historical clarification](https://meacms.mea.gov.in/Uploads/PublicationDocs/25403_India_foreign_relation_2013.pdf).
- Education, scholarships, cultural centres and people-to-people links complement logistics/energy/defence. Proposals: practical corridor completion, investment facilitation, resilient supply chains, sustained training/counter-terror engagement and cultural exchange; prioritise feasible milestones and diverse partners.

topics.title: Darvaza gas crater and methane emissions
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Karakum map and June 2025 report
- **Darvaza/Derweze gas crater, Karakum Desert, Turkmenistan**, “Gateway/Gates to Hell”: burning natural gas from a collapsed drilling site; **not a volcanic crater and not Kazakhstan**.
- Widely repeated story: Soviet drilling collapse and deliberate ignition **1971** to dispose of escaping gas. Origin/ignition chronology is incompletely documented and competing accounts exist; label **1971 as the conventional account**, not a securely established scientific date.
- **June 2025:** authorities reported the fire reduced **threefold**, associated with surrounding wells capturing/diverting gas; reduced visible flames do not by themselves establish a quantified reduction in methane leakage. Exact measurement basis/timeframe was not supplied. Reported control is not complete extinguishment.
- The PDF's **“longest continuously burning man-made fire”** is unsupported; long-burning coal fires have different histories. Do not equate a burning gas crater with the whole country's fossil-fuel leakage inventory.

## Climate distinctions
- **CH₄** is a potent, relatively short-lived greenhouse gas. Source **84× CO₂ over 20 years** is a specified assessment/time-horizon convention, not one universal potency at every horizon; 100-year factors differ.
- **Combustion converts methane mainly to CO₂/water**, reducing methane released if efficient; unburned leakage/venting still warms strongly. A smaller flame may reflect less inflow, but actual emissions need measurements.
- Turkmenistan has very high **oil/gas methane intensity** and major super-emitter leaks; it is not automatically the world's largest **absolute** methane emitter across all sectors. Source's two-field comparison with UK annual emissions is an attributed CO₂-equivalent calculation requiring year/horizon and is not an IEA ranking of all national emissions. [IEA 2025 tracker](https://www.iea.org/reports/global-methane-tracker-2025).
- Source ranks Turkmenistan **fourth in gas reserves**; ranking depends on reference year/reserve definition. Gas-resource abundance is distinct from current output or methane intensity.
- Priorities: leak detection/repair, capture and safe use of gas, measured verification and ending routine venting/flaring. Source practice answer **(b)** reflects its conventional history, but the ignition date and “largest emitter” explanation require these qualifications.

topics.title: Free-living amoebae and molecular diagnosis
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Kerala laboratory development: June 2025
- **State Public Health Laboratory, Thiruvananthapuram**, developed molecular/PCR testing for five listed amoeba targets: **Naegleria fowleri; Acanthamoeba spp.; Vermamoeba vermiformis; Balamuthia mandrillaris; Paravahlkampfia francinae**. **Acanthamoeba spp.** is a group, so this is not strictly five single species.
- Embedded clipping reports first successful human-sample **Acanthamoeba** identification after about **six months' test development**, reducing reliance on distant laboratories such as PGI Chandigarh. The laboratory's subsequent official account confirms the five-target molecular system. [Kerala I&PRD confirmation](https://www.prd.kerala.gov.in/ml/node/314820).
- **FLA** live in the environment; a small subset can infect humans. Source **“400+ species, only six pathogenic”** is a simplified count with uncertain taxonomic scope; do not assume all listed targets have equally established frequency/pathogenicity or that all brain infections are caused by Naegleria.
- **PCR amplifies selected DNA targets** for detection; RNA detection requires an appropriate reverse-transcription step. Identifying a target depends on specimen quality, assay specificity/validation and clinical correlation; a kit is not a guaranteed cure.

## Distinguish infection syndromes
- **Naegleria fowleri →primary amoebic meningoencephalitis (PAM)**, usually following contaminated warm freshwater entering the nose. **Acanthamoeba/Balamuthia →granulomatous amoebic encephalitis (GAE)** and other manifestations; routes/course differ. [CDC diagnostic overview](https://www.cdc.gov/dpdx/freeLivingAmebic/).
- Rapid diagnosis can guide expert combination treatment rather than presumptive single-organism therapy; these rare infections can be extremely severe, but species identification does not ensure survival.
- Surveillance, prompt clinical suspicion, safe water/public-health communication and referral/testing capacity matter; detection figures reflect testing/access as well as possible incidence changes.

topics.title: Tunnel boring machines and urban tunnelling
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mechanism and machine selection
**Rotating cutterhead → excavate soil/rock → remove spoil by conveyor/muck cars → advance thrust system → install appropriate support/lining.** TBMs (sometimes “moles”) excavate circular tunnels and reduce surface excavation; choice depends on ground, water pressure and project geometry.
| Type | Typical use |
|---|---|
| Earth Pressure Balance | Soft ground; conditioned excavated material balances face pressure |
| Slurry shield | Water-bearing/unstable ground; pressurised slurry supports face |
| Hard-rock TBM | Disc cutters fracture competent rock; shield/support configuration varies |
| Open/gripper design | Suitable stable rock; not interchangeable with all unsupported soil excavation |
- Benefits: mechanised precision, potential continuous operation and less urban surface disruption than open excavation. Not guaranteed faster/safer in every geology; monitor settlement/utilities/buildings, groundwater and worker safety.
- Constraints: high purchase/mobilisation cost, complex underground repair, fixed diameter, geological uncertainty and poor economics on some short drives. “Eco-sensitive” does not eliminate spoil disposal, groundwater, vibration or habitat impacts.
- Source generic **5–17 m diameter, 10–15 m/day, ₹100–150 crore, 500–2,000 m³/day, 15–30 workers/shift** are indicative, not universal specifications; rates vary with diameter/geology/support/down-time. Project examples: **GMLR Mumbai planned 14.5 m; Metro Line 3 ~6.68 m; Delhi ~6.5 m; Chennai Phase 2 ~6.6 m; Mumbai Coastal Road 12.19 m** need machine-specific comparison. **Silkyara is not a verified 9–10 m TBM project**; do not confuse main tunnel construction, rescue auger and tunnel dimensions. [MoRTH Silkyara record](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1521024&lang=2&reg=48).
## 7 June 2025: Delhi Golden Line breakthrough
- **Maa Anandmayee Marg → Tughlakabad Railway Colony**, Phase IV **Aerocity–Tughlakabad Golden Line**: TBM completed **792 m** drive. **96 m machine length** differs from bore diameter; tunnel roughly **18 m deep**, **566 precast rings**, **5.8 m inner diameter**; **EPB** method.
- Parallel second drive was expected **July 2025**; construction milestone is not opening the whole metro line. June clipping's **mid-2026** operations estimate is a forecast. DMRC gives **19.343 km underground** for this corridor and **40.109 km** approved Phase IV underground work. [DMRC 7 June release](https://delhimetrorail.com/pages/en/pressrelease_details/dmrc-completes-one-more-tunnelling-milestone-achie).

topics.title: Russia–Ukraine war: territorial claims and escalation
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## 8–9 June 2025: reported Dnipropetrovsk advance
- Source reports Russian Defence Ministry claim that tank forces reached the western Donetsk boundary and advanced towards/into **Dnipropetrovsk**. Treat as an attributed battlefield claim, not independently established final territorial control. June 2025 is the **fourth year since the 24 February 2022 full-scale invasion**, correcting PDF's “third year”.
- **Dnipro**, regional capital on Dnipro River; Dnipropetrovsk is central-eastern Ukraine, west of Donetsk, with mining/industrial/logistics importance. Source **~1 million city / ~3 million region pre-war** are approximate historical populations, not wartime census results.
- Industrial/economic pressure, supply-route disruption and bargaining effects are analytical possibilities; no proof every claimed military motive or future sanction/NATO response had materialised.
## Territory and international law
- Russia purported to annex **Crimea 2014; Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson, Zaporizhzhia 2022**; Dnipropetrovsk was outside those declared claims. Actual occupation, annexation claims and internationally recognised boundaries are distinct.
- **All these areas remain internationally recognised Ukrainian territory**. The UN Charter's prohibition on force/territorial acquisition does not apply only to areas Russia has not already claimed. **UNGA ES-11/4 (12 October 2022)** condemned attempted annexation of the four regions. [UN resolution account](https://press.un.org/en/2022/ga 12458.doc.htm).
- India calls for dialogue/diplomacy and respect for sovereignty/territorial integrity while maintaining Russia/Western relationships. Strategic autonomy does not validate occupation or mean every issue has the same voting/trade position.
- Mains: territorial integrity, civilian protection, industrial damage,energy/mineral supply and credible negotiations; distinguish conflict reporting from a final recognised change in borders.

topics.title: India–Mongolia relations and military exercises
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Nomadic Elephant 17: underway inJune 2025
- India–Mongolia **annual bilateral Army exercise**, alternating hosts; **17 th edition 31 May–13 June 2025,Ulaanbaatar SpecialForcesTrainingCentre**; **16 th at Umroi, Meghalaya, July 2024**. Source's “scheduled” misses the accompanying clipping showing it already underway. The claimed 2006 origin is source background requiring historical verification.
- **45 Indian personnel**, primarily **Arunachal Scouts**, with Mongolian **150 Special Forces unit** (a unit designation, not necessarily 150 participants); joint semi-conventional operations in semi-urban/mountain terrain, interoperability, operational tactics, cultural understanding. [Defence Ministry 29 May](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2132473&lang=2&reg=48).
- **UN Chapter VII** concerns Security Council action for threats/breaches of peace/aggression; exercise under a UN-mandate scenario is not itself an authorised UN deployment. **Khaan Quest** is a separate multinational peacekeeping exercise hosted in Mongolia; do not equate bilateral training with all UN peacekeeping law.
## Mongolia map and economic links
- **Landlocked between Russia (north) and China (south/east/west)**; capital **Ulaanbaatar**, plateau/high-altitude continental setting. **Altai, Khangai, Khentii** mountain systems; **Orkhon River / UNESCO Orkhon Valley cultural landscape**; **Lake Khuvsgul** major freshwater lake. “Younger sister of Baikal” is a nickname, not hydrological classification.
- Coal, copper, gold, fluorspar are major resource sectors; lithium prospects do not by themselves establish Mongolia as a leading commercial lithium producer.
- Source reports **trial coking-coal sourcing by India** to diversify steelmaking inputs beyond suppliers such as Australia. Plans/trials are not proof of major established deliveries or eliminated dependence; landlocked transport via neighbours affects cost/feasibility. Coking coal makes coke for conventional blast-furnace steelmaking, not every steel-production route.

## Khaan Quest 2025: scheduled 14–28 June
- Indian contingent arrived **Ulaanbaatar on 11 June** for the **22nd multinational peacekeeping exercise**, scheduled **14–28 June 2025**; **40 personnel**, mainly **Kumaon Regiment**, including **one woman officer and two women soldiers**.
- Origin **US–Mongolia bilateral 2003**, multinational since **2006**. Trains multinational interoperability/readiness for UN peace support, including checkpoints, cordon/search, patrols, civilian evacuation, counter-IED and combat first aid. This is separate from **Nomadic Elephant**. [Defence Ministry](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2135593).
- Peacekeeping training is not itself deployment authorisation. Mongolia's defence engagement supports India’s wider Asian partnerships; Mongolia is normally located in **East Asia**, despite broader Central Asian strategic linkages.

topics.title: Donkey-skin trade, welfare and rural livelihoods
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## African policy and livelihood risks
- **Ejiao** is gelatin made from donkey hides, used in Chinese traditional medicine/wellness products. Claimed fertility, blood-replenishment and anti-ageing effects are not established clinical benefits in this source.
- **Dar es Salaam Declaration, 1–2 December 2022**, proposed a **15-year moratorium on donkey slaughter for skins**; AU adopted a preservation/moratorium resolution in **2024**. **26 May 2025 AU-IBAR** urged member-state implementation and discussed a **draft** Pan-African preservation/welfare strategy. A continental decision is not proof uniform national enforcement or that 33 million donkeys have already been saved. [AU-IBAR implementation account](https://www.au-ibar.org/news/latest-news/au-ibar-urges-immediate-action-donkey-welfare-across-africa-woah-general-session).
- Theft, poorly regulated slaughter, animal cruelty and slow reproduction threaten working-animal populations. Loss of transport/ploughing/water-carrying capacity undermines farmer income, increases women's/children's labour and can disrupt schooling; unsafe slaughter creates occupational/zoonotic risks.
- Source market estimates **160% ejiao growth, 2016–21; ~6 million hides/year; 6.8 million slaughtered/year by 2027** combine growth estimates and a forecast. China **11 million donkeys in 1992 → under 2 million** and Botswana **493,000 in 2003 →125,000 in 2021** need original census verification. Do not equate demand with verified annual kills or infer all population decline caused by trade.
- SDG links include poverty/food security, health, gender, water access, decent work and sustainable ecosystems; “nine SDGs undermined” is advocacy framing, not a measured index.
## Indian equids
- **Kachchhi—Kutch, Gujarat; Halari—Saurashtra, Gujarat; Spiti—Himachal Pradesh** are donkey-breed anchors. Do not confuse **Kachchhi-Sindhi horse** with a formally registered Sindhi donkey breed. Source carrying/draught figures, especially **1,000–1,500 kg**, are not safe loading recommendations. [ICAR-NBAGR breed register](https://nbagr.res.in/horse-pony-donkey).
- Source reports **~61% domestic donkey decline, 2012–19**; monitor trafficking, abandonment, veterinary care and breed conservation. Welfare and livelihood support require coordinated enforcement, traceability and owner participation.

topics.title: Indian wild ass and protected-species conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Khur: identification and habitat
- **Equus hemionus khur**, Equidae; Indian subspecies of the Asiatic wild ass, called **khur/ghudkhur**. Pale reddish-brown body, pale underside/rump and dark dorsal stripe; not the domestic donkey or kiang.
- Surviving wild range centred on **Little Rann of Kachchh, Gujarat**, with adjoining Greater Rann/Banni and village/agricultural landscapes; source “exclusively inside Rann” is narrower than its own expansion account. Open saline desert, grassland and scrub; grazes grasses/saline vegetation and browses shrubs; freshwater access shapes movement.
- **Wild Ass Sanctuary, 1973**, roughly **5,000 km²**. Source **6,000+** population is undated; the infographic **4,800** reflects an older snapshot rather than the same survey.
- **Correction: Indian khur is CITES Appendix I**, not II. Species-wide **E. hemionus Near Threatened** assessment and a subspecies' status require separate taxon/date checks; source's Mongolian “Endangered” comparison cannot substitute for the applicable assessment. Indian protection **Schedule I**. [CMS/CITES species distinctions](https://cami.cms.int/species/equus-hemionus).
## Threats and protection
- Salt-pan/agricultural/infrastructure expansion fragments habitat; drought and water scarcity, livestock competition, domestic-equid disease and isolation create risks. **Surra—Trypanosoma evansi**; monitor veterinary spillover and avoid depicting all traditional pastoralists as illegal encroachers.
- Protect movement/water/forage, manage grazing and salt-pan pressures, monitor populations/disease and use evidence-based buffer/ESZ measures; a proposed buffer is not a notified operative zone.
- **2017 PYQ: (d), gharial, Indian wild ass and wild buffalo** protected against hunting except statutory permissions. Section 11 includes tightly conditioned orders for dangerous/irrecoverably injured animals; lawful good-faith defence and Section 12 special-purpose permits are separate provisions. **Schedule I does not mean no statutory exception whatsoever.**
- **2012 endangered-animal grouping: (a)** in the question's historical context; do not assign all four species today's same Red List category.

topics.title: Rainforest nutrient cycles and regeneration
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## 2011 PYQ: regeneration after clearance
- Answer **(a), rainforest soil nutrient deficiency**: heavy rainfall/leaching and rapid cycling concentrate much nutrient stock in living biomass/litter. Removing forest exports that stock and changes moisture/microclimate, hindering recovery.
- Deciduous forests often have less intense leaching and seasonal litter inputs; site soils and disturbance severity vary. High rainforest biodiversity/productivity does not imply uniformly fertile mineral soil; nor are every rainforest tree slow-growing or every propagule unviable.
- Restoration needs habitat/soil protection, native vegetation and connectivity rather than treating exotic invasion as the question's universal primary mechanism.

topics.title: Manipur conflict, hill governance and reconciliation
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Background and legal distinctions
- Imphal-valley Meitei and hill Kuki-Zo/Naga communities face intertwined land, identity, political representation, livelihoods and security tensions. Source **52% Meitei/10% valley geography** and **~40% hill tribes/90% hill geography** are rounded descriptive figures, not proof collective “ownership/control” of every parcel. **40 valley/20 hill constituencies** is not necessarily 40 Meitei MLAs.
- **Article 371 C** provides hill-area legislative-committee/Governor safeguards. Manipur hill areas are **not automatically Fifth-Schedule Scheduled Areas**, nor Sixth-Schedule autonomous areas. Land restrictions derive from applicable statutes/customary systems; ST status under **Article 342** is a distinct constitutional process. [Tribal Affairs constitutional distinctions](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/erelcontent.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=75098).
- Armed insurgency, cross-border trafficking/refugee displacement after Myanmar's crisis, Golden Triangle proximity and uneven hill infrastructure complicate governance. Do not conflate refugees, an ethnic community and narcotics networks; source ~30 outfits/40,000 crossers require dated evidence.
## 2023 triggers and dated consequences
- Source sequence: ST-demand litigation; April 2023 High Court direction to consider recommendations; February evictions of **16 households**; State's **10 March** withdrawal decision concerning particular SoO groups; **28 April** mobilisation and **3 May 2023** outbreak. It does not prove the entire tripartite SoO framework terminated or that every missing weapon came from SoO camps.
- Polarisation, looted armouries, divided trust in state/central agencies and weak coordinated response undermined law/order; source ~4,000 looted arms is a dated estimate. Sexual violence, segregation, disrupted schooling/health/trade and displacement require survivor-centred protection and justice.
- **Source snapshot as of 3 May 2024: ** **221 deaths, 60,000 displaced, 4,786 homes burnt, 386 religious sites damaged**; not June 2025 totals. “Exports down 80%” lacks a clear period/series and is not a statewide GDP measurement.
- **Correction for June 2025: ** N. Biren Singh was no longer serving CM; **President's Rule imposed 13 February 2025**. Historical criticism of his government should be time-labelled. [Home Ministry/Parliament](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2118913&lang=2&reg=48).
- Reconciliation: impartial investigations, weapons recovery, coordinated accountable security, relief/rehabilitation, dialogue, lawful land processes and equitable development. Naga participation/positions vary; smaller groups such as Hmar/Kom/Aimol/Chothe are not uniformly interchangeable with one ethnic umbrella.
## Cultural and tribe PYQs
- **2018: Chapchar Kut–Mizoram; Khongjom Parba–Manipur correct; Thang-Ta–Sikkim wrong → (b), 1 and 2.** Thang-Ta is Manipur's martial tradition.
- **2009 Shompen: Nicobar Islands (b)**, chiefly Great Nicobar; **2004 Onge: Andaman and Nicobar Islands (a)**, chiefly Little Andaman. Historical racial labels in source explanations are outdated classification shortcuts, not necessary exam facts.

topics.title: Farm ponds and decentralised water harvesting
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## 10 June 2025: Kukas model
- **Kukas near Jaipur, Rajasthan/Amber block**: farm ponds capture monsoon runoff on farmers' land where groundwater stress constrains agriculture. Source layout **~5% farmland, 10 ft deep, plastic-lined, fenced**; sizing needs rainfall/catchment/soil and safety assessment.
- Stored runoff can supplement kharif/rabi irrigation, livestock and horticulture; evaporation, rainfall variability, irrigation efficiency and maintenance determine duration. Source **14–21 lakh litres per hectare**, **50 built/25 under construction**, **50,000 villagers expected to benefit** are project estimates with distinct units/status; not demonstrated year-round security for every village.
- **Correction: ** a plastic liner limits seepage, so direct recharge cannot simultaneously be its principal function. Storage ponds reduce pumping pressure; separate unlined recharge works/infiltration elsewhere can replenish aquifers.
- Benefits: drought buffering, diversification, potential processing/dairy jobs. Assess land opportunity cost, runoff diversion/downstream impacts, liner disposal, safe fencing and fair access; no-river/no-canal claim is site-specific, not true of all Rajasthan.
- **2025 Araghatta PYQ: (b)**, wheel with earthen pots at spoke ends lifts water into channels. Ancient device is distinct from a rainfall-storage pond; similar water-wheel concepts do not prove a single undisputed invention history.

topics.title: Nickel ores and hydrogen-plasma extraction
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## 8 June 2025 research development
- Max Planck Institute for Sustainable Materials, Germany: **hydrogen-plasma reactor** combines smelting, reduction and refining of low-grade nickel ore; electrically excited hydrogen removes oxygen, producing **water** rather than carbon-reduction CO₂.
- **Correction: ** product is a refined **ferronickel alloy**, not necessarily pure nickel. Direct reactor chemistry avoids carbon reduction, while modelled life-cycle benefit **~84% less CO₂/up to 18% less energy** depends on **green hydrogen and renewable electricity**; not zero supply-chain emissions. [Research institution](https://www.mpg.de/24637660/green-nickel-for-sustainable-electrification).
- Conventional laterite routes are energy-intensive; source **~20 tonnes CO₂/tonne nickel**, projected **>6 million tonnes demand by 2040** depend on process/scenario. Laboratory demonstration ≠ commercial plant: scale-up, melt mixing/interface access, current/arc design, hydrogen cost/safety, power and capital are unresolved.
## Nickel, ores and use
- **Ni, atomic number 28**; silvery metal, ductile/malleable and useful corrosion-resistant alloying material. **Sulphide ores and weathered laterites** require different processing; “never native in nature” is too absolute given meteoritic/native occurrences.
- **Garnierite** is a green nickel-rich assemblage of hydrous silicates, including serpentine/talc-like minerals, **not one fixed mineral**. New Caledonia, Indonesia and Philippines laterites are important. Generic source **1–4% Ni** is an ore-grade guide, not a universal garnierite composition.
- Stainless steel is the largest use; also selected EV cathodes, NiMH batteries, aerospace/turbine alloys, plating, electronics and magnets. Not all lithium-ion batteries contain nickel; **LFP** is a notable exception.
- Sukinda, Odisha: nickel in chromite-overburden/lateritic limonite; Jharkhand and other occurrences need deposit-specific evidence. Source **92% Odisha** concerns resource concentration, **not proof 92% of mined production**. Resources, reserves, output and refining shares differ. [IBM nickel inventory](https://ibm.gov.in/writereaddata/files/02272023165341Nickel_2021.pdf).
- Source 2022 Indonesia/Philippines/Russia production list, **58.2% combined share**, China **50.4% consumption/75% Indonesian refining control** need dated denominators; not permanent rankings. Chinese-linked investment/oversupply can affect prices and ownership; assess supply concentration alongside domestic processing, recycling and environmental safeguards.
- Industrial dust/emissions, mining and waste exposure can cause dermatitis and respiratory disease; **certain nickel compounds are human carcinogens**, not identical risks for every form/dose. Protect workers and control air/water/soil releases.
## PYQ corrections
- **2025 Botswana–diamond, Chile–lithium, Indonesia–nickel: all three (c)**. Lithium Triangle = Chile/Argentina/Bolivia; resource abundance is not guaranteed extractable reserves or world-market dominance.
- **2010 mineral pairs: nickel–Orissa alone (b)**. The question claims **90% natural sources**, so simply finding some copper in Jharkhand does not make that pair true; source's answer (a) is wrong.
- **2025 battery cathodes: cobalt, lithium and nickel (c), only three; graphite generally anode.** These are component possibilities across usual chemistries, not proof every EV cathode uses all three.

topics.title: Asafoetida cultivation and import substitution
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Plant and cultivation milestones
- **Heeng/asafoetida**, oleo-gum-resin obtained by incising **Ferula** taproots/rhizomes; source **F. assa-foetida**, pungent culinary spice sold in lumps/powder. A herbaceous plant, not the infographic's “tree”. Traditional medical use does not validate graphic claims to cure epilepsy, viruses or depression.
- Cold/arid Iran/Afghanistan/Central Asian origins; well-drained sandy soils, low rainfall and suitable cool climate matter. Source **<300 mm,10–20°C,−4 to 40°C tolerance** are indicative, not guarantees every stage survives extremes. Long juvenile period (~five years) and seed dormancy/low germination obstruct establishment.
- **CSIR-IHBT, Palampur**, with **ICAR-NBPGR** legal seed import/quarantine; research/import work **2018–20**, first farm planting **15 October 2020, Kwaring, Lahaul, Himachal Pradesh**. Source further trial locations include Lahaul-Spiti (Keylong/Salgran/Madgran), Mandi (Janjheli/Karsog), Kinnaur (Kalpa/Reckong Peo), Kullu (Banjar/Sainj) and Chamba (Bharmour/Pangi).
- **May 2025 first flowering reported at IHBT Palampur (~1,300 m)**; source attributes flowering/seed-set milestone to **28 May**, but exact-date and viable-seed claims need institute records. Completion of flowering supports adaptability; does not establish nationwide commercial resin output or end to import dependence. [CSIR institutional account](https://csirnews.niscair.res.in/home/article/845).
- Source **2022 germplasm resource centre**, tissue-culture propagation/niche mapping, seed supply/training support expansion; preserve conservation, planting-material quality and crop economics. Potential farmer income/import substitution are prospective benefits requiring mature harvests and viable markets.
- Undated UPPSC/HSSC questions are held separately: root extraction, and first cultivation in **Himachal Pradesh cold desert**. Do not invent exam years.

topics.title: Portuguese crop introductions in India
topics.subject: Modern Indian History
topics.markdown:
## 2025 PYQ correction
- Source's answer **“only two”** is wrong: **papaya, pineapple and guava** are American-origin crops associated with Portuguese introduction to India in the question's sixteenth/seventeenth-century context; **all three (c)**.
- NHB records pineapple introduction **1548**; do not assign this exact year to papaya/guava without evidence. Source's assertion that guava reached India through Spaniards is unsupported; an ICAR-hosted horticulture paper attributes its Indian introduction to the Portuguese. [NHB pineapple](https://www.nhb.gov.in/report_files/pineapple/pineapple.htm), [ICAR guava paper](https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/153958/60535).
- Crop transfers illustrate the Columbian Exchange and maritime trade; native origin, introduction route and later cultivation are separate facts.

topics.title: Solar geoengineering and stratospheric aerosol injection
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Mechanism and research status
- **SAI** proposes injecting reflective particles/precursors into the stratosphere to reduce incoming solar energy; **solar radiation modification (SRM)** differs from CO₂ removal. Stratosphere roughly **10–50 km**, but actual injection altitude depends on latitude/tropopause and design.
- Proposed sulphate aerosols scatter sunlight and persist longer than lower-atmosphere particles, with limited rain removal aloft. **Mount Pinatubo, Philippines,1991** illustrates temporary volcanic aerosol cooling (~0.5°C globally at peak), not proof a controlled deployment is harmless.
- Sulphates, calcium carbonate and diamond particles are research proposals; cost, particle microphysics, chemistry and dispersal shape feasibility. **No automatic rule that SAI works better at the poles**, nor proof nanodiamonds are harmless. [IPCC assessment](https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg1/chapter/chapter-4/).
## Risks and alternatives
- Ozone chemistry, stratospheric heating, altered rainfall/monsoons, unequal regional effects and eventual deposition require assessment. Abrupt cessation after substantial sustained cooling can cause **termination shock**; warming gases/ocean acidification continue if emissions remain.
- **Marine cloud brightening** uses sea-salt particles to increase low-cloud reflectivity; “less risky” is not a settled universal comparison. **Space sunshades** near L1 are speculative costly engineering. **Cirrus thinning** aims to let **outgoing longwave heat escape**, not principally reflect sunlight; lumping it into incoming-solar reflection obscures the mechanism.
- These are debated climate-intervention ideas, not an established substitute for mitigation/adaptation. Governance requires transparent research, international cooperation, distributive justice and long-term responsibility.
- **2019 PYQ: reducing global warming (d)**. This does not establish no possible effect on cyclone/precipitation patterns; it identifies the proposed principal purpose.

topics.title: Rudram: anti-radiation and air-to-surface missiles
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## June 2025: verified capability and source caution
- DRDO's indigenous Rudram family supports the IAF's suppression of enemy air defences: anti-radiation weapons home on emissions from hostile radar, reducing exposure of strike aircraft. Standoff launch distance improves aircraft survivability; it does not guarantee interception is impossible.
- **RudraM-II** was successfully flight-tested from **Su-30 MK-I off Odisha on 29 May 2024**. Official release describes a **solid-propelled air-launched air-to-surface system** and validation of propulsion/control/guidance. [Defence Ministry](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2022076).
- The June 11 PDF gives inconsistent Rudram-4 ranges (300+, 550–600 and 600+ km), an unsupported hypersonic classification and claims Mirage/Rafale integration. These are **unverified specifications**, not established operational capabilities; likewise do not memorise its Rudram-II/III speed/range table as official data. GPS support alone cannot establish GPS-denied guidance capability.
- Indigenisation reduces supplier dependence but testing, aircraft integration, production and service induction are separate milestones.
- **2014 PYQ recall:** Agni-IV is a two-stage **solid-fuelled surface-to-surface ballistic missile**, about **4,000 km** range; the liquid-only and 7,500-km statements are false → **(a) 1 only**.

topics.title: UNFPA and reproductive agency
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Institution and reproductive rights
- UNFPA: UN sexual/reproductive-health agency, **New York** headquarters; trust fund established **1967**, operations began **1969**, renamed United Nations Population Fund in **1987** while retaining its acronym. Source's **1968** establishment date is incorrect. [UNFPA institutional history](https://www.unfpa.org/frequently-asked-questions-about-unfpa).
- Supports voluntary family planning, safe motherhood, reproductive health, gender equality and population research/census capacity, working with governments and country priorities. Its role is wider than demographic control; distinguish national primary statistical collection from UNFPA's analytical/technical support.
- Three transformative goals for 2030: **zero preventable maternal deaths, zero unmet family-planning need, zero gender-based violence/harmful practices**.
## 2025 population estimates
- Embedded June clipping: India's population **1,463.9 million (146.39 crore)** and **TFR 1.9 births per woman**. These are UN estimates, not a newly completed census; compare with **SRS 2021 TFR 2.0** using explicit source/reference year. [UNFPA India 2025 data](https://www.unfpa.org/data/world-population/IN).
- Below-replacement fertility does not immediately stop population growth: age structure and population momentum matter. The clipping's peak near 170 crore in roughly four decades is a projection, not an observed outcome.
- **2024 PYQ:** TFR is the average number of live births a woman would have by the end of childbearing under current age-specific fertility rates → **(d)**; distinguish crude birth rate per 1,000 population.

topics.title: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple and Travancore heritage
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Temple and June 2025 context
- **Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala**; Vishnu in **Anantha Shayanam** posture on Adishesha. Kerala and Dravidian architectural elements, **seven-tier gopuram**, about **80-foot gold-plated copper flagstaff**, stone/bronze work and murals including Vishnu, Ganapati, Gajalakshmi and Narasimha.
- Marthanda Varma reconstructed/patronised the shrine; **1750 Thrippadidanam** dedicated Travancore to the deity, underpinning the royal family's role as servants/trustees. Historical mentions do not establish an exact construction date.
- **Mathilakam palm-leaf records** document temple-town/Travancore administration and finance over centuries. Source cites roughly three million leaves/records; do not equate leaves with three million separate complete manuscripts. [Kerala Tourism](https://www.keralatourism.org/temples/thiruvananthapuram/sree-padmanabhaswamy).
- June issue reports **Maha Kumbhabhishekam after about 270 years**, following renovation; ritual consecration/purification is the cultural significance. **2011 vault inventory** revealed major treasures; monetary valuations remain estimates. The decorative graphic's supernatural vault claims are folklore, not evidence.
- PYQ distinctions: **Nagara/Dravida/Vesara = temple architecture (2012, c)**; famous **Virupaksha Temple = Hampi (2009, c)** on the Tungabhadra. The source conflates it with **Pattadakal's Virupaksha**, built by Lokamahadevi to commemorate Vikramaditya II's Pallava victory; keep the two sites separate.

topics.title: Child labour and the Velpur model
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## June 12: burden and statistical correction
- **World Day Against Child Labour: 12 June**, ILO; **SDG 8.7** targeted ending child labour by 2025. ILO–UNICEF **2024 estimates, released 11 June 2025:** about **138 million children (7.8% of ages 5–17)**, including **54 million in hazardous work**; source's **160 million/one in ten** belongs to **2020**, not the latest estimate. [ILO release](https://www.ilo.org/resource/other/2024-global-estimates-child-labour-frequently-asked-questions).
- India Census 2011 **43.53 lakh refers to main workers ages 5–14**, while roughly **10.1 million** includes main and marginal workers. The PDF's infographic and prose use different definitions, not interchangeable counts. [Labour Ministry clarification](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1539009).
- Poverty, parental debt, insecure informal livelihoods, inaccessible schooling and trafficking/bondage reinforce work in agriculture, beedi-making, carpets and fireworks.
## Framework and governance
- **1986 Act, amended 2016:** broadly prohibits work below 14; limited family-enterprise/child-artist exceptions have conditions and education safeguards; adolescents **14–18** prohibited from hazardous occupations/processes. The PDF's unconditional “complete prohibition in every circumstance” omits exceptions. [2017 rules](https://www.labour.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/06/bc8ab35458267a486ab2e574ba0b85fe.pdf).
- **RTE 2009: ages 6–14**; **National Policy on Child Labour 1987** and historical **NCLP (1988)** used withdrawal/bridge schooling/rehabilitation. Do not assume NCLP remains a separate current scheme merely because the case study describes its earlier schools.
- India ratified **ILO C138 (Minimum Age, 1973)** and **C182 (Worst Forms, 1999)** in **2017**. Worst forms include slavery/trafficking, forced recruitment for conflict, sexual exploitation, illicit activities and hazardous work. **2018 PYQ answer: (a) child labour**.
## Velpur: community ownership
- **Velpur Mandal, Nizamabad, Telangana** (then Andhra Pradesh): campaign began **June 2001**, declared child-labour-free **2 October 2001**. Source records a **20-year commemoration 8 October 2021**, presentation to parliamentary committee **24 November 2022** and continued retention reported in 2025; an exact 100% claim needs local monitoring data.
- Employer forgiveness of about **₹35 lakh parental hand loans**, village awareness/social commitments, sarpanch MoUs with Collector/DEO, teachers/infrastructure/mid-day meals and bridge schooling addressed demand, debt and access together. Village signboards reinforced the commitment.
- Recognition by ILO, **VVGNLI (Labour Ministry, Noida)**, NHRC and appreciation from A.P.J. Abdul Kalam supported wider learning. Lesson: combine debt relief/livelihood support, education quality, community mobilisation and labour–education–local government coordination; rescue alone cannot prevent relapse.

topics.title: Operation Secure and infostealer disruption
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## January–April operation; June 2025 announcement
- INTERPOL coordinated **Operation Secure** with **26 participating jurisdictions including India**: over **20,000 malicious IP addresses/domains** disrupted, **41 servers** and **100+ GB** seized, **32 suspects** arrested. Figures describe the combined operation, not India's individual totals. [INTERPOL, 11 June](https://www.interpol.int/News-and-Events/News/2025/20-000-malicious-IPs-and-domains-taken-down-in-INTERPOL-infostealer-crackdown).
- **Infostealers** extract passwords, browser credentials/cookies, payment and wallet data; stolen logs facilitate further fraud, ransomware or breaches. Locating servers, mapping physical networks and cross-border takedowns combine intelligence sharing with national law-enforcement powers.
- CERT-In (incident response) and NCIIPC (critical information infrastructure protection) are relevant Indian institutions; their general relevance does not prove each executed the raids or individual operational roles assigned in the source.

topics.title: BBNJ agreement and high-seas biodiversity
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Position as of June 2025
- **Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ)** agreement under **UNCLOS**: marine genetic resources/benefit sharing; area-based management tools including MPAs; environmental impact assessments; capacity building/marine technology transfer.
- India signed **September 2024**; June issue reports ratification still pending domestic legal preparations, including biodiversity legislation. A predicted parliamentary timeline is not a completed ratification or a verified session calendar.
- Source reports **49 ratifications as of 10 June**. Entry into force requires **120 days after deposit of the 60th instrument**, not immediate operation on the 60th ratification. This note records the June status, not later treaty developments. [UN agreement overview](https://www.un.org/Depts/los/bbnj.htm).
- Equity concerns: access to marine genetic resources, sharing benefits, scientific/financial capacity and protection of common ocean ecosystems. Areas beyond national jurisdiction include high-seas water and relevant seabed areas; water-column and continental-shelf rights are not identical.
## UNCLOS diagram/PYQ recall
- **Territorial sea: up to 12 nautical miles from baselines (Article 3)**; all States' ships enjoy **innocent passage (Article 17)** subject to applicable rules. **Contiguous zone: up to 24 nm**; **EEZ: up to 200 nm from baselines (Article 57)**, sovereign rights over resources rather than full territorial sovereignty. Source's “from coastline” is simplified.
- **2022 PYQ: all three statements correct → (d)**. Continental shelf can legally extend beyond 200 nm under qualifying criteria; do not treat the diagram as a universal shelf limit.
## UN Ocean Conference, Nice: Indian initiatives
- **Samudrayaan:** human-occupied submersible target **6,000 m**, expected deployment/trial in **2026** as described in June, not achieved descent. **SAHAV** digital ocean-data portal; source explicitly invents its acronym expansion, so retain the name only.
- India highlighted marine conservation, selected single-use-plastic restrictions, port development and fisheries. **US$80bn port projects** is not a single unrestricted blue-economy fund. [Earth Sciences Ministry, 10 June](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2135434).

topics.title: Global Gender Gap Report 2025 and women’s empowerment
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## 2025 report: read rank, score and ratios separately
- **WEF** index: economic participation/opportunity, education, health/survival, political empowerment. **India 131/148, score 64.4%**; source's **64.1%** is stale. Global **68.8%**, estimated **123 years** to parity at observed pace, not a guaranteed deadline. Iceland, Finland, Norway, UK, New Zealand lead; Bangladesh **24th**.
- India: economic parity **40.7% (+0.9 percentage points)**; estimated earned-income parity **28.6→29.9%**; labour-force-participation **parity ratio 45.9%**, not the proportion of Indian women in work. Education parity **97.1%**. Parliament women **14.7→13.8%**; these percentages are not the whole political subindex score. Health parity can improve even as life expectancy falls for both sexes. [WEF report](https://www.weforum.org/publications/global-gender-gap-report-2025/benchmarking-gender-gaps-2025).
- Rankings depend on other countries and coverage; the report's retrospective comparable-rank change need not equal a simple subtraction from the prior published 129th rank. Closing a relative gap does not prove adequate absolute opportunity or establish causation by a particular scheme.
## Policy links from the June issue
- **BBBP:** girl-child survival, protection and education; **KGBV:** residential schooling for disadvantaged girls; rural community empowerment/skills initiatives such as historical **Mahila Shakti Kendra**; **Sukanya Samriddhi** girl-child savings. Earlier **Rashtriya Mahila Kosh** microcredit and **Mahila-e-Haat** marketing exemplify programme approaches, not proof all historical schemes continued unchanged in 2025.
- **Stand-Up India:** loans historically **₹10 lakh–₹1 crore** for eligible SC/ST and women entrepreneurs; skills, childcare, safe transport, formal work and SHGs help translate education into employment. Audit observations about programme spending require a specific report/period, not generalisation.
- **73rd/74th Amendments:** at least **one-third** women's representation in rural/urban local bodies; States may provide more. **106th Amendment Act 2023** provides one-third reservation in Lok Sabha/State Assemblies (and Delhi Assembly), tied to its census/delimitation implementation trigger; it was **already enacted**, not a pending Bill, but not yet operating in the 2025 seat distribution.
- Address proxy representation, capacity, care burdens, wage gaps and data transparency. **2017 PYQ: Global Gender Gap Index—WEF (a); 2019: Global Competitiveness Report—WEF (c)**.

topics.title: Pokkali, integrated coastal farming and GIAHS
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Pokkali: saline rice–prawn rotation
- Indigenous **salinity-tolerant rice**, coastal **Ernakulam, Thrissur and Alappuzha, Kerala**; monsoon freshwater supports rice and drier brackish season supports prawns/shrimps on the same fields. **GI recognition 2008**; nutrient/tidal recycling reduces external inputs. Traditional organic practice does not itself establish every marketed lot has formal organic certification or medicinal efficacy.
- Tall rice and retained organic residues support the integrated cycle; protect local seed diversity, wetland habitat, food/income diversification and adaptation to salinisation. Source describes protein/fibre value without a comparative nutritional dataset.
- Challenges: scarce skilled labour, tools unsuitable for marshy fields, low farm-gate returns, encroachment, pollution and altered estuaries. Options: adapted tools, fair incentives/procurement, GI branding, youth skills and wetland restoration/protection.
## Compare regional systems
| System | Location and mechanism |
|---|---|
| Pokkali | Kerala saline rice–prawn seasonal rotation |
| Bheries | West Bengal brackish/freshwater fish ponds; associated regional rice/aquaculture systems, including Sundarbans and East Kolkata Wetlands, vary in water quality |
| Gajani | Coastal Karnataka reclaimed fields/polders and rice–fish practices |
| Khazan | Especially Goa tidal reclaimed estuarine lands, bunds and sluice-gate regulation of rice/fish/salt water; source also mentions Maharashtra |
| Kuttanad | Alappuzha/Kottayam/Pathanamthitta, Kerala; below-sea-level rice, polders/bunds, drainage and rice–fish livelihoods |
- Kuttanad diagram: major rivers **Pamba, Meenachil, Achankovil, Manimala** feed the Vembanad landscape; **Karappadam** alluvium, **Kari** organic-rich dark soils and **Kayal** reclaimed lake beds are local field categories. Below-sea-level farming here does not mean all Kerala rice fields lie below sea level.
## GIAHS and June 2025 snapshot
- **FAO Globally Important Agricultural Heritage Systems**, launched **2002**: safeguard living agricultural landscapes, biodiversity, knowledge, cultural heritage and resilient livelihoods through farmer/community participation, technical support and market opportunities.
- **95 systems in 28 countries** after May 2025 designations, a dated snapshot. [FAO, 21 May](https://www.fao.org/newsroom/detail/six-new-sites-recognized-as-globally-important-agricultural-heritage-systems/).
- India’s three sites at the June issue: **Kashmir saffron heritage** (Karewa soils), **Koraput traditional agriculture, Odisha** (millets, pulses, native paddy and tribal knowledge including Kondh/Paroja/Bonda and other communities), **Kuttanad below-sea-level farming, Kerala**.
- **2016 PYQ: (b) 2 only**—protect eco-friendly traditional farming, associated landscapes, biodiversity and knowledge. GIAHS does not automatically confer GI registration or mean replacement by modern methods; technical assistance/innovation compatible with living heritage remains possible.

topics.title: Urban mobility: public transport and lifecycle choices
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## June 2025 editorial: access before mode preference
- Rising urbanisation intensifies congestion, pollution and unequal access to work/services. Source projects over 60% urban by the 2060s; treat as a projection with an unstated methodology. Its **37% convenient public-transport access**, **35,000 buses versus two lakh needed** are source-context estimates, not universal current fleet totals.
- Metro systems need high ridership, affordable fares, first/last-mile access and integrated land use. Capital intensity and low farebox recovery do not by themselves establish lack of social value; assess congestion, emissions, access and urban form alongside finances.
- **PM-eBus Sewa (2023)** aims for **10,000 e-buses on PPP**; **Payment Security Mechanism (2024)** addresses operator-payment risk and is a distinct scheme. **PM E-DRIVE** supports electric mobility including buses, three-wheelers, trucks/ambulances and charging. Source's combined 1.1-lakh vehicle figure should not replace category-specific scheme limits. [10,000-bus scheme](https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/cabinet-approves-pm-ebus-sewa-for-augmenting-city-bus-operations-priority-to-cities-having-no-organized-bus-service/); [scheme distinction](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2081560).
## Compare technologies transparently
| Mode | Planning question |
|---|---|
| Metro | Corridor capacity, capital/operating costs, station access and integration |
| Tram | Electric rail, durable infrastructure; needs street space/right-of-way and sufficient demand |
| Trolleybus | Overhead power; corridor/wire investment versus flexibility |
| Battery e-bus | Flexible routing, charging/depot needs, battery replacement and grid emissions |
- Editorial favours trams/trolleybuses and proposes Kochi as a candidate. Its **70-year estimates: +45% tram returns versus 82% e-bus net loss** depend on financial assumptions; they are **not inherent profitability laws or proof electric buses always lose money**.
- Choose modes using lifecycle costs, passenger demand, energy/emissions, accessibility, service reliability and street constraints; integrate bus/rail/feeder routes, walking/cycling and common interchange hubs. Clear contracts, predictable funding, affordable fares and transparent private participation can reconcile viability with inclusion. An editorial discussion question without a year is not a UPSC PYQ.

topics.title: Aircraft black boxes and accident investigation
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Flight recorders
- Flight recorders preserve evidence for accident investigation; Australian scientist **David Warren** pioneered the combined flight-data/voice-recording concept. Bright orange casings aid recovery.
- **CVR:** cockpit conversations, radio traffic, alarms and ambient sounds. **FDR:** parameters such as speed, altitude, heading, engine performance, autopilot and attitude; the number recorded depends on aircraft/equipment standards.
- Crash-survivable memory uses strong steel/titanium protection and thermal insulation; underwater locator beacons assist searches. Installation is commonly towards the rear, but survival is never guaranteed; separate and combined recorder designs exist.
- June 2025 context: recorder recovery after the Ahmedabad Air India crash; recovery itself does not establish accident cause. DGCA ordered additional checks of Air India's Boeing 787 fleet, including fuel/control systems, cabin air-compressor components and engine/electronic controls.

## June 27 investigation status
- Contents reports **AI flight recorder data under analysis two weeks after the crash**. An older embedded clipping instead reports a recorder recovered from a hostel roof: distinguish recovery from later downloading/analysis and from a final finding of cause.
- Embedded clipping also reports **DGCA additional Boeing 787 checks**, including fuel/engine systems, hydraulic/flight controls and review of maintenance defects. These are precautionary oversight measures; they do not establish the crash's technical cause. Another clipping reports DNA-based victim identification, distinct from flight-data analysis.
- Source graphic advertises tolerance around **3,400 g, 1,100°C, 19,000-ft depth and 30-day beacon**; specifications vary with certified model/test duration and should not be treated as universal limits for all modern recorders.

topics.title: Radioisotope thermoelectric generators
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## RTG revision
- Radioisotope decay supplies heat, converted directly into electricity by thermoelectric materials; **RTGs are not miniature fission reactors**.
- **Pu-238** is a common heat-source isotope; applications include Voyager, New Horizons and Curiosity where durable power and weak sunlight favour radioisotope systems.
- PYQ 2024 supplied answer: **2 and 3 only (b)**. Retain the question's wording about weapons-development by-products, but do not confuse Pu-238 with the main weapons isotope Pu-239 or assume all modern Pu-238 is merely recovered weapons waste.

topics.title: Membrane bioreactors and wastewater treatment
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Mechanism and use
- **Biological wastewater treatment + microfiltration/ultrafiltration** combine in membrane bioreactors (MBRs), removing organic load and separating solids/microorganisms.
- Used for municipal sewage and industrial effluents; treated water can support reuse after meeting purpose-specific standards. Membrane treatment alone does not guarantee potable safety or removal of every dissolved contaminant.
- 2024 PYQ: **wastewater treatment technologies (d)**.

topics.title: Nandi Hills: heritage and tourism
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Place and heritage
- Hill fortress in **Chikkaballapur district, Karnataka**, about 60 km from Bengaluru. **Yoga Nandeeshwara Temple**, dedicated to Shiva at the summit, exhibits Dravidian architecture and Chola-period associations; the source cites Rajendra/Kulottunga Chola inscriptions and earlier Ganga associations.
- Heritage, elevated fortification and scenic tourism require conservation and carrying-capacity planning.
- **SAARC correction:** India's first hosted summit was the organisation's **second summit, Bangalore, 1986**; the first SAARC summit was Dhaka, 1985. Nandi Hills is associated with the Bangalore summit retreat, not the inaugural SAARC summit. [SAARC declarations](https://saarc-sec.org/resources/summit-declarations).

topics.title: Penna River and basin
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Map recall
- **Chenna Kesava hill, Nandidurg/Nandi Hills, Karnataka → Andhra Pradesh → Bay of Bengal**; an east-draining peninsular river with an initially northward course.
- Length about **597 km**; basin about **55,000 sq km**, spanning Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. Distinguish Penna from Tamil Nadu's Ponnaiyar/South Pennar.

topics.title: Forest Rights Act: recognition and implementation
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Statutory framework
- **Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006** addresses historical injustice and livelihood/tenure security. **Ministry of Tribal Affairs** is the nodal ministry; States implement it.
- Individual cultivation/residence rights recognise eligible pre-existing occupation, with **4 hectares as a ceiling**, not a fresh uniform grant. Community rights include minor forest produce, grazing, fishing and water use; **community forest resource rights** support protection, regeneration and management.
- Gram Sabha initiates claims/verification; Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees process/decide through the statutory framework, with State monitoring. No eviction before recognition/verification is completed under section 4(5).
- Delays, evidence burdens, wrongful rejection/eviction and pressure from conservation/infrastructure/mining projects require fair hearings, assistance and grievance redress.
## June 2025: dedicated FRA cells
- Source reports **324 district cells across 18 States/UTs**, plus State support, under **Dharti Aba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyaan**. These assist documentation, claimants/Gram Sabhas and data management; they do not replace statutory decision bodies.
- Reported sanctioned district counts: MP **55**, Chhattisgarh **30**, Telangana **29**, Maharashtra **26**, Assam **25**, Jharkhand **24**. MoTA grants: **₹8.67 lakh/district cell**, **₹25.85 lakh/State cell**.
- March 2025 source snapshot: **51.11 lakh claims**, **14.45% pending**; roughly **42% rejected among disposed claims**. These percentages have different denominators.
- Concern: parallel administrative structures could weaken Gram Sabha autonomy; preserve a clear assistance/decision boundary. The accompanying MoTA directive emphasises protection from unlawful eviction and grievance mechanisms.
- 2021 PYQ answer: **Ministry of Tribal Affairs (d)**.

## Chhattisgarh records: August 2025 concern
- RTI-based report found reductions in previously reported titles in at least **three districts over17 months**; officials attributed this to miscommunication/reporting corrections, denying actual loss of field titles. An aggregate data discrepancy alone does not establish legal cancellation of each claimant's right.
- Source **May 2025** snapshot across **30 districts:4.82 lakh individual titles,4,396 community forest-resource titles**. Embedded graphic reports **2,788 IFR titles missing from Bastar's records** and a **50% reduction in Rajnandgaon's CFR count within one month last year**; these are allegations/data comparisons requiring record reconciliation, not verified eviction totals.
- Reconcile registers with issued pattas/Gram Sabha records, audit changes and preserve reasons, accessible grievance redress and claimant assistance. Digitisation must not silently extinguish rights.
- **2019 PYQ:** bamboo is minor forest produce under FRA and ownership/collection/use/disposal rights are recognised; **2017 Indian Forest Act change concerned bamboo on non-forest land**, not unrestricted forest felling. **2 and 3 only (b)**. **2021 nodal-ministry PYQ: Tribal Affairs (d)**. Other FRA provisions repeat earlier notes.

topics.title: Oil palm and NMEO-OP
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Crop and trade
- African oil palm **Elaeis guineensis**, native to West/Central Africa, has high oil yield per hectare. Indonesia/Malaysia dominate production; India relies heavily on imports from them and Thailand.
- **Mesocarp/fruit pulp → palm oil; kernel → palm-kernel oil**. Uses include food, cosmetics, soaps, pharmaceuticals and biodiesel; kernel oil is not exclusively non-edible.
- Warm humid tropical conditions, ample rainfall and well-drained fertile soils favour the crop. Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Kerala are major Indian producers; Northeast/Andaman expansion needs water, biodiversity and land-use safeguards. The source's area/shares are dated estimates rather than current totals.
## NMEO–Oil Palm
- **Centrally sponsored scheme launched 2021** to reduce edible-oil import dependence; 2025–26 target: **additional 6.5 lakh hectares**, reaching about **10 lakh hectares**; CPO targets **11.2 lakh tonnes in 2025–26**, **28 lakh tonnes by 2029–30** are planned outcomes.
- **Viability Price** assures fresh-fruit-bunch remuneration, with viability-gap payments through DBT. Source support norms: planting **₹12,000→₹29,000/ha**, old-garden rejuvenation **₹250/plant**; special Northeast/Andaman support includes an additional **2% of CPO price**, terraces, fencing and associated works.
- Trade-off: high yields/import substitution versus plantation water demand, monocultures, habitat loss and chemical inputs; use suitable already-cleared land and transparent local consultation.
- PYQ recall: oil palm is African-origin, used in lipstick/perfume and biodiesel (**2021: statements 2,3**). Edible-oil imports exceeded domestic production in the 2018 question's reference period; blanket customs-duty exemption claim is false (**statement 1 only**). The supplied PDF omits answer-option sets for these two questions; review against the original papers before adding complete PYQs.

## August 2025 supply outlook
- Indonesia/Malaysia, roughly **85% of global supply** in source, face ageing plantations and farmers, slow subsidised replanting and higher domestic biodiesel demand. Report forecasts exports could fall **up to 20% by 2030**; a scenario, not an already-realised fall.
- Source peak yield **8–20 years** and **3–5-year income gap during replanting** explain smallholders' reluctance; alternatives include bridging finance, phased replacement and reliable planting material. Indonesian **2.5-million-ha replanting target/10% completion as of October 2024** and Malaysian **37% official versus over-50% industry ageing estimates** use different measures/periods.
- India risks import-price/food-inflation pressure; diversify suppliers/oils, improve domestic productivity and assess expansion's land/water/biodiversity costs. Source **9.2 million tonnes imports (2023–24), palm about 60% of edible-oil imports**, are dated estimates, not fixed shares.
- Repeated NMEO-OP targets/support are already in core notes. Source's starting CPO production **0.27 lakh tonnes** needs original-series/unit verification; do not treat this small baseline as established. [Original Cabinet targets](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1746943&lang=2&reg=48). Palm-kernel oil has edible as well as industrial uses; palm oil does not supply over half of all global vegetable oils under every measure.
- **2021 PYQ:** African origin makes statement 1 false; lipstick/perfume and biodiesel uses make **2,3 correct**. PDF again omits the full option set; preserve as revision and flag bank completion against original paper.

topics.title: Jumping spiders and taxonomic discoveries
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## June 2025 discovery
- **Spartaeus karigiri**, family **Salticidae**, subfamily **Spartaeinae**: reported from **Devarayanadurga, Karnataka**, and **Viluppuram, Tamil Nadu**, named for Karigiri/Elephant Hill. The species is catalogued in 2025. [World Spider Catalog](https://wsc.nmbe.ch/spec-data/71949).
- First Indian records reported for genera **Spartaeus and Sonoita**; do not extend this automatically to the whole subfamily. Sharp vision and predation involving invasion of other spiders' webs/aggressive mimicry differ from building orb webs for prey capture.
- **Sonoita cf. lightfooti** from Karnataka raises unresolved range-extension versus introduction questions; cf. signals provisional comparison, not certain species identification or proof of invasion.
- Source reports **Marpissa gangasagarensis (2005)** synonymised with **Phaeacius fimbriatus (1900)**: taxonomic revision avoids counting a known species twice.
- Reject the practice explanation that both discovery sites lie in the Western Ghats; Viluppuram is in eastern Tamil Nadu. Spider versus insect: **8 legs/two main body regions/no antennae** versus **6 legs/three regions/one antennal pair**.

topics.title: Animal classification and behaviour: PYQ recall
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Comparative recall
- **Orangutans** use sticks to extract insects/food; otters use stones for shells; sloth bears principally use snout/lips to feed on termites. Indian tree squirrels build dreys, cache food and have omnivorous diets; species/ecology matter.
- **Cicada, froghopper, pond skater:** insects, all Hemiptera. Cicadas have subterranean nymphs; froghopper nymphs form protective spittle; pond skaters exploit surface tension.
- **Ceylon frogmouth, coppersmith barbet, grey-chinned minivet, white-throated redstart:** birds. Frogmouth is nocturnal (Western Ghats/Sri Lanka); minivet/redstart recall Himalayan/Northeast habitats.
- **Mite, scorpion, spider:** Arachnida; crab is a crustacean. All are arthropods, so phylum alone does not distinguish the odd one out.
- **Peacock/Gooty tarantula, Poecilotheria metallica:** carnivorous arboreal spider with restricted Indian forest habitat; not an omnivorous crustacean. The historical Gooty collection locality should not be equated automatically with its entire extant habitat.
- Supplied answers: 2023 tool use **orangutan**, squirrel **only two**; 2024 insects **(c)**; 2020 birds **(a)**; 2014 odd-class **crab**; 2025 tarantula **2 and 3**.

topics.title: Medical Termination of Pregnancy: law and access
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Framework as discussed in June 2025
- **MTP Act 1971**, amended **2021**: legal termination on statutory grounds, including risk to life/grave injury to physical or mental health and serious fetal abnormality. Contraceptive-failure presumption extends to any woman and her partner; it is not confined to marriage.
- **Up to 20 weeks:** one RMP's good-faith opinion; **20–24 weeks:** two RMP opinions for prescribed categories, including sexual-assault survivors, minors, specified disabilities/illnesses, marital-status changes and fetal malformations. Supreme Court interpretation protects unmarried women's equal access; autonomy and statutory conditions must both be represented.
- For substantial fetal abnormalities diagnosed by a State/UT Medical Board, the ordinary gestational limit does not apply. **Section 5 separately permits immediately necessary life-saving termination**; therefore 'beyond 24 weeks only fetal abnormality' is incomplete.
- Ordinary authorised places include government hospitals **and approved private places**; the PDF's blanket exclusion of private hospitals is misleading. Confidentiality restricts identity disclosure except to legally authorised persons. [India Code](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/15312?locale=en), [section 5](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/6832/1/mtp-act-1971.pdf).
- Access barriers: delayed boards/referrals, rural service gaps, stigma, unclear operational protocols and clinician uncertainty. Timely care, informed consent, privacy and trained providers matter. Source's simplified foreign-country comparison is not a complete account of those jurisdictions.

topics.title: Natural rubber: cultivation, industry and governance
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Crop and production
- **Hevea brasiliensis**, native to Amazonian South America; latex is tapped from bark. A warm humid tropical crop: roughly **200–300 cm rainfall, 25–34°C, ~80% humidity**, deep well-drained acidic soils (approximately **pH 4.5–6**); flooding/high winds damage plantations.
- Kerala leads Indian production; Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Tripura, Assam and Meghalaya also contribute. Demand, especially from tyres/automotive industry, exceeds domestic output and requires imports. Source's **India third-largest producer/fourth consumer** and **Kerala >90%** claims are unreliable without a dated statistical table; do not memorise them.
- Other uses: gloves, footwear, seals/hoses, conveyor belts and consumer goods. Rubber's American origin is distinct from its later colonial transfer and present Asian production concentration.
## Constraints and response
- Untapped trees, labour shortages, weak prices and maintenance reduce output; source estimates **20–25% untapped** need a survey base. Heavy rain/dry spells affect tapping/yield; adapt clones, labour-saving techniques and training.
- EUDR raises traceability/deforestation-compliance requirements for relevant exports; expansion in the Northeast must assess ecological suitability and land/community rights.
- **Rubber Board:** statutory body under **Rubber Act 1947**, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, headquarters **Kottayam**; research, extension, training and development. Nutrient deficiency, including phosphorus deficiency, is a management problem—not a requirement that soil must be low in phosphorus.
- Old World = Europe/Asia/Africa; New World = Americas in historical European terminology. Indigenous American societies existed long before European arrival. 2019 PYQ group **tobacco, cocoa, rubber (a)** is American-origin.

## Kerala: beetle–fungus plantation threat
- July report identifies **Euplatypus parallelus**, a wood-boring ambrosia beetle of Central/South American origin, with **Fusarium ambrosium and F. solani** (the PDF writes “F. ambrosia”) in rubber plantations around **Iritty–Kannur**. It reports first Indian detection in **Goa cashew in 2012**; the new association is reported locally, not proof all Indian plantations are affected.
- Beetle tunnels carry fungal inoculum; fungi grow inside wood and provide food for beetles/larvae (**mutualism**). Tissue/xylem damage can cause leaf fall, trunk drying, reduced latex and tree death; deep galleries/systemic infection complicate treatment.
- Monitoring, sanitation/removal of infected material, appropriate traps and evaluated plant-protection measures need region-specific coordination among farmers, scientists and government. Antagonistic fungi/beneficial bacterial consortia are **proposed biological approaches**, not proven universal cures. Other woody hosts cited include cashew, coffee, mango, coconut and teak.
- The source's possible opportunistic Fusarium risk in immunocompromised people does not establish a demonstrated plantation-worker outbreak; assess occupational exposure separately.
- Taxonomic spelling: **Fusarium ambrosium**, also classified as *Neocosmospora ambrosia*; do not confuse ecological “ambrosia” with the printed species epithet. [EPPO taxon record](https://gd.eppo.int/taxon/FUSAAM/distribution/IN).

topics.title: SEEDS and India–Suriname development cooperation
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Development cooperation
- **SEEDS: Supply of Equipment for Efficient Development of SMEs**, MEA initiative donating machinery/tools to partner developing countries; promotes productive capacity, farmers' income, local value addition and South–South cooperation.
- June 2025 example: final consignment of **passion-fruit-processing machinery to Suriname**, source value **US$1 million**. Capacity building/maintenance and market access determine lasting benefits.
## Suriname map recall
- **Paramaribo** capital; **Dutch** official language; Surinamese dollar; northern South America with **Atlantic Ocean north, Guyana west, Brazil south, French Guiana east** (French Guiana is a French territory).
- **Suriname, Maroni/Marowijne and Courantyne rivers**; Bakhuys and Van Asch Van Wijck ranges; **Juliana Top in Wilhelmina Mountains** is highest point.
- Indian-origin population about **27%** in the source, with roots in nineteenth-century indentured migration; cultural/linguistic ties and Yoga strengthen relations.
- Programme/ministry PYQ revision: DPAP and Desert Development Programme belonged to Rural Development; **National Watershed Development Project for Rainfed Areas belonged to Agriculture**. Thus all three supplied pairs are incorrectly matched (**2014 answer d, None**), correcting the source's b. [Contemporary PIB account](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=78596).

topics.title: India, Cyprus and Croatia: June 2025 diplomacy
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## June 2025 diplomatic itinerary
- Cyprus visit preceded the Canada G7 outreach; Croatia visit was forthcoming in the June16 issue. Cyprus supports India's permanent UNSC-seat aspirations and counter-terrorism concerns; engage it through bilateral investment/trade and EU ties rather than reducing relations to rivalry with Türkiye.
- Cyprus President then **Nikos Christodoulides**; scheduled Council of EU presidency in **first half of 2026**. Source recalls Indira Gandhi's 1982 and Vajpayee's 2002 visits.
- **Croatia:** Adriatic/Balkan state, capital **Zagreb**; borders **Slovenia, Hungary, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro** (last omitted in source). **Dinaric Alps**, karst caves/sinkholes, highest peak **Dinara**; **Sava through Zagreb**, Drava joins Danube.
- Cultural links: Indology at University of Zagreb, Yoga/ISKCON; former Yugoslavia's non-aligned history supplies context but modern Croatia is an EU/NATO member.
- **2023 India–Croatia defence-cooperation MoU** supports further collaboration; do not rename it a completed combined defence-and-technology treaty. Ports/Adriatic access could support Europe connectivity; Croatia's role in **IMEC** was prospective, not a confirmed original corridor endpoint. [MEA May2025 background](https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/India-Croatia-May-2025.pdf).
## Sea-border PYQ recall
- Adriatic—Albania; Caspian—Kazakhstan; Mediterranean—Morocco are correct. **Croatia is not on the Black Sea; Syria is not on the Red Sea**; 2019 answer **1,3,4 (b)**.
- Adriatic littorals: Italy, Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Albania. Black Sea: Türkiye, Bulgaria, Romania, Ukraine, Russia, Georgia. Caspian: Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, Azerbaijan. Red Sea also has **Djibouti**, omitted in the source's short list.

## Bilateral significance: June 2025
- University of Zagreb's Indology and wider cultural contacts support people-to-people ties. Croatia's former Yugoslav context connects with India's non-aligned history; contemporary Croatia is an EU/NATO country, not automatically a NAM member.
- Adriatic ports and logistics offer potential India–Europe connectivity. **IMEC**, announced at G20 in **2023**, is a prospective cooperation framework; do not describe Croatia as an already operational mandated corridor endpoint.
- Source's claimed **2023 Raisina defence/technology MoU** requires verification rather than repetition as established treaty history. MEA's May 2025 bilateral account records cultural exchange renewals and science cooperation; separate proposed defence opportunities from signed instruments. [MEA bilateral brief](https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/India-Croatia-May-2025.pdf).
## Map recall
- Capital **Zagreb**; Adriatic coast in southeastern Europe. Land neighbours: **Slovenia, Hungary, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro** (the PDF omits Montenegro).
- **Dinaric Alps**, highest Croatian peak **Dinara**; limestone karst produces caves, sinkholes and underground drainage. **Sava** flows through Zagreb; **Drava** joins the Danube.
- Adriatic coastal States: **Italy, Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Albania**. The PDF's short list omits Italy and Bosnia.
- **2019 sea–country PYQ: (b), 1, 3 and 4 only**: Adriatic–Albania, Caspian–Kazakhstan and Mediterranean–Morocco correct; Croatia does not border the Black Sea, and Syria borders the Mediterranean rather than Red Sea.
- Caspian littoral: Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, Azerbaijan. Black Sea littoral: Türkiye, Bulgaria, Romania, Ukraine, Russia, Georgia. Red Sea also includes **Djibouti**, missing from the source list.

topics.title: Special Economic Zones and semiconductor reforms
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Framework
