- SEZ policy introduced **2000**; **SEZ Act 2005 and Rules2006** support exports, investment, employment and infrastructure. Deemed outside customs territory for authorised trade operations, while remaining Indian sovereign territory and subject to applicable laws.
- Benefits include duty-free authorised imports, single-window procedures and GST **zero-rating for authorised supplies**; zero-rating differs from a blanket exemption for every transaction. GIFT City's SEZ/IFSC illustrates specialised services.
- Source snapshot: **276 operational SEZs** and **US$163.69 billion exports in 2023–24**; retain reporting periods. DESH (**Development of Enterprise and Service Hubs**) was a proposed reform, not a replacement law already in force.
## 3 June2025 amendments
- Exclusive semiconductor/electronics-component SEZ minimum contiguous area **50→10ha** (Rule5); Board may relax encumbrance-free conditions for land mortgaged/leased to Central/State governments or their authorised agencies (Rule7), subject to conditions.
- Free-of-cost goods received/supplied can enter prescribed **NFE calculation**; Rule18 enables relevant units' domestic sales with applicable duties. Earlier DTA sales were not universally forbidden for every SEZ.
- **Micron, Sanand, Gujarat** and **Hubballi Durable Goods Cluster/Aequs, Karnataka** proposals: combined source investment **₹13,100 crore** (₹13,000cr and ₹100cr). These approvals are not proof production had begun.
- Correct source's **June2024** to **June2025**. [PIB,9June2025](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2135116&lang=2&reg=48).
- Constraints: high infrastructure/land costs, regulatory burdens, services/manufacturing imbalance, idle approved zones and environmental impacts. **Baba Kalyani committee2018** recommended employment/economic enclaves, outcome-based incentives, differentiated sector approaches and easier domestic integration/clearances.

topics.title: Rajasthan Cash Plus: maternal nutrition and behavioural support
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Model and implementation
- Combines **cash/DBT + Social and Behaviour Change Communication (SBCC)** through counselling, home visits, groups and digital/family outreach. Cash eases financial constraints; knowledge and services help translate it into nutrition/care.
- Source: pilot from **late2020** in **Udaipur,Banswara,Dungarpur,Pratapgarh,Baran**; statewide expansion **2022**; second-pregnancy support, annual programme outlay roughly **₹210crore**, target **3.5lakh women/year**. Distinguish scheme coverage from the evaluation sample.
- **2021–24 evaluation as reported:** early breastfeeding increased **49%** and reached about **90%**; counselling openness **+44%**, dietary diversity **+49%**, use of cash for nutrition **+54%**; **80%** reported improved nutrition access. These are reported changes, not automatically percentage-point gains or causal proof absent study design.
- Reported **3.3million** beneficiaries lacks clear cumulative/unit reconciliation with annual targeting; hold that total for verification. Incomplete data, remote access, poverty, literacy and monitoring gaps constrain scale; train frontline workers and track health/nutrition and respectful access.

topics.title: Nuclear power: global role and constraints
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Global role: June 2025 revision
- Nuclear fission plants have generated electricity since the 1950s. Nuclear supplies roughly **9% of global electricity** and is an important low-carbon source, with the US, China and France major producers. The PDF's 2023 generation figures must not be treated as 2025 output.
- Advantages: low operational carbon emissions, firm power, long plant lives and diversification of energy supply. Plants still need outages, cooling water, fuel services and grid integration; reliability is not literal uninterrupted operation.
- Constraints: high initial capital/financing cost, long construction and decommissioning, accident prevention/emergency response, radioactive-waste management and public trust. **Chernobyl 1986** and **Fukushima 2011** are key safety case studies.
- Bangladesh's Rooppur and Türkiye's Akkuyu exemplify newcomer programmes under construction at this date. The source's table of supposed 2025 new operational reactors is not a reliable commissioning list; distinguish construction, first criticality and grid connection.

## Indian fleet: correct the stale snapshot
- Source's **8.18GW/24reactors/19PHWR+2BWR+2PWR** mixes dates and has inconsistent arithmetic. **RAPP7 declared commercial15April2025**: July comparison is **24units/8,780MW excluding long-shut RAPS1**, or **25units/8,880MW including its100MW**. Fleet excluding RAPS1: **20PHWRs,2BWRs,2VVERs**. [NPCIL annual-report record](https://npcil.nic.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/file/Annual_Report_2024_25_22082025_01.pdf).
- Map recall: **Narora—UP;Rawatbhata/Rajasthan station—Rajasthan;Kakrapar—Gujarat;Tarapur—Maharashtra;Kaiga—Karnataka;Madras/Kalpakkam andKudankulam—TamilNadu**. Fleet counts include units not generating continuously; installed capacity is not annual output.
- Source **2.8%electricity in2022–23** is historical. Its 'tripleby2030' is a policy aspiration/snapshot, not achieved output or a guaranteed delivery schedule; **100GW by2047** remains a target.
- Closed cycle: reprocess → recover uranium/plutonium → refabricate/reuse; resource efficiency must be weighed against cost,proliferation/security and residual high-level waste. SMR generic benefits and fuel-cycle basics repeat the common topics.

topics.title: Shipki La: border tourism and trade
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Location and June 2025 development
- Himalayan pass in **Kinnaur, Himachal Pradesh**, on the India–Tibet (China) border; elevation about **3,930 m**. Source reports domestic border tourism opened with Aadhaar-based identification and removal of the earlier permit requirement; this is a **June 2025 development**, not proof of a 2024 opening.
- Trade was historically linked to **Bushahr/Rampur and Guge**. Wool, livestock, hides, yak hair, borax, turquoise and religious objects came from Tibet; grain, pulses, spices, vegetables, utensils, timber and iron goods went from India.
- Oral agreements, shared Tibetan Buddhist traditions, monasteries, festivals and pastoral ties sustained local relationships. Small national trade volumes can still matter greatly to border livelihoods and cultural continuity.
- The 1962 war interrupted trade, but later border trading resumed; COVID-19 closed it again in 2020. The source's claim of no commerce for decades is misleading. Tourism reopening is distinct from resuming international trade.
- Potential gains: border employment, reduced outmigration and people-to-people links. A shorter Kailash–Mansarovar route remains a **proposal requiring bilateral arrangements**, not an operational pilgrimage route.
- **2007 PYQ: Nathu La (Sikkim)** reopened for India–China trade in **July 2006**; distinguish it from Shipki La.

topics.title: Arabian Desert and the Green Arabia hypothesis
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Geography and ecology
- Arabian Desert: about **2.33 million km²**, largely Saudi Arabia and adjoining Arabian Peninsula States; among the largest hot deserts, not the second-largest desert if polar deserts are included.
- **Rub al-Khali/Empty Quarter**: vast sand sea; **An-Nafud** in the north; **Ad-Dahna** links major sand regions. Hyper-arid interiors, extreme heat and seasonal northwesterly **shamal** winds shape the landscape; rainfall varies, so <33 mm is not universal.
- Drought-adapted vegetation includes acacia, ghaf, saltbush and date palms in suitable sites; fauna include Arabian oryx, gazelles, camels, wolves, hyenas, caracals, dhub lizards, vipers and falcons.
## Evidence for wetter phases
- An **April 2025 speleothem study** found recurring humid intervals over approximately **8 million years** in central Arabia, rather than continuous desert conditions. Mineral deposits and fluid-inclusion isotope evidence indicate past infiltration and changing moisture sources.
- Dating used **uranium–lead for older samples and uranium–thorium for younger ones**; the entire multi-million-year sequence cannot be dated by U–Th alone. Wet intervals could facilitate plant/animal dispersal; they do not imply humans lived throughout all 8 million years. [Original study](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-08859-6).
- Complementary evidence: **Baynunah Formation, UAE**, fossils of water-dependent/savanna fauna; **Jubbah, Saudi Arabia**, palaeolakes, tools and early-human occupation evidence.
- Size revision: **Great Sandy < Gobi < Arabian < Sahara**. The printed UPPSC 2023 question lacks its full alternative answer sets; retain this explanation without reconstructing missing options.

topics.title: Levant: eastern Mediterranean geography
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Map recall
- The **Levant** roughly denotes the **eastern Mediterranean shores**: Syria, Lebanon, Israel, Palestine and Jordan, with boundaries sometimes extending into adjoining Türkiye.
- A historical crossroads between Africa, Asia and Europe; relevant to ancient civilisations, trade and contemporary Syrian/Israel–Palestine conflicts.
- French **lever**, to rise, evokes the eastern rising sun; Arabic **al-Mashriq** is related in meaning but geographically broader.
- **2022 Prelims: (a)** eastern Mediterranean shores; neither the entire Mediterranean nor the Persian Gulf/Horn of Africa.

topics.title: Global South and India’s development diplomacy
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Meaning and common concerns
- **Global South** is a broad political/development category, mainly countries in Africa, Asia and Latin America, rather than a literal southern-hemisphere division or a homogeneous bloc. Shared concerns include colonial legacies, poverty/inequality, commodity dependence, access to technology and unequal influence in global institutions.
- Global North broadly refers to richer industrialised economies, including Australia and New Zealand despite their latitude. The source associates **Third World** with Alfred Sauvy (1952) and the modern Global South formulation with Carl Oglesby (1969); the Cold War term initially related to bloc alignment.
- Growing influence of India, China and Brazil supports multipolarity, but national interests differ. Comparisons of BRICS/G7 economic size require a **PPP versus nominal GDP** distinction; a prediction about the four largest economies in 2030 is not an observed fact.
- Priorities: climate finance and fair transition, food/fuel security after the Ukraine war, debt sustainability, fairer trade, development finance and institutional reform. BRI infrastructure can offer connectivity while creating project-specific debt/governance risks; a universal debt-trap claim is not established.
## India’s initiatives
- At the **January 2023 Voice of Global South Summit**, India announced a Centre of Excellence, Science and Technology Initiative, **Aarogya Maitri** disaster/health support, Young Diplomats Forum and Global South scholarships.
- These combine knowledge sharing, capacity building, health solidarity and educational/diplomatic networks. Climate-fund inadequacy is an equity concern; use the correct named fund rather than the source's generic “Green Energy Fund”.

## Five-country tour planned for 2–9 July 2025
- Itinerary announced before this issue: **Ghana 2–3 July → Trinidad & Tobago 3–4 → Argentina 4–5 → Brazil 5–8 → Namibia 9 July**. Describe the tour's agenda prospectively, not as already signed outcomes. [27 June announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2140314&lang=2&reg=48).
| Partner | Agenda/geographic recall |
|---|---|
| Ghana | West Africa/Gulf of Guinea; Accra; neighbours Côte d’Ivoire, Burkina Faso, Togo. Agriculture, vaccines, digital infrastructure, minerals and ECOWAS/AU outreach |
| Trinidad & Tobago | Caribbean, near Venezuela; diaspora/culture, education, technology, small enterprises and climate cooperation. First **bilateral** Indian PM visit since 1999; Manmohan Singh attended CHOGM in 2009 |
| Argentina | Defence, agriculture, oil/gas, renewables, trade/investment and mining. **Lithium Triangle = Argentina–Bolivia–Chile**; lithium is not a rare-earth element |
| Brazil | BRICS summit, global-governance reform, climate/COP30, health, AI and proposed defence cooperation (communications, patrol vessels, air defence, artillery and submarine support) |
| Namibia | Southern Atlantic coast; Windhoek; uranium/critical minerals, agriculture, digital payments, industry and tribute to Sam Nujoma, who died February 2025 |
- Shared rationale: South–South cooperation, local value addition/jobs, defence/economic diversification, diaspora links and counter-terrorism. Suggested vaccine/payment/arms agreements remain proposals in this issue; Modi had met Javier Milei before, so “first meeting” is incorrect.
- Map recall: **Port of Spain—Trinidad & Tobago; Brasília—Brazil (Rio is the summit city); Namibia borders Angola, Zambia, Botswana and South Africa**, facing the Atlantic. Lithium-triangle salars shown include Uyuni (Bolivia), Atacama (Chile), and Olaroz/Jujuy (Argentina).

topics.title: G7: membership, institutions and summit diplomacy
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Composition and operation
- **US, Canada, UK, France, Germany, Italy, Japan**; EU participates alongside them. Informal forum: no founding treaty or permanent secretariat; annual rotating presidency, consensus-based political coordination, and no supranational lawmaking power.
- First **G6 summit in France, 1975**, amid the oil/financial crises; Canada joined **1976**. Russia's progressive inclusion produced the G8, whose first summit under that name was **Birmingham 1998**; Russia's participation was suspended **2014** after Crimea's annexation.
- The EU first participated in 1977 and has participated in all working sessions since **Ottawa 1981**. It is a regular participant, not merely an occasional guest like invited outreach countries.
- Agenda: economic stability, trade, security, health, climate and development. Economic influence is substantial but source percentages for global wealth/GDP lack a common reference year and should not be memorised as timeless shares.
- The printed “UPSC 2023” G7 exercise has a **disputed attribution and faulty key**: its 1998 G8 statement should not be dismissed just because Russia joined political discussions in 1997. Keep for review rather than label it a verified UPSC PYQ. [Canadian G7 material](https://g7.canada.ca/assets/ea689367/Attachments/student-teacher/2025-mock-g7-summit-teacher-workbook.pdf).
- **2020 G20 PYQ: Argentina, Mexico, South Africa, Türkiye (a)**. Malaysia, New Zealand, Iran, Vietnam and Singapore were not G20 country members in that question.

topics.title: Single-use plastics, microbeads and circularity
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Problem and policy
- SUP products are intended for one/few uses before disposal: bags/films, cutlery, straws and other packaging; medical disposables also require safe segregated handling. Persistence, fragmentation into microplastics, blocked drains and wildlife exposure make brief use costly environmentally.
- India's **2021 rule amendment** prohibited identified low-utility/high-litter SUP items **from 1 July 2022**. Packaging outside that list is governed through plastic-waste rules and **2022 EPR guidelines**; this is not a ban on all plastics. Multilayer packaging poses recycling challenges, but not every multilayer structure has identical recyclability. [MoEFCC account](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1882855&lang=2&reg=48).
- Barriers: cheap incumbent materials, costly/inaccessible substitutes, livelihood dependence, poor segregation/collection and uneven enforcement. Responses: transparent compliance data and inspections, reuse/refill systems, support for alternatives and reliable collection/recycling. A ban on bags of every thickness is a **proposal in the source**, not the prevailing national rule.
- International examples include Bangladesh's 2002 thin-bag ban and EU restrictions taking effect in 2021. **UNEA resolution 5/14, 2 March 2022**, launched negotiations for a legally binding plastics instrument; it was not itself a completed treaty signed by 124 countries. [UNEP resolution](https://wedocs.unep.org/items/2d9aca95-4286-4b5e-a7db-984df28553ea).
## Microbeads and PYQ
- Manufactured tiny plastic particles, commonly PE/PP/polystyrene, used as scrubbers in some personal-care/cleaning products; often <5 mm. Escape through wastewater depends on treatment, rather than all plants filtering none.
- Ingestion can expose aquatic organisms and food webs to persistent plastics and associated contaminants. **2019 Prelims: (a), harmful to marine ecosystems**.

## Industry influence and inclusive recycling
- July editorial compares plastics lobbying with tobacco-industry tactics: shifting responsibility to consumers, sponsoring favourable science/PR, misleading green claims and resisting production controls. These are analytical allegations, not proof every producer or recycling technology behaves identically.
- “Biodegradable/compostable” claims require specified conditions and actual collection/treatment systems; recycling claims should state material, technical feasibility and economic limits. Transparent conflicts of interest, producer accountability, reuse and reliable collection complement informed consumers.
- Informal collectors/sorters face toxic exposures, insecure work and poor social protection. PDF's **70% recycling contribution**, **36% lobbyist increase at INC-3** and Asia-triples-by-2060 claim lack full denominator/baseline here; do not treat as reconciled current national totals.

## INC-5.2: negotiations in progress
- **Geneva, opened 5 August 2025**, originally scheduled through 14 August; resumed fifth session follows Busan 2024. On this issue date negotiations were ongoing, not an adopted global plastics treaty. [UNEP opening account](https://www.unep.org/en/news-and-stories/press-release/resumed-fifth-session-negotiations-global-plastic-pollution-treaty).
- Full lifecycle means **production/raw polymers → product design → use → disposal/waste management**. Plenary, contact/technical groups and stakeholder input negotiate articles; bracketed text marks unresolved language.
- Fault lines: production limits/chemicals, binding versus voluntary measures, finance, compliance, equity and national capabilities. A legally binding instrument can contain both binding and voluntary approaches; the resolution does not guarantee every clause is mandatory.
- Source describes India opposing production caps/fixed phase-out dates, defending development needs and supporting waste management/EPR and just transition. Separate this negotiating position from an agreed treaty obligation; the source's “like-minded” country list is a contemporaneous alignment, not formal treaty membership.
- Practice: INC **C (2,3)**; UNEA 5/14 description **B**. March 2022 is the mandate date; INC work began later in 2022.

topics.title: India’s carbon emissions: sectors and comparison
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## 2025 PYQ revision
- India's per-capita CO₂ emissions are **well above 0.5 tonnes**, though below many richer economies. Per-capita values need a year and accounting boundary; the source's ~1.9 tonnes is an illustrative older estimate.
- In the question's **fuel-combustion/Asia-Pacific** comparison India follows China; electricity and heat producers are the largest source category. Distinguish total emissions, per-capita emissions and sector-specific measures.
- Printed **2025 Prelims key: (c), II and III only**; statement I is false. Historical question context is not a claim that every contemporary emissions dataset uses identical boundaries.

topics.title: Cocoa cultivation and West African producers
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Commodity recall
- Cocoa requires warm, humid tropical conditions, fertile soils and adequate rainfall. **Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana**, both West African, are the two countries identified by the **2024 Prelims question: (c)**.
- Other important producers include Ecuador, Nigeria and Indonesia. Annual country rankings/volumes can shift with harvests and weather; source rounded production figures lack a common crop-year label.
- Algeria/Morocco and Botswana/Namibia are largely too arid for the role suggested; Madagascar/Mozambique are not the top pair in that question.

topics.title: Lightning, thunder and disaster risk
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Mechanism
Water/ice collisions + convective updrafts → charge separation in a thundercloud → electrical discharge when the field is sufficient → air heats rapidly and expands → shock wave heard as **thunder**.
- Typical cloud structure has positive charge higher up and negative charge below, though real storms are more complex. Discharge may be intra-cloud, inter-cloud or cloud-to-ground; cloud-to-ground strikes are a direct surface hazard. In-cloud lightning is still hazardous to aviation.
- A properly earthed conductor offers a protected current path; protection is not a guarantee against every strike or a reason to shelter under an isolated tree.
## India and prevention
- Northeast/eastern India have high activity; deaths are also concentrated in exposed rural populations in central/eastern States. Frequency of lightning and number of deaths are different risk measures. Source cites >2,800 deaths in 2021, about 40% of deaths attributed to forces of nature in that dataset.
- Warming, convection, urban heat, land use and aerosols can influence storms; the source's **12% per °C** is a study-based projection, not a universal measured rule for India.
- IMD warnings/nowcasts and the Lightning Resilient India Campaign support early action; warning lead time and local accuracy vary. Improve last-mile alerts, safe shelters, school/farm-worker awareness and building earthing.
- **2013 Prelims: (d)**. Thunder comes from rapidly expanding lightning-heated air, not clouds colliding/separating or upward motion alone.

topics.title: Lake Maracaibo and Catatumbo lightning
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Location and lightning hotspot
- **Northwestern Venezuela**; Catatumbo River enters Maracaibo, a large lake/estuarine basin connected to the Caribbean via the Gulf of Venezuela.
- **Catatumbo lightning / Beacon of Maracaibo / Everlasting Storm**: frequent nocturnal thunderstorms, especially in the wetter part of the year. Warm moist lowland air and surrounding mountain circulation favour convergence and convection.
- Source cites roughly **260 storm days annually**, with strong October activity; these are descriptive averages, not guaranteed daily conditions. Lightning density, not simply total storm count, underlies its hotspot designation; sailors historically used the glow for navigation.
- Lake–country revision: **Maracaibo—Venezuela; Onega—Russia; Michigan—USA; Baikal—Russia**. Michigan lies entirely in the USA; Baikal is the deepest freshwater lake. The UPPSC 2023 Onega–Canada pairing is false.

topics.title: Synthetic aperture radar and NISAR
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## How SAR forms an image
Microwave pulse from moving satellite/aircraft → surface backscatter → coherent measurements at successive positions → signal processing synthesises a large aperture → high-resolution image.
- Active microwave sensing works day/night and through cloud/smoke/haze; performance in rain depends on wavelength/intensity. It does not mean all radar penetrates every material.
- Repeated observations reveal floods, ground deformation, earthquakes, landslides, glaciers and crop/forest change; interpretation depends on geometry, wavelength and processing.
## NISAR: June 2025 context
- **NASA–ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar**, then a forthcoming mission planned from Sriharikota. NASA contributes **L-band SAR**, reflector/boom and key electronics; ISRO contributes **S-band SAR**, spacecraft and launch services (source diagram).
- Repeat mapping is designed on a **12-day cycle**, with ascending/descending observations; the source's “twice every 12 days” should not be read as a guaranteed uniform cadence for every surface point.

## July 21 launch announcement, reported July 22
- NISAR then scheduled for **30 July 2025,17:40 IST**, aboard **GSLV-F16** from Sriharikota; source prelaunch specification **2,392 kg,743 km sun-synchronous orbit,98.4° inclination**.
- **12 m deployable mesh reflector** serves L/S-band radar; source **242 km swath**, SweepSAR and modified **I3K bus**. These are planned mission/configuration figures, not proof launch or commissioning had occurred byJuly 22. [ISRO dated prelaunch release](https://new1.isro.gov.in/ISRO_HINDI/Mission_GSLVF16_NISAR.html).
- Applications include deformation/subsidence, shoreline, ecosystem/vegetation, ice and disaster monitoring; retain the core note's qualified 12 day repeat-cycle/rain-penetration explanation.

## Image-only July clipping
- The old infographic's **“expected launch 2024”** is stale; launch remained forthcoming at this issue date. Source describes a planned science phase of about **three years**; this is a mission-design duration, not proof of commissioning. Prior July coverage already records the upcoming 30 July launch, dual L/S-band radar, 12 m reflector and ground/ice/forest monitoring, so those facts are not duplicated here.

## July 29 prelaunch revision
- Mission remained scheduled for **30 July, 17:40 IST** in this issue, not already launched. **90-day commissioning** is a planned testing/calibration phase; the quoted five-year science phase is a design period, not elapsed operation.
- The embedded orbit graphic mislabels geostationary orbit as 'LEO': geostationary altitude is about **35,786 km**, while NISAR's planned **743 km sun-synchronous polar orbit** is in low Earth orbit. Sun-synchronous means near-consistent local solar crossing time, not a stationary spacecraft. A **12-day repeat** is not continuous real-time flood surveillance.
- NASA specifies **at least three years of L-band science** after commissioning; ISRO requires **five years for S-band**. Distinguish partner requirements from the generic five-year figure. [NASA mission design](https://nisar.jpl.nasa.gov/mission/observatory/overview/).

topics.title: Marsupials: development and distribution
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Identification and PYQ
- Mammals whose young are born relatively undeveloped and continue developing attached to teats, often within a pouch. Examples: **kangaroos, koalas, wombats, Tasmanian devils** in Australasia; **opossums** in the Americas.
- Occupy forests, deserts, wetlands and savannas, and coexist with predators; not confined to predator-free montane grasslands. India has **no native marsupials**.
- **2023 Prelims: (c)** — statement I is correct, statement II incorrect. Pouches are common but not universal across all marsupials.

topics.title: Cobia and marine cage aquaculture
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Species and habitat
- **Rachycentron canadum**, also cobia/black kingfish/crab-eater; marine finfish found in tropical/subtropical seas and coastal/brackish waters, migratory within the sea (**oceanodromous**).
- Naturally present in **Indian waters**: the source's claim it is not native to India is incorrect. MPEDA illustration specifically notes Tamil Nadu/Kerala coastal availability. Avoid an absolute pelagic-versus-demersal dichotomy because it occurs in different coastal habitats. [CMFRI research catalogue](https://eprints.cmfri.org.in/view/subjects/cobia1.html).
## Mariculture potential
- Rapid growth (source **6–8 kg in a year** under suitable farming conditions), high-value white meat and export demand make it attractive for sea cages; used in markets including Taiwan/Japan and sashimi preparations.
- CMFRI has developed breeding/seed-production and farming protocols. Cage culture requires suitable sites, healthy seed, feed, biosecurity and environmental carrying capacity; fast growth alone does not assure profits. Link to India's mariculture/PMMSY and Blue Revolution context. [CMFRI mariculture](https://www.cmfri.org.in/division/mariculture).
- **2022 PYQ: golden mahseer is a fish (a)**; Indian nightjar, spoonbill and white ibis are birds. Cobia is a marine fish; mahseer is a freshwater fish.

topics.title: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana: rural and urban housing
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Rural and urban tracks
| Aspect | PMAY-Gramin | Original PMAY-Urban |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start | IAY restructured from **1 April 2016** | **25 June 2015** |
| Ministry | Rural Development | Housing and Urban Affairs |
| Purpose | Pucca houses/basic amenities for rural homeless or kutcha/dilapidated-house households | Urban affordable housing, including slum households |
| Selection/features | SECC 2011 deprivation, Gram Sabha verification, geo-tagged monitoring | Female/joint ownership emphasis; statutory towns/planning areas |
- Rural priority groups include SC/STs, freed bonded labourers, vulnerable poor households, eligible defence/paramilitary families, persons with disabilities and minorities, subject to scheme criteria.
- PMAY-G cost sharing: generally **60:40** Centre:State, **90:10** NE/Himalayan arrangements, and central funding for relevant UT arrangements. Avoid treating the source's simplified J&K/UT table as a timeless universal funding rule.
- **Original PMAY-U** four verticals: in-situ slum redevelopment using land as resource; credit-linked interest subsidy; affordable housing in partnership; beneficiary-led construction/enhancement. Original AHP/BLC central support was ₹1.5 lakh per eligible EWS house. Source CLSS examples: 6.5% subsidy up to ₹6 lakh EWS/LIG loan, 4% on ₹9 lakh MIG-I, 3% on ₹12 lakh MIG-II; historical windows/eligibility apply.
## June 18 development: PMAY-U 2.0
- CSMC approved **2,34,864 homes across nine States**, taking total PMAY-U 2.0 sanctions to about **7.10 lakh**. States: Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh. [MoHUA, 18 June 2025](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2137416&lang=2&reg=48).
- This clipping concerns **Urban 2.0**, even though placed beside rural background in the PDF. “Housing for All by 2022” is an original target, not a claim that the programme ended or achieved universality in 2022. Source March 2023 rural figures (2.85 crore sanctioned/2.22 crore complete) and undated original-urban dashboard figures (118.64/83.67 lakh) are older snapshots, not June 2025 progress.

topics.title: DAY-NRLM: self-help groups and rural livelihoods
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Mechanism and PYQ
- **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission** organises rural poor households, especially women, into SHGs and supports skills, financial inclusion/bank linkage, micro-enterprises, entrepreneurship and market/service access.
- **2012 Prelims: (b), statement 2 only**. Its core approach is strengthening SHGs and skill development; the listed options about directly setting up large numbers of factories or universally giving seeds/fertiliser/pumps free do not describe the Mission.
- Source's comparison is also overbroad: **PM-KISAN is income support and PMFBY is crop insurance**, neither a universal free-input supply scheme.

topics.title: National arts Akademies: literature, performance and visual arts
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Sahitya Akademi
- National Academy of Letters, **1954**, autonomous Ministry of Culture institution; promotes Indian multilingual literature through original-work and translation awards. Recognises **24 languages: 22 Eighth Schedule languages + English + Rajasthani**.
- Sahitya Akademi Fellowship is its highest honour; yearly literary awards are distinct. **Bal Sahitya Puraskar** recognises children's literature; **Yuva Puraskar** encourages young authors (up to 35 under its rules). **Gramalok** supports rural literary engagement and **Dalit Chetna** highlights marginalised voices.
- June 2025 clipping: **23 Yuva and 24 Bal Sahitya recipients** announced; examples include Yuva winners **Advait Kottary (English), Parvati Tirkey (Hindi), Lakshmihar (Tamil), Prasad Suri (Telugu)**; Bal winners **Nitin Kushalappa M.P. (English), Sushil Shukla (Hindi), Tridib Kumar Chattopadhyay (Bengali), K. Shivalingappa Handihal (Kannada), Vishnupuram Saravanan (Tamil)**. Award includes copper plaque and **₹50,000** as reported.
## Sangeet Natak Akademi
- Ministry of Education resolution **31 May 1952**; inaugurated/functional **1953**; autonomous national performing-arts academy now under Culture. Covers music, dance, theatre, folk/tribal arts, puppetry and scholarship.
- Highest honour: **Akademi Ratna Fellowship**; source cites ₹3 lakh, copper plaque and angavastram. Annual **Akademi Puraskar**: ₹1 lakh plus plaque/angavastram. Fellowship rules and monetary values are dated, not constitutional provisions. [Official institutional history](https://sangeetnatak.gov.in/sections/drama).
- Established **NSD, New Delhi (1959)**; **JN Manipur Dance Academy, Imphal (1954)**; **Kathak Kendra, New Delhi (1964)**. NSD later became autonomous; founding affiliation does not imply it remains a department of SNA.
## Lalit Kala Akademi
- National Academy of Art, New Delhi, inaugurated **5 August 1954** by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad; registered as a **society on 11 March 1957**. Society registration does not confer “statutory-body” status. Visual arts include painting, sculpture, prints and photography. [Official history](https://lalitkala.gov.in/).
- Printed **2009 PYQ**: NSD founded by SNA in 1959 and Sahitya Akademi Fellowship highest honour — both true; source omits alternative answer options, so do not invent them for JSON.

topics.title: Rice: seasons, growing conditions and exports
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Cultivation and distribution
- Major staple, predominantly **kharif**, needing high temperature (source >25°C), humidity and ample water; rainfall above 100 cm is favourable, while irrigation permits growing in drier regions.
- Suitable climates allow two/three annual crops: **Aus** pre-monsoon, **Aman** principal monsoon and **Boro** winter/irrigated crop in West Bengal. Crop calendar terminology varies by region.
- Important producers include West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh and Punjab; high-yield regions also include Haryana, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. PDF production map is explicitly **2016–17**, not a June 2025 State ranking; its ~25% cropped-area statement is only a rounded background estimate.
- For this historical question context India is the **second-largest producer after China** and leading exporter of basmati/non-basmati rice. **2019 Prelims: India (b)** was largest exporter over the preceding five years; avoid converting a dated question into an eternal ranking.

topics.title: Tea cultivation, Tea Board and export performance
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Crop and regions
- **Camellia sinensis**; origins in the China–northeast India–northern Myanmar region. **International Tea Day: 21 May**.
- Warm humid tropical/subtropical climate, approximately **20–30°C**, **150–300 cm well-distributed rain**, slightly acidic well-drained porous soils; frost/extreme heat are harmful. Management and cultivar affect these ranges.
- Assam: Brahmaputra/Assam Valley and Cachar; West Bengal: **Darjeeling, Dooars, Terai**; southern production: **Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka**, notably Nilgiris. India is a major producer/consumer and black-tea supplier; most output is consumed domestically.
- **Darjeeling Tea** was India's first GI-registered product; premium origin protection is distinct from a generic variety name.
## Institutions and 2024 exports
- **Tea Board**, statutory body under the **Tea Act 1953**, constituted **1954**, Commerce Ministry; HQ **Kolkata**. Functions include industry development, producer support and export promotion.
- Source/Akashvani March 2025 reporting places **2024 exports at 255 million kg**, about 10% above 231.69 million kg in 2023, and describes India as second-largest exporter after Kenya, surpassing Sri Lanka. Preserve this as a **dated reported ranking**, with product coverage/China comparison requiring care. [Akashvani report](https://newsonair.gov.in/india-achieves-significant-milestone-in-global-tea-industry-becomes-worlds-2nd-largest-exporter-of-tea-in-2024/).
- Main markets include Iraq/West Asia, UAE, Iran, Russia, US and UK; exports predominantly black tea. The source's percentages/overseas-office list have no clear data date and are not fixed institutional facts.

topics.title: Strait of Hormuz: geography and energy security
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Location and shipping
**Persian Gulf → Strait of Hormuz → Gulf of Oman → Arabian Sea**.
- Strait between **Iran and Oman's Musandam Peninsula**; UAE lies near the southern approaches. About **33 km** wide at narrowest point; traffic separation lanes are narrow and heavily used.
- Critical outlet for Persian Gulf oil producers and Qatar's LNG. Conflict/blockade can disrupt supply, freight/insurance and energy prices, affecting importing countries including India.
## Correct denominator: June 2025
- EIA's **16 June 2025** account: **2024 flow ~20 million barrels/day**, equal to about **20% of global petroleum-liquids consumption**; the PDF incorrectly labels this simply 20% of seaborne oil trade. Use a common year and denominator when comparing flows.
- Saudi and UAE pipelines offer limited bypass capacity; EIA estimated **~2.6 million b/d available additional capacity**, far smaller than total strait flows. This limits complete substitution. Qatar is a leading LNG exporter; the source's claim it is unqualified world number one is not reliable for 2024. [EIA June 16 analysis](https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=65504).

topics.title: Shanghai Cooperation Organisation: membership and India
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Origins and institutions
- Shanghai Five (1996): China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan; SCO founded **15 June 2001 in Shanghai**, adding Uzbekistan. Origins include border confidence-building and regional security after the Soviet breakup.
- **June 2025 membership: ten**—the six founders plus India and Pakistan (2017), Iran (2023), Belarus (2024). Afghanistan and Mongolia were observers. Do not revise from the source's pre-Belarus nine-member snapshot. [SCO 2024 accession statement](https://eng.sectsco.org/20240704/1460010.html).
- Council of Heads of State is the highest decision-making body; Council of Heads of Government handles cooperation including economic priorities. Permanent bodies: **Secretariat, Beijing**, and **Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS), Tashkent**; exercises, intelligence and cooperation against terrorism, extremism and trafficking.
## India's interests and constraints
- Access to Central Asian partners and dialogue on security, Afghanistan, connectivity, trade and energy; participation can support strategic autonomy in a multipolar setting.
- China–Pakistan tensions, sovereignty concerns over BRI, uneven connectivity and balancing Russia/China constrain benefits. India did not endorse BRI in the 2024 declaration. [Astana declaration](https://eng.sectsco.org/20240709/1438929.html).
- Source's roughly 40% world population and US$23-trillion GDP are approximate dated estimates; membership and nominal/PPP/year definitions affect such totals. SCO is not a collective-defence alliance.

## Membership PYQ
- **2022 PYQ: AIIB, MTCR and SCO—all three (d)**. India: AIIB founding membership 2016, MTCR 2016, SCO 2017. Background repeats June 20 notes; Belarus was already the tenth member in June 2025.

## June 27 development
- Source reports **India declined to sign the SCO Defence Ministers' joint statement** because the Pahalgam attack was omitted; failure to reach consensus prevented adoption. This demonstrates the limits of regional counter-terrorism cooperation when members differ on terrorism narratives; it does not mean India left SCO.
- Existing ten-member list, RATS/Secretariat and India interests apply. **2022 membership PYQ: (d), all three**—India belongs to AIIB, MTCR and SCO. The complete question was already captured from the June24 issue, so it is not duplicated in the bank.

topics.title: Alcohol control: public health and federal policy
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Health burden and determinants
- Alcohol raises cancer, injury, mental-health, suicide and violence risks; dependence affects livelihoods and families. No consumption level can be guaranteed risk-free; risk varies with dose, pattern and context. [WHO alcohol factsheet](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/alcohol).
- NFHS-5 source figures are rounded: about **23% men and 1% women** report consumption (adult survey population), not 23% of every age group.
- Biological susceptibility and reward pathways interact with stress/anxiety, peer norms and urban lifestyles; commercial drivers include flavoured products, surrogate sponsorship, influencers, price promotions and dense retail access. Genetic susceptibility does not make addiction inevitable.
- Source cites **2.6 million DALYs in 2021**, **₹6.24 trillion economic harm**, **240% growth over 20 years** and **~50% unrecorded use** without sufficient definitions/citations; treat as source estimates pending verification, not comparable established national totals.
## Policy and reform
- Intoxicating liquor is primarily a State subject; excise revenue creates a public-health/revenue tension. Prohibition in Gujarat/Bihar and differing State sales policies produce varied enforcement contexts.
- Relevant frameworks include NAPDDR/Nasha Mukt Bharat, National Health Policy 2017, Mental Health Policy 2014, National Suicide Prevention Strategy 2022 and NCD action planning. NDPS Act 1985 is not the ordinary beverage-alcohol control statute; source conflates NAPDDR and campaign launch dates.
- A coordinated national alcohol-control policy is an **editorial proposal**, requiring Centre–State and health–finance–social-justice cooperation.
- **Seven A's:** affordability (effective taxation plus illicit-market enforcement); allocation (public-health/de-addiction funding); accessibility (outlet density/hours/delivery controls); advertising (surrogate/digital marketing); attractiveness (warnings, packaging and promotion restrictions); awareness (health/family harms); AI (detect misleading online promotion, subject to human oversight).
- Pair prevention with accessible treatment, counselling, surveillance and illicit-supply control; high prices alone can displace demand toward unsafe liquor.

topics.title: Skin diseases: WHA priority and equitable care
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## WHA78 and equity
- In **May 2025**, WHA78 recognised **skin diseases as a global public-health priority** (WHA78.15). WHO's May 26 report dates committee adoption to May 24; final resolution records the May 27 plenary. [WHO report](https://www.who.int/news/item/26-05-2025-progress-for-ntds-two-resolutions-adopted-at-wha78).
- Nearly **two billion people** are affected in the source estimate; skin disease brings disability, pain, stigma, mental distress and employment/social exclusion, beyond cosmetic concerns.
- Low-resource countries face specialist shortages, underfunding and delayed diagnosis. Darker skin tones are underrepresented in training/research, risking diagnostic inequity.
- Priorities: integrate dermatology into primary care, train workers, improve affordable diagnostics/treatment, invest in inclusive research and public awareness, reduce stigma and monitor access. Resolution-supported priorities are not proof that all countries have already funded implementation.
## ILDS
- **International League of Dermatological Societies**: global nonprofit federation, formally founded **1935**, based in London; source reports over 200 societies across more than 100 countries. [ILDS history](https://www.ilds.org/who-we-are/our-history/).
- Supports WHO collaboration, training/resources, skin-of-colour inclusion and neglected conditions such as leprosy, scabies and fungal disease; organises the **World Congress of Dermatology every four years**.
- Côte d’Ivoire, Nigeria, Togo and Micronesia were among countries supporting the initiative. ILDS advocacy and professional collaboration complement governments' responsibility for equitable services.

topics.title: Invasive alien species: trade pathways and biosecurity
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Concepts and pathways
- **Alien species:** introduced outside its natural range through human activity; **naturalised:** self-sustaining population; **invasive alien:** establishes/spreads and causes ecological, economic or health harm. Alien/naturalised does not automatically mean invasive; boundaries need not be national borders.
- Deliberate introductions: biocontrol (Gambusia/Poecilia), food (tilapia), ornamental/aquarium/pet trade. Accidental introductions: seeds/pests in crops, timber and cargo; ship ballast water and associated organisms.
- Changing trade partners can connect previously unlinked ecosystems while quarantine infrastructure lags. Climate change, disturbed habitats and pollution can increase establishment risks.
## Illustrative cases
| Species | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| Giant African snail | Introduced to India in the nineteenth century (source says around 1847); crop/garden damage, native-snail competition, potential rat-lungworm host |
| Parthenium | Associated with contaminated wheat imports in the 1950s/PL-480 era; competes with vegetation and causes allergies |
| Tilapia and Gambusia | Food/biocontrol introductions can harm native freshwater communities |
| Red-eared slider | Released pets compete with native turtles |
| Cotton mealybug | Crop losses, including cotton in the Deccan |
| African catfish | Source cites Keoladeo, Rajasthan: predation can disrupt native fish and waterbirds |
- Ballast-water example in source: Asian paddle crab introduction to New Zealand; distinguish an introduction pathway from proof that every introduced individual carries white-spot virus.
## Costs and response
- Original study estimated **US$127.3 billion observed, high-reliability costs, 1960–2020 (~₹8.3 trillion)**; the PDF's **₹830 crore** conversion is wrong. Total costs under the study's wider dataset were US$182.6 billion. Sparse coverage means recorded costs underestimate impacts. [Original study](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10530-022-02780-z).
- Source's >2,000 count concerns alien species, not proof all are invasive; its 3% economic-study coverage and aquatic-cost comparisons depend on dataset/scope.
- Strengthen port/airport quarantine, import risk assessments, surveillance/early warning, real-time tracking and rapid control; combine climate/trade data under cross-sector **One Biosecurity** cooperation. Assess consequences after introduction as well as before imports.
- CBD obligations and **Kunming–Montreal Target 6** address pathways, priority species and sites. Target: **reduce introduction/establishment rates of other known/potential IAS by at least 50% by 2030**, not a generic 50% reduction in every impact. [CBD Target 6](https://www.cbd.int/gbf/targets/6).
- Plant Quarantine Order 2003 and biodiversity planning are relevant Indian tools. Source's claimed operational **NAPINVAS** and Indian **National Invasive Species Information Centre (NISIC)** are unverified; do not memorise as confirmed national institutions.
- **PYQ 2023:** Invasive Species Specialist Group belongs to **IUCN**, under its Species Survival Commission; supports the Global Invasive Species Database and management/policy knowledge.

topics.title: Assisted dying, living wills and dignity
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## England and Wales: position on June 21, 2025
- Commons passed the **Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill** at third reading on **20 June 2025, 314–291**. It still required further parliamentary passage; assisted dying was **not already legalised**. [Parliament record](https://hansard.parliament.uk/commons/2025-06-20/debates/525F3344-9DEB-4821-8F8D-01BE7B5E80B0/TerminallyIllAdults%28EndOfLife%29Bill).
- Proposed eligibility: adult 18+, decision-making capacity, terminal illness with six months or less expected life, England/Wales residence for at least 12 months; disability/mental disorder alone does not qualify. Proposed assistance requires a voluntary, informed request and patient self-administration.
- Medical assessments by two doctors and reflection periods are safeguards. **June version used Assisted Dying Review Panels, replacing the original mandatory High Court approval**; PDF mixes the original and amended versions. Panels include legal, psychiatry and social-work expertise. [Commons Library bill history](https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cbp-10256/).
- Suicide Act 1961 criminalises assistance in England and Wales, with up to 14 years' imprisonment; Northern Ireland has separate legislation. Do not assign that Act identically to the whole UK.
## India and ethical distinctions
| Term | Meaning / June 2025 Indian position |
| --- | --- |
| Active euthanasia | Direct intentional lethal intervention; not authorised |
| Assisted suicide | Another facilitates patient's lethal self-administration; not authorised |
| Withholding/withdrawing life-sustaining treatment | Permissible under judicial safeguards in appropriate terminal/irreversible circumstances |
| Advance medical directive / living will | Adult records future treatment wishes for incapacity; implementation requires safeguards and medical assessment |
- **Aruna Shanbaug (2011)** recognised a framework for withdrawal; **Common Cause (2018)** recognised dying with dignity within **Article 21** and advance directives; **2023** order simplified procedures. This is not an unrestricted general right to suicide.
- Compare autonomy/dignity and relief of suffering with coercion, prognostic uncertainty, disability discrimination, unequal care and the duty to protect vulnerable people. Strengthen palliative care and meaningful informed consent.
- Netherlands/Belgium/Luxembourg, Switzerland and some US jurisdictions have differing assisted-death rules; no single international model. **France's National Assembly passed a proposal at first reading on May 27, 2025; it was not operative assisted-dying law in June.** [French legislative record](https://www.assemblee-nationale.fr/dyn/17/dossiers/fin_de_vie_17e).

topics.title: DNA identification and disaster victim identification
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Identification after disasters
- June 2025 Air India crash illustrates DNA identification when visual recognition/fingerprints fail. DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) profiles compare remains with direct reference material (e.g. toothbrush) or biological relatives; results require statistical kinship/match assessment and corroboration, not a bare “match means certainty”.
- Collect/document specimens, avoid contamination, maintain chain of custody and preserve material promptly; DNA degrades with heat, moisture and time. Bones/teeth can protect DNA better than exposed soft tissue. Source suggests ethanol preservation/cold storage; actual protocols depend on tissue and laboratory requirements.
| Method | Use and limitation |
| --- | --- |
| Nuclear STR | Variable short tandem repeats; routine individual/kinship profiling; degraded samples can require shorter targets |
| Mitochondrial DNA | Many copies; useful in damaged remains and maternal-line comparison, but shared maternal relatives limit individual discrimination |
| Y-chromosome markers | Paternal male-line comparison; paternal relatives may share the profile |
| SNPs | Single-base variants; short targets help degraded DNA, but no single SNP uniquely identifies each person |
- Mature human red cells lack nuclei/mitochondria: PDF's “every cell has mitochondria” is incorrect. Identical twins usually share routine DNA profiles. [NIST disaster identification](https://www.nist.gov/blogs/taking-measure/reflections-assisting-911-world-trade-center-dna-identifications), [NIST SNP review](https://www.nist.gov/publications/review-snp-assays-dvi-cost-time-and-performance-information-decision-makers).
## DNA barcoding: different purpose
- Short standardised DNA regions identify **species**, especially look-alike/cryptic species, and detect undesirable plant/animal material in processed foods. It does **not determine organism age**.
- **2022 PYQ:** statements 2 and 3 are correct (d). Species barcoding differs from human individual/kinship profiling.

topics.title: e-RaktKosh and rare blood donor coordination
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Blood safety and rare donors
- **e-RaktKosh**, launched **7 April 2016**, is a centralised blood-centre management platform: donor records/biometric identification, blood grouping, transfusion-transmitted infection screening, antibody screening, stock management and biomedical-waste records. Works within Drugs and Cosmetics law and National Blood Policy standards. [Official functions](https://eraktkosh.mohfw.gov.in/BLDAHIMS/bloodbank/about.cnt).
- June reporting describes planned integration of the **Rare Donor Registry of India** with e-RaktKosh: a national search/coordination system helps locate compatible blood in emergencies. **Bombay phenotype and Rh-null** illustrate rare blood groups; a rare phenotype is not itself a blood disorder.
- Revision: red-cell disorders include anaemias; leucocyte/haematological malignancies include leukaemia, lymphoma and myeloma; haemophilia/von Willebrand disease concern clotting; thrombocytopenia means low platelets. Thalassaemia/sickle-cell disease are inherited red-cell conditions, whose frequency varies substantially by population—do not label them universally rare.
- Real-time availability, confirmatory compatibility testing, donor consent/privacy and reliable transport all matter; a donor match in a database does not by itself complete safe transfusion.

topics.title: Dual-use technology and export-control regimes
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Dual-use controls
- **Dual-use** goods/technology have civilian and military applications. Industrial **autoclaves** may also be used in missile-motor manufacture; the source recalls the **Da Cui Yun** shipment detained at **Kandla, Gujarat, February 2020**, and alleged links to Pakistan's National Development Complex. An allegation or controlled capability is distinct from proof of an individual financing offence.
- **MTCR**, established **1987**, is an informal voluntary political arrangement with **35 partners** and no permanent secretariat; India joined **27 June 2016**. Category I covers complete rocket/UAV delivery systems capable of **at least 500 kg payload to at least 300 km**, plus specified major subsystems/production facilities; Category II covers other specified missiles, components and technology. The source's simple 'all components = Category II' is incomplete.
- Export licensing, end-use/end-user checks and national implementation are central; membership does not grant automatic access to technology or permission for every missile export.
| Regime | Focus | India's June2025 position |
|---|---|---|
| MTCR | Missile/UAV proliferation | Member, 2016 |
| Nuclear Suppliers Group | Nuclear exports | Not a member |
| Wassenaar Arrangement | Conventional arms and dual-use items | Member, 2017 |
| Australia Group | Chemical/biological proliferation-related exports | Member, 2018 |
- **Proliferation financing** means financing WMD proliferation-related activities; FATF assesses national controls, while customs/export-control agencies enforce shipment rules.

topics.title: Iran, the NPT and nuclear verification
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Treaty framework and Iran
- **NPT** opened for signature **1 July1968**, entered into force **5 March1970**; pillars: non-proliferation, peaceful nuclear use and disarmament. Recognised nuclear-weapon states are the US, Russia, UK, France and China under its pre-1967 test definition. India, Pakistan and Israel never joined; North Korea announced withdrawal. [UN treaty account](https://legal.un.org/avl/ha/tnpt/tnpt.html).
- Iran signed in1968 under **Mohammad Reza Pahlavi**, remained a party after the **1979 revolution**; undeclared-site disclosures in **2002** and safeguards disputes led to inspections, negotiations and sanctions. Safeguards non-compliance must not be equated automatically with proof that Iran possessed a bomb.
- **JCPOA2015:** Iran and P5+1 (five permanent UNSC members plus Germany), alongside EU coordination, agreed enrichment/verification restrictions for sanctions relief. US withdrawal in **2018** and renewed sanctions preceded Iran exceeding agreement limits.
- June2025 attacks on Iranian nuclear facilities intensified debate over inspections, regional security and proliferation risks. Iran's assertion of peaceful intent and Israeli/US threat assessments are competing claims; enrichment capability and weaponisation are different.
- **Article X** permits withdrawal when extraordinary treaty-related events jeopardise supreme national interests, with **three months' notice** to all parties and UNSC explaining those events. Withdrawal does not retroactively erase breaches or automatically make weapon acquisition lawful under all other obligations. The PDF's 'leave and legally build a bomb' is unsound.
- Risks: weakened verification, regional arms competition and escalation; diplomatic verification and security assurances remain relevant alongside non-proliferation commitments.

## June 25: material accountancy after strikes
- Source questions whereabouts of roughly **400 kg of up-to-60%-enriched uranium** after Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan strikes. **Unverified whereabouts do not establish lost/stolen material**; truck satellite images cannot prove cargo or final storage location.
- Claims of movement to Isfahan, weapon timelines and 'ten bombs' are attributed political/intelligence estimates, not verified weapons. Producing weapon-usable material, weaponisation and a deliverable device are distinct steps.
- IAEA access, material accountancy and restored monitoring are essential; Iran asserted peaceful intent. Threats to leave NPT do not prove lawful withdrawal by June 25.
- Source's **GBU-37** is wrong: B-2 bunker penetrator was **GBU-57 MOP**. Damage/material assessments remained unresolved at the issue date.

## 25 July 2025: Iran–E3 talks
- **E3 = France, Germany, UK**. Istanbul talks resumed diplomacy after June's attacks/conflict; source reports no major breakthrough, agreement to continue, and disputes over enrichment, sanctions relief and verification.
- **UNSCR 2231** endorsed the JCPOA. Its **snapback** procedure can restore prior UN sanctions after specified notification and failure to adopt continued relief; it is not an instant sanction triggered by any allegation. Reverse voting means a veto cannot simply preserve relief.
- Iran asserted peaceful-enrichment rights and opposed snapback. Source's October 2025 deadline was prospective diplomatic/legal context, not proof sanctions already reimposed by 25 July.
- The nuclear-deal question is **CAPF AC 2014**, excluded from CSE banks. A 2014 question cannot refer to the completed 2015 JCPOA; distinguish interim negotiations from the final agreement.

topics.title: Quantum key distribution and entanglement
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## June2025 demonstration
- **DRDO–IIT Delhi**, via DIA-CoE, demonstrated entanglement-based secure communication over a **free-space optical link exceeding1km** on the IIT campus; announced **16 June2025**, key rate **nearly240bits/s**, **QBER below7%**. [DRDO release](https://drdo.gov.in/drdo/en/documents/press-release/drdo-iit-delhi-demonstrate-quantum-entanglement-based-free-space-quantum).
- **QKD distributes encryption key material**, not the whole message. Photons encode quantum states; measurement correlations plus authenticated classical communication, error estimation/correction and privacy amplification establish a shared key.
- **Prepare-and-measure** protocols (e.g. BB84) differ from **entanglement-based** protocols. Entanglement creates statistical correlations; it does **not transmit usable information instantaneously**, nor does every disturbance establish deliberate spying.
- **QBER** is the fraction of differing bits; excessive error can reveal noise/eavesdropping and require aborting. It is not an infallible real-time intruder alarm. A qubit is a quantum two-level system that can be in superposition; a photon may carry a qubit.
- Earlier Indian milestones cited: **Vindhyachal–Prayagraj intercity fibre link2022** and **100km entanglement-based fibre QKD2024**. Free-space, fibre and satellite links face different loss and infrastructure constraints.
- Potential uses: defence, government, finance and future quantum networks. Limits: equipment cost, optical loss/weather/alignment, detector/source vulnerabilities, integration and denial-of-service. **Authentication is still required**; QKD does not itself authenticate a stranger. Security depends on protocol assumptions and implementation; 'future-proof/unhackable' overstates it.

topics.title: B-2 Spirit and bunker-penetrating munitions
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Platform and June2025 use
- Northrop Grumman **B-2 Spirit**, US Air Force long-range low-observable bomber; first flight **1989**, first operational delivery **1993**. Flying-wing shape, radar-absorbent materials and management of infrared/acoustic signatures reduce detectability; **stealth is not invisibility**.
- Two-person crew; four turbofans; high-subsonic flight; unrefuelled range about **6,000 nautical miles**, extended by aerial refuelling. Carries conventional and nuclear weapons. Exact radar-cross-section/cost comparisons in the source are not reliable universal figures.
- **GBU-57 Massive Ordnance Penetrator (MOP)** is an approximately **30,000lb conventional bunker-penetrating bomb**, distinct from a nuclear weapon. The B-2 can deliver it against hardened underground targets.
- **Operation Midnight Hammer,22 June2025 Iran time:** US strikes targeted Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan; B-2s delivered MOPs at Fordow/Natanz while submarine-launched cruise missiles also participated. Damage assessments and political claims of complete destruction were not settled facts at the issue date. The June25 text misidentifies the weapon as GBU-37. [US Defence account](https://www.defense.gov/News/News-Stories/Article/Article/4227082/historically-successful-strike-on-iranian-nuclear-site-was-15-years-in-the-maki/).

topics.title: Critical and Emerging Technologies Index
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Index and interpretation
- **Harvard Belfer Center,5 June2025:** model/dashboard compares technological power across25 countries plus a Europe aggregate; adjustable indicators/weights mean rankings depend on methodology. Five sectors: **semiconductors35%, AI25%, biotechnology20%, space15%, quantum5%** under default weights.
- Source reports India **15.2**, below France and above Russia/Canada/Australia; relatively stronger **space rank7**. These are index-specific assessments, not universal measures of research quality or all innovation. US leads overall, followed by China and Europe; Europe aggregate overlaps separately listed European states.
- Assessed pillars include economic resources/funding, human capital, regulation/security/global influence and sector capabilities: chip design/manufacturing, AI data/compute/algorithms, biotech/pharma/vaccines, space launch/navigation/defence and quantum core technologies.
- India: space ecosystem, talent/startups and market size offer strengths; semiconductor infrastructure, sustained R&D/private finance, talent retention, applied AI compute and academia–industry links remain constraints. Execute National Quantum Mission and use international collaboration with domestic capacity building. [Original index/methodology](https://www.belfercenter.org/critical-emerging-tech-index).

topics.title: Infrastructure financing and the Deepak Parekh Committee
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Committee recall
- **Deepak Parekh Committee** examined **financing infrastructure development**: long-term domestic/private/foreign capital, institutional barriers and policy reforms. Roads, ports, power, urban systems, water and sanitation illustrate investment needs.
- **2009 PYQ answer (b):** financing infrastructure; distinct from minority socio-economic surveys, GM crop policy and general fiscal-deficit reduction.

topics.title: ASEAN and India’s Act East partnership
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Organisation and June 2025 membership
- **ASEAN: Bangkok Declaration, 8 August 1967**; founders Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand. June 2025 ten members add Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Cambodia. Secretariat **Jakarta**; Summit, Coordinating Council and Secretariat coordinate cooperation; consultation/consensus and non-interference shape decisions.
- **ARF began 1994; India joined 1996**. Vietnam's ASEAN Future Forum is a dialogue initiative, not a treaty body with India as a founding member.
- India: sectoral dialogue 1992 → full dialogue 1995 → summit partnership 2002 → strategic partnership 2012 → comprehensive strategic partnership 2022.
- **2024 Vientiane 21st Summit:** ten years of Act East, theme *Enhancing Connectivity and Resilience*, ten-point agenda, digital public infrastructure, fintech/cybersecurity and ASEAN–India Fund for Digital Future. **2026–2030 Plan of Action** was to be developed, not already operative. [Summit statement](https://asean.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Final-Chairmans-Statement-of-the-21st-ASEAN-India-Summit.pdf).
## Trade and connectivity
- **FY2023–24 trade ~US$120.9 billion**, exports ~41.2 billion/imports ~79.7 billion; deficit ~38.5 billion versus 43.57 billion in 2022–23 and 9.66 billion in 2016–17 (source figures). Imports include electronics, machinery, palm oil; exports minerals/pharmaceuticals. Source FDI estimates: ASEAN→India US$156 billion (2000–2023), India→ASEAN US$56 billion; Singapore leads inward flows.
- Review **AITIGA**, preference utilisation, non-tariff barriers and imbalances; negotiating friction does not prove talks permanently ended.
- **Kaladan:** Kolkata–Sittwe (sea)–Paletwa (river)–Zorinpui/Mizoram (road); alternative Northeast access bypassing Siliguri. **IMT Highway:** Moreh–Myanmar–Mae Sot, ~1,360 km; proposed extensions to Cambodia, Laos and Vietnam. Forecast completion is not operational completion; Myanmar conflict, funding and missing roads constrain progress.
- **RCEP:** negotiations launched 2012; India stepped back 2019 over import competition, safeguards, agriculture/MSMEs and services. Signed 2020: ten ASEAN countries plus China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand. **India is not a member**.
- Trade/investment, Northeast development, Malacca maritime security, tourism and education matter. China's BRI/economic presence constrains India's influence, but ASEAN states retain agency.
- **2016 PYQ:** RCEP is ASEAN-led. **2018 PYQ:** Australia, China, India, Japan are FTA partners among the listed countries; Canada/US are not. ASEAN+1 agreements differ from RCEP membership.
- Embedded article reports nine review meetings without adequate progress and flags rules-of-origin/value-addition concerns over goods processed through ASEAN. These are negotiating concerns, not proof every ASEAN import circumvents rules.

topics.title: Green hydrogen and off-grid production
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Kutch pilot
- **ANIL**, Adani Enterprises subsidiary, announced **23 June 2025** commissioning of a **5 MW off-grid green hydrogen pilot, Kutch, Gujarat**: solar power + BESS and automated closed-loop electrolyser responsive to renewable variability. The company's first-of-kind claim concerns this category. [Company release](https://connect.adani.com/media/2025/jun25/anil/).
- Renewable-powered electrolysis splits water into hydrogen and oxygen; off-grid means independent of central grid supply. Direct fossil-carbon emissions can be avoided; lifecycle emissions still depend on equipment, power and water supply.
- Uses: replace grey hydrogen in ammonia/fertiliser and refining; hydrogen direct-reduced iron can replace carbon reductants in steel. Storage adds flexibility but entails conversion losses, cost, transport and safety issues.
- **National Green Hydrogen Mission 2023:** at least five million tonnes annual production by 2030; projected **over ₹8 lakh crore investment** differs from government budget outlay; supports industrial decarbonisation/2070 net zero.
- **2023 PYQs:** adapted internal-combustion engines, natural-gas blending for heat/power and fuel cells all use hydrogen; fertilisers, refineries and steel all offer applications. Permissible blending depends on infrastructure, not a universal 20% rule.
- **2024 PYQ:** fuel-cell vehicle exhaust is **water vapour**; 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O + electricity + heat. Clean tailpipe does not prove a zero-emission supply chain.

## Better green technology: August editorial
- **Laboratory cell efficiency, commercial module efficiency and field yield differ**; 15–18% is not a universal 2025 silicon ceiling. Higher efficiency can reduce land per output, but costs/materials/ecology matter.
- Roughly 47% laboratory result refers to **multijunction III–V cells under concentrated illumination**, not ordinary single-junction GaAs panels at everyday sunlight. [NREL](https://www.nrel.gov/docs/fy20osti/76570.pdf).
- **Artificial photosynthesis:** research using light, catalysts, water/CO₂ to produce fuels such as methanol; not already a scaled universal substitute for electrolysis.
- **RFNBO=renewable fuel of non-biological origin**, renewable non-biomass energy inputs; renewable electrolytic hydrogen itself qualifies under EU conditions. Hydrogen-derived fuels add conversion/lifecycle costs; RFNBO is not wholly separate from hydrogen. [European Commission](https://energy.ec.europa.eu/topics/eus-energy-system/hydrogen/renewable-hydrogen_en).
- Source “85% energy import dependency” confuses oil with total energy. India does not import a majority of every fuel. Diversification, efficiency, R&D, domestic manufacturing and reliable grids improve security amid Ukraine/West Asia disruptions.
- Less efficient panels raise land/cost requirements, not automatically fossil-based hydrogen; evaluate full-chain emissions, water, storage/transport and energy losses.

topics.title: Sustainable Development Report and SDG progress
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## 2025 SDG Index
- **Sustainable Development Report 2025**, **SDSN**, reports **India 99th of 167, score 67.0/100**; Finland leads, then Sweden and Denmark. This independent index is distinct from the official UN statistical SDG report. [2025 report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/sustainabledevelopment.report/2025/sustainable-development-report-2025.pdf).
- Earlier edition ranks cited: **2021:120; 2022:121; 2023:112; 2024:109; 2025:99**. Method/data changes limit comparisons; source's 'improved every year' is contradicted by 2022.
- Source comparators: US44/75.2, China49/74.4, Bhutan74/70.5, Nepal85/68.6, Bangladesh114/63.9, Pakistan140/57; Maldives53 and Sri Lanka93. Aggregate rank does not prove every goal/group improved.
- **17 SDGs adopted 2015, target 2030**; score nearer100 means closer aggregate achievement; **lower rank number is better**. Health, education, water, gender, climate and poverty need goal-level monitoring; high-ranked states also face biodiversity/climate and consumption spillovers.
- Conflict, fiscal space, inequality and institutions constrain progress. Source's **17% of targets on track** is also a UN 2024/early-2025 assessment, not 17% of the 17 goals. [UNDP March2025](https://www.undp.org/blog/bringing-everyone-table).
- Finance services, clean energy and waste management while targeting exclusion; do not optimise only rank.
- **2018 PYQ:** Climate Neutral Now—UNFCCC Secretariat (c), measure/reduce/offset. **2016 PYQ:** 2030 correct; Club of Rome 1972 origin claim false—2 only (b).

topics.title: Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Scheme and June outreach
- **DAJGUA**, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, launched **2 October 2024, Hazaribagh, Jharkhand**, not2023; honours **Birsa Munda, Dharti Aaba**. **25 interventions,17 ministries**, 63,000+ tribal villages, **₹79,156 crore** approved outlay: infrastructure, health, education and livelihoods through convergence. [Launch release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2061196&lang=2&reg=48).
- Issue reports **22,000 Jan Seva camps in nine days, over53lakh people reached**: Aadhaar1.38lakh, Ayushman cards1.68lakh, PM-Kisan46,000, Ujjwala22,000, Jan Dhan32,000. Enrolments do not establish unique beneficiaries across schemes or actual sustained use.
- **Saturation:** every eligible person/household receives entitled schemes. Doorstep documentation, banking, health and livelihood access address remoteness; monitor exclusions and actual service outcomes.
- Adjacent **2014 watershed PYQ: None(d)**, not3only: DPAP/DDP—Rural Development; NWDPRA—Agriculture. Already captured June16. [Contemporary PIB](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=78596).

topics.title: Enhanced rock weathering and carbon removal
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Mechanism, benefits and limits
- **ERW:** fine crushed silicate rock, e.g. **basalt**, on farmland accelerates weathering. CO₂+water forms carbonic acid, reacting with minerals; bicarbonate can be stored in water/transported to oceans. Grinding raises surface area; not all carbon immediately becomes limestone.
- Possible soil benefits: lower acidity, nutrients and crop growth. Rates vary with rock, grain size, rainfall/temperature, soil acidity and management; source examples are Brazilian sugar farms and Indian tea plantations.
- Source US experiment: **50 tonnes basalt/ha/year;10.5 tonnes CO₂/ha over four years**; other field tests lower. Rock mass differs from CO₂ mass; one trial is not a universal rate.
- **Measurement:** cations may arise from non-carbonic-acid reactions, so ion release alone cannot prove net atmospheric removal. Neutralising acidity can also avoid downstream CO₂ release; avoided emissions differ from removal.
- Assess grinding/transport emissions, heavy metals, inhalable dust, soil/water impacts, durability and additionality before carbon credits. Credit purchases do not prove measured removal.
- **2023 PYQ:** farmland basalt, ocean alkalinity with lime, and carbonated-water storage in abandoned mines are all discussed capture/sequestration approaches; project safety/effectiveness still need assessment.

topics.title: In vivo CAR T-cell engineering
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Conventional and experimental therapy
- **CAR: chimeric antigen receptor**; engineered T cells recognise target antigen. Conventional autologous workflow: collect T cells → laboratory engineering/expansion → conditioning chemotherapy → reinfusion. Time, facilities, cost and immune toxicity limit access; source's ₹60–70lakh is not a fixed nationwide price.
- **June2025 preclinical study:** antibody-targeted lipid nanoparticles deliver **mRNA to CD8+ T cells in vivo**, inducing temporary CAR expression without external cell manufacturing; differs from permanent viral integration. [Original study](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.ads8473).
- Humanised mice: tumour control. **Cynomolgus monkeys:** B-cell depletion, up to85% CAR expression in CD8+ T cells under study conditions; returning B cells largely naive. This is not proof of durable human cure or harmlessness of every returning cell.
- Potential cancer/autoimmune applications could reduce complexity/cost, but clinical efficacy, safety, durability and repeat dosing remained research questions. Severe illness after repeated doses in one animal highlights toxicity risk.
- Animal results are not routine IV cancer treatment; avoid universal claims of no chemotherapy/hospitalisation. **2022 B/T-cell PYQ:** protection from pathogens, already captured June11; B cells and T-cell subsets have distinct functions.

topics.title: Cookes Peak: new minerals and crystal polymorphism
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Cookes Peak mineral discoveries
- **Raydemarkite, virgilluethite and stunorthropite** occur at **Cookes Peak, Luna County, New Mexico, USA**, a mineral-rich mountain with a granodioritic core. Mineral species are naturally occurring crystalline solids distinguished by composition and structure; finding a natural analogue of a synthetic compound establishes a mineral occurrence, not a previously unknown chemical element.
- Raydemarkite: flexible, slender needle-like crystals, about **1 mm**; **MoO₃·H₂O**. Virgilluethite has the **same composition but different crystal structure** (polymorphism), with sheet-like architecture. Stunorthropite forms milky, short blade-like crystals.
- Correct the diagram wording: raydemarkite contains double chains of **MoO₆ / MoO₅(H₂O) coordination octahedra**, linked through hydrogen bonding; “MoO₅ octahedra” omits the sixth coordinating oxygen. [Original mineral description](https://www.geo.arizona.edu/xtal/group/pdf/TCJoMaP61_2023_203-213.pdf).
- Natural–synthetic comparisons clarify crystallisation, hydration/dehydration and mineral evolution. Related molybdenum oxides attract battery, sensing and catalytic research; this is **not proof the three rare natural minerals are commercially mined for those uses**.
- June coverage revisits discoveries already documented before 2025, including the **2023** mineral descriptions. Cookes Peak is **8,404 ft** high; raydemarkite is the natural analogue of a compound synthesised in **1903**. The source's **5,998** world-mineral count is a dated snapshot, not a fixed total. [New Mexico Bureau report](https://geoinfo.nmt.edu/news/home.cfml?id=750); [2023 symposium](https://geoinfo.nmt.edu/museum/nmms/abstracts/2023/2023-NMMS_p17.pdf).

topics.title: GST, GST Council and appellate tribunal
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## GST and appellate resolution
- **GST began 1 July 2017**, enabled by **101st Amendment Act, 2016**; destination-based indirect tax with input-tax credit, subsuming many earlier Union/State levies. The supplier generally collects/remits tax; the economic burden usually passes to consumption.
- **CGST + SGST/UTGST** generally apply to intra-State supplies; **IGST** to inter-State supplies and imports. Exports are **zero-rated**, so “IGST on exports/imports” without qualification is misleading.
