June source recalls nil/5/12/18/28% principal bands; exemptions/special rates exist and bands are date-dependent.
- **Article 279A GST Council:** Union Finance Minister chairs; Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue/Finance and State finance/taxation or nominated ministers participate. Quorum **half the total membership**; decisions need **three-fourths weighted votes of members present and voting**, Centre weight **one-third**, States together **two-thirds**. The graphic's simple head-count interpretation is incorrect.
- **GSTAT**, constituted under **CGST Act section 109**, hears appeals from first appellate/revisional authorities, providing a common Centre–State forum and consistent interpretation. It is the second appellate level, not a substitute for the first appeal. [GSTAT](https://gstat.gov.in/).
- Source's “tribunal may be headed by a former SC judge/HC Chief Justice” repeats an old proposal: former Jharkhand Chief Justice **Sanjaya Kumar Mishra had already become the first President in May 2024**. Appointment/constitution does not establish every bench was operational by June 2025. [President biography](https://gstat.gov.in/president).
## June clipping and PYQ recall
- Embedded newspaper clipping discusses possible **12% slab rationalisation** and removal of tax on specified intermediary services; these were **reported agenda/proposals**, not enacted June rate changes.
- **2017 GST PYQ: (a), 1 only**—tax harmonisation supports a common market; it does not guarantee a drastic CAD reduction or overtaking China's economy. **2018 exempt-items PYQ: (c), 1, 2 and 4** in its historical tax context; canned/processed fish is the excluded item. Do not turn the PDF's speculative cooked-egg vendor explanation into a universal exemption rule.

## 16 August: proposed rate rationalisation
- The embedded clipping reports a Centre proposal to move most items in the **12%/28%** bands to **5%/18%**, with a proposed **40% special demerit rate**. These are proposals at this issue date; the speech promised reforms by Diwali, not immediate replacement of the operative rate schedule. [15 August PM address](https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/pms-address-from-the-ramparts-of-red-fort-on-the-occasion-of-79th-independence-day/).
- Generic prose still repeats an older GSTAT-constitution proposal. First President **Sanjaya Kumar Mishra was appointed in May 2024**; this August recycling does not move his appointment back into the future. Constitution, appointment and operational readiness of individual benches remain distinct. Existing GST Council, zero-rating and historical PYQ notes apply.

topics.title: Liver disease and patterns in certified mortality
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Certified deaths: interpret the denominator
- The clipping analyses **annual Medical Certification of Cause of Death (MCCD)** data, **2012–2022**. Digestive-system diseases ranked **eighth among certified causes in 2022**; these are not automatically nationally representative all-death rates.
- Male certified digestive deaths were about **3–3.5 times** female deaths; **3.5:1 in 2022**. Liver-related causes represented **70–75% of male** versus **52–57% of female** digestive-disease deaths across the period; digestive disease and liver disease are not identical categories.
- **2022 age distribution:** about **30% of female digestive deaths at 65+**; male concentration greatest at **45–54**, followed by **35–44**. These are shares of deaths, not age-specific population mortality risk.
- Map: **Sikkim ~19.7%, Mizoram ~17.9%, Manipur ~16.1%, Meghalaya ~12.3%** of certified deaths due to digestive diseases. The text reports five northeastern States above 10%, while only four are labelled in this map. Certification coverage and age/comorbidity differences affect comparisons.
- NFHS alcohol-use comparison cited: **~19% men /1% women**. Alcohol is an established liver-disease risk, but cross-State/sex associations here cannot establish the causes of individual deaths. The source's meat-intake explanation is a **hypothesis requiring clinical/epidemiological testing**, not proof meat caused these regional patterns.
- Revision: improve cause-of-death certification, separate age-standardised rates from raw counts/shares, and combine metabolic-risk, alcohol-use and viral-hepatitis prevention with timely diagnosis.

topics.title: Emergency provisions and the legacy of 1975
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## 1975 Emergency: anniversary and framework
- **25 June 2025 marked 50 years** since the 1975 proclamation; source text “2024/49th” is stale. **Part XVIII, Articles 352–360** covers national emergency, constitutional breakdown in States and financial emergency. National proclamations: **1962 and 1971 external aggression; 1975 internal disturbance**, the last ending in **1977**.
## National Emergency — Article 352
- Grounds now: **war, external aggression, armed rebellion**; may cover all or part of India. President requires the **Union Cabinet's written decision**. The 44th Amendment replaced “internal disturbance” with “armed rebellion”.
- Both Houses must approve within **one month**. Approval/renewal requires **majority of total membership plus at least two-thirds present and voting**; approved continuation is **six months**, renewable. If Lok Sabha is dissolved, the special survival window is **30 days after its first sitting**, provided Rajya Sabha approved in time.
- President may revoke without parliamentary approval; must revoke if Lok Sabha disapproves. **One-tenth of Lok Sabha members** may trigger a special sitting for disapproval, to be held within **14 days**.
- **Article 358:** Article 19 restrictions relax only during emergency based on **war/external aggression**, subject to constitutional conditions. **Article 359:** a presidential order can suspend court enforcement of specified rights, **excluding Articles 20 and 21**. A proclamation does **not automatically suspend every fundamental right**. [Constitution, Part XVIII](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/19150/1/constitution_of_india.pdf).
## President's Rule — Article 356
- Constitutional machinery breakdown; **S.R. Bommai (1994)**: judicial review, relevant material, floor-test principle for legislative majority and no irreversible assembly dissolution before parliamentary approval. **Rameshwar Prasad (2006)** reinforces limits on arbitrary dissolution.
- Approval normally within **two months**; continuance **six months at a time**, ordinarily up to **three years**, with additional constitutional conditions beyond one year. Distinguish this from the national-emergency one-month/special-majority regime.
- Source examples require correction: Uttarakhand's floor-test crisis was **2016, not 2020**; UP's **June–July 1991** President's Rule followed dismissal after Rajiv Gandhi's assassination, while **December 1992** followed the Babri Masjid demolition—separate episodes. Punjab **1987–1992** concerned militancy; Maharashtra **November 2019** concerned government formation.
- **Sarkaria:** last resort, reasoned Governor report, alternatives first and assembly initially suspended. **Punchhi:** proposed localised intervention and short duration; recommendations **are not existing permission for ordinary district-wise President's Rule**.
## Financial Emergency — Article 360
- Threat to India's/part's financial stability or credit; both Houses approve within **two months**. Once approved, no six-month renewal rule; revocable by President. It can permit financial directions, salary reductions including judges and reservation of State financial bills. **Never proclaimed as of June 2025**.
## Amendments and safeguards
- **38th Amendment Act, 1975:** attempted immunity for emergency satisfaction; **44th Amendment Act, 1978** removed that shield and strengthened safeguards. **42nd Amendment Act, 1976:** allowed territorial limitation of a national proclamation and increased centralising powers; its provisions need clause-specific treatment.
- **39th Amendment Act, 1975** inserted Article 329A concerning high-office election disputes; **Article 329A(4)** shielding the PM's election was struck down in **Indira Nehru Gandhi v Raj Narain (1975)**. Do not describe every provision/the whole amendment as judicially invalidated.
- The 42nd Amendment's six-year legislative terms were reversed by the 44th; restrictions on judicial review/basic-structure questions require provision-specific analysis. Emergency review and civil liberties show why effective crisis powers need parliamentary, judicial and federal checks.

topics.title: Chemotherapy drugs and medicine-quality safeguards
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Treatment principle
- Cytotoxic chemotherapy damages DNA, DNA synthesis or cell-division processes; systemic treatment can reach disseminated cancer and blood malignancies. Administration may be IV, oral, injected or topical depending on the drug; surgery/radiotherapy mainly act locally.
- Rapidly dividing normal cells also suffer: marrow suppression (anaemia, infection risk, bruising/bleeding), gastrointestinal effects, hair loss and fatigue. Toxicity depends on drug, dose/regimen and patient; side-effect severity does not establish tumour response. [National Cancer Institute](https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/treatment/types/chemotherapy).
| Drug | Main mechanism / examples | Important toxicity recalled |
|---|---|---|
| Cisplatin | Platinum DNA damage; testicular, ovarian, bladder, some lung cancers | Kidney and hearing injury, marked nausea/vomiting, marrow suppression |
| Oxaliplatin | Platinum DNA damage; colorectal regimens | Peripheral neuropathy, GI effects, marrow suppression |
| Cyclophosphamide | Alkylating DNA damage; breast cancer, leukaemia, lymphoma, sarcoma | Haemorrhagic cystitis, immunosuppression, alopecia |
| Doxorubicin | Anthracycline disrupting DNA-related processes; breast/haematological cancers, sarcoma | Cumulative cardiotoxicity, marrow suppression, hair loss |
| Methotrexate | Antifolate impeding nucleotide/DNA synthesis; leukaemia, lymphoma, selected solid tumours | Liver injury, mucositis, marrow suppression, lung/kidney toxicity |
| Leucovorin (folinic acid) | Companion drug: rescue from high-dose methotrexate; enhances 5-FU regimens | Distinguish supportive rescue/potentiation from a cytotoxic drug itself; rare allergy |
- Regimens/indications are selected clinically; the table is revision material, not a dosing guide. [NCI regimen safety tables](https://ctep.cancer.gov/protocolDevelopment/sideeffects/regimes/regimes.htm).
## Medicine quality and governance
- The clipping reports roughly **20% of tested chemotherapy samples failed quality standards**, with **16 of 17 implicated manufacturers Indian**, and distribution across **100+ countries**. These are an investigation's sample-specific findings; do **not** infer one-fifth of all Indian cancer medicines fail or that every product from each manufacturer is defective.
- Quality assurance requires good manufacturing practice, independent batch testing, procurement traceability, pharmacovigilance, recalls and transparent regulator follow-up. Affordable generic access must retain potency and safety.

topics.title: Tawi River and Jammu geography
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Location recall
- The issue flags **Tawi River** under Places in News without a detailed article. It flows through **Jammu**, part of the **Chenab/Indus drainage**; distinguish Jammu Tawi from other similarly named streams in the region. [MoEF regional river account](https://moef.gov.in/uploads/2017/08/Jammu-Kashmir.pdf); [Jammu district](https://jammu.nic.in/about-district/).

topics.title: Tansen, Muhammad Ghaus and Gwalior heritage
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Gwalior complex and June 2025 court report
- Madhya Pradesh High Court rejected a private plea for religious/cultural practices at the **Sheikh Muhammad Ghaus tomb complex, Gwalior**, containing musician **Tansen's grave**. The clipping says ASI has maintained it since **1962** as a centrally protected monument; the Court stressed prior litigation, no established petitioner/family control and protection from activities/structures compromising integrity. Do not generalise this case into a ban on every observance at every monument.
- Sheikh Muhammad Ghaus died **1563**; his mausoleum was built in Akbar's reign (**1556–1605**). **Square plan, large squat dome, surrounding chhatris, encircling veranda and carved stone jalis** show early Mughal/Gujarat-linked architectural traditions. The saint's tomb and Tansen's grave are distinct structures within one complex.
## Tansen and music
- Celebrated **Akbar navratna**, associated with the Gwalior musical tradition and Muhammad Ghaus; a major **Dhrupad** exponent. Composed devotional Dhrupads and songs praising patrons; credited with ragas such as **Miyan ki Todi, Miyan ki Malhar and Miyan ki Sarang**.
- Source approximate life dates **c.1500 to c.1586–1589** are disputed, not exact consensus. Legends of producing rain (**Megh Malhar**) or fire/lighted lamps (**Deepak**) are musical folklore, not demonstrated physical events.
- **2019 PYQ: (a)** is the incorrect statement: “Tansen” was **not** a title conferred by Akbar; distinguish it from honorific **Mian**. Other statements recall Hindu devotional compositions, patron praise and ragas.
- Revision value: architectural conservation, Sufi–musical interaction, cultural patronage and the balance between inherited practice and statutory monument protection.

topics.title: K-6 reports and submarine-launched ballistic missiles
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Reported K-6 development
- The issue reports an **8,000-km, nuclear-capable K-6 SLBM** under development at DRDO's Advanced Naval Systems Laboratory, Hyderabad, intended for future S-5 ballistic-missile submarines. Range, Mach 7.5, dimensions and payload are **reported specifications, not independently confirmed operational capabilities**.
- **SSBN:** nuclear-powered submarine carrying ballistic missiles; the sea-based leg improves survivability of nuclear deterrence. **MIRV:** a missile deploys several re-entry vehicles capable of independently targeting different locations.
- The source's 12 m × 2 m dimensions cannot describe an S-5 submarine; do not reproduce its claims of K-3/K-5 testing/induction as established facts. High speed alone does not make interception impossible.
- **Agni-IV PYQ 2014:** surface-to-surface, two-stage solid-propellant missile; approximately 4,000-km range and one-tonne payload. Answer: **(a) 1 only**; liquid-only propulsion and 7,500-km range are incorrect.

topics.title: World Drug Day and organised drug crime
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## World Drug Day 2025
- Observed **26 June**, established by UNGA in **December 1987**; 2025 theme: **“Break the cycle. #StopOrganizedCrime”**. DoSJE held an observance at Dr Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi.
- UNODC publishes the **World Drug Report**. Its 2025 edition estimates **316 million people used drugs in 2023**, excluding alcohol/tobacco; only **1 in 12 people with drug-use disorders** received treatment. These are 2023 estimates published in 2025, correcting the issue's 1-in-8 figure. [UNODC release](https://www.unodc.org/documents/data-and-analysis/WDR_2025/Press_release_WDR_2025_English.pdf).
- Synthetic opioids and stimulants require separate terminology: **fentanyl is an opioid; methamphetamine is a stimulant**. Prevention, evidence-based treatment, social support, financial investigation and international cooperation address both health harms and organised crime.
- Fentanyl practice-question revision: synthetic opioid analgesic, much more potent than morphine; the claim that India is the largest supplier to the US is unsupported. The question has no explicit exam/year, so is excluded from PYQ banks.
- **BPA PYQ 2021:** answer **polycarbonate**; BPA also occurs in epoxy-resin manufacture and has endocrine-disrupting potential. Do not generalise that every plastic contains BPA.

topics.title: Trigeminal neuralgia
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Core facts
- **Tic douloureux:** chronic facial pain involving the trigeminal nerve, often experienced as brief, severe electric-shock-like attacks on one side. Touch, chewing, toothbrushing or smiling can trigger attacks.
- Compression by a blood vessel is a common cause; the disorder is more common in women and older adults. Episodes may become more frequent/prolonged. Treatment can involve medicines or surgery; the colloquial “suicide disease” is not a clinical classification.
- Diagram recall: **ophthalmic V1 → upper face; maxillary V2 → midface; mandibular V3 → lower face/jaw**.
- **ACE2 PYQ 2021:** answer **spread of viral diseases**; ACE2 is a host receptor used by SARS-CoV-2 for cell entry.
- Clinical reference: [NIH/NIDCR](https://www.nidcr.nih.gov/health-info/trigeminal-neuralgia).

topics.title: Registrar General of India and civil registration
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Birth certificates and population statistics
- RGI asked States to issue newborns' birth certificates to mothers **before hospital discharge**, especially in public hospitals: registration is essential for identity, services and reliable population statistics.
- RGI's office was set up in **1949 under MHA**; Registrar General and ex-officio Census Commissioner oversees Census and civil-registration coordination. Census is periodic; **Civil Registration System records births/deaths continuously**.
- **Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969, section 12:** certificate/extract after registration. The **2023 amendment**, effective **1 October 2023**, strengthens national/state electronic databases; avoid implying every local registrar's workflow is identical or every civil-registration event is a Census enumeration.
- Linguistic surveys document India's language diversity; Grierson's original Linguistic Survey culminated in **1928**. Avoid assigning the RGI a fixed Joint Secretary rank or claiming every linguistic survey is inseparable from a decennial Census.
- **AG/SG PYQ 2022:** neither statement correct. Attorney General has parliamentary speaking/participation rights without voting under Article 88; Solicitor General lacks the same constitutional right. AG holds office at President's pleasure under Article 76(4); resignation upon a government change is not constitutionally mandated.

topics.title: Adamya Fast Patrol Vessel
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Induction and capability
- **26 June 2025, Goa:** ICG inducted **Adamya**, first of **eight FPVs** built by Goa Shipyard Limited. First ship of its class in the ICG fleet with **controllable-pitch propellers and indigenous gearboxes**, improving manoeuvrability and operational flexibility.
- Equipment: **30-mm CRN-91 gun; two 12.7-mm stabilised remote-control guns** with fire control; integrated bridge/platform-management systems and automated power management.
- Roles: maritime law enforcement, coastal surveillance, search and rescue, EEZ protection; illustrates domestic shipbuilding capacity. [Defence Ministry](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2139879&lang=2&reg=48).
- **INS Astradharini PYQ 2016:** torpedo launch and recovery vessel; distinguish it from a submarine, aircraft carrier or amphibious warfare ship.

topics.title: Salkhan Fossil Park and stromatolites
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Fossil geoheritage
- **Salkhan/Sonbhadra Fossil Park, Uttar Pradesh:** added to UNESCO's **Tentative List on 4 June 2025**, not inscribed as a World Heritage Site. In the Vindhyan region, within Kaimoor Wildlife Sanctuary's Gurma range.
- Approximately **1.4-billion-year-old Mesoproterozoic stromatolites**, layered structures formed through microbial communities including cyanobacteria. Domal/columnar forms reveal water-depth, sedimentation and wave conditions; “Evolution of life” is an IUCN geoheritage category. [UNESCO nomination](https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/6842).
- Cyanobacterial oxygen production transformed Earth's atmosphere; the **Great Oxidation Event about 2.4 billion years ago** substantially predates these fossils. Oxygen did not become the predominant atmospheric gas; nitrogen dominates today. Do not confuse ancient fossil stromatolites with modern living microbial structures at Shark Bay.
- **2024 PYQ recall:** Santiniketan and Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas entered the World Heritage List in **2023**; Rani-ki-Vav **2014**, Mahabodhi complex **2002**. Thus **only two**.
- Among the intangible-heritage options: Chhau **2010**, Kumbh Mela **2017**, Durga Puja in Kolkata **2021**, **Garba 2023**—latest among those choices.

topics.title: New criminal codes: digital evidence and implementation
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## One-year implementation review
| Earlier law | Replacement enacted in 2023 |
|---|---|
| IPC 1860 | Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) |
| CrPC 1973 | Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) |
| Indian Evidence Act 1872 | Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) |
- Main commencement: **1 July 2024**; enactment year is not commencement year. CrPC 1973 was enacted after independence, although it replaced an earlier colonial procedural code.
- **e-Sakshya:** capture crime-scene photos/videos, timestamps/location and witness-related evidence; secure storage and chain of custody matter. Recording does not make tampering logically impossible or evidence automatically admissible.
- **BNSS 176(3): forensic expert visit and videography for offences punishable by seven years or more**, from a date notified by the State within the statutory five-year window; not mandatory attendance at every crime scene. [BPRD compendium](https://bprd.nic.in/uploads/pdf/Compendium_11zon.pdf).
- Reported field constraints: insufficient compatible phones/tablets; cloud evidence still copied to pen drives for courts; forensic capacity/certification gaps; delayed post-mortem/medical reports and resistance to recording discovery proceedings. **MedLEaPR** piloting in Chhattisgarh aims to digitise medico-legal reports.
- BNS **112** deals with petty organised crime; BNS **303(2)** has a specific first-conviction provision for theft below ₹5,000 with restoration/return of property. It does not decriminalise all small thefts. BNSS **184** provides a seven-day period for sending a rape survivor's medical report.
- Priorities: investigators' equipment/training, labs, interoperable police–court systems, evidence authentication, victim safeguards and feedback from police, courts, lawyers and citizens. Lack of IT Act examiner notification does not automatically exclude every electronic record.

topics.title: Political-party registration and RUPP delisting
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## June 2025 scrutiny
- ECI initiated verification/show-cause proceedings concerning **345 RUPPs** for non-contestation since 2019 and absence at registered addresses; this was **not a completed June cancellation of all 345**.
- Article **19(1)(c)** protects association; **RPA 1951, section 29A** governs registration. Apply within **30 days of formation**; party constitution must affirm constitutional allegiance, socialism, secularism, democracy and India's sovereignty, unity and integrity; changes in material particulars must be reported.
- **Registration ≠ recognition:** RUPPs are registered but have not met national/state-party recognition criteria. Benefits can include conditional income-tax exemption under **section 13A**, common-symbol concessions and up to **20 star campaigners**. Only qualifying campaigners' travel expenditure receives the statutory exclusion, not all their campaign spending.
- Reports of **2,800+ RUPPs/~750 participating in 2024** are dated context. Registration alone does not guarantee tax exemption: accounts, audit and contribution disclosure requirements apply, including contributions above ₹20,000.
- **Indian National Congress (I) v Institute of Social Welfare, 2002:** ECI's quasi-judicial registration power does not confer a general power of deregistration for mere inactivity; narrow exceptions include fraud, abandonment of constitutional allegiance and unlawful-association circumstances. Delisting/compliance action must be distinguished from a general statutory deregistration power.
- Reform options: express legal powers with due process, internal democracy, regular audited returns, transparent donations, verification and appropriate election-participation criteria; Law Commission recommendations are not already enacted law.

topics.title: Sariska: tiger habitat and mining boundaries
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Boundary proposal and ecology
- The issue reports a proposal to rationalise **Critical Tiger Habitat (CTH)** boundaries at Sariska, potentially affecting **50+ marble/dolomite mines** shut following court action. Treat this as a contested proposal, not reopening approval; balance livelihoods against fragmentation, pollution, disturbance and ecological integrity.
- **Alwar, Rajasthan; Aravalli landscape** of hills, valleys, cliffs and plateaus; tropical dry-deciduous/thorn forest dominated by **dhok (Anogeissus pendula)**, with ber, gugal, kadaya, bamboo and kair.
- Tiger, leopard, caracal, sambar, chital, nilgai, wild boar and four-horned antelope; peafowl, partridges and monitor lizards. **Kankwari Fort** is inside; Pandupol, Siliserh Lake and Bhangarh are geographic/heritage recall points.
- Project Tiger inclusion **1978–79**; **Ranthambore entered in 1973–74**, so Sariska was not Rajasthan's first tiger reserve. NTCA records sanctuary upgrading in **1958** and preliminary national-park notification in **1982**, contradicting the issue's 1979 park date. [NTCA profile](https://ntca.gov.in/assets/uploads/Reports/MEE/Evaluation_reports_TRs.pdf).
- CTH is the core area identified scientifically under **Wild Life (Protection) Act 1972**; legal safeguards and community rights cannot be replaced by a blanket claim that every human activity is prohibited.
- **PYQ recall:** Dampa—Mizoram; Gumti—Tripura (not Sikkim); Saramati—Nagaland. Pakhui/Pakke—Arunachal Pradesh. Among Corbett/Ranthambore/Nagarjunasagar–Srisailam/Sundarbans, **Nagarjunasagar–Srisailam** has the largest CTH (**2,595.72 km²**); its current Andhra Pradesh reserve should not be conflated with Telangana's separately notified Amrabad.

topics.title: Noble rot and fungal chromosome partitioning
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Noble rot and a genome exception
- **Botrytis cinerea** can cause noble rot in grapes: skin penetration/water loss concentrates sugars, enabling sweet wines such as **Sauternes (France), Trockenbeerenauslese (Germany/Austria), Tokaji Aszú (Hungary)**. Selective hand-picking adds labour/cost; the fungus is also a plant pathogen.
- May 2025 research in **Science** on B. cinerea and **Sclerotinia sclerotiorum** found haploid chromosomes distributed across multiple nuclei: each nucleus contains only a subset. This challenges “one nucleus, one complete genome”; it does **not** mean the fungi cannot reproduce or be propagated clonally by any method.
- UV-mutagenesis observations prompted chromosome counting, **FISH**, DNA-content measurement and single-nucleus PCR. **Ascomycetes** form sexual ascospores within an **ascus** (plural asci). [Primary study](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abn7811).
- **Revision:** cnidarians (coral–algal partners), fungi (lichens/mycorrhizae) and protozoa (e.g. termite-gut mutualists) all include symbiotic species. Lichen = fungal partner + photosynthetic alga/cyanobacterium; fungal structure/moisture support plus photosynthesis enables pioneer colonisation of bare rock and soil formation.
- Bacteria/fungi can grow in suitable artificial media; viruses require living hosts and are not independent decomposers. Fungi and bacteria recycle nutrients from dead matter.
- Viruses lack independent energy-generating machinery; transmission is not restricted to biological vectors. Marine viruses exist, **bacteriophages infect bacteria**, and viruses can alter host transcription: all three negative assertions in the issue's 2025 question are false. Incomplete option sets are flagged separately.

topics.title: Bonnet macaque and conflict management
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Species and Kerala proposal
- **Bonnet macaque (Macaca radiata):** southern Indian primate with a cap-like crown of radiating hair; occupies forests including Western Ghats and human-dominated farms, settlements and temple/tourist sites.
- Diurnal, arboreal and terrestrial; social multi-male/multi-female troops, quadrupedal movement. Omnivorous: fruit/leaves, insects, small vertebrates/eggs and human food. Females mature around 3–4 years; gestation about six months, nursing roughly 6–7 months with longer maternal association.
- Kerala proposed seeking Union permission for sterilisation following crop/property damage and conflict. It was a **proposal requiring wildlife-law permissions**, not an implemented blanket programme; anaesthesia, veterinary risks/welfare, monitoring and prevention of feeding/open waste matter. Do not call surgery inherently painless or risk-free.
- Source conservation status: **IUCN Vulnerable; Schedule I, Wild Life (Protection) Act**. Local conflict does not establish a growing population across the species' range.
- **PYQ 2023 revision:** lion-tailed macaque is diurnal; Malabar civet is nocturnal; sambar often crepuscular/nocturnal. Answer **only two** active mainly after sunset.

topics.title: WaveX BhashaSetu language-technology challenge
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Challenge launched 30 June 2025
- Ministry of Information & Broadcasting's **WaveX**, under WAVES, invited startups to develop **BhashaSetu**: real-time translation, transliteration and voice localisation across **at least 12 Indian languages**.
- Translation changes language/meaning; transliteration changes script while retaining sound; voice localisation adapts spoken delivery. Uses include regional media, entertainment, education and public communication; accessibility and emotion-aware communication are goals.
- Open to startups at any stage with **no minimum eligibility criteria**; scalable, affordable open-source/low-cost models encouraged, proprietary solutions also permitted. Winning startup receives accelerator incubation/mentoring; prototype deadline **22 July 2025**. [PIB launch](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2140887&lang=2&reg=48).
- India's Constitution lists **22 Scheduled languages**, not 22 universally applicable national official languages. The challenge was an invitation to build a solution, not proof of a fully deployed service.

topics.title: India’s 2024 species discoveries and new records
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Additions to biodiversity records
- Reports released in Kolkata: **683 faunal additions = 459 species new to science + 224 new Indian records**; **433 floral taxa = 410 species + 23 infraspecific taxa**. Combined **1,116 additions** is not “1,116 species newly discovered globally”. New record means previously known elsewhere, recorded in India for the first time.
| Faunal region | Total | New species | New Indian records |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Kerala | 101 | 80 | 21 |
| Karnataka | 82 | 68 | 14 |
| Tamil Nadu | 63 | 50 | 13 |
| Arunachal Pradesh | 72 | 42 | 30 |
| Meghalaya | 42 | 25 | 17 |
| West Bengal | 56 | 25 | 31 |
| Andaman & Nicobar | 43 | 14 | 29 |
- Zoological Survey's report gives **22 new genera**, correcting source's “2”; it also notes **37 reptile and five amphibian species**. [ZSI report](https://zsi.org.in/uploads/Animaldiscoveries2024report.pdf).
- Named examples: **Dravidoseps gouensis** (lizard; Dravidoseps is a new genus) and **Anguiculus dicaprioi**, a colubrid snake.
- Floral additions: **Kerala 58, Maharashtra 45, Uttarakhand 40**; Western Ghats and northeast contributed about **35%**. Categories: angiosperms **154**, pteridophytes **4**, bryophytes **15**, lichens **63**, fungi **156**, algae **32**, microbes **9** (total 433).
- Orchids: **Bulbophyllum gopalianum, Coelogyne tripurensis, Gastrodia indica, G. sikkimensis**. The report's cumulative botanical documentation count is **56,177** across its broad organism categories, which include fungi/algae etc. India is among **17 megadiverse countries**; discovery counts measure documentation effort as well as biodiversity.

topics.title: Kombucha and the gut microbiome
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Human study and limits
- Kombucha is fermented tea made with a **SCOBY (symbiotic culture of bacteria and yeast)**. Fermentation transforms sugars through microbial metabolism; live microbes in a drink do not by themselves establish proven probiotic clinical benefit.
- Brazilian **pre–post study**: 46 healthy adults initially (23 with obesity, 23 normal weight), **200 ml black-tea kombucha daily for eight weeks**; stool sequencing assessed bacteria/fungi. It was not a large randomised trial proving treatment of obesity. [Journal of Nutrition study](https://research.unipd.it/retrieve/318591d5-861e-40e5-9bf5-4dc18e4dcd2b/1-s2.0-S0022316624012392-main.pdf).
- Overall bacterial diversity changed little; selected taxa shifted, especially in obesity. Source reports increases in **Akkermansiaceae/Prevotellaceae** in obesity, **Bacteroidota** across groups and **Parabacteroides** in normal-weight participants; decreases included **Ruminococcus gnavus, Dorea** and fungi **Exophiala/Rhodotorula**. Associations with metabolism/inflammation do not make whole taxa universally “good” or “bad”.
- Source polyphenol breakdown: **81% flavonoids, 19% phenolic acids**. Microbial processing of tea compounds and short-chain-fatty-acid pathways are possible mechanisms; not all polyphenols bypass small-intestinal absorption.
- No significant improvement in glucose, insulin or inflammatory markers in this short study. Diet, region, baseline microbiota and preparation vary; Indian populations' microbial diversity cannot be reduced to a single profile. Larger controlled/longer trials are needed; do not present kombucha as a medical treatment. Source market-value figures are commercial estimates, not biological evidence.

topics.title: GOSAT-GW and Japan’s H-IIA final flight
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Launch and climate monitoring
- **29 June 2025 JST** (28 June UTC), Tanegashima: **50th and final H-IIA mission** launched **GOSAT-GW — Global Observing SATellite for Greenhouse gases and Water cycle**. H-IIA began in 2001 and completed **49 successes in 50 launches (98%)**, its failure occurring in 2003; Hayabusa2 (2014) and SLIM (2023) are earlier missions.
- Third GOSAT-series spacecraft combines greenhouse-gas and water-cycle observations: **TANSO-3** for CO₂/CH₄ and **AMSR3** microwave observations for water-cycle/weather variables. It continues earlier GOSAT and Shizuku/AMSR observations; climate/forecasting, floods/droughts, sea temperature and atmospheric moisture applications matter. [JAXA mission](https://www.jaxa.jp/projects/pr/model/files/p_gosat-gw_2025.pdf).
- Operational data release follows commissioning/calibration; “within a year” is a forecast, not data already available on 1 July. **H3** is Japan's successor large launcher; **Epsilon** serves smaller missions. Claimed cost reductions are design goals, not a universal guaranteed price.

topics.title: Employment-linked incentives, skilling and internships
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## July 2025 Cabinet approval versus earlier Budget proposal
- **1 July approval:** ₹99,446-crore ELI scheme, two parts, for eligible jobs created **1 August 2025–31 July 2027**; target **over 3.5 crore jobs**, including **1.92 crore first-time workers**. These are targets, not jobs already delivered.
- **Part A:** first-time EPFO employees, salary up to ₹1 lakh/month; one month's EPF wage up to **₹15,000 in two instalments**, after six and twelve months, second linked to financial literacy; a portion is retained in savings. **Part B:** employers receive up to **₹3,000/month per eligible additional employee**, generally two years, manufacturing four; at least six months' retention. EPFO establishments must add **two employees if under 50 staff/five if 50+**. [Cabinet terms](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2141129&lang=2&reg=3).
- The PDF's three-scheme/three-instalment narrative with targets **210 lakh/30 lakh/50 lakh** is the older **2024 Budget design**; do not mix it with the July approval. Registration/formalisation and net additional employment differ; guard against substitution, temporary hiring and subsidy capture.
- Separate 2024 package components: **20 lakh youth trained in five years through 1,000 upgraded ITIs** in hub-and-spoke arrangements; internship ambition **1 crore in five years**, twelve-month exposure, **₹5,000/month plus₹6,000 one-time** support, company training cost/10% CSR contribution. An internship is not a guaranteed permanent job.

topics.title: Operation Conviction and prosecution outcomes
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Uttar Pradesh campaign
- Launched **1 July 2023** to prioritise serious-crime prosecution, including murder, rape, organised crime and crimes against children; the July 2025 report claims **97,158 people convicted** by mid-June 2025.
- Source dataset: **114,029 identified cases;74,388 disposed;69,422 conviction cases**. People and cases are different denominators; **69,422/74,388≈93.3%** is the reported selected-case conviction ratio, not a statewide conviction rate for all registered crimes or causal proof of campaign effectiveness.
| Sentence category | Reported people |
|---|---:|
| Death |68|
| Life |8,172|
| Over 20 years |1,453|
| Up to 20 years |87,465|
- POCSO cases: **17 death/619 life sentences**. Organised-crime figures: **395 people convicted in 272 major cases;29 of 69 identified mafia figures convicted**. Daily averages **143 disposals/187 people convicted** are source working-day averages.
- Assess investigation quality, timely evidence/witness support, prosecution coordination and victim support alongside fair trial, legal aid and appeal outcomes. High conviction counts alone cannot establish reduced crime or justify coercive investigation.

topics.title: Narcotics Control Bureau and darknet trafficking
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Mandate and Operation Melon
- **NCB constituted 17 March 1986 under NDPS Act 1985 section 4(3)**; HQ New Delhi, under **MHA**, headed by a Director General. Source's 14 November 1985 date is the Act's commencement, not NCB's formation. [Constitution order](https://www.mha.gov.in/en/commoncontent/office-order).
- Coordinates State/Central enforcement under NDPS and related Customs/drug laws; intelligence on routes/seizures/networks, direct investigations, international cooperation and drug-abuse coordination. Cooperation with UNODC/INTERPOL and foreign authorities differs from those bodies being Indian enforcement agencies.
- Source clipping reports **Operation Melon, NCB Cochin Zonal Unit**, against darknet vendor **Ketamelon**: alleged 600 shipments in 14 months; seized **1,127 LSD blots,131.66 g ketamine and₹70-lakh digital assets**. These are reported seizure/allegation figures, not convictions.
- Geographic recall: **Golden Crescent=Afghanistan–Pakistan–Iran; Golden Triangle=Myanmar–Laos–Thailand**. These names identify regions, not uniform guilt of populations.
- **2025 PYQ:** ED enforces Fugitive Economic Offenders Act 2018 but belongs to **Revenue/Finance**, not MHA; DRI and DG Systems/Data Management rows belong to Revenue/Finance—**only two rows correct**. Demand reduction/rehabilitation requires health/social-justice institutions as well as interdiction.

topics.title: Industrial process safety and migrant-worker protection
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Sigachi blast and safety culture
- **30 June 2025, Sigachi Industries, Pashamylaram near Hyderabad, Telangana:** microcrystalline-cellulose manufacturing blast; the issue reports **36 deaths**, mainly migrant workers. This is the report's evolving toll, not a final casualty count.
- **MCC** is used as a pharmaceutical excipient and in food/cosmetics; relative inertness of the final material does not make high-temperature/pressure/dust-handling manufacturing safe. Equipment failure/temperature build-up were suspected, not a concluded investigation finding.
- **HAZOP=hazard and operability study**: systematic process-hazard examination. Maintain equipment/interlocks, temperature/pressure monitoring linked to shutdowns, dust/fire controls, trained operators, audits, emergency response/evacuation and management accountability.
- The source's Anakapalli comparison misdates the widely reported pharma blast: **August 2024**, not 2023. Other incidents are context, not proof identical causes.
- Source reports Telangana's **₹1-crore ex gratia** announcement. Compensation needs accessible claims, migrant-family support, medical care, social security and labour-law enforcement; relief does not substitute for prevention or lawful accountability.

## Accountability and human cost
- August editorial emphasises repeated accidents as preventable governance failures: missing fire approvals, blocked exits, unreliable firefighting equipment, unsafe maintenance/hazardous work without **permit-to-work**, superficial audits and inadequate migrant/contract-worker training.
- Beyond process controls already noted, build transparent **near-miss/hazard reporting**, worker whistleblower protection, multilingual induction, independent inspections and meaningful management accountability. Safety must enter plant design, maintenance budgets, procurement and production targets.
- Worker death/disability can trigger household poverty, school dropout, mental distress and productivity loss; prompt medical care, compensation and portable social protection complement prevention.
- Source reports **~6,500 deaths in factories/construction/mines over fiveyears**, **130+chemical accidents/218 deaths/300+injuries in30 months after 2020**, with informal-sector undercount. Treat these as separately scoped source aggregates; no shared denominator or verified single official census is supplied.
- Source advocates corporate-manslaughter reform, stronger inspections and repeat-offender sanctions; “India has no executive criminal accountability” is too categorical—existing penal/factory-law liability exists. Assess investigation, proof, enforcement and coverage gaps; the editorial's proposed law is not an enacted national entitlement.

topics.title: Sports policy, governance and physical literacy
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## National Sports Policy 2025
- Cabinet approved **NSP 2025 on 1 July**, superseding 2001 policy. Five pillars: **global excellence; economic development; social development; mass movement; education integration**. Whole-government coordination, State model policies, sport science/technology, governance, PPP/CSR and measurable monitoring support implementation; **2036 Olympic hosting is an aspiration**, not an award already secured. [Cabinet](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2141141&lang=2&reg=48).
| Milestone | Revision |
|---|---|
|1951|First Asian Games, New Delhi|
|1954|All-India Council of Sports|
|1982|Delhi Asian Games|
|1984|First National Sports Policy; **SAI established 25 January 1984**, not 1986|
|1986|National Education Policy integrated physical education/sport|
|1997|Draft policy/decentralisation proposal; distinguish draft from adoption|
|2000|Separate Youth Affairs and Sports Ministry|
|2001|Revised sports policy|
|2011|National Sports Development Code|
|2014|TOPS elite-athlete support|
|2017|Revamped Khelo India framework; first School Games 2018|
|2019|Fit India Movement|
|2024|Draft governance legislation/policy consultation|
|2025|NSP 2025 approval|
- State-subject status, fragmented funding, weak coordination, limited infrastructure and undervaluing sport careers constrain mass participation. Promote school physical literacy, qualified coaches, rural access, women/disability inclusion, independent fair anti-doping procedures, athlete welfare and dual careers. WADA positive-test statistics are not automatically finally adjudicated doping violations.
- Sporting recall: men's hockey success 1928–1980; Milkha Singh, Gurbachan Singh, Kamaljeet Sandhu; Rathore Olympic silver 2004, Bindra gold 2008,**Vijender bronze 2008** (not 2012), Mary Kom bronze 2012. Later medals cannot be causally attributed solely to one scheme.
- **Tokyo 2020 PYQ 2021: (b)2 only.** Tokyo Games slogan **“United by Emotion”**; “A New World” belonged to Rio 2016. IOC's 2021 addition of “Together” to the general Olympic motto is a separate fact. Tokyo included sport climbing, surfing, skateboarding, karate and returning baseball/softball. [Tokyo organising account](https://www.paralympic.org/news/united-emotion-be-tokyo-2020-games-motto).

topics.title: Ancient Egyptian whole-genome research
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Nuwayrat genome
- **Nature,2 July 2025:** whole genome from a man buried at **Nuwayrat, about 265 km south of Cairo**, around 4,500–4,800 years ago; Old Kingdom/early dynastic context. Ceramic-pot burial in a rock-cut tomb may have aided preservation; DNA extracted from tooth roots.
- Estimated age 44–64, height≈157–161 cm; brown-eye/hair and pigmentation predictions are probabilistic, not a photograph or proof of a racial category.
- Best-fit ancient comparison model: **≈78% North-African-related ancestry and≈22% eastern-Fertile-Crescent/Mesopotamian-related**. This is one individual's model using available ancient reference samples—not a literal percentage of modern nationalities or representative sample of all ancient Egyptians. Direct/Levantine migration route remains uncertain. [Primary study](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09195-5).
- Hot climate and preservation conditions obstruct ancient-DNA research; the result demonstrates regional ancestry links but cannot establish a uniform Egyptian population across millennia.
- Map recall: Egypt's Mediterranean coast/Nile delta in north, Red Sea/Sinai east, Libya west, Sudan south; Suez Canal connects Mediterranean and Red Sea. Levant is eastern Mediterranean (Syria, Lebanon, Israel/Palestine, Jordan;definitions vary), not synonymous with all Mesopotamia.

topics.title: Custodial violence, data and police accountability
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Ajith Kumar case and accountability
- **June 2025:** security guard Ajith Kumar died in police custody in Sivaganga, Tamil Nadu; Madurai Bench's response renewed scrutiny of police violence. **Sathankulam 2020** and **Ambasamudram 2023** are earlier cases, not current incidents.
- Custodial death includes **police custody and judicial custody**; a death in custody is not automatically established murder/torture. Independent investigation and medical evidence determine cause/liability.
- Source **2016–17 to 2021–22:** **11,656 reported custodial deaths nationally;UP 2,630;Tamil Nadu 490**; combines custody categories and is not all deaths caused by police assault. Embedded map also lists Maharashtra 755, West Bengal 955.
- Separate **2017–2022 police-custody death cases:** **123 police arrested,79 chargesheeted, zero convicted** in the source dataset. Broader police human-rights chart gives **75 arrested,41 chargesheeted,3 convicted**; the issue's prose says 74 cases whereas chart shows 78—do not merge these into one consistent national total.
- **Preventive detenues,31 December 2022:** TN 2,129, SC share 38.5% versus 20.01% population. Chart comparators: J&K 546(1.3%SC/7.38%population), Gujarat 334(9.6%/6.74%), Haryana 326(1.3%/20.17%), UP 172(7.6%/20.7%). These are detention-composition snapshots, not direct measures of the caste share of torture victims or causal proof about every arrest.
- Detenue≠convict; preventive detention differs from pretrial remand. Protect Articles 21/22 safeguards, prompt independent inquiry, legal aid, medical documentation, court/NHRC oversight, witness protection and police accountability; conviction counts lag incidents and need case-year/outcome interpretation.

## Safeguards and reform
- Physical assault, sexual violence, denial of medical care, threats and coercive interrogation violate dignity and life/liberty. **Articles 14, 21 and 20(3)** support equality, liberty and protection against compelled self-incrimination; Article 20(1) concerns retrospective criminal punishment.
- **BNS Section 120** addresses hurt/grievous hurt to extort confession or compel restoration of property; it is not limited to police. **BNSS Section 35** governs specified arrest powers/procedures; **BSA Section 22** excludes confessions caused by inducement, threat, coercion or promise under its conditions. [BNS text](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/20062/1/a2023-45.pdf).
- **D.K. Basu (1997)**: arrest memo, informing relatives, medical examination and access to legal safeguards. **Nambi Narayanan (2018)** illustrates compensation for wrongful arrest. The sheet's Ram Sagar Yadav (1985) sentence should not be memorised as an automatic universal reversal of the criminal burden of proof; custodial evidence requires careful judicial evaluation.
- India signed **UNCAT in 1997** but had not ratified it in the source period. Ratification and a dedicated anti-torture framework, independent complaints/investigation, medical documentation, witness/victim protection, legal aid and separation of investigation from routine law-and-order duties are reform proposals. Do not equate preventive detention with proof a person was about to commit an offence, or every custodial death with proven torture.

## Evidence-led interrogation
- July 31 editorial contrasts coercive 'Dirty Harry' policing with professional investigation. Source's **687 deaths,2018–19 to 2022–23**, is a reported **police-custody** series; do not merge it with all police+judicial custody deaths or assume every death was proven torture.
- Torture undermines memory and encourages false confessions. Better methods: **PEACE—Preparation and Planning, Engage and Explain, Account, Closure, Evaluation**; rapport, open questions, recorded interviews, corroboration and forensic evidence. HIG research and wrongful-confession histories support examining reliability rather than romanticising coercion.
- Source cites **Global Torture Index 2025 high-risk classification**, an external assessment, not a court finding in every case. Law Commission's **273rd report (2017)** recommended a dedicated anti-torture law; existing July 11 notes cover UNCAT status, D.K. Basu and legal safeguards.
- Invest in forensic capacity/training, independent complaints and investigation, witness protection, medical access and accountable supervision. The daily mains prompt is publisher practice, not a UPSC PYQ.

topics.title: QS university rankings and higher-education quality
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## QS 2026 edition released in 2025
- **54 Indian institutions**, versus 11 in 2015; **IIT Delhi 123** leads, with IIT Bombay, IIT Madras, IIT Kharagpur and IISc among prominent entries. **Ashoka and Shiv Nadar** are among eight first-time Indian entrants. Ranking edition year is not release year. [QS 2026](https://www.topuniversities.com/world-university-rankings/2026).
| Weighted indicator | Weight |
|---|---:|
|Academic reputation|30%|
|Citations/faculty|20%|
|Employer reputation|15%|
|Faculty/student ratio|10%|
|International faculty ratio|5%|
|International student ratio|5%|
|International research network|5%|
|Employment outcomes|5%|
|Sustainability|5%|
- Source combines international-faculty/student weights into 10%; separate indicators explain the nine weighted dimensions. Ratios reflect the selected population/institution; source **national 19:1/Ashoka 11.5:1/desired 10–15:1** are contextual, not a universal legal standard.
- Improvement priorities: research quality and integrity, faculty hiring/time, international collaboration/student access, industry-linked employment support and sustainable campuses. Reputation/citation metrics are partial proxies; rank changes do not prove equal improvement in every institution or guarantee graduate jobs.

topics.title: Lunar dust simulants and astronaut health
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Cell-model study
- **Life Sciences in Space Research 2025** compared **LMS-1(mare) and LHS-1(highland) lunar simulants** with terrestrial urban dust in bronchial **BEAS-2B** and alveolar **A549** cell models. Simulants are engineered Earth materials, not samples proving every lunar region's hazard.
- Compared fine **≤2.5µm particles** at controlled doses/times. Earth dust produced more inflammation/toxicity; lunar simulants still caused dose-dependent loss of viability, especially fine particles. “Less toxic than this comparator” does not mean safe to inhale. [Primary paper](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.lssr.2025.02.005).
- Sharp/abrasive grains and electrostatic adhesion can transport dust on suits into habitats and allow re-aerosolisation. Use suit/cabin isolation, filtration and exposure control; cell experiments do not establish a safe lifelong human dose.
- PM 2.5 refers to fine airborne particulate size, not a particular chemical. Artemis/other lunar mission planning motivates habitat/astronaut protection; launch schedules in the issue are forecasts.

topics.title: India–Ghana relations and Volta geography
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## July visit and bilateral background
- **2–3 July visit:** Modi received **Officer of the Order of the Star of Ghana** from President John Dramani Mahama and addressed Parliament. The clipping emphasises Global South cooperation, UN/global-governance reform and African Union participation in G20; historical bonds do not remove present trade/development challenges.
- Representative office **1953**, full diplomatic ties **1957**, shared Nehru–Nkrumah/NAM legacy. Ghana was a pioneer of **sub-Saharan African decolonisation in 1957**, not the first independent African country in all history.
- Source's “Kalam 2004/Vice-President 2016” visits are mistaken: **President Pranab Mukherjee made the first Indian presidential visit in June 2016**. Avoid using the source's undated~US$2 bn trade/~10,000 diaspora as 2025 totals: 11 June official brief gives **FY 2024–25 US$3.137 bn trade/15,000+ Indian community**. [High Commission brief](https://audit.hciaccra.gov.in/index.php/pages/Nzg2).
- India exports pharmaceuticals, vehicles, machinery; imports gold, cocoa, timber/cashew products. Lines of credit, water/power/agriculture, ITEC/ICCR scholarships and Pan-African e-network/e-VBAB education/health links support cooperation; defence training, peacekeeping and UN/NAM/Commonwealth engagement add strategic depth.
## Map and resources
- **Tema/Takoradi ports** serve Atlantic/Gulf of Guinea trade; gateway routes extend to Burkina Faso and other landlocked States—Ghana does not directly border Mali/Niger. **Kwahu Plateau/Gambaga Scarp** are physical features.
- **Lake Volta, Akosombo Dam; Black Volta, White Volta, Oti:** hydropower, inland transport, fisheries/irrigation. Hydropower is important, but do not assume it is the majority of Ghana's current electricity without a dated generation mix.
- **Accra coastal capital; Kumasi Ashanti cultural/trade centre; Tamale northern hub**. Gold in southern/central Ashanti/Western areas; cocoa forest belt; oil offshore western coast. Map also marks Mole, Bui, Digya, Kakum and Bia protected areas and Mt Afadjato; country/resource geography differs from the location of every mine.

topics.title: Bonalu festival and Telangana folk traditions
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Festival and rituals
- Telangana folk festival, especially **Hyderabad, Secunderabad and surrounding areas**, during **Ashada Masam**; thanksgiving and vow fulfilment to **Mahakali** and local forms **Yellamma, Pochamma, Maisamma, Mateshwari**.
- **Bonalu derives from Bonam (meal)**: women carry decorated brass/earthen pots of rice cooked with milk/jaggery, neem/turmeric/vermilion decorations and a lamp to temples; women are central to community participation.
- Celebrations begin at **Golconda Fort**, then different temple days over several weeks, including **Balkampet Yellamma, Ujjaini Mahakali (Secunderabad), Katta Maisamma, Pochamma (Chilkalguda), Lal Darwaza**. Do not impose an identical week schedule on every year/temple.
- **Rangam:** ritual oracle, traditionally a woman in trance; **Pothuraju**, regarded as the goddess's brother, dances/leads the procession, turmeric-smeared. Folk music, dance and devotion combine.
- Tradition associates its origin with a **19 th-century plague**; this is an origin belief, not evidence of biomedical causation. Telangana designated Bonalu a **State festival in 2014**.

topics.title: Apache AH-64E attack helicopter
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Capability and July delivery forecast
- **Boeing AH-64 E Apache Guardian, US-origin, multi-role attack helicopter**: open-system architecture, digital interoperability, targeting/night/thermal vision and survivability aids; Hellfire missiles, rockets and 30-mm chain gun. Improved engines/lift do not guarantee equal payload at every altitude or make it an invisible stealth aircraft.
- **IAF: 22 ordered in 2015, deliveries completed in 2020; Army: six ordered in 2020**. At this issue date Army deliveries were awaited: clipping forecasts the first three by **15 July 2025**, not already operational Army aircraft.
- Roles: anti-armour, armed reconnaissance/close combat support and coordinated air–ground operations; terrain/weather, payload, maintenance and crew training affect performance. Foreign users of the Apache family do not all operate the same E configuration.

## 22 July 2025: Army delivery
- The embedded newspaper clipping reports the Army received its **first three AH-64E helicopters at Hindon on Tuesday, 22 July**, with joint receipt inspection before deployment to **Jodhpur, Army Aviation Corps**. This updates the earlier forecast; arrival is distinct from inspection, induction and full operational deployment.

topics.title: Judicial review, legislative power and contempt
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Nandini Sundar and Chhattisgarh's 2011 Act
- **5 July 2011 judgment:** arming/deployment of inadequately trained SPOs for anti-Maoist activity violated **Articles 14/21**; directions included stopping such use, recalling firearms, ending Union funding for that purpose and preventing/disbanding vigilante activity such as Salwa Judum/Koya Commandos.
- Chhattisgarh enacted the **Auxiliary Armed Police Force Act, 2011**; its screening, training, service, role and control provisions were cited in later proceedings. Enactment does not establish that all abuses ended or all provisions are immune from review.
- **15 May 2025 order:** mere enactment of a law is not contempt; constitutional challenge tests **legislative competence and constitutional validity**. Legislatures can remove a judgment's legal basis through valid legislation but cannot simply declare judicial findings wrong without curing the defect.
- Separation of powers includes checks and balances: **courts can review and strike down invalid legislation**. Dismissal of contempt is not a blanket merits endorsement of the Act. Interim stay, final invalidation and punishment for wilful disobedience are distinct.
- State/Concurrent List competence remains subject to constitutional distribution, repugnancy and fundamental rights; equality and life/dignity protect both recruits and affected communities.
- [Supreme Court order, 15 May 2025](https://indiankanoon.org/doc/173622808/).

topics.title: BHARAT study and healthy-ageing biomarkers
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## India-specific ageing research
- **BHARAT = Biomarkers of Healthy Aging, Resilience, Adversity and Transitions**, an IISc Bengaluru population study under **Longevity India**, seeks a healthy-ageing baseline and indicators of age-related risk. [IISc study](https://www.longevity.iisc.ac.in/the-bharat-study).
- **Chronological age:** elapsed time; **biological age:** estimated physiological condition from selected markers. Models measure aspects of ageing, not a single universal “true age”.
- Integrate genomic, proteomic, metabolomic and other biomarkers with clinical, lifestyle/environmental and social information. AI/ML may identify trajectories, predictors and candidate interventions, which still need external validation.
- Population-specific reference ranges require diverse, well-characterised samples. Longitudinal follow-up, healthy-volunteer selection, urban/rural/regional representation, funding, consent and genomic/data privacy are key challenges.
- Source examples about CRP, vitamin D and cholesterol illustrate hypotheses about baselines; do not conclude that elevated inflammation/lipid abnormalities are harmless for Indians or validated clinical thresholds can be ignored.

topics.title: Ethane carriers and petrochemical feedstock logistics
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## ONGC–MOL heads of agreement
- **3 July 2025:** ONGC and Japan's **Mitsui O.S.K. Lines (MOL)** reported heads of agreement for a partnership to build, own and operate **two Very Large Ethane Carriers (VLECs)**, subject to ONGC Board approval; this is not delivery or commencement of transport.
- Intended to carry imported ethane for **ONGC Petro additions Ltd (OPaL), Dahej SEZ, Gujarat**. Source plans for **800,000 tonnes/year from May 2028** are future targets.
- **Ethane (C₂H₆)**, obtained from natural-gas liquids, is cracked to **ethylene (C₂H₄)** for plastics and other petrochemical derivatives; distinguish methane, ethanol and LNG. Ethylene-derived chains include antifreeze/detergent materials, rather than every product being made by one direct reaction.
- OPaL's dual-feed cracker handles naphtha and gaseous feedstocks; propylene and other products form part of the wider complex. VLECs need specialised low-temperature gas logistics, not ordinary oil-tanker arrangements.
- Long-term shipping arrangements can secure feedstock and reduce spot-market dependence; supply, cost, utilisation and demand risks remain. Japan cooperation does not guarantee automatic technology transfer.

topics.title: India–Trinidad and Tobago: Girmitiyas and diaspora diplomacy
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## July 2025 diaspora engagement
- PM's **3–4 July 2025 official visit** was an in-person bilateral visit, not merely the PDF's virtual outreach. **30 May2025** marked **180 years since first Indian arrivals in1845**; conferred **Order of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago**, its highest national honour. [Joint statement](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2142390&lang=2&reg=48).
- **Girmitiya**, from “agreement”: Indian indentured plantation labourers taken to colonies after abolition of slavery, principally from Bihar/eastern UP in this Caribbean context. Destinations included Trinidad, Guyana, Mauritius, Fiji and South Africa; indenture involved exploitative conditions, not ordinary free migration.
- Diaspora framed as **Rashtradoots**, cultural ambassadors: language, yoga, festivals, heritage, business and people-to-people ties add strategic value alongside remittances. PBD, Know India Programme, OCI and scholarships illustrate engagement.
- Announced **OCI eligibility up to sixth-generation Indian-origin persons in Trinidad and Tobago**, extending the earlier fourth-generation limit for this community. OCI is a foreign-national status with specified privileges, **not dual citizenship or unrestricted property/political rights**; eligibility/registration conditions still apply.
- **Mapping the Past** initiative described in the speech: document ancestral villages, settlements and contributions of Girmitiya communities, with regular World Girmitiya Conferences proposed. Archives and genealogy preserve historical memory; proposals are not proof an exhaustive database already exists.
- Joint statement welcomes Trinidad and Tobago as the **first Caribbean country to adopt UPI**; implementation/merchant access differs from a fully operational universal cross-border remittance system. Supports digital public infrastructure diplomacy and diaspora/business links.

topics.title: Copper: supply chains and Vision Document
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Properties, uses and geography
- Copper conducts heat/electricity well, is malleable/ductile and corrosion-resistant. Wires, motors, electronics, transmission, EVs, buildings/pipes, defence/aerospace and selected antimicrobial surfaces drive demand. Copper sulphides such as **chalcopyrite** differ from oxide ores; ore, concentrate and refined metal are different products.
- **Khetri—Rajasthan; Singhbhum—Jharkhand; Malanjkhand/Balaghat—Madhya Pradesh**. Source lists smaller occurrences in Sikkim, Karnataka, Manipur and West Bengal; occurrences do not prove economic reserves/mines. Chile, DR Congo and Peru are major mined-copper producers in the source's2024 comparison, not necessarily the same ranking for smelting/refining.
- Source's **~164million tonnes** is **copper ore reserves**, not contained copper metal. The older **1April2020** inventory was about **1.66billion tonnes total ore resources**, of which **163.89million tonnes reserves**. State resource shares and reserve shares must not be mixed; the PDF's52/23/15 state table lacks a reliable matching category/year. [Mines Ministry inventory](https://xn--i1b3b2bo4aigq6hf7n.xn--11b7cb3a6a.xn--h2brj9c/website/internationalmineralscenario).
- **3.78million tonnes FY2023–24 refers to ore**, not refined copper. Comparing it with source FY2018–19 ~4.1million tonnes is a five-year comparison, not proof an annual decline in FY2023–24; smelter closure cannot directly explain all mine-output changes. Copper-concentrate imports reported doubled to **₹26,000crore FY2019→FY2024**; import dependence, ore grades, costs and processing constraints require separate analysis.
## Vision and overseas exploration
- **Copper Vision Document,4July2025:** projected **sixfold demand by2047**, planned **5million tonnes/year additional smelting/refining by2030**, more secondary refining/recycling and overseas assets/partnerships. Capacity plans are not current output. [Mines release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2142191&lang=2&reg=48).
- Source reports **9,000km² exploration block in Zambia** for copper/cobalt under government cooperation; exploration is not a producing mine or guaranteed extractable reserve. Fits critical-mineral security and diversification amid Chinese commercial influence; overseas access must complement domestic efficiency, recycling and environmental/community safeguards.

topics.title: Mycotecture and fungal construction materials
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## NASA's off-planet concept
- **Mycotecture Off Planet**, led by **Lynn Rothschild,NASA Ames**: dormant fungi in compact lightweight frameworks could grow structures at destination using water/nutrients, reducing launch mass. **NIAC PhaseIII,2024 award** supports continued development; this is research toward demonstration, not a working lunar/Martian settlement. [NASA](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-advances-research-to-grow-habitats-in-space-from-fungi/).
- **Mycelium is a network of fungal hyphae**, not a true root; fungal fruiting body is distinct. Containment/sterilisation and controlled growth protect both habitat reliability and planetary environments.
- Research investigates mouldability, insulation and potential radiation protection. Strength, fire behaviour, shielding and durability depend on composite/design/testing; no blanket guarantee every fungal brick withstands space conditions. NASA also notes Earth uses in filtration/mineral extraction from wastewater.
## Mycelium composites on Earth
- Agricultural residues **husk,straw,sawdust** + fungal inoculum → growth binds substrate → moulding → drying/heat treatment stops growth. The PDF's five-day cycle is illustrative, not universal.
- Potential products: insulation/interior panels, packaging alternatives, furniture/sports goods, leather-like materials, filtration/bioremediation and fungal chitin/chitosan for medical research. Species-specific termite biocontrol does not make every dried mycelium brick a pesticide.
- Low density, thermal/acoustic insulation, residue use and biodegradability can reduce material impacts, but coatings/additives, production energy and end-of-life affect results. **Biodegradable does not automatically mean carbon-neutral or pollution-free**.
- Constraints: limited load-bearing strength versus concrete/steel, moisture sensitivity, reproducibility, fire/building certification, cost and manufacturing scale. Source's universal '100times weaker', zero-waste and emissions figures are not general verified performance specifications.

topics.title: Microcrystalline cellulose: excipients and food uses
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Material and manufacture
- **MCC**: purified, partially depolymerised cellulose derived from plant fibres/refined wood pulp; cellulose is a structural plant-cell-wall polymer, **(C₆H₁₀O₅)n**. Acid hydrolysis preferentially removes less-ordered regions, followed by drying/milling; residual microcrystalline regions are stabilised by molecular packing/hydrogen bonding.
- White free-flowing powder, insoluble in water; humans lack enzymes to digest cellulose. Food-additive safety at authorised uses is different from universal harmlessness at every dose/exposure; inhalable manufacturing dust has separate occupational risks. [EU specification](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX%3A32018R0075).
- Pharmaceutical **excipient**, not the active drug: binder, filler/bulking agent and disintegrant support tablet manufacture/drug release. Food uses include texture, bulk, fat replacement, stabilisation and anti-caking under applicable standards.
- **Cellulose**, **MCC/E460(i)** and **carboxymethylcellulose(CMC)** are not identical: CMC is chemically modified and commonly used for thickening/stabilisation.
- The Sigachi accident is covered in industrial-process safety. Safety of the finished excipient does not establish safety of drying, pressure, dust/solvent or acid-handling operations; the PDF's possible causes are not concluded findings.

topics.title: Financial Stability Report and systemic resilience
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## June2025 report, discussed in July6 material
- **RBI's half-yearly FSR**, normally June/December, reflects the **FSDC Sub-Committee's collective assessment** of systemic risks and financial resilience; covers banks, NBFCs, markets and connected financial institutions.
- **30June2025 assessment:** Indian macroeconomic fundamentals and domestic financial balance sheets remained resilient despite global trade/policy uncertainty, volatile markets, debt/asset valuations and geopolitical risks. Banks' capital, earnings and asset quality and NBFC buffers improved; weather/climate shocks remain risks.
- **Stress tests are scenario exercises, not forecasts or guarantees**. RBI says most SCBs maintain adequate capital under specified adverse scenarios; the PDF overstates this as every bank safe even in any worst-case event. [RBI release reproduced by FIDC](https://www.fidcindia.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/RBI-FINANCIAL-STABILITY-REPORT-30-06-25.pdf).
- **GNPA ratio2.3%,March2025** is an observed aggregate; the PDF's **2.5%March2026/2.6%March2027 under stress** table is not a reliable reproduction of the scenario results and should not be memorised. Use baseline/adverse labels, horizon and bank sample from the original report.
- **Capital adequacy** measures eligible capital against risk-weighted assets, not idle cash set aside; regulatory thresholds/buffers vary. Scheduled banks are included in the RBI Act'sSecondSchedule, not simply any RBI-approved bank. NBFCs provide specified financial services under a distinct regulatory framework.
- Lower food inflation means prices rise more slowly, not necessarily fall; good harvests can improve supply without guaranteeing higher farmer incomes. RBI/MPC, rather than the government directly, sets the monetary-policy repo rate.

topics.title: Financial Stability and Development Council
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Structure and mandate
- **Non-statutory council established December2010**, chaired by **Union Finance Minister**; not a NITI Aayog organ. Coordinates regulators and financial-sector development without replacing their statutory powers.
- Members include RBI Governor, heads of SEBI,IRDAI,PFRDA, finance/economic-affairs/financial-services leadership and CEA; **2018 expansion** added Minister of State responsible for DEA, Revenue/MeitY secretaries and IBBI chair. The PDF's abbreviated 'after2018' list is not exhaustive; **FMC merged into SEBI in2015** and is not a separate current regulator.
- Functions: financial stability, macroprudential supervision of the whole economy/system, inter-regulatory coordination, sector development, financial inclusion/literacy, and addressing gaps/risks from fintech and interconnected markets. **Macroprudential** concerns system-wide spillovers, distinct from supervision of a single institution.
- RBI Governor chairs its **Sub-Committee**; RBI's FSR reports that collective risk assessment. International shock transmission after2008 explains the need for coordination; a council's existence does not guarantee crisis prevention.
- **2016PYQ:** statements2 and3 correct; chair is Finance Minister and mandate includes macroprudential supervision. The complete official question is in the shared bank: **(c), 2 and 3 only**.
- [DEA institutional overview](https://www.dea.gov.in/financial-stability-and-cyber-security-division), [2018 Ministry meeting](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=184478).

topics.title: PHWRs and Kakrapar operating licences
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## July2025 regulatory milestone
- **AERB** granted **NPCIL** five-year operating licences for **Kakrapar Units3and4,Gujarat**, India's first indigenous **700MWe PHWRs**; formally handed over **3July2025**. Permission for full-power commissioning came earlier: **KAPS3August2023;KAPS4August2024**. Licence, first criticality, full-power permission and commercial operation are distinct stages.
- Review covered design, siting,construction andcommissioning over approximately15years, with multi-tier assessment and technical-support organisations; operating experience at rated power informed the final licence. [AERB announcement](https://aerb.gov.in/storage/uploads/News/newsd7RsE.pdf).
- **PHWR:** heavy water(D₂O) moderator/coolant and natural-uranium fuel; supports indigenous design/manufacture, resource use and low-carbon electricity. Relative cost/safety depend on the design/project, not a universal advantage over every LWR.
- Common700MWe design supports the **ten-unit fleet-mode programme**; licensing these two does not prove ten more are already built. Independent review, emergency readiness and safe waste management remain necessary.

topics.title: Plant Treaty: genetic resources and benefit sharing
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Treaty structure
- **International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture**, under FAO: adopted **2001**, in force **2004**; conservation,sustainable use and fair/equitable benefit sharing for food security. India is a contracting party, not merely an interested observer.
- **Article9:Farmers' Rights;Article10:Multilateral System;Article11:coverage;Article12:facilitated access/SMTA;Article13:benefit sharing**. The PDF inaccurately assigns all SMTA rules toArticle11. **AnnexI:35food crops/crop complexes and29forages** under the established list. [Treaty text](https://www.fao.org/plant-treaty/overview/text-treaty/en), [AnnexI](https://www.fao.org/plant-treaty/areas-of-work/the-multilateral-system/annex1/).
- Current MLS coverage principally concerns AnnexI material under contracting parties' management/control and in the public domain; access is for research,breeding,training for food/agriculture. Recognises sovereignty and national implementation of farmers' rights; it is not a blanket commercial transfer of ownership over every farmer's seed.
## July2025 negotiations and concerns
- **Fourteenth working-group meeting,7–11July2025,Lima,Peru**, discussed an enhanced MLS/package of measures for later GoverningBody consideration. Scope expansion,SMTA/payment arrangements and benefit sharing were being negotiated, **not already adopted as Indian operative law**. [FAO opening account](https://www.fao.org/plant-treaty/news/news-detail/historic-opportunity-to-strengthen-the-multilateral-system--working-group-opens-final-talks-in-lima/en).
- Source concerns from **Bharath Beej Swaraj Manch,Rashtriya Kisan Mahasangh,Kerala representatives and scientists**: wider germplasm access, inequitable commercial capture, farmers' knowledge/rights and inadequate consultation. These are stakeholder objections, not a final finding the proposal violates the treaty or abolishes all Indian seed law.
- **ICAR-NBPGR/Sunil Archak** represented technical negotiating interests; ICAR said India would protect its interests. Evaluate exact proposed scope,access conditions,farmer participation,traceability and enforceable benefit sharing.
- Biodiversity PYQ explanation remains useful: **Plant Treaty,UNCCD and World Heritage Convention all have a bearing on biodiversity**. Printed2020year is doubtful and held for review rather than copied into a bank.

topics.title: Helgoland and the birth of matrix mechanics
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## 1925 centenary
- **Helgoland**, German NorthSea island group, red-sandstone main island, about50km offshore; the source's sub-1km²size is a rough historical description, not a precise modern municipal area. Former naval/fortress role and tourism form geographical context.
- **Werner Heisenberg**, aged23, visited in **June1925** seeking relief from hay fever and developed the observable-based approach behind **matrix mechanics**. **MaxBorn andPascualJordan** developed its mathematical formulation; **Schrödinger's wave mechanics** later proved equivalent. [Heisenberg Society history](https://www.heisenberg-gesellschaft.de/3-die-entstehung-der-quantenmechanik-1925-ndash-1927.html).
- Classical orbit pictures could not fully explain atomic spectra. Matrix/operator treatment encodes measurable transitions and intensities; position and momentum operators generally **do not commute**: order matters.
