- **1927uncertainty principle:** inherent limits on simultaneously sharp position/momentum distributions, **ΔxΔp≥ℏ/2**, not merely poor instruments. [Nobel educational account](https://educationalgames.nobelprize.org/educational/physics/quantised_world/final-3.html).
- Quantum theory underpins semiconductors/transistors,lasers,nuclear physics and MRI/PET. Calling Helgoland a birthplace of modern quantum mechanics recognises a crucial1925step; quantum theory also had earlier foundations.

topics.title: Bonn climate talks 2025 and the road to COP30
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## SB62: June 16–26, 2025
- UNFCCC subsidiary bodies met in **Bonn, Germany**, preparing technical negotiations for **COP30, Belém, Brazil**. The July 8-labelled material highlights an agenda impasse of nearly two days over developed-country finance duties under **Paris Article 9.1** and unilateral trade measures.
- **Finance:** developing countries sought predictable grants rather than debt-creating loans, accountability for contributors and the **Baku-to-Belém roadmap towards US$1.3 trillion annually**. A roadmap/goal is not money already disbursed.
- **Adaptation:** refine indicators for the Global Goal on Adaptation; measuring finance, technology and capacity-building support remained contested. Technical progress did not settle financing obligations.
- **Mitigation Work Programme:** cooperation and implementation support versus fears of externally imposed national targets; a proposed digital platform raised duplication concerns. Article 6 cooperation and transparency also advanced technically.
- **Loss and damage:** the Santiago Network concerns technical assistance; arrangements for assistance do not by themselves establish adequate funding or compensate every loss.
- **Just transition:** protect workers, vulnerable communities and Indigenous knowledge while shifting to clean energy; developing countries questioned carbon-border trade barriers. Gender negotiations included unpaid care, reproductive health, violence, diversity and intersectionality.
- India uses **LMDC** and **BASIC (Brazil, South Africa, India, China)** to press equity, finance and technology access. [UNFCCC SB62](https://unfccc.int/sb62).
## COP milestone revision from the embedded chart
| COP | Main distinction |
|---|---|
| Kyoto 1997 | Protocol with quantified developed-country commitments |
| Marrakesh 2001; Delhi 2002 | Kyoto implementation rules; development priorities |
| Bali 2007; Copenhagen 2009 | Negotiating roadmap; fast-start finance pledge for 2010–12 |
| Cancún 2010; Doha 2012 | Green Climate Fund; Kyoto second commitment period |
| Warsaw 2013 | REDD+ framework and Warsaw loss-and-damage mechanism |
| Paris 2015; Glasgow 2021 | Paris Agreement; Glasgow Pact and India's 2070 pledge |
| Sharm el-Sheikh 2022; Dubai 2023 | Establishing loss-and-damage funding arrangements; operationalisation at COP28 and first global stocktake |
| Baku 2024 | New climate-finance goal and Baku-to-Belém roadmap |
- The chart's COP28 wording needs care: global-stocktake language was **transitioning away from fossil fuels**, not a universal legal fossil-fuel phase-out by 2050; coal wording concerned **phase-down of unabated coal**. The US$100-billion finance commitment predates Paris. Renewable/nuclear/cooling pledges have differing participants, and are not identical universally binding treaty obligations.

topics.title: Women-led MSMEs and access to finance
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Credit gap behind enterprise ownership
- Embedded analysis reports women-led firms at **20.50% of registered MSMEs**, but **18.73% of employment, 11.15% of investment and 10.22% of turnover**. These are shares of different totals, not firm-level productivity measurements.
- The cited SIDBI comparison puts the gap between requested and received credit at **35% for women versus 20% for men**. Limited property collateral, financial literacy, documentation, bank access and lender bias restrict formal finance; informal high-interest loans can deepen vulnerability.
- **MUDRA, 2024:** women held **42,492,281 of 66,777,013 loan accounts (~64%)**, receiving **₹2,25,887.08 crore of ₹5,41,012.86 crore (~42%; article rounds to 41%)**. Account share is not loan-value share, and accounts are not necessarily unique borrowers.
- **Udyam Assist:** article reports over **1.86 crore informal micro-enterprises**, with women-led units **70.5%** and their employment share **70.8%**. Its universe differs from all registered MSMEs; formal recognition supports access but does not itself guarantee a loan.
- MSMEs' roughly **30% GDP contribution** is a dated sector estimate; **35%** is the article's ambition, not an achieved share. RBI's June repo reduction to **5.5%** and announced CRR easing can support liquidity, but phased CRR cuts were not already fully implemented in July.
- Improve credit appraisal, outreach, financial capability, documentation and collateral substitutes; measure loan size, costs and successful utilisation as well as registrations/accounts.

topics.title: Great hornbill: ecology and conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Species and habitat
- **Buceros bicornis**: great/Great Indian/concave-casqued hornbill, a large canopy bird of tall evergreen and moist deciduous forests in the **Western Ghats, Northeast and lower Himalayan foothills**, extending into Southeast Asia. A reported **Ezhimala, Kannur, Kerala** sighting highlights habitat connectivity.
- Approximate size **95–130 cm**, wingspan up to **1.5 m**; large yellow bill/casque, with yellow coloration influenced by preen-gland secretions. Males are generally larger. Frugivory, particularly figs, supports long-distance seed dispersal; diet also includes small animals.
- Female seals herself in a tree cavity, leaving a slit through which the male feeds her and the young. Long nesting cycles and dependence on large old cavity trees make logging especially damaging; breeding timing varies by region.
- **IUCN Vulnerable; CITES Appendix I; Wildlife (Protection) Act Schedule I**. Threats: habitat fragmentation and hunting for meat, feathers and casques. Community nest adoption, forest protection and artificial casques replacing hunting in **Nyishi** traditions support conservation. State bird of **Kerala and Arunachal Pradesh**.
## Embedded nine-species chart: habitat distinctions
- **Rufous-necked, wreathed and Austen's brown hornbills:** Northeast; **Narcondam hornbill:** endemic to Narcondam Island in the Andamans; **Malabar grey:** Western Ghats; **Malabar pied:** forested peninsular India and Sri Lanka; **Oriental pied:** tropical/subtropical lowland forests; **Indian grey:** more widespread Indian subcontinent.
- Species have separate conservation assessments: the Narcondam hornbill was downlisted to **Vulnerable in the 2020 IUCN assessment**, while some older pages still say Endangered. [IUCN 2020 category changes](https://nc.iucnredlist.org/redlist/content/attachment_files/2020-3_RL_Stats_Table7.pdf). PYQ natural-habitat choice for great hornbill is **Western Ghats**, not desert, salt marsh or high-altitude Kashmir.

topics.title: Brazil: physical geography and regional links
topics.subject: India And World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Location and map
- South America's largest country and fifth-largest globally by area; capital **Brasília**, Atlantic coast, crossed by the **Equator and Tropic of Capricorn**. Neighbours: Argentina, Bolivia, Peru, Colombia, Venezuela, Paraguay, Uruguay, Guyana, Suriname, plus **French Guiana (France)**. It borders neither Chile nor Ecuador; French Guiana is not an independent country.
- **North:** Amazon lowlands/rainforest and Guiana Highlands; **centre/southeast:** Brazilian Highlands and Cerrado savanna; **west-central:** seasonally flooded **Pantanal in the Paraguay basin**; **northeast:** semi-arid Caatinga; **east:** Atlantic coastal plains/forest. Southern Brazil is chiefly subtropical; occasional snow occurs in southern highlands, so the source's blanket no-snow claim is wrong.
- **Amazon:** largest discharge/basin; absolute longest-river ranking is disputed. Major mapped tributaries: **Negro, Solimões, Madeira, Purus, Juruá, Tapajós and Xingu**; **Marajó** lies at the mouth. **São Francisco** serves the northeast; **Paraná** links to **Itaipu on the Brazil–Paraguay border**; **Tocantins–Araguaia** is another major system. Locate Mato Grosso, Patos Lagoon, Manaus, Belém, São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Salvador.
## Economy and cooperation
- Coffee, soybeans, sugarcane, oranges, cotton and cattle are important; iron ore, bauxite, gold, oil and hydropower support industry. Petrobras is the national oil-company example.
- Amazon deforestation/mining/cattle expansion, Pantanal fires and habitat degradation create conservation pressures. Brazil participates in **Mercosur, IBSA, G4, G20 and BRICS**; BRICS is no longer limited to the original five. India–Brazil cooperation includes agriculture, space, pharmaceuticals, energy and UN Security Council reform.

topics.title: PARAKH and school learning assessment
topics.subject: Governance
topics.markdown:
## Institution and portal
- **Performance Assessment, Review and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development**, established within **NCERT in 2023** under **NEP 2020**. It develops competency-based assessment norms, large-scale surveys, board equivalence and holistic progress cards for foundational, preparatory, middle and secondary stages; it is not an independent statutory school regulator.
- The dissemination portal opens national/State learning data for officials, educators and researchers to identify gaps and target interventions. **PARAKH Rashtriya Sarvekshan, 4 December 2024:** **21,15,022 pupils in Grades 3, 6 and 9**, **74,229 schools**, **781 districts**; questionnaires from **2,70,424 teachers/school leaders**. Do not replace Grade 6 with Grade 5.
- Article highlights Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Kerala, Chandigarh and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, with rankings varying by grade/subject. Kendriya Vidyalayas were weak in Grade 3 mathematics but strong across Grade 9 subjects; this is not one universal school-type ranking.
- Illustrative competency results: Grade 3 **55%** could arrange numbers up to 99; Grade 6 **54%** could represent numbers using Indian place value and **38%** solve specified whole-number problems; Grade 9 **54%** could identify main textual points, **31%** understand specified number sets and **45%** explain the Constitution's emergence/ideals. These are item/competency performance percentages, not board-examination pass rates.

topics.title: Sierra Leone and Nyangai coastal displacement
topics.subject: India And World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Nyangai case study
- **Nyangai**, in the **Turtle Islands off southern Sierra Leone's Atlantic coast**, illustrates erosion, inundation and saltwater intrusion. Reported remaining dimensions are about **200 ×100 m**, after loss of over two-thirds of its land in less than a decade; the article places residents at **under 300 from roughly 1,000**. These are report estimates, not a new national census.
- Loss of homes, coconut/mango trees, fields and fishing access combines with unsafe drinking water, sanitation and health-service gaps. Remoteness (reported seven-hour canoe access from Freetown) complicates relocation; residents reported inadequate practical support. Attribution must consider local erosion processes as well as sea-level rise.
- **Climate justice:** communities with small emissions face severe losses; planned relocation needs livelihoods, consent, services and finance. “Climate refugee” here is descriptive, not automatic status under the 1951 Refugee Convention. The claimed June 2024 estimate of two million people at risk needs the original report and is not retained as verified.
## Geography, society and economy
- West African Atlantic state; **Guinea north/east, Liberia southeast; capital Freetown** with a major natural harbour. Coastal mangroves give way to inland hills/uplands. Rivers: **Rokel, Taia, Sewa and Moa**. Map: **Lungi, Banana Islands, Sherbro Island, Turtle Islands and Kilimi National Park**.
- English is official; **Krio** is widely used. Presidential constitutional republic with a unicameral legislature; the source's ~7.5-million population is undated and should not be treated as a July 2025 estimate.
- Freetown-area settlements of freed Black people: **1787** arrivals from London, **1792** from Nova Scotia, **1800** Jamaican Maroons; **1808** Crown colony concerned Freetown/peninsula rather than all modern Sierra Leone. Independence **1961**; civil war ended **2002**.
- Farming includes rice, cassava, cocoa and oil palm; minerals include diamonds, bauxite, gold and **rutile (TiO₂)**. Post-war infrastructure, education and health deficits interact with coastal/mangrove degradation.

topics.title: National Population Register: residents, Census and citizenship
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Definition and legal basis
- **NPR** records India's **usual residents**, regardless of nationality: a person who has lived in an area for the preceding **six months OR intends to live there for the next six months**. The source incorrectly requires both conditions. NPR entry is not citizenship or proof that a foreign national's stay is lawful.
- Legal framework: **Citizenship Act 1955, section 14A**, and **Citizenship (Registration of Citizens and Issue of National Identity Cards) Rules 2003**, including **rule 3(4)**. First prepared **2010**, updated **2015**; the planned 2020 update was postponed. The July clipping said a further update alongside the coming Census remained undecided. [Census NPR information](https://censusindia.gov.in/census.website/en/node/343).
| Instrument | Main distinction |
|---|---|
| NPR | Administrative register of usual residents, including non-citizens |
| Census | Statistical enumeration under Census Act 1948; individual returns protected by statutory confidentiality |
| NRIC/NRC | Register of Indian citizens; citizenship verification involves its own prescribed procedure |
- The 2003 Rules link population registration and citizenship-register preparation, but being recorded in NPR does not itself decide citizenship or automatically label anyone an illegal migrant.
- Potential administrative uses include planning and reducing duplicate identity records, subject to accuracy, purpose limits and privacy. A proposed unified identity card does not mean NPR already replaces passports, Aadhaar or voter ID. The source's 2020 digital/self-enumeration claim conflates Census-rule changes with NPR and is not treated as proof of a new NPR legal rule.

topics.title: Four labour codes: coverage and implementation debate
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Enacted framework as of July 10, 2025
- **29 central laws → four Codes** enacted in 2019–20. Their principal consolidated provisions were **not yet brought into force in July 2025**; enactment, draft rules, commencement and actual benefit delivery are distinct stages. Labour is in the Concurrent List; Centre–State rules and enforcement capacity matter.
| Code | Laws consolidated | Main scope |
|---|---|---|
| Code on Wages, 2019 | 4 | Minimum/floor wage framework, timely wage payment, bonus and equal remuneration |
| Industrial Relations Code, 2020 | 3 | Trade unions, industrial disputes, standing orders, retrenchment/closure and fixed-term employment |
| Code on Social Security, 2020 | 9 | PF, ESI, maternity, gratuity and frameworks/schemes for unorganised, gig and platform workers |
| Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 | 13 | Workplace safety/health, hours and welfare; factories, mines, plantations, contract and inter-State migrant labour |
- Universalising minimum-wage coverage beyond scheduled employments differs from already paying every worker a common wage. Social-security recognition does not automatically give every gig worker all EPF/ESI benefits; scheme design, eligibility, contributions and implementation matter. OSH coverage/obligations have establishment-specific thresholds.
## Strike and implementation concerns
- **July 9 nationwide strike:** ten central trade unions claimed over **25 crore participants**, protesting labour codes, prices, insecure work and unemployment. Participation is a union claim, not a verified official headcount. The clipping points to a roughly decade-long gap since the **2015 Indian Labour Conference**.
- Article's 2024 committee account of draft rules in 32 States/UTs and historical shortages must retain that reference period. Priorities: tripartite consultation, clear rules, inspection/grievance capacity, informal-worker inclusion and outcome monitoring.
- Women's **worker-population ratio, age 15+, usual status: 28.7% (2019–20) →40.3% (2023–24)**; this is not female labour-force participation or proof all new work is formal/decent. National Career Service, rural/tribal skills and social protection complement legal simplification.
- PYQ revision: **Factories Act 1948 and Plantations Labour Act 1951 → OSHWC Code 2020**.

topics.title: Nistar: indigenous diving support vessel
topics.subject: Internal Security
topics.markdown:
## Delivery and capability
- **Hindustan Shipyard Limited, Visakhapatnam delivered Nistar to the Indian Navy on July 8, 2025**, announced by PIB July 9. The source wrongly calls July 9 commissioning; delivery and commissioning are separate events. [Navy delivery release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2143335&lang=2&reg=48).
- First indigenously designed/built diving support vessel of this project: approximately **118 m, 10,000 tonnes, 75% indigenous content**, built to Indian Register of Shipping classification rules.
- **Saturation diving to 300 m; side diving to 75 m; ROV operations to 1,000 m**. These are different capabilities, not interchangeable diver depths. Acts as mothership for a **Deep Submergence Rescue Vehicle**, supporting submarine rescue, deep-sea diving, salvage and underwater repair.
- Sanskrit name conveys liberation/rescue/salvation. Capability supports maritime safety, shipbuilding self-reliance and sustained operations away from shore. PYQ distinction: **INS Astradharini is a torpedo launch/recovery vessel; Dhruv is an advanced light helicopter**.

## Commissioning: 18 July 2025
- The July 19 clipping reports **INS Nistar commissioned**, following delivery on July 8. Commissioning, delivery and earlier launch are distinct milestones; existing diving-depth/ROV/DSRV capabilities remain unchanged.
- Official commissioning release reports **over 80% indigenous content and 120 MSMEs**, compared with the PDF/earlier delivery summary's roughly 75%. Treat these as differently reported event-stage figures; the commissioning announcement is the later official account. [Navy commissioning release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2145766&lang=2&reg=48).

topics.title: Irregular migration and the donkey route
topics.subject: Internal Security
topics.markdown:
## Migration, smuggling and exploitation
- “Donkey/dunki route” describes circuitous, often irregular cross-border journeys arranged by agents, including routes through Latin America towards the US. The **Darién Gap lies across the Colombia–Panama border**. The map's Delhi/Punjab/Gujarat/Mumbai–Istanbul–Guatemala/US paths are illustrative, not one fixed itinerary.
- Source reports agent demands of **₹40–60 lakh** and dangerous forest/desert/sea crossings, document fraud, extortion, injury, trafficking and deportation; costs vary by route/case. Its old graphic's Guatemala/US price ranges use different endpoints. Do not reproduce its unverified visa-free claims as current travel rules.
- **Migrant smuggling** facilitates irregular entry; **trafficking** involves exploitation and can occur without border crossing. They can overlap but are not synonyms. Seeking asylum is not automatically fraudulent and does not itself guarantee permission to stay.
## July 9 enforcement report and response
- ED searches at **11 locations in Punjab/Haryana** were linked to a money-laundering investigation based on **17 police FIRs** against agents/middlemen; the clipping cites alleged charges around **₹45–50 lakh per person**. Allegations are not convictions, and PMLA proceedings require the applicable scheduled-offence/proceeds-of-crime nexus.
- Responses: prosecute fraudulent/exploitative networks, regulate recruitment agents, improve safe legal migration information and livelihoods, cooperate across borders, and provide victim/consular support. Distinguish criminal organisers from migrants and protect privacy and due process.
- The source's proposed 250-word mains question is a practice prompt, not an authenticated PYQ.

topics.title: Fenugreek: cultivation, uses and nitrogen fixation
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Crop revision
- **Trigonella foenum-graecum**, family **Fabaceae**; methi/Vendhayam. Seeds are a spice, fresh/dried leaves a vegetable/flavouring; also fodder and traditional herbal/nutraceutical uses.
- Mainly cool-season **rabi** crop: well-drained loam/clay loam, roughly **10–25°C**; typical October–November sowing and March–April harvest vary by location. Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Punjab and Tamil Nadu are listed. Varieties include **RMt-305, RMt-1, Hisar Sonali**; the source's **10–12 quintals/ha** is indicative, not assured yield.
- Rhizobium-related root-nodule symbiosis supports nitrogen fixation; performance depends on inoculum, soil and crop conditions. Pests/diseases include aphids, pod borers, root rot and powdery mildew; avoid waterlogging. Research/extension through ICAR/KVKs and relevant horticulture schemes can help, without implying automatic scheme eligibility.
- Contains protein, fibre, minerals and compounds such as **trigonelline, saponins and diosgenin**. Traditional diabetes/lactation/digestive claims are not established treatment recommendations; high-quality clinical evidence is limited. [NIH evidence note](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USNIHNCCIH/bulletins/2fac823?reqfrom=share).
## Nitrogen-fixer PYQ revision
- **Alfalfa, chickpea and clover** form nitrogen-fixing symbioses; amaranth, purslane and spinach are not corresponding nodulated nitrogen-fixing legumes.
- **Frankia** supports actinorhizal plants such as alder, Casuarina and sea buckthorn. **Nostoc/Anabaena** are cyanobacteria, while **Azolla is a fern with a cyanobacterial symbiont**, not itself a cyanobacterium.

topics.title: India–Namibia relations and Namibia geography
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## July 9 state visit
- Prime Minister Modi met President **Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah** and addressed Namibia's Parliament. Agreements covered **health/medicine** and an **Entrepreneurship Development Centre**; Namibia completed steps to join **CDRI** and the **Global Biofuel Alliance**. President conferred the **Order of the Most Ancient Welwitschia Mirabilis**, Namibia's highest civilian honour. [Official award announcement](https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/pm-conferred-with-namibias-highest-civilian-award/?comment=disable).
- **April 26, 2024 NIPL–Bank of Namibia technology agreement** supports deployment of a **UPI-like domestic real-time payments system**. July 9 reporting anticipated a launch later in 2025; the notes' “by end-2024” line is stale and not proof the system was already live. [Official bilateral agreements](https://ns.hciwindhoek.gov.in/bilateral-agreement.php).
- India's anti-colonial support dates to UN advocacy in the 1940s; later support for **SWAPO** must not be backdated to 1946, before SWAPO's formation. Partnership stresses African value addition, skills, health and South–South cooperation alongside minerals.
## Map essentials
- **Southwestern Africa, Atlantic coast; capital Windhoek; Southern/Eastern hemispheres; Tropic of Capricorn**. Land neighbours: **Angola, Zambia, Botswana and South Africa**; **no Zimbabwe land border**.
- West → east: **Namib coastal desert, central plateau, Kalahari basin**. Cold **Benguela Current** contributes to coastal aridity/fog. Highest point **Königstein in the Brandberg massif**, rather than treating the whole massif as one peak.
- Northern/northeastern rivers: **Kunene, Okavango (Cubango), Zambezi, Mashi/Kwando**; **Orange** forms much of the South African border. Many interior rivers are ephemeral. **Okavango ends in Botswana's inland delta; Zambezi reaches the Indian Ocean**.
- Locate **Caprivi/Zambezi strip, Etosha Pan, Skeleton Coast, Swakopmund, Walvis Bay, Lüderitz, Namib-Naukluft and Fish River Canyon**. The Zambezi basin map includes **Kariba/Cahora Bassa and Victoria Falls**, outside Namibia as appropriate.
- Major resources: **diamonds, uranium, gold, zinc and copper**; desert/coastal ecosystems and tourism complement mining.
## PYQ map distinctions
- **Atlas Mountains → northwestern Africa; Abyssinian Plateau → Ethiopia; Guiana Highlands → northeastern South America; Okavango basin → southern Africa**, not Patagonia.
- River outlets: **Mekong → South China Sea; Thames → North Sea; Volga → Caspian Sea; Zambezi → Indian Ocean**.

## August editorial: sustain the July partnership
- Repeats the **9 July 2025 visit**, health/entrepreneurship agreements, CDRI/GBA links and map facts; source's additional editorial emphasis is sustained skills, digital public infrastructure, local value addition and accountable delivery rather than intermittent high-level visits.
- Source cites **US$800 million bilateral trade**, **US$12 billion Africa-wide development partnership** and a **US$12 million Ongwediva India Wing** grant; these are source-era figures with different geographic/programme scopes and incompletely specified reference periods, not one Namibia aid total.
- Technology-sharing requires local regulation, data safeguards, training and follow-through. Source practice assumes a Namibian UPI system already operating; existing notes retain the **2024 technology agreement and July 2025 prospective rollout** distinction. No July uranium supply deal is demonstrated by the listed visit outcomes, but that does not erase earlier bilateral nuclear-cooperation agreements.
- SWAPO solidarity and Lt Gen **Diwan Prem Chand's UN role** illustrate historical links; do not backdate SWAPO support to 1946. Capacity building, climate/food security and mineral partnerships are policy opportunities; a mineral-rich country is not automatically free of development constraints.

topics.title: Maratha Military Landscapes of India
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## July 2025 inscription
- UNESCO inscribed the **Maratha Military Landscapes of India** as India's **44th World Heritage property** in July 2025. The serial property combines **12 forts: 11 in Maharashtra and Gingee in Tamil Nadu**, representing a landscape-based defence network developed during the seventeenth to early nineteenth centuries. [UNESCO property](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1739).
- **Hill forts:** Salher, Shivneri, Lohgad, Raigad, Rajgad, Gingee; **hill-forest:** Pratapgad; **hill-plateau:** Panhala; **coastal:** Vijaydurg; **island:** Khanderi, Suvarnadurg, Sindhudurg. Forts relate to the Sahyadris, Deccan Plateau, Konkan coast and Eastern Ghats.
- **ASI protects eight:** Shivneri, Lohgad, Raigad, Panhala, Suvarnadurg, Vijaydurg, Sindhudurg, Gingee. Maharashtra protects Salher, Rajgad, Pratapgad and Khanderi.
- Local terrain, walls, watchtowers, secret routes, granaries and water storage supported command, supplies, surveillance and **Ganimi Kava** guerrilla tactics. Networked forts embody **Swarajya** and resistance, with use continued under Sambhaji/Peshwas until the 1818 defeat of Maratha power.
- Correct the sheet's approximate “reign ~1670”: Shivaji's coronation was **1674**; distinguish the emergence of the system from his formal kingship. Its sweeping “purely indigenous/no foreign architects” statement is not required to establish the property's heritage value. Conservation and sustainable tourism must protect the landscape as well as masonry.

topics.title: PM E-DRIVE and electric-truck incentives
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Scheme and July 2025 truck incentive
- Correct expansion: **PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement**; Ministry of Heavy Industries scheme, notified September 2024, **₹10,900 crore**. Original source-period implementation was **1 October 2024–31 March 2026**, subsuming earlier EMPS spending; the sheet's “Electric Demand Reduction…” expansion is wrong. Covers electric 2/3-wheelers, ambulances, trucks, buses, charging infrastructure and testing-agency upgrades; private electric cars are excluded. [Scheme portal](https://pmedriveuat.heavyindustries.gov.in/).
- E-truck incentive was announced **11 July 2025**, not July 12 as the sheet says: **₹500 crore**, about **5,600 trucks**, maximum **₹9.6 lakh/truck** depending on weight. Categories **N2: above 3.5–12 tonnes; N3: above 12–55 tonnes**. Delhi allocation: **₹100 crore/about 1,100 trucks**. Purchase-price reduction is reimbursed to OEMs; scrapping an old truck is required. Warranty: battery **five years/5 lakh km**; vehicle/motor **five years/2.5 lakh km**, whichever earlier. [Launch release](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2143995&lang=2&reg=48).
- Earlier **FAME-I (2015–2019)** supported hybrid/EV adoption, pilots and charging; **FAME-II (2019–2024)** initially had ₹10,000 crore, including public/commercial e-buses, 3-wheelers, 4-wheelers and 2-wheelers. Original FAME-II targets included 7,000 buses, five lakh 3-wheelers, 55,000 4-wheelers and ten lakh 2-wheelers; targets are not actual sales.
- Truck incentives address high upfront cost and diesel freight pollution; charging reliability, battery life, domestic supply, electricity mix and total cost of ownership determine results. Cleaner urban air, energy security and green jobs are intended benefits; lifecycle emissions and implementation must be measured. Source's mains prompt is a practice question, not a PYQ.

topics.title: Baltic grey seals, declining ice and marine protection
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Ice loss and breeding
- **Grey seal (*Halichoerus grypus*)** breeds on Baltic drift ice and coastal islets; globally listed Least Concern in the source period. Reduced ice can concentrate land breeding, disturb colonies and lower pup survival. A suggested reassessment is **not an accomplished IUCN status change**; the sheet's ~3,000 annual pups lacks a clear year/geographic denominator.
- Grey seals are **facultative ice breeders**; distinguish more ice-dependent ringed seals. HELCOM finds reduced ice can affect breeding and pups born on land can fare worse; threats also include disturbance, bycatch, pollution and food-web changes. [HELCOM reproduction assessment](https://indicators.helcom.fi/indicator/seal-reproduction/).
- **Baltic Sea:** low-salinity, semi-enclosed northern European sea bordered by Denmark, Germany, Poland, Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, Russia, Finland and Sweden. “Mediterranean-type sea” describes enclosure; **it is not the Mediterranean Sea**. Eutrophication, pollution and climate change interact.
- **1992 Helsinki Convention:** Convention on the Protection of the Marine Environment of the Baltic Sea Area; cooperation through **HELCOM**. Protect breeding habitat, reduce disturbance/bycatch/pollution and mitigate warming.
## Treaty-term revision
- Annex-I countries originate in **UNFCCC**; Kyoto sets differentiated commitments. **CERs** and **Clean Development Mechanism** belong to Kyoto, not Nagoya. **Cartagena** concerns biosafety/GMOs; **Nagoya** access and benefit sharing under CBD.
- The printed **2016** pairing exercise has only pair 3 correct, but omits the full option block; retain as revision and flag for PYQ review.

topics.title: Bulgaria and euro-area accession
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## July 2025 decision
- **8 July 2025:** EU Council adopted final legal acts for Bulgaria to introduce the euro on **1 January 2026**, becoming the **21st euro-area member**. In this July source it is a future change, not already operating euro circulation. Croatia joined in 2023; euro-area membership stood at 20 before Bulgaria's changeover. [Council decision](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2025/07/08/bulgaria-ready-to-use-the-euro-from-1-january-2026-council-takes-final-steps/).
- Euro introduced in 1999 by 11 countries; **ECB, Frankfurt** manages monetary policy. National budgets/taxes remain national, subject to EU coordination/rules. Andorra, Monaco, San Marino and Vatican City use euro by agreement; Kosovo/Montenegro use it unilaterally and are not euro-area EU members.
- Maastricht convergence: price stability, sound public finances, long-term interest-rate convergence, and **at least two years in ERM II without severe tensions**. The fiscal reference values are **3% deficit/GDP and 60% debt/GDP**; legal assessment has qualifications, so do not treat the sheet's strict less-than shorthand as the entire rule.
## Map recall
- **Sofia** capital; southeastern Europe/eastern Balkans, Black Sea coast. Neighbours: Romania north (Danube for much of border), Serbia west, North Macedonia southwest, Greece/Turkey south.
- Balkan Mountains centrally; Rhodopes near Greece; Rila's **Musala 2,925 m** highest Bulgarian peak. Rivers include Danube, Iskur, Maritsa, Struma, Tundzha and Yantra. Mostly continental climate with southern Mediterranean influence.

topics.title: Accelerator mass spectrometry and radiocarbon dating
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Method and use
- **Accelerator mass spectrometry (AMS)** directly counts rare isotopes such as **carbon-14**, rather than waiting to measure radioactive decays. Convert sample carbon to ions → accelerate → separate isotopes/interferences → measure isotope ratios → calibrate age.
- Useful for organic archaeological remains such as charcoal, wood and bone, geological/environmental reconstruction, and biomedical tracers. Small samples and high sensitivity preserve precious material; contamination, pretreatment, reservoir effects and calibration still matter.
- The source reports Tamil Nadu archaeology authorities sending **23 charcoal samples to Beta Analytic, USA**, to date archaeological layers. Sample submission is not a published age/result or proof every artefact in that layer is identical in age.
- Its **20 mg vs ≥10 g**, hours vs days comparison is illustrative rather than universal laboratory requirements; AMS counts atoms/isotopic ratios, not “extremely small radioactivity”. Material age must be interpreted with stratigraphy and archaeological context.

topics.title: BIND and public broadcasting infrastructure
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Public broadcasting
- **Broadcasting Infrastructure and Network Development (BIND)** is a Central Sector scheme supporting **Prasar Bharati: Akashvani/AIR and Doordarshan**. Embedded Cabinet graphic gives **₹2,539.61 crore** outlay.
- Modernises broadcasting equipment/studios, content production, civil infrastructure and DTH channel capacity; expands reliable information in remote, tribal, border and Left Wing Extremism areas. Domestic/regional programming and DD India's international reach support cultural access and public communication.
- Source targets AIR FM reach **59% →66% geographic area** and **68% →80% population**: these are separate denominators and intended coverage, not already achieved results. It reports an **Akashvani Kendra at Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh** under the scheme.
- Digital/HD/satellite upgrades, accessibility and credible regional content matter alongside transmitter coverage; equipment installation can support indirect employment.

topics.title: Mahi River and Gambhira bridge collapse
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## River map
- West-flowing **Mahi/Mahisagar** originates in the **Vindhya region, Madhya Pradesh**; passes through **MP → Rajasthan (Banswara/Vagad) → Gujarat**, reaching the **Gulf of Khambhat, Arabian Sea**, through an estuary.
- **583 km; basin approximately 34,842 km²**. The embedded graphic rounds basin area to 36,000; retain the specified hydrological value. [Gujarat river data](https://guj-nwrws.gujarat.gov.in/showpage.aspx?contentid=1486&lang=English).
- Important tributaries: **Som, Anas and Panam**; the sheet also lists Jakham, Eru, Moran, Bhadar, Chap and Nori. Basin lies between Aravalli/Malwa/Vindhya regions and Gulf of Khambhat. Map identifies **Mahi Bajaj Sagar and Kadana dams**.
- Source reports **Gambhira–Mujpur bridge collapse in Padra taluka, Vadodara**, over Mahi. Bridge inspection, maintenance, flood/scour and structural assessment require engineering investigation; the river's presence alone does not establish the cause.

topics.title: SEPECAT Jaguar and fleet modernisation
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Aircraft and Indian service
- **Anglo-French SEPECAT Jaguar**, British Aircraft Corporation/Breguet lineage, is a twin-engine deep-penetration ground-attack aircraft; Indian name **Shamsher**. Distinguish strike role from strategic transport and fifth-generation fighter classifications.
- India began induction in **1979**, with imported aircraft and HAL licence manufacture. Sheet's roughly **160 inducted/~120 operational/six squadrons** are source-period estimates, not a current verified inventory.
- Variants: **IS single-seat strike; IB two-seat trainer; IM maritime strike**. Refuelling probe, navigation/attack avionics, radar altimeter, inertial navigation and upgraded cockpit support range/precision. Equipment differs by variant/upgrade; a list is not proof every airframe carries every listed system.
- Source specifications: up to **4,500 kg payload**, about **1,699 km/h**, ceiling **46,000 ft**, combat-radius figures **850 km/internal fuel, 1,400 km/drop tanks**; mission profiles/load determine actual performance. Its “introduced 1968” conflates early flight/development with service introduction; do not use it as IAF induction year.
- July clipping reports two pilots killed in a crash near **Churu, Rajasthan**, described as the third Jaguar crash that year. Ageing fleets require maintenance, accident investigation and replacement planning; no specific cause is established merely from aircraft age.

topics.title: Lake Turkana and ancient enamel proteins
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Image-only July clipping
- **Lake Turkana (Lake Rudolf/Jade Sea)** lies mainly in northern Kenya and extends into Ethiopia; **Omo** is its main perennial inflow. Africa's fourth-largest lake and world's largest permanent desert lake; saline water and arid Rift Valley setting support distinctive ecology/palaeontology.
- **Lake Turkana National Parks** World Heritage property comprises **Sibiloi, Central Island and South Island**; this does not designate the entire lake/basin as one national park. [UNESCO description](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/801).
- Source says researchers extracted 18–20-million-year-old mammal tooth-enamel proteins. Primary study reports enamel protein fragments from **Buluk (~16 Ma) and Loperot (~18 Ma), Turkana Basin**, with preservation extending to at least 18 million years; do not inflate this to a demonstrated exact 20-million-year age or imply extraction from lake water. [Nature study](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09040-9).
- Ancient proteins can reveal evolutionary relationships beyond some DNA-preservation limits; protein recovery is distinct from recovering intact ancient DNA or resurrecting an extinct animal.

topics.title: Talisman Sabre: multinational military interoperability
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## July 2025 exercise
- Biennial Australia–US exercise begun **2005**; **11th edition opened 13 July 2025**, with an opening estimate of **35,000+ personnel from 19 countries**, including India. Major domains: sea, land, air, space and cyber; amphibious operations, live fire, logistics and command coordination build interoperability. [Australian Defence opening release](https://www.defence.gov.au/news-events/releases/2025-07-13/exercise-talisman-sabre-2025-opens).
- Activities across Queensland, Northern Territory, Western Australia, New South Wales and Christmas Island; **Papua New Guinea hosts elements for the first time outside Australia**. Opening estimates should not be silently replaced with later final totals.
- India gains joint operational experience and stronger Australian/Indo-Pacific defence ties. Participation does not itself establish a mutual-defence alliance; Quad is a separate grouping.

topics.title: Jarawa and Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups
topics.subject: Anthropology
topics.markdown:
## Jarawa: habitat and protection
- Indigenous **Middle and South Andaman** community; a **PVTG**, traditionally hunting, gathering and fishing in tropical forests/coastal habitats. Contact with outsiders increased in the late 1990s; infection exposure, poaching, encroachment, tourism and the Andaman Trunk Road threaten habitat and autonomy.
- The graphic identifies their language as **Ongan**; do not repeat the text's claim that it is unrelated to every other Andamanese language. Claims of descent from the extinct Jangil or a precisely dated migration are not established here. Source population **250–400** is an undated estimate, not a verified July 2025 census.
- Graphic reports **19 Jarawa members enrolled on electoral rolls**; inclusion is distinct from compulsory assimilation or loss of habitat protections. Protect voluntary contact, culturally appropriate healthcare, land/resource access and community consent. [Government Jarawa policy](https://tribal.nic.in/downloads/PVTG/The%20Andaman%20And%20Nicobar%20Gazette%20dated%2021-12-2004-Policy%20on%20Jarawa%20Tribe%20of%20Andaman%20Islands.pdf).
## PVTG recall
- **75 groups across 18 States and one UT**, Andaman & Nicobar Islands. Core identification characteristics: pre-agricultural technology, stagnant/declining population, very low literacy and subsistence/economic backwardness. Remoteness increases vulnerability but is not a substitute for the core criteria. [Ministry of Tribal Affairs](https://tribal.nic.in/PM-JANMAN.aspx).
- Examples: Jarawa, Great Andamanese, Onge, Sentinelese; Birhor/Asur; Baiga; Saharia; **Irular and Konda Reddi**. Source village/district/population totals lack a common dated survey basis and should not be memorised as an exact current count.
- **2019 PYQ:** statements **1, 2 and 4** correct; **95 groups** is false. Supplied page lacks the answer-option list, so the incomplete question is flagged rather than reconstructed.

topics.title: Ordinary residence and migrant voting rights
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Statutory framework
- **RPA 1950 section 19:** eligible adult citizens ordinarily resident in a constituency can enter its electoral roll, subject to disqualifications. **Section 20:** owning a house alone does not establish residence; temporary absence alone does not end it. Residence is determined from the facts, not ownership or a universal permanent-home test. [India Code](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/indiacode/handle/123456789/1663).
- Special deeming provisions cover service-qualified persons and their eligible wives residing with them, and declared office-holders under the applicable provisions. Service qualification includes armed forces, forces subject to Army Act provisions, State armed police serving outside their State and Government of India staff posted abroad. Avoid treating every government employee or every spouse as automatically eligible under identical rules.
- **Section 20A**, inserted 2010: an eligible Indian citizen abroad who has not acquired foreign citizenship can register at the Indian passport address. Overseas elector registration does not itself provide ordinary postal/online voting. [ECI overseas-elector explanation](https://www.eci.gov.in/faq/2/9).
- **Registration of Electors Rules 1960** regulate roll preparation/revision. Avoid duplicate enrolment; ordinary-residence assessment and deletion require lawful procedure.
## Migrant inclusion: July editorial
- Seasonal workers may retain family/social ties at origin while living temporarily near work. Rigid assessment and costly travel can exclude them; the source estimates roughly **15 crore migrants**, not a precisely verified eligible-elector count.
- Proposed reforms: clarify economic-migration treatment, accessible enrolment/objections, portable participation and tested remote voting. ECI's remote-voting exploration is not proof of nationwide implementation. Aadhaar-related reform proposals do not make Aadhaar mandatory proof of citizenship or justify automatic deletion.

## Bihar Special Intensive Revision: July 25 debate
- ECI's **24 June2025 SIR order** and **21 July counter-affidavit** were challenged before the Supreme Court. ECI defended electoral eligibility/citizenship verification; critics questioned evidence, burden of documents, treatment of post-2003 voters and exclusion risks. These were competing submissions, not a final judgment of illegality.
- **Article326**, RPA1950 **sections15,16,19,20 and21**, and electoral-registration rules must be read together: rolls are constituency-specific; citizenship, age and residence are distinct conditions; **section21** addresses preparation/revision. Source's “section15 alone authorises fresh citizenship proof from all” is incomplete.
- **2003 Bihar rolls** provided a documentary baseline/exemption for listed electors; critics ask why a later existing entry should not receive comparable weight. Aadhaar establishes identity rather than citizenship; neither a ration card nor an EPIC is conclusive citizenship proof. This does not settle which combinations ECI must accept as evidence.
- The PDF conflates **Citizenship Amendment Act2003**, citizenship-by-birth rules and the contested **CAA2019**; these are separate enactments. Birth/parentage criteria depend on birth periods in the Citizenship Act, not an automatic power to conduct a nationwide NRC through electoral revision. NRC and electoral rolls have different purposes/procedures.
- Issue reports forms from over90% of **7.89crore electors**, possible deceased/migrated/multiple registrations, and incomplete documents. Its **53lakh/not-found**, **~21.6lakh deceased,31.5lakh migrated,7lakh duplicates** categories are overlapping/changing reports, not quantities to add into a reconciled deletion count. Submission, draft inclusion, verification, objection and final deletion are different stages.
- Safeguards: accessible forms/help for migrants and vulnerable groups, transparent constituency-level data, individual notice/hearing, reasoned correction and appeal, ample document opportunities and non-arbitrary standards. Compare Assam NRC only as a caution on costs/exclusion; electoral revision is not legally identical.
- [ECI source-period progress release,23July2025](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2147413&lang=2&reg=48).

## Bihar draft roll: 1 August 2025
- Draft after SIR enumeration includes **over 7.24 crore**, roughly **65 lakh below earlier 7.89 crore**. Draft omission is not proof every excluded person is foreign or permanently disenfranchised.
- **Claims/objections 1 August–1 September** through prescribed forms/EROs; opportunities for inclusion/correction, individual reasons and due process. ECI release records **90,712 booths, 243 constituencies, 38 districts**, with distinct BLO, volunteer and party BLA roles. [ECI press note 1 August](https://www.eci.gov.in/eci-backend/public/api/download?url=LMAhAK6sOPBp%2FNFF0iRfXbEB1EVSLT41NNLRjYNJJP1KivrUxbfqkDatmHy12e%2Fzznw5Qtyss%2B8ILdni0Z0RBAkwVPAdy67ySd4dS2SdwaNNq0p8WWXDoViUeHPyzG9HgKdCmUSHqA1uyd%2BQgGswdQ%3D%3D).
- **RPA 1950 section 21(3)** permits special revision for recorded reasons; **Article 324** covers supervision/direction/control of rolls/elections. Practice wrongly cites RPA 1951.
- Inclusive documentation, migrant assistance, transparent data, notice, hearing, reasoned decisions and remedies balance clean rolls with enfranchisement. Foreign-infiltration assertions/arbitrary-cutoff criticisms remain competing claims, not final findings.
- **Mohinder Singh Gill** was decided **2 December 1977**, reported as **(1978) 1 SCC 405**; distinguish judgment date from report citation. Article 324 supplements statutory law, not overriding it. [Supreme Court judgment](https://api.sci.gov.in/jonew/judis/5188.pdf). Aadhaar/EPIC identity differs from citizenship proof; wider-document proposals do not make every card conclusive citizenship evidence.

## 14 August 2025: Supreme Court transparency directions
- Interim order required publication of roughly **65 lakh names omitted from Bihar's1 August draft roll**, with reasons, online through DEOs/CEO and physically at Panchayat/BDO offices; names should be searchable by EPIC. Court also directed publicity that aggrieved persons could submit claims with Aadhaar. **Deadline19 August** was a direction, not proof compliance was already achieved. [SupremeCourt order](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2025/35785/35785_2025_2_34_63142_Order_14-Aug-2025.pdf).
- Omission from the draft is distinct from final rejection, non-citizenship or permanent disenfranchisement. Aadhaar's use to support a claim does not make it conclusive citizenship proof. This interim safeguard did not finally decide every challenge to SIR legality.
- Wider discussion repeats existing notes on **RPA1950 s21(3), Article 324,2003 baseline**, migrant/document burdens, party BLAs, notice/hearing and accessible correction. Source's practice key is **2,3 only(C)**; options referring to statement4 are malformed. Existing note distinguishes the1977 decision date and 1978 citation of MohinderSinghGill.

topics.title: Open ecosystems: grasslands, savannas, scrublands and deserts
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Ecological and livelihood value
- **Grasslands, savannas, scrublands and deserts are functioning ecosystems**. Treating every treeless tract as degraded forest or wasteland can drive inappropriate plantations, fencing, infrastructure and industrial conversion.
- Habitat for **Great Indian Bustard, Indian wolf and caracal**; soil and roots store carbon, alongside ecosystem services and climate resilience. Forests also store below-ground carbon; the distinction is not an absolute forest-above/grassland-below divide.
- **Dhangar, Rabari and Kuruba** pastoral communities depend on access and seasonal grazing mobility. Their knowledge and stewardship should inform restoration; enclosure/afforestation may damage livelihoods and biodiversity.
- Drylands supported Mesopotamian, Egyptian and Indus civilisations and adaptive water-management traditions. A naturally arid desert is distinct from **land degradation/desertification**.
## Restoration suited to place
- Assess baseline ecology before tree planting; use water harvesting, appropriate rotational grazing, natural regeneration and local knowledge. Conserve open habitat and reward sustainable land use/soil-carbon maintenance.
- Replacing the blanket “wasteland” label and renaming the desertification observance are **editorial proposals**, not enacted classifications or a new UN day. Avoid assuming every grazing regime is sustainable without local assessment.

topics.title: Operation Shiva and Amarnath Yatra security
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## July 2025 operation
- Indian Army's **Operation Shiva** secures Amarnath Yatra with CAPFs, J&K Police and civil authorities; combines counter-terrorism, convoy/route surveillance, crowd/disaster response and high-altitude medical support.
- Source deployment snapshot: **8,500+ troops**, **50+ counter-UAS units and 50 electronic-warfare systems**, UAV/PTZ-camera surveillance and bomb-detection/disposal teams. These are dated reported figures, not permanent establishment strengths.
- **150+ medical personnel**, two Advanced Dressing Stations, nine Medical Aid Posts, 100-bed hospital and 26 oxygen booths; source reports 200,000 litres oxygen support. Engineers widen tracks, build/maintain crossings and clear landslides; EME repairs equipment and signals teams maintain communication.
- Live convoy tracking helps coordinate response to terror incidents, accidents and weather hazards. Preventive deployment must remain adaptable to terrain and emerging drone threats.
## Shrine and route recall
- Amarnath cave in J&K, source identifies Pahalgam/Anantnag region, **about 3,888 m** high; ice stalagmite revered as Shiva Lingam. Religious explanations of lunar waxing/waning should not be presented as an established physical law.
- Traditional **Pahalgam–Chandanwari–Sheshnag–Panchtarni** approach is longer; **Baltal–Domail** route is shorter, steep, approximately 14 km. Routes converge near the shrine. Do not confuse Amarnath cave with the distinct **Amarnath Peak** (source elevation ~5,186 m).
- High altitude, rain, landslides, snow and crowd pressure require medical screening, oxygen, warning/evacuation capacity and coordinated civilian support.

topics.title: Machilipatnam port: revival and coastal logistics
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Historical and geographical recall
- **Machilipatnam/Masulipatnam**, coastal Andhra Pradesh on the Bay of Bengal near the Krishna delta; source associates ancient **Masula** with early maritime trade. Avoid locating the town exactly at the present Krishna river mouth.
- Flourished as a textile and maritime trading centre, especially **16th–18th centuries**, with Arab/European commercial connections; colonial trade increasingly favoured Madras/Chennai. Historical names/trade claims should not imply uninterrupted modern port operation.
## July 2025 construction snapshot
- New greenfield harbour under construction near Machilipatnam; source reports **~48% complete**, ~1,250 workers in shifts and an **end-2026 operations target**. Target is not completion.
- Source engineering figures: **56 million m³ dredging**, **2.5-km breakwater**, ~**2.1 million tonnes rock**; dredging creates navigable depth and breakwater reduces wave exposure. The simplified “Manginapudi” site description should not replace detailed port-project boundaries.
- Potential Krishna/Guntur industrial/export support, coastal shipping and links toward Southeast Asia; warehousing, cold chains and road/rail connectivity determine real benefits. Port-led/Sagarmala and Blue Economy opportunities require environmental safeguards and commercial viability; decongestion of other ports is an expected benefit.

topics.title: Super-Earths: TOI-1846 b and HD 20794 d
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Classification and July 2025 discoveries
- **Super-Earth** denotes planets above Earth's mass/size and below Neptune's regime; it does **not** establish terrestrial composition, life or habitability. Rocky, volatile-rich and gas-envelope possibilities require observations; “mini-Neptune” is not interchangeable with every super-Earth.
- **TOI-1846 b**, TESS transit discovery around a nearby M dwarf, **~154 light-years**, radius **1.79 ±0.07 Earth radii**, period **~3.93 days**. **4.4 Earth masses is predicted from a mass–radius relation**, not a directly measured mass. Paper gives equilibrium temperature **589 ±20 K for zero Bond albedo**, rather than source's unqualified 568 K. [Discovery paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.18550).
- Host source parameters: ~0.42 solar masses, ~0.40 solar radii, ~3,568 K, estimated age ~7.2 billion years. Small stars favour transit detection, but red dwarfs are not universally quiet; flares and stellar activity matter.
- Possible volatile/water-rich interior or atmosphere remains a model, not confirmed liquid oceans. **HD 20794 d**, ~20 light-years away, reported mass scale ~6 Earth masses and an eccentric orbit affecting habitable-zone residence. A habitable zone allows possible surface liquid water under suitable atmospheric conditions; it is not evidence of inhabited or assured habitable conditions.

topics.title: Linguistic diversity and constitutional accommodation
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Constitutional framework
- “Linguistic secularism” is the editorial's argument for equal respect and pluralism, not a separately defined constitutional office or an absolute ban on official-language policies.
- India has **no constitutionally designated national language**. **Article 343** specifies Hindi in Devanagari as Union official language; English continues under law. **Article 345** enables States' official-language choices; **Eighth Schedule lists 22 scheduled languages**, not a declaration that all 22 are Union official languages.
- **Article 29(1)** protects any section of citizens with a distinct language/script/culture; **29(2)** bars specified admission discrimination in State-maintained/aided institutions. These clauses are not simply a general minority-only language provision. **Articles 25–28** concern religious freedom; religious and linguistic protections are related pluralist commitments with different texts.
## Census and public policy
- **Census 2011 language tabulation:** **121 languages**, including **22 scheduled and 99 non-scheduled**, and **270 mother-tongue groupings with 10,000+ speakers**; not all mother tongues spoken in India. About **96.71%** reported scheduled languages as mother tongue. [Census language paper](https://www.censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/42458/study-description).
- Hindi imposition disputes and hostility toward non-Marathi speakers illustrate the tension between identity preservation and chauvinism. Protect local languages through teaching, materials and cultural support alongside mobility, multilingual access and non-discrimination.
- Parties, schools and media should discourage intimidation and preserve federal choice. Source's unitary “Western secularism” history is oversimplified; Western constitutional models differ. Its 250-word/15-mark answer-writing prompt is coaching practice, not an authenticated PYQ.

topics.title: Black-hole mergers and GW231123
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Gravitational waves and detection
- A black hole has an **event horizon** beyond which light cannot escape. Massive-star collapse is one formation route; “cosmic vacuum cleaner” is a misleading analogy because distant orbital gravity follows the mass, not indiscriminate suction.
- Binary inspiral loses orbital energy through **gravitational waves**, accelerating toward merger and ringdown. These spacetime ripples were predicted by general relativity; **LIGO (US), Virgo (Italy), KAGRA (Japan)** form a detector network.
## GW231123
- Detected **23 November 2023 by the two LIGO observatories**, reported in July 2025. Inferred component masses roughly **137 and 103 solar masses**, with broad uncertainty and high inferred spins; do not treat them as exact measurements.
- Masses challenge simple stellar-collapse/pair-instability expectations; hierarchical mergers are one possible origin, not proven history. The event does not mean the theory of gravity failed. [LIGO discovery paper](https://dcc.ligo.org/LIGO-P2500026-v6/public).
- The remnant mass is below the sum because energy is radiated as gravitational waves. Signal inference requires waveform models and uncertainty assessment; detector operation at the time differs from the membership of the full collaboration.

topics.title: Exoplanet biosignatures and the value of null results
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Asking testable questions
- A search should distinguish **habitability**, life's actual presence and remotely **detectable biosignatures**. No detected sign is not proof life is absent; weak biospheres, abiotic look-alikes and limited instruments produce false negatives/positives.
- **Bayesian analysis** updates prior beliefs with observations and detection-model assumptions. Carefully selected, well-characterised null results constrain occurrence rates; unrepresentative samples or uncertain detection sensitivity weaken inference.
- ETH-led study: idealised **40/80 no-detection observations** could yield **99.9% upper limits of ~20%/~10%** for the observed occurrence parameter. These are conditional statistical bounds for similar sampled planets, not an actual survey proving how rare all life is. [Primary paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.06779).
- **LIFE—Large Interferometer for Exoplanets** and **HWO—Habitable Worlds Observatory** are proposed future observing concepts; improved spectra could assess water/atmospheric chemistry, with theory and contextual validation required. Detecting water, oxygen or methane alone does not establish biological origin or confirm extraterrestrial life.

topics.title: Hypersonic cruise missiles and scramjet development
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## July 2025: separate demonstrated technology from reported weapon specifications
- Hypersonic flight exceeds Mach 5. A scramjet uses atmospheric oxygen and maintains supersonic airflow through combustion; it differs from a ramjet and from an unpowered hypersonic glide vehicle. Sustained combustion, thermal protection, control and guidance are major challenges.
- Officially demonstrated: DRDL's actively cooled subscale scramjet combustor ran for over 1,000 seconds on **25 April 2025**, following January's 120-second ground test. This validates combustor/test-facility technology; it is not an operational missile deployment. [DRDO release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2124415&lang=2&reg=48).
- July PDF reports an **ET-LDHCM / Project Vishnu**, Mach 8, 1,500-km range, 1,000–2,000-kg payload, multiple launch platforms, 12 weapons, 2027–28 glide vehicles and 2030 deployment. These detailed specifications/timelines lack confirmation in the cited official test release; retain them as reported claims, not established capability. Speed/manoeuvrability can complicate interception but do not prove immunity to every defence system.

topics.title: PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Cabinet approval: 16 July 2025
- Six-year programme from **2025–26**, covering **100 districts** selected for low productivity, low cropping intensity and low credit disbursement; states' shares reflect net cropped area and operational holdings, with at least one district per state.
- Converges **36 existing schemes across 11 departments**, state schemes and local private partnerships. Convergence does not itself mean repeal or legal abolition of PM-KISAN/PMFBY. Budget announcement envisaged about **1.7 crore farmers**; July briefing reported **₹24,000 crore annually**, not wholly new expenditure additional to every converged scheme.
- Raise productivity, diversify crops/sustainable practices, improve irrigation, panchayat/block storage and short-/long-term credit. Inspired by Aspirational Districts Programme.
- District Agriculture and Allied Activities Plans, prepared by district samitis including progressive farmers; district/state/national committees, NITI guidance and central nodal officers. **117 indicators**, monthly dashboard monitoring. [Cabinet decision](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2145146&lang=2&reg=3).

## Delivery and public-investment assessment
- Convergence must complement adequate public spending, irrigation/research/storage investment and locally tailored district plans. A common umbrella can reduce duplication but may obscure declining resources or create uniform targets unsuited to local agro-climatic conditions.
- Include states, Panchayats, primary agricultural cooperatives, universities, FPOs and farmers; assess private partnerships against food security, transparency and smallholder benefits.
- PDF gives agriculture allocation shares declining **3.53% (2021–22) → 3.14% → 2.57% → 2.54% → 2.51% (2025–26)**; denominator is insufficiently explained and “Central Plan outlay” is dated terminology. Do not equate an allocation share with measured real public investment or spending delivered.
- Source's October/Rabi launch date is a July implementation expectation; six-year approval begins FY2025–26. Coaching questions are practice, not past UPSC questions.

topics.title: Star formation, stellar evolution and variable stars
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## July 2025 protostar finding
- IIST-led researchers reported first radio-continuum **circular polarisation** toward massive protostar **IRAS 18162−2048**, using the **Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array at 4–6 GHz**. It probes magnetic/particle processes near the forming star; proposed mechanisms include gyrosynchrotron emission and Faraday conversion. Do not present the PDF's “100 times Earth's field” as a uniquely established direct measurement. [Research preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.04913).
## Revision chain
- Gas/dust nebula → gravitational collapse → accreting protostar → stable core hydrogen fusion on main sequence. **T Tauri** describes young low-mass stars; it is not a compulsory stage for every massive star.
- Sun-like stars: red giant → shed outer layers/planetary nebula → white dwarf. Massive stars: advanced burning, core collapse/supernova → neutron star or black hole, depending on remnant properties. A simple single birth-mass cut-off does not capture every outcome.
- Pulsars are rotating neutron stars observed through pulsed emission; magnetars have exceptionally strong magnetic fields. Black-hole accretion can emit observable radiation outside the horizon.
- Intrinsic variability reflects stellar processes; extrinsic variability includes eclipsing binaries. **Cepheids are pulsating variable stars; nebulae are gas/dust clouds**. In the supplied **2023 PYQ**, only pair 3 (pulsars—neutron stars) is correct: **(a)**. The ordinary Sun being eclipsed does not make every solar-eclipse event a separate stellar-evolution stage.

topics.title: Akash Prime and high-altitude air defence
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Ladakh trial: 16 July 2025
- Upgraded **Akash Prime** destroyed two high-speed unmanned aerial targets in Ladakh during First of Production Model firing trials. Customised for altitudes above **4,500 m**, with an **indigenous radio-frequency seeker**; Army Air Defence/DRDO, BDL, BEL and industry participated. Trial success enables induction; it is not proof all planned regiments were already inducted. [Defence release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2145517&lang=2&reg=48).
- Akash is an indigenous mobile surface-to-air weapon family; ground radar/command guidance of original Akash must not obscure Prime's seeker upgrade. Rajendra multifunction radar, electronic counter-countermeasures, mobility and integration support air defence.
- Source original-system figures about **25-km range, 18-km altitude, Mach 2.5–3.5 and 60-kg warhead** are configuration-dependent. Do not treat advertised hit percentages as battlefield guarantees or endorse the PDF's unsupported nuclear-warhead claim.
- Separate source news: **Prithvi-II and Agni-I** ballistic-missile user trials under Strategic Forces Command at Chandipur; these are not Akash interceptors.

- **Cold-weather adaptation** improves high-altitude operation; July 20 source range **about 25–30 km** is an indicative configuration figure, not a universal range for every Akash-family variant.

topics.title: Political leadership: age, accountability and renewal
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## July 2025 debate
- A proposal for political retirement at 75 reopened questions of generational representation, fitness and party succession. **India has no constitutional upper age limit for MPs/MLAs or a general two-term PM/CM limit**; a party convention is not a legal disqualification.
- **Articles 84(b)/173(b)**: minimum 25 for Lok Sabha/Legislative Assembly; 30 for Rajya Sabha/Legislative Council. Article 326 concerns adult suffrage, not by itself every qualification to stand for election. Assess any proposed cap against the full constitutional/legal framework, rather than assert automatic invalidity under Article 326.
- For a cap: renewal, opportunities for younger members, planned succession and concerns about capability. Against: voters' choice, experience, age discrimination and wide variation in fitness. Chronological age alone does not establish incapacity.
- Alternatives: transparent candidate selection/internal party democracy, mentoring, meaningful performance scrutiny and proportionate health transparency balanced with privacy. Fixed term limits, lower contesting age and compulsory health certification are reform proposals, not enacted rules.
- PDF's Biden-as-current-President/Trump-as-future-contender examples are stale in July 2025; exclude speculative diagnoses of named leaders.

topics.title: Swachh Survekshan 2024–25 and urban sanitation
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Awards presented 17 July 2025
- MoHUA survey under Swachh Bharat Mission–Urban promotes sanitation, waste management and competitive improvement. **78 awards**, including **23 Super Swachh League cities across all population categories**; 23 is not the number in the million-plus category alone.
- Separate league recognises sustained performance. Source eligibility: top-three position at least once in preceding three years plus top 20% of current population category. Assessment uses **10 parameters/54 indicators**; five population bands: under 20,000; 20,000–50,000; 50,000–3 lakh; 3–10 lakh; above 10 lakh.
- Swachh Shehar top three: **above 10 lakh—Ahmedabad, Bhopal, Lucknow**; **3–10 lakh—Mira-Bhayandar, Bilaspur (Chhattisgarh), Jamshedpur**. The source wrongly places Bilaspur in Madhya Pradesh.
- Source graphic also shows **50,000–3 lakh: Dewas, Karhad, Karnal; 20,000–50,000: Panaji, Aska, Kumhari; under 20,000: Bilha, Chikiti, Shahganj**.
- League examples: Indore, Surat, Navi Mumbai, Vijayawada; Noida, Chandigarh, Mysuru; New Delhi. Best Ganga town **Prayagraj**, best cantonment **Secunderabad**. Awards also recognise SafaiMitra safety and promising state/UT cities; rankings complement, not replace, sustained service delivery and worker safety. [MoHUA announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2145461&lang=2&reg=48).

## Additional award recall
- **34 Promising Swachh Shehars** recognised improvement; **Visakhapatnam, Jabalpur and Gorakhpur** received SafaiMitra safety recognition. Special Mahakumbh waste-management recognition went to Uttar Pradesh government, Prayagraj Mela administration and municipal corporation; source footfall **66 crore** is event-reported attendance, not unique persons.
- July 20's ordinal **Indore 1st/Surat 2nd/Navi Mumbai 3rd/Vijayawada 4th** is the award-list sequence of million-plus Super Swachh League cities, not an overall national ranking across all categories. Distinguish that league from **Ahmedabad/Bhopal/Lucknow**, ranked in the million-plus Swachh Shehar category. [Official award categories](https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/jul/doc2025717588801.pdf).

topics.title: UN Security Council ISIL/Al-Qaida sanctions regime
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Regime and national-list distinction
- Security Council's **1267 regime began in 1999**; later **1989 (2011)** and **2253 (2015)** resolutions underpin the ISIL (Da’esh)/Al-Qaida regime. Committee comprises all **15 Council members** and oversees listing/delisting and implementation.
- Listed individuals/entities face **asset freeze, travel ban and arms embargo**, subject to applicable exemptions. Committee decisions follow its procedures, generally consensus; individual states implement obligations.
- July clipping concerns **US designation of The Resistance Front**: a US national designation is not automatic inclusion on the UN list. Do not treat every terrorist organisation as already listed under this particular regime. [UN committee](https://main.un.org/securitycouncil/en/sanctions/1267).

## July 31 clipping: TRF distinction
- Issue discusses inclusion of **The Resistance Front** in a UN monitoring-team report and the separate US terrorist designation. A monitoring report's mention is **not automatic 1267 listing**, and US national designation is not a UN committee decision. The repeated composition/sanctions material is already covered.

topics.title: Nord Stream pipelines and European energy security
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Baltic Sea route and chronology
- Nord Stream connects Russia directly to Germany under the **Baltic Sea**, bypassing transit routes through Ukraine. Nord Stream 1: **Portovaya near Vyborg → Lubmin**, about **1,224 km**, first line operational November **2011**, second in 2012.
- Nord Stream 2: **Ust-Luga → German Baltic coast**, designed **55 bcm/year**, construction completed **September 2021**, not the source's 2019. Completion did not establish commercial operation. [Developer chronology](https://www.gazprom.com/projects/nord-stream2/).
- Direct pipelines reduce transit dependence but concentrate supplier/infrastructure risks. Diversification, storage, LNG and demand measures influence energy security; source's language of uninterrupted present supply ignores subsequent disruptions. The map marks September 2022 leak areas near **Bornholm**, not active new July 2025 leaks.
- Source reserve/budget charts lack common year/definitions; do not use their 40% oil/gas budget claim as a timeless figure.

topics.title: Trade Connect ePlatform and MSME export access
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Platform and July 2025 outreach
- **DGFT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry**, provides a one-stop trade-information/service portal for exporters and MSMEs, linking Indian Missions, Export Promotion Councils, Commodity Boards and government agencies.
- July outreach at the **71st India International Garment Fair** and **16th Toy Biz International B 2 B Expo** aimed to improve adoption. The source describes collaboration with MSME Ministry, EXIM Bank, DFS and MEA.
- Tools cover tariffs, certification, FTAs, buyers, trade events and eCommerce; multilingual interactive courses explain export procedures. Electronic preferential/non-preferential **Certificates of Origin** can be issued/validated through authorised agencies.
- Lower information/intermediary costs and better overseas coordination can widen MSME participation; adoption still depends on digital access and usable support. [DGFT July 17 announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2145471&lang=2&reg=48).
## MSME graphic
- Revised investment/turnover ceilings (₹ crore): **micro 2.5/10; small 25/100; medium 125/500**, against earlier **1/5; 10/50; 50/250**. Both criteria matter; these are classification limits, not grants.
- Image flags credit gaps, delayed payments, low digital access and compliance burdens; links include Udyam, ECLGS, RAMP, ODOP and TReDS. Its undated GDP/export/employment/₹20-lakh-crore credit-gap figures should not be treated as a harmonised July 2025 statistical series.
- Revised classification took effect **1 April 2025**; [official MSME comparison table](https://www.msmedikarnal.gov.in/pdf/msme_defination.pdf).

topics.title: Hydrogen peroxide: oxidising agent and applications
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Chemistry and uses
- **H₂O₂**; commonly encountered as a colourless aqueous liquid. Trace vapour occurs naturally; unstable decomposition releases heat: **2 H₂O₂ → 2 H₂O + O₂**.
- **Nonflammable but a strong oxidiser**: contact with organic material can intensify fire or cause spontaneous combustion. Decomposition to water/oxygen does not make concentrated peroxide harmless.
- Dilute household formulations (source **3–9%**) have medicinal/bleaching uses; higher concentrations serve textile/paper bleaching, chemical manufacture and rocket propulsion. Other oxidising applications include sterilisation, wastewater treatment and chemical synthesis. The clipping concerns alleged milk adulteration, not an approved food-preservation use. [ATSDR chemistry/use account](https://wwwn.cdc.gov/TSP/substances/ToxSubstance.aspx?toxid=55).
- The advertising inset's general wound-healing/safe-daily-use claims should not be memorised as medical advice; toxicity depends on concentration and exposure.

topics.title: Reykjanes Peninsula: rifting, eruptions and geothermal activity
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## July 2025 eruption and setting
- Southwest **Iceland**, where the **Mid-Atlantic Ridge** emerges on land and the **North American/Eurasian plates diverge**; fissures, lava fields, craters, earthquakes and geothermal activity illustrate constructive plate margins.
- Eruption began **16 July 2025** at the Sundhnúkur crater row: ninth in that local series since December 2023. Do not confuse this with the total for all Reykjanes eruptions since renewed activity in 2021. [Icelandic Meteorological Office](https://en.vedur.is/about-imo/news/a-magma-instrusion-has-started-on-sundhnuksgigarod-crater-row?gsid=d4201c00-d860-4cdd-9a3c-02a31dcdc835).
- **Reykjanes UNESCO Global Geopark**, designated 2015, lies near Reykjavík; the source's claim that Reykjavík is a major settlement inside the geopark/peninsula should not be used as a precise boundary fact. The source's **829 km²** peninsula figure differs from UNESCO's **818 km² geopark** boundary. [UNESCO](https://www.unesco.org/en/iggp/reykjanes-unesco-global-geopark).
- **Gunnuhver** is a geothermal area with hot springs/steam vents. The inset oceanic-subduction cross-section illustrates a different plate setting; it does not explain Iceland's divergent ridge.

topics.title: Chronic venous insufficiency
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mechanism and effects
- Inadequate venous return from legs to heart: weakened vein walls/damaged one-way valves allow backward flow and **blood pooling**, especially while standing.
- Symptoms include aching/heavy legs, swelling, cramps, varicose veins and skin discolouration; advanced disease can cause leg ulcers.
- Risks include ageing, obesity, pregnancy, family history and previous deep-vein thrombosis; prolonged sitting/standing also matters. The source's **1-in-20 adults** prevalence lacks a specified population/date.
- Management may involve exercise, leg elevation, weight management, compression and clinician-directed medicines/procedures; severe disease may need vein ablation/removal or other intervention. These are revision categories, not a prescription for unexplained swelling. [MedlinePlus](https://www.medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000203.htm).

topics.title: Poshan Tracker and Anganwadi nutrition monitoring
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Digital service delivery
- **Women and Child Development Ministry**, with **National e-Governance Division (NeGD)**; rolled out **1 March 2021** as a mobile governance tool for Anganwadi nutrition services.
- Records beneficiary attendance, supplementary nutrition, growth/health parameters and service delivery; dashboards aid tracking of children, pregnant women and lactating mothers, resources and gaps.
