Official platform access is role-based; a tracking entry is not itself proof a nutritional outcome improved.
- July source reports **technical glitches and weak internet** impeding frontline workers' real-time updates. Priorities: reliable devices/connectivity, usable workflows, training, data quality and privacy, with service continuity during failures.
- **POSHAN Abhiyaan**, launched **8 March 2018**, combines departmental convergence, technology and community participation. Objectives: reduce stunting/underweight among children 0–6, anaemia among children 6–59 months and women 15–49, and low birth weight; adolescent girls, pregnant/lactating women and young children are key groups. [MoWCD account](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1776877&lang=2&reg=48); [MoWCD rollout bulletin](https://www.nipccd.nic.in/uploads/pdf/e-BulletinPoshanSep2022pdf-026613228c26ed82aaf5d7739ee96c3a.pdf).

topics.title: Brahmaputra hydropower and India–China river cooperation
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## July 2025 project
- China announced construction commencement **19 July 2025** for the lower **Yarlung Zangbo/Tsangpo** project in **Nyingchi, Tibet**; Mainling was the groundbreaking location. It comprises **five cascade stations**, investment about **1.2 trillion yuan (source US$167.8 bn)**; source projected annual generation **300 billion kWh** is a future estimate, not operating output. [Chinese government announcement](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202507/19/content_WS687b6a8ac6d0868f4e8f4486.html).
- The river bends around the eastern Himalaya before entering Arunachal Pradesh as Siang and forming the Brahmaputra in Assam; it continues to Bangladesh. Upstream/downstream location matters for India and Bangladesh.
## Risk assessment and cooperation
- Potential concerns: altered seasonal releases, sediment trapping and floodplain fertility, aquatic/wetland ecology, livelihoods and water security; seismicity/landslides create infrastructure risk. A possible sudden-release/failure hazard is not proof deliberate water weaponisation has occurred.
- Assess actual design/storage, rainfall and tributary contributions, cumulative impacts and transparent operating rules; the source's unsupported label **world's largest infrastructure project** is broader than a hydropower comparison.
- **Expert Level Mechanism (2006)** supports dialogue; India–China have hydrological-data arrangements, **not a comprehensive water-sharing treaty**. Source wrongly implies regular data continued: later official reply confirms Brahmaputra data suspended from **June 2023**, Sutlej data not received since **2022**. [Parliamentary clarification](https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/268/AU3287_qYFiZe.pdf?source=pqars).
- India's priorities: resume data/early warnings, obtain design and environmental information, diplomatic engagement and basin cooperation. Dibang/Upper Siang projects feature in debate, but **Dibang is on a tributary** and the Upper Siang proposal should not be described as an already completed counter-dam. Domestic hydropower also requires ecological/community safeguards.

topics.title: AI governance: inclusion, safety and India’s global role
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## July 2025 editorial proposals
- With India then preparing to host the **AI Impact Summit in February 2026**, the editorial proposes using DPI experience (Aadhaar/UPI/CoWIN), technical skills and Global South diplomacy to promote human-centred AI. These are source-era proposals, not agreed summit outcomes.
- **Accountability:** public, measurable pledges by governments/companies/universities, tracked for a year; examples include greener computing, wider training and local-language public services.
- **Inclusion:** proposed **AI for Billions Fund** for cloud credits, fellowships and local-language datasets; development-bank/Gulf support and an underserved-language model challenge are suggestions.
- **Safety:** proposed collaborative sharing of red-team tests, incident logs and model stress tests, plus open tools to assess bias/fairness.
- **Regulation:** proposed voluntary frontier-model code building on Seoul commitments, with timely safety disclosures (editorial suggests 90 days), compute transparency and an accident-reporting channel.
- **Cooperation:** connect existing institutions, broaden developing-country participation and avoid rival blocs fragmenting standards. Balance innovation with safeguards; simplistic US/EU/China labels do not capture every law or policy.
- MyGov consultation is presented as participatory preparation; it does not establish that no previous host consulted its public. The printed mains question is coaching practice, not a UPSC PYQ.

topics.title: EU age verification and children’s online safety
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## July 2025 blueprint
- European Commission released an **open-source age-verification blueprint on 14 July 2025**, supporting child protection under the **Digital Services Act, Article 28**. Pilot states: **Denmark, France, Greece, Italy and Spain**.
- Issuer checks age using identity evidence; website receives only **over-18 proof**, not name/date of birth. Separate issuance/presentation and single-use proofs aim to prevent cross-service tracking.
- Built for compatibility with forthcoming **European Digital Identity Wallets** (then expected by end 2026). **Zero-knowledge-proof integration was ongoing**, not an already completed feature of the initial July version. [Commission's dated release](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/commission-makes-available-age-verification-blueprint).
- Debate: child safety versus data minimisation/security, usability, tracking and displacement towards unregulated sites. Industry's proposed device/OS-level checks are an alternative policy position, not an adopted EU rule. Source French under-15 social-media restriction is a political proposal, not proof of a uniform EU ban.
- Distinguish age verification (threshold proof) from age estimation, and assess effective privacy guarantees across issuer, device and platform.

topics.title: National Disaster Response Force and specialised search capability
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Institutional role
- **NDRF force**, constituted under **Disaster Management Act 2005, section 44**, raised 2006 with 8 battalions; source-era strength 16. Under **Ministry of Home Affairs**, headed by a Director General, with personnel drawn from BSF/CRPF/CISF/ITBP/SSB/Assam Rifles. [NDRF](https://www.ndrf.gov.in/en/about-us).
- Specialised multi-skilled response to natural/man-made disasters; pre-positioning reduces response time. International deployments include Japan 2011 and Nepal 2015. Do not confuse the force with the similarly abbreviated disaster-response **fund**.
## July 2025 cadaver-dog training
- Source reports first batch of about **six Belgian Malinois/Labrador dogs** trained at **Arakkonam (Tamil Nadu) and Ghaziabad (UP)** to locate human remains using specialised decompositional scent training.
- Cadaver detection complements live-victim search; finding remains supports identification and families' closure. It does not replace rapid rescue during the crucial early response period.

topics.title: International Moon Day and peaceful lunar exploration
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Observance and meaning
- **20 July** marks the **Apollo 11 lunar landing in 1969**; UN recognised International Moon Day in 2021 following COPUOS recommendation. Focus: international lunar exploration, peaceful cooperation, sustainability and responsible use of resources.
- Landing date is 20 July; Armstrong's first step was **21 July 1969,02:56 UTC**. These refer to different events/time references, not competing dates for one identical event.
- Outreach/sky-watching/education can encourage participation. The source's criticism about privileging an American achievement is a viewpoint; modern lunar activity is multinational.
- [UN observance](https://www.un.org/en/observances/moon-day); [NASA event times](https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/static/history/ap11ann/ap11events.html).

topics.title: Indonesia peatland fires and transboundary haze
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Image-only place in news
- Caption depicts firefighters on peatland in **Riau province, Indonesia,20 July 2025**.
- Peat fires can smoulder slowly/deeply and be difficult to extinguish; smoke/haze can travel towards **Malaysia and Singapore**, creating transboundary air-quality concerns. The caption describes a hazard pathway, not a measured air-quality episode for every neighbouring country.

topics.title: Vice-President of India: election, functions and vacancy
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Constitutional office
- **Article 63** establishes the office; **64** makes the Vice-President ex-officio Rajya Sabha Chairman; **65** provides presidential substitution. The source clipping reports **Jagdeep Dhankhar's resignation on 21 July 2025**, addressed to the President.
- Chairman maintains order, administers committee arrangements under rules and has **only a casting vote**. While acting as President, does not perform Chairman's duties; Deputy Chairman/other authorised presiding officer handles the House.
## Election and eligibility
- **Article 66:** electoral college comprises **all members of both Houses, elected and nominated**; excludes state MLAs. Proportional representation by **single transferable vote, secret ballot**; Supreme Court finally decides election disputes under **Article 71**.
- Indian citizen, **35+**, qualified for Rajya Sabha membership; office-of-profit disqualification has constitutional exceptions. Cannot simultaneously retain a parliamentary/state-legislative seat or another office of profit.
- **Article 69 oath** administered by President/authorised person: allegiance to Constitution and faithful discharge.
## Term, resignation and removal
- **Article 67:** five years, eligible for re-election and ordinarily continues until successor enters office; may resign to President.
- Removal: **Rajya Sabha majority of all then members (effective majority)** plus Lok Sabha agreement (ordinary majority), with **14 days' notice**. No presidential-style impeachment; the summary's generic special-majority label is misleading.
- **Article 68:** ordinary election before term expiry; casual-vacancy election as soon as possible, successor receives full five-year term from entry. **Article 70** covers presidential contingencies beyond the standard arrangements.
- When President's office becomes vacant, presidential election must take place within **six months**; temporary inability is a different Article 65 contingency.
- [Official former Vice-Presidents record](https://vicepresidentofindia.nic.in/former-vice-presidents/) confirms Dhankhar’s tenure ended 21 July 2025.

## July 24: election preparations
- Following the resignation, ECI began preparing the electoral-college list, appointing Returning/Assistant Returning Officers and background materials; schedule was still to be announced in this issue.
- **Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act 1952 and Rules 1974** govern conduct under ECI's Article324 authority. By convention a Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha Secretary-General serves as RO by rotation, assisted by Parliament Secretariat officers.
- Nomination requires **at least 20 proposers and 20 seconders** from the electoral college. Party whip does not govern the secret-ballot election. [ECI election resources](https://www.eci.gov.in/vice-presidential-election-2025).

topics.title: FIDE and international chess
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Organisation
- **Fédération Internationale des Échecs (FIDE)**, international chess governing body; founded **1924, Paris**, headquarters **Lausanne, Switzerland**; motto **Gens Una Sumus (We are one family)**.
- Standardises rules, rankings/titles and organises the World Championship cycle, Olympiad, World Cup/Candidates; recognised by IOC in 1999. Source 199 national federations is a dated membership count, not a permanent total.
## July 2025 Indian hosting announcement
- FIDE announced India as **2025 World Cup host** on 21 July; then scheduled **30 October–27 November**, with **206 players**, knockout format and qualification places for 2026 Candidates. Host-city selection was still pending in this source; do not import later Goa confirmation into the July announcement. [FIDE July 21 release](https://www.fide.com/fide-world-cup-2025-to-be-hosted-in-india/).
- AICF is India's national federation; players including Anand, Praggnanandhaa and Gukesh illustrate India's competitive growth.
- [FIDE institutional profile](https://worldchesschampionship2023.fide.com/about-fide) supports the organisation, headquarters, motto and source-era membership details.

## Divya Deshmukh: 28 July 2025 milestone
- **19-year-old Divya Deshmukh, Nagpur**, defeated **Koneru Humpy** in rapid tiebreaks at **Batumi, Georgia**, becoming the **first Indian winner of the FIDE Women's World Cup**, India's **88th Grandmaster** and fourth Indian woman GM after Humpy, D. Harika and R. Vaishali. Both finalists qualified for the Women's Candidates. [FIDE final report](https://www.fide.com/divya-deshmukh-becomes-third-womens-world-cup-champion-defeats-humpy-koneru-in-tiebreak/).
- Her **World Junior Girls title was 2024**, not the PDF's 2023; its table also incorrectly dates the Women's World Cup win to 2024. She contributed to India's **2024 Budapest Olympiad women's team gold**. [FIDE profile](https://womengrandprix.fide.com/profile/2024/divyadeshmukh).
## Chess revision
- **Chaturanga** developed in India around the sixth century: infantry, cavalry, elephants and chariots; transmission through Persia/Shatranj preceded European modern rules in the fifteenth–sixteenth centuries.
- **Checkmate:** king attacked with no legal escape; **stalemate:** no legal move while king is not in check, hence draw. Elo measures competitive performance; GM and IM are FIDE titles, distinct from World Champion.
- **Anand:** first Indian GM (1988), five-time World Champion; World Cup winner in 2000/2002 (older tournament format). **Praggnanandhaa:** 2023 World Cup finalist. **Gukesh:** youngest undisputed world champion, defeating Ding Liren in Singapore in 2024; he did not take the title directly from Carlsen.
- India hosted the **44th Olympiad, Chennai 2022** and won **both open and women's team gold in 2024**. PDF's 'open bronze in 2020' is wrong: India shared online Olympiad gold in 2020; open bronze came in 2014/2022. Keep online and over-the-board events distinct.

topics.title: Right to vote and universal adult suffrage
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Constitutional foundation and legislation
- **Article 326** provides adult suffrage for Lok Sabha/Assembly elections: citizens **18+**, subject to lawful disqualifications; **Article 325** prohibits exclusion from a general electoral roll solely on religion, race, caste or sex. Representation of the People Act 1950 regulates registration; **1951 Act, section 62** governs voting subject to its conditions/disqualifications.
- Distinguish **entitlement to vote**, traditionally characterised as statutory in *N.P.Ponnuswami (1952), Jyoti Basu(1982), Kuldip Nayar(2006)*, from **freedom of voting/expression**, protected by Article 19(1)(a). Constitutional origin does not mean every detail is a fundamental right or immune from statutory conditions.
- *PUCL(2003)* and *Raj Bala(2015)* discuss constitutional foundations. In *Anoop Baranwal(2023)*, Justice **Ajay Rastogi wrote a separate concurring opinion**, arguing for fundamental-right protection in direct elections by reading Article 326 with Articles 15,17,19,21. The PDF wrongly calls it a dissent and reduces it to a mere request for future consideration; do not attribute his separate reasoning to the whole Bench. [Reported judgment, especially pp 199–205](https://patnahighcourt.gov.in/ILR/viewpdf.aspx?ID=NjYx-dRYRy6tBACQ%3D&T=EN).
## Universal adult suffrage
- Inclusive political voice irrespective of property, education, caste, gender or religion; India adopted adult franchise from the Republic's beginning rather than a property-based gradual extension. The original age was 21, reduced to 18 by the 61st Amendment; do not project 18 backwards to 1950.
- **New Zealand 1893** is the landmark national women's-franchise example. Voting and eligibility to stand are distinct rights.
- Democratic benefits: participation, accountability, empowerment of marginalised groups and a more representative party system. Obstacles include migrant/disability access, unequal civic awareness, misinformation, vote buying and exclusionary registration practices.
- Bihar electoral-roll debate illustrates why classification and due process matter. Statutory rights remain constrained by constitutional equality/non-arbitrariness; they are not freely removable without review. Printed 250 word/15 mark question is coaching practice.

topics.title: Global Capability Centres and India–UK services cooperation
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## GCC model
- **Global Capability Centres**, also called captive/global in-house centres, are MNC units abroad handling IT, BPM, R&D, AI, analytics, cybersecurity, finance, tax/legal and other core functions. Their role increasingly includes innovation/centres of excellence, beyond cost-saving back-office work.
- India's talent, English skills, lower costs, IT/startup ecosystem and established clusters (Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Gurugram, Chennai, Noida) support growth. Source **1,500+ centres/1.9 million employees** are dated, unharmonised industry estimates, not a fresh national census.
## July 2025 FTA editorial
- The editorial argues India–UK trade cooperation can support a knowledge corridor through investment, professional mobility, clear data/cybersecurity standards, IP protection and resolution of tax/regulatory uncertainty. These are potential benefits/negotiating priorities, **not proof each is a binding FTA obligation**.
- Source's final-negotiation description should be dated: negotiations had been concluded inMay 2025, while signature was still forthcoming inJuly.
- Budget 2025 proposed a national framework guiding states to promote GCCs in emerging tier 2 cities; the source discusses MeitY expert consultation and state incentives/conclaves. Proposed national support differs from an already enacted uniform GCC law.
- Policy trade-offs: state competition versus national coordination; infrastructure/talent diversity; cross-border mobility, double taxation, data localisation and legal predictability. Measure value addition, skills and innovation, not simply number of foreign-owned offices.
- [Official 6 May conclusion announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2127321&lang=2&reg=48) distinguishes conclusion of negotiations from signature/entry into force.

topics.title: AK-203 rifle and Indo-Russian small-arms production
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## AK-203 and localisation
- **7.62×39 mm Kalashnikov-family assault rifle**, intended to replace INSAS rifles using 5.56×45 mm ammunition; gas-operated rotating-bolt action, automatic/semi-automatic fire and 30-round magazine. Source approximate weight **3.8 kg without magazine**, cyclic rate **700 rounds/minute**; its **400–800 m** range figure depends on target/sighting conditions, not guaranteed precision at 800 m.
- Made at **Korwa, Amethi, Uttar Pradesh**, by **Indo-Russian Rifles Private Limited (IRRPL)**, incorporated in 2019. Indian partners are **AWEIL 42.5% and Munitions India 8%**; Russian partners **Kalashnikov 42%, Rosoboronexport 7.5%**. OFB was corporatised into several companies; it did not simply become AWEIL alone. [Defence Production company profile](https://www.ddpmod.gov.in/sites/default/files/9c3f5b880209268b9f396531b32801dd9bd35cc3f66f48932b502c43112d919e/96af4231d657538353efbf754977f9048b1dca9bd0211e9919edd14d2d2f1ed2.pdf).
- July source reports a **~₹5,200-crore, over-six-lakh rifle programme**, **48,000 completed** and delivery target **December 2030**; these are the issue's dated progress/forecast, not all rifles delivered.
- Reliability in difficult terrain, modern optics/accessories and local production support readiness, technology absorption, jobs/MSMEs and reduced import dependence. Calibre alone does not establish battlefield effectiveness; training, maintenance, accuracy and logistics matter.

topics.title: Alternative Indian constitutional drafts, 1895–1948
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Competing visions before the 1950 Constitution
| Draft | Revision focus |
|---|---|
| **Constitution of India Bill, 1895** | Early nationalist self-government draft, often associated with Tilak but anonymous authorship; 110 provisions, civil liberties, property and legal equality |
| **M. N. Roy, Constitution of Free India, 1944** | Radical-democratic vision: linguistic federal units, civil/economic rights, citizens’ committees and popular sovereignty, including resistance to tyranny |
| **Hindusthan Free State, 1944** | Mahasabha-associated draft; popular sovereignty, legal equality, religious freedom/no State religion, elected institutions and judicial remedies |
| **Shriman Narayan Agarwal, Gandhian Constitution, 1946** | Village-centred decentralisation, khadi/cottage industry, nonviolence and self-sufficiency; Gandhi wrote the foreword, not the draft |
| **Socialist Party draft, 1948** | Democratic socialism, planned economy, public/cooperative ownership, workers’ welfare and social equality; Jayaprakash Narayan wrote the foreword |
- **Corrections from the original texts:** the 1944 Hindusthan draft explicitly establishes a **federation** and a **bicameral Congress**, contrary to the PDF's “unitary” shorthand. It protects religious/cultural rights; do not reduce it to “one culture” or assert a secession right without the actual provision. [1944 draft](https://www.constitutionofindia.net/historical-constitution/the-constitution-of-the-hindusthan-free-state-act-1944-no-of-1944/).
- The Socialist draft permits a **controlled private sector** alongside state/cooperative sectors; the PDF's “no private ownership of means of production” overstates it. It includes political/civil rights as well as economic aims. [1948 draft](https://www.constitutionofindia.net/historical-constitution/draft-constitution-of-the-republic-of-india-socialist-party-1948/).
- Gandhian draft included a regulated **right to keep/bear arms**, an interesting tension with nonviolence; this was not adopted as a Fundamental Right in 1950. [1946 text](https://www.constitutionofindia.net/historical-constitution/gandhian-constitution-for-free-india-shriman-narayan-agarwal-1946/).
- Compare individual liberty, social/economic equality, centralisation and village participation. Similarities with Fundamental Rights/DPSPs/Panchayati Raj show a wider intellectual context; similarity alone does not prove direct borrowing from every draft.

topics.title: Remote work: flexibility, care and workplace organisation
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Global Survey of Working Arrangements, 2024–25
- Survey covered **16,422 full-time college-educated workers in 40 countries**, November 2024–February 2025; it is not representative of every worker or manual occupation. Average actual WFH **1.27 days/week**, compared with **1.6 in 2022 and 1.33 in 2023**; researchers describe broad stabilisation since 2023 rather than continuing global collapse. [Stanford research summary](https://siepr.stanford.edu/publications/essay/working-home-2025-five-key-facts).
- Source reports desired WFH about **2.6 days/week**; women with children desired **2.66**, versus **2.53** without children. Desire and actual availability differ; family/care needs shape preferences, while fathers and childless men also value flexibility. Do not infer all mothers prefer home working for one reason.
- North American/European adoption generally exceeds Asia; office-presence norms, role suitability, broadband, crowded housing and management practices can influence access. The PDF's regional averages are illustrative, not uniform rates for every named country.
## Mains: make flexibility inclusive
- Benefits: less commuting, autonomy, wider talent access and potential work–care compatibility. Risks: unequal unpaid-care burdens, isolation/digital fatigue, poor ergonomics, blurred hours and collaboration/supervision problems; outcomes depend on job and design.
- Use planned hybrid schedules, output-based assessment, good collaboration tools, ergonomic support, breaks and boundaries; improve broadband and care infrastructure. Hybrid working is a policy option, not automatically best for every occupation. Share domestic responsibilities so flexibility does not entrench gender inequality.

topics.title: Non-animal biological models and research ethics
topics.subject: Ethics
topics.markdown:
## Ethical and scientific case
- Editorial urges replacement of avoidable live-animal experiments with **human-relevant biological models**: cultured tissues/organoids, engineered skin/muscle/cartilage, organ-on-chip systems, 3D models and computational methods.
- Animals can suffer; human welfare and scientific validity must be balanced with compassion and minimisation of harm. Species differences can limit prediction, but this does not prove every animal experiment is scientifically useless or every alternative already replaces a whole organism.
- **Replacement, reduction and refinement (3Rs)** provide the practical frame: use validated alternatives where suitable, minimise animal numbers and suffering when still necessary, and scrutinise study design.
- Proposed amendment to **Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act 1960** would encourage alternatives; it is the author's reform recommendation, not a newly enacted clause. Tissue engineering/regenerative medicine offers experimental models, not proof all listed full organs are routinely manufactured for testing.
- Ethical action: fund validation and shared facilities, train researchers, integrate alternatives in education, transparent review and welfare oversight; change scientific incentives as well as legal language.

topics.title: HOPS-315 and the earliest planet-forming solids
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## July 2025 observation
- **HOPS-315**, a young protostar in **Orion**, roughly **1,300 light-years** away: **JWST infrared spectroscopy** and **ALMA millimetre observations in Chile** identified **silicon monoxide gas and crystalline silicates** in the inner protoplanetary disc.
- Hot dust vaporises; cooling gas condenses into refractory crystalline grains, potential building blocks that can aggregate into planetesimals and planets. Similar mineral records survive in ancient Solar-System meteorites.
- Crucially the signals originate **in the disc atmosphere, within about 2.2 AU**, distinct from the outward jet; ALMA helped locate the source. This is evidence of an early condensation stage, not observation of completed Earth-like planets. [ESO discovery release](https://www.eso.org/public/news/eso2512/).
- Source lists forsterite, enstatite/silica and approximate **1,300 K hot /470 K cooler components**; these should not be read as one universal crystallisation temperature for every mineral. Observations test whether Solar-System formation processes recur elsewhere.

topics.title: Bannerghatta: elephant exchange with Japan
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## July 2025 zoo exchange
- **Bannerghatta Biological Park, Bengaluru**, planned its first international animal transfer: four **Asian elephants**, one male/three females, to **Himeji Central Park–Safari Park, Japan**. Source names **Suresh, Gowri, Shruthi and Tulsi**.
- Multi-species exchange envisages BBP receiving **four each cheetahs, jaguars and pumas, three chimpanzees and eight black-capped capuchins**; planned receipts are not proof all animals had arrived.
- Transport via Bengaluru–Kansai/Osaka, medical clearance, trained crates/handling and accompanying veterinarians/caretakers; source says Indian staff would remain two weeks and Japanese keepers trained at BBP in May. Travel-time figures vary by flight/ground segment, so avoid treating “20 hours” as a reconciled end-to-end duration.
- Conservation education/research and ex-situ management require welfare, veterinary quarantine, lawful exchange authorisation and post-transfer monitoring. A zoo collection exchange is distinct from wild population reintroduction.

topics.title: IRDAI: insurance regulation and policyholder protection
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Institution and July appointment
- **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India:** statutory authority under **IRDA Act1999**; headquarters **Hyderabad**. **Section4 composition: Chairperson, up to five whole-time and up to four part-time members**, appointed by Central Government; statutory maximum is not evidence all seats filled.
- **24 July2025:** government notified **Ajay Seth's appointment as Chairperson**. Notification and taking charge are distinct events. [Finance Ministry appointment](https://www.financialservices.gov.in/appointment-sh-ajay-seth-ias-former-finance-secretary-and-secretary-dea-chairperson-irdai).
- Regulates/develops insurance and protects policyholders: registration, solvency, investments, reporting, inspections, intermediary qualifications/conduct, grievance/claim standards and rural/social obligations.
- Covers life/general/standalone-health/reinsurance entities and authorised intermediaries such as agents, brokers, TPAs, surveyors and loss assessors. A TPA supports health-claim services; it is not itself an insurer.
- Product/pricing oversight varies by insurance class and regulatory framework; avoid the PDF's implication that IRDAI individually pre-approves every premium/policy in every market. Protection, competition and financial soundness must be assessed together.

## Regulatory enforcement clipping
- Embedded report: IRDAI imposed **₹50 million (₹5 crore)** on **Policybazaar**, PB Fintech's insurance-broking/aggregation arm, for regulatory lapses, including managerial-personnel directorship issues. A regulatory penalty is distinct from a court conviction and should not imply every company product invalid.
- The Ajay Seth appointment clipping repeats the July appointment already retained; statutory composition, insurer/intermediary coverage and policyholder mandate add no separate new institutional facts.

topics.title: Adoption: child-centred safeguards and CARA
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Streamline procedures while protecting children
- July discussion cites **13 prospective parents per child legally free for adoption**; this is a source snapshot of registered demand/eligible supply, not all children in shelters or all Indian couples. Many applicants seek young healthy infants while eligible children may be older or have special needs.
- Children in institutions are **not automatically orphans or legally adoptable**: tracing family, restoration possibilities and Child Welfare Committee due process matter. Simplifying lawful identification/coordination differs from removing anti-trafficking safeguards.
- Digitised district records, trained CWCs/agencies and timely eligibility decisions; effective home studies, parent preparation, older/special-needs support, counselling and post-adoption follow-up improve safe placements. Principle: find a suitable family for the child, not a child to satisfy demand.
## Central Adoption Resource Authority
- Established as an autonomous body in **1990**; statutory under **JJ(Care and Protection of Children)Act2015 section68**, **Ministry of Women and Child Development**. Nodal authority for in-/inter-country adoption of orphaned, abandoned and surrendered children through recognised agencies.
- India ratified **1993 Hague Intercountry Adoption Convention in2003**; CARA is Central Authority, with international NOC/conformity processes, including **Article23 certificates**.
- **CARINGS:** Child Adoption Resource Information and Guidance System; supports registration, child/parent matching workflow and monitoring with SARA,DCPU,SAA,CWC and authorised foreign agencies. Confidentiality/data accuracy and verified legal status are essential. [CARA Bench Book](https://cara.wcd.gov.in/PDF/Bench%20Book%20For%20Adoptions.pdf).
- Legal routes: secular **JJAct** adoption and **Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act1956** for those covered. **Guardians and Wards Act1890 creates guardianship, not full adoption**, correcting the source's adoption-route shorthand; JJ adoption is available irrespective of religion.
- CARA training, counselling, public awareness, agency recognition/oversight and international coordination support ethical placement; child safety and speed are complementary when administrative bottlenecks are removed.

topics.title: Hydrogen trains and fuel-cell rail mobility
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## July 2025 prototype milestone
- Source reports successful testing of India's first hydrogen **Driving Power Car at Integral Coach Factory, Chennai**; a coach test is distinct from regular passenger-service commissioning. The printed **1,200 HP**, top-speed and early-2025 operational-date graphic are not reliable final specifications; retain the demonstrated milestone without treating those graphic claims as achieved performance.
- **Fuel cell:** hydrogen + atmospheric oxygen → electricity for traction + water/heat. Tailpipe CO₂ is absent, but lifecycle emissions depend on hydrogen production, electricity and supply chains. A hydrogen train still uses electric traction.
- **Hydrogen for Heritage:** 35 trains envisaged for heritage/hill routes; original estimates **₹80 crore/train + ₹70 crore ground infrastructure/route**. Separate **₹111.83 crore DEMU retrofit pilot**, including facilities, on **Jind–Sonipat, Haryana**. These are programme estimates, not an identical ₹150-crore final cost for every route. [Railways programme](https://www.pib.gov.in/Press Release Iframe Page.aspx?PRID=1896102&lang=2&reg=48).
- Benefits: lower local emissions, reduced diesel dependence, demonstration of indigenous fuel-cell integration. Constraints: initial cost, reliable low-emission hydrogen, storage/refuelling, safety and maintenance; scale may reduce cost. Source recalls Indian Oil's hydrogen-bus demonstration to Bhutan's PM in 2024 as another mobility application.

topics.title: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR)
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Institution, composition and appointment
- **Statutory body, established 2007**, under the **Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005**; child means **below 18**. India's CRC accession was in **1992**. Central Government appoints chairperson and **six members**, including **at least two women**, with expertise in education, health, welfare/development, juvenile justice, psychology/sociology or child law.
- Chairperson: eminent person with outstanding work for children's welfare. Terms **three years**, maximum **two terms**; age ceilings **65 chairperson /60 member**. Chair selection committee has **three members**, chaired by **Minister in charge of Women and Child Development**, correcting the PDF's Education-Minister claim. [Official Act](https://cdnbbsr.s 3 waas.gov.in/s 34 e 2974 dee 6 f 85 b 79404 d 688858 db 7 e 21/uploads/2025/07/20250704161385547.pdf).
## Powers and safeguards
- Reviews safeguards/laws and policy implementation; investigates complaints and acts **suo motu**; research, awareness, institutional inspections and recommendations to government. Monitors **RTE 2009 Section 31**, **POCSO 2012** and relevant **JJ 2015** implementation; it does not replace criminal courts or itself create POCSO Special Courts.
- Inquiry powers resemble a civil court: summon witnesses, require records/documents and receive evidence. Can recommend prosecution/action or interim relief and approach **SC/HC** for appropriate directions; recommendations are distinct from a court conviction.
- Central removal grounds include insolvency, impermissible paid work, incapacity/refusal, abuse of position and conviction involving moral turpitude; relevant statutory grounds require a reasonable opportunity of hearing.
- **POCSO e-Box:** online sexual-abuse reporting; **MASI**, Monitoring App for Seamless Inspection, for child-care institutions; **GHAR**, GO Home and Re-Unite, tracks restoration/repatriation; source describes **Samvardhan** vulnerability mapping against child trafficking.
- Embedded clipping links NCPCR/child protection with the Centre blocking **25 OTT platforms** for obscene/vulgar content. Blocking under IT-law procedures is a government action; NCPCR is not itself the blocking authority.

topics.title: Thailand–Cambodia border temples: Ta Muen Thom and Preah Vihear
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## July 2025 border conflict and Ta Muen group
- Source describes artillery, drones and Thai airstrikes amid Thailand–Cambodia border clashes. **Dangrek/Dongrak Mountains** separate northern Cambodia from northeastern Thailand; colonial demarcation, contested boundaries and nationalism complicate shared Khmer heritage.
- **Ta Muen Thom**, a Shiva temple of Angkorian/Khmer tradition, lies at the contested border by **Surin, Thailand**, on the ancient **Angkor–Phimai highway**. South-facing sandstone sanctuary, natural-rock linga and drainage channel; surrounding laterite structures and pool.
- Distinguish adjacent structures: **Ta Muen**, dharmasala/traveller shelter; **Ta Muen Tot**, hospital shrine associated with Khmer royal public-health infrastructure. Do not assign all three the same builder/date: source inconsistently attributes the main complex to the 11 th/12 th centuries and later Jayavarman VII additions.
- **Ta Muen Thom is not a UNESCO World Heritage property** and has no equivalent ICJ title judgment. Its territorial dispute must not be resolved merely by labelling it an undisputed temple in one country.

## Preah Vihear and the ICJ distinction
- **Preah Vihear**, Shiva temple on a Dangrek cliff in northern Cambodia, developed chiefly in the **11 th–12 th centuries**, associated with **Suryavarman I/II**; successive sanctuaries, stairways and gopuras along an **~800 m ascending axis**. UNESCO inscription **2008**.
- **1904/1907 Franco-Siamese demarcation** forms the colonial background; Thai occupation after French withdrawal in 1954 preceded **ICJ 1962** judgment establishing Cambodian sovereignty over the temple. Clashes recurred in 2011.
- **2013 interpretation:** Cambodian sovereignty over the **Preah Vihear promontory** and Thai withdrawal from it; **not an award of the entire contested 4.6 km² surrounding region**. The Court did not settle Ta Muen Thom or the full border. [ICJ case 151](https://www.icj-cij.org/case/151).
- Shared heritage can support cultural cooperation, but legal scope, bilateral border demarcation, civilian protection and de-escalation matter alongside national symbolism. Source comparison MCQ is practice, not a CSE PYQ.

topics.title: Workplace sexual harassment: Internal Committees and accountability
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Legal framework and composition
- **Vishaka 1997** guidelines preceded the **Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act,2013**. Bhanwari Devi's case exposed the legal gap; the statute covers public/private workplaces, educational institutions and other covered settings, not government offices alone.
- **Internal Committee (IC, commonly ICC)** at workplaces with **ten or more employees**—not “more than ten”. **Local Committee** handles establishments with fewer than ten and complaints against an employer; domestic workers also have a statutory route. [Act, India Code](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/2104?view_type=browse).
- Presiding Officer: **senior woman employee**; at least **two employee members** committed to women's cause/social-work or legal experience; **one external NGO/association member or person familiar with harassment issues**. **At least half women**. External participation does not make the outsider chairperson.
- Inquiry within **90 days**; statutory civil-court powers for summoning/examining and requiring documents. Conciliation only on the aggrieved woman's request; **monetary settlement cannot be its basis**. Confidentiality protects identities and proceedings. Committee recommends action; employer implements lawful recommendations; criminal-law assistance is separate.
## Implementation and July 2025 case study
- Source reports a Balasore student died after self-immolation following a disputed institutional sexual-harassment grievance response. Allegations of committee bias/training failure are allegations, not adjudicated conclusions about every member.
- Failures: committees absent/on paper, poor training, institutional conflicts, power imbalance, retaliation and confidentiality breaches. The Supreme Court's December 2024 compliance concerns underscore enforcement rather than a new statute.
- Improve composition/compliance audits, regular training, safe reporting, anti-retaliation safeguards, external independence and anonymised reporting. Disclosure of aggregate compliance must preserve survivor privacy. Source MCQ is practice, not a dated CSE PYQ.

topics.title: India–UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## July 2025 agreement: commitments versus entry into force
- **Signed 24 July 2025**, following negotiations begun January 2022 and conclusion announced May 2025; goods, services and wider economic rules. It was **not yet in force at this issue date**: domestic legal/ratification processes and agreed commencement remained; a projected 6–12 months was not a guaranteed deadline.
- UK commits to tariff elimination on **99% of Indian tariff lines**; India liberalises **90% of tariff lines**, covering roughly**92% of UK goods exports**. Newly duty-free exports differ from exports already at zero duty: source identifies textiles, leather/footwear, carpets, seafood, fruit and engineering/auto products as potential beneficiaries.
- Whisky/gin tariffs **150%→75% on entry,40% by year 10**; cars can reach**10% within quotas**. Product/quota schedules matter; this is not a 10% tariff on unlimited imports. Source notes delayed treatment of EV/hybrid/hydrogen vehicles.
- Services commitments include IT/consultancy and selected financial, telecom, environmental/professional services, with reservations and regulation. Recognition frameworks **do not automatically license every UK lawyer/accountant to practise in India**. UK access to specified Indian central-government procurement is subject to coverage/thresholds; it does not open every public contract.
- **Double Contributions Convention:** July side-letter commitment to reciprocal exemption for qualifying temporarily detached workers, initially up to**three years**, while continuing home-system contributions. The source's **75,000** is an estimate, not an immigration quota or universal exemption for all Indian hires; DCC is distinct from income-tax relief and from visa rights. [UK July explainer, with later changes separately dated](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/uk-india-trade-deal-double-contributions-convention-explainer).
- Opportunities: labour-intensive exports, investment, service mobility and supply-chain links. Evaluate preference utilisation, rules of origin, standards, sector adjustment and procurement safeguards; projected trade gains are not realised outcomes.

## Digital sovereignty: law and editorial
- Digital sovereignty concerns control over data, infrastructure and regulation. CETA was signed, but **not yet operative at this issue date**.
- **Article 12.15** source-code protection preserves **regulatory, judicial, inspection, enforcement/conformity-assessment exceptions**, with confidentiality safeguards; not a total loss of regulator access.
- **Article 12.12** concerns **non-proprietary government information made public**, not compulsory release of all sensitive data.
- **Article 12.20** specified later third-country commitments can trigger **consultations on equivalent data-flow/localisation disciplines**, not automatic present blanket free-flow concessions. [Treaty Chapter 12](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/uk-india-ceta-chapter-12-digital-trade/chapter-12-digital-trade-web-version).
- Editorial concerns about dependence should be evaluated with these safeguards; response: technology/cybersecurity expertise in negotiations, public scrutiny, clear data policy, indigenous capabilities and implementation monitoring.

topics.title: Startup20 and G20 entrepreneurship cooperation
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Institution and 2025 agenda
- **Startup 20**, official G 20 engagement group initiated under **India's 2023 presidency**, gives startups/ecosystem actors a policy voice; followed by **Brazil 2024, South Africa 2025**. Recommendations work through consensus and feed G 20 discussions, not binding supranational startup law.
- Source describes the third edition's launch in**Johannesburg**, with five task forces: **Foundation and Alliances; Finance and Investment; Inclusion and Sustainability; Trade and Market Access; Township and Rural Entrepreneurship**. Private-sector/entrepreneur participation seeks practical market access, capital, collaboration and inclusion.
- G 20 began**1999** as Finance Ministers/Central Bank Governors' forum;19 countries plus**EU and African Union(AU joined 2023)**. B 20 business, C 20 civil society, L 20 labour, S 20 science, W 20 women, T 20 think tanks, Y 20 youth are distinct engagement groups.
- PYQ recall: Argentina, Mexico, South Africa, Turkey all G 20 members(2020); finance-minister origins and India's DPI priority both correct(2023). **Common Framework 2020**, endorsed with Paris Club, coordinates debt treatment for eligible low-income countries; debt distress support is not universal debt cancellation.
- South Africa's **22 On Sloane** served as its 2025 Secretariat; the source's generic reference to an Indian Sherpa/secretariat should not imply permanent Indian control. [Startup20 South Africa](https://su20.org/).

topics.title: NASA Dynamic Targeting and autonomous Earth observation
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## July 2025 demonstration
- NASA/JPL's **Dynamic Targeting** lets a satellite analyse look-ahead imagery onboard and choose observations without awaiting ground commands. **Cogni SAT-6**, commercial Cube Sat launched March 2024, hosted July flight tests; Open Cosmos satellite/Ubotica AI payload.
- Look ahead roughly**500 km**→identify clouds→plan clear views→repoint and image: **60–90 seconds**. Saves storage/downlink and improves usable optical observations; onboard AI complements mission planning.
- First test proved **cloud avoidance**; wildfire/volcano thermal anomalies and storms were further test goals, not all established operational services. [NASA/JPL 24 July account](https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/how-nasa-is-testing-ai-to-make-earth-observing-satellites-smarter/).
## Linked satellite revision
- **Astro Sat**, India's first dedicated multiwavelength space observatory, launched**2015**,~**1,515 kg**,~**650 km** orbit. The 2016 PYQ's 2000 kg/1650 km and India-only-besides-US/Russia claims are false.
- **IRS**, imaging/remote sensing since**IRS-1 A 1988**, supports crop assessment, groundwater prospects, mineral exploration, forestry, water, planning and disasters. **GSAT-type communications satellites** serve telecom.2015 PYQ accepts crop, groundwater, mineral exploration; do not turn its exclusion of“traffic studies” into a universal claim that remote-sensing data can never support transport planning.

topics.title: Kala Utsav and Indian painting traditions
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Artists in residence: July 2025
- **29 Sohrai, Pattachitra and Patua artists** stayed at Rashtrapati Bhavan **14–24 July 2025**, creating, interacting and exhibiting traditional art under **Kala Utsav–Artists in Residence**. Source recalls an earlier Artists-in-Residence programme inaugurated in 2013; do not date every detail of the present Kala Utsav programme to that launch. [President's account](https://www.presidentofindia.gov.in/press_releases/saoharaaya-patatacaitara-aura-pataua-kalaa-kae-kalaakaaraon-nae-avaasaiya-kalaakaara).
| Tradition | Region and medium | Recall |
|---|---|---|
| **Sohrai** | Jharkhand; murals on house walls with earth/clay pigments | Women artists; harvest festival after Diwali; animals, plants and local symbols |
| **Pattachitra** | Odisha and Bengal; painted cloth/scroll traditions | Jagannath, Krishna and epic imagery; cloth preparation may use chalk and tamarind paste; regional forms differ |
| **Patua** | West Bengal; narrative cloth/paper scrolls | Patua artists sing while unrolling images; religious, folk and contemporary social/political themes |
- Visibility supports artist livelihoods, cultural diversity and transmission to younger generations.
## PYQ-linked painting recall
- **Bani Thani → Kishangarh school**, Rajasthan; **Nihal Chand**, mid-eighteenth century, associated with **Sawant Singh/Nagari Das**; elongated eyes, graceful devotional Radha–Krishna imagery.
- **Padmapani → Ajanta, Cave 1**, Maharashtra; lotus-bearing bodhisattva/compassion in Buddhist art. Ajanta's phases span roughly second century BCE–sixth century CE; murals on prepared plaster are distinguished from true wet-plaster fresco.
- **Kalamkari → hand-painted cotton textile, South India**, especially Andhra Pradesh: **Srikalahasti**, freehand pen and epic themes; **Machilipatnam**, block-printed floral/decorative tradition. Processes use indigo, myrobalan, pomegranate and iron preparations; myrobalan is not simply a black pigment.

topics.title: Maritime financing and Amrit Kaal Vision2047
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Maritime Financing Summit: 24 July 2025
- **Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, New Delhi**; financing, capacity, demand and skills support **Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047**. **Financial Digital Maturity Matrix (FDMM)** assesses and improves major ports' digital financial readiness.
- Proposed **₹25,000 crore Maritime Development Fund**, blended finance with government up to **49%**, remaining participation from ports, PSUs and private investors; aims to reduce capital cost and attract long-term investment. Announcement is distinct from disbursement.
- **100% automatic-route FDI** in covered shipping activities; GIFT IFSC ship finance/leasing, infrastructure recognition for qualifying large ships and greenfield/brownfield shipyards support capacity. Legislative reforms include **Bills of Lading 2025**, Merchant Shipping and Coastal Shipping measures; bill passage, assent and commencement differ.
- Official summit claims: turnaround **under one day**, versus four earlier, and container capacity up **70%**; specified periods/port metrics matter. Source's **819.22 million tonnes in FY2023–24** refers to **major-port cargo**, not all Indian ports. [Ministry release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2147994&lang=2&reg=48).
- Source's 20% cargo-carriage ambition and **₹1.5 lakh crore investment by 2030** are targets, not India's realised share of all global cargo. Complementary initiatives: Sagarmala, Maritime India Vision 2030, Major Port Authorities Act 2021 and National Logistics Portal (Marine).
## Ocean-group PYQ recall
- **IONS:** Indian Navy initiative; inaugural meeting **2008, New Delhi**; voluntary naval cooperation among Indian Ocean littorals, confidence building, safety and disaster response. Not founded in 2015.
- **IORA**, formerly IOR-ARC: **1997**; Secretariat **Ebène, Mauritius**, correcting the PDF's Durban headquarters. Trade, investment, fisheries, blue economy, disaster response and academic exchange extend beyond maritime security; not created solely in response to piracy/oil spills. [IORA Secretariat location](https://www.iora.int/sites/default/files/2025-04/IORA%20enewsletter%20Jan-March%202025%20Final_0.pdf).

topics.title: Climate finance taxonomy and credible green investment
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Draft framework: 2025
- **Department of Economic Affairs, Finance Ministry** released a draft in May 2025, following Budget 2024–25; comments invited until **25 June 2025**. It classifies climate-aligned activities to guide capital, reduce greenwashing and support **net zero 2070**, adaptation and reliable/affordable energy. A classification framework is not itself a fund. [DEA communiqué](https://www.dea.gov.in/files/announcements_documents/DraftFrameworkIndiasClimateFinanceTaxonomyPublication6thMay2025.pdf).
- **Mitigation:** reduce/avoid emissions; **adaptation:** improve resilience; **transition:** improve hard-to-abate sectors without assuming immediate zero emissions. Source outlines climate-supportive **Tier 1/Tier 2** and transition activities; detailed sectoral annexures/thresholds require separate development.
- Focus includes **power, transport, buildings, iron/steel/cement, agriculture, water and food security**. The PDF's claim that energy/transport/cement are ignored contradicts its own sector list; treat it as criticism of prioritisation/stringency, not literal absence.
- Evaluation: scientific thresholds, measurable outcomes, disclosure/verification, clear governance and periodic updates; include states, local bodies, workers, tribal/farming communities and traditional ecological knowledge. Protect food security, labour rights and equity; avoid locking in high-emission assets under a loose transition label.
- **EU taxonomy:** substantial contribution, enabling and transitional activities with safeguards; copying labels cannot establish India-appropriate criteria. Claims that India's draft simply copies the EU or entirely lacks safeguards are editorial criticism, not independently established facts.
## Related EU revision
- **European Stability Mechanism:** euro-area financial assistance, not a refugee/trade-dispute body.
- **BTIA:** India–EU trade/investment negotiations begun in 2007.
- **Nature Restoration Law 2024:** EU ecosystem-restoration framework; measures aim to cover at least **20% of EU land and sea areas by 2030**, with longer-term restoration objectives. The 2025 PYQ identifies the EU.

topics.title: Glacial lake outburst floods: Himalayan risk and preparedness
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Mechanism and exposure
- Glacier retreat/melt creates lakes: **supraglacial** lakes sit on the glacier; **moraine-dammed** lakes are impounded by debris, often ice-cored. Sudden release after dam failure/overtopping is a **GLOF**. Avalanches, landslides, earthquakes, heavy inflow and weak moraine can trigger cascading floods; not every lake is equally dangerous.
- **4 October 2023, South Lhonak, Sikkim:** outburst in the Teesta basin destroyed **Teesta III/Chungthang dam**, damaging bridges, homes, roads and downstream hydropower. Source counts **14 bridges, 1,320 houses and 35+ deaths** are dated estimates, not a final reconciled toll.
- Warming/retreat can enlarge lakes; avalanches and dam geometry govern individual hazard. Infrastructure/settlements in flood paths increase exposure. **Kedarnath 2013 was a multicausal flood/debris disaster**, not proof every Himalayan flood is a GLOF; volcanic jökulhlaups elsewhere are not a dominant Indian Himalayan trigger.
- Source's **28,000+ lakes**, Sikkim **733/10 highly vulnerable**, Uttarakhand **486/13 vulnerable**, and J&K superlative mix inventory years, boundaries and screening methods; treat as source-specific figures pending matched primary inventories, not a current national ranking.
## Preparedness
- Satellite mapping, field bathymetry/moraine assessment, weather/lake/river sensors and **SAR interferometry** for slope motion; prioritise hazards and update downstream flood models.
- Early warning must connect detection to redundant communications, community evacuation drills and safe shelters. Dams, bridges and highways need sediment/debris, seismic and cascading-risk assessment; evaluate cumulative catchment/hydropower impacts and regulate construction near flow paths.
- Protect lives, livelihoods, connectivity and water security with science-led catchment planning and local participation; afforestation or one sensor alone cannot remove GLOF risk.

## Mechanism
- Glacier melt/retreat creates lakes; **supraglacial lakes** sit on ice, while **moraine-dammed lakes** are held by loose rock/debris, sometimes ice-cored. Failure releases a sudden downstream flood (**GLOF**); retreat alone does not guarantee an outburst.
- Ice/rock avalanche → displacement wave/overtopping → moraine erosion/breach → debris-rich downstream flood. Earthquakes, slope failure, rapid inflow and weak dams compound risk; glacier surges can temporarily block drainage. Construction/deforestation can increase exposure or slope instability. Volcanic melting is a global trigger, not a typical Indian Himalayan explanation.
## South Lhonak and exposure
- **4 October 2023, South Lhonak, Sikkim:** outburst devastated the Teesta valley and **1,200 MW Teesta III/Chungthang dam**; roads, bridges, homes, hydropower and livelihoods were damaged. Source reports **14 bridges,1,320 homes,35+ deaths**: dated reported estimates, not a final reconciled toll. Kedarnath 2013 involved intense rain and Chorabari lake flooding; the disasters are not identical mechanisms.
- Issue cites **28,000+ lakes** for the Indian Himalayan region; embedded clipping distinguishes the wider Himalayan region and **over 7,500 in India**. Inventory boundary, minimum size and survey date matter—do not use 28,000 as a verified India-only total. Its Sikkim **733/10 high-risk**, Uttarakhand **486/13 vulnerable** and J&K ranking are differently sourced snapshots, not a common current risk census.
## Reduce risk
- Satellite/drone mapping, field bathymetry and moraine/slope assessment; **SAR interferometry** detects slope movement. Weather/lake/river sensors, resilient warning communication and evacuation drills require local maintenance and community participation.
- Risk-based prioritisation, lake-lowering or other engineering where scientifically justified, land-use restrictions and sediment/runout modelling; assess cascading effects on hydropower, roads and bridges.
- **NDMA National GLOF Risk Mitigation Programme**, coordination with States/scientific agencies, catchment-scale risk assessment and updated design standards support preparedness. Avoid presenting continuous monitoring or every planned mitigation survey as already completed.

topics.title: India–Japan strategic and economic partnership
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## July 28 dialogue
- Foreign Secretary **Vikram Misri** met Japanese Vice-Minister **Takehiro Funakoshi** in Delhi ahead of the planned prime-ministerial visit: defence/security, trade/investment, infrastructure, economic security, technology and people-to-people ties; Quad cooperation and a **free and open Indo-Pacific**. [Japanese Foreign Ministry](https://www.mofa.go.jp/press/release/pressite_000001_01492.html).
- **Special Strategic and Global Partnership** links India's Act East policy with Japan's Indo-Pacific vision. **JIMEX** is their maritime exercise; supply-chain resilience includes critical minerals, rare-earth diversification, semiconductors, AI, cyber and clean technologies. **SCRI**, India–Japan–Australia, launched in 2021.
## Mumbai–Ahmedabad high-speed rail
- India's first high-speed rail corridor, about **508 km**, Japanese **Shinkansen** technology, operating design target **320 km/h**. Japanese concessional finance cited at **0.1%, 50 years**; loan totals are project/source-period figures, not proof full cost has been disbursed.
- Issue reports Gujarat section targeted **December 2027**, full corridor **December 2029**: schedules, not completed milestones. **E10** introduction in India/Japan was officially agreed in July; this is a future rolling-stock commitment, not delivery of two gifted E10 sets. [Railways July 14 release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2144522&lang=2&reg=3).
- Strategic value: long-term infrastructure finance, technology transfer and resilient production networks. Assess completion, domestic capability, viability and actual mineral supply arrangements separately from diplomatic announcements.

topics.title: Contaminated sites: remediation rules and pollution boards
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Rules notified 24 July 2025
- **Environment Protection (Management of Contaminated Sites) Rules, 2025**, under the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**. A contaminated site is formally declared by **SPCB/PCC** after detailed assessment finds prescribed contaminants above thresholds; suspected site is an earlier screening category. Legacy industrial dumping, chemical spills and waste handling/storage can leave contamination. [Gazette record](https://www.mpcb.gov.in/en/node/7336), [ministry clarification of July rules](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2157518&lang=2&reg=48).
- Local bodies/district administrations identify and list suspected sites, including public complaints; preliminary and detailed scientific assessment precedes a remediation design and follow-up monitoring. Issue describes **half-yearly reporting**, preliminary assessment within **90 days** and detailed assessment within **three months of probable-site listing**; these are specific procedural stages, not a universal three-month cleanup promise.
- **Polluter pays:** responsible persons bear remediation cost; orphan/untraceable/defunct polluters require public funding arrangements and later recovery where possible. Death/injury can attract the **BNS**, alongside environmental liability; every contaminated site is not automatically a proven criminal case.
- Issue inventory: **103 identified sites; remediation initiated at seven**. 'Initiated' does not mean cleaned; inventory is dated and differs from newly confirmed sites under the rules.
## Boards and implementation
- **CPCB:** statutory body constituted in **September 1974 under Water Act 1974**; Air Act 1981 and EPA functions supplement its mandate. Coordinates State boards, sets/supports standards, compiles pollution data, trains and advises.
- **SPCBs:** State statutory boards; inspect, monitor water/air, administer industrial **Consent to Establish/Operate**, and enforce waste rules. **PCCs** perform corresponding UT functions. Their mandates differ from local waste collection duties.
- Capacity gaps: scientific/legal vacancies, expanding mandates, weak coordination, inconsistent enforcement. Priorities: transparent inventories, site-risk ranking, competent laboratories, cost recovery, community health protection and post-remediation monitoring.

## Scope caution
- Issue distinguishes hazardous industrial chemical spills and polluted groundwater from streams addressed under separate regimes (radioactive waste, mining operations, marine oil and solid-waste processing sites). Apply the exact notified exclusions rather than assuming every landfill or every polluted site follows the same rule.
- Existing environmental duties preceded 2025; the source's “no legal process until now” overstates the novelty. These rules provide a specific contaminated-site identification/remediation framework, not the first environmental liability in India.

topics.title: Chola legacy: maritime power, temples and local assemblies
topics.subject: Ancient and Medieval India
topics.markdown:
## July 2025 commemoration
- **Aadi Thiruvathirai**, Tamil Shaiva festival associated with Rajendra I's birth star; the PM visited **Gangaikonda Cholapuram on 27 July** and released a commemorative coin. Event marked the millennium of the **1025 Southeast Asian maritime expedition** and commencement of temple construction; source also reports planned statues of Rajaraja I/Rajendra I. [Official event](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2149075&lang=2&reg=3).
- Shaiva Bhakti of **63 Nayanmars**, Tamil devotional literature and Chola patronage provide cultural context; the July festival is not proof that every temple was completed in 1025.
## Dynasty and major rulers
- **Muvendhar:** Chola, Chera, Pandya; early Cholas appear in Sangam traditions and Ashokan inscriptions. Imperial resurgence from the ninth century under **Vijayalaya**, who captured Thanjavur (source reign c.848–871).
| Ruler | Source-period reign and significance |
|---|---|
| Rajaraja I | **985–1014**; expansion including Sri Lanka/Maldives; strong naval activity; **Brihadisvara, Thanjavur** |
| Rajendra I | **1014–1044**; northern/Ganges campaign, new capital **Gangaikonda Cholapuram**, naval expedition against **Srivijaya (1025)**; maritime trade and irrigation, including **Cholagangam** |
| Kulottunga I | **1070–1122** in source; Chola–Eastern Chalukya dynastic connection, revenue/land administration |
- Source maps distinguish **territory**, **trade routes** and **cultural influence**. A raid on Srivijaya or contact with Southeast Asia does not establish permanent annexation of the entire region. Unsupported claims that Cholas built Java's Buddhist monasteries or caused Angkor Wat/Borobudur architecture should not be memorised; Nagapattinam's Buddhist patronage is a separate history.
## Village administration: Kudavolai
- **Sabha:** Brahmin village assembly; **ur:** wider non-Brahmin village assembly. Committees administered irrigation/tanks, taxation, temple affairs and local justice.
- Kudavolai selected eligible candidates by drawing named palm-leaf slips from a pot, including a child's draw. Qualifications included **tax-paying landownership, age 35–70, learning and probity**; failure to submit accounts and misconduct attracted disqualification. Do not translate this into universal adult suffrage: caste, property and gender exclusions limited participation.
- Modern relevance: accountable local administration, audits, water management, maritime connections and cultural exchange. The PDF's 'first navy'/'oldest democracy' superlatives and precise child-age requirement are not established historical rankings.

topics.title: International Big Cat Alliance
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Conservation platform
- India-led **IBCA**, launched **9 April 2023** on Project Tiger's 50th anniversary after the PM's 2019 call for cooperation. Seven cats: **tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar, puma**; India hosts the first five, including reintroduced cheetahs.
- Cooperation covers habitat protection, anti-poaching/illegal trade, research, technical expertise, conservation finance and climate resilience. Both range and interested non-range countries can participate; finding all seven species is not a membership condition.
- Cabinet approved headquarters in India and **₹150 crore support, FY 2023–24 to FY 2027–28**; governance includes **Assembly of Members, Standing Committee, Secretariat**. [Cabinet decision](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2010124&lang=2&reg=48).
## July 2025 membership snapshot
- Issue distinguishes **24 countries agreeing to join** from **12 members**: India, Armenia, Bhutan, Cambodia, Ethiopia, Eswatini, Guinea, Liberia, Nicaragua, Rwanda, Somalia, Suriname. Agreement/intention, ratification and full membership are different stages; the practice question's 'as of 2024' dates this July snapshot incorrectly.
- Landscape conservation protects prey, habitat and ecosystem functions, not only individual flagship cats. Link **Project Tiger 1973**, Gir lion conservation and **2022 Kuno cheetah reintroduction**; the source's 96-country reach is not a permanent membership total.

topics.title: Barbados threadsnake and endemic habitat conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Rediscovery corrected to 2025
- **Tetracheilostoma carlae**, endemic Barbados threadsnake, smallest known snake (about **9–10 cm** adult). Re:wild and the Barbados environment ministry rediscovered it in **March 2025**, announced **23 July 2025**, after nearly 20 years without scientifically verified sighting. The PDF's 2024 dates are wrong. [Re:wild announcement](https://www.rewild.org/press/barbados-threadsnake-rediscovery).
- Cryptic burrower in soil/leaf litter, feeds on **ants/termites**; reduced vision, pale dorsal stripes and lateral eyes help distinguish it from introduced **Brahminy/flowerpot blind snake**. Females lay **one slender egg**; rediscovery is not proof of population recovery or removal of extinction risk.
- Described as a distinct species by **S.Blair Hedges in 2008**, named for Carla. Microscopic identification and continued field surveys matter; conserve remaining forest/gullies, control habitat degradation and invasive threats.

topics.title: Barbados: Atlantic geography and coral limestone
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Map and relief
- Independent island state, capital **Bridgetown**, in the **Atlantic east of the main Caribbean Sea**, northeast of Venezuela; part of the wider Caribbean/West Indies.
- **Easternmost Lesser Antilles island** in conventional regional geography, lying east of the volcanic island arc. The PDF incorrectly turns its position outside that volcanic arc into exclusion from the Lesser Antilles. [Regional climate centre country profile](https://rcc.cimh.edu.bb/files/2018/06/Country-Profile-Barbados.pdf).
- Predominantly uplifted **coral limestone**, rather than a volcanic cone; gullies and terraced relief. **Mount Hillaby**, Scotland District, about **340 m**, highest point. Coral cover does not make every part of the island a reef-built atoll; Scotland District exposes older sedimentary material. [Barbados national biodiversity report](https://biodiversity.gov.bb/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/1st-National-Report.pdf).

topics.title: Gini index and multidimensional inequality
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Read the measure correctly
- Gini describes distribution of a specified variable: **0 (equality) to 1 (inequality)**, or 0–100. Income, consumption and wealth Ginis answer different questions; a single aggregate cannot measure every form of inequality.
- India's **25.5** cited in July debate is a **consumption-based measure for 2022–23**, not a comprehensive 2023 income/wealth Gini. World Bank derives it from household surveys, not only tax returns/formal wages. The PDF's assertion that informal workers are simply excluded is false; survey coverage, rich-household underrepresentation, top-end consumption and expenditure definitions can still bias inequality downward. [World Bank methodology](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099060325033540333/pdf/P180633-e1a59178-dc78-4b14-8928-1c88d02240f3.pdf).
- Consumption can be smoother/more equal than income or wealth; do not infer a low consumption Gini means low asset concentration. Source **top 1% income share 22.6%,2022–23** is an income-share estimate, not a wealth share or mathematical contradiction of consumption Gini.
## Overlapping disadvantages
- Analyse gender, caste/location, employment quality, property/inheritance, health, education and digital access alongside distribution. Source reports school computer/internet access **52.7%/53.9%**, household broadband **41.8%**, rural female/male internet **25%/49%**, women managers **12.7%** and women-run startups **7.5%**; these have unspecified survey periods/denominators and should not be treated as one verified July 2025 census. 'Women35.9% of workforce' is also not the same as female labour-force participation rate.
- Digital exclusion compounds gender/education gaps through online banking, learning and job access. Combine disaggregated household surveys, administrative/tax and wealth evidence, service-access indicators and qualitative fieldwork; comparing countries requires matching variable, year and method.

topics.title: MoSPI: statistical rebasing and new household surveys
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Plans announced in July 2025
- Issue schedules new **GDP base 2022–23** series for **27 February 2026**, replacing 2011–12; **IIP base 2022–23** planned from April 2026 and **CPI base 2024** planned earlyFY 2026–27, replacing 2012. These are **then-announced schedules**, not July implementation or guaranteed eventual launch dates.
- Rebasing updates weights, production/consumption structures and methods. It does not itself create real output or automatically lower inflation; old/new series need methodological reconciliation.
- **DTES (Domestic Tourism Expenditure Survey)** and **NHTS (National Household Travel Survey)** run **July 2025–June 2026**, NSS 80th round: tourism spending and travel purpose/modes/origin-destination patterns. NHTS is not confined to international tourism. [NSO announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2137863&lang=2&reg=48).
- **Annual Survey of Service Sector Enterprises (ASSSE)** planned for January 2026 to improve formal-services evidence, analogous to industrial surveys. GST, e-Vahan, UPI, online prices and web-scraped data were being explored as administrative/digital inputs, not complete replacements for surveys.
## Institution and outputs
- **NSO, MoSPI** handles national accounts, CPI, IIP and major surveys; CSO/NSSO are predecessor organisational components, not unchanged standalone current departments. Ministry also monitors **MPLADS/Twenty Point Programme**.
- **National Statistical Commission** is an advisory body created by government resolution, not a constitutional commission. **ISI** is a statistics research/teaching institution; **eSankhyiki, EnviStats India, HCES, National Accounts Statistics** are useful portal/publication/survey links.

topics.title: Legal aid, NALSA and Lok Adalats
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Constitutional and statutory basis
- **Article 39A**, added by **42nd Amendment Act 1976**, is a **Directive Principle**, not itself a Fundamental Right. Articles 14,21 and 22(1) support equality, fair procedure and counsel safeguards.
- **Legal Services Authorities Act 1987**; NALSA established **1995**. Earlier **CILAS 1980** under Justice P.N. Bhagwati helped coordinate legal aid. Distinguish enactment, commencement and institutional creation.
- National: CJI **Patron-in-Chief**, executive chairman a serving/retired SC judge nominated under the Act (conventionally second senior-most sitting judge); State: HC chief justice Patron-in-Chief; High Court legal-services committee; district authority chaired by district judge; taluk committee by senior-most judicial officer as prescribed. Source's second-senior-most phrasing is convention, not the statute's only possible appointee.
## Eligibility and services
- Section 12 categories include women/children, SC/ST, trafficking/begar victims, persons with disability, industrial workmen, disaster/violence victims, persons in custody and persons within prescribed income limits. Category-based eligibility need not depend on low income.
- **Income ceilings vary by State/court**; the PDF's₹1 lakh is not one universal national cap. Supreme Court threshold cited₹5 lakh. Services include advice, counsel, pleadings/translations, court/process expenses and certified documents subject to eligibility/procedure.
## Lok Adalat
- Statutory settlement/conciliation forum for pending or pre-litigation disputes; ordinary Lok Adalat cannot impose its own merits decision where no compromise occurs. No fee; court fee refunded after settlement where applicable.
- Award deemed civil-court decree,**final/binding, no statutory appeal**; excludes non-compoundable criminal offences. Failure to settle permits ordinary litigation; mere dissatisfaction is not a universal right to reopen a valid consent award. **Permanent Lok Adalats** for public-utility disputes have distinct statutory adjudicatory powers. [NALSA](https://nalsa.gov.in/lok-adalats/), [NALSA FAQs](https://nalsa.gov.in/faqs/).
## Capacity constraints:July 2025 editorial
- Source reports over 80% potentially eligible but only **15.5 lakh recipients between April 2023 andMarch 2024**; coverage denominator differs from actual demand. Legal-aid budget below 1% of the wider justice-system budget; some States₹2–₹3 per capita,**para-legal volunteers down 38% since 2019**.
- Embedded clipping: funding about₹601 crore in 2017–18 to₹1,086 crore in 2022–23 across25 States; rising allocation can coexist with underutilisation. Volunteer honoria differ; low pay, thin rural staffing and rigid spending rules limit reach/quality.
- **Legal Aid Defence Counsel Scheme 2022:** salaried criminal-defence/public-defender model; issue reports610 of 670 districts. Adequate funding, training, retention, awareness, mobile advice, flexible local spending, beneficiary feedback and quality audits matter more than case counts alone.

topics.title: Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana: food processing
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Food processing and July 2025 allocation
- **Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana**, MoFPI **Central Sector** scheme approved May 2017; distinct from **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana**, which shares PMKSY acronym. Farm-to-market infrastructure reduces post-harvest loss, adds value, supports farmer returns/rural jobs and processed-food exports.
- **31 July 2025 Cabinet:** total **₹6,520 crore**, including **₹1,920 crore additional**, for **15th FC cycle 2021–22 to 2025–26**, rather than all spending in FY 2025.
- Additional **₹1,000 crore** supports **50 multi-product irradiation units** under Integrated Cold Chain/Value Addition and **100 NABL-accredited food-testing labs** under Food Safety/Quality Assurance; **₹920 crore** for other component projects. Approved investments, not completed facilities. Irradiation controls microbes/pests and extends shelf life; testing checks safety/quality/export compliance. [Cabinet](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2150646&lang=2&reg=48).
- Current components: cold chain, processing/preservation capacity, agro-processing clusters, food safety, R&D and Operation Greens. **Mega Food Parks, separate Backward/Forward Linkages and specified promotional/skill/HACCP components discontinued for new support**, committed liabilities continue; PDF's seven-component list is historical. [MoFPI](https://www.mofpi.gov.in//Schemes/about-pmksy-scheme).
- Practice key prints “2 and 3 only” for two statements: intended **statement 2 only**, since PMKSY is Central Sector.

topics.title: HOPE: Himalayan Outpost for Planetary Exploration
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Tso Kar analogue mission
- **HOPE=Himalayan Outpost for Planetary Exploration**, correcting “Human Outer Planet Exploration”. Inaugurated **31 July 2025**, **Tso Kar Valley, Ladakh**; industry partner **Protoplanet**, with ISRO's Human Space Flight Centre leading analogue research. Not NASA-led or a Mars landing.
