- **Two crew**, planned **1–10 August 2025** isolation; experiments examine physiological, psychological, genomic/epigenetic responses, health monitoring, surface operations and sampling/microbiology.
- High UV, low pressure, cold extremes, saline permafrost simulate some early-Mars conditions. Connected **8 m living habitat/5 m utility module** support operations.
- Findings support protocols, habitat design, teamwork, resources and environmental adaptation; Earth cannot reproduce all off-world conditions. Earlier **Ladakh Human Analog Mission, November 2024**, and **Anugami, July 2025**, qualify any “first analogue study” claim. [ISRO 1 August](https://www.isro.gov.in/ISRO_EN/Space_Analog_Mission.html).
- Source comparisons: **HI-SEAS, Hawaii; Mars Desert Research Station, Utah; Iceland**. Private/public collaboration complements Gaganyaan/future exploration.

topics.title: National Film Awards
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Institution
- **1954 institution**, first recognising 1953 films, initially State Awards; **feature, non-feature, best writing on cinema** sections. National juries reward artistic/technical excellence, cultural diversity and socially relevant cinema.
- **NFDC under Information and Broadcasting Ministry** now manages awards; DFF historically administered them from 1973. Source's unqualified 2025 DFF claim is outdated. **CBFC certifies films**, rather than choosing winners. [NFDC document](https://nfdcindia.com/nfdcapi/api/gallery/1747660305018_5874827.pdf).
## 71st awards: announced 1 August 2025, for 2023 films
| Honour | Winner |
|---|---|
| Feature | **12th Fail, Vidhu Vinod Chopra** |
| Actor | **Shah Rukh Khan, Jawan; Vikrant Massey, 12th Fail** |
| Actress | **Rani Mukerji, Mrs. Chatterjee Vs Norway** |
| Supporting actor | **Vijayaraghavan; Muthupettai Somu Bhaskar** |
| Supporting actress | **Urvashi; Janki Bodiwala** |
| Direction | **Sudipto Sen, The Kerala Story** |

| Debut director | **Ashish Bende, Aatmapamphlet** |
| National/social/environmental values | **Sam Bahadur** |
| AVGC | **Hanu-Man** |
- **Flowering Man** best non-feature; **God Vulture and Human** documentary; **Giddh The Scavenger** short film. 2025 announcement differs from 2023 film/award reference year. [Official announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2151537&lang=2&reg=48).
- Practice key wrongly accepts “instituted 1953”; distinguish film year and award establishment.

topics.title: BlueBird and direct-to-device satellite communications
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Planned commercial launch: August 2025
- **BlueBird Block 2**, **AST SpaceMobile (USA)**, communications satellite for **direct-to-device mobile broadband**, including ordinary phones through compatible networks; distinct from NISAR radar/Gaganyaan crew capsule.
- Issue reports **~6,500 kg**, **LVM3 (formerly GSLV Mk III)** launch from **Sriharikota**; satellite arrival expected September 2025 and launch late 2025/early 2026. Forecasts, not completed milestones in this issue.
- Heavy commercial launches support revenue, domestic skills and India–US cooperation. Coverage, spectrum authorisation, bandwidth, terrestrial integration and delivered service differ from launch success.
- **NISAR=NASA–ISRO**, not ESA; L/S radar observes Earth. LVM3 naming does not make every configuration human-rated.

topics.title: Mithun: Northeast livestock and cultural heritage
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## August 2025: livestock inclusion demand
- Northeast scientists and tribal farmers sought Mithun's inclusion in national livestock support schemes, including NLM, for breeding, veterinary care and livelihoods; a demand is not proof inclusion has been notified.
- **Mithun/Gayal/Drung ox, Bos frontalis**, semi-domesticated bovine associated with the gaur; hill forests of **Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram**, with related populations in neighbouring countries. Arunachal has the largest Indian population; state animal of **Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland**. Adi **Solung** and ceremonial exchanges connect cattle with social/cultural life.
- Embedded graphic: FSSAI food-animal recognition in **2023**, ICAR **M-ANITRA** market-linkage app; traditional free-ranging herds also need habitat, breeding and health management. The source's 2019 population of about four lakh is a dated census estimate.
- **Correction:** do not transfer wild gaur's conservation labels to domestic Mithun. CITES Appendix I entry for **Bos gaurus explicitly excludes the domesticated Bos frontalis**. The PDF's unqualified 'Mithun: IUCN Vulnerable/CITES I' conflates taxa; no separate wild-species IUCN category is established here for the domestic form. [CITES appendices](https://cites.org/eng/app/appendices.php), [ICAR Mithun research](https://www.icar.gov.in/en/node/4152).

topics.title: Oreshnik: Russian intermediate-range ballistic missile
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Source-period Russian announcement
- **Oreshnik** (hazel tree) is Russia's mobile, solid-fuelled **intermediate-range ballistic missile**; first combat use reported **21 November 2024, Dnipro, Ukraine**. August 2025 announcement described serial production and planned deployment in **Belarus by end-2025**; that was a prospective deployment at this issue date.
- Source reports roughly **5,000-km range**, speeds up to **Mach 10**, nuclear/conventional capability and multiple re-entry vehicles. Treat these as reported/claimed capabilities, not independently demonstrated exact performance or proof of immunity to interception.
- **MIRV** means independently targetable re-entry vehicles; multiple payloads/submunitions alone do not establish independent targeting. The worksheet's confident MIRV and mid-air manoeuvrability claims should not be learned as verified specifications. A ballistic weapon reaching hypersonic speeds is distinct from a powered hypersonic cruise missile.

topics.title: Red panda: Eastern Himalayan forest conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Sikkim conservation breeding
- Red panda cubs were born at **Himalayan Zoological Park near Gangtok** after a reported seven-year interval; embedded clipping recalls earlier losses to **canine distemper**. Captive breeding supports conservation but does not itself prove wild populations recovered.
- **Ailurus fulgens**, lesser/red panda: small, largely solitary, arboreal mammal; order **Carnivora**, but bamboo dominates its diet, with fruit/insects/eggs and occasional small animals. Long tail helps balance and warmth; Sikkim's state animal.
- Mountain forests with bamboo understorey in the **Eastern Himalayas and adjoining southwest China**: India (Sikkim, northern West Bengal, Arunachal), Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar and China—not Western Ghats/Terai plains. Himalayan/Chinese red-panda taxonomic treatments differ; do not read the graphic's subspecies map as a settled universal classification.
- **IUCN Endangered; CITES Appendix I; Wildlife (Protection) Act Schedule I**. Habitat/bamboo loss and fragmentation are major threats. Decline can signal forest degradation; indicator species is an ecological use, not a separate legal protection category.

topics.title: Indo-Burma Ramsar Regional Initiative
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## COP15: Strategic Plan 2025–2030
- **IBRRI** brings together **Cambodia, Lao PDR, Myanmar, Thailand and Viet Nam**; India/Bangladesh are not its five participating countries. New **2025–2030 plan** launched at Ramsar COP15, **Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe**, in July 2025.
- Aims to reverse wetland loss through restoration, better management, policy/investment integration, awareness and regional cooperation. Wetlands support water purification, flood regulation, biodiversity, livelihoods and carbon storage.
- Government focal points form the steering mechanism; **IUCN Asia Regional Office, Bangkok** hosts secretariat; stakeholder participation brings experts, NGOs and communities into advice. IUCN's **BRIDGE** work supports shared-water cooperation. The source's Indo-Burma biogeographic map covers more territory than the five-country membership.
- Practice key has a letter mismatch: statements **1,3,4 correspond to (c)**, not printed '(a)'. [IUCN plan](https://iucn.org/resources/file/indo-burma-regional-ramsar-initiative-strategic-plan-2025-2030), [COP15 report](https://iucn.org/news/202507/ramsar-cop15-concludes-strengthened-global-commitment-wetland-restoration-and-inclusive).

topics.title: Wind farms: bird mortality and biodiversity safeguards
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Thar evidence and a headline correction
- WII-led **2020–21 Jaisalmer study**, published June 2025: **3,000 km²**, about **900 turbines**, sample **90 turbines**, seven seasonal searches; **124 carcasses**, none in a single concurrent survey at **28 control sites**.
- Bias-adjusted estimate **1.24 ±0.18 birds/turbine/month**, about **14.9/year** or **4,464 birds/year/1,000 km²**. These are estimated rates, not 124 deaths every month.
- **Not the world's highest:** original paper cites **Belgium 19.1–34.3/turbine/year**, and calls Thar near the upper global range. Search-radius deaths combine turbines and nearby associated power lines; control comparison does not prove every death was blade collision. **No bustard–turbine collision was observed**; power lines are an established bustard threat. Raptors are especially vulnerable after adjusting for crossings. [Original study](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-03407-8).
## Planning response
- Thar is a **Central Asian Flyway** wintering/conservation landscape; renewable projects can cause collisions, habitat loss/displacement and cumulative infrastructure pressures.
- Avoid sensitive sites; test painting part of one blade black, seasonal/detection-triggered shutdowns, and robust monitoring. **BirdLife International's AVISTEP** maps avian sensitivity; ground surveys remain necessary. [BirdLife tool](https://datazone.birdlife.org/tools/avistep).
- Issue advocates mandatory environmental assessment for onshore wind and stronger ecological surveys; do not infer exemption removes every forest/wildlife/coastal permission. Offshore expansion is not risk-free: construction noise, marine fauna, migration routes and submarine cabling require assessment. Source's **30-GW by 2030/4-GW bidding** are plans, not operating capacity.

topics.title: Biosimilars: comparability, testing and affordable biologics
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Scientific distinction
- Small-molecule generics reproduce a relatively simple chemical active substance; **biologics** are complex products made using living systems, such as insulin and monoclonal antibodies. **Biosimilars are highly similar to a reference biologic**, with no clinically meaningful differences in relevant safety/efficacy; they are not ordinary chemically identical generics.
- Manufacturing complexity and costly comparative testing contribute to development cost; increased competition can improve access to expensive therapies.
## August 2025 regulatory debate
- Editorial proposes proportionate Indian requirements, using strong analytical/functional comparability and clinical studies only where remaining uncertainty justifies them. Do not record the proposal as a completed universal Indian waiver.
- **UK MHRA February 2025 guidance** does not request animal in-vivo studies for biosimilar comparability and generally permits omission of comparative efficacy trials when justified; quality and appropriate human evidence still matter. [MHRA guidance](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/guidance-on-the-licensing-of-biosimilar-products/guidance-on-the-licensing-of-biosimilar-products).
- **US FDA April 2025 roadmap** announced staged adoption of human-relevant methods, including computational and organ-based models, especially for monoclonal antibodies. A roadmap is not proof all animal/clinical testing of every US drug was abolished by August. [FDA April announcement](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-announces-plan-phase-out-animal-testing-requirement-monoclonal-antibodies-and-other-drugs).
- Reform must validate alternatives and preserve manufacturing consistency, immunogenicity assessment and post-marketing surveillance; lower testing burden does not mean lower safety standards.

topics.title: Nangarni Spardha and agrarian racing traditions
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Konkan monsoon tradition
- **Nangarni Spardha**, traditional oxen race at **Dervan, Ratnagiri, Maharashtra**, organised during the monsoon by village communities. Barefoot drivers guide decorated oxen along muddy tracks; an expression of farmer–animal ties, skill and agrarian/community identity.
- Compare **Kambala—Karnataka, buffalo racing** and **Maramadi—Kerala, cattle/ox racing**. Worksheet explanation wrongly numbers an extra statement; its two-statement key remains **1 only**.

topics.title: Xenophobia and racism
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Distinguish basis of exclusion
| Concept | Basis and reach |
|---|---|
| Xenophobia | Fear/hostility toward foreigners or people perceived as outsiders; may target someone of the same racial background |
| Racism | Racial/ethnic hierarchy, prejudice or discrimination; can affect fellow citizens within one country |
- Greek **xenos (stranger) + phobos (fear)**. Both can overlap in anti-immigrant violence and exclusionary nationalism; racism need not require foreign nationality, and xenophobia need not require racial difference.
- Source reports attacks in China/Japan as context; avoid attributing such conduct to whole national populations. Equal protection, effective investigation, inclusive public communication and institutional anti-discrimination practices address individual and systemic dimensions.

topics.title: Central Industrial Security Force
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Institution and August expansion reporting
- **CISF**, Ministry of **Home Affairs**, headquarters **New Delhi**, headed by a Director-General; established under **CISF Act 1968**, operationally raised **10 March 1969**; **1983 amendment** made it an armed force of the Union. The Act title year differs from raising year. [India Code](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/indiacode/handle/123456789/1599?view_type=browse).
- Embedded clipping: Centre approved expansion with about **58,000 additional recruits over five years**; source reports roughly **1.88 lakh existing personnel** and deployment at **359 establishments**. These are issue-period staffing/deployment figures and recruitment plans.
- Industrial/critical infrastructure security: airports, nuclear/space/power installations, ports, Delhi Metro, Parliament and selected monuments; specialised **fire wing**, VIP security and security consultancy, including approved private-sector deployment. Airport-security expansion followed the IC-814 hijacking; private-security mandate expanded through later legal changes.
- Source's seven-sector list is an organisational snapshot. Its claim CISF is the **only CAPF with daily public interaction** is overbroad; retain distinctive infrastructure/public-facing mandate, not exclusivity. Practice answer is **(a) 1 only**, not nonsensical printed '1 and 3 only' for two statements.

topics.title: Asian giant tortoise: community conservation in Nagaland
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Reintroduction in Nagaland
- Ten captive-bred **Asian giant tortoises, Manouria emys**, released into a **soft-release enclosure at Zeliang Community Reserve, Peren, Nagaland**, near **Ntangki National Park**. Nagaland Forest Department, India Turtle Conservation Programme and communities participated; bred at **Nagaland Zoological Park, Chümoukedima**.
- Soft release acclimatises animals and encourages site fidelity before dispersal; release counts are not evidence of a self-sustaining recovered wild population.
## Species revision
- **Largest mainland Asian tortoise**, terrestrial, forest-dwelling; subspecies **M. e. emys and M. e. phayrei**. Northeastern India through Bangladesh/Myanmar to Southeast Asia, including Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia.
- **Critically Endangered; CITES Appendix II**. Builds above-ground leaf-litter nest mounds, unusual among tortoises; seed dispersal supports forest regeneration. Late maturity/slow life history make recovery difficult.
- Deforestation, habitat change, bushmeat hunting and illegal pet trade threaten it. Avoid turning the infographic's simplified turtle/tortoise comparison into rules that every turtle is carnivorous or every tortoise freshwater-living. [Specialist biological account (2015; its Red List table is older)](https://iucn-tftsg.org/cbftt/species-accounts/manouria-emys-086/), [Nagaland recovery project](https://www.rufford.org/projects/sushmita-kar/building-road-recovery-asian-brown-tortoise-manouria-emys-phayrei-nagaland-northeast-india/).

topics.title: Women in the armed forces: inclusion and institutional reform
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Source-period inclusion review
- Defence Minister highlighted expanding women's participation. Source **2024 officer counts**: Army **1,735**, IAF **1,614**, Navy **674**, compared with **767/574/154 in 2005**. Its **13.4% IAF/6.85% Army/6% Navy** figures should be read with officer-category denominators, not as shares of all ranks or nursing/medical personnel combined.
- **30 May 2025: first 17 female NDA cadets passed out**, 148th Course, after entry in 2022. Graduation from NDA precedes further service-academy training/commissioning. [MoD milestone](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2132691&lang=2&reg=3).
- Women serve across Air Force branches; Navy opened branches apart from source-period submarine restrictions; Army entry/PC remains arm/service-specific, not universal entry into every combat role. The PDF's '12 branches including combat' cannot be read as opening infantry/armoured combat arms without restriction.
- **Permanent Commission** opportunities expanded, Army aviation helicopter-pilot entry from **2021**, women at sea and eligible Agniveer routes are distinct reforms. Training/physical eligibility is role/service-specific; 'identical standards everywhere' is too sweeping.
## Equality and operational capacity
- Articles **14,15,16**, broader talent pool and community engagement support inclusion; women exemplified by **Col. Sofiya Qureshi/Wing Commander Vyomika Singh** challenge stereotypes.
- Priorities: merit and role-specific standards, gender-sensitive accommodation/equipment, predictable career/command progression, childcare/posting support, fair grievance processes and prevention of harassment. Technology does not eliminate physical demands; care responsibilities should not be assumed exclusively female.
- Inset chronology: **1888 military nursing**, **1958 regular medical commissions**, **1992 Women Special Entry**, **2005 SSC replacing WSES**, **2020 Babita Puniya**, **2021 NDA litigation (Kush Kalra)**. Distinguish medical/nursing, officer and other-rank pathways.

topics.title: Battery waste: EPR pricing and critical-mineral recovery
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Battery Waste Management Rules 2022
- Growing EV/storage deployment creates spent batteries needing safe collection, recycling/refurbishment and recovery of lithium, nickel/cobalt where present. Battery chemistry differs: not every lithium-ion battery contains cobalt/nickel.
- **BWMR 2022** places extended producer responsibility on producers; registered recyclers/refurbishers and **EPR certificates** underpin compliance. Battery waste has its own rules: do not automatically count it within the e-waste inventory or transfer e-waste certificate price bands unchanged.
## Editorial: adequate EPR floor pricing
- Genuine recycling requires machinery, collection/transport, skilled labour and safe processes. Too-low certificate remuneration can undermine viable recovery and reward paper compliance, unsafe informal processing or fake certificates.
- Reform proposals: cost-based predictable remuneration, audited recovery/traceability, genuine enforcement against fraud, producer compliance and domestic recovery capacity. Critical-mineral recovery can reduce import/foreign-exchange exposure; it does not remove all virgin-mineral demand.
- Editorial forecasts **139 GWh demand by 2035 from 4 GWh in 2023** and **over US$1 billion forex loss by 2030** depend on scope/assumptions; keep as attributed projections. The printed **700,000 tonnes lithium batteries within 1.6-million-tonne 2022 e-waste** is unverified and mixes legal/statistical categories; do not learn it as established inventory.
- Lower global metal prices may give producers room to absorb compliance costs, but **no increase in consumer prices** is not guaranteed; assess cost pass-through and fair competition. Better EPR helps circularity, energy security and India's **2070 net-zero** ambition alongside repair/reuse.

topics.title: Cloudbursts and Himalayan flash-flood risk
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Hazard and August 2025 context
- Embedded report describes flash floods through **Dharali, Uttarkashi**, from **Kheer Ganga**, with early deaths/missing-person reports. Treat casualties as preliminary; a devastating flash flood alone does not prove a measured cloudburst at the site.
- IMD definition centres on **100 mm or more rainfall in an hour over a small local area**, often cited **20–30 km²**; NDMP 2019 uses roughly **less than 100 km²**. Area descriptions are not competing rainfall thresholds. [IMD study](https://mausamjournal.imd.gov.in/index.php/MAUSAM/article/view/5084), [NDMP 2019](https://rsmcnewdelhi.imd.gov.in/images/pdf/NDM_Plan_2019.pdf).
- Moisture-rich air rises/cools rapidly in strong convection; mountain uplift can intensify rainfall. **Not exclusive to orographic lifting or July–August/18–28°C**, despite the source graphic. Warmer air's moisture potential can intensify extreme rain; it does not establish a uniform measured increase in every Himalayan valley.
- Steep slopes, unstable sediment, constricted drainage and exposed settlements convert intense rain into flash floods, debris flows and landslides; deforestation/poor construction amplify vulnerability rather than directly defining a cloudburst.
## Reduce exposure and impacts
- Local rain/radar monitoring and impact-based warnings, catchment/landslide hazard zonation, protected drains, slope-sensitive building/road siting, resilient bridges, evacuation planning and community drills. Insurance assists recovery but cannot replace safe siting.

## Kishtwar flash-flood report, August 2025
- Embedded clipping reports a flash flood at **Chisoti village, Kishtwar, Jammu&Kashmir**, on the **Machail Mata pilgrimage route**; early toll **at least40 dead,100+missing**. These are preliminary issue-time reports, not final totals; extreme flood damage alone does not verify a measured100mm/hour cloudburst at the exact site.
- NDRF/SDRF, Army, police and local volunteers undertook rescue; safety of pilgrims, evacuation routes, settlement siting and exposed bridges matter alongside rainfall warning. Definition/process and NDMP2019 measures repeat existing notes.
- Practice answer **1 only(A)** is consistent with its statements; the explanation accidentally swaps statement numbers. Cloudbursts are localised, and orographic uplift can contribute; fixed18–28°C/July–August conditions are not universal requirements.

topics.title: Money laundering: PMLA, evidence and international cooperation
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Process and prevention
- Concealing criminal origins to make proceeds appear legitimate: **placement → layering → integration**. Banks, shell entities, property or businesses may be abused; these stages need not always occur as a neat sequence. 'Laundromat' is a metaphor for a laundering network, not proof the term's popular mafia origin story.
- **PMLA 2002**, effective **1 July 2005**, targets laundering and attachment/confiscation of proceeds of crime. Money laundering must connect to criminal activity relating to a **scheduled offence**; it is not every unexplained asset or tax irregularity automatically.
## Correct the worksheet's blanket legal claims
- **Section 24**: specified presumptions apply in proceedings involving proceeds of crime; prosecution must establish foundational facts. This is not a universal obligation on every person to prove innocence in every respect. [PMLA text](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/2036/5/A2003-15.pdf).
- **ECIR** is ED's internal record, not the same as a police FIR. The civil provisional-attachment/inquiry route and criminal prosecution/arrest requirements must be distinguished; the text's 'no FIR ever needed for PMLA' is too broad. **Vijay Madanlal Choudhary (2022)** addresses this distinction; do not rely on the PDF's unverified attribution of a 2017 Vir Bhadra Singh ruling to the Supreme Court.
- **DTAAs** avoid double taxation and may provide information-exchange cooperation; not immunity for illicit transfers. Treaty scope/conditions, FATF standards, beneficial-ownership transparency and cross-border cooperation support enforcement.
- Rising case registrations/low convictions alone do not establish guilt, misuse or the final effectiveness of pending cases; analyse timelines, completed trials and evidence quality. Strengthen trained investigation, reasoned decisions, judicial oversight and due process alongside recovery.

topics.title: Assets under management: funds and NBFC portfolios
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Meaning and limits
- **AUM** is the value of assets managed; for mutual funds, these are investor portfolios, not the fund manager's own corporate assets. Stocks, bonds/cash and other permitted investments may be included. In NBFC reporting, AUM commonly refers to the managed lending portfolio; distinguish it from mutual-fund AUM.
- Market changes, subscriptions and redemptions alter fund AUM. Reinvestment retains value within a fund compared with a payout; it does **not independently create wealth or mechanically raise AUM by the dividend amount**, since NAV adjusts for distributions.
- High AUM can permit scale/diversification but does not guarantee performance, low fees, good liquidity, investor trust or redemption resilience. Asset quality, concentration and liability/liquidity management matter.
## August clipping and statistical correction
- Embedded **India Ratings FY26 projection**: NBFC AUM growth may slow **25% (FY25)→18.5%**, with constrained bank funding and stress in microfinance/unsecured lending; higher-rated firms may access capital markets. A forecast, not realised FY26 growth.
- The PDF's **₹74.40 lakh crore mutual-fund AUM** belongs to approximately **June 2025**, not its summary's '2024 data'. AMFI's contemporaneous June note reported crossing **₹74 lakh crore**; do not conflate that industry stock with the NBFC growth forecast. [AMFI June 2025](https://www.amfiindia.com/Themes/Theme1/downloads/AMFIMonthlyNote_June2025.pdf).

topics.title: India–Philippines: geography and strategic partnership
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## 5 August 2025 strategic partnership
- During **President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s India visit**, both countries elevated relations to a **Strategic Partnership**, with **2025–2029 Plan of Action**. Priorities include defence/maritime security, trade, connectivity and technology; talks toward a preferential trade agreement and direct flights are initiatives, not proof a completed FTA or all flights already operating.
- Embedded clipping mentions first joint naval exercise with three visiting Indian ships and hydrographic cooperation; **freedom of navigation**, HADR and search/rescue are shared priorities. Philippines is the first overseas BrahMos customer (**2022 contract**, deliveries from 2024), distinct from new August procurement.
- [Philippine presidential announcement](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/philippines-india-forge-strategic-partnership-through-landmark-agreements/), [Indian economic-diplomacy account](https://indbiz.gov.in/india-philippines-advance-trade-and-strategic-ties-with-preferential-trade-framework/).
## Map recall
- Southeast Asian archipelago, western Pacific, **7,000+ islands**; **Luzon north (Manila), Visayas central, Mindanao south**. Presidential republic; unitary Philippines differs from the **federal US**, despite the source analogy.
- **Philippine Sea east, South China Sea west/northwest, Sulu Sea southwest, Celebes Sea south**. **Mount Apo, Mindanao (~2,954 m)** highest; **Cagayan, Luzon** longest river; **Agusan/Mindanao rivers** in the south. Tropical maritime/monsoonal climate varies regionally; June–November rainy/December–May dry is a broad pattern, not uniform for every island.
- US mutual defence treaty and maritime disputes explain Indo-Pacific salience. **2016 South China Sea award** was by an **UNCLOS Annex VII arbitral tribunal with PCA as registry**, not a PCA court awarding sovereignty over all disputed islands/seas; distinguish maritime entitlements from territorial sovereignty.
- [PCA 2016 award announcement](https://pca-cpa.org/en/news/pca-press-release-the-south-china-sea-arbitration-the-republic-of-the-philippines-v-the-peoples-republic-of-china/).

topics.title: Red-eared slider turtle and pet-release invasions
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Identity and invasion
- **Trachemys scripta elegans**, a semi-aquatic slider native to the southern United States/northeastern Mexico; distinctive red patch behind each eye, dark green/brown shell and yellow markings. Omnivorous; feeds in water and basks on logs/rocks; long-lived (source range **20–50 years**).
- Mainly freshwater habitats; can tolerate some brackish conditions. Pet releases establish alien populations competing with native turtles for food, basking sites and habitat; India's occurrence does not make it native.
- Source **Least Concern** refers to conservation assessment of the slider taxon; abundance in its native range is compatible with invasive harm elsewhere. Listed in the widely used **100 worst invasive alien species** compilation, not a current numerical rank.
- Practice trap: **statement 2 only = option B**. PDF prints “A. 2 only” despite its option A being “1 only”; statements about Indian nativity and Critically Endangered status are false. [USDA invasive-species profile](https://www.invasivespeciesinfo.gov/aquatic/fish-and-other-vertebrates/red-eared-slider).

topics.title: Biochar: carbon storage and productive uses
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Process → uses
- **Biomass → pyrolysis (limited/absent oxygen; source diagram 300–700°C) → carbon-rich biochar + bio-oil + combustible syngas.** Feedstock and process determine safety, yield and properties; mixed municipal waste requires segregation/contaminant control.
- Stable carbon can persist for centuries; porous biochar improves soil structure, water/nutrient retention and habitats for beneficial microbes. It can reduce some soil greenhouse-gas emissions, but effects vary with soil, crop, dose and char quality.
- Other uses: modified char for industrial CO₂ adsorption; wastewater pollutant adsorption; additives in construction materials; syngas for electricity and upgraded bio-oil for fuel substitution. These are potential applications, not universal performance guarantees.
## India: source scenario, not achieved output
- PDF estimates annual feedstock **600 Mt farm residues +60 Mt municipal waste**. Using **30–50%** could yield **15–26 Mt biochar**, roughly **0.1 Gt emission-removal potential**, and **8–13 TWh electricity (~0.5–0.7%)**; bio-oil could substitute some imports (source projects ~2% fossil-emission reduction). The emission quantity's carbon/CO₂ basis is unspecified; do not convert it into a verified national removal inventory.
- Illustrative source ranges: **10–25% crop-yield gains;10–20% less fertiliser;30–50% less N₂O**; concrete **2–5% char /115 kg CO₂ stored per m³**; **200–500 L wastewater/kg char**, **2.5–6.3 Mt char demand**, against **70 billion L/day wastewater**. All require study/process conditions, not guaranteed field/design rules. **N₂O GWP100≈273** is a mass-based climate metric, not general toxicity.
## Adoption priorities
- Obstacles: feedstock collection and quality, upfront cost, awareness, uncertain demand/business models, evolving technology, weak agriculture–energy–climate coordination and credible measurement/reporting/verification (MRV).
- Establish regional feedstock/process standards, field trials, residue/bioenergy and State climate-plan links, local production, farmer training and verified carbon finance. Source projects **5.2 lakh rural jobs**; this is an opportunity estimate.
- Source's blanket “no carbon-credit systems” claim is too broad: crediting depends on the scheme, approved methodology, additionality, permanence and lifecycle accounting. Avoid claiming every farmer automatically earns credits.
- **2020 PYQ: (d), all three**—vertical growing media, nitrogen-fixing microbial habitat and longer water retention. [USDA biochar/soil-carbon overview](https://nrcs-prod.azureedge.us/conservation-basics/soil/soil-health/soil-carbon-amendments).

topics.title: Accessible India Campaign and barrier-free access
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Campaign and implementation
- **Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan / Accessible India Campaign**, launched **3 December 2015** by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment; supports UNCRPD obligations.
- Three verticals: **built environment; transport; information/communication ecosystem**. Accessibility audits, retrofitting, ramps/lifts/tactile signage, accessible websites/documents and the Sugamya Bharat mobile app address physical/digital barriers.
- Campaign work continued through **Creation of Barrier-Free Environment under SIPDA**; the PDF's March 2024 completion reference is a programme milestone, not the end of the State's continuing accessibility duty.
- **6 August 2025 Rajya Sabha reply: ₹564.50 crore released for retrofitting 1,835 government buildings**. Funding/coverage does not establish every building's completed, independently verified accessibility. The source's older “700+” list and inset “1,748” describe different snapshots; do not combine them into one current achievement total. [Parliament reply](https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/268/AU2059_Ws1BZj.pdf?source=pqars).
- Practice: coverage of all three verticals is correct; the nodal ministry is Social Justice and Empowerment. The PDF explanation refers to statements 3/4 absent from its two-statement question.

topics.title: Maritime law reform and port-sector development
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## 6 August 2025: distinguish the Houses
- **Lok Sabha passed the Merchant Shipping Bill** (introduced in 2024; passed as the **2025** Bill), replacing the **Merchant Shipping Act, 1958**; modernises ship registration, safety, seafarer welfare, environmental compliance and alignment with IMO conventions. On this issue date it had **not completed both Houses**; Rajya Sabha passage came on 11 August.
- **Rajya Sabha passed the Carriage of Goods by Sea Bill, 2025**, completing parliamentary passage; replaces the **Indian Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 1925**, updating cargo-carriage rights, duties/liabilities and contractual clarity. Passage is distinct from assent and commencement. [6 August Ministry release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2153211&lang=2&reg=48).
## Sector opportunities and constraints
- Sea routes carry approximately **95% of Indian trade by volume/70% by value**; India's position between Suez and Malacca supports ports, transshipment, shipbuilding/repair, recycling and marine services. Source lists **13 major/200+ other ports**; administrative designation and operational status differ.
- **MIV 2030**: port/logistics modernisation; **Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047** supplies the longer horizon. **Sagarmala**: port-led development and hinterland/coastal connectivity; **Major Port Authorities Act, 2021**: greater port-board autonomy. National Logistics Portal (Marine)/Sagar Setu reduce paperwork and coordinate logistics.
- Vadhavan and Great Nicobar/Galathea Bay are planned developments, not completed operating container hubs. JNPA's **10+ million TEU** milestone is **capacity**, not evidence of annual throughput above 10 million; retain the existing JNPA distinction.
- Source **820 MMT handled/1,630 MMT capacity** are dated major-port metrics; **10,000 MMT by 2047**, **₹5 lakh crore by 2030/$1 tn by 2047 investment needs** are planning estimates, not present output/funds already spent. Its “16 th maritime nation,” turnaround **0.9 days**, dwell **3 days**, nine ports in a performance index require the named metric/year; do not treat them as universal current rankings.
- **LPI 2023 international-shipment rank22 vs44** is a sub-index, not India's overall LPI rank. Capacity, cargo handled, container TEUs and efficiency rankings measure different things.
## Greening and safeguards
- **Green Tug Transition Programme:** all tugs at **Indian major ports** envisioned green by **end 2040**, a scope-specific transition goal. Green-hydrogen hub ports include **Paradip, V.O.Chidambaranar (Tuticorin), Deendayal (Kandla)**. [GTTP announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2045946&lang=2&reg=48).
- **Hong Kong Convention**, adopted 2009, entered into force **26 June 2025**; safe/environmentally sound ship recycling, hazardous-material inventories and authorised facilities. Alang's role does not certify every yard automatically compliant.
- Mains: resolve berth/equipment bottlenecks, last-mile rail/road gaps, skills shortages and financing; combine digitisation/clean fuels with oil-spill control, coastal ecosystems, community consultation and fair rehabilitation.

topics.title: Haemophilia and preventive care
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Deficiency → bleeding → prevention
- Inherited haemophilia impairs coagulation: **A = factor VIII deficiency; B = factor IX deficiency**. Spontaneous joint/muscle bleeds cause pain, chronic arthropathy/disability; intracranial bleeding can be life-threatening.
- **Prophylaxis** means regular preventive haemostatic treatment before bleeding; **on-demand/episodic** treatment follows a bleed. WFH recommends sustained prophylaxis for severe bleeding phenotypes to protect joints, activity and quality of life. Factor replacement is commonly intravenous; some non-factor treatments are subcutaneous. Treatment choice requires specialist assessment. [WFH 2020 guidelines](https://guidelines.wfh.org/guidelines/).
- Early diagnosis, district testing/referral, high-risk-family screening, reliable affordable factor supply, trained clinicians, physiotherapy and a patient registry reduce avoidable disability. School/work participation, mental health and household costs are policy outcomes alongside hospital admissions.
- Source estimates **1–1.5 lakh expected Indian cases versus~29,000 diagnosed**; these are approximate source figures, not a complete prevalence census. Rural access, cost, stigma and low awareness contribute to underdiagnosis. Its “each untreated bleed shortens life by16 days” is an unsupported universal calculation and should not be memorised.
- Source proposes subsidised treatment/NHM–Ayushman Bharat integration, domestic production and non-factor/gene-therapy research; these recommendations do not establish universal national coverage. Practice answer **2 only**: factor IX causes B, not A.

topics.title: Goldilocks economy and household welfare
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Aggregate balance versus lived welfare
- **Goldilocks economy**: sustainable growth without overheating/recession, with low/stable inflation and supportive macroeconomic conditions. A favourable aggregate reading does not establish that all households benefit equally.
- PDF cites **May 2025 CPI2.82% versusMay 2024 4.80%**; these are dated readings, not August inflation. RBI target was **4%±2 percentage points**, not “a2–6% target” with no central aim. [NSO June release with May final data](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2144511&lang=1&reg=6).
- **October 2024 CPI6.21% /CFPI10.87%** illustrates a period when food inflation exceeded headline inflation; food carries larger budget weight for poorer households. This does not mean food inflation was above headline in every subsequent month.
- **Real wage growth adjusts nominal gains for inflation**; source examples **2023 nominal9.2%/real2.5%;2020 real−0.4%** are dataset-dependent, not proof about every Indian worker. Weak real incomes constrain consumption and savings despite headline GDP growth.
- **K-shaped recovery** describes divergent outcomes between better-off/organised groups and vulnerable workers/households. Taxable-income Gini, consumption Gini and wealth concentration measure different populations/variables; a decline in a tax-return Gini does not settle national inequality.
- **FY 2025–26 Union fiscal-deficit BE4.4% of GDP** differs in scope from **~81% general-government debt/GDP**. Debt service can squeeze fiscal space; borrowing can crowd out private credit, while well-designed public investment may also crowd investment in. Fiscal consolidation does not automatically prove that every welfare/public-investment outlay fell.
- The source's old **FY 2023–24 growth7.6%/$3.6 tn** snapshot and FY25 forecast are not the latest releases available by August 2025; use the existing GDP topic's dated national-account estimates. Evaluate employment, real wages, distribution, health/education and fiscal composition together.

topics.title: North Eastern Council: statutory composition and regional planning
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Body and role
- **NEC Act, 1971**; Council inaugurated **7 November 1972**, headquartered **Shillong**, administratively under **Ministry of DoNER**. Statutory regional planning/advisory institution; Article263 does not create NEC.
- **2002 amendment** added Sikkim and strengthened regional planning, project formulation, monitoring/evaluation. Members enumerated in section 3: **Governors and Chief Ministers of constituent States +three Presidential nominees**; President nominates Chairman from members.
- **2018 repositioning:** Union Home Minister nominated **ex-officio Chairman**, DoNER Minister Vice-Chairman. Thus the PDF's absolute “Home Minister is not a member of the Council” is misleading: the **2024 PYQ asks the statutory composition after 2002**, not the later chairmanship arrangement. [2018 Cabinet decision](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=179941).
- Supports coordinated transport, power, health, education, skills and entrepreneurship; inter-State consultation complements State/Centre planning. Delayed implementation, limited resources, conflict, terrain and coordination gaps impede delivery. Do not categorically equate every NEC role with either an executing department or a body barred from programme implementation.
- Embedded August clipping reports **₹11.31 crore released in July 2025**, including **₹2.09 crore for kiwi orchards**; funds released are not completed project outcomes.
- **2024 PYQ:(a),1,2,3 only**; retain the question's legal/time qualification alongside the 2018 distinction.

topics.title: Biofortified potatoes and micronutrient security
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Nutrition through crop development
- **Biofortification** raises micronutrient density during crop growth through breeding, agronomic methods or biotechnology; **food fortification** adds nutrients during processing. Biofortified does not automatically mean genetically modified.
- **CIP (International Potato Center), Lima, Peru**, develops iron-rich potatoes through **conventional crossing/selection**, combining nutrition with acceptable yield, taste and disease resistance. August coverage describes testing/adaptation for India; it does not establish nationwide commercial availability or identical yield everywhere. [CIP breeding explanation](https://cipotato.org/potato/biofortified-potatoes/).
- Iron-rich potatoes target hidden hunger/iron deficiency; orange-fleshed sweetpotatoes supply **beta-carotene (provitamin A)**. Source reports their availability in Karnataka, Assam, West Bengal and Odisha; dietary diversity, bioavailability and seed access still matter.
- **CIP South Asia Regional Centre, Singna, Agra**, Cabinet-approved in 2025; potato/sweetpotato/root-crop research, quality seed, climate resilience, pests and value chains. Construction/establishment should not be assumed completed just from approval. [CIP26 June 2025 announcement](https://cipotato.org/pressreleases/cip-announces-launch-south-asia-regional-centre-agra/).
- Correct the PDF's “61 biofortified varieties”: the **11 August 2024 release involved109 varieties of 61 crops—34 field and 27 horticultural crop species/categories**; all 109 were not necessarily biofortified. Salt/pest resistance, e.g.CR Dhan 416, is not itself proof of nutritional biofortification. Durum wheat composition depends on the named variety; “12%protein” is not a universal biofortification criterion. [2024 release](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2044052&lang=2&reg=48).

topics.title: El Salvador: geography and presidential re-election
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## July 2025 constitutional change
- **31 July 2025**, Legislative Assembly approved/ratified changes allowing **indefinite presidential re-election**, extending terms **five→six years**, eliminating presidential runoffs and aligning election cycles. Source raises democratic-backsliding concerns: assess term limits, checks/balances and electoral competition. [Assembly announcement](https://asamblea.gob.sv/node/13645).
## Map recall
- **Central America**, capital **San Salvador**; Guatemala northwest, Honduras northeast, Pacific south; **only Central American country without Caribbean frontage**.
- Mountain/volcanic terrain; **Cerro El Pital (~2,730 m)** at Honduras border is highest. **Lempa River**; lakes **Ilopango, Coatepeque, Güija**; volcanoes **San Salvador, Ilopango, San Vicente**. Tropical climate varies with altitude; Pacific coastal lowlands can be hot despite cooler uplands.

topics.title: iSAT and AI-based agrometeorological advisories
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Initiative and delivery
- ICRISAT-led **AI-powered Context-Specific Agromet Advisory Services for Climate-Resilient Agriculture at Scale**, inception workshop **29–30 July 2025, Hyderabad**, supported by **Monsoon MissionIII**.
- Builds on **Intelligent Systems Advisory Tool (iSAT)** piloted under Monsoon MissionII; combines weather forecasts, historical climate, soil/crop calendars, crop models and AI/ML to tailor sowing, irrigation and pest-management advice.
- Maharashtra initial implementation through **ICAR Agro-Meteorological Field Units (AMFUs)**; WhatsApp bots/digital channels aim to reach smallholders. Nationwide/Global South expansion is planned, not completed adoption.
- Consortium: **ICRISAT, ICAR-CRIDA, ILRI**; technical support **IITM, IMD, IIT Ropar, CSIR-CSIO, IISc**. Forecast uncertainty, local-language delivery, connectivity, agronomic validation and farmer feedback determine usefulness. [ICRISAT initiative account](https://isscanews.icrisat.org/copy-icrisat-and-partners-launch-ai-powered-climate-advisory-initiative-to-boost-farmer-resilience).

topics.title: Rhisotope: nuclear markers against wildlife trafficking
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Marker → border detection → deterrence
- **University of the Witwatersrand (South Africa)** with **IAEA** and partners: insert low-level radioisotopes into rhino horns so existing customs radiation detectors can identify trafficking; project moved to operational deployment in **August 2025**.
- Radioisotopes are unstable nuclei emitting radiation during decay; natural (C-14) and artificial (Co-60) examples illustrate the class, not disclosure of the exact horn isotope. Other uses include medical imaging/radiotherapy, industrial inspection/sterilisation, tracers and agriculture.
- Pilot **20 rhinos** in **Waterberg Biosphere, Limpopo**; veterinary/blood-cell tests found no observed harm at tested doses. Detection tests used **3D-printed horns** with comparable shielding, including a **40-foot container**. Distinguish tested safety/detection from proven long-term reductions in poaching.
- PDF claims horns become “toxic to humans/worthless” and calls procedure non-invasive; do not use these as established conclusions. It involves inserting markers, with dose controlled for safety; the verified mechanism is **traceability/deterrence**, not poisoning consumers. [Wits1 August 2025 operational report](https://www.wits.ac.za/future/stories/2025/rhisotope-project-goes-live.html).
- Poaching for traditional-medicine/status markets persists; source global population~27,000 and historical500,000 are approximate dated estimates. It lists103 early 2025 cases without a clear period/geography; not a verified whole-year South African total.
- **Waterberg**: Bushveld landscape, water/biodiversity and San cultural heritage; **Nylsvley** is a Ramsar wetland in Limpopo, but proximity/region alone does not prove inclusion within the biosphere's boundary. Nuclear markers supplement surveillance, habitat protection and community action; scaling to elephants/pangolins remains a possibility.

topics.title: Apna Ghar: highway rest facilities for truck drivers
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Design and progress
- Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas initiative; **public-sector Oil Marketing Companies** provide safe, hygienic rest at highway retail fuel outlets.
- **1 July 2025: 368 facilities/4,611 beds**. Dormitories typically **10–30 beds**, dhabas/restaurants, self-cooking spaces, toilets, bathing areas (**houdas**) and purified drinking water; app supports bookings and user feedback.
- Rest/access improves truck-driver welfare and can reduce fatigue-related road risk. An OMC delivery model does not establish every facility is a separately procured PPP. [31 July 2025 Parliament-reply release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2150823&lang=2&reg=48).

topics.title: IEPFA and recovery of unclaimed investor assets
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Authority and fund
- **Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority**, established 2016 under **Companies Act, 2013**, Ministry of Corporate Affairs; administers refunds and investor education.
- IEPF receives specified unpaid/unclaimed sums after the statutory **seven-year** period, including dividends, matured deposits/debentures and refundable application money; interest/grants are also fund receipts. Share transfer has its own conditions under section 124; do not apply “all assets idle sevenyears” indiscriminately.
- **1 August 2025:** Integrated Portal in **final testing**, planned to connect companies, depositories and **PFMS**, simplify claims/status access and improve data quality. Low-value documentation review and integrated call-centre support were announced; planned simplification is not an already universal instant-refund entitlement.
- Awareness initiatives: **Niveshak Didi**(women-led literacy), **Niveshak Panchayat**(community outreach), **Niveshak Shivir**(investor camps). [MCA announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2151474&lang=2&reg=48).

topics.title: Alpine musk deer and conservation-breeding identification
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Species and identification
- **Moschus chrysogaster**, family **Moschidae**, distinct from true deer (Cervidae); solitary, largely crepuscular herbivore of high-altitude Himalayan/Asian forest–scrub, approximately **3,000–5,000 m**. Browses grasses, forbs, lichens/mosses and twigs.
- **Endangered**; threats: musk poaching and habitat disturbance. Indian protection **Schedule I**. **CITES population qualification:** Moschus populations of Afghanistan, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan are Appendix I; other populations Appendix II. Appendix I restricts international commercial trade; it is not an absolute ban on every permitted movement. [CITES taxonomic/trade assessment](https://cites.org/sites/default/files/eng/com/ac/16/16-7-4.pdf).
- Distinguish **Alpine M.chrysogaster** and **Himalayan M.leucogaster**. CZA review found taxonomic confusion and **no currently reported captive stock of Alpine musk deer in recognised Indian zoos**, suggesting its breeding programme was never initiated. Historic Chopta/Darjeeling stock was probably Alpine; Himachal stock probably Himalayan. PDF's assertion of a definitively started programme “for the wrong species” overstates this qualified assessment. [CZA planned-breeding review, p22](https://cza.nic.in/uploads/documents/publications/english/review.pdf).
- Correct species identity, genetic/studbook records and appropriate founder populations are prerequisites for ex-situ conservation; a photograph labelled Himalayan cannot establish Alpine identity.
- Source range countries: **India, Nepal, Bhutan and China**; species-level identification matters because Himalayan musk deer has overlapping distribution.

topics.title: Kopili River and National Waterway 57
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## River and navigation
- Inter-State river of **Meghalaya/Assam**, **left/south-bank tributary of Brahmaputra**; important drainage through the Dima Hasao/North Cachar, Karbi Anglong, Nagaon–Morigaon region. Source length **256 km (78 km border reach+178 km Assam)**; its origin wording conflates Meghalaya with North Cachar Hills, so do not memorise that administrative description without a basin map.
- **2 August 2025:** **MV V. V. Giri** trial carried **300 MT cement** from **Govardhan Bridge, Chandrapur (Kamrup)** to **Hatsingimari**, using **NW57+NW2**; **~300 km/12–14 hours**. First cargo trial on **46 kmNW57 since 2014**, part of revival of intra-State freight. River length, designated waterway length and total voyage distance differ. [Ministry release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2151729&lang=2&reg=48).
- Assam's operational national-waterway network reported **1,168 km** across **BrahmaputraNW2, BarakNW16, DhansiriNW31, KopiliNW57**. A cargo trial is not proof of year-round deep-draft navigation or every segment's commercial viability.
- Inland transport can reduce road congestion/freight emissions; needs terminals, last-mile links, adequate water levels and ecological safeguards. Meghalaya coal-mining-related **acidification** threatens river health and infrastructure.
- Embedded old map mislabels Barak **NW6**; the **National Waterways Act, 2016 expanded the total to111**, and **Barak=NW16**. Do not use the inset's old “five waterways/4,603 km” as a 2025 inventory. Declared status and navigational operationalisation are different dates.

topics.title: Palmyra livelihoods and Udangudi palm jaggery
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Sap → sweeteners → livelihood
- **Palmyra (Borassus flabellifer)**, Tamil Nadu's State tree; Thoothukudi climbers tap **pathaneer** from inflorescences. Lime-coated collection pots inhibit fermentation; sap is boiled/concentrated, then cooled in coconut-shell moulds into **karupatti**; crystallisation produces **panangkarkandu**, sometimes flavoured with ginger/pepper/long pepper.
- Source describes a roughly **five-month season**, collections before sunrise, mid-morning and evening, and multi-day processing. Dangerous climbing without adequate safety equipment, low returns, seasonal employment and younger workers leaving threaten skill continuity.
- August source prices: producers **₹200–250/kg**, retail up to **₹380/kg**; these are local reported prices, not a national minimum or current quotation. Improve safety gear/training, insurance, producer collectives, direct marketing, quality assurance and off-season income.
## Udangudi GI
- **Udangudi Panangkarupatti**, Thoothukudi, is palm jaggery, not coconut jaggery. GI register **application 691; certificate 3 October 2023**—“recently” in the practice prompt does not mean first registered in August 2025. [GI Registry](https://search.ipindia.gov.in/GIRPublicSearch/Application/Details/691).
- Source links its character to red sand-dune soils and dry conditions; traditional processing avoids additives such as phosphoric acid/triple superphosphate. Source export destinations: Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Singapore. GI protects origin-linked reputation and authorised production; it does not guarantee every seller's purity, income or medical efficacy.
- Tamil Nadu source distinguishes permitted fresh-sap sweeteners from prohibited toddy fermentation. “Chemical-free” is marketing shorthand; jaggery remains sugar and the source's medicinal/health superiority claims are not clinical proof. Practice answers: palmyra **B (2,3)**; Udangudi **D (neither)**.

topics.title: Kaleshwaram lift irrigation and project accountability
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## River and engineering
- Telangana's **Godavari** lift-irrigation scheme draws downstream of the **Pranahita–Godavari confluence** near Kaleshwaram/Medigadda; it is not a Krishna–Godavari confluence. Pumping lifts low-level water in stages to irrigation/drinking/industrial uses; gravity canals distribute water where levels permit.
- Three main Godavari barrages: **Medigadda (Lakshmi), Annaram (Saraswati), Sundilla (Parvati)**. The source's “four barrages including Ramadugu” conflates different infrastructure. [CAG performance audit, 2024](https://cag.gov.in/uploads/download_audit_report/2024/Report-1-of-2024%2C-Govt.-of-Telangana%28new%29-06a2be633637950.38261365.pdf).
- Source design figures: **1,800+ km canals**, 13-district reach; allocations **169 TMC irrigation; 30 Hyderabad drinking;16 industry/miscellaneous;10 village drinking**. Designed reach/new ayacut/stabilisation differ from achieved irrigated area; source's 16-lakh/45-lakh-acre references have different scopes and should not be combined.
## Feasibility, damage and inquiry
- Redesigned earlier **Pranahita–Chevella** proposal from **Tummidihatti** to Medigadda. Source reports earlier works ~₹11,000 crore, initial project estimate ~₹71,000 crore in 2015, later costs exceeding ₹1 lakh crore; estimates, spending and final costs are distinct.
- Inquiry controversy concerns water availability, location/design choices, permeable foundations, operating storage, Cabinet approval and financial accountability. Source attributes unilateral decisions to critics/inquiry and records BRS's denial/statutory-clearance defence; allegations are not convictions.
- Do not memorise the PDF's claim that Sundilla was the barrage whose piers sank: **Medigadda suffered the major October 2023 subsidence**, while Annaram/Sundilla also faced safety scrutiny. Site-specific investigations, foundation/seepage analysis and operating limits matter; construction on alluvial foundations is not inherently proof of negligence.
- Lessons: independently test hydrology and lifecycle energy/maintenance costs, scrutinise redesign and sunk costs, ensure collective approvals and transparent procurement, monitor dam safety and verify actual water delivery. Practice **B, statement2 only**. Krishna and Godavari are distinct river systems; the explanation's supposed confluence in Andhra Pradesh is also misleading.

topics.title: Rabies: transmission, prevention and public health
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Infection and prevention
- **Rabies virus**, an **RNA virus (Rhabdoviridae)**, causes a zoonotic neglected tropical disease of the central nervous system. Infected mammal saliva enters via bites/scratches or broken skin/mucosa; dogs cause up to **99% of human cases**.
- Virus moves from exposure tissues along peripheral nerves → brain → salivary glands. Incubation commonly **2–3 months**, varying from about a week to a year. Early fever/pain/tingling may progress to furious disease (hydrophobia, agitation) or paralytic disease; clinically apparent rabies is virtually always fatal.
- Prompt **post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP)** prevents disease: thorough wound washing for at least **15 minutes**, urgent professional care, a validated vaccine schedule and **RIG when indicated**. Do not delay for symptoms. The source's universal “HRIG +4–5 doses” is too rigid: route/regimen/prior immunisation and exposure category determine treatment.
- Mass dog vaccination, bite prevention, surveillance and accessible PEP form a **One Health** response; pre-exposure vaccination serves selected high-risk groups. WHO's **~59,000 annual deaths** is a modelled global estimate, not reported cases; under-reporting is substantial. [WHO fact sheet](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/rabies).
## August source context
- Newspaper clipping concerns SC directions on Delhi stray-dog capture/non-release. This is the issue's stage of an evolving case, not a permanent nationwide rule. Another clipping reports **3.7 million dog-bite cases and54 suspected rabies deaths in2024**; these reported surveillance figures are not directly comparable with estimated true rabies mortality.
- Practice **B (2 only)**: RNA, not DNA; timely complete PEP is highly effective before symptoms.

topics.title: Marital cruelty law and safeguards against violence
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Statutory offence
- **IPC498A inserted1983**; under the BNS, **section85** punishes cruelty by husband/his relative with **up to three years and fine**; **section86** defines cruelty. It covers wilful conduct likely to drive suicide or cause grave injury/danger to life, limb or mental/physical health, and harassment linked to unlawful property/valuable-security demands. [BNS official text](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/indiacode/bitstream/123456789/20062/1/a202345.pdf).
## July 2025 decision and editorial debate
- **Shivangi Bansal v Sahib Bansal,22 July2025**, not the PDF's July2024. Source discusses endorsement of Allahabad HC Family Welfare Committee guidelines and a two-month cooling period before coercive action in covered matrimonial complaints. This is an account of the July2025 ruling, not an instruction to delay emergency protection or a substitute for reading its scope. [SC judgment](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2023/35609/35609_2023_11_1502_62486_Judgement_22-Jul-2025.pdf).
- Editorial concern: delayed intervention can expose complainants to violence/intimidation or coerced compromise, while treating criminal complaints as only family disputes. Balance prompt protection/investigation with reasoned arrest safeguards and due process; **Arnesh Kumar(2014)** opposed automatic arrest, not investigation itself.
- Source recalls **Sushil Kumar Sharma(2005)** and **Preeti Gupta(2010)** on misuse concerns; individual false allegations do not establish nationwide misuse rates. Conversely, low conviction cannot by itself prove false cases: evidence, investigation, compromise and reporting barriers matter.
- Source cites **NCRB2022:1,34,506 cases/~18% conviction**, plus NFHS-5 under-reporting concerns; keep reporting and conviction denominators separate. Practice **A (1 only)**: punishment is three, not five years. Gender-sensitive legal aid, shelters and safety assessment should accompany procedural safeguards.

topics.title: Piprahwa relics and cultural repatriation
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Discovery and 2025 return
- **1898: William Claxton Peppé**, Piprahwa stupa, present-day **Siddharthnagar district, Uttar Pradesh**, near Nepal. Assemblage includes reliquaries, bone fragments and precious offerings/jewels, associated through inscription/tradition with Buddha and the Sakya community; distinguish sacred remains from accompanying gems.
- **30 July2025**: return of the overseas-held relic jewels after127years through Government–**Godrej Industries Group** cooperation. Sotheby's Hong Kong auction planned **7 May2025** was halted after intervention; the PDF's “2024 auction” is incorrect. Many objects were already held by Indian museums; this was not recovery of every Piprahwa object from abroad. [Culture Ministry announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2150352&lang=2&reg=3), [official backgrounder](https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/aug/doc2025811604701.pdf).
## Heritage governance
- Sacred objects carry religious meaning beyond auction value; recovery supports Buddhist cultural diplomacy, scholarship and public access. Coordinate Culture/External Affairs/diplomatic missions with credible private partners; preserve provenance, conservation and public custody.
- Editorial proposals: digitised cross-border provenance registries, auction/customs alerts, clearer ownership/export evidence and international cooperation. Existing heritage conventions/laws are not absent, although retrospective colonial claims and sacred-object sales face gaps; a proposed global ban is not already binding law.
- Embedded graphic's **~480BCE** Buddha chronology is approximate/disputed, not an exact death date. Its Mauryan-era enshrinement relates to the deposit, not excavation. Practice **A (1 only)**: location is UP, not Bihar.

topics.title: SC/ST and other disadvantaged-group scholarships
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## August 2025: proposed eligibility expansion
- Ministries were considering income-ceiling revisions for **2026–27 to 2030–31**; reported ST proposal **₹2.5 lakh→₹4.5 lakh** and upward review for SC/OBC/DNT schemes are proposals, not operative revised entitlements.
- **Tribal Affairs** administers ST scholarships; **Social Justice and Empowerment** covers relevant SC/OBC/EBC/DNT schemes. Pre-matric generally targets school access; post-matric supports study after ClassX. Top-class schemes have separate rules.
- Important exception to source's blanket₹2.5-lakh claim: **SC pre-matric ComponentI** covers ClassesIX–X with₹2.5-lakh ceiling; **ComponentII** covers ClassesI–X children of persons in specified unclean/hazardous occupations **irrespective of caste/religion, with no family-income ceiling**. [Official scheme](https://socialjustice.gov.in/schemes/23).
- Source CSS comparison **60:40 general/90:10 northeastern States** must be checked against the particular scheme's guidelines; it is not one funding rule for every scholarship/UT.
- Source **2025–26** budget comparisons: social-justice scholarships **66.7%of₹13,611 crore**; tribal scholarships **18.6%of₹14,925.81 crore**. These are ministry allocation shares, not all national education spending.
- Source beneficiary trends: SC pre-/post-matric **−30.63%/−4.22%(2020–21 to 2024–25)**; OBC/EBC/DNT pre-matric **58.62 lakh(2021–22)→20.25 lakh(2023–24)**, post-matric **43.34→38.42 lakh**; ST reported falls **4.63/3.52 lakh**. Periods/scheme redesign/data completeness differ; low ceilings are a proposed explanation, not demonstrated sole causation.
- Parliamentary recommendations: higher ceilings, OBC pre-matric from ClassV, broader top-class coverage. Index ceilings to costs, simplify applications, ensure timely payments and measure retention/outcomes. Source practice is unyearred and its universal income/funding statements are overbroad; do not memorise the printed key without the exceptions.

topics.title: Water hyacinth: invasion, livelihoods and collective control
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Kerala backwaters and livelihood impacts
- **Water hyacinth, Eichhornia crassipes /Pontederia crassipes**, South American floating invasive with lilac flowers, introduced ornamentally during the colonial period. Avoid the source practice's unsupported named-introducer claim; it is not native to India.
- Dense mats in **Vembanad–Kuttanad, Kerala** obstruct irrigation, boats/nets, fish habitat and tourism; shade vegetation and impede surface gas exchange. Decomposition consumes oxygen and can emit methane; oxygen is not simply unable to “reach” water by a single mechanism.
- Source infestation estimate **over2 lakh hectares nationally** lacks survey year/method; a source-period estimate, not a current measured inventory. Its **methane25×CO₂** figure uses an older100-year warming metric and should not be treated as timeless or a toxicity comparison.
- Odisha SHGs use dried biomass for baskets/furniture; source Assam/West Bengal examples include paper/biogas. Compost/textile/biofuel uses require contamination checks and viable processing/markets; biomass enterprise must not create incentives to spread the weed.
- Combine nutrient-load reduction, early detection, locally suitable removal, safe biomass handling, monitoring and tested biological approaches; short clearance drives allow regrowth. Coordinate agriculture/fisheries/irrigation/environment agencies with clear accountability, mechanisation, local participation and shared research.
- Source JainUniversity, Kochi workshop proposed outreach/discussion paper and science–local-knowledge integration; these were proposed actions. National policy/innovation incentives/private investment are editorial recommendations, not an enacted new scheme.
- **2018 PYQ Prosopis juliflora:(b)**, reduces biodiversity; arid/semi-arid invasive thickets can affect pastoral livelihoods. This is a separate invasive plant, not water hyacinth. Water-hyacinth practice intended **2 only(b)**; its fourth option contains a stray statement3.

topics.title: Religious conversion: autonomy, safeguards and State laws
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## August 2025 legal debate
- Embedded news describes a **proposed Uttarakhand amendment Bill**, including severe punishment up to life for specified offences. The issue says it would be tabled; do not record proposed provisions as already commenced law.
- State freedom-of-religion laws prohibit specified forced/fraudulent/coerced/allurement-based conversions; definitions, notice requirements, enhanced penalties and burden provisions vary. **Voluntary change of faith and freedom of conscience remain protected**; interfaith marriage alone does not establish unlawful conversion.
- Historical source examples: princely **Raigarh1936, Patna1942, Sarguja1945, Udaipur1946** laws; unsuccessful central Bills **1954,1960,1978**; Odisha's **1967** and MP's **1968** enactments. TamilNadu's later law was repealed. Do not treat the issue's State list as a verified operative-law inventory.
- Correct “religion is a State subject”: legislative competence depends on the measure and relevant entries, including **State public order**; there is no single blanket State-list religion entry. Failed central proposals alone do not establish Parliament can never legislate.
## Constitution and case-law distinctions
- **Article 25**: conscience/profession/practice/propagation, subject to public order, morality, health and other PartIII provisions; regulation of secular activities/social reform permitted. **Article 26** protects denominational religious management subject to its limits. **27** concerns taxes specifically appropriated to promote/maintain a particular religion.
- **Article 28(1)** concerns institutions **wholly maintained by State funds**, with clause2 exception and clause3 consent safeguards; not a blanket ban across every aided institution. **Article 29(1)** protects any section of citizens with a distinct language/script/culture, not only minorities; **30** concerns religious/linguistic minority educational institutions. [Constitution](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/359f70a69695affb9d72f8393102bd2e.pdf).
- **Rev.Stainislaus(1977)** upheld MP/Odisha anti-conversion laws and distinguished propagation from a right to convert another; freedom of conscience is equal for all. **Sarla Mudgal(1995), Lily Thomas(2000)**: conversion does not automatically dissolve an existing Hindu marriage or legitimise a second marriage; “all conversion to Islam is invalid” is incorrect.
- **Puttaswamy(2017)** links belief/faith/personal choice with privacy, dignity and autonomy. Notice rules, vague allurement definitions, reverse burdens and misuse allegations require scrutiny for necessity, proportionality and fair process. Source HP2012/Gujarat2021 references concern particular provisions/interim relief, not invalidation of every State law.
- Source **M.Chandra(2010)** concerns evidence of conversion/community status in its context; do not turn it into one mandatory ritual for every faith. The GrahamStaines discussion is not authority to legitimise violence or override conscience.
- Way forward: precise offences, protect voluntary adult choice, fair investigation/hearing, accessible remedies and interfaith dialogue. Practice intended **two statements(b)**; privacy PYQs point to **Article 21/PartIII**.

topics.title: Ideonella sakaiensis and enzymatic PET recycling
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Organism → enzyme pathway
- **Ideonella sakaiensis**, genus Ideonella/family **Comamonadaceae**: Gram-negative, rod-shaped, motile with a single flagellum, non-spore-forming and non-pigmented; source dimensions **1.2–1.5 × 0.6–0.8 μm**. Identified from a PET-recycling-site microbial community in **Sakai, Japan**; reported in **2016**. Isolation near polluted material does not prove pollution newly created the species.
- **PET → PETase → chiefly MHET → MHETase → terephthalic acid + ethylene glycol → microbial assimilation/recovered feedstock.** Experiments establish the two enzymes' roles; performance depends on substrate crystallinity and conditions. [Gene-disruption study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8388835/).
- **PET = polyethylene terephthalate**, a thermoplastic polyester from ethylene glycol/terephthalic acid; strong, lightweight and transparent; bottles, food packaging and textile fibres. Degrading PET does not establish degradation of polyethylene, PVC or every mixed plastic.
## Recycling opportunity and limits
- Source describes moist, oxygenated contaminated soils/sludge; a laboratory recycling pathway is not permission to release organisms into ecosystems. Biological depolymerisation could recover monomers and complement collection/segregation, reuse and conventional recycling.
- Source calls the products “harmless”; **ethylene glycol is hazardous if ingested**, so avoid treating monomers or incompletely treated effluent as universally environmentally benign. Recovered chemicals need controlled handling, purification and process assessment. [CDC ethylene-glycol toxicology](https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/ershdb/emergencyresponsecard_29750031.html).
- Practice: the Gram-positive/spore-forming/marine-origin statement is false. PDF selects **(b), 2 and 3**, but its blanket “benign compounds” wording needs the handling qualification above; this is source practice, not a dated CSE PYQ.

topics.title: Gaur and Palamau prey-base conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Palamau concern and species recall
- Source reports declining **gaur in Palamau Tiger Reserve, Jharkhand**, described as the State's last stronghold; it supplies no population time series, so do not infer a precise decline percentage.
- **Bos gaurus**, family **Bovidae**, commonly called Indian bison but a wild cattle species, among the largest living bovines. Native to South/Southeast Asia; Indian distribution includes Western Ghats, central India and Northeast.
- Evergreen, semi-evergreen/moist deciduous forests with grassy openings and dependable water; source preference below **1,500–1,800 m** is a habitat generalisation, not an absolute altitudinal boundary. Not a Thar-desert scrub specialist.
- **IUCN Vulnerable; CITES Appendix I; Wild Life (Protection) Act Schedule I**. International trade regulation, domestic legal protection and extinction-risk assessment are different systems. [Amended statute](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1726/1/aA1972-53.pdf).
## Threat → response
- Habitat fragmentation, mining/agriculture, disturbance, hunting and domestic-cattle disease exposure reduce viable herds. Gaur are important large prey for tigers; herbivory and seed movement influence vegetation.
- Source names rinderpest and foot-and-mouth disease; **rinderpest is a historical threat, globally eradicated in 2011**, not an established active 2025 outbreak. [WOAH eradication history](https://www.woah.org/en/disease/rinderpest/). Maintain livestock disease surveillance/immunisation, grazing safeguards, water/forage habitat and connected undisturbed forest.
- Practice: **1, 2 and 4 only (a)**; habitat restricted to Thar/Deccan dry scrub is false. Disease susceptibility does not establish that disease caused every observed decline.

topics.title: Kodali Karuppur sari and textile-craft revival
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Technique, patronage and motifs
- Named for **Karuppur near Kumbakonam, Tamil Nadu**; combines **hand painting, block printing and brocade weaving**, including gold/silver effects. Textile heritage connects Thanjavur Maratha patronage with Saurashtrian weaving communities.
- Source associates royal patronage with **Serfoji II** and gives **1787–1832** as a broad patronage period; it should not be treated as his lifetime or an uninterrupted reign. Worn by Thanjavur royal women; presented as **khillat/clothes of honour**, entering wedding trousseaux in Maratha courts such as Baroda, Kolhapur and Satara; related turbans for men.
- Motifs: geometric/linear patterns, vines, stars, **Veldarri chevrons** and **thazhambu/screw-pine flower**. Source's **400–500 migrant families** is an undated historical estimate, not a present artisan census.
## Threatened transmission and GI distinction
- Dwindling traditional weavers threaten knowledge transmission; apprenticeships, documentation, fair artisan incomes, authentic markets and design support are revival priorities.
- **Kodali Karuppur Saree application 409** is listed **withdrawn**, not registered; distinguish it from separately registered **Karuppur Kalamkari Paintings (424)**. Absence of a GI does not mean the craft has no possible legal protection of any kind. [GI sari record](https://search.ipindia.gov.in/GIRPublicSearch/Application/Details/409), [painting record](https://search.ipindia.gov.in/GIRPublicSearch/Application/Details/424).
- Practice: Tamil Nadu/Thanjavur patronage is correct; a claim that this sari currently has a registered GI is unsupported by that record. Do not transfer the painting's registration to the sari.

topics.title: Smooth-coated otter and wetland conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Source report and identification
- Source reports a **pair transferred from Surat to National Zoological Park, Delhi**, an exchange after a long gap; exchange supports captive conservation/awareness, not proof wild populations recovered.
- **Lutrogale perspicillata**, traditionally the only living Lutrogale species; large, social semi-aquatic otter with shorter, smoother brown fur and lighter underside.
