Dense underfur insulates; guard hairs repel water. Strong swimmers, can move over land; cooperative fish hunting may use a V-like formation.
- Lowland rivers/lakes, freshwater wetlands, mangroves, peat swamps and rice-growing landscapes across South/Southeast Asia; an isolated **Iraqi** population extends beyond that core range. Habitat loss, pollution and illegal fur/pet trade threaten it. [IUCN SSC species profile](https://www.otterspecialistgroup.org/otter-species/lutrogale-perspicillata/).
## Protection and practice correction
- **IUCN Vulnerable**. The PDF's **Schedule II** label is outdated: the amended Wild Life (Protection) Act, consolidated **5 June 2025**, lists **Smooth-coated Otter, item 105 of Schedule I**. [Primary statute](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1726/1/aA1972-53.pdf).
- Practice statements on its Southeast Asian size and Iraqi population are both intended correct: **option (c), both 1 and 2**. Printed “(a) 1 and 2” is an option-letter error; (a) actually says “1 only”.

topics.title: Patent landscape: universities and commercialisation
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Filing, grant and innovation are separate measures
- Universities' IP cells, legal assistance, incentives and technology-transfer offices can convert research into protectable inventions; patent counts alone do not measure scientific quality, successful products or public benefit.
- **WIPO 2024 report, calendar 2023:** resident applications were **55.2% of filings received by India's office**, not the PDF's 57%; Indian-origin applicants ranked **sixth globally** in filings. Source's claim India overtook the US as second-largest patent-grant recipient in 2021 is unsupported and should not be memorised. Resident share, applicant origin, receiving office and grant counts have different denominators. [WIPO resident-share report](https://www.wipo.int/web-publications/world-intellectual-property-indicators-2024-highlights/en/patents-highlights.html), [global origins](https://www.wipo.int/pressroom/en/articles/2024/article_0015.html).
- Source **2023 institution/company/individual shares 43%/17%/32%** and computer/electrical/biomedical/physics shifts **1.27→26.5% /8.27→16.4% /0.6→10% /2→4%** concern its reported dataset; the scope is insufficient to make them shares of every Indian-office patent. Likewise IIT Madras **156→300** and IIT Bombay **421 (2023–24)** are institutional examples, not a verified national league table.
## Enabling policy and bottlenecks
- **National IPR Policy 2016; Atal Innovation Mission 2016; KAPILA 2020** support IP awareness/innovation. Digital filing, eligible expedited examination and fee concessions support participation; fee reductions depend on applicant category/rules.
- Source reports grant times shortening from **8–10 to 2–3 years**, sometimes less; these are not a guaranteed statutory processing time. Its **80% awaiting decision** is an inadequately scoped backlog assertion, not a verified share of every application.
- **R&D ~0.67% GDP** is a dated expenditure estimate, not a 2025 measurement. Limited research resources, legal/administrative capacity and weak university–industry links impede commercialisation.
- Priorities: sustained R&D investment (source proposes **2% GDP**), examiner capacity, IP literacy, fair licensing, proof-of-concept support and research–industry collaboration; evaluate use, licensing revenue and societal outcomes alongside grant volume. Practice answer's categorical “universities largest share in India” needs its dataset denominator, so do not reproduce the supplied answer as a verified all-India fact.

topics.title: Honour crimes: caste, patriarchy and adult choice
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Social mechanism and constitutional harm
- “Honour” killings are murders justified by claimed family/community reputation, often targeting women/couples over inter-caste or inter-faith relationships, partner choice, sexuality or perceived sexual conduct. Caste endogamy, patriarchy, control over women's autonomy and informal community sanctions reinforce each other.
- Caste/khap assemblies have no authority to order violence or override adult consent. Harm includes loss of life/liberty, trauma, exclusion, restricted education/work and weakened confidence in policing; **Articles 14, 19 and 21** supply the equality, freedom and dignity frame.
- Source attributes **25 cases in each of 2019 and 2020, 33 in 2021** to NCRB. Treat these as recorded motive-based cases, not prevalence estimates; underreporting and misclassification limit inference.
## Legal framework: correct the source's numbering
- PDF recites **IPC 299–304/307–308/34–35**, which are legacy provisions; they do not become BNS provisions simply by adding “now BNS”. For post-commencement conduct use the applicable **BNS** provisions; murder punishment is **section 103**. Section **103(2)** addresses murder by **five or more acting in concert** on specified identity grounds, with death/life imprisonment and fine; every honour crime does not automatically meet those elements. [December 2024 official explanation](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2080661&lang=2&reg=48).
- Source's **2011 draft unlawful-assembly/matrimonial-interference proposal** and **Law Commission 242nd Report (2012)** are reform history, not an enacted national standalone honour-killing statute. Proposed new disqualification or shorter marriage-notice period is a recommendation, not existing law.
## Courts → implementation
- **Lata Singh (2006)**: protect inter-caste couples; **Krishna Master (2010)** and **Arumugam Servai (2011)** condemn caste-based violence/intimidation. **Shakti Vahini (27 March 2018)** protects consenting adults' choice; directions include preventive action, district special cells/helplines, protection/safe accommodation and prompt investigation/trial. [Supreme Court judgment](https://cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in/s3ec0490f1f4972d133619a60c30f3559e/documents/aor_notice_circular/46.pdf).
- Combine enforceable protection, accountable policing, witness/survivor support, timely designated trials, legal aid and education challenging caste/patriarchal control. Any marriage-procedure reform must protect safety and adult choice. Source daily mains **250 words/15 marks** is useful practice, without a supplied CSE year.

topics.title: Dibru-Saikhowa: grassland change and feral horses
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Floodplain setting and area distinction
- Eastern **Assam, Tinsukia/Dibrugarh**, riverine habitat bounded broadly by **Brahmaputra north and Dibru south**; grasslands, semi-evergreen/moist deciduous forest, bamboo and wetland mosaics. National-park status **1999**; biosphere reserve **1997**.
- PDF/tourism sources give **425 km²** for the park, but the Forest Department and district biosphere description give **340 km² core/park +425 km² buffer =765 km² biosphere reserve**. Keep these administrative scopes distinct; do not use 425 km² as an unquestioned park statistic. [Assam Forest Department](https://forest.assam.gov.in/portlets/national-park), [district explanation](https://tinsukia.assam.gov.in/tourist-place-detail/274).
- Known for **feral horses**, free-living descendants of domestic stock; source links them to WWII military horses and estimates **~200**. These are reported origin/count claims, not a current census or a separate wild-horse species. “Only habitat in India” is too absolute without a defined population scope.
## Grasslands in flux: study reported in August
- Remote-sensing/GIS LULC study covers **1999/2000–2024**; PDF gives grassland starting share **28.78% (2000)** but omits its ending share. Do not invent a final percentage; source reports decline and conversion to shrubland. **Degraded forest 80.52 km² by 2024** is the study's reported land-cover estimate, not necessarily the entire park's degraded area under every classification.
- Native woody encroachers **Bombax ceiba (simalu), Lagerstroemia speciosa (ajar)** can reduce open-grassland habitat. Alien invaders named: **Chromolaena odorata, Ageratum conyzoides, Parthenium hysterophorus, Mikania micrantha**. Native encroachment and alien invasion differ even when both alter grasslands.
- Flood dynamics, invasive plants, settlement/resource pressure and vegetation succession interact. Protect habitat for **Bengal florican, hog deer, swamp grass babbler** and other grassland-dependent fauna; not all species named are endemic to the park.
- Restoration needs habitat-specific invasive control, floodplain monitoring, community participation and grassland conservation alongside forest protection. More trees are not automatically better for every grassland ecosystem; habitat loss can increase conflict and ecological instability.

topics.title: SWAYAM and SWAYAM Plus: online learning and employability
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Access and academic value
- **SWAYAM: Study Webs of Active–Learning for Young Aspiring Minds**, Ministry of Education's national MOOC platform, formally launched in 2017; the issue reports free AI courses. Covers Class 9 through postgraduate learning; courses are free, while an optional certificate generally requires a fee and proctored examination. University credit transfer follows applicable UGC/AICTE rules rather than automatic acceptance of every course.
- Four learning quadrants: **video lectures → downloadable reading → self-assessment → discussion forum**. Access, equity and quality are aims; devices, connectivity, accessibility, language and completion support determine effective inclusion. [SWAYAM](https://swayam.gov.in/about).
- Coordinator anchors: **NPTEL** engineering; **UGC** non-technical postgraduate; **CEC** undergraduate; **NCERT/NIOS** school; **IGNOU** out-of-school learners; **IIM Bangalore** management; **NITTTR** teacher training; **AICTE** self-paced/international; source also lists Institutes of National Importance for non-technical courses. Institutional remit matters more than memorising an undated coordinator count.
- **SWAYAM Plus**, managed by IIT Madras, links industry and academia for employability: manufacturing, energy, IT/ITES, management, healthcare, hospitality/tourism and Indian knowledge systems. Source describes multilingual content, AI guidance, credit recognition and employment pathways; completing a course is not a job guarantee.
- **2016 PYQ: education access, option D**; the 2016 question predates the 2017 formal launch, so these dates are not contradictory.

topics.title: Halman apricot: Ladakh horticulture and Gulf exports
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## First reported Gulf consignment
- Source reports **1.5 metric tonnes of Halman apricots** sent to **Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Qatar** for the first time. This is the reported export milestone for this variety/consignment; do not infer Ladakh had never exported any apricot before.
- **Prunus armeniaca**, a cultivated apricot variety associated with Ladakh, especially **Sham/western Ladakh**: Dha-Hanu, Garkhon, Skurbuchan, Domkhar, Wanla, Khaltse and Timosgang. Source traces introduction to China/Central Asia over a century ago without an exact introduction year.
- Fresh/dried fruit, jams, chutneys and apricot oil connect horticulture with Ladakhi cuisine, rituals and livelihoods. Provides fibre and micronutrients; folk medicinal use does not demonstrate treatment efficacy.
- Export constraints: **short shelf life + remote mountain transport → cold-chain/packaging costs → quality losses**. Farmer training, processing, branding, cooperatives and market links can support premium sales and women's livelihoods. ODOP promotion and prospective GI branding are distinct; this source does not establish an awarded Halman GI.
- **2011 antioxidants PYQ: option C**, neutralisation of free radicals produced during metabolism. Antioxidants are not proof that a single fruit prevents cancer or ageing.

topics.title: Mount Elbrus and Caucasus mountain geography
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Map anchors
- Source reports an Arunachal Pradesh mountaineer's ascent of **Mount Elbrus, 5,642 m**, southwestern **Russia**, in the **Caucasus between the Black and Caspian Seas**. Conventionally Europe's highest summit and one of the Seven Summits; Europe–Asia boundaries are geographic conventions.
- Twin-summit volcanic massif; distinguish volcanic Elbrus from the wider Caucasus mountain belt formed in the Arabia–Eurasia collision zone. The source's “formed over 2.5 million years ago” is not a verified date for the present volcanic edifice. It is a dormant volcano, not a frequently erupting twentieth-century volcano.
- Glaciers including Bolshoi Azau and Irik sustain the **Baksan, Malka and Kuban drainage**; Prielbrusye National Park protects alpine ecosystems. Cold, altitude illness and crevasses require preparation even when a route has relatively modest technical difficulty.
- **2024 mountain-range PYQ: B, only two**. Vosges are European block mountains; Alps European fold mountains; Appalachians North American fold mountains; Andes South American fold mountains. Source Elbrus practice **C (1, 3 and 4)**; its option B is misprinted.

topics.title: Jellyfish blooms and coastal infrastructure risk
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Ecology meets power-plant resilience
- Embedded report describes an **August 2025 jellyfish swarm blocking cooling-water intakes at a French nuclear plant**, prompting shutdown. Marine organisms can disrupt critical infrastructure without damaging the reactor itself; intake monitoring, screening and safe cooling resilience matter.
- True jellyfish belong to **Cnidaria**, like corals and sea anemones; gelatinous, radially symmetrical zooplankton. **Epidermis → mesoglea → gastrodermis**; mesoglea is jelly-like material, not a third embryonic germ layer. They lack a central brain/heart/blood system, possess a nerve net and tentacular stinging structures (**nematocysts**), and pulse their bell while drifting with currents.
- Blooms can be favoured by warm water, removal of predators/competitors, eutrophication/hypoxia and artificial surfaces supporting life stages; species/local conditions determine outcomes. Pollution does not invariably cause a bloom, and no single bloom proves climate change as its sole cause.
- Large blooms can consume fish eggs/larvae, compete for plankton, foul fishing nets, sting tourists and obstruct power-plant intakes. Some jellyfish tolerate low oxygen better than competitors; avoid saying all survive every anoxic condition.
- **2021 detritivores PYQ: C (earthworms, millipedes, woodlice)**. Jellyfish and seahorses are predators; detritivores ingest dead organic matter, unlike microbial extracellular decomposition. Unyearred bloom practice: **D (all four)** within the source's broad framing.

topics.title: Union Territory assemblies: nomination and democratic accountability
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## August controversy and statutory architecture
- Issue reports Home Ministry's position that **J&K Lieutenant Governor can nominate up to five MLAs without Council of Ministers consultation**; this reported executive interpretation must be distinguished from a final judicial determination of the disputed procedure.
- **J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019**: **90 elected seats** after delimitation; **Section 15** permits up to two women if inadequately represented; **2023 amendment Sections 15A and 15B** add **up to two Kashmiri migrants, one a woman**, and **one displaced person from Pakistan-occupied J&K**. The two migrant seats are not two unrestricted discretionary nominees. [Amending Act](https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/247633.pdf).
- **Puducherry:** 30 elected MLAs and up to three Central-government nominees under the **Government of Union Territories Act, 1963**. **Delhi:** 70 elected seats and no analogous nominated-MLA provision under its 1991 Act. Different UT statutes require separate analysis.
- Comparators: **Rajya Sabha 12 presidential nominees**; State Legislative Councils approximately **one-sixth governor nominees**, ordinarily on ministerial advice. Anglo-Indian nomination to Lok Sabha/State Assemblies ceased in 2020 under the 104th Amendment's effect on Article 334.
- Source discusses the 2018 Puducherry litigation and elected-government consultation. Nominated voting members can affect majority arithmetic; clear statutory procedure and democratic accountability matter, especially when Union and UT governments differ politically.
- Correction: the December 2023 Article 370 judgment **did not finally decide the validity of converting J&K as a whole into a UT**; it recorded the assurance of restoration of statehood and upheld Ladakh's separate UT status. Do not repeat the source's blanket claim that the whole conversion was upheld.
